# 牛津习语词典


2576 个单词，7266 条习语。其中 7266 条（100.0%）的释义和例句经过校对重写。


<table>
<thead><tr><th>单词</th><th>习语</th><th>中文解释</th><th>例句</th></tr></thead>
<tr><td><b>A</b></td><td>from A to ˈB</td><td>从一处到另一处</td><td>She spends two hours a day just getting from A to B in traffic.<br>她每天光是堵在路上从一处赶到另一处就要两小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from A to ˈZ</td><td>从头至尾；详尽彻底地</td><td>He knows this old engine from A to Z, so let him fix it.<br>这台老发动机他门儿清，让他修吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>aback</b></td><td>be taken aˈback (by sb/sth)</td><td>大吃一惊；被吓一跳</td><td>I was taken aback by how rude the waiter was to my mother.<br>服务员对我妈那么无礼，我简直惊呆了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>about</b></td><td>be about to do sth</td><td>正要做某事；即将做某事</td><td>I was about to call you when your message popped up on my screen.<br>我正想给你打电话，你的消息就跳出来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how/what about...?</td><td>（询问情况或提出建议）怎么样</td><td>We've tried everything else, so how about asking your brother for help?<br>别的法子都试过了，找你哥帮忙怎么样？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how/what about ˈthat (, then)? (informal)</td><td>（表示惊讶或赞叹）是吗；太妙了</td><td>She got the scholarship on her first try — how about that, then!<br>她第一次申请就拿到奖学金了，你说妙不妙！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be about to do sth</td><td>不愿做某事；无意做某事</td><td>I'm not about to lend him money again after what happened last time.<br>出了上次那事，我可不打算再借他钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's about ˈall/it</td><td>就这些；没别的要说了</td><td>Milk, bread, a bag of rice — that's about it for the shopping list.<br>牛奶、面包、一袋米，购物清单就这些了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>above</b></td><td>above ˈall (ˈelse)</td><td>尤其是；最重要的是</td><td>Above all, remember to lock the back door before you leave tonight.<br>最要紧的是，今晚走之前记得锁后门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>aˌbove and beˈyond sth (formal)</td><td>超越（职责等）；不止于</td><td>Staying up all night with the patient was above and beyond her normal duties.<br>整夜守着病人，远远超出了她的分内职责。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get aˈbove yourself (disapproving)</td><td>自命不凡；狂妄自大</td><td>Ever since his promotion he's been getting a bit above himself.<br>自从升职以后，他就有点儿不知天高地厚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>abreast</b></td><td>keep aˈbreast of sth</td><td>了解…的最新情况；跟上…的发展</td><td>As a nurse she has to keep abreast of the latest research on infections.<br>当护士就得随时了解感染方面的最新研究。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>absence</b></td><td>ˌabsence makes the heart grow ˈfonder (saying)</td><td>离别情更浓；小别胜新婚</td><td>They text all day now he's abroad — absence makes the heart grow fonder.<br>他出国后两人整天发消息，真是小别胜新婚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave of ˈabsence (formal)</td><td>准假；休假</td><td>He asked for three months' leave of absence to look after his sick father.<br>他申请了三个月假期去照顾生病的父亲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>accident</b></td><td>by ˈaccident</td><td>偶然；意外地</td><td>I found the old photo album by accident while clearing out the attic.<br>我清理阁楼时偶然翻出了那本旧相册。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(whether) by ˌaccident or deˈsign</td><td>不论是偶然还是有意</td><td>Whether by accident or design, his email went to the whole company.<br>不管是无心还是有意，他那封邮件发给了全公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>accidentally</b></td><td>acciˌdentally on ˈpurpose (informal, ironic)</td><td>故作意外地；假装无意地</td><td>She accidentally on purpose left her number on his desk.<br>她故作无意地把电话号码留在了他桌上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>accidents</b></td><td>accidents will ˈhappen (saying)</td><td>意外总是难免的</td><td>Don't cry over the broken vase, sweetheart — accidents will happen.<br>别为打碎的花瓶哭了，宝贝，意外总是难免的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>accord</b></td><td>of your own acˈcord</td><td>自愿地；主动地</td><td>Nobody pushed him; he handed in his resignation of his own accord.<br>没人逼他，辞职信是他自己主动交的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>account</b></td><td>of little/no acˈcount (formal)</td><td>无关紧要；无足轻重</td><td>To the manager, our objections were clearly of no account at all.<br>在经理看来，我们的反对意见根本无足轻重。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈno account •not on ˈany account</td><td>决不；无论如何都不</td><td>On no account should you open that door while the machine is running.<br>机器运转时你决不能打开那扇门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on your own acˈcount</td><td>为自己；自行负责地</td><td>She quit the agency and started trading on her own account last spring.<br>去年春天她离开中介，开始自己单干做买卖。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/turn sth to good acˈcount (formal)</td><td>充分利用（金钱、才能等）</td><td>He put his years in the kitchen to good account when he wrote the book.<br>写这本书时，他把多年的厨房经验用了个够。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth into acˈcount •take account of sth</td><td>考虑到；把…考虑在内</td><td>We must take rising prices into account when we plan next year's budget.<br>做明年预算时我们一定要把物价上涨考虑进去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>accounting</b></td><td>there's no accounting for ˈtaste(s) (saying)</td><td>人各有所好；好恶无从解释</td><td>He put ketchup on his noodles — well, there's no accounting for taste.<br>他往面条上浇番茄酱，唉，人各有所好吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>accounts</b></td><td>by/from ˈall accounts</td><td>据大家所说；据说</td><td>By all accounts the new manager is much easier to work with.<br>据大家说，新来的经理好相处多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ace</b></td><td>play your ˈace</td><td>打出王牌；使出绝招</td><td>He waited until the last minute of the meeting to play his ace.<br>他一直等到会议最后一刻才打出王牌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>within an ace of sth/of doing sth (BrE)</td><td>差一点儿；几乎</td><td>Our team came within an ace of winning the championship last night.<br>昨晚我们队差一点点就拿下冠军了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>aces</b></td><td>have/hold (all) the ˈaces (also hold all the ˈcards)</td><td>握有王牌；占绝对优势</td><td>With three job offers in hand, she holds all the aces in this negotiation.<br>手握三个录用通知，这场谈判她占尽优势。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>achilles</b></td><td>an/sb's Achilles' ˈheel</td><td>致命弱点；阿喀琉斯之踵</td><td>His temper has always been his Achilles' heel in front of clients.<br>在客户面前，他的脾气一直是他的致命弱点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>acid</b></td><td>the ˌacid ˈtest (of sth) (also the ˈlitmus test especially in AmE)</td><td>决定性的考验；试金石</td><td>The real acid test of the new brakes will be a rainy mountain road.<br>这套新刹车真正的考验是雨天的山路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>acquaintance</b></td><td>make sb's acˈquaintance •make the acˈquaintance of sb</td><td>结识某人；与某人初次相见</td><td>I made her acquaintance at a rather boring conference in Shanghai.<br>我是在上海一个挺无聊的会议上认识她的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>acquired</b></td><td>an acquired ˈtaste</td><td>逐渐培养出来的爱好</td><td>Blue cheese is definitely an acquired taste, but now I love it.<br>蓝纹奶酪绝对是慢慢才吃得惯的，可现在我爱死它了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>act</b></td><td>read (sb) the ˈRiot Act</td><td>严厉训斥；警告不得再犯</td><td>Dad read us the Riot Act after he saw the mess in the kitchen.<br>爸爸看到厨房一团糟，把我们狠狠训了一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>act</b></td><td>an ˌact of ˈGod (law)</td><td>天灾；不可抗力</td><td>The insurer refused to pay, calling the flood an act of God.<br>保险公司称洪水属不可抗力，拒绝赔付。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈbalancing/juggling act</td><td>搞平衡；两头兼顾</td><td>Raising twins while finishing her thesis was a constant balancing act.<br>一边带双胞胎一边写论文，她天天都在走钢丝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get in on the ˈact (informal)</td><td>（在他人成功后）插一手；参与分羹</td><td>Once the café took off, every landlord wanted to get in on the act.<br>咖啡馆一火，每个房东都想来插一脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do/perform/stage a disapˈpearing/ˈvanishing act (informal)</td><td>（需要时）不见踪影；溜之大吉</td><td>Whenever there's washing-up to do, my brother does a disappearing act.<br>一到要洗碗的时候，我弟弟就消失得无影无踪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈvanishing act (informal)</td><td>（需要时）消失不见；找不到人</td><td>He pulled his usual vanishing act the moment the bill arrived.<br>账单一送来，他又照例玩起了人间蒸发。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈact together •get sth/it toˈgether</td><td>振作起来；把事情安排妥当</td><td>You need to get your act together before the exams start next month.<br>下个月考试前你得好好振作起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(informal) (also get/have your ˈshit together, ◆ slang)</td><td>更有条理；更好地安排（或管理）</td><td>Give him a week to get his shit together and he'll finish the report.<br>给他一周把事情理顺，报告他就能写完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a hard/tough act to ˈfollow</td><td>难以超越的人（或事）</td><td>Our old teacher was so popular that she's a tough act to follow.<br>以前那位老师太受欢迎了，谁接手都难以企及。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>action</b></td><td>ˈaction stations (spoken, especially BrE)</td><td>（下令准备行动）各就各位</td><td>Action stations, everyone — the inspectors will be here in ten minutes!<br>各就各位，各位，检查员十分钟后就到！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>There's a bus full of tourists arriving in five</td><td>还有五分钟一车游客就到（例句片段）</td><td>There's a bus full of tourists arriving in five minutes, so look busy.<br>再过五分钟一大巴游客就到，都装忙一点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈaction</td><td>在工作；在运转；活动中</td><td>I'd love to see the new printing press in action before we buy it.<br>买之前我很想看看这台新印刷机怎么运转。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of ˈaction</td><td>（因伤病）不能工作；（因损坏）失灵</td><td>A knee injury has put our best striker out of action for six weeks.<br>膝伤让我们的主力前锋六周不能上场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a piece/slice of the ˈaction (informal)</td><td>（利益的）一份；一杯羹</td><td>Everyone wants a slice of the action now the shop is making money.<br>店里开始赚钱了，人人都想分一杯羹。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>where the ˈaction is</td><td>热闹之处；活动中心</td><td>If you want nightlife, the harbour district is where the action is.<br>想找夜生活，港口区才是热闹的地方。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ad</b></td><td>ad ˈhoc (from Latin)</td><td>临时的；特设的；专门的</td><td>They set up an ad hoc committee to deal with the parking complaints.<br>他们成立了一个临时委员会处理停车投诉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ad infiˈnitum (from Latin)</td><td>无休止地；反复不停地</td><td>He repeats the same three jokes ad infinitum at every family dinner.<br>每次家宴他都把那三个笑话翻来覆去地讲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ad ˈnauseam (from Latin)</td><td>（因重复而）令人厌烦地</td><td>The coach discussed our defensive mistakes ad nauseam after the match.<br>赛后教练把我们的防守失误说得人耳朵起茧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>adam</b></td><td>not know sb from ˈAdam</td><td>完全不认识某人</td><td>He waved at me in the street, but I don't know him from Adam.<br>他在街上冲我招手，可我根本不认识他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>add</b></td><td>add ˌfuel to the ˈfire/ˈflames</td><td>火上浇油</td><td>Bringing up her ex at dinner just added fuel to the flames.<br>晚饭时提起她前任，简直是火上浇油。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pour oil on troubled ˈwater(s)</td><td>平息争端；调解纠纷</td><td>Grandma poured oil on troubled waters by changing the subject quickly.<br>奶奶赶紧换了话题，把这场争吵平息了下去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>add ˌinsult to ˈinjury</td><td>雪上加霜；伤害之外又加侮辱</td><td>They cancelled my flight, then, to add insult to injury, lost my suitcase.<br>航班取消了，更气人的是他们还弄丢了我的箱子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ado</b></td><td>without further/more aˈdo (old-fashioned)</td><td>立即；干脆地；不再耽搁</td><td>Without further ado, let me introduce tonight's very special guest.<br>闲话少说，我来介绍今晚这位特别嘉宾。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>advance</b></td><td>in adˈvance (of sth)</td><td>预先；事先</td><td>You have to book the tickets at least two weeks in advance.<br>票必须至少提前两周订。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>advantage</b></td><td>take adˈvantage of sth/sb</td><td>利用某机会；占某人便宜</td><td>We took advantage of the sunny weather and cycled along the river.<br>我们趁着天气晴朗，沿着河骑了一圈车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to sb's adˈvantage</td><td>对某人有利</td><td>Learning Spanish will be to your advantage if you move to Madrid.<br>如果你搬去马德里，学西班牙语对你有好处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to (good, better, etc.) adˈvantage</td><td>有效地；更出色地</td><td>The soft lighting shows the old paintings to great advantage.<br>柔和的灯光把这些旧画衬托得格外好看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn sth to your (own) adˈvantage</td><td>转害为利；为己所用</td><td>She turned her boss's mistake to her own advantage and got promoted.<br>她把老板的失误变成了自己的机会，还升了职。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>afield</b></td><td>far/farther/further aˈfield</td><td>在远处；到远方</td><td>We looked for cheaper rent further afield, out past the ring road.<br>我们把找便宜房租的范围扩大到了环路以外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Journalists came from as far afield as China</td><td>记者远自中国等地赶来（例句片段）</td><td>Journalists came from as far afield as China and Brazil to cover it.<br>来采访的记者远自中国、巴西等国。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>aforethought</b></td><td>with ˌmalice aˈforethought (law)</td><td>蓄意地；预谋地</td><td>The prosecutor argued he had acted with malice aforethought that night.<br>检察官称他那晚是有预谋地行事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>afraid</b></td><td>I'm afraid (that)... (spoken)</td><td>（礼貌地表歉意）恐怕；很遗憾</td><td>I'm afraid the last train left about twenty minutes ago, sir.<br>先生，恐怕末班车二十分钟前就开走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>after</b></td><td>after ˈall</td><td>毕竟；终究；还是</td><td>The rain stopped, so we had the picnic in the garden after all.<br>雨停了，我们最后还是在院子里野餐了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>again</b></td><td>aˌgain and aˈgain</td><td>一再；反复地；屡次</td><td>I told him again and again not to leave the gate open at night.<br>我一遍遍跟他说晚上别让大门开着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>then/there aˈgain (informal)</td><td>另一方面；话说回来</td><td>The flat is small, but then again the rent is really cheap.<br>房子是小，不过话说回来，租金真便宜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>age</b></td><td>ˌact/ˌbe your ˈage (informal)</td><td>别孩子气；举止要与年龄相称</td><td>Stop sulking about the cake and act your age, you're forty!<br>别为块蛋糕生闷气了，都四十的人了，成熟点！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌcome of ˈage</td><td>成年；达到法定年龄；发展成熟</td><td>Electric cars have really come of age in the last five years.<br>近五年电动车真正走向成熟了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌlook your ˈage</td><td>看上去与年龄相称</td><td>She's sixty but she certainly doesn't look her age at all.<br>她六十了，可看着一点都不像。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌunderˈage</td><td>未成年；未到法定年龄</td><td>The bar was fined for serving drinks to underage customers.<br>这家酒吧因向未成年人售酒被罚款。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>aggregate</b></td><td>on ˈaggregate (BrE, sport)</td><td>按（比赛）总比分</td><td>They lost four-three on aggregate after a dramatic second leg.<br>次回合跌宕起伏，他们总比分三比四出局。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>agree</b></td><td>aˌgree to ˈdiffer</td><td>各自保留意见；同意存异</td><td>We'll never agree about politics, so let's agree to differ.<br>政治上我们永远谈不拢，还是各持己见吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I ˌcouldn't agree (with you) ˈmore</td><td>我完全同意</td><td>The service here has gone downhill — I couldn't agree with you more.<br>这儿的服务越来越差，我完全同意你的看法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>aid</b></td><td>in aid of sb/sth (BrE)</td><td>为支援（或帮助）某人（某事）</td><td>The whole village ran a concert in aid of the children's hospital.<br>全村办了一场音乐会为儿童医院筹款。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's (all) ˈthis, etc. in aid of? (BrE, spoken)</td><td>这究竟是为什么；这有什么用</td><td>Balloons, cake, streamers — what's all this in aid of, exactly?<br>气球、蛋糕、彩带，这一通折腾究竟为哪般？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>aim</b></td><td>take ˈaim at sb/sth (AmE)</td><td>把矛头指向；集中批评</td><td>The mayor took aim at developers who leave building sites unfinished.<br>市长把矛头对准了那些烂尾的开发商。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>air</b></td><td>float/walk on ˈair (informal)</td><td>欢天喜地；喜气洋洋</td><td>She's been walking on air since she heard she got the job.<br>自从听说拿到那份工作，她一直乐得飘飘然。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈair</td><td>（想法、气氛等）在流传；即将到来</td><td>There's change in the air at the office, and everyone can feel it.<br>办公室里有种要变天的气氛，人人都感觉得到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(up) in the ˈair</td><td>（计划等）悬而未决；未确定</td><td>Our holiday plans are still up in the air until Dad hears about work.<br>爸爸的工作没定，我们的假期计划还悬着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌon/ˌoff the ˈair</td><td>正在／停止播出</td><td>Careful what you say — we're back on the air in ten seconds.<br>说话注意点，十秒后我们就恢复直播了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>airs</b></td><td>airs and ˈgraces (BrE, disapproving)</td><td>摆架子；矫揉造作</td><td>She came back from Paris full of airs and graces about food.<br>她从巴黎回来，一谈到吃就装腔作势。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give yourself/ˌput on ˈairs</td><td>摆架子；装腔作势</td><td>He puts on airs at parties, but he grew up on our street.<br>他在派对上装模作样，其实就在我们这条街长大。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>aladdin</b></td><td>an Aladdin's ˈcave</td><td>藏有大量珍宝的地方</td><td>Her grandfather's workshop was an Aladdin's cave of tools and old radios.<br>她爷爷的工作间简直是个工具和旧收音机的宝库。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>alive</b></td><td>aˌlive and ˈkicking (informal)</td><td>健在的；生气勃勃的</td><td>The old pub is still alive and kicking after eighty years.<br>这家老酒吧开了八十年，如今依旧红火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring sth aˈlive</td><td>使生动有趣；使活起来</td><td>Her funny stories really brought the history lesson alive for us.<br>她那些趣事让历史课一下子生动了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come aˈlive</td><td>（话题或活动）活跃起来；变得有趣</td><td>The square comes alive at night when the food stalls open.<br>夜里小吃摊一开张，广场就热闹起来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>all in ˈall</td><td>从各方面看；总的来说</td><td>All in all, it was a pretty good trip despite the awful weather.<br>总的来说，尽管天气糟糕，这趟旅行还不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>all ˈround (BrE) (AmE all aˈround)</td><td>全面地；在各方面</td><td>It was a better performance all round than the one last season.<br>比起上赛季，这场表现全面提升。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌall ˈthere (informal)</td><td>头脑清醒；思维清晰</td><td>Grandpa is ninety-two and still completely all there.<br>爷爷九十二了，脑子还清楚得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>and all ˈthat (rubbish, stuff, etc.) (informal)</td><td>以及诸如此类的事情</td><td>He kept going on about targets and deadlines and all that stuff.<br>他一个劲儿念叨指标、期限之类的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) at ˈall</td><td>一点儿也不；丝毫不</td><td>I didn't enjoy the film at all, and neither did my sister.<br>这电影我一点儿也不喜欢，我妹妹也是。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all about sb/sth (informal)</td><td>以…为主题（或核心）</td><td>For my father, weekends are all about football and nothing else.<br>对我爸来说，周末就只有足球这一件事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all sb can/could ˈdo (not) to do sth (informal)</td><td>要（不）做某事很难</td><td>It was all I could do not to laugh when his wig slipped.<br>他假发歪了，我憋着不笑真是费了老劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) be/take all ˈday, ˈmorning, etc. (to do sth)</td><td>（不要）花太长时间做某事</td><td>Don't take all day choosing a shirt; the shop closes at six.<br>别挑衬衫挑一整天，店里六点关门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>•not have all ˈday, etc. (informal)</td><td>（催促）没那么多时间；快点</td><td>Hurry up and decide — I haven't got all day to stand here.<br>快点定吧，我可没工夫在这儿干站着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all for sth/for doing sth</td><td>完全赞成；坚信应该做某事</td><td>I'm all for letting the kids walk to school by themselves.<br>我完全赞成让孩子们自己走路上学。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all ˈgo (BrE, informal)</td><td>忙个不停；十分活跃</td><td>It's been all go in the kitchen since the tour bus arrived.<br>旅游大巴一到，厨房里就忙得不可开交。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all ˈover sb (informal)</td><td>巴结某人；对某人大献殷勤</td><td>The salesman was all over us the moment we walked in.<br>我们一进门，销售员就围上来大献殷勤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all the ˈsame to sb (also be all ˈone to sb old-fashioned)</td><td>无所谓；对某人都一样</td><td>Tea or coffee, it's all the same to me this early.<br>这么早，茶还是咖啡对我都一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all ˈthat (AmE, informal)</td><td>了不起；很有魅力</td><td>He thinks he's all that just because he drives a new car.<br>就因为开了辆新车，他就觉得自己了不得。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈall</td><td>一共；总计</td><td>There were about forty people in all at the wedding lunch.<br>婚宴午餐一共来了大约四十人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's/they're ˌall ˈyours</td><td>（移交时说）全交给你了</td><td>Here are the keys and the paperwork — it's all yours now.<br>钥匙和文件都在这儿，现在全归你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Mr Brown, ˈshe said, taking him into the class-</td><td>她把他带进教室时说道（例句片段）</td><td>Mr Brown, she said, taking him into the classroom, they're all yours.<br>她把他领进教室说：布朗先生，这些孩子交给你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not all that ˈgood, ˈwell, etc.</td><td>不是特别好；没那么好</td><td>The soup smells great but it's not all that good, honestly.<br>汤闻着香，说实话味道并没多好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not as ˌbad(ly), ˌtall, etc. as all ˈthat</td><td>没有说的那么糟（或高等）</td><td>The exam wasn't as hard as all that; I finished with time to spare.<br>考试没传的那么难，我还提前做完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of ˌall the ˈcheek, ˈnerve, stupid things to ˈdo, etc.! (informal)</td><td>（表恼怒）竟做出这种事</td><td>Of all the stupid things to do, he posted the photo online!<br>真是蠢到家了，他居然把照片发到网上！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>all-clear</b></td><td>give sb/get the all-ˈclear</td><td>发出／收到警报解除的信号</td><td>The doctors gave her the all-clear after the second scan last week.<br>上周第二次检查后，医生说她没事了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>alley</b></td><td>a ˌblind ˈalley</td><td>死胡同；徒劳无功的路子</td><td>That line of research turned out to be a blind alley after two years.<br>两年下来，那条研究路线证明是条死胡同。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>allow</b></td><td>allow ˈme (spoken)</td><td>（礼貌地提出帮忙）我来吧</td><td>Allow me, that suitcase looks far too heavy for one person.<br>我来吧，那箱子一个人拎太沉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give/allow sb/sth free/full ˈrein</td><td>放手让…自由发挥</td><td>The editor gave the young writer free rein with the travel column.<br>编辑放手让这位年轻作者自由写旅行专栏。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>allowances</b></td><td>make alˈlowances for sb</td><td>体谅某人；考虑到某人的难处</td><td>You should make allowances for him; he's only been here a month.<br>你该体谅他，他才来了一个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>alone</b></td><td>go it aˈlone (informal)</td><td>单干；独立去做</td><td>After the partnership broke up, she decided to go it alone.<br>合伙散了以后，她决定自己单干。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave/let sb aˈlone •leave/let sb ˈbe</td><td>别打扰某人；别干预</td><td>Just leave him alone for an hour; he'll calm down on his own.<br>让他一个人待一小时，他自己会平静下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave/let sth aˈlone •leave/let sth ˈbe</td><td>别碰；别乱动</td><td>Leave that wound alone or it will never heal properly.<br>别老碰那个伤口，不然永远好不了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let aˈlone</td><td>更不用说；遑论</td><td>He can't boil an egg, let alone cook dinner for eight people.<br>他连鸡蛋都煮不好，更别提给八个人做饭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>along</b></td><td>along with sth</td><td>连同；除…之外还有</td><td>Send your passport along with two recent photos to this address.<br>请把护照连同两张近照寄到这个地址。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>always</b></td><td>as ˈalways</td><td>一如既往；像平常一样</td><td>As always, she arrived ten minutes early and made the coffee.<br>一如既往，她提早十分钟到，还煮好了咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>amends</b></td><td>make aˈmends (to sb) (for sth/for doing sth)</td><td>赔罪；补偿；将功补过</td><td>He cooked dinner to make amends for forgetting their anniversary.<br>他做了顿晚饭，弥补自己忘了纪念日的过失。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>american</b></td><td>as Aˌmerican as ˌapple ˈpie</td><td>地道美国式的</td><td>Pick-up trucks and county fairs are as American as apple pie.<br>皮卡车和乡村集市是地道的美国味儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>amiss</b></td><td>not come/go aˈmiss (BrE)</td><td>倒也不错；正合时宜；有用</td><td>A cup of hot tea wouldn't go amiss on a night like this.<br>这样的夜里来杯热茶倒是不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth aˈmiss (BrE)</td><td>（因误会）对…生气；见怪</td><td>Please don't take it amiss if I leave the party early tonight.<br>今晚我要是早走，请别见怪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>opp take sth in good ˈpart</td><td>不见怪地接受；一笑置之</td><td>He took the teasing about his haircut in good part.<br>大家拿他的发型开玩笑，他一笑置之。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>amok</b></td><td>run aˈmok</td><td>失去控制；发狂；肆虐</td><td>The puppy ran amok in the kitchen while we were out.<br>我们出门时，小狗在厨房里撒了欢儿地闹。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>amount</b></td><td>any aˈmount/number of sth</td><td>大量的；许多的</td><td>There are any number of reasons why the deal might fall through.<br>这笔生意谈不成的理由多得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no aˈmount of sth</td><td>再多…也没用</td><td>No amount of apologising will get your sister's bike back.<br>再怎么道歉也换不回你姐姐那辆自行车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>amused</b></td><td>keep sb aˈmused</td><td>让某人开心；给某人解闷</td><td>A box of crayons kept the kids amused for the whole train ride.<br>一盒蜡笔让孩子们在整趟火车上都玩得开心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>analysis</b></td><td>in the ˌlast/ˌfinal aˈnalysis</td><td>归根结底；总之</td><td>In the final analysis, it comes down to whether we trust him.<br>归根结底，问题在于我们信不信他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>anger</b></td><td>do sth more in ˈsorrow than in ˈanger</td><td>痛心多于气愤地做某事</td><td>She spoke to her son more in sorrow than in anger about the lies.<br>说起那些谎话，她对儿子是痛心多过生气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>answer</b></td><td>the ˌanswer to sb's ˈprayers</td><td>求之不得的人（或事物）</td><td>That second-hand washing machine was the answer to our prayers.<br>那台二手洗衣机简直是我们的救命稻草。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not take ˌno for an ˈanswer</td><td>非让人答应不可；不容拒绝</td><td>Come to dinner on Sunday — and I won't take no for an answer.<br>周日来吃饭，别想拒绝我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>answers</b></td><td>have/know all the ˈanswers</td><td>自以为无所不知；万事通</td><td>My nephew is sixteen and thinks he knows all the answers.<br>我侄子十六岁，觉得自己什么都懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ante</b></td><td>raise/up the ˈante</td><td>加大筹码；提高要价</td><td>The union raised the ante by threatening a strike before Christmas.<br>工会以圣诞前罢工相要挟，加大了筹码。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ants</b></td><td>have ˈants in your pants (informal)</td><td>坐立不安；焦躁不安</td><td>He's had ants in his pants all morning waiting for the results.<br>等成绩等得他一上午坐立不安。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>anything</b></td><td>anything ˈbut</td><td>绝对不；恰恰相反</td><td>The journey was anything but relaxing with three kids in the car.<br>车里坐着三个孩子，这趟旅程一点也不轻松。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>anything ˈgoes</td><td>怎么都行；没有任何规矩</td><td>At my aunt's house on New Year's Eve, anything goes.<br>除夕在我姑妈家，什么都随便。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>anything ˈlike</td><td>（用于否定或疑问）差不多；有点像</td><td>Is the sequel anything like as funny as the first film?<br>续集有第一部一半好笑吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) easy, clear, quick, etc. as ˈanything</td><td>极其容易（或清楚、迅速等）</td><td>Fixing that leak was as easy as anything once I found the valve.<br>找到阀门以后，修那个漏水口简单得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like ˈanything (BrE, informal)</td><td>非常；拼命地</td><td>It was raining like anything when we got off the bus.<br>我们下车时雨下得特别大。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not for ˈanything (informal)</td><td>决不；无论如何也不</td><td>I wouldn't move back to that town for anything.<br>打死我也不搬回那个镇子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>or ˈanything (spoken)</td><td>或类似的什么</td><td>If you need a lift or anything, just give me a ring.<br>要是需要搭车什么的，给我打个电话就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>apart</b></td><td>be ˈpoles/ˈworlds apart</td><td>天差地别；大相径庭</td><td>The two brothers are poles apart when it comes to money.<br>在花钱这件事上，兄弟俩天差地别。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come/fall apart at the ˈseams (informal)</td><td>土崩瓦解；开始崩溃</td><td>The band started coming apart at the seams during the second tour.<br>第二轮巡演途中，乐队开始分崩离析。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>After only six months, their marriage has come</td><td>才半年他们的婚姻就破裂了（例句片段）</td><td>After only six months, their marriage has come apart at the seams.<br>才过了六个月，他们的婚姻就散了架。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>apology</b></td><td>an aˈpology for sth</td><td>勉强凑合的替代品</td><td>They served us a sad apology for a breakfast at that hotel.<br>那家旅馆给我们端上的所谓早餐真够寒碜的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make no aˈpology/aˈpologies for sth</td><td>不为某事道歉；问心无愧</td><td>I make no apologies for asking hard questions at the meeting.<br>我在会上问了尖锐的问题，对此毫不抱歉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>appearances</b></td><td>keep up apˈpearances</td><td>装门面；维持体面</td><td>They kept up appearances long after the money had run out.<br>钱早就花光了，他们还硬撑着面子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the apple doesn't fall/never falls far from the ˈtree (saying, especially AmE)</td><td>有其父必有其子</td><td>She paints just like her mother; the apple never falls far from the tree.<br>她画画跟她妈一模一样，真是一脉相承。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌapple of sb's ˈeye</td><td>掌上明珠；心肝宝贝</td><td>His youngest granddaughter has always been the apple of his eye.<br>小孙女一直是他的掌上明珠。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a bad/rotten ˈapple</td><td>害群之马</td><td>One rotten apple in the team can ruin the mood for everyone.<br>队里一个害群之马能坏了所有人的心情。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>apple-pie</b></td><td>in apple-pie ˈorder</td><td>井井有条；整整齐齐</td><td>She left the workshop in apple-pie order before her holiday.<br>休假前她把工作间收拾得井井有条。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>apples</b></td><td>ˌapples and ˈoranges (AmE)</td><td>截然不同的事物；不可比</td><td>Comparing his novel to her poetry is apples and oranges.<br>拿他的小说比她的诗，根本不是一回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how do you like ˈthem apples? •how</td><td>（得意地）怎么样，服不服</td><td>I finished the whole race without walking — how do you like them apples?<br>全程跑下来没走一步，怎么样，服不服？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>about ˈthem apples? (AmE, informal, usually spoken)</td><td>（得意或挑衅）你觉得如何</td><td>We beat the champions on their own field — how about them apples?<br>我们在冠军队主场赢了他们，你说厉害不厉害？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>she's ˈapples (AustralE, New Zealand, informal)</td><td>没问题；一切都好</td><td>Fix the tyre and she's apples, mate, we'll be on the road again.<br>轮胎补好就没问题了，哥们儿，咱们又能上路了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>approach</b></td><td>a/the ˌsoftly-ˈsoftly approach</td><td>温和谨慎的做法</td><td>With teenagers, a softly-softly approach usually works better.<br>对青春期的孩子，温和一点的办法通常更管用。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>approval</b></td><td>on apˈproval</td><td>（商品）供试用的；可退还的</td><td>The bookshop sent me the atlas on approval for ten days.<br>书店把那本地图册寄给我试看十天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌseal of apˈproval</td><td>认可；批准；正式肯定</td><td>The plan finally got the council's seal of approval last Thursday.<br>这项计划上周四总算得到了议会的正式认可。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>apron</b></td><td>(tied to) your mother's, wife's, etc. ˈapron strings</td><td>受母亲（或妻子等）控制</td><td>At thirty he's still tied to his mother's apron strings.<br>三十岁了，他还事事听母亲的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>continue</b></td><td>continue to disagree about a decision, especial-</td><td>对已定之事作无谓争执</td><td>They continue to disagree about a decision that was made years ago.<br>他们对多年前的决定还在争个没完。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ark</b></td><td>be out of the ˈark •went out with the ˈark</td><td>（物品或习俗）极为老旧过时</td><td>That printer is out of the ark; it still uses floppy disks.<br>那台打印机老掉牙了，还在用软盘。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>arm</b></td><td>cost/pay an ˌarm and a ˈleg (informal)</td><td>花一大笔钱；价格昂贵</td><td>Getting the roof fixed cost us an arm and a leg last winter.<br>去年冬天修屋顶花了我们一大笔钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep sb at arm's ˈlength</td><td>与某人保持距离；不与之亲近</td><td>She keeps her colleagues at arm's length outside working hours.<br>下班后她跟同事保持距离。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put the ˈarm/ˈbite on sb (AmE, informal)</td><td>向某人讨要（尤指钱）</td><td>My cousin put the arm on me for gas money again yesterday.<br>我表弟昨天又找我要油钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>armchair</b></td><td>ˈa:rmtʃer; a:rmˈtʃer/</td><td>armchair 的读音标注</td><td>He sank into the old armchair and fell asleep before the news ended.<br>他陷进那把旧扶手椅，新闻没播完就睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a person who knows about a subject only from</td><td>纸上谈兵者；坐而论道的人</td><td>He's a person who knows about sailing only from books, an armchair sailor.<br>他只从书上懂航海，是个纸上谈兵的水手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>armed</b></td><td>armed to the ˈteeth (with sth) (informal)</td><td>全副武装；武装到牙齿</td><td>The hikers arrived armed to the teeth with maps, ropes and snacks.<br>徒步的人带着地图、绳子和零食，装备到了牙齿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>armour (BrE) (AmE armor) /ˈa:mə(r); AmE</td><td>armour 的拼写与读音标注</td><td>The museum displays a full suit of armour from the fifteenth century.<br>博物馆展出了一套十五世纪的全身盔甲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>arms</b></td><td>up in ˈarms (about/over sth) (informal)</td><td>强烈抗议；极力反对</td><td>Parents are up in arms about the plan to close the village school.<br>家长们对关闭村小学的计划强烈反对。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌbabe in ˈarms</td><td>襁褓中的婴儿；天真无助的人</td><td>In business he's still a babe in arms and trusts everyone.<br>在生意场上他还是个雏儿，谁都信。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>arrows</b></td><td>the ˌslings and ˈarrows (of sth)</td><td>（命运等的）打击与磨难</td><td>She has survived the slings and arrows of twenty years in politics.<br>她挺过了二十年政坛的种种打击。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>arse</b></td><td>My ˈarse! (BrE, ◆ slang)</td><td>胡说；我才不信</td><td>He was stuck in traffic? My arse! He just overslept again.<br>他堵车了？扯淡！他不过是又睡过头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>work your ˈarse off (BrE) (AmE work your ˈass off) (◆ slang)</td><td>拼命干活</td><td>I worked my arse off all summer to pay for that guitar.<br>整个夏天我拼命打工，就为买那把吉他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>arsed</b></td><td>can't be ˈarsed (to do sth) (BrE, ◆ slang)</td><td>懒得做某事</td><td>I can't be arsed to cook tonight; let's just order noodles.<br>今晚我懒得做饭，叫碗面吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>as</b></td><td>as aˈgainst sth</td><td>与…相比；与…相对照</td><td>We sold nine hundred units this month as against six hundred last year.<br>本月售出九百台，而去年同期是六百台。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌas and ˈwhen</td><td>在…的时候；一旦</td><td>I'll deal with those emails as and when I get a free hour.<br>等哪会儿有空我再处理那些邮件。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as for sb/sth</td><td>至于某人（某事）；关于</td><td>As for the leftovers, just put them in the fridge for tomorrow.<br>至于剩菜，放冰箱里明天吃吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈas from (also ˈas of especially AmE)</td><td>自…起</td><td>As from Monday, the office will open half an hour earlier.<br>从周一起，办公室提前半小时开门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as ˈif (spoken)</td><td>（表不信或否认）才怪；好像似的</td><td>Me, marry him? As if! We've argued every day this week.<br>我嫁他？才怪！这周我们天天吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as ˈif/as ˈthough</td><td>好像；仿佛</td><td>He talks about the war as though he had actually been there.<br>他谈起那场战争，好像自己真去过一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌas it ˈis</td><td>照现状看；实际上</td><td>I'd love another coffee, but as it is I'm already late.<br>我很想再来杯咖啡，可眼下我已经迟到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as to sth</td><td>至于某事；关于某事</td><td>As to the cost, we'll discuss that after you see the plans.<br>至于费用，等你看过图纸我们再谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as you ˈdo (BrE)</td><td>（调侃）人之常情嘛；就这样呗</td><td>So I bought a boat on holiday, as you do, and now regret it.<br>度假时我买了条船，人之常情嘛，现在后悔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ask</b></td><td>ˈask for trouble/it (informal)</td><td>自找麻烦；自讨苦吃</td><td>Riding without a helmet in this traffic is just asking for trouble.<br>这种车流里不戴头盔骑车纯属自找麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>don't ˈask (spoken, informal)</td><td>别问了；不问为好</td><td>How was the interview? Oh, don't ask, it was a disaster.<br>面试怎么样？唉，别问了，一塌糊涂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌdon't ask ˈme (spoken, informal)</td><td>别问我；我怎么知道</td><td>Don't ask me why he left early; he never explains anything.<br>别问我他为什么早走，他从来不解释。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I ˈask you! (spoken, informal)</td><td>（表震惊）真是的；你说气不气人</td><td>He charged forty pounds for a haircut. I ask you!<br>剪个头发收四十镑，你说这像话吗！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if you ask ˈme (spoken, informal)</td><td>依我看；我认为</td><td>If you ask me, that jacket is far too thin for winter.<br>依我看，那件夹克过冬太薄了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>asking</b></td><td>be sb's for the ˈasking</td><td>只要开口就能得到</td><td>The spare room is yours for the asking whenever you visit.<br>你来的时候想住客房，说一声就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>asleep</b></td><td>asleep at the ˈwheel (especially BrE) (AmE</td><td>玩忽职守；没留意潜在问题</td><td>The regulators were asleep at the wheel while the bank collapsed.<br>银行垮台时，监管机构完全在打瞌睡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>usually asleep at the ˈswitch) (informal)</td><td>玩忽职守；疏于警觉</td><td>Someone was asleep at the switch when these figures were checked.<br>核对这些数字时，有人明显在开小差。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ass</b></td><td>get your ˈass over/in ˈhere, etc. (◆ slang, especially AmE)</td><td>（粗俗）快滚过来；到这边来</td><td>Get your ass over here and help me move this couch!<br>快给我滚过来帮忙抬沙发！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>astray</b></td><td>go aˈstray</td><td>丢失；误入歧途</td><td>Two of the parcels went astray somewhere between Leeds and here.<br>有两个包裹在利兹到这儿的路上弄丢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lead sb aˈstray</td><td>把某人引入歧途；带坏某人</td><td>His mother blamed the older boys for leading him astray.<br>他母亲怪那些大孩子把他带坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>atmosphere</b></td><td>you could ˌcut the atmosphere with a ˈknife (informal)</td><td>气氛紧张；剑拔弩张</td><td>At the family dinner you could cut the atmosphere with a knife.<br>那顿家宴上，气氛压抑得让人喘不过气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>attendance</b></td><td>be in atˈtendance (formal)</td><td>出席；到场</td><td>Two doctors were in attendance throughout the long ceremony.<br>整场冗长的典礼上都有两名医生在场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take atˈtendance (AmE)</td><td>点名；查考勤</td><td>The teacher takes attendance every morning before the first lesson.<br>老师每天早上第一节课前点名。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>attention</b></td><td>get/have sb's unˌdivided atˈtention</td><td>得到某人的全神贯注</td><td>Put your phone down — I want your undivided attention for five minutes.<br>把手机放下，我要你专心听我说五分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>authority</b></td><td>have sth on good auˈthority</td><td>有可靠根据；消息来源可靠</td><td>I have it on good authority that the shop is closing in June.<br>我有可靠消息，这家店六月要关门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>automatic</b></td><td>be on ˌautomatic ˈpilot</td><td>不假思索地做；机械地做</td><td>I was so tired I drove home on automatic pilot.<br>我累得糊里糊涂，一路机械地开回了家。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>avail</b></td><td>of little/no aˈvail (formal)</td><td>没有多大用处；无济于事</td><td>His long letters of complaint were of no avail whatsoever.<br>他那些长篇投诉信一点用都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to little/no aˈvail (formal)</td><td>徒劳无功；没有成效</td><td>We searched the whole beach for her ring, to no avail.<br>我们把整片海滩找遍了，还是没找到她的戒指。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>avoid</b></td><td>avoid sb/sth like the ˈplague (informal)</td><td>极力躲避；避之唯恐不及</td><td>Since the argument he's been avoiding me like the plague.<br>自从吵过之后，他躲我躲得像躲瘟疫。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>awe</b></td><td>be/stand in ˈawe of sb/sth</td><td>敬畏；对…肃然起敬</td><td>As a student I stood in awe of that quiet old professor.<br>当学生时，我对那位安静的老教授敬畏有加。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>awkward</b></td><td>the ˈawkward age</td><td>尴尬年龄（青春期初）</td><td>He's at the awkward age when nothing his parents say is right.<br>他正处在那个别扭的年纪，爸妈说什么都不对。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>axe</b></td><td>have an ˈaxe to grind</td><td>别有用心；另有企图</td><td>She has no axe to grind; she just wants the road repaired.<br>她没什么私心，只是想把路修好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>babe</b></td><td>a ˌbabe in ˈarms (old-fashioned)</td><td>襁褓中的婴儿；不谙世事的人</td><td>When it comes to contracts, he's still a babe in arms.<br>一说到合同，他还完全是个新手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌbabe in the ˈwoods (AmE)</td><td>毫无经验的人；易受骗的人</td><td>On his first day trading he was a babe in the woods.<br>他做交易的头一天完全是只小白兔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the Woods in which two children are left alone</td><td>《林中孩子》故事：两孩子被弃林中</td><td>The old ballad tells of two children left alone in the woods to die.<br>那首老歌谣讲两个孩子被丢在林中等死。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>baby</b></td><td>boom), especially after the Second World War</td><td>（尤指二战后）生育高峰期出生的人</td><td>My parents were born in the boom, especially after the Second World War.<br>我父母就出生在二战后的生育高峰。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be sb's ˈbaby (informal)</td><td>是某人的心血；归某人负责</td><td>The community garden is entirely her baby, from plan to planting.<br>这个社区花园从设计到种植全是她的心血。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw the ˌbaby out with the ˈbathwater</td><td>把精华与糟粕一起丢掉</td><td>Scrapping the whole system throws the baby out with the bathwater.<br>把整套系统废掉，等于连好东西一块儿扔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the back ˈburner</td><td>暂缓处理；搁置一边</td><td>We've put the kitchen renovation on the back burner until spring.<br>厨房翻新的事我们先搁到春天再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(in) back of sth (AmE, informal)</td><td>在…后面；在…背后</td><td>The kids' bikes are in back of the garage, behind the old fridge.<br>孩子们的自行车在车库后面，旧冰箱那边。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌback of beˈyond (informal)</td><td>偏远之地；穷乡僻壤</td><td>Her cottage is out in the back of beyond, an hour from the nearest shop.<br>她的小屋在鸟不拉屎的地方，离最近的商店一小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌback to ˈback</td><td>背靠背；接连地</td><td>We watched two films back to back and forgot to have dinner.<br>我们连着看了两部电影，忘了吃晚饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/put sb's ˈback up</td><td>惹恼某人；使某人生气</td><td>His know-it-all tone really put my back up at the meeting.<br>他那副什么都懂的口气在会上真把我惹毛了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get off sb's ˈback •get sb off your ˈback</td><td>不再纠缠某人；摆脱某人的烦扰</td><td>Just finish the report and your boss will get off your back.<br>把报告写完，你老板就不烦你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>never/not look ˈback (informal)</td><td>从此一帆风顺；蒸蒸日上</td><td>She opened the bakery in 2019 and has never looked back since.<br>她二〇一九年开了那家面包房，此后一路顺风。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put your ˈback into sth</td><td>全力以赴做某事；卖力干</td><td>If we all put our backs into it, we'll finish the fence today.<br>大家一起使把劲，今天就能把栅栏弄好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn your ˈback on sb/sth</td><td>不理睬；拒绝帮助；弃之不顾</td><td>He turned his back on his old friends the moment he got rich.<br>一发财，他就把老朋友都甩在了脑后。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>backhanded</b></td><td>a ˌbackhanded ˈcompliment (AmE also a ˌleft-handed ˈcompliment)</td><td>假恭维；表面赞扬实则讥讽</td><td>Saying I look rested for my age was a backhanded compliment.<br>说我这个年纪气色不错，这夸奖听着真别扭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>back-room</b></td><td>the ˈback-room boys (BrE)</td><td>幕后工作的科研人员；幕后英雄</td><td>The back-room boys spent two years perfecting that tiny battery.<br>幕后那帮技术员花了两年才把这块小电池做好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>back-seat</b></td><td>a ˌback-seat ˈdriver (disapproving)</td><td>指手画脚的人；爱管闲事者</td><td>My uncle is a terrible back-seat driver on every family trip.<br>每次全家出游，我叔叔都在后座上指挥个不停。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>backwards</b></td><td>bend/lean over ˈbackwards to do sth</td><td>竭力做某事；不遗余力</td><td>The staff bent over backwards to find us a room that night.<br>那天晚上工作人员想尽办法给我们找了间房。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>backyard</b></td><td>in your (own) backˈyard</td><td>在自家后院；在身边不远处</td><td>Nobody wants a waste plant in their own backyard.<br>谁都不想垃圾处理厂建在自家门口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bad</b></td><td>for the nouns or verbs in the idioms, for have got it ˈbad (informal, humorous)</td><td>深陷情网；着迷得不行</td><td>He's texting her at three in the morning — he's got it bad.<br>凌晨三点还给她发消息，他这是陷得不轻。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not (so/too) ˈbad (spoken)</td><td>还不错；还行</td><td>The soup's not bad at all, considering I used leftovers.<br>用剩菜煮的汤，味道居然还不赖。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˌbad with the ˈgood</td><td>好坏都要接受</td><td>Farming means taking the bad with the good, drought years included.<br>务农就得好坏都受着，包括旱年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(it's) too ˈbad (spoken)</td><td>太遗憾了；真可惜</td><td>Too bad you missed the concert; the band played for three hours.<br>你没赶上演唱会真可惜，乐队演了三个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>badly</b></td><td>be badly ˈoff</td><td>贫穷；境况不佳</td><td>They were badly off for years before he found steady work.<br>他找到稳定工作前，他们家穷了好几年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be badly ˈoff for sth (BrE)</td><td>缺少某物；某物不够用</td><td>We're badly off for chairs, so bring one if you can.<br>我们这儿椅子不够，你能带一把最好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bag</b></td><td>(not) your ˈbag (informal)</td><td>（不）是某人的兴趣或长项</td><td>Loud clubs really aren't my bag; I'd rather sit and talk.<br>吵闹的夜店真不是我的菜，我宁愿坐着聊天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌbag and ˈbaggage</td><td>连同全部家当</td><td>They threw him out, bag and baggage, on a Sunday morning.<br>周日早上，他们把他连人带行李都轰了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈbag lady (informal)</td><td>拎着家当流浪的女人</td><td>A bag lady sleeps in the church doorway most winter nights.<br>冬天的夜里，常有个流浪女睡在教堂门口。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌbag of ˈbones (informal)</td><td>骨瘦如柴的人（或动物）</td><td>The stray dog was a bag of bones when we first took him in.<br>我们刚收养这只流浪狗时，它瘦得皮包骨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈbag (informal)</td><td>十拿九稳；已稳操胜券</td><td>With two goals in ten minutes, the match was in the bag.<br>十分钟进两球，这场比赛稳了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let the ˌcat out of the ˈbag</td><td>泄露秘密；说漏嘴</td><td>Don't let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party.<br>惊喜派对的事你可别说漏嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>way out of a paper ˈbag</td><td>（否定用法）极其无能；一无是处</td><td>He couldn't fight his way out of a paper bag, let alone win.<br>他连纸袋都撕不开，还想赢？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bags</b></td><td>ˈbags (I)... (BrE) (AmE ˈdibs on...) (informal)</td><td>（多为儿语）我要；这归我</td><td>Bags I the window seat on the way back!<br>回程靠窗的座位归我！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>baker</b></td><td>a ˌbaker's ˈdozen (old-fashioned)</td><td>十三个</td><td>She came home with a baker's dozen of eggs from the market.<br>她从集市带回来十三个鸡蛋。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>balance</b></td><td>(be/hang) in the ˈbalance</td><td>悬而未决；尚未确定</td><td>His place on the team hung in the balance until the final trial.<br>直到最后一次选拔，他能否入队都还悬着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(catch/throw sb) off ˈbalance</td><td>使失去平衡；使措手不及</td><td>Her blunt question caught the minister completely off balance.<br>她那个直白的问题让部长完全乱了阵脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈbalance</td><td>权衡之后；总的看来</td><td>On balance, I think moving to a smaller town was the right call.<br>权衡下来，我觉得搬到小城是对的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>balancing</b></td><td>a ˈbalancing/juggling act</td><td>两头兼顾；搞平衡</td><td>Running a shop and studying at night is quite a juggling act.<br>一边开店一边上夜校，真是两头兼顾不容易。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bald</b></td><td>(as) bald as a ˈcoot</td><td>头顶全秃</td><td>By forty my uncle was as bald as a coot and quite proud of it.<br>我叔叔四十岁就全秃了，还挺得意。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ball</b></td><td>the whole ball of ˈwax (AmE, informal)</td><td>全部；一切</td><td>The rent, the bills, the repairs — she pays for the whole ball of wax.<br>房租、账单、维修，全都是她掏钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ballistic</b></td><td>go balˈlistic (informal)</td><td>勃然大怒；暴跳如雷</td><td>Dad went ballistic when he saw the scratch on the car door.<br>爸爸看到车门上的划痕，气得暴跳如雷。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>balloon</b></td><td>when the balˈloon goes up (informal)</td><td>麻烦（或大事）临头时</td><td>Keep your phone on; when the balloon goes up we'll need everyone.<br>手机开着，一出事我们就得召集所有人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ballpark</b></td><td>a ˈballpark figure</td><td>大概的数字；估算值</td><td>Just give me a ballpark figure for the repairs before I decide.<br>你先给个修理费的大概数，我再决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in the same/right ˈballpark (especially AmE)</td><td>大致相当；数字差不多</td><td>Their quote and ours are in the same ballpark, so either works.<br>他们的报价和我们的差不多，选哪个都行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>balls</b></td><td>break your ˈballs (AmE, ◆ slang)</td><td>拼命干；累死累活</td><td>I broke my balls on that job and still got no bonus.<br>那活儿我拼了老命，奖金还是没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bananas</b></td><td>go baˈnanas (slang)</td><td>发疯；大发脾气；乐疯了</td><td>The crowd went bananas when the winning goal went in.<br>制胜球一进，全场都疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bandwagon</b></td><td>climb/jump on the ˈbandwagon (informal, disapproving)</td><td>随大流；赶时髦</td><td>Every café jumped on the bandwagon and started selling bubble tea.<br>每家咖啡馆都跟风卖起了奶茶。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bane</b></td><td>the bane of sb's ˈlife/eˈxistence</td><td>让人不得安宁的祸根；灾星</td><td>That noisy scooter outside is the bane of my existence.<br>外面那辆吵人的摩托简直是我的克星。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bang</b></td><td>ˌbang for your ˈbuck (AmE, slang)</td><td>钱花得值；性价比高</td><td>This little car gives you more bang for your buck than the newer models.<br>这辆小车比新款更划算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bang goes sth (informal)</td><td>（某事）泡汤了；没指望了</td><td>It's pouring again — bang goes our afternoon at the beach.<br>又下大雨了，我们下午去海边的计划泡汤了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bang/spot ˈon (informal)</td><td>完全准确；分毫不差</td><td>Your guess about the price was bang on, to the penny.<br>你猜的价格分毫不差。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bang to ˈrights (BrE) (AmE dead to ˈrights)</td><td>当场抓获；人赃俱获</td><td>The security camera got him bang to rights with the stolen watch.<br>监控把他偷表的过程拍了个正着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈbang (informal)</td><td>爆裂；砰的一声炸开</td><td>The balloon went bang and the baby burst into tears.<br>气球砰的一声炸了，宝宝哇地哭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go (off) with a ˈbang (informal)</td><td>（活动等）非常成功；圆满热闹</td><td>The school concert went off with a bang this year.<br>今年的学校音乐会办得非常成功。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bang/beat the ˈdrum (for sb/sth)</td><td>为…大力宣传；摇旗呐喊</td><td>She's been banging the drum for local farmers for a decade.<br>十年来她一直为本地农民奔走呼吁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bank</b></td><td>not ˌbreak the ˈbank (informal)</td><td>花不了多少钱；负担得起</td><td>A weekend in the countryside won't break the bank.<br>在乡下待个周末花不了几个钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>baptism</b></td><td>a ˌbaptism of ˈfire</td><td>严峻的初次考验；火的洗礼</td><td>Teaching thirty teenagers alone was a real baptism of fire.<br>独自面对三十个青少年，真是一场严酷的初考验。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bar</b></td><td>bar ˈnone</td><td>毫无例外；首屈一指</td><td>She is the best cook in this family, bar none.<br>她是我们家最会做饭的，没有之一。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all over, bar the ˈshouting</td><td>大局已定；胜负已分</td><td>With a four-goal lead it's all over bar the shouting.<br>领先四球，胜负已经没有悬念了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have a ˈbar of sth (AustralE, New Zealand)</td><td>不愿沾边；坚决不接受</td><td>He wouldn't have a bar of their plan to sell the farm.<br>他们要卖农场，他一点也不肯掺和。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bare</b></td><td>the bare ˈbones (of sth)</td><td>梗概；基本要点</td><td>He gave me the bare bones of the story on the phone last night.<br>昨晚他在电话里把事情的大概跟我说了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bare your ˈsoul</td><td>倾诉衷肠；吐露心事</td><td>After two glasses of wine he bared his soul to a total stranger.<br>两杯酒下肚，他对一个陌生人吐尽了心事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bare your ˈteeth</td><td>龇牙（示威）；露出凶相</td><td>The dog bared its teeth as soon as we got near the gate.<br>我们一走近大门，那狗就龇起了牙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with your bare ˈhands</td><td>赤手空拳；徒手</td><td>He built that stone wall with his bare hands over one summer.<br>那道石墙是他一个夏天徒手垒起来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bargain</b></td><td>into the ˈbargain (AmE in the ˈbargain)</td><td>而且；此外还</td><td>The flat is cheap and has a balcony into the bargain.<br>这套房便宜，而且还带阳台。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bargaining</b></td><td>ˈbargaining chip (AmE, BrE)</td><td>谈判筹码</td><td>The unused land became their main bargaining chip in the talks.<br>那块闲置土地成了他们谈判的主要筹码。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bargepole</b></td><td>not touch sb/sth with a ˈbargepole</td><td>唯恐避之不及；碰都不愿碰</td><td>That car's been in two crashes; I wouldn't touch it with a bargepole.<br>那车撞过两次，白送我都不要。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>barking</b></td><td>be barking ˈmad •be ˈbarking (BrE, informal)</td><td>完全疯了；疯疯癫癫</td><td>Swimming in the river in February? You're barking mad.<br>二月份去河里游泳？你真是疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be barking up the wrong ˈtree</td><td>找错了对象；完全搞错</td><td>If you think I took your charger, you're barking up the wrong tree.<br>你要是以为充电器是我拿的，那可找错人了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>barrel</b></td><td>(get/have sb) over a ˈbarrel (informal)</td><td>使处于被动；任人摆布</td><td>With no other supplier left, they've got us over a barrel.<br>没有别的供货商了，我们只能任他们摆布。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bars</b></td><td>behind ˈbars (informal)</td><td>坐牢；被监禁</td><td>He spent nine years behind bars for a crime he didn't commit.<br>他为一桩没犯过的罪蹲了九年牢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>base</b></td><td>off ˈbase (AmE, informal)</td><td>大错特错；完全不对</td><td>Your estimate of the crowd size was way off base.<br>你对人数的估计错得离谱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get to ˌfirst ˈbase (with sb/sth)</td><td>迈出第一步；取得初步进展</td><td>We never even got to first base with the planning committee.<br>我们在规划委员会那儿连第一步都没迈出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bash</b></td><td>have a ˈbash at (doing) sth (BrE, spoken)</td><td>试着做某事</td><td>I've never baked bread, but I'll have a bash at it tonight.<br>我从没烤过面包，今晚试试看。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>basics</b></td><td>get/go back to ˈbasics</td><td>回归基本；从头抓起</td><td>The coach took us back to basics after three straight defeats.<br>三连败之后，教练带我们从基本功练起。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>basket</b></td><td>a ˈbasket case (informal)</td><td>濒临崩溃的国家（或组织）</td><td>Ten years ago the airline was a complete basket case.<br>十年前这家航空公司简直是烂摊子一个。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bat</b></td><td>ˌbat your ˈeyelashes/ˈeyes</td><td>眨眼放电；眉目传情</td><td>She batted her eyelashes and he agreed to pay for lunch.<br>她眨了眨眼，他就答应请午饭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bat a ˈthousand (AmE, informal)</td><td>大获成功；百发百中</td><td>Three job offers in one week — you're batting a thousand.<br>一周三个录用通知，你可真是无往不利。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to ˈbat for sb (AmE, informal)</td><td>为某人出头；支持某人</td><td>My old boss went to bat for me when the funding was cut.<br>经费被砍时，我以前的老板站出来替我说话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like a ˌbat out of ˈhell (informal)</td><td>飞快地；风驰电掣</td><td>He came out of the driveway like a bat out of hell.<br>他把车从车道上开出来，快得像飞一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not bat an ˈeyelid (BrE) (AmE not bat an ˈeye)</td><td>面不改色；毫不动容</td><td>She didn't bat an eyelid when the bill came to two hundred pounds.<br>账单两百镑，她眼皮都没眨一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(right) off the ˈbat (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>立即；马上</td><td>Right off the bat he told us the roof would need replacing.<br>他一上来就告诉我们屋顶得换。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>off your own ˈbat (BrE, informal)</td><td>自作主张；靠自己</td><td>She organised the whole fundraiser off her own bat.<br>这场募捐活动全是她自己张罗起来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bated</b></td><td>with ˌbated ˈbreath</td><td>屏息以待；急切期盼</td><td>We waited with bated breath for the exam results to appear.<br>我们屏住呼吸等着成绩公布。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bath</b></td><td>take a ˈbath (AmE, informal, business)</td><td>（生意上）亏大钱</td><td>Investors took a bath when the property market collapsed.<br>楼市崩盘时投资者亏得很惨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bathroom</b></td><td>go to the ˈbathroom (AmE)</td><td>上厕所；大小便</td><td>Ask the driver to stop; the little one needs to go to the bathroom.<br>让司机停一下，小家伙要上厕所。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bats</b></td><td>have ˌbats in the ˈbelfry (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>疯疯癫癫；古里古怪</td><td>The neighbours say the old man has bats in the belfry.<br>邻居们说那老头有点神神叨叨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>batten</b></td><td>ˌbatten down the ˈhatches</td><td>做好准备迎接困难</td><td>With the audit coming, it's time to batten down the hatches.<br>审计要来了，该做好应对准备了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>battle</b></td><td>the ˌbattle lines are ˈdrawn</td><td>战线已划定；阵营已分明</td><td>The battle lines are drawn between the residents and the developer.<br>居民和开发商之间已经摆开了阵势。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌbattle of ˈwills</td><td>意志的较量</td><td>Bedtime with a toddler is a nightly battle of wills.<br>哄幼儿睡觉每晚都是一场意志的较量。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌbattle of ˈwits</td><td>斗智；智力的较量</td><td>The trial turned into a long battle of wits between the two lawyers.<br>庭审变成了两位律师之间漫长的斗智。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do/join ˈbattle (with sb)</td><td>与某人激烈交锋（或争论）</td><td>She joined battle with the council over the parking charges.<br>她为停车费的事和市政会杠上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bay</b></td><td>at ˈbay</td><td>陷入绝境；作困兽之斗</td><td>The fox stood at bay against the wall, surrounded by dogs.<br>狐狸被狗围住，靠着墙做困兽之斗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold/keep sb/sth at ˈbay</td><td>不让…逼近；抵挡住</td><td>Hot soup and thick socks kept the cold at bay all evening.<br>热汤加厚袜子，整晚都挡住了寒气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be</b></td><td>be ˈat it (informal)</td><td>在忙着做；争论（或做得）没完</td><td>The neighbours were at it again, shouting until well past midnight.<br>邻居又吵上了，一直闹到后半夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be yourˈself</td><td>举止自然；表现本色</td><td>Just be yourself at the interview and they'll like you.<br>面试时自然点就行，他们会喜欢你的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so ˈbe it (formal)</td><td>就这样吧；只好如此</td><td>If he'd rather walk home in the rain, then so be it.<br>他宁愿冒雨走回家，那就随他吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beady</b></td><td>keep a beady ˈeye on sb/sth •have your beady ˈeye on sb/sth</td><td>盯住不放；密切留意</td><td>She had her beady eye on the boys near the sweet counter.<br>她一直盯着糖果柜台旁边那几个男孩。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be-all</b></td><td>the ˌbe-all and ˈend-all (of sth) (informal)</td><td>最要紧的事；唯一目的</td><td>Winning isn't the be-all and end-all of playing football.<br>踢球并不是只有赢球才重要。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beam</b></td><td>off ˈbeam (informal)</td><td>偏离正确；大错特错</td><td>His guess about the cause of the fault was completely off beam.<br>他对故障原因的猜测完全跑偏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bean</b></td><td>not (have) a ˈbean (BrE, informal)</td><td>身无分文</td><td>How much have you saved? Not a bean, I'm afraid.<br>你攒了多少钱？一分也没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bear</b></td><td>bear the ˈbrunt of sth</td><td>首当其冲；承受主要压力</td><td>Coastal villages bore the brunt of the storm on Tuesday night.<br>周二夜里的风暴中，沿海村庄首当其冲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bear ˈfruit</td><td>取得成果；奏效</td><td>After three years the language classes finally began to bear fruit.<br>三年之后，语言课终于见到了成效。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bearings</b></td><td>find/get your ˈbearings</td><td>辨明方向；熟悉环境</td><td>Give me a minute to get my bearings in this huge station.<br>这站太大了，让我先弄清方向。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose your ˈbearings</td><td>迷失方向；不知所措</td><td>We lost our bearings in the fog and ended up by the river.<br>我们在雾里迷了路，最后走到了河边。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beat</b></td><td>beat about the ˈbush (BrE) (AmE ˌbeat around the ˈbush)</td><td>拐弯抹角；绕圈子</td><td>Stop beating about the bush and tell me how much it cost.<br>别绕弯子了，直说多少钱吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat sb at their own ˈgame</td><td>以其人之道还治其人之身</td><td>The small shop beat the chain at its own game with cheaper prices.<br>小店以更低的价格在对手的强项上赢了连锁店。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat your ˈbrains out (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>绞尽脑汁；冥思苦想</td><td>I beat my brains out for hours over that last puzzle.<br>最后那道谜题我想了好几个钟头，脑袋都想破了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat the ˈbushes (especially AmE)</td><td>到处搜寻；四处寻觅</td><td>The team beat the bushes for a goalkeeper before the season started.<br>赛季开始前，球队到处找门将。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat the ˈclock</td><td>提前完成；抢在时限之前</td><td>We beat the clock and posted the forms ten minutes before closing.<br>我们赶在关门前十分钟把表格寄了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat sb/sth ˈhollow</td><td>彻底击败；远远胜过</td><td>Her homemade bread beats the supermarket stuff hollow.<br>她自己烤的面包比超市的强太多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈbeat it (informal)</td><td>（多用于命令）走开；滚</td><td>The shopkeeper told the kids to beat it before he called the police.<br>店主叫那几个孩子快走，不然就报警。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat a path to sb's ˈdoor</td><td>纷纷登门；争相前往</td><td>Once word got out, buyers beat a path to her door.<br>消息一传开，买家纷纷找上门来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat the ˈrap (AmE, slang)</td><td>逃脱惩罚；免于定罪</td><td>He beat the rap because the main witness never showed up.<br>主要证人没出庭，他就这么逃过了处罚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat a (hasty) reˈtreat</td><td>仓皇撤退；匆匆离开</td><td>When her father appeared, the boys beat a hasty retreat.<br>她父亲一出现，那几个男孩撒腿就跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat ˈtime</td><td>（随音乐）打拍子</td><td>Grandma beat time on the arm of her chair throughout the song.<br>整首歌里，奶奶都在椅子扶手上打拍子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>can you ˈbeat it/ˈthat? (spoken)</td><td>（表惊讶或恼怒）竟有这等事</td><td>He forgot his own birthday party — can you beat that?<br>他连自己的生日会都忘了，你说奇不奇？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if you can't ˈbeat them, ˈjoin them (saying)</td><td>打不赢就加入；不如随大流</td><td>Everyone's cycling to work now, so if you can't beat them, join them.<br>现在人人骑车上班，打不过就加入吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a rod/stick to ˈbeat sb with</td><td>用来指责（或惩罚）某人的把柄</td><td>One late report became a stick to beat him with for years.<br>一份报告交晚了，成了多年攻击他的把柄。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beaten</b></td><td>off the ˌbeaten ˈtrack</td><td>偏僻；人迹罕至</td><td>We found a quiet guesthouse well off the beaten track.<br>我们找到一家偏僻幽静的小客栈。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beating</b></td><td>take a ˈbeating (AmE also take a ˈlicking)</td><td>遭受重创；被打得很惨</td><td>Our reputation took a beating after the story hit the papers.<br>报纸一登，我们的名声大受打击。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take some ˈbeating (BrE)</td><td>难以超越；很难比得上</td><td>Her lemon cake takes some beating, and I have tried plenty.<br>她做的柠檬蛋糕真难有人比得上，我可吃过不少。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beats</b></td><td>it ˌbeats ˈme (why, how, etc.) (informal)</td><td>我真不明白；这可难倒我了</td><td>It beats me how he passed that exam without opening a book.<br>他连书都没翻就过了考试，我真想不通。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beauty</b></td><td>ˌbeauty is in the ˌeye of the beˈholder (saying)</td><td>情人眼里出西施；美丑因人而异</td><td>You hate that green sofa, but beauty is in the eye of the beholder.<br>你讨厌那张绿沙发，可各人审美不同嘛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beauty is only skin-ˈdeep (saying)</td><td>美貌只是表象；不可以貌取人</td><td>He's handsome but unkind — beauty is only skin-deep.<br>他长得帅却不厚道，美貌不过一层皮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the beauty of sth/of doing sth</td><td>（做）某事的妙处</td><td>The beauty of working from home is that I skip the commute.<br>在家办公的妙处就是不用挤通勤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈbeauty sleep (humorous)</td><td>睡美容觉</td><td>I'm off to bed early; I need my beauty sleep before the wedding.<br>我早点睡了，婚礼前得睡个美容觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beck</b></td><td>at sb's ˌbeck and ˈcall</td><td>随叫随到；唯命是从</td><td>She's tired of being at her brother's beck and call every weekend.<br>每个周末都得随叫随到伺候哥哥，她烦透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>become</b></td><td>what will become/has become/became of</td><td>（某人或某物）后来怎么样了</td><td>I often wonder what became of the boy who sat next to me.<br>我常想，当年坐我旁边那男孩后来怎么样了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bed</b></td><td>be in bed with sb/sth •get into bed with</td><td>（人或组织）与…关系过密</td><td>Critics say the regulator is in bed with the big banks.<br>批评者说监管方与大银行走得太近。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>> Investors are wary of getting into bed with an get out of bed on the wrong ˈside (BrE) (AmE</td><td>一起床就心情不好</td><td>Don't mind him; he got out of bed on the wrong side today.<br>别理他，他今天起床气重。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to ˈbed with sb (informal)</td><td>与某人上床</td><td>She told him she wasn't going to bed with anyone on a first date.<br>她跟他说，第一次约会她不会跟谁上床。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have ˌmade your bed and have to ˈlie on it</td><td>自作自受；自食其果</td><td>He quit without a plan, so he's made his bed and has to lie on it.<br>他没打算就辞了职，只能自食其果。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈbed</td><td>在床上（指性行为）</td><td>They rarely argue, but they don't talk much in bed either.<br>他们很少吵架，但床上也没什么话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take to your ˈbed</td><td>卧病在床</td><td>Granny took to her bed for a week with a bad chest.<br>奶奶胸闷得厉害，卧床躺了一星期。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bedfellows</b></td><td>be/make ˌstrange ˈbedfellows</td><td>凑到一起的奇怪搭档</td><td>A rock band and a church choir make strange bedfellows indeed.<br>摇滚乐队和教堂唱诗班凑一块儿真是奇怪的组合。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bee</b></td><td>the ˌbee's ˈknees (informal)</td><td>出类拔萃的人（或事物）</td><td>He thinks his new phone is the bee's knees.<br>他觉得自己的新手机简直棒极了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈbee in your bonnet (informal)</td><td>念念不忘；痴迷于某事</td><td>Dad has a bee in his bonnet about turning off every light.<br>爸爸对随手关灯这事儿念叨个没完。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beeline</b></td><td>make a ˈbeeline for sb/sth (informal)</td><td>直奔；径直冲向</td><td>The kids made a beeline for the cake as soon as they arrived.<br>孩子们一到就直奔蛋糕去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>been</b></td><td>ˌbeen ˈthere, ˌdone ˈthat (informal)</td><td>早经历过了；没什么新鲜</td><td>Backpacking across Europe with a tent? Been there, done that, twice.<br>背着帐篷穿越欧洲？我早玩过了，还两回呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have been aˈround (informal)</td><td>见多识广；阅历丰富</td><td>Ask Mei about landlords; she's been around and knows the tricks.<br>房东的事问阿梅，她见得多，门道清楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have been there beˈfore (informal)</td><td>以前也经历过</td><td>I know how you feel about failing; I've been there before.<br>失败的滋味我懂，我也经历过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bees</b></td><td>the ˌbirds and the ˈbees</td><td>性知识（婉辞）</td><td>Dad finally explained the birds and the bees to my little brother.<br>爸爸终于给我弟弟讲了讲男女之事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beg</b></td><td>ˌbeg, ˌborrow or ˈsteal (also ˌbeg, ˌsteal or ˈborrow)</td><td>千方百计弄到手</td><td>We'll beg, borrow or steal a van to move the piano tomorrow.<br>明天搬钢琴，我们想尽办法也得弄辆货车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beg the ˈquestion</td><td>引出尚未触及的问题；回避实质</td><td>That answer begs the question of who is paying for all this.<br>这个回答让人不禁要问，这一切谁来买单。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I beg to ˈdiffer</td><td>恕我不能苟同</td><td>You say the film was boring; I beg to differ.<br>你说这电影无聊，恕我不能苟同。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I beg your ˈpardon (formal)</td><td>（礼貌地道歉）对不起；请原谅</td><td>I beg your pardon, I didn't mean to step on your foot.<br>对不起，我不是故意踩到你的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>begging</b></td><td>go ˈbegging (BrE, spoken)</td><td>（东西）没人要；闲置着</td><td>There's a slice of pizza going begging if anyone wants it.<br>还剩一块披萨没人要，谁想吃？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beyond beˈlief</td><td>难以置信；令人无法相信</td><td>The queue at the passport office was long beyond belief.<br>护照办事处的队伍长得难以置信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to beˈgin with</td><td>起初；首先</td><td>To begin with, we only had two customers a day.<br>起初我们一天只有两个客人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beginner</b></td><td>ˌbeginner's ˈluck</td><td>新手的好运气</td><td>She won her first game of chess, but that was beginner's luck.<br>她第一盘棋就赢了，不过是新手的运气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beˌlieve (you) ˈme (spoken)</td><td>（强调）相信我；我向你保证</td><td>Believe you me, that road is far worse in the rain.<br>相信我，那条路一下雨更难走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>don't you beˈlieve it! (spoken)</td><td>千万别信；根本不是那么回事</td><td>He says the exam is easy? Don't you believe it!<br>他说考试简单？你可千万别信！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb to beˈlieve/underˈstand (that)...</td><td>（常用被动）使某人相信（或明白）</td><td>I was given to believe that the rent included the water bill.<br>我一直以为房租里包含水费。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I don't beˈlieve it! (spoken)</td><td>（表惊讶或恼怒）我简直不敢相信</td><td>I don't believe it — they've cancelled the train again!<br>真是的，火车又取消了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>they'll, etc. believe ˈanything (informal)</td><td>（这种人）什么都肯信</td><td>He thinks the moon landing was faked; they'll believe anything.<br>他觉得登月是假的，这种人什么都信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'll believe it/that when I ˈsee it (informal)</td><td>我要亲眼见了才信</td><td>He's giving up sweets? I'll believe that when I see it.<br>他要戒甜食？我要亲眼看到才信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>says he's going to give up smoking. ˈYl believe</td><td>他说要戒烟，我才不信（例句片段）</td><td>He says he's going to give up smoking. I'll believe it when I see it.<br>他说要戒烟，我得亲眼见了才信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make beˈlieve (that)...</td><td>假装；佯装</td><td>The children made believe that the sofa was a pirate ship.<br>孩子们把沙发当成了海盗船。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not beˌlieve your ˈeyes/ˈears</td><td>不敢相信自己的眼睛（或耳朵）</td><td>I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the price tag.<br>看到价签时我简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>would you beˈlieve (it)? (spoken)</td><td>（表惊讶或恼怒）你敢信吗</td><td>Would you believe it, he turned up two hours late again.<br>你敢信吗，他又迟到了两个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lead sb to beˈlieve (that)...</td><td>使某人相信；让人以为</td><td>The advert led us to believe breakfast was included.<br>广告让我们以为含早餐。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>believer</b></td><td>be a great/firm beˈliever in sth</td><td>坚信；极力推崇某事物</td><td>My aunt is a firm believer in a cold shower every morning.<br>我姑妈笃信每天早上冲个冷水澡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bell</b></td><td>give sb a ˈbell (BrE, informal)</td><td>给某人打电话</td><td>Give me a bell when you get to the station and I'll come.<br>你到站给我打个电话，我去接你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bells</b></td><td>ˌbells and ˈwhistles</td><td>花哨的附加功能；点缀</td><td>I just want a basic phone without all the bells and whistles.<br>我只想要个简单手机，不需要那些花哨功能。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>belly</b></td><td>go belly ˈup</td><td>（企业等）破产；垮掉</td><td>The little printing firm went belly up after the contract fell through.<br>合同一黄，那家小印刷厂就倒闭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bellyful</b></td><td>have had a ˈbellyful of sb/sth (informal)</td><td>受够了某人（或某事）</td><td>I've had a bellyful of his excuses this month.<br>这个月他的借口我听够了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>belt</b></td><td>below the ˈbelt</td><td>不公正；暗中伤人；下作</td><td>That joke about his divorce was really below the belt, and everyone went quiet.<br>那句拿他离婚开玩笑的话太下作了，全场都安静了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bend sb's ˈear (about sth) (informal)</td><td>缠着某人唠叨；向某人诉苦</td><td>He bent my ear about his noisy neighbours for a solid two hours.<br>他缠着我唠叨了整整两个小时他那吵闹的邻居。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bend your ˈmind/ˈefforts to sth (formal)</td><td>专心于某事；竭尽全力做某事</td><td>She bent her mind to the problem and found a solution by midnight.<br>她全神贯注地琢磨这个难题，半夜前就想出了办法。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bend the ˈtruth</td><td>歪曲事实；说得不尽属实</td><td>He bent the truth a little to make his fishing story sound better.<br>他把事实稍微歪曲了一下，好让钓鱼的故事更精彩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(drive sb/be/go) round the ˈbend/ˈtwist</td><td>（使）发疯；（把人）惹恼</td><td>That dripping tap is driving me round the bend at three in the morning.<br>凌晨三点那个滴水的龙头快把我逼疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go round the ˈtwist</td><td>发疯；抓狂</td><td>I'm going round the twist trying to repair this ancient washing machine.<br>修这台老掉牙的洗衣机快把我逼疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈbest/ˈworst</td><td>充其量；往最坏处说</td><td>At best the repair takes a week; at worst, it takes a month.<br>往好里说修一周，往坏里说得一个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on bended ˈknee(s)</td><td>跪着恳求；低声下气地请求</td><td>He practically begged on bended knee for one more chance at the job.<br>他几乎是跪下来求人再给他一次工作机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for sb's ˈbenefit</td><td>为了帮助某人；为某人好</td><td>I repeated the whole announcement for the benefit of the people who arrived late.<br>我把整个通知又说了一遍，是为了照顾迟到的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for my ˈbenefit</td><td>专门为了照顾我</td><td>There's no need to repeat everything for my benefit; I heard it fine.<br>不用专门为我把所有内容再说一遍，我听清楚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb the ˌbenefit of the ˈdoubt</td><td>因证据不足而姑且相信某人</td><td>She was late again, but I gave her the benefit of the doubt.<br>她又迟到了，但我还是姑且相信她有苦衷。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your best bib and ˈtucker (humorous)</td><td>最好的衣服；盛装行头</td><td>Put on your best bib and tucker — we're eating at a fancy restaurant.<br>换上你最好的行头，我们要去高档餐厅吃饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the best ˈmedicine</td><td>最好的良药；最有效的办法</td><td>After a rotten week, a long walk by the sea is the best medicine.<br>过了糟糕的一周，去海边走走就是最好的良药。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the best of a bad ˈbunch/ˈlot (BrE)</td><td>差中较好者；矮子里拔将军</td><td>None of the flats were nice, but this one was the best of a bad bunch.<br>这些公寓都不理想，这套算是矮子里拔将军。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the best of ˈboth/ˈall (possible) worlds</td><td>两全其美；兼得多方好处</td><td>Working from home two days a week gives me the best of both worlds.<br>每周在家办公两天，让我两头的好处都占了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the best of ˈluck (to sb) (old-fashioned, informal, often ironic)</td><td>祝你好运（多含反语，暗指难成）</td><td>You want him to apologize? Well, the best of luck to you.<br>你想让他道歉？那祝你好运吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the best of ˈthree, ˈfive, etc.</td><td>三局两胜（或五局三胜等）</td><td>Let's play the best of three and the loser buys dinner.<br>我们打三局两胜，输的人请客吃饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the best thing since sliced ˈbread (informal, spoken)</td><td>好得不得了的东西</td><td>He thinks his new coffee machine is the best thing since sliced bread.<br>他觉得他那台新咖啡机简直是天底下最棒的发明。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring out the ˈbest in sb</td><td>使某人显现出最佳品质</td><td>A crisis like this really brings out the best in ordinary people.<br>这样的危机最能激发出普通人身上最好的一面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do, mean, etc. sth for the ˈbest</td><td>出于好意做（或说）某事</td><td>I know I upset you, but I only said it for the best.<br>我知道惹你不高兴了，可我说那话是出于好意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for a/some reason/reasons best known to himˈself, herˈself, etc. (humorous)</td><td>出于只有本人才明白的理由</td><td>For reasons best known to himself, he painted the whole kitchen bright orange.<br>出于只有他自己清楚的原因，他把整个厨房刷成了亮橙色。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/have the ˈbest of sth</td><td>占上风；获益最多</td><td>She had the best of the argument and he finally stopped talking.<br>这场争论她占了上风，他最后不吭声了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give it your best ˈshot</td><td>全力一试；尽最大努力</td><td>I know the exam is hard, but just give it your best shot.<br>我知道考试很难，你尽力一试就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look your/its ˈbest</td><td>呈现最佳状态；显得最漂亮</td><td>The garden looks its best in late May when the roses open.<br>五月底玫瑰开放的时候，这座花园最好看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make the best of sth/things/a bad job</td><td>在逆境中尽力而为；随遇而安</td><td>The hotel was awful, but we made the best of a bad job.<br>酒店很糟，但我们还是尽量往好处过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put your best foot ˈforward</td><td>加紧赶路；全力以赴</td><td>If we put our best foot forward, we can finish before it gets dark.<br>我们加把劲的话，天黑前就能干完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the best of your beˈlief/ˈknowledge</td><td>据某人所知；就某人所信</td><td>To the best of my knowledge, nobody has lived in that house for years.<br>据我所知，那房子已经好些年没人住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with the ˈbest of them</td><td>不亚于任何人；不比别人差</td><td>She's seventy, but she can dance with the best of them all night.<br>她七十岁了，可跳起舞来一点不输年轻人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with the ˌbest will in the ˈworld</td><td>不管用意多好；纵然竭尽全力</td><td>With the best will in the world, I can't finish this by Friday.<br>就算我再想帮忙，周五前也做不完。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bet</b></td><td>bet the ˈfarm/ranch (AmE)</td><td>孤注一掷；押上全部身家</td><td>Don't bet the farm on a start-up that hasn't earned a penny yet.<br>别把全部身家押在一家还没赚过一分钱的初创公司上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(you can) bet your bottom ˈdollar/your ˈlife</td><td>可以肯定；打包票</td><td>You can bet your bottom dollar he'll be late to his own wedding.<br>可以打包票，他连自己的婚礼都会迟到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I/I'll ˈbet (that...) (informal)</td><td>我敢打赌；我肯定</td><td>I bet that she forgot the tickets again — she always does.<br>我敢打赌她又忘带票了，她老这样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I wouldn't ˈbet on it • don't ˈbet on it</td><td>我看未必；很难说</td><td>He says he'll pay you back tomorrow, but I wouldn't bet on it.<br>他说明天还你钱，可我看未必。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you ˈbet (informal)</td><td>当然；那还用说</td><td>"Coming to the match tonight?" "You bet, I've had my ticket for weeks."<br>“今晚来看比赛吗？”“当然，票我几周前就买好了。”</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>noire</b></td><td>your, his, etc. bête ˈnoire (from French)</td><td>特别讨厌的人（或事物）</td><td>Early morning meetings are my bête noire, especially on a rainy Monday.<br>一大早开会是我最讨厌的事，尤其是下雨的周一。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bets</b></td><td>all bets are ˈoff</td><td>结果难料；一切都说不准</td><td>If the star player is injured, all bets are off for the final.<br>要是主力受伤，决赛的结果就完全说不准了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>better</b></td><td>against your better ˈjudgement (especially BrE) (AmE usually against your better ˈjudgment)</td><td>明知不妥仍为之</td><td>Against my better judgement, I lent him the car for the whole weekend.<br>尽管明知不妥，我还是把车借给他过了整个周末。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be better ˈoff</td><td>更富裕；处境更好</td><td>We're better off now that both of us are working full-time.<br>我们俩都全职上班以后，日子宽裕多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>better the ˌdevil you ˈknow (than the devil you don't) (saying)</td><td>宁用熟悉的坏，不用陌生的坏</td><td>I'll stay with my old boss — better the devil you know.<br>我还是跟着老板干吧，熟悉的魔鬼总好过陌生的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>better ˌlate than ˈnever (saying)</td><td>迟做总比不做好</td><td>He sent the birthday card in March, but better late than never.<br>他三月才寄来生日贺卡，不过迟到总比不到强。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>better luck ˈnext time (spoken)</td><td>祝下次好运</td><td>You missed the penalty, mate — better luck next time.<br>兄弟，你罚丢了点球，下次好运吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>better (to be) ˌsafe than ˈsorry (saying)</td><td>稳妥总比后悔好</td><td>Take an umbrella with that sky; better safe than sorry.<br>这天色，带把伞吧，小心总比后悔强。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌbigger, ˌfaster, etc. the ˈbetter</td><td>越大（或越快等）越好</td><td>When it comes to pizza, the bigger the better as far as I'm concerned.<br>说到披萨，在我看来越大越好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do better to do sth</td><td>最好做某事；做某事更明智</td><td>You'd do better to apologize now than wait until she hears it elsewhere.<br>你最好现在就道歉，别等她从别处听说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˌbetter or (for) ˈworse</td><td>不管是好是坏；无论结果如何</td><td>For better or worse, we've sold the house and moved to the coast.<br>不管是好是坏，我们卖了房子搬到海边了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get the ˈbetter of sb/sth</td><td>战胜；占上风；使无法克制</td><td>Curiosity got the better of me and I opened the letter.<br>好奇心占了上风，我把那封信拆开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go one ˈbetter (than sb/sth)</td><td>更胜一筹；比…做得更好</td><td>She baked a cake, then he went one better and cooked a whole dinner.<br>她烤了个蛋糕，他更胜一筹，做了一整桌晚饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>had better/best do sth</td><td>最好做某事；应该做某事</td><td>You'd better leave now if you want to catch the last train.<br>你要赶末班车的话，最好现在就走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have seen/known better ˈdays</td><td>今不如昔；已经破旧</td><td>That armchair has seen better days, but I can't bear to throw it out.<br>那把扶手椅早就旧了，可我舍不得扔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>little/no ˈbetter than</td><td>简直等于；好不到哪去</td><td>The so-called hotel was little better than a shed with beds in it.<br>那所谓的旅馆简直就是个摆了床的棚子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so much the ˈbetter/ˈworse (for sb/sth)</td><td>那就更好（或更糟）</td><td>If he brings the car, so much the better; we won't need a taxi.<br>他要是把车开来就更好了，我们就不用打车了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a ˌturn for the ˈbetter/ˈworse</td><td>好转；恶化</td><td>Her health took a turn for the worse a week after the operation.<br>手术一周后，她的身体状况恶化了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's (much) ˈbetter</td><td>这样好多了</td><td>You've stopped crying — that's much better. Now tell me what happened.<br>你不哭了，这样好多了。现在告诉我出了什么事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you/you'd better beˈlieve it! (spoken)</td><td>那是千真万确；你别不信</td><td>Is the boss angry? You'd better believe it — he's been shouting all morning.<br>老板生气了吗？你别不信，他吼了一上午。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>betting</b></td><td>what's the ˈbetting...? • the betting ˈis that...</td><td>很可能…；大概会…</td><td>What's the betting he turns up an hour late with no apology?<br>他八成会迟到一小时还不道歉，你信不信？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>between</b></td><td>between ourˈselves • between you and ˈme</td><td>你我之间的秘密；私下说说</td><td>Between you and me, I think she's planning to hand in her notice.<br>私下跟你说，我觉得她打算辞职了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in beˈtween</td><td>介于二者之间；在中间</td><td>He's not tall and not short — somewhere in between, I'd say.<br>他不高也不矮，我看是介于二者之间。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>twixt</b></td><td>be ˌtwixt and beˈtween (old-fashioned)</td><td>非此非彼；不上不下</td><td>The colour is twixt and between — neither proper blue nor proper green.<br>这颜色不上不下，说蓝不蓝说绿不绿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beyond</b></td><td>be beˈyond sb (informal)</td><td>为某人所不能理解；某人力所不及</td><td>Why anyone would queue overnight for a phone is quite beyond me.<br>为什么会有人为买手机通宵排队，我实在想不通。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bide</b></td><td>bide your ˈtime</td><td>等待时机</td><td>He bided his time and asked for a raise after the deal closed.<br>他等待时机，等合同签下来才开口要求加薪。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>big</b></td><td>ˌBig ˈBrother (is watching you)</td><td>老大哥（监控一切的当权者）</td><td>With cameras on every corner, Big Brother really is watching you now.<br>街角都是摄像头，老大哥真的在盯着你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>big</b></td><td>a ˌbig ˈcheese (informal)</td><td>大人物；要员</td><td>He's a big cheese at the bank now, with his own corner office.<br>他现在是银行里的大人物，有自己的独立办公室。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>big ˈdeal (informal, ironic)</td><td>没什么了不起</td><td>So he won one game against me. Big deal.<br>他不过赢了我一局，有什么了不起。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the big enchiˈlada (AmE, informal, humorous)</td><td>最重要的人（或事物）；头号角色</td><td>Forget the small contracts; this deal is the big enchilada.<br>别管那些小合同了，这笔生意才是重头戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a big ˈfish (in a little/small pond)</td><td>小圈子里的大人物</td><td>He was a big fish in a small pond until he moved to London.<br>搬到伦敦之前，他在小地方算是个大人物。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌbig girl's ˈblouse (informal, humorous)</td><td>娘娘腔；软弱怯懦的男人</td><td>Stop being such a big girl's blouse and get in the cold water.<br>别那么娘们儿唧唧的了，下冷水里去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a big ˈname/ˈnoise • a ˈbig shot (informal)</td><td>要人；名人；大腕</td><td>They hired a big name to open the new shopping centre.<br>他们请了个大腕来给新商场剪彩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈbig time (informal)</td><td>巨大成功；大红大紫</td><td>After that album she finally hit the big time and toured the world.<br>那张专辑之后她终于大红大紫，开始全球巡演。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb a big ˈhand (informal)</td><td>热烈鼓掌</td><td>Let's give the band a big hand — they played for three hours.<br>我们给乐队热烈鼓掌，他们演了三个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>me and my big ˈmouth (spoken)</td><td>我这张大嘴巴；我真多嘴</td><td>I told her about the surprise party — me and my big mouth.<br>我把惊喜派对的事说漏了，我这张大嘴巴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no big ˈdeal (spoken)</td><td>没什么要紧；无所谓</td><td>You forgot my birthday? Honestly, it's no big deal.<br>你忘了我生日？说真的，没什么要紧的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one ˌbig ˌhappy ˈfamily (informal)</td><td>欢乐的大家庭</td><td>In this office we're one big happy family, at least most days.<br>我们办公室就像个欢乐的大家庭，至少大多数时候是。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>too ˌbig for your ˈboots (informal)</td><td>自大；自以为是</td><td>Since the promotion he's got far too big for his boots.<br>自从升职以后，他就变得特别自以为是。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bike</b></td><td>on your ˈbike! (BrE, informal)</td><td>走开；滚开</td><td>On your bike! I'm not lending you money a third time.<br>滚吧！我不会第三次借钱给你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bill</b></td><td>head/top the ˈbill</td><td>主演；压轴；名列榜首</td><td>A local band will top the bill at the festival this summer.<br>今年夏天的音乐节将由一支本地乐队压轴。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>billy-o</b></td><td>like ˈbilly-o (BrE, informal)</td><td>猛烈地；拼命地</td><td>It rained like billy-o all afternoon and the match was called off.<br>整个下午雨下得特别猛，比赛取消了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bind</b></td><td>in a ˈbind (AmE)</td><td>陷入困境；进退两难</td><td>I'm in a bind — my babysitter cancelled an hour before the show.<br>我进退两难，保姆在演出前一小时取消了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bird</b></td><td>the bird has ˈflown</td><td>要找的人已逃走</td><td>The police kicked the door in, but the bird had already flown.<br>警察踹开了门，可要抓的人早跑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌbird in the ˈhand is worth two in the ˈbush (saying)</td><td>一鸟在手胜过二鸟在林</td><td>Take the offer they made; a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.<br>接受他们的报价吧，双鸟在林不如一鸟在手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌbird of ˈpassage</td><td>漂泊不定的人；过客</td><td>He's a bird of passage who never stays in one city long.<br>他是个漂泊不定的人，从不在一个城市久留。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>flip/give/shoot sb the ˈbird (AmE, slang)</td><td>冲某人竖中指（表示侮辱）</td><td>The driver gave me the bird when I honked at the traffic lights.<br>我在红灯处按喇叭，那司机冲我竖了中指。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>birds</b></td><td>the birds and the ˈbees (old-fashioned or humorous)</td><td>基本的性知识</td><td>Dad went red trying to explain the birds and the bees to us.<br>爸爸满脸通红地想给我们讲那些性知识。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>birds of a ˈfeather (flock toˈgether) (saying)</td><td>物以类聚，人以群分</td><td>Those two are always plotting together — birds of a feather, I suppose.<br>那俩人总凑一块儿谋划，真是物以类聚。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give</b></td><td>give ˈbirth (to sb/sth)</td><td>生孩子；产生（新事物）</td><td>She gave birth to twin boys in the back of a taxi.<br>她在出租车后座生下了一对双胞胎男孩。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bit</b></td><td>the (whole) ... ˈbit (informal, disapproving)</td><td>一整套典型做派（或说辞）</td><td>He gave us the whole struggling-artist bit again over dinner.<br>晚饭时他又把那套穷困艺术家的说辞搬了出来。</td></tr>
