<tr><td></td><td>a bit ˈmuch (informal)</td><td>有点过分；太过头</td><td>Charging for tap water is a bit much, even in this city.<br>自来水都收费，就算在这座城市也有点过分了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a bit of ˈrough (BrE, slang)</td><td>（社会地位低的）粗野情人</td><td>She told her friends she rather fancied a bit of rough.<br>她跟朋友说，她还挺喜欢粗野型的男人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not a ˈbit • not one (little) ˈbit</td><td>一点也不；毫不</td><td>I'm not a bit surprised that he forgot to call again.<br>他又忘了打电话，我一点都不意外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not a ˈbit of it! (BrE, informal)</td><td>根本不是那样；压根儿没有</td><td>I expected him to apologize, but not a bit of it.<br>我以为他会道歉，结果压根儿没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bite</b></td><td>a bite at/of the ˈcherry (BrE)</td><td>做某事的机会</td><td>Everyone deserves a bite at the cherry before the jobs are filled.<br>职位定下来之前，每个人都该有一次机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a second/another bite at/of the ˈcherry (BrE)</td><td>第二次机会；再来一次的机会</td><td>He failed the driving test but gets another bite at the cherry in June.<br>他驾照没考过，六月还有一次机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bite the ˈbig one (AmE, slang)</td><td>糟透了；失败</td><td>This assignment bites the big one; I've rewritten it four times already.<br>这作业烂透了，我都重写四遍了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bite the ˈbullet (informal)</td><td>咬紧牙关应付；硬着头皮做</td><td>I finally bit the bullet and told my boss I was leaving.<br>我终于咬紧牙关告诉老板我要走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bite the ˈdust (informal)</td><td>失败；完蛋；被摧毁</td><td>Another small bookshop on the high street has bitten the dust.<br>大街上又一家小书店倒闭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bite the hand that ˈfeeds you</td><td>恩将仇报；以怨报德</td><td>Criticizing the charity that pays your salary is biting the hand that feeds you.<br>批评给你发工资的慈善机构，就是恩将仇报。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bite your ˈlip</td><td>咬住嘴唇忍住不说（或不哭）</td><td>She bit her lip and said nothing when he took all the credit.<br>他把功劳全揽走时，她咬着嘴唇一句话没说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bite your ˈnails/fingernails</td><td>焦虑不安地咬指甲</td><td>He sat biting his nails while the jury argued in the next room.<br>陪审团在隔壁争论时，他坐着咬指甲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bite off ˌmore than you can ˈchew (informal)</td><td>不自量力；贪多嚼不烂</td><td>Taking three courses at once, she'd bitten off more than she could chew.<br>一下选三门课，她真是贪多嚼不烂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bite your ˈtongue</td><td>忍住不说；把话咽回去</td><td>I bit my tongue when she criticized my cooking in front of guests.<br>她当着客人批评我的厨艺，我忍住没吭声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I, etc. won't ˈbite (you) (humorous)</td><td>我又不会吃了你</td><td>Go and ask her yourself — honestly, she won't bite you.<br>你自己去问她，真的，她又不会吃了你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>biter</b></td><td>the biter ˈbit</td><td>害人反害己；作法自毙</td><td>The biter bit: his own prank ended up soaking him instead.<br>作法自毙，他自己的恶作剧最后把他淋了个透。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bits</b></td><td>bits and ˈpieces (also ˌbits and ˈbobs BrE)</td><td>零星物品；零七八碎</td><td>I keep bits and pieces of old jewellery in this biscuit tin.<br>我把零星的旧首饰都放在这个饼干盒里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a bitter ˈpill (for sb) (to swallow)</td><td>难以接受的苦果</td><td>Losing the final at home was a bitter pill for the fans to swallow.<br>在主场输掉决赛，对球迷来说是难以下咽的苦果。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the bitter ˈend</td><td>坚持到底；一直到最后</td><td>They fought the eviction to the bitter end and lost anyway.<br>他们抗争驱逐令直到最后，结果还是输了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>black and ˈblue</td><td>青一块紫一块；遍体鳞伤</td><td>He fell off his bike and his knees were black and blue.<br>他从自行车上摔下来，膝盖青一块紫一块。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(in) black and ˈwhite</td><td>非黑即白；看问题绝对化</td><td>She sees every issue in black and white, with no middle ground.<br>她看什么问题都非黑即白，没有中间地带。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a black ˈday (for sb)</td><td>倒霉的一天；黑暗的日子</td><td>It was a black day for the town when the factory closed.<br>工厂关闭那天，对这个镇子来说是黑暗的一天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the black ˈmarket</td><td>黑市</td><td>Tickets for the final were selling on the black market for hundreds.<br>决赛的门票在黑市上炒到了好几百。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈblack spot</td><td>事故多发地段；问题严重的地方</td><td>This junction is a notorious black spot for cyclists in winter.<br>这个路口是冬天骑车人出事的著名黑点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈblack (business)</td><td>有盈余；账面不亏损</td><td>The café has finally been in the black for three months running.<br>这家咖啡馆终于连续三个月有盈余了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>he, it, etc. is not as black as he, it, etc. is ˈpainted</td><td>并不像人们说的那么坏</td><td>Her new boss isn't as black as he's painted, honestly.<br>说实话，她新老板并不像传言说的那么坏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look ˈblack</td><td>前景暗淡；希望渺茫</td><td>Things looked black for the team after two players were sent off.<br>两名队员被罚下后，球队前景一片暗淡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blame</b></td><td>be to ˈblame (for sth)</td><td>对（坏事）负有责任</td><td>Nobody is to blame for the accident; the road was simply icy.<br>这场事故谁也不怪，路面结冰了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>don't blame ˈme (spoken)</td><td>别怪我（用于劝阻他人）</td><td>Swim in that river if you like, but don't blame me afterwards.<br>你爱去那条河游就去，出了事别怪我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I don't ˈblame you/her, etc. (for doing sth)</td><td>我不怪你（或她等）；情有可原</td><td>You walked out of the meeting? I don't blame you one bit.<br>你退出了会议？我一点也不怪你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blank</b></td><td>a blank ˈcheque (BrE) (AmE a blank ˈcheck)</td><td>自由处理权；全权委托</td><td>The board gave her a blank cheque to rebuild the whole department.<br>董事会给了她全权去重建整个部门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blanket</b></td><td>a wet ˈblanket (informal)</td><td>扫兴的人；爱泼冷水的人</td><td>Don't be a wet blanket; everyone else wants to stay out longer.<br>别扫大家的兴，其他人都还想再待会儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blast</b></td><td>a ˌblast from the ˈpast (informal)</td><td>勾起回忆的旧人旧事旧物</td><td>That song on the radio was a real blast from the past.<br>收音机里那首歌真是勾起了满满的回忆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blaze</b></td><td>blaze a/the ˈtrail</td><td>开辟道路；作先驱</td><td>Her lab blazed a trail in treating the disease with cheap drugs.<br>她的实验室在用廉价药治这种病上开了先河。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blazes</b></td><td>like ˈblazes (old-fashioned, spoken)</td><td>猛烈地；飞快地</td><td>We ran like blazes to catch the last bus home.<br>我们飞奔着去赶回家的末班车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what/where/who the ˈblazes...? (old-fashioned, spoken)</td><td>到底是什么（哪儿、谁）</td><td>Where the blazes did I put my reading glasses this time?<br>我这回到底把老花镜放哪儿了？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bleed</b></td><td>bleed sb ˈdry/ˈwhite (disapproving)</td><td>榨干某人的钱财</td><td>The lawsuit bled the small company dry within a single year.<br>这场官司一年之内就把这家小公司榨干了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bless</b></td><td>bless (BrE, spoken, approving)</td><td>真可爱；真难为他（表示喜爱）</td><td>He made me a birthday card all by himself — bless!<br>他自己给我做了张生日卡，真可爱！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌbless his, her, etc. (little) cotton ˈsocks (BrE, humorous)</td><td>真难为他（她）；太可爱了</td><td>He waited two hours in the rain for me, bless his cotton socks.<br>他在雨里等了我两个小时，真是难为他了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈbless you</td><td>上帝保佑你（他人打喷嚏时说）</td><td>"Atishoo!" "Bless you — there's a box of tissues on the table."<br>“阿嚏！”“上帝保佑你，桌上有纸巾。”</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a blessing in disˈguise</td><td>因祸得福；看似祸实是福</td><td>Missing that flight turned out to be a blessing in disguise.<br>没赶上那班飞机，结果是因祸得福。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌblind ˈalley</td><td>死胡同；行不通的办法</td><td>The investigation went down a blind alley for almost six months.<br>调查在死胡同里绕了将近六个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) blind as a ˈbat (humorous)</td><td>视力极差；几乎看不见</td><td>Without my glasses I'm as blind as a bat in this light.<br>不戴眼镜，这种光线下我几乎什么都看不见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌblind ˈdate</td><td>相亲；与陌生人的约会</td><td>My sister set me up on a blind date with her colleague.<br>我姐姐给我安排了和她同事的相亲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blind ˈdrunk (informal)</td><td>烂醉如泥</td><td>He came home blind drunk and fell asleep on the stairs.<br>他烂醉如泥地回到家，睡在了楼梯上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blind sb with ˈscience</td><td>用专业术语把人唬住</td><td>The salesman tried to blind us with science instead of quoting a price.<br>推销员净拿专业术语唬人，就是不肯报价。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn a blind ˈeye (to sth)</td><td>视而不见；睁一只眼闭一只眼</td><td>Managers turned a blind eye to staff leaving early on Fridays.<br>经理对员工周五早退睁一只眼闭一只眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blink</b></td><td>in the blink of an ˈeye</td><td>一眨眼的工夫；转眼间</td><td>The whole summer went by in the blink of an eye.<br>整个夏天一眨眼就过去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈblink (informal)</td><td>（机器）失灵，出毛病</td><td>The washing machine is on the blink again, twice this month.<br>洗衣机又出毛病了，这个月第二回。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>block</b></td><td>have been around the ˈblock (a few times)</td><td>经验丰富；见多识广</td><td>Don't try to trick her; she's been around the block a few times.<br>别想骗她，她可是见过世面的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/lay your head/neck on the ˈblock</td><td>甘冒风险；把自己置于受责难之地</td><td>I put my neck on the block by recommending him for the job.<br>我推荐他做这份工作，是把自己搭进去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blood</b></td><td>bad ˈblood (between A and B) (old-fashioned)</td><td>积怨；仇恨</td><td>There's been bad blood between the two families since the land dispute.<br>自那场土地纠纷后，两家就一直有积怨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be after/out for sb's ˈblood (informal, often humorous)</td><td>想报复某人；找某人算账</td><td>The coach is out for my blood after I missed training twice.<br>我两次没去训练，教练正找我算账呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blood and ˈguts (informal)</td><td>血腥暴力场面</td><td>The film is all blood and guts with hardly any plot.<br>这部电影全是血腥场面，几乎没什么情节。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blood and ˈthunder (informal)</td><td>耸人听闻的煽情场面</td><td>The old play is pure blood and thunder, and the crowd loves it.<br>这出老戏纯是刀光剑影，观众就爱看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blood is thicker than ˈwater (saying)</td><td>血浓于水；家人总比外人亲</td><td>They argue constantly, but blood is thicker than water when trouble comes.<br>他们老吵架，可一有事就血浓于水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your/sb's ˌblood is ˈup (BrE)</td><td>怒火中烧；血气上涌</td><td>Once his blood was up, nobody could talk him out of fighting.<br>他一上火，谁也劝不住他动手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌblood, sweat and ˈtears</td><td>血汗；艰苦付出</td><td>This restaurant took ten years of blood, sweat and tears to build.<br>这家餐馆是十年的血汗才做起来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fresh/new/young ˈblood</td><td>新生力量；新鲜血液</td><td>The committee badly needs new blood and a few younger voices.<br>委员会很需要新鲜血液和一些年轻人的声音。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have (sb's) ˈblood on your hands</td><td>对某人的死负有罪责</td><td>The company has blood on its hands after ignoring the safety warnings.<br>公司无视安全警告，手上沾着人命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the/sb's ˈblood/genes</td><td>与生俱来；天生如此</td><td>Sailing is in his blood; his grandfather fished these waters for decades.<br>航海是他骨子里的东西，他祖父在这片海打了几十年鱼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like getting ˌblood out of/from a ˈstone</td><td>极难办到；难于登天</td><td>Getting an apology out of him is like getting blood from a stone.<br>想让他道歉，比登天还难。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make sb's ˈblood boil</td><td>使某人怒火中烧</td><td>The way he talks to waiters makes my blood boil every time.<br>他跟服务员说话的那副样子每次都让我火冒三丈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make sb's ˈblood run cold • make sb's ˈblood freeze</td><td>令人毛骨悚然</td><td>The scream from the empty flat made my blood run cold.<br>空屋里传出的尖叫让我毛骨悚然。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your (own) flesh and ˈblood</td><td>亲骨肉；至亲</td><td>You can't turn your back on her; she's your own flesh and blood.<br>你不能不管她，她是你的亲骨肉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blot</b></td><td>a blot on the ˈlandscape</td><td>煞风景的东西（尤指丑陋建筑）</td><td>That concrete car park is a real blot on the landscape.<br>那座水泥停车场真是大煞风景。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blow</b></td><td>blow your/sb's ˈbrains out (informal)</td><td>开枪打爆脑袋；饮弹自尽</td><td>In the film the villain threatens to blow his own brains out.<br>电影里那个反派威胁说要开枪自尽。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow ˈchunks (AmE, slang)</td><td>呕吐；糟糕透顶</td><td>He ate three hot dogs and then blew chunks on the ride.<br>他吃了三个热狗，然后在游乐设施上吐了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow sb's ˈcover (informal)</td><td>暴露某人身份；揭穿伪装</td><td>One careless phone call completely blew the agent's cover last night.<br>昨晚一个不小心的电话彻底暴露了那名特工的身份。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow a ˈfuse (informal)</td><td>大发雷霆；勃然大怒</td><td>Dad blew a fuse when he saw the dent in the car.<br>爸爸看到车上的凹痕，勃然大怒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow the ˈgaff (on sb/sth) (BrE, informal)</td><td>泄密；抖出真相</td><td>Somebody blew the gaff on the surprise party before the weekend.<br>周末前有人把惊喜派对的秘密抖了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow hot and ˈcold (informal)</td><td>忽冷忽热；三心二意</td><td>She blows hot and cold about moving abroad, so nothing gets decided.<br>她对出国的事忽冷忽热，什么也定不下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow your/sb's ˈmind (informal)</td><td>使极度兴奋；令人震撼</td><td>The view from the top of the ridge completely blew my mind.<br>从山脊顶上看到的景色让我震撼极了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈmind-blowing (adj.)</td><td>令人震撼的；极其惊人的</td><td>We were stunned by the mind-blowing scenery on the drive north.<br>北上路上那令人震撼的景色让我们都看呆了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow sb/sth out of the ˈwater (informal)</td><td>彻底击败；证明毫无价值</td><td>Their new phone blows the competition out of the water on price.<br>他们的新手机在价格上把对手打得落花流水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow your own ˈtrumpet (especially BrE) (informal)</td><td>自吹自擂</td><td>He never stops blowing his own trumpet about that one big sale.<br>他没完没了地吹嘘那一笔大单。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow/toot your own ˈhorn (AmE, informal)</td><td>自吹自擂；自我吹嘘</td><td>I hate to toot my own horn, but I fixed the boiler myself.<br>我不想自夸，但锅炉确实是我自己修好的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow sb/sth ˌsky-ˈhigh (informal)</td><td>炸飞；彻底摧毁</td><td>One spark could blow the whole fuel depot sky-high.<br>一个火星就可能把整个油库炸上天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow ˈsmoke (up sb's ass) (AmE, slang)</td><td>说好话蒙人；放烟雾弹</td><td>Stop blowing smoke and tell me what the repair actually costs.<br>别跟我兜圈子了，直说修一下到底多少钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow your ˈtop (BrE) (AmE blow your ˈstack)</td><td>大发雷霆；火冒三丈</td><td>She blew her top when she found the kitchen in that state.<br>她看到厨房那副样子，气得暴跳如雷。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow up in sb's ˈface</td><td>（计划等）突然砸锅、失败</td><td>His clever plan to impress the boss blew up in his face.<br>他讨好老板的妙计彻底砸了锅。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>blow the ˈwhistle (on sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>检举揭发（某人某事）</td><td>An accountant blew the whistle on the firm's fake expense claims.<br>一名会计揭发了公司虚假报销的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cushion/soften the ˈblow</td><td>缓和打击；减轻冲击</td><td>A month's extra pay helped soften the blow of losing the job.<br>多发一个月工资，多少缓和了失业的打击。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blow-by-blow</b></td><td>a ˌblow-by-ˌblow acˈcount, deˈscription, etc.</td><td>详尽的叙述（或描述）</td><td>He gave a blow-by-blow account of the match to everyone at work.<br>他把比赛过程一五一十地讲给单位同事听。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blows</b></td><td>come to ˈblows (over sth)</td><td>动武；打起来</td><td>The two neighbours nearly came to blows over a parking space.<br>两个邻居为一个车位差点动起手来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blue</b></td><td>out of the ˈblue</td><td>突然；出乎意料地</td><td>She called me out of the blue after twenty years of silence.<br>沉寂二十年后，她突然给我打来电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(do sth) till you're ˌblue in the ˈface</td><td>说到口干舌燥（也无济于事）</td><td>You can explain till you're blue in the face; he won't listen.<br>你说到口干舌燥也没用，他根本不听。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blue-eyed</b></td><td>your, sb's, etc. ˌblue-eyed ˈboy (informal, disapproving)</td><td>红人；宠儿</td><td>Everyone knows he's the manager's blue-eyed boy around this office.<br>谁都知道他是经理在办公室里的红人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blushes</b></td><td>save/spare sb's ˈblushes (informal)</td><td>免得使某人难堪</td><td>I changed the subject quickly to spare her blushes at dinner.<br>我赶紧换了话题，免得她在饭桌上难堪。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>board</b></td><td>above ˈboard</td><td>光明正大；公开合法</td><td>The accounts were all above board when the inspectors checked them.<br>检查员查账时，账目全都清清白白。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>aˌcross the ˈboard</td><td>全面地；一律地</td><td>Wages went up three per cent across the board this April.<br>今年四月工资全面上涨了百分之三。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go by the ˈboard</td><td>（计划等）被放弃，落空</td><td>Our holiday plans went by the board when the baby arrived early.<br>孩子提前出生，我们的假期计划就泡汤了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈboard</td><td>在船（飞机、火车）上</td><td>There were forty passengers on board when the engine suddenly failed.<br>发动机突然故障时，船上有四十名乘客。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth on ˈboard (informal)</td><td>采纳（意见）；考虑到（问题）</td><td>The designers took our complaints on board and changed the whole layout.<br>设计师采纳了我们的意见，把布局全改了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>boat</b></td><td>be in the ˌsame ˈboat</td><td>处境相同；同病相怜</td><td>Don't worry, we're all in the same boat with these rising rents.<br>别急，房租都在涨，大家处境都一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bob</b></td><td>(and) Bob's your ˈuncle (BrE, informal)</td><td>这就成了；大功告成</td><td>Add the eggs, stir for a minute, and Bob's your uncle.<br>加进鸡蛋，搅一分钟，就大功告成了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bode</b></td><td>bode ˈwell/ill (for sb/sth) (formal)</td><td>是吉兆；是凶兆</td><td>The empty seats did not bode well for the rest of the tour.<br>空荡荡的座位对后面的巡演可不是好兆头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>body</b></td><td>body and ˈsoul</td><td>全身心地；完完全全</td><td>She threw herself body and soul into running the little corner shop.<br>她全身心地扑在经营那家街角小店上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep body and ˈsoul together (often humorous)</td><td>勉强维持生计</td><td>Two part-time jobs barely keep body and soul together these days.<br>如今两份兼职也只够勉强糊口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bog</b></td><td>bog ˈstandard (BrE, informal)</td><td>普普通通的；毫无特色的</td><td>It's a bog standard hotel room, but the bed is comfortable.<br>就是间普普通通的酒店房间，不过床挺舒服。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>boil</b></td><td>off the ˈboil (BrE)</td><td>不再活跃；热度消退</td><td>Their relationship has gone off the boil since he moved away.<br>他搬走以后，他们的关系就淡下来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈboil</td><td>十分活跃；如火如荼</td><td>The campaign is really on the boil in this final week.<br>最后这一周，竞选活动搞得如火如荼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bold</b></td><td>be/make so ˈbold (as to do sth) (formal)</td><td>不揣冒昧；斗胆</td><td>Might I be so bold as to ask what this painting cost?<br>恕我冒昧，能问问这幅画多少钱吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) bold as ˈbrass (BrE, informal)</td><td>厚颜无耻；大模大样</td><td>He walked in bold as brass and helped himself to the coffee.<br>他大模大样地走进来，自己倒了杯咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bolt</b></td><td>a ˌbolt from the ˈblue</td><td>晴天霹雳；突如其来的事</td><td>The redundancy notice came as a complete bolt from the blue.<br>裁员通知来得像晴天霹雳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bolt ˈupright</td><td>笔直地（坐起）</td><td>She sat bolt upright when she heard the front door open.<br>听到前门打开的声音，她一下子直挺挺地坐了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈbolt/ˈdash for it/sth (informal)</td><td>拔腿就跑；夺路而逃</td><td>When the rain eased, we made a dash for the car.<br>雨小些时，我们撒腿冲向汽车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bomb</b></td><td>be the ˈbomb (AmE)</td><td>特别棒；顶呱呱</td><td>That taco place downtown is the bomb, especially late at night.<br>市中心那家玉米卷店特别棒，尤其是深夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go down a ˈbomb • go (like) a ˈbomb (BrE)</td><td>大获成功；十分轰动</td><td>Her speech went down a bomb with the students last night.<br>昨晚她的演讲在学生中大受欢迎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go like a ˈbomb (BrE)</td><td>（车辆）跑得飞快</td><td>That old van still goes like a bomb on the motorway.<br>那辆旧货车在高速上还是跑得飞快。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bond</b></td><td>your word is your ˈbond</td><td>说话算数；一诺千金</td><td>With him a handshake is enough; his word is his bond.<br>跟他握个手就行了，他说话向来算数。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bone</b></td><td>bone ˈidle (BrE, informal)</td><td>懒到极点</td><td>He's bone idle and hasn't cut the grass since April.<br>他懒到家了，四月以来一次草都没割。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a bone of conˈtention</td><td>争议的焦点</td><td>The shared driveway has long been a bone of contention between them.<br>那条共用车道一直是他们之间的争议焦点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>close to/near the ˈbone (informal)</td><td>过于直露；容易伤人</td><td>His jokes about her weight were a bit close to the bone.<br>他拿她体重开的玩笑有点太伤人了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cut, pare, etc. sth to the ˈbone</td><td>削减到最低限度</td><td>The council has cut library funding to the bone this year.<br>今年市政厅把图书馆经费砍到了最低。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈbone to pick with sb (informal)</td><td>要跟某人理论；有账要算</td><td>I've got a bone to pick with you about last night's phone call.<br>昨晚那通电话，我得跟你说道说道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have a ... ˈbone in your body</td><td>全无某种品性</td><td>She doesn't have a jealous bone in her body, honestly.<br>说真的，她身上一点嫉妒心都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw sb a ˈbone</td><td>施以小惠；给点好处</td><td>The boss threw me a bone and let me leave early on Friday.<br>老板给了点甜头，让我周五早走。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bones</b></td><td>make no ˈbones about sth/about doing sth</td><td>直言不讳；毫不掩饰</td><td>She makes no bones about wanting her old job back.<br>她毫不掩饰想要回原来的工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>boo</b></td><td>he, she, etc. wouldn't say ˈboo to a goose</td><td>非常腼腆胆小</td><td>Quiet Tom wouldn't say boo to a goose, let alone argue.<br>文静的汤姆连大气都不敢出，更别提争辩了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>book</b></td><td>bring sb to ˈbook (for sth) (formal, especially BrE)</td><td>追究责任；使受惩罚</td><td>The families want the company brought to book for the accident.<br>遇难者家属要求追究公司在这起事故中的责任。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by the ˈbook</td><td>照章办事；循规蹈矩</td><td>Our new manager does everything by the book, even the coffee rota.<br>新经理什么都照章办事，连轮流泡咖啡都不例外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in sb's ˈbook (spoken)</td><td>依某人看；照某人的观点</td><td>In my book, anyone who helps a stranger like that deserves thanks.<br>在我看来，那样帮陌生人的人值得道谢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw the ˈbook at sb (informal)</td><td>严厉惩处某人；从重发落</td><td>The judge threw the book at him for driving without insurance again.<br>他又无保险驾驶，法官从重判了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>close the ˈbook on sth</td><td>结束某事；不再过问</td><td>Police have closed the book on the case after thirty long years.<br>三十年后，警方给这个案子画上了句号。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>books</b></td><td>be in/get into sb's ˈgood/ˈbad books (informal)</td><td>得（或失）某人欢心</td><td>Washing his car got me back into my father's good books.<br>给我爸洗了车，我又讨他喜欢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on/off the/sb's ˈbooks (business)</td><td>记（或不记）在正式账目上</td><td>The firm has forty staff on the books and a few casuals.<br>公司账上有四十名员工，另有几个临时工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one for the ˈbooks (especially AmE)</td><td>值得记上一笔的稀奇事</td><td>Snow in April — now that really is one for the books.<br>四月下雪，这可真是件稀罕事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>boot</b></td><td>the boot is on the other ˈfoot (BrE, informal)</td><td>情况反过来了；此一时彼一时</td><td>Now that she's the manager, the boot is on the other foot.<br>现在她当了经理，情况可反过来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the shoe is on the other ˈfoot (AmE, informal)</td><td>形势反转；轮到对方了</td><td>He used to lend me money; now the shoe is on the other foot.<br>过去是他借钱给我，如今反过来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/get the ˈboot (informal)</td><td>解雇；被炒鱿鱼</td><td>He got the boot for turning up drunk on a Monday morning.<br>他周一早上喝醉了来上班，被炒了鱿鱼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/stick the ˈboot in (BrE, informal)</td><td>落井下石；猛踢倒地者</td><td>The papers put the boot in when the manager was already struggling.<br>经理本已焦头烂额，报纸还落井下石。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈboot (old-fashioned or humorous)</td><td>此外；而且还</td><td>The flat is cheap, central, and has a small garden to boot.<br>这套公寓便宜、地段好，还带个小花园。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bootstraps</b></td><td>drag/pull yourself up by your (own) ˈbootstraps (informal)</td><td>靠自身努力改善处境</td><td>He dragged himself up by his own bootstraps after leaving school at fifteen.<br>他十五岁辍学，全靠自己打拼出头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bore</b></td><td>bore sb to ˈtears • bore sb ˈstiff (informal)</td><td>使某人厌烦透顶</td><td>His holiday photos bored us to tears for a solid hour.<br>他的度假照片让我们整整烦了一个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bore sb out of their ˈmind (informal)</td><td>使某人极其厌倦</td><td>I was bored out of my mind during that three-hour lecture.<br>那节三小时的课听得我烦透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>born</b></td><td>be born with a silver ˈspoon in your mouth</td><td>生于富贵之家；含着金汤匙出生</td><td>He was born with a silver spoon in his mouth and never worked.<br>他生在富贵人家，从来没上过班。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌborn and ˈbred</td><td>土生土长</td><td>She's a Yorkshire woman born and bred, and proud of it.<br>她是土生土长的约克郡人，对此很自豪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I wasn't born ˈyesterday (spoken)</td><td>我可不傻；别想骗我</td><td>Don't tell me the dog ate it — I wasn't born yesterday.<br>别说是狗吃了，我可不是三岁小孩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in all my born ˈdays (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>有生以来；这辈子（从未）</td><td>I've never seen such a mess in all my born days.<br>我这辈子就没见过这么乱的场面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's one born every ˈminute (saying)</td><td>天下傻瓜多的是</td><td>He paid double for that car; there's one born every minute.<br>那车他花了双倍的钱，真是傻瓜年年有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know you're ˈborn (BrE, informal)</td><td>身在福中不知福</td><td>Kids today don't know they're born, with heating in every room.<br>现在的孩子身在福中不知福，每间屋子都有暖气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>borrowed</b></td><td>be/live on borrowed ˈtime</td><td>时日无多；勉强支撑</td><td>The old bridge has been living on borrowed time for several years.<br>那座老桥这几年一直是勉强撑着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈbosom of sth</td><td>在…的怀抱中；受…庇护</td><td>He spent Christmas in the bosom of his family for once.<br>他难得一回在家人的怀抱里过了圣诞。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the bottom drops/falls out of the ˈmarket</td><td>市场行情暴跌</td><td>The bottom fell out of the market for second-hand phones last year.<br>去年二手手机的市场行情一落千丈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'm not ˈbothered (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>我不在意；我无所谓</td><td>Pizza or curry — honestly, I'm not bothered either way.<br>披萨还是咖喱都行，我真的无所谓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈbottle it (BrE, informal)</td><td>临阵退缩；不敢做</td><td>He was going to propose, but he bottled it at the restaurant.<br>他本打算求婚，到了餐厅却怂了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have, show, etc. (a lot of) ˈbottle (BrE, informal)</td><td>很有胆量；有勇气</td><td>It takes real bottle to speak up at a meeting like that.<br>在那种会上敢开口，是真有胆量。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from the ˌbottom of your ˈheart</td><td>由衷地；打心眼里</td><td>I thank you from the bottom of my heart for staying tonight.<br>今晚你能留下来，我打心底里感谢你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈbottom</td><td>归根结底；本质上</td><td>At bottom, the argument was about money rather than principles.<br>归根结底，这场争论是为了钱而不是原则。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at the bottom/top of the ˈpile/ˈheap</td><td>处于社会最底层（或最上层）</td><td>You've no idea what life at the bottom of the pile is like.<br>你根本不知道社会最底层的日子是什么样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/lie at the ˈbottom of sth</td><td>是…的根本原因</td><td>Money worries lay at the bottom of most of their arguments.<br>钱的烦恼是他们大多数争吵的根源。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the bottom of the ˈhour (especially AmE)</td><td>半点整（如三点半）</td><td>The station broadcasts headlines at the top and bottom of the hour.<br>电台在整点和半点播报新闻提要。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get to the ˈbottom of sth</td><td>弄清真相；查明原委</td><td>I'm determined to get to the bottom of who took the money.<br>我一定要查清是谁拿走了那笔钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bottomless</b></td><td>a bottomless ˈpit (of sth)</td><td>无底洞；无休止的事物</td><td>Repairing this old house is a bottomless pit for our savings.<br>修这栋老房子简直是吞钱的无底洞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bottoms</b></td><td>bottoms ˈup! (old-fashioned, spoken)</td><td>干杯</td><td>Bottoms up, everyone — here's to the happy couple!<br>大家干杯，祝这对新人幸福！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bouncing</b></td><td>be ˌbouncing off the ˈwalls (informal)</td><td>兴奋得坐不住；激动难平</td><td>The kids were bouncing off the walls after all that chocolate.<br>吃了那么多巧克力，孩子们兴奋得停不下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bound</b></td><td>be/feel duty/honour ˈbound to do sth (BrE)</td><td>感到有义务做某事</td><td>I felt duty bound to tell her what I had overheard.<br>我觉得有义务把无意听到的事告诉她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/feel duty/honor ˈbound to do sth (AmE)</td><td>责无旁贷；有不可推卸的责任</td><td>As a doctor she feels honor bound to report the injury.<br>作为医生，她觉得有责任上报这处伤情。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bound and deˈtermined (AmE)</td><td>下定决心；矢志不渝</td><td>She's bound and determined to run the marathon before she turns forty.<br>她铁了心要在四十岁前跑完马拉松。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bounds</b></td><td>out of ˈbounds</td><td>（体育运动）出界</td><td>The ball landed out of bounds, so the throw goes to us.<br>球出界了，所以由我们发界外球。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of ˈbounds (to/for sb) (especially BrE)</td><td>禁止入内；不准进入</td><td>The staff kitchen is out of bounds to visitors during the day.<br>白天员工厨房不许访客进入。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌoff ˈlimits (AmE)</td><td>禁止入内的；不准接近的</td><td>The old quarry is off limits to anyone without a permit.<br>没有许可证的人不得进入这座旧采石场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bow</b></td><td>bow and ˈscrape (disapproving)</td><td>卑躬屈膝；点头哈腰</td><td>I refuse to bow and scrape just to keep this contract.<br>我才不愿为保住这份合同而卑躬屈膝。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>boy</b></td><td>a ˈmummy's/ˈmother's boy (BrE, disapproving)</td><td>离不开母亲的男孩（或男人）</td><td>At thirty he's still a mummy's boy who phones her daily.<br>三十岁了他还是个妈宝男，天天给他妈打电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈmama's boy (AmE, disapproving)</td><td>妈宝男；离不开母亲的男人</td><td>Her new boyfriend is a total mama's boy, and everyone notices.<br>她新男友完全是个妈宝男，谁都看得出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>boys</b></td><td>the ˌboys in ˈblue (informal, humorous)</td><td>警察</td><td>The boys in blue turned up ten minutes after we called.<br>我们报警十分钟后警察就到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌboys will be ˈboys (saying)</td><td>男孩终归是男孩</td><td>They came home covered in mud again — boys will be boys.<br>他们又浑身是泥地回来了，男孩就是男孩。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>brain</b></td><td>the ˈbrain drain</td><td>人才外流</td><td>The brain drain has left the country short of qualified doctors.<br>人才外流让这个国家缺少合格的医生。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>brains</b></td><td>the ˈbrains behind sth</td><td>幕后策划者；智囊</td><td>She was the brains behind the campaign that saved the local library.<br>她是那场拯救社区图书馆运动的幕后策划人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>brave</b></td><td>a ˌbrave new ˈworld (often ironic)</td><td>美好新世界（常含讽刺）</td><td>They promised a brave new world of paperless offices and endless leisure.<br>他们许诺了一个无纸办公、闲暇无限的美好新世界。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put a brave ˈface on sth • put on a brave ˈface</td><td>强装镇定；佯装无事</td><td>She put a brave face on the news and went back to work.<br>她强作镇定地接受了消息，回去继续工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bread</b></td><td>your ˌbread and ˈbutter</td><td>生计；谋生之道</td><td>Wedding photography is my bread and butter; the art shows are extra.<br>婚礼摄影是我的饭碗，办画展只是额外的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>breadline</b></td><td>on the ˈbreadline</td><td>极为贫困；勉强糊口</td><td>Three years of rising bills left the family on the breadline.<br>账单连涨三年，这家人过得极其困窘。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>breadth</b></td><td>a hair's ˈbreadth</td><td>一发之差；极小的距离</td><td>The car missed the cyclist by a hair's breadth this morning.<br>今早那辆车差一根头发丝就撞上骑车人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>break</b></td><td>break your ˈback doing sth/to do sth</td><td>拼命干；全力以赴</td><td>I broke my back getting the garden ready before the guests arrived.<br>客人来之前，我拼了老命把花园收拾好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>break the ˈback of sth</td><td>完成某事最艰难的部分</td><td>We've broken the back of the move; only the books remain.<br>搬家最难的部分已经搞定，只剩书了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>breaking</b></td><td>ˌbreaking and ˈentering</td><td>非法闯入（民宅、店铺）</td><td>He was charged with breaking and entering a shop on Mill Street.<br>他被控非法闯入米尔街的一家商店。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without breaking ˈstride (especially AmE)</td><td>未停下脚步；不间断地</td><td>She answered the question without breaking stride and kept walking to class.<br>她脚步不停地回答了问题，径直走向教室。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>breast</b></td><td>make a clean ˈbreast of sth</td><td>彻底坦白；和盘托出</td><td>He made a clean breast of it and admitted taking the cash.<br>他和盘托出，承认拿了那笔现金。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>breath</b></td><td>a breath of fresh ˈair</td><td>令人耳目一新的人（或事物）</td><td>The new teacher is a breath of fresh air in this school.<br>这位新老师给学校带来一股清新之风。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈbreath back</td><td>喘过气来；歇口气</td><td>Let me sit down and get my breath back after those stairs.<br>爬完那些楼梯，让我坐下喘口气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold your ˈbreath</td><td>屏住呼吸（因紧张或期待）</td><td>We held our breath as the referee walked over to check.<br>裁判走过去查看时，我们都屏住了呼吸。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsay, etc. sth in the same ˈbreath</td><td>同时又说；紧接着又讲</td><td>He praised the plan and criticized the cost in the same breath.<br>他刚夸完这个方案，紧接着又批评成本。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb's ˈbreath away</td><td>令人惊叹；美得让人屏息</td><td>The view from the cliff top simply took my breath away.<br>崖顶的景色让我惊叹得说不出话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under your ˈbreath</td><td>低声地；小声嘀咕地</td><td>He swore under his breath when the printer jammed again.<br>打印机又卡纸时，他低声骂了一句。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>breathe your ˈlast (formal)</td><td>咽气；去世</td><td>The old king breathed his last late that same night.<br>老国王就在那天深夜咽了气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>breathe (new) ˈlife into sth</td><td>给…注入新活力</td><td>The festival breathed new life into the sleepy little seaside town.<br>这个节庆给冷清的海滨小镇注入了新活力。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>brewing</b></td><td>ˌbricks and ˈclicks</td><td>实体与网络并行的经营方式</td><td>The chain went bricks and clicks and doubled its sales last year.<br>这家连锁店线上线下并行，去年销售额翻了一番。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a few, two, etc. ˌbricks short of a ˈload</td><td>（人）不太聪明；缺根筋</td><td>Anyone who parks there is a few bricks short of a load.<br>在那儿停车的人脑子多少有点缺。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a few, two, etc. ˌsandwiches short of a ˈpicnic</td><td>（人）愚蠢；脑子不灵光</td><td>He's a sandwich short of a picnic, but he's kind enough.<br>他脑子不太灵光，人倒是挺善良。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˌbricks without ˈstraw (BrE)</td><td>做无米之炊；无材料强做事</td><td>Without any data we're making bricks without straw in this report.<br>没有数据，写这份报告就是做无米之炊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bridge</b></td><td>bridge the ˈgap</td><td>弥合差距；消除隔阂</td><td>Evening classes help bridge the gap between school and full-time work.<br>夜校有助于弥合学校与全职工作之间的落差。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bridge the ˈgulf (between A and B) (less frequent)</td><td>消除（两方之间的）鸿沟</td><td>Nothing could bridge the gulf between the two sides of the family.<br>什么也弥合不了这个家族两边的鸿沟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>brief</b></td><td>hold no ˈbrief for sb/sth (formal)</td><td>不支持；不袒护</td><td>I hold no brief for the council, but this decision seems fair.<br>我并不袒护市政厅，但这个决定看着还算公道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈbrief</td><td>简言之；简要地说</td><td>In brief, we need more staff and a much bigger budget.<br>简而言之，我们需要更多人手和大得多的预算。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bright</b></td><td>bright and ˈearly</td><td>一大清早</td><td>Be here bright and early tomorrow; the van leaves at six.<br>明天一大早就到，车六点出发。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) bright as a ˈbutton (BrE)</td><td>机灵活泼</td><td>Her little boy is as bright as a button at four.<br>她的小男孩才四岁，机灵得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the bright ˈlights (informal)</td><td>都市的繁华生活</td><td>He left the village for the bright lights of the capital.<br>他离开村子，奔向首都的繁华。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(a) bright ˈspark (BrE, informal, often ironic)</td><td>机灵鬼（常反语指办蠢事者）</td><td>Some bright spark left the freezer door open all weekend.<br>某个“机灵鬼”整个周末都没关冰柜门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˈbright spot</td><td>亮点；令人高兴的方面</td><td>Her recovery was the one bright spot in a dreadful year.<br>她的康复是那个糟糕年头里唯一的亮点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look on the ˈbright side</td><td>看事情积极的一面；保持乐观</td><td>Look on the bright side: the rain means we can skip watering.<br>往好处想，下雨了我们就不用浇水了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bright-eyed</b></td><td>ˌbright-eyed and ˌbushy-ˈtailed (informal)</td><td>精神抖擞；兴致勃勃</td><td>She arrived bright-eyed and bushy-tailed after only four hours' sleep.<br>她只睡了四小时，来时却精神抖擞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>broad</b></td><td>a broad ˈchurch (BrE)</td><td>广纳众议的团体</td><td>Our party is a broad church, so arguments are only natural.<br>我们党内兼容各派，有争论很正常。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in broad ˈdaylight</td><td>光天化日之下</td><td>The bike was stolen in broad daylight outside the police station.<br>自行车是在警局门口光天化日下被偷的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's as ˌbroad as it's ˈlong (old-fashioned, BrE, spoken)</td><td>两种选择都一样</td><td>Bus or train, it's as broad as it's long at this hour.<br>这个点儿坐公交还是坐火车都一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>broke</b></td><td>go for ˈbroke (informal)</td><td>孤注一掷；全力一搏</td><td>With ten minutes left they went for broke and pushed everyone forward.<br>还剩十分钟，他们孤注一掷，全线压上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if it ain't ˈbroke, don't ˈfix it</td><td>没坏就别修；好用就别改</td><td>The old system works fine; if it ain't broke, don't fix it.<br>旧系统好好的，没坏就别瞎改。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>brownie</b></td><td>ˈbrownie points</td><td>（讨好上级挣得的）好印象</td><td>He washed everyone's mugs to earn a few brownie points.<br>他给大家洗杯子，是想挣点好印象。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>buck</b></td><td>the buck stops ˈhere</td><td>责任到此为止；责无旁贷</td><td>I'm the head teacher here, so the buck stops here.<br>我是这里的校长，出了事责任在我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>buck up your ˈideas • buck your ˈideas up</td><td>振作起来；打起精神</td><td>You'd better buck your ideas up before the inspection next week.<br>下周检查之前，你最好打起精神来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a fast/quick ˈbuck (informal, often disapproving)</td><td>赚快钱；捞一笔</td><td>He's just trying to make a quick buck off the tourists.<br>他只不过想从游客身上赚点快钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Buckley's</b></td><td>have ˈBuckley's (chance) (AustralE, New Zealand, informal)</td><td>毫无机会；希望渺茫</td><td>You've got Buckley's chance of getting tickets the day before.<br>提前一天才想买票，你根本没戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>buff</b></td><td>in the ˈbuff (informal)</td><td>一丝不挂；赤身裸体</td><td>He answered the door in the buff and horrified the poor postman.<br>他光着身子去开门，把邮递员吓坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bug</b></td><td>be bitten by/have the ˈbug (informal)</td><td>突然迷上；着了迷</td><td>Since that trip she's been bitten by the travel bug.<br>自那次旅行以后，她就迷上了到处跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bug ˈoff! (AmE, spoken)</td><td>走开；别烦我</td><td>Bug off and let me finish this crossword in peace.<br>走开，让我安安静静把这填字游戏做完。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>buggers</b></td><td>play silly ˈbuggers (with sth) (BrE, slang)</td><td>胡闹；瞎折腾</td><td>Stop playing silly buggers with the thermostat and just leave it.<br>别瞎摆弄温控器了，就那么放着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>build</b></td><td>build ˈbridges (between A and B/with sb)</td><td>搭建沟通桥梁；改善关系</td><td>The visit helped build bridges between the two neighbouring villages.<br>这次走访帮两个邻村搭起了沟通的桥梁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>built</b></td><td>be built like a ˈtank (also be built like a ˌbrick ˈshithouse, slang)</td><td>体格健壮；五大三粗</td><td>The new goalkeeper is built like a tank and fears nothing.<br>新守门员体格壮得像坦克，什么都不怕。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bull</b></td><td>like a ˌbull in a ˈchina shop</td><td>笨手笨脚；莽撞行事</td><td>He went through the negotiations like a bull in a china shop.<br>他在谈判中横冲直撞，全无分寸。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˌbull by the ˈhorns (informal)</td><td>果断迎难而上</td><td>She took the bull by the horns and asked for a raise.<br>她果断出手，开口要求加薪。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bum</b></td><td>a bum ˈsteer (AmE, informal)</td><td>错误的消息（或指点）</td><td>The guy at the desk gave us a bum steer about the ferry.<br>柜台那家伙给我们指错了渡轮的路。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/get the ˌbum's ˈrush (slang, especially AmE)</td><td>把人轰走；被草草打发</td><td>He got the bum's rush from the club well before midnight.<br>他没到半夜就被轰出了俱乐部。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bumper</b></td><td>bumper to ˈbumper</td><td>（车辆）首尾相接，排成长龙</td><td>Traffic was bumper to bumper for six miles on the motorway.<br>高速上车辆首尾相接，堵了六英里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bums on ˈseats (BrE, informal)</td><td>上座率；观众人数</td><td>The theatre needs a famous name to get bums on seats.<br>剧院需要请个名角来拉观众。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈbun in the oven (informal, humorous)</td><td>怀孕了</td><td>Judging by that grin, she's got a bun in the oven.<br>看她那笑容，八成是有了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>burn your ˈbridges (BrE also burn your ˈboats)</td><td>自断退路；破釜沉舟</td><td>Don't burn your bridges with that firm; you may need them later.<br>别跟那家公司把关系闹死，以后可能还用得着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>burn the candle at both ˈends</td><td>起早贪黑；过度耗费精力</td><td>She's burning the candle at both ends, working days and studying nights.<br>她白天上班晚上读书，简直是在透支自己。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>burn the midnight ˈoil</td><td>熬夜苦干；开夜车</td><td>We burned the midnight oil to get the proposal in on time.<br>为了按时交上方案，我们熬了通宵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>burn sth to a ˈcinder/ˈcrisp</td><td>把…烧焦；烤糊</td><td>I forgot the toast and burned it to a crisp again.<br>我忘了烤面包，又给烤成了炭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>burner</b></td><td>on the back ˈburner (informal)</td><td>暂缓处理；搁置一旁</td><td>The kitchen extension is on the back burner until next spring.<br>厨房扩建的事要搁到明年春天再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>burning</b></td><td>his, her, etc. ˈears are burning</td><td>感觉有人在背后议论自己</td><td>My ears were burning all evening; I knew they were gossiping.<br>我整晚都觉得耳朵发烫，知道他们在议论我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>burnt</b></td><td>get your ˈfingers burnt/burned</td><td>吃亏；栽跟头</td><td>He got his fingers burnt investing in that friend's little café.<br>他投资朋友的小咖啡馆，结果栽了跟头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>burst</b></td><td>ˌburst a ˈblood vessel (informal)</td><td>大发雷霆；气得要命</td><td>Calm down before you burst a blood vessel over a parking ticket.<br>为张罚单别气坏了身子，冷静点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌburst sb's ˈbubble</td><td>打破某人的美梦；泼冷水</td><td>I hate to burst your bubble, but the tickets sold out yesterday.<br>我不想扫你的兴，可票昨天就卖完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌburst ˈopen • ˌburst (sth) ˈopen</td><td>（使）猛然打开</td><td>The cupboard door burst open and tins rolled across the kitchen floor.<br>柜门猛地弹开，罐头滚了一地。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bursting</b></td><td>be bursting to do sth (informal)</td><td>迫不及待想做某事</td><td>She was bursting to tell someone about the new job offer.<br>她迫不及待想把新工作的事告诉别人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'm ˈbursting (BrE, informal)</td><td>我快憋不住了（要上厕所）</td><td>Stop at the next services — I'm bursting and it's getting urgent.<br>下个服务区停一下，我实在憋不住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bury</b></td><td>ˌbury the ˈhatchet • ˌbury your ˈdifferences</td><td>捐弃前嫌；言归于好</td><td>The brothers finally buried the hatchet at their mother's birthday dinner.<br>兄弟俩终于在母亲的生日宴上冰释前嫌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bush</b></td><td>ˌbush ˈtelegraph</td><td>小道消息的传播；口耳相传</td><td>News of the closure spread by bush telegraph before any official announcement.<br>停业的消息还没正式公布就已口耳相传开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>business</b></td><td>be (back) in ˈbusiness</td><td>（恢复）正常运转</td><td>The generator's fixed, so we're back in business by lunchtime.<br>发电机修好了，午饭前我们就恢复运转了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be none of sb's ˈbusiness • be no business of sb's</td><td>不关某人的事</td><td>How much I paid for the ring is none of your business.<br>这戒指我花多少钱买的不关你的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈbusiness end (of sth) (informal)</td><td>（工具、武器）起作用的一端</td><td>Never point the business end of a drill at anyone, ever.<br>千万别把电钻的钻头对着人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>business is ˈbusiness</td><td>公事公办；生意归生意</td><td>I like him, but business is business and his quote is too high.<br>我挺喜欢他，可生意归生意，他报价太高。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get down to ˈbusiness</td><td>言归正传；着手办正事</td><td>Right, the coffee's finished, so let's get down to business.<br>好了，咖啡喝完了，咱们说正事吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go about your ˈbusiness</td><td>忙自己的事；照常做事</td><td>The market traders went about their business as if nothing had happened.<br>市场里的摊贩照常忙活，好像什么都没发生。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have no business doing sth/to do sth</td><td>无权做某事；不该做某事</td><td>You had no business reading my letters while I was away.<br>我不在的时候你没资格看我的信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's business as ˈusual</td><td>一切照常；照常营业</td><td>Despite the flood damage, it's business as usual at the bakery.<br>尽管遭了水灾，面包店照常营业。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like ˈnobody's business (informal)</td><td>飞快地；厉害得很</td><td>That old dog of theirs can still run like nobody's business.<br>他们那条老狗跑起来还是快得不得了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be in the business of doing sth</td><td>无意做某事；不做那种事</td><td>We're not in the business of giving refunds after six months.<br>我们不做六个月后还退款这种事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of ˈbusiness</td><td>停业；倒闭</td><td>Two more shops on this street went out of business last month.<br>这条街上个月又有两家店倒闭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>busman's</b></td><td>a busman's ˈholiday (informal)</td><td>照常干本行的假日</td><td>A chef cooking at a friend's wedding is a real busman's holiday.<br>厨师去朋友婚礼上掌勺，真是休假不离本行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bust</b></td><td>bust sb's ˈchops (AmE, rather old-fashioned, slang)</td><td>痛斥；数落；找碴儿</td><td>Quit busting my chops about the dishes; I'll do them later.<br>别老唠叨洗碗的事，我一会儿就洗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bust a ˈgut (informal)</td><td>拼尽全力（做某事）</td><td>Don't bust a gut trying to finish the whole thing tonight.<br>别拼了命想今晚就全干完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈbust (informal)</td><td>（企业）破产，倒闭</td><td>The travel agency went bust and left hundreds of people stranded.<br>那家旅行社倒闭了，几百人滞留在外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>or ˈbust (informal)</td><td>不成功便成仁；豁出去了</td><td>It's the coast by Friday or bust, whatever the weather does.<br>不管天气怎样，周五必须赶到海边。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>break sb's ˈballs (slang)</td><td>折磨某人；死命催逼</td><td>The sergeant broke our balls for three solid months of training.<br>那个中士在整整三个月训练里把我们往死里操。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>busy</b></td><td>(as) busy as a ˈbee</td><td>忙得团团转</td><td>Gran's been as busy as a bee getting the house ready.<br>奶奶为收拾房子忙得像只蜜蜂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌbusy ˈbee (informal)</td><td>大忙人；闲不住的人</td><td>You're a busy bee this morning, up before six again.<br>你今早可真忙，六点前又起来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep yourself ˈbusy</td><td>让自己有事可做；不让自己闲着</td><td>Since retiring he keeps himself busy with the allotment and the choir.<br>退休后他侍弄菜地、参加合唱，让自己不闲着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>butt</b></td><td>be the butt of sth</td><td>成为嘲弄（或批评）的对象</td><td>He was the butt of every joke at the office party.<br>在公司聚会上，他成了所有玩笑的靶子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>butter</b></td><td>ˌbutter wouldn't ˈmelt (in sb's ˈmouth)</td><td>装出一副天真无辜的样子</td><td>She looks as if butter wouldn't melt in her mouth.<br>她看上去一副天真无辜的样子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your ˌbread and ˈbutter</td><td>饭碗；主要收入来源</td><td>Repair work is our bread and butter; the new builds are bonuses.<br>维修活儿是我们的饭碗，新建项目算是额外收入。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>butterflies</b></td><td>get/have ˈbutterflies (in your stomach)</td><td>心里紧张；七上八下</td><td>I get butterflies in my stomach before every parents' evening.<br>每次家长会前我心里都七上八下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>button</b></td><td>ˈbutton it! (BrE, spoken)</td><td>闭嘴；住口</td><td>Button it, both of you — the baby has only just gone down.<br>你俩闭嘴，宝宝刚睡着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈbutton (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>准时；分毫不差</td><td>The train arrived at nine on the button for once.<br>火车难得一回九点整准时到站。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>buy</b></td><td>buy the ˈfarm (informal, humorous, especially AmE)</td><td>死；丧命</td><td>He nearly bought the farm when the ladder slipped last summer.<br>去年夏天梯子一滑，他差点没命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>buy ˈtime</td><td>拖延时间；争取时间</td><td>Asking for more figures was just a way to buy time.<br>要更多数据不过是拖延时间的手段。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sell sb/buy a ˈpup (BrE, informal)</td><td>卖（或买）到无用之物；上当</td><td>I bought a pup with that car; it has broken down twice.<br>那辆车我买亏了，都抛锚两次了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>buzz</b></td><td>give sb a ˈbuzz (informal)</td><td>给某人打电话</td><td>Give me a buzz when you get home from the airport.<br>你从机场到家后给我打个电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>caboodle</b></td><td>the ˌwhole caˈboodle</td><td>全部；一整套</td><td>He sold the boat, the trailer, the whole caboodle, in one weekend.<br>一个周末他把船、拖车，全套家当都卖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌwhole kit and caˈboodle</td><td>全部家当；所有的东西</td><td>They packed the whole kit and caboodle into one small van.<br>他们把全部家当塞进了一辆小货车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cackle</b></td><td>cut the ˈcackle (informal)</td><td>别闲扯了；言归正传</td><td>Let's cut the cackle and decide who is driving tonight.<br>别闲扯了，定一下今晚谁开车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cahoots</b></td><td>be in caˈhoots (with sb) (informal)</td><td>与某人勾结；串通一气</td><td>The guard was in cahoots with the thieves the whole time.<br>那个保安一直和窃贼串通一气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cake</b></td><td>have your cake and ˈeat it (BrE)</td><td>又要马儿跑又要马儿不吃草</td><td>You can't have your cake and eat it — choose one job.<br>你不能又要这个又要那个，选一份工作吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a share/slice of the ˈcake (BrE) (AmE a piece/share/slice of the ˈpie)</td><td>分得的一份好处；应得的一份利益</td><td>Local firms all want a slice of the cake now that the new port is open.<br>新港口一开，本地企业都想分一杯羹。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>call</b></td><td>beyond the call of ˈduty (formal)</td><td>超出职责要求；分外尽力</td><td>Staying all night to finish the report went far beyond the call of duty.<br>熬通宵写完报告，这远远超出了本职要求。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call sb's ˈbluff</td><td>要求某人摊牌；逼某人兑现威胁</td><td>She threatened to quit, so I called her bluff and handed her a resignation form.<br>她扬言要辞职，我就把辞职表递过去逼她摊牌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call a ˈhalt (to sth)</td><td>叫停；终止（某活动）</td><td>The referee called a halt to the match when the rain got too heavy.<br>雨下得太大，裁判叫停了比赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call it a ˈday (informal)</td><td>收工；到此为止</td><td>We've been painting since dawn, so let's call it a day and grab a beer.<br>我们从天亮就在刷漆，今天就到这儿吧，去喝杯啤酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call it ˈquits (informal)</td><td>同意就此罢手；两清</td><td>You paid for dinner and I paid for the taxi, so let's call it quits.<br>你请了饭我付了车钱，就算两清吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call sb ˈnames</td><td>辱骂；谩骂</td><td>He got detention for calling the new boy names during the lunch break.<br>他午休时辱骂新来的男生，被罚留校。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call sth your ˈown</td><td>拥有；可称之为自己的</td><td>After ten years of renting, they finally have a small flat to call their own.<br>租了十年房，他们终于有了一套属于自己的小公寓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call the ˈshots/the ˈtune (informal)</td><td>发号施令；说了算</td><td>Now that Dad's retired, my sister calls the shots in the family business.<br>爸爸退休后，家里的生意由我姐姐说了算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call a ˌspade a ˈspade</td><td>直言不讳；有啥说啥</td><td>Let's call a spade a spade: the plan failed because nobody bothered to test it.<br>说白了吧，计划失败是因为根本没人去测试。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call sb to acˈcount (for/over sth) (formal)</td><td>责成某人解释；追究某人责任</td><td>The minister was called to account for the missing funds at yesterday's hearing.<br>昨天的听证会上，部长被要求就资金去向作出交代。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call yourself a ˈteacher, a ˈfriend, etc.? (informal)</td><td>你也配称作教师（朋友等）</td><td>You call yourself a friend? You didn't even answer the phone when I needed help.<br>你也配叫朋友？我需要帮忙时你连电话都不接。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>call yourself a ˈmusician? (informal)</td><td>你也好意思自称音乐家</td><td>How can he call himself a musician when he's never even heard of Schubert?<br>他连舒伯特都没听说过，怎么好意思自称音乐家？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>candle</b></td><td>cannot hold a candle to sb/sth (informal)</td><td>远远比不上；无法与…相媲美</td><td>Her new album is fine, but it cannot hold a candle to her first one.<br>她的新专辑还行，但跟第一张比差远了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>candy</b></td><td>be like taking ˌcandy from a ˈbaby (also be like shooting ˌfish in a ˈbarrel)</td><td>极其容易；易如反掌</td><td>Beating that team was like taking candy from a baby—we won by four goals.<br>赢那支球队易如反掌，我们净胜四球。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cannon</b></td><td>ˈcannon fodder</td><td>炮灰</td><td>The general treated the new recruits as little more than cannon fodder.<br>那位将军把新兵不过当成炮灰。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cap</b></td><td>go cap in ˈhand (to sb) (BrE) (AmE go hat in ˈhand)</td><td>低声下气地求人；恭敬讨要</td><td>He had to go cap in hand to his father for next month's rent.<br>他只好低声下气地找父亲要下个月的房租。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if the cap fits (, wear it) (BrE) (AmE if the shoe fits (, wear it)) (saying)</td><td>说得对就接受；有则改之</td><td>I never said you were lazy, but if the cap fits, wear it.<br>我可没说你懒，不过要是说中了就认了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a feather in your ˈcap</td><td>值得骄傲的成就；荣誉</td><td>Winning that contract was a real feather in her cap at such a young age.<br>这么年轻就拿下那份合同，实在是她的一大荣耀。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>capital</b></td><td>make ˈcapital of/out of sth</td><td>利用…捞取好处</td><td>The opposition made capital out of the minister's clumsy remarks about teachers.<br>反对党拿部长关于教师的失言大做文章。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with a capital ˈA, ˈB, ˈC, etc.</td><td>（强调）真正的；不折不扣的</td><td>He's lazy with a capital L—he hasn't washed a dish all week.<br>他懒得出奇，一整周连个碗都没洗过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>captain</b></td><td>a captain of ˈindustry</td><td>实业巨头；工商界领袖</td><td>The dinner was full of captains of industry swapping stories about the new tax.<br>晚宴上满是工商界巨头，都在议论新税。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>carbon</b></td><td>a ˌcarbon ˈcopy</td><td>极其相似的人（或物）；翻版</td><td>Their second album is a carbon copy of the first, right down to the artwork.<br>他们的第二张专辑简直是第一张的翻版，连封面都一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cards</b></td><td>keep/hold/play your cards ˌclose to your ˈchest</td><td>守口如瓶；不露意图</td><td>The manager kept his cards close to his chest until the transfer deadline.<br>转会截止前，主教练一直守口如瓶。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈcards (BrE) (AmE in the ˈcards) (informal)</td><td>很可能发生</td><td>A cabinet reshuffle has been on the cards ever since the election result.<br>自从选举结果出来，内阁改组就一直被看作大有可能。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/lay your ˈcards on the table (informal)</td><td>摊牌；坦白说出想法</td><td>Let's put our cards on the table: how much are you really willing to pay?<br>咱们摊牌吧，你到底愿意出多少钱？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play your ˈcards right (informal)</td><td>行事精明；处理得当</td><td>If you play your cards right, the boss might send you to Tokyo.<br>你要是会来事儿，老板说不定会派你去东京。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>care</b></td><td>ˈcare of sb (AmE also in ˈcare of sb)</td><td>由某人转交</td><td>Send the letter care of my sister; I'll be travelling all next month.<br>信寄给我姐姐转交吧，我下个月一直在外面跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>couldn't care ˈless (informal)</td><td>毫不在乎；才不管呢</td><td>He couldn't care less what the neighbours think about his purple front door.<br>邻居怎么看他那扇紫色大门，他压根不在乎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for all I, you, etc. ˈcare (spoken)</td><td>才不管呢；随他去</td><td>For all I care, he can stay out there in the rain all night.<br>他要愿意在雨里站一夜，我才不管呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈcare (BrE)</td><td>由政府照管；受福利机构监护</td><td>The two boys were taken into care after their mother fell seriously ill.<br>母亲重病后，两个男孩被政府接管照料。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have a ˌcare in the ˈworld</td><td>无忧无虑；无牵无挂</td><td>Lying on the beach, she looked like she didn't have a care in the world.<br>躺在沙滩上的她，看着一副无忧无虑的样子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without a ˌcare in the ˈworld</td><td>无忧无虑地</td><td>The kids ran through the sprinkler without a care in the world all afternoon.<br>孩子们一下午都在洒水器下疯跑，无忧无虑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈcare (that.../to do sth)</td><td>务必小心；注意做到</td><td>Take care to lock the back door when you leave the cottage.<br>离开小屋时务必锁好后门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈcare of yourself/sb/sth</td><td>照顾；照料；处理</td><td>Don't worry about the bills—I'll take care of them while you're away.<br>账单别操心，你不在的时候我来处理。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈtake care (spoken)</td><td>（道别用语）保重</td><td>Take care, and text me as soon as your plane lands in Sydney.<br>保重，飞机一落地悉尼就给我发消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>would you ˈcare for... (formal)</td><td>（客气提议）您要…吗</td><td>Would you care for another slice of cake before I put it away?<br>我收起来之前，您还要再来一块蛋糕吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>would you ˈcare to... (formal)</td><td>（客气邀请）您愿意…吗</td><td>Would you care to join us for dinner at the hotel this evening?<br>今晚您愿意到酒店和我们一起吃饭吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>careful</b></td><td>you can't be too ˈcareful</td><td>越小心越好；再小心也不为过</td><td>Lock your bike even in the yard—you can't be too careful these days.<br>就算在院子里也把车锁上，如今再小心也不为过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cares</b></td><td>who ˈcares? (informal)</td><td>谁在乎呢；管它呢</td><td>So the shirt's a bit creased—who cares? It's only a picnic.<br>衬衫皱一点又怎样？管它呢，不过是去野餐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what do I, you, etc. ˈcare? (informal)</td><td>我（或你等）才不管呢</td><td>What do I care if he's angry? He started the whole argument.<br>他生气关我什么事？这场争吵是他挑起的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>caring</b></td><td>be beyond/past ˈcaring (about sth)</td><td>不再在乎；无所谓了</td><td>After three delays at the airport, I was beyond caring about my luggage.<br>在机场被延误三次后，我已经懒得管行李了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>carpet</b></td><td>be on the ˈcarpet (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>被上司叫去训斥</td><td>He was on the carpet again for missing two deadlines in one week.<br>他一周误了两个期限，又被叫去挨训了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sweep/brush sth under the ˈcarpet (informal)</td><td>掩盖错事；藏着掖着</td><td>The school tried to sweep the bullying complaints under the carpet for years.<br>多年来学校一直想把霸凌投诉压下去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sweep sth under the ˈrug (AmE, informal)</td><td>掩盖问题；遮掩过去</td><td>You can't just sweep the budget shortfall under the rug and hope nobody notices.<br>你不能把预算缺口一藏了之，指望没人发现。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>carried</b></td><td>be/get carried aˈway</td><td>忘乎所以；失去自制</td><td>I got carried away at the sale and spent half my salary on shoes.<br>打折时我一激动，半个月工资全买了鞋。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>carrot</b></td><td>the carrot and/or (the) stick</td><td>胡萝卜加大棒；软硬兼施</td><td>The coach used the carrot and stick approach to get everyone training again.<br>教练软硬兼施，让大家重新开始训练。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>carry</b></td><td>carry all beˈfore you</td><td>所向披靡；大获全胜</td><td>The young team carried all before them and won the league by ten points.<br>这支年轻队伍所向披靡，以十分优势夺冠。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>carry the ˈball (AmE, informal)</td><td>挑大梁；承担主要责任</td><td>With the director away, Maria carried the ball on the whole marketing launch.<br>总监不在，整个营销发布由玛丽亚挑大梁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>carry the ˈcan (for sb/sth) (BrE, informal)</td><td>代人受过；背黑锅</td><td>As usual, the junior staff carried the can for their manager's bad decision.<br>和往常一样，经理决策失误却由基层员工背黑锅。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pass the ˈbuck (to sb) (informal)</td><td>推卸责任；把责任推给别人</td><td>Stop passing the buck and admit that the mistake was yours from the start.<br>别再推卸责任了，承认这错从一开始就是你的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>carry a ˈtorch for sb</td><td>暗恋某人；单相思</td><td>He's carried a torch for her since university, but he's never said a word.<br>他从大学起就暗恋她，却始终没开过口。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>carry ˈweight</td><td>有分量；有影响力</td><td>Her opinion carries a lot of weight with the hiring committee this year.<br>今年招聘委员会很看重她的意见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cart</b></td><td>put the ˌcart before the ˈhorse</td><td>本末倒置；顺序颠倒</td><td>Buying furniture before you've found a flat is putting the cart before the horse.<br>房子还没找到就先买家具，这是本末倒置。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>carte</b></td><td>ˌcarte ˈblanche (to do sth) (from French)</td><td>全权；自由处理权</td><td>The new chef was given carte blanche to redesign the entire dinner menu.<br>新主厨获得全权，可以重新设计整个晚餐菜单。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>carved</b></td><td>be carved/set in ˈstone</td><td>一成不变；板上钉钉</td><td>The schedule isn't carved in stone, so tell me if Friday doesn't work.<br>日程不是定死的，周五不行你就说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>case</b></td><td>as the ˌcase may ˈbe</td><td>视具体情况而定</td><td>You'll be fined or simply warned, as the case may be, after the review.<br>复核之后，视情况你会被罚款或只是被警告。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be on sb's ˈcase (informal)</td><td>不停地数落某人；纠缠某人</td><td>My mother's been on my case about finding a job since I graduated.<br>自打毕业，我妈就一直催我找工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be on the ˈcase</td><td>正在处理此事</td><td>Don't worry about the leak—the plumber is on the case already.<br>漏水的事别担心，水管工已经在处理了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a case in ˈpoint</td><td>恰当的例子；明证</td><td>Cheap flights harm small airports, and this closed runway is a case in point.<br>廉价航班伤害小机场，这条关闭的跑道就是明证。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>case the ˈjoint (informal)</td><td>（为行窃）踩点探路</td><td>The police think the two men were casing the joint before the robbery.<br>警方认为这两人在抢劫前先去踩了点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get off sb's ˈcase (informal)</td><td>别再唠叨某人；别再挑剔</td><td>Get off my case—I said I'd wash the car on Sunday.<br>别念叨我了，我说了周日会洗车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈany case</td><td>无论如何；反正</td><td>It's raining, and in any case the museum closes at four on Mondays.<br>在下雨，再说周一博物馆四点就关门了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) in ˈcase</td><td>以防万一</td><td>Take an umbrella just in case the weather turns while you're out walking.<br>带把伞，以防你散步时天气变脸。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈthat case</td><td>既然那样；如果那样的话</td><td>You've already booked the tickets? In that case, I'll cancel my other plans.<br>你已经订好票了？那我就把别的安排取消。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈthat case (spoken)</td><td>既然如此；那样的话</td><td>I've already made up my mind. In that case, there's no point discussing it further.<br>我已经拿定主意了。既然如此，再讨论也没意义。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make out a ˈcase (for sth)</td><td>提出理由支持；据理论证</td><td>She made out a strong case for hiring two more nurses this year.<br>她有力地论证了今年应再招两名护士。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cash</b></td><td>cash ˈdown (BrE) (also ˌcash up ˈfront AmE, BrE)</td><td>现款支付；即期付清</td><td>The dealer wanted cash down before he'd hand over the keys to the van.<br>车商要求先付现款才交出货车钥匙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cash in your ˈchips (especially AmE)</td><td>兑换筹码收手；抽身退出</td><td>After thirty years in the trade, he cashed in his chips and moved abroad.<br>干了三十年这行，他收手不干，搬到了国外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cash on the ˈbarrelhead (AmE)</td><td>（购物时）现金付讫</td><td>The farmer sells his hay cash on the barrelhead—no cheques, no credit.<br>这农户卖干草只收现金，不收支票也不赊账。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cast</b></td><td>cast/run an ˈeye/your ˈeyes over sth</td><td>扫一眼；粗略看一下</td><td>Could you cast an eye over my essay before I send it to the tutor?<br>我交给导师之前，你能帮我扫一眼论文吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cast your ˈmind back to sth</td><td>回想；追忆</td><td>Cast your mind back to that summer we spent fixing up the old boat.<br>回想一下我们修那条旧船的那个夏天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cast ˌpearls before ˈswine (saying)</td><td>明珠暗投；对牛弹琴</td><td>Serving him vintage wine is casting pearls before swine; he adds lemonade.<br>给他喝年份酒纯属对牛弹琴，他还要兑汽水。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>casting</b></td><td>the ˈcasting couch (informal, humorous)</td><td>以性交易换取角色</td><td>She spoke out about the casting couch long before anyone else dared to.<br>早在别人不敢开口时，她就揭露了选角潜规则。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>castles</b></td><td>(build) ˌcastles in the ˈair</td><td>空中楼阁；白日梦</td><td>Stop building castles in the air and send out a few real job applications.<br>别做白日梦了，实实在在投几份简历吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cat</b></td><td>(play) cat and ˈmouse (with sb) (informal)</td><td>猫捉老鼠般戏弄；欲擒故纵</td><td>The detective played cat and mouse with the suspect for nearly two hours.<br>警探同嫌疑人玩了近两个小时的猫鼠游戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the cat's ˈwhiskers/pyjamas (informal, often ironic)</td><td>顶呱呱的人（或物）</td><td>In his new leather jacket he thinks he's the cat's whiskers.<br>穿上那件新皮夹克，他觉得自己帅得没边了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let the ˈcat out of the bag (informal)</td><td>（无意中）泄露秘密</td><td>Dad let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party before Saturday.<br>周六还没到，爸爸就把惊喜派对的事说漏了嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(look) like sth the ˈcat brought/dragged in</td><td>看上去邋遢不堪</td><td>You look like something the cat dragged in—did you sleep in that shirt?<br>你这一身狼狈样，是穿着那件衬衫睡的吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like a ˌcat on hot ˈbricks (BrE, informal)</td><td>如坐针毡；坐立不安</td><td>She was like a cat on hot bricks waiting for her exam results.<br>等考试成绩时，她急得如坐针毡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like a ˌcat on a hot tin ˈroof (AmE, informal)</td><td>焦躁不安；像热锅上的蚂蚁</td><td>He paced the corridor like a cat on a hot tin roof all morning.<br>他一上午都在走廊里踱步，像热锅上的蚂蚁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like the ˌcat that got, stole, etc. the ˈcream</td><td>洋洋得意；沾沾自喜</td><td>She walked in grinning like the cat that got the cream after her promotion.<br>升职后她笑着进来，一脸得意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have a cat in ˈhell's chance (also not have a ˈdog's chance) (informal)</td><td>毫无机会；一点希望也没有</td><td>Without a passport you don't have a cat in hell's chance of boarding.<br>没有护照，你根本别想登机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>when the cat's aˈway the mice will ˈplay (saying)</td><td>猫儿不在，鼠儿造反</td><td>The teacher stepped out and chaos erupted: when the cat's away the mice will play.<br>老师一出门就乱成一锅粥，真是猫儿不在鼠儿造反。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch</b></td><td>catch your ˈdeath (of cold) (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>得重感冒</td><td>Put a coat on or you'll catch your death out there in the wind.<br>穿上外套，不然在外头吹风会感冒得厉害。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch sb's ˈeye</td><td>引起某人注意；吸引某人目光</td><td>A red dress in the window caught my eye as we walked past.<br>路过时，橱窗里一条红裙子吸引了我的目光。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch sb in the ˈact (of doing sth)</td><td>当场抓住；抓个正着</td><td>The guard caught him in the act of slipping a watch into his pocket.<br>保安当场抓住他正把一块表塞进口袋。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈcatch it (BrE) (AmE catch ˈhell, ˈget it) (spoken)</td><td>挨骂；受罚</td><td>You'll catch it from Mum when she sees the mess in the kitchen.<br>妈妈看到厨房这么乱，你可要挨骂了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch sb ˈnapping (informal)</td><td>使人措手不及；趁人不备</td><td>The defence was caught napping and conceded a goal in the first minute.<br>后防线一时松懈，开场一分钟就丢了球。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch sb off (their) guard</td><td>趁某人不备；使措手不及</td><td>The question about her divorce caught her off guard during the live interview.<br>直播采访中关于离婚的提问让她措手不及。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch sb on the ˈhop (BrE, informal)</td><td>使某人措手不及；出其不意</td><td>The early inspection caught the whole kitchen staff on the hop.<br>提前到来的检查让整个后厨措手不及。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch some ˈrays (especially AmE, slang)</td><td>晒太阳</td><td>We're heading to the roof to catch some rays before the clouds roll in.<br>云还没上来，我们去屋顶晒会儿太阳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch the ˈsun</td><td>晒黑；晒伤</td><td>You've caught the sun on your shoulders—they're already bright pink.<br>你肩膀晒着了，都红得发亮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch sb with their ˈpants down (informal)</td><td>使人措手不及；当场撞破</td><td>The surprise audit caught the whole department with their pants down.<br>突击审计打了整个部门一个措手不及。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch sb with their ˈtrousers down (BrE, informal)</td><td>出其不意抓个正着；冷不防</td><td>The reporters caught the minister with his trousers down over the missing files.<br>记者就失踪文件一事把部长打了个措手不及。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catches</b></td><td>the early ˈbird catches the ˈworm (saying)</td><td>早起的鸟儿有虫吃；捷足先登</td><td>Get to the market at six, because the early bird catches the worm.<br>六点就去市场，早起的鸟儿才有虫吃。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play ˈcatch-up</td><td>奋起直追；拼命赶超</td><td>After a slow first quarter, the company has been playing catch-up all year.<br>第一季度开局不利，公司一整年都在追赶。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>caught</b></td><td>be caught in the ˈcrossfire</td><td>殃及池鱼；卷入争斗受害</td><td>Junior staff got caught in the crossfire when the two directors started arguing.<br>两位总监一吵起来，基层员工就跟着遭殃。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wouldn't be seen/caught ˈdead (in/with/at sth) (informal)</td><td>打死也不会（穿、去等）</td><td>He wouldn't be caught dead in a suit, not even at his own wedding.<br>他打死也不肯穿西装，连自己婚礼上都不穿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cause</b></td><td>be (all) for/in a good ˈcause</td><td>是为做好事；有意义</td><td>The run was exhausting, but it was all in a good cause for the hospice.<br>跑得筋疲力尽，但都是为了给临终关怀院做善事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a lost ˈcause</td><td>注定失败的事；没指望的人</td><td>Persuading Dad to use a smartphone is a lost cause at this point.<br>到这份上，劝我爸用智能手机已经没戏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>caution</b></td><td>throw caution to the ˈwind(s) (often humorous)</td><td>不顾一切；放胆行事</td><td>She threw caution to the wind and booked a one-way ticket to Lisbon.<br>她一狠心，订了张飞里斯本的单程票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cent</b></td><td>be the ˌcentre of atˈtention (BrE) (AmE be the ˌcenter of atˈtention)</td><td>成为众人瞩目的焦点</td><td>At every party my little brother has to be the centre of attention.<br>每次聚会我弟弟都非得当全场焦点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>century</b></td><td>the ˌturn of the ˈcentury/ˈyear</td><td>世纪之交；年头岁尾</td><td>The house was built around the turn of the century by a local shipbuilder.<br>这房子约在世纪之交由本地造船匠建造。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ceremony</b></td><td>stand on ˈceremony (BrE)</td><td>讲究礼节；拘礼</td><td>Don't stand on ceremony—grab a plate and help yourself to the food.<br>别客气，拿个盘子自己动手吃吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without ˈceremony</td><td>不拘礼节地；随随便便地</td><td>He dropped the box on my desk without ceremony and walked straight out.<br>他随手把箱子往我桌上一放就走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>certain</b></td><td>for ˈcertain</td><td>确切地；肯定地</td><td>Nobody knows for certain why the factory closed so suddenly last winter.<br>去年冬天工厂为何突然关门，谁也说不准。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈcertain (that...)</td><td>弄清楚；查明</td><td>Make certain that the windows are shut before you set the alarm.<br>设警报前先确认窗户都关好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make certain of sth/of doing sth</td><td>确保（某事发生）</td><td>Book early to make certain of a seat on the last train home.<br>早点订票，确保回家末班车有座位。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>any</b></td><td>by ˈany chance</td><td>（询问时用）或许；有没有可能</td><td>Do you have a spare charger by any chance? Mine died this morning.<br>你身上碰巧有多余的充电器吗？我的今早没电了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chances</b></td><td>(the) chances ˈare (that) (informal)</td><td>很可能</td><td>Chances are that the shop is shut by now, so try again tomorrow.<br>这会儿店多半关门了，明天再去吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈchances</td><td>冒险；碰运气</td><td>I don't take chances with ice on the road; I just stay home.<br>路上结冰我从不冒险，干脆待在家里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take your ˈchances (informal)</td><td>抓住机会；碰碰运气</td><td>There's no guarantee of a refund, but you can take your chances at the desk.<br>不保证能退款，不过你可以去柜台碰碰运气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>change</b></td><td>change ˈhands</td><td>易主；转手</td><td>The pub has changed hands three times since we moved to the village.<br>自从我们搬到村里，这家酒馆已经转手三次了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>change your ˈmind</td><td>改变主意</td><td>She changed her mind about the job the night before she was due to start.<br>上班前一晚，她改主意不去那份工作了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌchange of ˈheart</td><td>态度转变；改变看法</td><td>He had a change of heart and let his son keep the stray dog.<br>他转了念头，让儿子留下那只流浪狗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>change the ˈsubject</td><td>转换话题</td><td>Every time I mention money, he changes the subject to the weather.<br>我一提钱，他就把话题扯到天气上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>change your ˈtune (informal)</td><td>改变态度；改口</td><td>You'll change your tune when you see how much the repairs actually cost.<br>等你看到维修真要多少钱，就会改口了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>change your ˈways</td><td>改变生活方式；改过</td><td>The doctor told him to change his ways or expect another heart attack.<br>医生让他改改生活方式，否则还会再犯心脏病。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for a ˈchange</td><td>换换花样；改变一下</td><td>Let's walk to work for a change instead of squeezing onto the bus.<br>换个花样走路上班吧，别再挤公交了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get no ˈchange out of sb (BrE, informal)</td><td>从某人处得不到帮助（或消息）</td><td>You'll get no change out of the landlord about the broken heating.<br>暖气坏了的事，你从房东那儿问不出什么来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a wind/the winds of ˈchange</td><td>变革之风；变化的征兆</td><td>A wind of change is blowing through the department since the new director arrived.<br>新总监到任后，部门里刮起了一阵变革之风。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chapter</b></td><td>ˌchapter and ˈverse</td><td>详细出处；确切依据</td><td>He can quote chapter and verse on every rule in the tenancy agreement.<br>租约里的每条规定他都能说出确切出处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌchapter of ˈaccidents</td><td>接二连三的不幸；祸不单行</td><td>The trip was a chapter of accidents: lost bags, food poisoning and a strike.<br>这趟旅行祸不单行：丢行李、食物中毒，还赶上罢工。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>character</b></td><td>ˌin/ˌout of ˈcharacter</td><td>符合（或不符合）某人性格</td><td>Shouting at a waiter is completely out of character for my gentle uncle.<br>冲服务员大喊大叫，完全不像我那温和的叔叔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get a ˈcharge out of sth (AmE)</td><td>从…中获得乐趣</td><td>My grandmother gets a real charge out of beating us all at cards.<br>我奶奶打牌赢我们所有人，觉得特别过瘾。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈcharge (of sth)</td><td>接管；开始负责</td><td>When the manager fell ill, Priya took charge of the whole project.<br>经理病倒后，普里娅接管了整个项目。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>charity begins at ˈhome (saying)</td><td>仁爱始于家庭；先顾自家人</td><td>Before donating abroad, remember that charity begins at home.<br>往国外捐款前，别忘了行善要先从家里做起。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>charm</b></td><td>work like a ˈcharm (informal)</td><td>非常奏效；很灵验</td><td>A spoonful of honey worked like a charm on my sore throat.<br>一勺蜂蜜治我的嗓子疼特别灵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>charmed</b></td><td>lead/have a charmed ˈlife</td><td>总是好运；如有神助</td><td>He's walked away from two crashes, so the man leads a charmed life.<br>两次车祸他都毫发无伤，这人真是命大。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>charts</b></td><td>off the ˈcharts</td><td>高得离谱；超出正常范围</td><td>Ticket demand for the reunion tour has been off the charts all week.<br>重组巡演的票务需求这一周高得离谱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chase</b></td><td>chase your (own) ˈtail</td><td>瞎忙活；徒劳无功</td><td>I spent all morning chasing my own tail between three different offices.<br>我一上午在三个办公室之间瞎跑，一无所获。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈtail-chasing</td><td>瞎忙；徒劳的奔忙</td><td>After a week of pure tail-chasing, we finally got a straight answer.<br>瞎折腾了一星期，我们总算得到一个明确答复。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cheap</b></td><td>be going ˈcheap (informal)</td><td>廉价出售；降价卖</td><td>These strawberries are going cheap because the market closes in ten minutes.<br>这些草莓在贱卖，因为市场十分钟后就收摊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cheap and ˈcheerful (informal)</td><td>物美价廉；便宜实惠</td><td>It's a cheap and cheerful little diner, but the breakfasts are excellent.<br>这是家便宜实惠的小餐馆，早餐特别棒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cheap and ˈnasty (informal)</td><td>质劣价廉；便宜没好货</td><td>The souvenirs were cheap and nasty, so I bought nothing at the airport.<br>纪念品又便宜又劣质，我在机场什么也没买。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cheap at ˈtwice the price</td><td>非常划算；再贵一倍也值</td><td>That old bike lasted me ten years, so it was cheap at twice the price.<br>那辆旧自行车我骑了十年，再贵一倍也值。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not come ˈcheap</td><td>价格不菲；不便宜</td><td>Good childcare doesn't come cheap in this part of the city.<br>在城里这一带，好的托儿服务可不便宜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈcheap (informal)</td><td>廉价地；花小钱</td><td>They renovated the whole flat on the cheap using second-hand materials.<br>他们用二手材料，花小钱翻新了整套公寓。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>check</b></td><td>keep/hold sb/sth in ˈcheck</td><td>控制；抑制</td><td>Regular exercise keeps his blood pressure in check without any medication.<br>规律锻炼让他不吃药也能把血压控制住。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>checks</b></td><td>checks and ˈbalances</td><td>制约与平衡；权力制衡</td><td>Without proper checks and balances, one loud person can run any committee.<br>没有像样的制衡，任何委员会都会被一个大嗓门把持。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cheek</b></td><td>cheek by ˈjowl (with sb/sth)</td><td>紧挨着；密集相邻</td><td>Tiny workshops sit cheek by jowl with luxury hotels in this old district.<br>在这片老城区，小作坊和豪华酒店紧挨在一起。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn the other ˈcheek</td><td>逆来顺受；不予还击</td><td>He insulted her twice, but she turned the other cheek and kept working.<br>他两次出言侮辱，她却不予计较，继续做事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blank</b></td><td>a blank ˈcheque (BrE) (AmE a blank ˈcheck)</td><td>空白支票；全权处置</td><td>The council gave the developer a blank cheque to redesign the waterfront.<br>议会给了开发商全权，随意重新规划滨水区。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chest</b></td><td>get sth off your ˈchest (informal)</td><td>倾诉心事；一吐为快</td><td>Tell me what's wrong—you'll feel better once you get it off your chest.<br>说说怎么了，吐露出来你会好受些。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chew</b></td><td>ˌchew the ˈfat (BrE) (AmE ˌchew the ˈrag)</td><td>闲聊；唠嗑</td><td>We sat on the porch chewing the fat until it got completely dark.<br>我们坐在门廊上闲聊，一直聊到天全黑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chicken</b></td><td>ˈchicken feed (informal)</td><td>小钱；微不足道的钱</td><td>Two hundred pounds is chicken feed compared with what the repairs will cost.<br>跟修理费一比，两百英镑只是小钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chickens</b></td><td>(your/the) chickens come home to ˈroost</td><td>自食其果；恶有恶报</td><td>His chickens came home to roost when the inspectors found the faulty wiring.<br>检查员查出线路有问题，他终于自食其果。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>don't count your ˈchickens (before they're hatched) (saying)</td><td>别过早乐观；勿盲目自信</td><td>Don't count your chickens—the buyer hasn't actually signed anything yet.<br>别高兴太早，买家其实还没签任何字。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chiefs</b></td><td>too many ˌchiefs and not enough ˈIndians (saying)</td><td>指挥的多，干活的少</td><td>Nothing gets finished here: too many chiefs and not enough Indians.<br>这儿什么都做不完，指挥的多，干活的少。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>child</b></td><td>ˈchild's play</td><td>极容易的事；小菜一碟</td><td>After climbing that mountain, a five-mile walk feels like child's play.<br>爬过那座山之后，走五英里简直是小菜一碟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chill</b></td><td>a ˈchill runs/goes down sb's spine</td><td>令人毛骨悚然；不寒而栗</td><td>A chill ran down my spine when I heard footsteps in the empty house.<br>空房子里传来脚步声，我不寒而栗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>send a ˈchill up/down sb's spine</td><td>使人不寒而栗</td><td>The recording of that phone call sent a chill down my spine.<br>那通电话的录音让我脊背发凉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>chill sb to the ˈbone/ˈmarrow</td><td>使人透心凉；使极为恐惧</td><td>The wind off the sea chilled us to the bone within five minutes.<br>海风吹了不到五分钟就把我们冻透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chin</b></td><td>(keep your) ˈchin up (informal)</td><td>振作起来；别灰心</td><td>Chin up—there'll be other auditions before the end of the year.<br>振作点，年底前还有别的试镜机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth on the ˈchin (informal)</td><td>勇敢承受（挫折或批评）</td><td>She took the criticism on the chin and rewrote the whole chapter.<br>她坦然接受批评，把整章重写了一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chink</b></td><td>a chink in sb's ˈarmour (BrE) (AmE a chink in sb's ˈarmor)</td><td>弱点；薄弱环节</td><td>His impatience is the one chink in his armour as a negotiator.<br>作为谈判者，他唯一的软肋就是缺乏耐心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chip</b></td><td>a ˌchip off the old ˈblock (informal)</td><td>酷似父母的人</td><td>The boy fixes engines just like his dad—a real chip off the old block.<br>这男孩修发动机跟他爸一个样，真是有其父必有其子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈchip on your shoulder (informal)</td><td>心怀不满；动辄发火</td><td>He's had a chip on his shoulder ever since they passed him over.<br>自从升职没轮到他，他就一直忿忿不平。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chips</b></td><td>have had your ˈchips (BrE, informal)</td><td>完蛋了；注定要失败</td><td>One more loss and the manager has had his chips at this club.<br>再输一场，主教练在这家俱乐部就干到头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let the chips fall where they ˈmay (AmE, informal)</td><td>顺其自然；不计后果</td><td>Tell them the truth and let the chips fall where they may.<br>把真相告诉他们，后果怎样就怎样吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>when the chips are ˈdown (informal)</td><td>在关键时刻；危急关头</td><td>When the chips are down, you find out who your real friends are.<br>到了关键时刻，你才看得出谁是真朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>choice</b></td><td>be spoilt/spoiled for ˈchoice</td><td>选择太多，难以取舍</td><td>With twelve desserts on offer, we were spoilt for choice at the bakery.<br>面包店有十二种甜点，我们挑花了眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by ˈchoice</td><td>出于自愿；主动地</td><td>He works nights by choice because the office is quiet after midnight.<br>他自愿上夜班，因为过了午夜办公室很安静。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of ˈchoice (for sb/sth)</td><td>首选的；特选的</td><td>Denim is still the fabric of choice for anyone working outdoors all day.<br>对整天在户外干活的人来说，牛仔布仍是首选面料。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of your ˈchoice</td><td>自己挑选的</td><td>The winner gets dinner for two at a restaurant of their choice.<br>获胜者可在自选餐厅享用双人晚餐。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>choose</b></td><td>there's nothing, not much, etc. to ˈchoose between A and B</td><td>两者不相上下；难分高低</td><td>There's nothing to choose between the two phones; both take excellent photos.<br>这两款手机不相上下，拍照都很出色。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chop</b></td><td>be for the ˈchop (BrE, informal)</td><td>可能被解雇；将被砍掉</td><td>Three regional offices are for the chop under the new cost-cutting plan.<br>按新的削减成本方案，三个地区办事处要被砍掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌchop and ˈchange (BrE, informal)</td><td>反复变化；朝令夕改</td><td>Stop chopping and changing—pick one supplier and stick with them.<br>别再变来变去了，选定一家供应商就别换了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/be given the ˈchop (BrE, informal)</td><td>被解雇；被取消</td><td>Her show got the chop after just two seasons on the network.<br>她的节目在该台只播了两季就被砍掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not much ˈchop (AustralE, NZE, informal)</td><td>不怎么样；没多大用处</td><td>The new coffee place is not much chop; the beans taste burnt.<br>新开的咖啡店不怎么样，豆子有糊味。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cigar</b></td><td>ˌclose but no ciˈgar (informal)</td><td>差一点；功亏一篑</td><td>You guessed the year but not the month—close but no cigar.<br>年份猜对了月份没猜中，就差那么一点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>circles</b></td><td>go round in ˈcircles</td><td>原地打转；毫无进展</td><td>The meeting went round in circles for two hours without a single decision.<br>会开了两小时一直在兜圈子，一个决定也没做。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run around in ˈcircles (BrE also run round in ˈcircles)</td><td>瞎忙活；徒劳奔波</td><td>I ran around in circles all day and still didn't finish the paperwork.<br>我一整天瞎忙活，文件还是没弄完。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>circumstances</b></td><td>in/under the ˈcircumstances</td><td>在这种情况下；既然如此</td><td>Under the circumstances, a written apology is the least he owes us.<br>在这种情况下，他至少该写份书面道歉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/under no ˈcircumstances</td><td>决不；无论如何都不</td><td>Under no circumstances should you open that door while the machine runs.<br>机器运转时，你绝对不能打开那扇门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>claim</b></td><td>ˌclaim to ˈfame (often humorous)</td><td>出名的资本；成名之处</td><td>The village's only claim to fame is a bridge that appeared in a film.<br>这村子唯一出名的地方是一座上过电影的桥。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clam</b></td><td>(as) happy as a ˈclam (AmE)</td><td>非常快乐；乐呵呵</td><td>Give him a fishing rod and a quiet lake and he's happy as a clam.<br>给他一根鱼竿和一片静湖，他就乐得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clappers</b></td><td>like the ˈclappers (BrE, informal)</td><td>飞快地；拼命地</td><td>We ran like the clappers and just caught the last train home.<br>我们撒腿狂奔，刚好赶上回家的末班车。</td></tr>
