<tr><td><b>class</b></td><td>be in a ˈclass of your, its, etc. own</td><td>独一无二；出类拔萃</td><td>As a live performer, she is in a class of her own.<br>论现场表演，她是独一无二的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>claws</b></td><td>get your ˈclaws into sb</td><td>（女子）死死缠住某人</td><td>His mother thinks that girl has got her claws into him already.<br>他妈妈觉得那姑娘已经把他缠得死死的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clean</b></td><td>(as) clean as a ˈwhistle (informal)</td><td>干干净净；清白无瑕</td><td>The kitchen was as clean as a whistle when the inspectors came round.<br>检查员来的时候，厨房干净得一尘不染。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a clean bill of ˈhealth</td><td>健康证明；合格证明</td><td>The surveyor gave the old cottage a clean bill of health, surprisingly enough.<br>勘验师居然给这栋老屋出具了合格证明。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a clean ˈbreak</td><td>彻底决裂；一刀两断</td><td>She made a clean break with her old firm and started her own agency.<br>她与老东家彻底了断，自己开了家代理公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>clean ˈhouse (AmE)</td><td>清理整顿；裁撤冗员</td><td>The new owner cleaned house and replaced most of the senior managers.<br>新老板大清洗，换掉了大部分高层经理。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>clean up your ˈact (informal)</td><td>改邪归正；改进作风</td><td>The restaurant cleaned up its act after failing two hygiene inspections.<br>两次卫生检查不合格后，这家餐馆彻底整改了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come ˈclean (with sb) (about sth) (informal)</td><td>坦白；全盘招供</td><td>He finally came clean about denting the car on the way to work.<br>他终于坦白，上班路上把车刮凹了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have clean ˈhands ◆ your hands are ˈclean</td><td>清白无辜；没做亏心事</td><td>Whatever the papers say, my hands are clean in this whole affair.<br>不管报纸怎么写，这件事上我是清白的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a clean ˈbreast of sth</td><td>彻底坦白；如实招认</td><td>He made a clean breast of the missing money before anyone accused him.<br>还没人指责他，他就把钱的去向全招了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a clean ˈsweep (of sth) (informal)</td><td>彻底清除；大获全胜</td><td>The team made a clean sweep of every medal at the regional championships.<br>这支队伍在地区锦标赛上包揽了全部奖牌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your ˈnose clean (informal)</td><td>安分守己；不惹麻烦</td><td>Keep your nose clean for six months and they'll consider you for parole.<br>安分守己半年，他们就会考虑给你假释。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cleaners</b></td><td>take sb to the ˈcleaners (informal)</td><td>骗光某人钱财；痛宰某人</td><td>The divorce lawyers took him to the cleaners and he lost the house.<br>离婚律师把他榨得精光，房子都没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clear</b></td><td>clear the ˈair</td><td>消除误会；缓和紧张气氛</td><td>A long, honest talk cleared the air between the two flatmates at last.<br>一次坦诚长谈终于化解了两个室友间的芥蒂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) clear as a ˈbell</td><td>非常清晰；听得一清二楚</td><td>Her voice came through the old radio as clear as a bell.<br>她的声音从旧收音机里传出来，清晰得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>clear the ˈdeck(s)</td><td>清除障碍；准备行动</td><td>Let's clear the decks this morning so we can start the audit tomorrow.<br>今天上午先把杂事清掉，明天好开始审计。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>clear sb's ˈname</td><td>为某人洗清罪名</td><td>It took eight years of appeals to clear her brother's name completely.<br>申诉了八年，才彻底为她哥哥洗清了罪名。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>clear your ˈthroat</td><td>清嗓子</td><td>He cleared his throat nervously before reading the speech to the guests.<br>给来宾念讲稿前，他紧张地清了清嗓子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>clear the ˈway (for sth/for sth to happen)</td><td>为…扫清障碍；铺路</td><td>The ruling clears the way for thousands of similar compensation claims.<br>这项裁决为数千宗类似索赔扫清了障碍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/keep a clear ˈhead</td><td>保持头脑清醒</td><td>I skip wine at lunch so I can keep a clear head all afternoon.<br>午饭我不喝酒，好让整个下午头脑清醒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈclear (informal)</td><td>摆脱嫌疑；脱离危险</td><td>The tests came back fine, so the doctor says she's in the clear.<br>检查结果正常，医生说她没事了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>steer/stay/keep clear (of sb/sth)</td><td>避开；躲开</td><td>Steer clear of the coast road tonight; there's flooding near the bridge.<br>今晚别走海滨公路，桥附近发大水了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cleft</b></td><td>be (caught) in a cleft ˈstick (informal)</td><td>进退两难；左右为难</td><td>She's caught in a cleft stick: quit the course or lose the scholarship.<br>她进退两难：要么退课，要么丢掉奖学金。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clever</b></td><td>ˈclever Dick (also ˈclever clogs) (BrE, informal, disapproving)</td><td>自作聪明的人</td><td>Some clever Dick reprogrammed the office printer to beep every hour.<br>哪个自作聪明的家伙把办公室打印机改成每小时叫一次。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈclever clogs (BrE, informal, disapproving)</td><td>自作聪明的家伙</td><td>All right, clever clogs, if you know the answer, come and fix it.<br>行了，聪明人，你既然知道答案就过来修吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>climbing</b></td><td>be climbing the ˈwalls (informal)</td><td>急得团团转；烦躁不安</td><td>Stuck indoors for a week with flu, I was climbing the walls.<br>得流感在家闷了一周，我快憋疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clip</b></td><td>at a fast, good, steady, etc. ˈclip (especially AmE)</td><td>以…的速度；快速地</td><td>Orders have been coming in at a steady clip since the review appeared.<br>自从那篇评论出来，订单一直稳步不断。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>clip sb's ˈwings</td><td>限制某人的自由（或权力）</td><td>The new rules have clipped the wings of the more ambitious department heads.<br>新规定限制住了那些野心较大的部门主管。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clock</b></td><td>around/round the ˈclock</td><td>昼夜不停；夜以继日</td><td>Engineers worked around the clock to get the power back on by Monday.<br>工程师昼夜赶工，赶在周一前恢复了供电。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/turn the ˈclock back</td><td>开倒车；倒退回过去</td><td>You can't turn the clock back and undo what was said last night.<br>你没法让时光倒流，收回昨晚说过的话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run out the ˈclock (AmE)</td><td>（比赛中）拖延时间保住比分</td><td>Leading by two, they simply ran out the clock in the final minutes.<br>领先两分，他们在最后几分钟干脆拖时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clockwork</b></td><td>go/run like ˈclockwork</td><td>进展顺利；按部就班</td><td>The whole wedding went like clockwork, right down to the last speech.<br>整场婚礼顺利极了，连最后的致辞都分毫不差。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>close</b></td><td>close the ˈbook on sth</td><td>结束某事；不再过问</td><td>The police finally closed the book on the case after thirty long years.<br>三十年后，警方终于给这桩案子画上句号。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>close your ˈmind (to sth)</td><td>拒不接受（新想法）</td><td>Don't close your mind to online courses just because you prefer classrooms.<br>别因为偏爱课堂就对网课一概不听。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>closed-ˈminded (disapproving)</td><td>思想封闭的；固执己见的</td><td>He's too closed-minded to admit that the younger staff might be right.<br>他太固执，不肯承认年轻同事也许是对的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>close</b></td><td>at ˌclose ˈquarters</td><td>近距离地；贴近地</td><td>Watching the sculptor at close quarters, you notice how tiny each cut is.<br>近距离看雕刻家干活，你会发现每一刀都极细。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>close ˈby (sb/sth)</td><td>在附近；离…不远</td><td>They bought a cottage close by the lake so the kids could swim.<br>他们在湖边不远处买了间小屋，方便孩子游泳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>close ˈto ◆ close ˈup</td><td>近看；靠近时</td><td>The painting looks messy close up, but it's stunning from the doorway.<br>这幅画近看很乱，从门口望过去却很惊艳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>close to ˈhome</td><td>戳到痛处；说得太贴切</td><td>His joke about lazy relatives hit a bit close to home for me.<br>他拿懒亲戚开的玩笑，对我来说有点戳心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cloth</b></td><td>be ˌcut from the same ˈcloth</td><td>一路货色；如出一辙</td><td>The two brothers are cut from the same cloth: stubborn and impossible to argue with.<br>兄弟俩是一个路子，倔得没法跟他们讲理。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌcut from the same ˈcloth (informal)</td><td>一个模子里出来的；十分相像</td><td>Don't assume all the women in our family are cut from the same cloth.<br>别以为我们家的女人都是一个模子刻出来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cut your ˈcoat according to your ˈcloth (saying)</td><td>量入为出；看菜吃饭</td><td>We cut our coat according to our cloth and skipped the holiday this year.<br>我们量入为出，今年的假期就不去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clothes</b></td><td>the emperor's new ˈclothes</td><td>皇帝的新装；自欺欺人的假象</td><td>The strategy is the emperor's new clothes: nobody dares say it makes no sense.<br>这套战略就是皇帝的新装，没人敢说它根本讲不通。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cloud</b></td><td>a ˈcloud hangs over sb/sth</td><td>笼罩在阴影之下</td><td>A cloud has hung over the company since the fraud investigation began.<br>自欺诈调查开始，公司就一直笼罩在阴影中。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a (small) cloud on the hoˈrizon</td><td>隐忧；不祥的苗头</td><td>Rising fuel prices are the only cloud on the horizon for the airline.<br>油价上涨是这家航空公司眼下唯一的隐忧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>every ˌcloud has a silver ˈlining (saying)</td><td>黑暗中总有一线光明</td><td>I lost the job but met my business partner: every cloud has a silver lining.<br>我丢了工作却遇到合伙人，真是祸中有福。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on cloud ˈnine (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>欣喜若狂；乐不可支</td><td>She's been on cloud nine since the university offered her a place.<br>自从大学录取她，她就一直乐得飘飘然。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under a ˈcloud</td><td>受到怀疑；名誉受损</td><td>He left the department under a cloud after the expenses story broke.<br>报销丑闻曝光后，他不光彩地离开了部门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clover</b></td><td>in ˈclover (informal)</td><td>生活优裕；养尊处优</td><td>Since the shop took off, the family has been living in clover.<br>自打店里生意火起来，这家人过得相当滋润。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>club</b></td><td>be in the ˈclub (BrE, informal)</td><td>怀孕；有了身孕</td><td>Word got round the office that Anna is in the club again.<br>办公室里传开了，安娜又怀上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clue</b></td><td>not have a ˈclue (informal)</td><td>一无所知；毫无头绪</td><td>I don't have a clue how the boiler works, so call a plumber.<br>我完全不懂锅炉怎么运作，还是叫水管工吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>coalface</b></td><td>at the ˈcoalface (BrE)</td><td>在第一线；在工作现场</td><td>Managers should spend a week at the coalface before rewriting the rules.<br>经理们该先去一线待一周，再来改规矩。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>coals</b></td><td>(carry/take) coals to ˈNewcastle (BrE)</td><td>多此一举；徒劳无功</td><td>Bringing wine to a vineyard is like carrying coals to Newcastle.<br>带酒去酒庄，简直是多此一举。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>coast</b></td><td>the ˌcoast is ˈclear (informal)</td><td>没人发现；平安无事</td><td>Wait until the coast is clear before you sneak the cake upstairs.<br>等没人注意了，再把蛋糕偷偷端上楼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>coat</b></td><td>cut your ˈcoat acˌcording to your ˈcloth</td><td>量入为出</td><td>They cut their coat according to their cloth and bought a smaller car.<br>他们量入为出，买了辆小一点的车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cock</b></td><td>a ˌcock and ˈbull story (informal)</td><td>无稽之谈；荒诞的借口</td><td>He gave me some cock and bull story about his phone falling in the canal.<br>他编了套鬼话，说手机掉进运河里了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cock an ˈear/ˈeye at sb/sth</td><td>侧耳倾听；凝神细看</td><td>The dog cocked an ear at the sound of keys in the front door.<br>听见大门钥匙响，狗竖起了耳朵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cock a ˈsnook at sb/sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>公然蔑视；做鬼脸表示不敬</td><td>The young artists cocked a snook at the gallery by exhibiting in a car park.<br>年轻艺术家在停车场办展，公然蔑视那家画廊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cog</b></td><td>a cog in the maˈchine/the ˈwheel (informal)</td><td>大机构中无足轻重的一员</td><td>After twenty years he still felt like a cog in the machine.<br>干了二十年，他还是觉得自己只是颗螺丝钉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cold</b></td><td>ˌcold ˈcomfort</td><td>无济于事的安慰</td><td>A refund is cold comfort when you've missed your daughter's graduation.<br>错过女儿的毕业典礼，退钱也无济于事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌcold ˈfish (disapproving)</td><td>冷漠的人；冷血动物</td><td>He's a cold fish at work but surprisingly warm with his grandchildren.<br>他工作中冷冰冰的，对孙辈却出奇地热络。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/get the cold ˈshoulder</td><td>冷落某人；受到冷遇</td><td>Ever since the argument, the neighbours have given us the cold shoulder.<br>自那次争吵以后，邻居就一直对我们爱答不理。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in cold ˈblood</td><td>残忍地；蓄意冷酷地</td><td>The novel opens with two strangers murdered in cold blood on a farm.<br>小说开篇便是两名陌生人在农场被冷血杀害。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˌcold light of ˈday</td><td>冷静下来时；事后清醒地看</td><td>In the cold light of day, quitting my job seemed a terrible idea.<br>冷静下来一想，辞职真是个糟糕的主意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave sb ˈcold</td><td>打动不了某人；提不起兴趣</td><td>Everyone raves about that band, but their music leaves me completely cold.<br>人人都夸那支乐队，可他们的音乐一点也打动不了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pour/throw cold ˈwater on sth (informal)</td><td>泼冷水；打击积极性</td><td>Dad poured cold water on my plan to cycle across France alone.<br>我想独自骑车穿越法国，被爸爸泼了冷水。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>come</b></td><td>come ˈoff it (spoken)</td><td>别胡扯了；得了吧</td><td>Come off it—you can't have finished the whole report in twenty minutes.<br>得了吧，你不可能二十分钟写完整份报告。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come to ˈnothing ◆ not come to ˈanything</td><td>毫无结果；落空</td><td>All those meetings about the new library came to nothing in the end.<br>关于新图书馆的那些会最后都不了了之。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>come</b></td><td>ˌcome and ˈgo</td><td>来来去去；转瞬即逝</td><td>Fashions come and go, but a good wool coat lasts forever.<br>潮流来来去去，一件好羊毛大衣却能穿一辈子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come, ˈcome ◆ ˈcome, now (old-fashioned)</td><td>（劝人冷静）得了吧；好啦</td><td>Come, come, nobody is going to be sacked over one broken mug.<br>好啦好啦，没人会为一个摔碎的杯子被开除。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come ˈeasily, ˈnaturally, etc. to sb</td><td>对某人而言轻而易举；天生就会</td><td>Talking to strangers comes naturally to her, which makes her a great host.<br>跟陌生人搭话对她来说毫不费力，所以她很会招待人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈcome it (with sb) (informal)</td><td>装模作样；摆架子</td><td>Don't come it with me—I've known you since you were seven.<br>别跟我摆谱，你七岁起我就认识你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>coming</b></td><td>have it/that ˈcoming (to you) (informal)</td><td>活该；自食其果</td><td>He had it coming after ignoring every warning the inspector gave him.<br>检查员的警告他一概不听，落到这步是活该。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see sb ˈcoming (informal)</td><td>看出某人好骗</td><td>The dealer saw him coming and charged double for a rusty old bike.<br>车贩子看他好糊弄，一辆锈自行车要了双倍价。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see sth ˈcoming</td><td>预料到（坏事）会发生</td><td>Nobody saw the closure coming; the shop was busy right up to Christmas.<br>没人料到会关门，店里一直忙到圣诞节。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>where sb is ˈcoming from (informal, spoken)</td><td>某人的出发点；某人的用意</td><td>Once you know where she's coming from, her objections make much more sense.<br>一旦明白她的出发点，她的反对就说得通了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>comings</b></td><td>ˌcomings and ˈgoings</td><td>来来往往；进进出出</td><td>From her window she watches all the comings and goings on the street.<br>她从窗口看着街上的人来人往。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>command</b></td><td>at your comˈmand</td><td>可自由支配；运用自如</td><td>With three languages at her command, she had no trouble finding work abroad.<br>她掌握三门语言，在国外找工作毫不费劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be at sb's comˈmand (formal)</td><td>听候某人吩咐</td><td>The whole kitchen staff was at the duchess's command for the entire weekend.<br>整个周末，全体厨房人员都听候公爵夫人差遣。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>company</b></td><td>get into/keep bad ˈcompany</td><td>结交坏人；与坏人为伍</td><td>He got into bad company at sixteen and dropped out of school soon after.<br>他十六岁交了坏朋友，没多久就辍学了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep sb ˈcompany</td><td>陪伴某人</td><td>I'll keep you company at the hospital until your sister arrives.<br>你姐姐来之前，我在医院陪着你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>compare</b></td><td>beyond/without comˈpare (literary)</td><td>无与伦比；举世无双</td><td>The view from that ridge at sunrise is truly beyond compare.<br>日出时从那道山脊望去的景色实在无与伦比。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>compare ˈnotes (with sb) (on sth)</td><td>交换意见；互通情况</td><td>After the exam we met in the café to compare notes on the questions.<br>考完试我们在咖啡馆碰头，交流各自的答题情况。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>confidence</b></td><td>be in sb's ˈconfidence</td><td>受某人信任</td><td>Only two advisers were really in the president's confidence during those years.<br>那些年真正得到总统信任的只有两位顾问。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb into your ˈconfidence</td><td>向某人吐露秘密</td><td>She took her sister into her confidence about the job offer in Berlin.<br>她向姐姐透露了柏林那份工作邀约。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>conflict</b></td><td>conflict of ˈinterest(s)</td><td>利益冲突</td><td>Judging a contest your own students entered is a clear conflict of interest.<br>给自己学生参加的比赛当评委，明显存在利益冲突。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>conjunction</b></td><td>in conˈjunction with (formal)</td><td>与…一起；连同</td><td>The course runs in conjunction with a local hospital and includes ward placements.<br>这门课与本地医院合办，包含病房实习。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>connect</b></td><td>connect the ˈdots (BrE also join (up) the ˈdots)</td><td>把线索联系起来；理清关系</td><td>Once you connect the dots, the two robberies were obviously planned together.<br>把线索一串，两起抢劫显然是一起策划的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>conscience</b></td><td>in all/good ˈconscience</td><td>凭良心说；公平地讲</td><td>I cannot in all conscience recommend a builder who left our roof leaking.<br>凭良心讲，我没法推荐一个把我家屋顶弄漏的建筑商。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on your ˈconscience</td><td>使人内疚；良心不安</td><td>Sacking him just before Christmas will be on your conscience, not mine.<br>圣诞前把他辞了，那是你良心上的事，不是我的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈconsequences (of sth)</td><td>承担后果</td><td>If you skip training all week, you take the consequences on match day.<br>一周不训练，比赛日的后果你自己扛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈconsequence (of sth) (formal)</td><td>因此；由于…的结果</td><td>The bridge closed and, in consequence, the village lost its bus service.<br>桥关闭了，村里因此没了公交服务。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>consideration</b></td><td>in consideˈration of sth (formal)</td><td>作为…的报酬；考虑到</td><td>He received a small pension in consideration of forty years of loyal service.<br>为酬谢他四十年的忠诚服务，他领到一笔小额养老金。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth into consideˈration</td><td>考虑到；顾及</td><td>The judge took his age and clean record into consideration when sentencing him.<br>量刑时法官考虑了他的年龄和无前科记录。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>considered</b></td><td>your conˌsidered oˈpinion</td><td>深思熟虑后的看法</td><td>It is my considered opinion that the roof needs replacing before another winter.<br>我仔细想过，屋顶得在下个冬天前换掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in my conˌsidered oˈpinion</td><td>依我看；我仔细想来认为</td><td>In my considered opinion, 'Trainspotting' is the best British film of the nineties.<br>仔细想来，《猜火车》是九十年代最好的英国电影。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>conspicuous</b></td><td>conˌspicuous by your ˈabsence</td><td>缺席引人注目</td><td>The manager was conspicuous by his absence at yesterday's staff meeting.<br>昨天的员工会上，经理的缺席格外显眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>conspiracy</b></td><td>a conˌspiracy of ˈsilence</td><td>保持缄默的默契</td><td>There was a conspiracy of silence in the village about what happened that night.<br>那晚发生的事，村里人默契地都不吭声。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>contact</b></td><td>be/get out of conˈtrol</td><td>失去控制；无法管理</td><td>The bonfire got out of control and the fire brigade had to come.<br>篝火失控了，消防队只好赶来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beneath conˈtempt</td><td>极其卑劣；不屑一顾</td><td>Stealing from a charity box is beneath contempt, whatever your excuses are.<br>偷募捐箱的钱，不管什么理由都卑劣至极。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>contention</b></td><td>in/out of conˈtention (for sth)</td><td>有（或没有）获胜机会</td><td>One more win puts them back in contention for a European place.<br>再赢一场，他们就重新有望拿到欧战名额。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>contrary</b></td><td>contrary to popular beˈlief/oˈpinion</td><td>与普遍看法相反</td><td>Contrary to popular belief, most bats have excellent eyesight and hunt visually.<br>与普遍看法相反，多数蝙蝠视力极好，靠视觉捕食。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈcontrary ◆ ˌquite the ˈcontrary</td><td>正相反；恰恰相反</td><td>I'm not bored; on the contrary, I could listen to him all evening.<br>我不觉得无聊，恰恰相反，我能听他讲一整晚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in conˈtrol (of sth)</td><td>掌控；主管</td><td>She stayed calm and in control of the class throughout the fire drill.<br>整个消防演习中她都镇定自若，把班级管得井井有条。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cook</b></td><td>cook sb's ˈgoose (informal)</td><td>毁掉某人的计划；断送前程</td><td>That leaked email really cooked his goose with the board of directors.<br>那封外泄的邮件彻底断送了他在董事会的前途。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cooking</b></td><td>be cooking with ˈgas (AmE, informal)</td><td>进展顺利；干得漂亮</td><td>Once the second engine started, we were really cooking with gas.<br>第二台发动机一启动，我们就干得顺风顺水了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's ˈcooking? (informal)</td><td>在搞什么名堂；怎么回事</td><td>You two look guilty—what's cooking in here this early on a Sunday?<br>你俩一脸心虚，周日一大早在这儿捣鼓什么呢？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cooks</b></td><td>too many cooks spoil the ˈbroth (saying)</td><td>厨子多了烧坏汤；人多手杂反坏事</td><td>Three of us in one kitchen? Too many cooks spoil the broth.<br>三个人挤一个厨房？人多反而坏事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cool</b></td><td>(as) ˌcool as a ˈcucumber (informal)</td><td>极为冷静；泰然自若</td><td>She stayed as cool as a cucumber while the alarms went off around her.<br>警报响成一片，她却依旧镇定自若。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌcool your ˈheels (informal)</td><td>被迫久等</td><td>They left me cooling my heels in reception for nearly an hour.<br>他们让我在前台干等了将近一个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈcool it (informal)</td><td>冷静点；别激动</td><td>Cool it, you two—the neighbours can hear every word through the wall.<br>你俩冷静点，隔着墙邻居一句不落全听得见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep/lose your ˈcool (informal)</td><td>保持冷静；沉不住气</td><td>He lost his cool when the referee awarded the penalty against him.<br>裁判判他犯规罚点球时，他沉不住气了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play it ˈcool (informal)</td><td>保持镇定；不动声色</td><td>Play it cool at the interview and don't mention money until they do.<br>面试时沉住气，他们不提钱你就别提。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cop</b></td><td>ˈcop it (BrE, slang)</td><td>挨罚；挨骂</td><td>You'll cop it if Mum finds out you took the car again.<br>要是妈妈发现你又开走了车，你可要挨训了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cop a ˈplea (AmE, informal)</td><td>认罪求轻判</td><td>His lawyer advised him to cop a plea rather than risk a trial.<br>律师建议他认罪求轻判，别冒险受审。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not much ˈcop (BrE, slang)</td><td>不怎么样；没多大用处</td><td>That new detective series isn't much cop after the first two episodes.<br>那部新侦探剧头两集之后就不怎么样了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's a fair ˈcop (BrE, informal, humorous)</td><td>（认错时说）我认了；抓得没错</td><td>It's a fair cop—I did eat the last three biscuits after all.<br>我认了，最后三块饼干确实是我吃的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>core</b></td><td>to the ˈcore</td><td>彻头彻尾；透顶</td><td>He's a Yorkshireman to the core and won't hear a word against it.<br>他是个地道的约克郡人，容不得别人说半句不是。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>corner</b></td><td>back/paint sb/yourself into a ˈcorner</td><td>使陷入绝境；自陷困境</td><td>By promising everyone a raise, he painted himself into a corner.<br>他答应给每个人加薪，把自己逼进了死角。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>corner the ˈmarket (in sth)</td><td>垄断（某商品）市场</td><td>One family has cornered the market in wedding cakes in this small town.<br>这座小城的婚礼蛋糕生意被一家人垄断了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have the market ˈcornered (in sth)</td><td>垄断某一市场</td><td>Bestsave has the market cornered in cheap groceries across the whole region.<br>倍省超市垄断了整个地区的廉价杂货生意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>just around/round the ˈcorner</td><td>即将来临；近在咫尺</td><td>Exam season is just around the corner and nobody has started revising.<br>考试季马上就到，可谁都还没开始复习。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be around the ˈcorner</td><td>近在眼前；即将发生</td><td>Success is around the corner, so the work must not be stopped now.<br>成功就在眼前，现在决不能停下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of the corner of your ˈeye</td><td>用眼角余光</td><td>Out of the corner of my eye I saw him slip the envelope into his bag.<br>我用余光瞥见他把信封塞进了包里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn the ˈcorner</td><td>度过难关；出现转机</td><td>The patient turned the corner on Tuesday and is now sitting up eating.<br>病人周二挺过了危险期，现在能坐起来吃饭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>corners</b></td><td>cut ˈcorners (disapproving)</td><td>走捷径；偷工减料</td><td>The builders cut corners on the insulation and now the flat is freezing.<br>施工队在保温上偷工减料，现在屋里冷得要命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the four corners of the ˈearth/ˈworld</td><td>天涯海角；世界各地</td><td>Fans came from the four corners of the earth for the band's final concert.<br>歌迷从世界各地赶来看乐队的告别演唱会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>corridors</b></td><td>the corridors of ˈpower</td><td>权力中枢；政府高层</td><td>She spent thirty years in the corridors of power advising four different ministers.<br>她在权力中枢待了三十年，先后为四位大臣出谋划策。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cost</b></td><td>at ˈany cost</td><td>不惜任何代价</td><td>They wanted to keep the factory open at any cost, even losing money.<br>他们想不惜代价保住工厂，哪怕亏本。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it will ˈcost you (spoken)</td><td>那可得花大价钱</td><td>I can get you tickets for tonight, but it will cost you.<br>今晚的票我能弄到，不过你得出血。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to your ˈcost</td><td>吃了亏才知道；付出代价后才明白</td><td>As I know to my cost, that garage never finishes a job on time.<br>我是吃过亏才知道，那家修车行从不按时完工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈall costs</td><td>不惜一切代价</td><td>We must avoid a strike at all costs before the holiday season starts.<br>假期旺季开始前，我们必须不惜一切代价避免罢工。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>couch</b></td><td>a ˈcouch potato (informal, disapproving)</td><td>终日窝在沙发看电视的懒人</td><td>His mother warns him he'll turn into a couch potato over the long summer.<br>他妈妈警告说，这个长假他会变成沙发土豆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>count</b></td><td>be able to count sb/sth on (the fingers of) one ˈhand</td><td>屈指可数；寥寥无几</td><td>You can count the good restaurants in this town on one hand.<br>这镇上好餐馆一只手就数得过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>count sth on the fingers of one ˈhand</td><td>少得可数；寥寥可数</td><td>I could count on the fingers of one hand the times he has apologised.<br>他道歉的次数一只手就数得完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>count your ˈblessings</td><td>知足；想想还有什么值得庆幸</td><td>Count your blessings—at least the car was insured when the tree fell.<br>知足吧，树砸下来时车好歹上了保险。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>count the ˈcost</td><td>考虑代价（或风险）</td><td>The town is still counting the cost of last winter's floods.<br>这座小镇仍在承受去年冬天洪水带来的损失。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>count ˈsheep</td><td>数羊（以求入睡）</td><td>I lay there counting sheep until nearly three in the morning.<br>我躺着数羊，一直数到快凌晨三点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep (a) ˈcount (of sth)</td><td>记住数目；数得清</td><td>I've stopped keeping count of how many times he has changed jobs.<br>他换过多少次工作，我已经懒得数了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose ˈcount (of sth)</td><td>记不清数目；数不过来</td><td>I've lost count of the emails I've sent about that broken lift.<br>为那部坏电梯我发了多少封邮件，自己都记不清了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not count your ˈchickens (before they're hatched)</td><td>别过早乐观；勿盲目自信</td><td>Don't count your chickens—the results aren't published until Friday afternoon.<br>别高兴太早，结果周五下午才公布。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out for the ˈcount (BrE) (AmE ˌdown for the ˈcount)</td><td>不省人事；累得酣睡</td><td>Two minutes on the sofa and Dad was out for the count.<br>在沙发上待了两分钟，老爸就睡得人事不省。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>counted</b></td><td>stand up and be ˈcounted</td><td>公开表明立场；挺身表态</td><td>It's time for parents to stand up and be counted at the council meeting.<br>家长们该在议会会议上公开表态了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>counter</b></td><td>over the ˈcounter</td><td>（买药）不需处方</td><td>You can buy these painkillers over the counter at any chemist here.<br>这些止痛药在这里任何一家药店都能直接买到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under the ˈcounter</td><td>私下地；偷偷地；非法地</td><td>During the shortage, sugar was sold under the counter at triple the price.<br>短缺期间，白糖以三倍价格私下出售。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>counting</b></td><td>who's ˈcounting? (informal)</td><td>谁在乎呢；谁数着呢</td><td>That's my fourth coffee today, but who's counting?<br>这是我今天第四杯咖啡了，不过谁数着呢？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>country</b></td><td>a country ˈbumpkin/ˈcousin (informal, usually disapproving)</td><td>乡巴佬；没见过世面的人</td><td>He felt like a country bumpkin during his first week in London.<br>在伦敦的头一周，他觉得自己像个乡巴佬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to the ˈcountry (BrE)</td><td>举行大选</td><td>The prime minister decided to go to the country a full year early.<br>首相决定提前整整一年举行大选。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>courage</b></td><td>have/lack the courage of your conˈvictions</td><td>有（或没有）勇气坚持信念</td><td>She had the courage of her convictions and voted against her own party.<br>她坚持自己的信念，投票反对本党。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pluck up (the) ˈcourage (to do sth)</td><td>鼓起勇气（做某事）</td><td>It took him a month to pluck up the courage to ask her out.<br>他花了一个月才鼓起勇气约她出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take your ˌcourage in both ˈhands</td><td>鼓起勇气；壮起胆子</td><td>She took her courage in both hands and told the boss she was leaving.<br>她鼓起勇气告诉老板自己要走。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>course</b></td><td>a course of ˈaction</td><td>行动方针；处事办法</td><td>The safest course of action is to postpone the trip until early spring.<br>最稳妥的做法是把行程推迟到早春。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˌnormal/ˌordinary course of eˈvents</td><td>在通常情况下；照常规</td><td>In the normal course of events, the results arrive within about ten days.<br>通常情况下，结果十天左右就会寄到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of ˈcourse</td><td>当然；自然</td><td>Of course you can borrow the car, just fill the tank afterwards.<br>你当然可以借车，用完加满油就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of ˈcourse (spoken)</td><td>（礼貌应允）当然可以</td><td>Can I use your phone? Of course—help yourself, it's on the table.<br>我能用下你的电话吗？当然，请便，就在桌上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of ˈcourse not (also ˈcourse not informal)</td><td>当然不；才不呢</td><td>Of course not! I'd never tell your sister about the surprise trip.<br>当然不会！我绝不会把这次惊喜旅行告诉你姐姐。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>court</b></td><td>hold ˈcourt (often ironic)</td><td>成为众人焦点；高谈阔论</td><td>Uncle Ray was holding court in the kitchen with his fishing stories again.<br>雷叔叔又在厨房里大讲他的钓鱼故事，众人围听。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rule/throw sth out of ˈcourt</td><td>断然拒绝；不予考虑</td><td>The committee threw the proposal out of court before lunch on the first day.<br>委员会第一天午饭前就把这份提案否决了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ball is in your/sb's ˈcourt</td><td>该你（或某人）作决定了</td><td>I've made my offer, so now the ball is in their court.<br>我已经开出条件，现在轮到他们决定了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>courtesy</b></td><td>courtesy of sb/sth</td><td>蒙…好意；由…提供</td><td>The photographs are reproduced courtesy of the city museum and its archive.<br>这些照片蒙市博物馆及其档案室惠允转载。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sb the courtesy of doing sth</td><td>出于礼貌为某人做某事</td><td>At least do me the courtesy of telling me before you cancel.<br>你要取消，至少有礼貌地事先跟我说一声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have the courtesy to do sth</td><td>有礼貌地做某事；懂规矩</td><td>He didn't even have the courtesy to reply to my second email.<br>他连回一封我第二封邮件的礼貌都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cover</b></td><td>cover all the/your ˈbases (especially AmE)</td><td>考虑周全；面面俱到</td><td>Bring both passports and the printout so we cover all the bases.<br>两本护照和打印件都带上，这样万无一失。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cover your ˈback (informal) (AmE also cover your ˈass, slang)</td><td>预防日后被追责；留一手</td><td>Copy me into that email just to cover your back if things go wrong.<br>那封邮件抄送我一份，万一出事你也有个交代。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cover your ˈtracks</td><td>掩盖行踪；不留痕迹</td><td>The thieves covered their tracks by wiping the security footage before leaving.<br>窃贼离开前删掉监控录像，抹去了痕迹。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from ˌcover to ˈcover</td><td>从头至尾（读完）</td><td>She read the manual from cover to cover before touching the machine.<br>她把说明书从头读到尾才去碰那台机器。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under ˈcover</td><td>秘密地；伪装身份地</td><td>Two officers worked under cover in the warehouse for almost six months.<br>两名警官在仓库卧底了将近半年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under cover of sth</td><td>在…的掩护下</td><td>They crossed the river under cover of darkness and reached the border.<br>他们借着夜色掩护渡过河，抵达了边境。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cow</b></td><td>have a ˈcow (AmE, slang)</td><td>大发雷霆；急得跳脚</td><td>Don't have a cow—I'll pay for the window I broke.<br>别急得跳脚，我打碎的窗户我赔。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cows</b></td><td>till/until the ˈcows come home (informal)</td><td>很久很久；无限期地</td><td>You can argue about politics till the cows come home and change nothing.<br>你可以没完没了地争政治，什么也改变不了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crack</b></td><td>crack a ˈjoke</td><td>讲笑话；开玩笑</td><td>He cracked a joke about the weather and the whole room relaxed.<br>他拿天气开了个玩笑，全场气氛顿时轻松下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the crack of ˈdawn (informal)</td><td>黎明；破晓时分</td><td>We left at the crack of dawn to beat the holiday traffic.<br>我们天一亮就出发，好避开假日车流。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>crack the ˈwhip</td><td>严加督促；施压逼人干活</td><td>The deadline is Friday, so the editor is cracking the whip today.<br>周五截稿，所以编辑今天开始严加督促。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be all it's cracked ˈup to be (informal)</td><td>并不像人们说的那么好</td><td>The famous beach was not all it's cracked up to be: crowded and grey.<br>那片名滩并没有传说中那么好，又挤又灰蒙蒙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get ˈcracking (informal)</td><td>赶紧开始；抓紧干</td><td>Let's get cracking on the packing or we'll miss the morning ferry.<br>赶紧收拾行李吧，不然赶不上早班渡轮。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cradle</b></td><td>from the ˌcradle to the ˈgrave</td><td>从生到死；一辈子</td><td>The system was meant to care for citizens from the cradle to the grave.<br>这套制度本意是从生到死照顾国民。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cramp sb's ˈstyle</td><td>妨碍某人自由发挥；碍手碍脚</td><td>Having my little brother along really cramped my style at the party.<br>带着弟弟去派对，实在让我放不开。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>credit</b></td><td>do sb ˈcredit ◆ do ˈcredit to sb</td><td>为某人增光；值得称许</td><td>Her calm handling of the whole crisis really does her credit.<br>她冷静应对整场危机，实在令人称许。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be to sb's ˈcredit</td><td>值得赞扬；给某人长脸</td><td>It is to his credit that he apologised in front of the whole team.<br>他能在全队面前道歉，这一点值得称赞。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have sth to your ˈcredit</td><td>取得（成就）；名下有</td><td>She already has three novels and a stage play to her credit.<br>她名下已有三部小说和一部舞台剧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈcredit side</td><td>就好的方面而言；从有利一面看</td><td>On the credit side, the flat is cheap and close to the station.<br>好的方面是，这公寓便宜，又离车站近。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>creek</b></td><td>up the ˈcreek (informal) (also up shit ˈcreek (without a ˈpaddle), slang)</td><td>陷入困境；麻烦大了</td><td>If the generator fails tonight, we are really up the creek.<br>今晚发电机要是罢工，我们就麻烦大了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>creep</b></td><td>make your ˈflesh creep/crawl</td><td>使人毛骨悚然；起鸡皮疙瘩</td><td>The way he stared at us across the room made my flesh creep.<br>他隔着房间那样盯着我们，看得我头皮发麻。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>creme</b></td><td>the ˌcreme de la ˈcreme (from French, formal or humorous)</td><td>精华；最优秀的人</td><td>These students are the creme de la creme of the entire music school.<br>这些学生是整所音乐学院里的精英。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crest</b></td><td>(on) the crest of a ˈwave</td><td>处于鼎盛时期；春风得意</td><td>Right after the album went platinum the band was on the crest of a wave.<br>专辑大卖之后，乐队正当红得发紫。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crew</b></td><td>a skeleton ˈcrew/ˈstaff/ˈservice</td><td>最低限度的人员；基本运作的班子（或服务）</td><td>Over Christmas the hospital runs with a skeleton staff and only urgent cases.<br>圣诞期间医院只留最少人手，仅处理急诊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cricket</b></td><td>it's (just) not ˈcricket (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>不公平；不光明正大</td><td>Reading someone else's emails is just not cricket, even if you're the boss.<br>偷看别人的邮件太不地道了，就算你是老板也一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crimp</b></td><td>put a ˈcrimp in/on sth (AmE, informal)</td><td>妨碍；对…有负面影响</td><td>The rain really put a crimp in our plans for the weekend barbecue.<br>这场雨把我们周末烧烤的计划全搅黄了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put a ˈcrimp on sth (AmE, informal)</td><td>使…受影响；给…添麻烦</td><td>The extra expense of moving can put a crimp on your monthly budget.<br>搬家多出来的花销会把你每月的预算压得很紧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crock</b></td><td>a ˌcrock of ˈshit (taboo, slang, especially AmE)</td><td>屁话；胡说八道</td><td>Honestly, that excuse about traffic is a crock of shit and everyone knows it.<br>说什么堵车，全是屁话，谁都看得出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crocodile</b></td><td>ˈcrocodile tears</td><td>鳄鱼的眼泪；假慈悲</td><td>He cried crocodile tears at the funeral of the uncle he'd ignored for years.<br>他在多年不理的叔叔葬礼上挤出几滴鳄鱼的眼泪。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crook</b></td><td>by ˈhook or by ˈcrook</td><td>千方百计；不择手段</td><td>By hook or by crook, I'll get those tickets before the concert sells out.<br>不管用什么办法，我一定在售罄前弄到票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cropper</b></td><td>come a ˈcropper (BrE, informal)</td><td>摔跟头；遭惨败</td><td>He came a cropper on the icy steps and broke his wrist.<br>他在结冰的台阶上摔了一跤，手腕都断了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/talk at cross ˈpurposes</td><td>各说各话；互相误解</td><td>We talked for ten minutes at cross purposes before realizing we meant different people.<br>我们各说各话聊了十分钟，才发现说的不是同一个人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cross a ˈbridge when you ˈcome to it</td><td>问题出现时再解决；船到桥头自然直</td><td>Let's cross that bridge when we come to it instead of worrying about it now.<br>等真出了问题再说吧，现在别瞎操心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cross your ˈbridges when you ˈcome to them</td><td>待问题出现时再设法解决；到时再说</td><td>She always crosses her bridges when she comes to them and never plans ahead.<br>她总是遇到问题再解决，从不提前打算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cross sb's ˈmind</td><td>掠过某人心头；某人想到</td><td>It suddenly crossed my mind that I hadn't seen her for months.<br>我突然想起，好几个月没见到她了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it never ˈcrossed my mind (that…)</td><td>我从未想到；压根没想过</td><td>It never crossed my mind that she would turn down such a generous offer.<br>我从没想过她会拒绝这么优厚的条件。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cross my ˈheart (and hope to ˈdie) (spoken)</td><td>我发誓；千真万确</td><td>I didn't touch your chocolate, cross my heart and hope to die.<br>我真没动你的巧克力，我发誓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cross sb's ˈpath • our/their paths ˈcross</td><td>与某人不期而遇；偶然相遇</td><td>Our paths crossed again at a conference ten years after university.<br>毕业十年后我们在一次会议上又碰上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cross the ˈRubicon (formal)</td><td>破釜沉舟；作出不可逆的重大决定</td><td>By handing in her resignation she crossed the Rubicon and never looked back.<br>递上辞呈那一刻她已破釜沉舟，再没回头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a (heavy) ˈcross to bear</td><td>背负沉重的负担；有难言的苦衷</td><td>Caring for both parents alone, she has a heavy cross to bear.<br>独自照顾双亲，她的担子实在太重。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bear/carry your ˈcross</td><td>背负自己的十字架；默默承受苦难</td><td>Everyone has to bear their own cross, and complaining rarely makes it lighter.<br>人人都有自己的苦要吃，抱怨也轻不了多少。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈlines/ˈwires crossed</td><td>沟通串线；彼此误会</td><td>We got our wires crossed and both showed up at the wrong café.<br>我们沟通串了线，两个人都跑错了咖啡馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have crossed ˈlines/ˈwires (informal)</td><td>话说岔了；沟通有误</td><td>Somewhere along the way we had crossed wires about who was booking the hotel.<br>中间不知哪里说岔了，谁订酒店都没弄清。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at a ˈcrossroads</td><td>处于十字路口；面临重大抉择</td><td>After losing the job he was at a crossroads in his career.<br>丢了工作后，他的事业正处在十字路口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crow</b></td><td>as the ˈcrow flies (informal)</td><td>以直线距离计算</td><td>The village is only five miles away as the crow flies, but twelve by road.<br>那村子直线距离才五英里，走公路却要十二英里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cruel</b></td><td>be ˌcruel to be ˈkind</td><td>忠言逆耳；为对方好而狠心</td><td>Sometimes you have to be cruel to be kind and tell them the truth.<br>有时候必须狠下心说实话，才是真为他好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crunch</b></td><td>if/when it comes to the ˈcrunch (informal)</td><td>到了紧要关头；关键时刻</td><td>When it comes to the crunch, she always backs her team without hesitation.<br>到了关键时刻，她总会毫不犹豫地力挺自己的团队。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's ˈcrunch time (informal)</td><td>关键时刻到了；到了紧要关头</td><td>With two days until the deadline, it's crunch time for the whole department.<br>离截止只剩两天，整个部门都到了拼命的时候。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cry</b></td><td>cry your ˈeyes out</td><td>痛哭；哭得死去活来</td><td>She cried her eyes out when the puppy had to be put down.<br>小狗不得不安乐死时，她哭得眼睛都肿了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cry ˈfoul (informal)</td><td>喊冤；抗议不公</td><td>The losing team cried foul over the referee's decision in the final minute.<br>输球的一方对最后一分钟的判罚大喊不公。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cry ˈwolf</td><td>谎报险情；发假警报</td><td>He's cried wolf so often that nobody believes he's really ill now.<br>他谎报了太多次，现在真病了也没人信。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crying</b></td><td>be a crying ˈshame (spoken)</td><td>太可惜了；令人痛心</td><td>It's a crying shame that such a beautiful old theatre is being demolished.<br>这么漂亮的老剧院要拆掉，真是太可惜了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a crying ˈneed (for sth)</td><td>迫切的需要</td><td>There's a crying need for affordable housing in this part of the city.<br>这一带迫切需要能负担得起的住房。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˌcrying out ˈloud (spoken, informal)</td><td>我的天哪；真是岂有此理</td><td>For crying out loud, will somebody please answer that phone?<br>我的天，谁去接一下电话行不行？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's no good/use crying over spilt ˈmilk</td><td>木已成舟，后悔无用</td><td>The money's gone, and it's no use crying over spilt milk now.<br>钱已经没了，现在后悔也没用。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crystal</b></td><td>ˌcrystal ˈclear</td><td>一清二楚；极易理解</td><td>Let me make one thing crystal clear: nobody leaves until the job's finished.<br>我把话说明白：活儿干完之前谁也不许走。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cudgels</b></td><td>take up the ˈcudgels for sb/sth</td><td>挺身而出支持；毅然力挺</td><td>She took up the cudgels for the students whose grants had been cut.<br>她挺身而出，为被削减助学金的学生说话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cue</b></td><td>(right) on ˈcue</td><td>恰在此时；说来就来</td><td>I mentioned his name and, right on cue, he walked through the door.<br>我刚提到他，他就正好推门进来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take your ˈcue from sb</td><td>效仿某人；照某人的样子做</td><td>Just take your cue from Lisa; she knows how these meetings work.<br>照着丽莎做就行，她熟悉这种会怎么开。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cup</b></td><td>not be sb's cup of ˈtea (informal, spoken)</td><td>非某人所好；不合某人心意</td><td>Opera really isn't my cup of tea, but I'll come along anyway.<br>歌剧真不合我胃口，不过我还是陪你去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cupboard</b></td><td>ˈcupboard love (BrE)</td><td>有所图的假亲热；为好处装亲昵</td><td>The cat only rubs against my legs at dinner time — pure cupboard love.<br>猫只在开饭时蹭我的腿，纯粹是有所图。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play ˈCupid</td><td>做媒；当红娘</td><td>Stop trying to play Cupid; I can find my own girlfriend, thanks.<br>别老想着给我做媒，我自己会找女朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play ˈCupid (humorous)</td><td>扮演爱神；给人牵红线</td><td>My aunt loves to play Cupid at every family wedding she attends.<br>我姑妈每次参加家族婚礼都爱给人牵红线。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the/a ˌcurate's ˈegg (BrE)</td><td>好坏参半的事物</td><td>The new album is a bit of a curate's egg, brilliant in places.<br>这张新专辑好坏参半，有几首确实精彩。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>curiosity</b></td><td>curiosity killed the ˈcat (saying)</td><td>好奇害死猫；过于好奇会惹祸</td><td>Don't open that box — curiosity killed the cat, you know.<br>别开那个盒子，好奇害死猫，你懂的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>curry</b></td><td>curry ˈfavour (with sb) (BrE) (AmE curry ˈfavor (with sb)) (disapproving)</td><td>讨好；奉承拍马屁</td><td>He's always bringing the boss coffee to curry favour with management.<br>他老给老板端咖啡，就为了讨好上头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>curtain</b></td><td>bring/ring down the ˈcurtain (on sth)</td><td>使…落下帷幕；使…结束</td><td>That defeat brought down the curtain on his long international career.<br>那场失利为他漫长的国家队生涯画上了句号。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring/ring the ˈcurtain down (on sth)</td><td>使…结束；为…画上句号</td><td>The company rang the curtain down on the project after three costly years.<br>烧了三年钱之后，公司叫停了这个项目。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the curtain comes down on sth</td><td>…闭幕；…结束</td><td>The curtain came down on the festival with a huge fireworks display.<br>音乐节在一场盛大的烟花中落下帷幕。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>curtains</b></td><td>be ˈcurtains (for sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>完蛋；到头了</td><td>If the bank refuses the loan, it's curtains for the little bookshop.<br>银行要是不批贷款，这家小书店就完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>curve</b></td><td>ahead of/behind the ˈcurve (especially AmE, business)</td><td>领先／落后于趋势</td><td>Their design team stayed ahead of the curve for almost a decade.<br>他们的设计团队领先行业将近十年。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>curveball</b></td><td>throw sb a ˈcurveball (AmE)</td><td>出其不意地为难某人；抛出难题</td><td>The interviewer threw me a curveball with that question about my worst failure.<br>面试官问我最惨的失败，一下把我问懵了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cushy</b></td><td>a cushy ˈnumber (BrE)</td><td>美差；轻松舒服的工作</td><td>Watching the car park all night sounds like a cushy number to me.<br>整晚看着停车场，在我看来算是美差。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cut</b></td><td>be cut ˈout for sb/sth • be cut ˈout to be sth</td><td>天生适合；是做…的料</td><td>I'm just not cut out for office work; I need to be outdoors.<br>我天生不是坐办公室的料，我得在户外干活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a cut aˈbove sb/sth</td><td>略胜一筹；比…强</td><td>Her cooking is a cut above anything else you'll find in this town.<br>她做的菜比这镇上任何一家都强。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cut and ˈrun (informal)</td><td>溜之大吉；急忙逃走</td><td>When the police arrived, his partners decided to cut and run.<br>警察一到，他的同伙就撒腿开溜了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cute</b></td><td>(as) cute as a ˈbutton (AmE)</td><td>小巧可爱（多指婴儿或小物件）</td><td>Their new baby is as cute as a button in that little hat.<br>他们的宝宝戴着小帽子，可爱得不得了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cutting</b></td><td>(be at) the cutting ˈedge (of sth)</td><td>处于（某领域的）最前沿</td><td>This lab is at the cutting edge of cancer research in Europe.<br>这家实验室处在欧洲癌症研究的最前沿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cylinders</b></td><td>firing/working on all ˈcylinders (informal)</td><td>开足马力；全力运转</td><td>With everyone back from holiday, the office is firing on all cylinders again.<br>大家休假回来后，办公室又开足了马力。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dab</b></td><td>be a dab ˈhand at sth/at doing sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>擅长；是行家里手</td><td>My dad's a dab hand at fixing bikes, so bring yours over.<br>我爸修自行车是把好手，把你的推过来吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>daft</b></td><td>(as) ˌdaft as a ˈbrush (BrE, spoken)</td><td>傻里傻气；十分愚蠢</td><td>He's as daft as a brush, but everyone in the office loves him.<br>他傻里傻气的，可办公室里人人都喜欢他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>daggers</b></td><td>be at daggers ˈdrawn (with sb)</td><td>势不两立；剑拔弩张</td><td>The two brothers have been at daggers drawn since their father's will was read.<br>自从宣读父亲遗嘱，兄弟俩就势不两立。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look ˈdaggers at sb</td><td>对某人怒目而视</td><td>She looked daggers at me when I mentioned her ex-husband.<br>我一提她前夫，她就狠狠瞪了我一眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>daily</b></td><td>your daily ˈbread</td><td>生计；每日的口粮</td><td>Driving a taxi at night is how he earns his daily bread.<br>他靠晚上开出租车养家糊口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>daisies</b></td><td>be pushing up (the) ˈdaisies (humorous)</td><td>已经入土；死了</td><td>By the time they finish arguing about it, we'll all be pushing up daisies.<br>等他们吵完，我们早就入土了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>damage</b></td><td>what's the ˈdamage? (BrE, informal)</td><td>要付多少钱？</td><td>That was a great meal — so what's the damage?<br>这顿吃得真好，一共多少钱？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>damn</b></td><td>damn the consequences, expense, etc.</td><td>管它什么后果（或花多少钱）</td><td>He booked the flight anyway, damn the expense, because his sister was ill.<br>他还是订了机票，管它多贵，妹妹病了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>damn it (all) (informal)</td><td>该死；见鬼（表示恼火）</td><td>Damn it, I've left my keys locked inside the car again.<br>见鬼，我又把钥匙锁车里了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>damn sb/sth with faint ˈpraise</td><td>寓贬于褒；用淡淡的赞扬贬低</td><td>The review damned her novel with faint praise, calling it competent but forgettable.<br>那篇书评寓贬于褒，说她的小说尚可却难留印象。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not care/give a ˈdamn (about/for sb/sth)</td><td>毫不在乎；根本不放在心上</td><td>He doesn't give a damn about what the neighbours think of him.<br>邻居怎么看他，他根本不在乎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'll be ˈdamned (old-fashioned, spoken)</td><td>真没想到；真叫人吃惊</td><td>Well, I'll be damned — you actually finished the whole thing yourself!<br>哎哟，真没想到，你居然自己全做完了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'm/I'll be ˈdamned if… (BrE also I'm/I'll be ˈblowed if…) (spoken)</td><td>我决不…；我绝对不会…</td><td>I'll be damned if I apologize to him after what he said.<br>他说了那种话，我才不会向他道歉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do/try your ˈdamnedest (informal)</td><td>竭尽全力；拼尽全力</td><td>We did our damnedest to finish before the deadline, but the server crashed.<br>我们拼了命想赶在截止前完成，结果服务器崩了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>damp</b></td><td>a damp ˈsquib (BrE, informal)</td><td>虎头蛇尾的事；令人扫兴之事</td><td>The much-hyped launch party turned out to be a complete damp squib.<br>炒得沸沸扬扬的发布会最后完全没掀起水花。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>damper</b></td><td>put a ˈdamper on sth (also put a ˈdampener on sth) (informal)</td><td>使扫兴；给…泼冷水</td><td>The bad weather put a damper on our first day at the beach.<br>坏天气让我们海边第一天玩得很扫兴。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>damsel</b></td><td>a ˌdamsel in diˈstress (humorous)</td><td>落难少女；等人搭救的女子</td><td>She hates being treated like a damsel in distress just because she's small.<br>就因为个子小，她讨厌被当成待人搭救的弱女子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dance atˈtendance on sb (BrE, formal)</td><td>殷勤伺候；曲意奉承</td><td>The junior staff were expected to dance attendance on him all afternoon.<br>下属们整个下午都得在他跟前殷勤伺候。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dance to sb's ˈtune (BrE)</td><td>唯命是从；任人摆布</td><td>I'm tired of dancing to his tune every time he changes the schedule.<br>他一改日程我就得跟着转，我受够了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>danger</b></td><td>be on/off the ˈdanger list (BrE)</td><td>处于病危状态；脱离危险</td><td>Her father came off the danger list two days after the operation.<br>手术两天后，她父亲脱离了危险期。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dangerous</b></td><td>dangerous ˈground</td><td>危险话题；棘手处境</td><td>Asking about his divorce is dangerous ground, so let's talk about football.<br>问他离婚的事很犯忌，还是聊球吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dare</b></td><td>don't you ˈdare (do sth)! (spoken)</td><td>你敢！；不许你…</td><td>Don't you dare tell my mother about the parking ticket!<br>你敢跟我妈说罚单的事试试！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how ˈdare you, etc. (spoken)</td><td>你（他等）怎么敢；岂有此理</td><td>How dare you go through my bag without even asking me first!<br>你怎么敢不打招呼就翻我的包！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I dare ˈsay (spoken)</td><td>我想；大概；很可能</td><td>I dare say she's forgotten all about it by now, honestly.<br>说真的，我想她这会儿早忘干净了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dark</b></td><td>a dark ˈhorse (BrE)</td><td>深藏不露的人；黑马</td><td>You're a dark horse — you never told us you could sing!<br>你可真深藏不露，从没说过你会唱歌！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈdark (about sth)</td><td>蒙在鼓里；对…一无所知</td><td>They kept the staff in the dark about the merger until the last minute.<br>直到最后一刻，公司才把合并的事告诉员工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a shot/stab in the ˈdark</td><td>瞎猜；胡乱一试</td><td>It was a shot in the dark, but my guess turned out right.<br>纯属瞎猜，可我居然蒙对了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>darn</b></td><td>darn it! (spoken, especially AmE)</td><td>见鬼；真讨厌（表示恼火）</td><td>Darn it, the store closed five minutes before I got there.<br>真见鬼，我到之前五分钟店就关门了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>darned</b></td><td>I'll be ˈdarned! (spoken, especially AmE)</td><td>真没想到；真让人意外</td><td>Well, I'll be darned, they actually let him back on the team.<br>嘿，真没想到，他们居然让他回队里了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dash</b></td><td>cut a ˈdash (BrE)</td><td>风度翩翩；引人注目</td><td>He cut quite a dash in his white suit at the wedding.<br>他穿一身白西装出席婚礼，格外惹眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>date</b></td><td>out of date</td><td>过时的；过期的</td><td>Half the information on that website is completely out of date.<br>那个网站上一半的信息都过时了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈdate</td><td>迄今为止；到目前为止</td><td>To date we've had over three hundred applications for the single post.<br>到目前为止，这一个职位已收到三百多份申请。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌup to date</td><td>最新的；包含最新信息的</td><td>Please keep the sales figures up to date so I can check them.<br>请把销售数据随时更新，方便我核对。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>daunted</b></td><td>nothing ˈdaunted (BrE, formal)</td><td>毫不气馁；无所畏惧</td><td>Nothing daunted, she climbed back on the horse and rode off.<br>她毫不气馁，重新翻身上马跑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>day</b></td><td>all day and ˈevery day</td><td>天天如此；成天不变</td><td>He plays that same song all day and every day.<br>他天天从早到晚都放那首歌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>all in a day's ˈwork</td><td>家常便饭；分内之事</td><td>Dealing with angry passengers is all in a day's work for her.<br>应付发火的乘客对她来说是家常便饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>any day (now) (spoken)</td><td>就这一两天；很快</td><td>The baby could arrive any day now, so keep your phone on.<br>孩子这一两天就可能出生，手机别关。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈany day (of the week)</td><td>无论何时都；怎么都（表示更喜欢）</td><td>I'd take a quiet beach over a crowded city any day.<br>安静的海滩和拥挤的城市，我怎么都选前者。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>carry/win the ˈday (formal)</td><td>获胜；占上风</td><td>Her calm argument finally carried the day at the committee meeting.<br>她冷静的论述最终在委员会上占了上风。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>day after ˈday</td><td>日复一日；一天又一天</td><td>Day after day he waited by the phone for news from the hospital.<br>他一天又一天守在电话旁等医院的消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>day by ˈday</td><td>一天天地；逐日</td><td>Day by day her Chinese improved until she could argue with taxi drivers.<br>她的中文一天天进步，后来都能跟出租车司机吵架了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>day ˌin, day ˈout</td><td>天天如此；日复一日不间断</td><td>He eats the same sandwich day in, day out, and never complains.<br>他天天吃同一种三明治，从来不抱怨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the day of ˈreckoning (formal)</td><td>算账的日子；遭报应之时</td><td>The accounts were a mess, and the day of reckoning came in April.<br>账目一团糟，四月份终于到了算账的时候。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>don't give up the ˈday job (informal, humorous)</td><td>别丢了老本行（讽刺水平不行）</td><td>That was an interesting song, Dave, but don't give up the day job.<br>戴夫，这歌挺有意思，不过老本行还是别丢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from day ˈone (spoken)</td><td>从第一天起；从一开始</td><td>From day one she knew the job wasn't going to work out.<br>从第一天起她就知道这份工作干不长。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from day to ˈday</td><td>过一天算一天；日复一日地</td><td>They live from day to day, never knowing where the rent will come from.<br>他们过一天算一天，房租都不知道从哪来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from ˌone day to the ˈnext</td><td>一天一个样；变化无常</td><td>His moods change from one day to the next, so nobody knows what to expect.<br>他的情绪一天一个样，谁也摸不准。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have had your/its ˈday</td><td>风光不再；已过全盛期</td><td>Fax machines have definitely had their day in most modern offices.<br>在多数现代办公室里，传真机早就风光不再了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌif he's, she's, etc. a ˈday (informal)</td><td>（说年龄）少说也有；至少</td><td>She's seventy if she's a day, though she still runs marathons.<br>她少说也有七十了，可还在跑马拉松。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in sb's day/time</td><td>在某人的年代；在某人的鼎盛时期</td><td>In my grandfather's day you could buy a house for a few thousand pounds.<br>在我爷爷那年头，几千英镑就能买套房。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈthis day and age</td><td>在当今这个时代</td><td>In this day and age nobody should have to work without a contract.<br>在当今这个年代，谁都不该没有合同就上班。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make sb's ˈday (informal)</td><td>让某人高兴一整天</td><td>Your postcard from Lisbon absolutely made my day.<br>你从里斯本寄来的明信片让我高兴了一整天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈday of it (spoken)</td><td>好好玩上一整天</td><td>Since we're driving all that way, let's make a day of it.<br>既然要开那么远，就干脆玩上一整天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be sb's ˈday (spoken)</td><td>是某人倒霉的一天</td><td>First I missed the bus, then I lost my wallet — not my day.<br>先是错过公交，又丢了钱包，今天真不是我的日子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈone day</td><td>有朝一日；（过去的）某一天</td><td>One day I'll save enough money to travel across South America.<br>总有一天我会攒够钱去南美旅行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈsome day</td><td>将来有一天；总有一天</td><td>Some day you'll look back on all this and laugh about it.<br>将来某一天你回头看这些，会笑出来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take it/things one ˌday at a ˈtime (spoken)</td><td>一天天慢慢来；不去多想以后</td><td>Since the diagnosis he's just taking things one day at a time.<br>确诊之后，他只能一天一天地过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈthat'll be the day (spoken, ironic)</td><td>那才怪呢；根本不可能</td><td>Him cooking dinner for everyone? That'll be the day.<br>他给大家做饭？那才怪呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the ˈday</td><td>恰好；一天不差</td><td>We met exactly ten years ago today, to the day.<br>我们相识到今天正好十年，一天不差。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to this ˈday</td><td>直到今天；至今</td><td>To this day nobody knows who left the flowers on her doorstep.<br>直到今天也没人知道是谁在她门口放的花。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>daylight</b></td><td>ˌdaylight ˈrobbery (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>漫天要价；明抢</td><td>Five pounds for a small coffee is absolute daylight robbery.<br>一小杯咖啡卖五镑，简直是明抢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see ˈdaylight</td><td>恍然大悟；看到希望</td><td>After weeks of confusing accounts, I'm finally beginning to see daylight.<br>对着乱账折腾几周后，我总算看出点门道了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>daylights</b></td><td>beat/scare the (living) ˈdaylights out of sb</td><td>把某人痛打一顿；把某人吓个半死</td><td>That horror film scared the living daylights out of my little brother.<br>那部恐怖片把我弟弟吓得魂都没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>days</b></td><td>your, its, etc. days are ˈnumbered</td><td>时日无多；撑不了多久了</td><td>With sales falling like this, the shop's days are numbered.<br>销量这么跌下去，这家店撑不了多久了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈone of these days</td><td>总有一天；改天</td><td>One of these days I'm going to tell him exactly what I think.<br>总有一天我要把心里话全告诉他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) one of those ˈdays</td><td>诸事不顺的一天</td><td>The printer jammed, then the coffee spilled — it's just one of those days.<br>打印机卡纸，咖啡又洒了，今天真是诸事不顺。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈthese days</td><td>如今；现在（与过去相比）</td><td>These days hardly anyone writes letters by hand any more.<br>如今几乎没人再手写信了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈthose were the days</td><td>那才是好时光；那才叫好年头</td><td>We played football until dark every evening — those were the days!<br>我们每天踢球踢到天黑，那才叫好日子！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have seen/known better ˈdays</td><td>今非昔比；已破旧不堪</td><td>This old jacket has seen better days, but I can't throw it out.<br>这件旧外套早不行了，可我舍不得扔。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dead</b></td><td>cut sb ˈdead</td><td>故意不理睬某人；装作没看见</td><td>She cut me dead in the corridor as if we'd never met.<br>她在走廊里当没看见我，好像从不认识。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dead and ˈburied/gone</td><td>早已过去；不复存在</td><td>That argument is dead and buried, so let's not bring it up.<br>那场争执早就翻篇了，别再提。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) dead as a/the ˈdodo (informal)</td><td>彻底过时；早已绝迹</td><td>Cassette tapes are as dead as a dodo in most people's homes.<br>磁带在多数人家里早就绝迹了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) ˌdead as a ˈdoornail (informal)</td><td>死透了；彻底不动了</td><td>I tried the engine again, but the battery was as dead as a doornail.<br>我又试了一次，可电瓶彻底没电了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a dead ˈcert (informal)</td><td>十拿九稳的事；必胜者</td><td>With that lineup, they're a dead cert for the semi-finals.<br>凭这个阵容，他们进半决赛十拿九稳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a dead ˈduck (informal)</td><td>注定失败的计划；没戏的想法</td><td>Without funding, the whole recycling scheme is a dead duck.<br>没有资金，整个回收计划就是没戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a dead ˈend (informal)</td><td>死胡同；僵局</td><td>The investigation reached a dead end when the only witness disappeared.<br>唯一的证人一消失，调查就走进了死胡同。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be dead in the ˈwater</td><td>（人或计划）已失败；毫无进展</td><td>The merger talks have been dead in the water since last month.<br>合并谈判从上个月起就彻底停摆了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a dead ˈletter</td><td>形同虚设的规定；无人理会的建议</td><td>That old parking rule is a dead letter now; nobody enforces it.<br>那条老停车规定形同虚设，没人执行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a dead ˈloss</td><td>一无是处的人（或物）</td><td>As a plumber he's a dead loss; the leak is worse now.<br>他当水管工一无是处，现在漏得更厉害了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dead ˈmeat (informal)</td><td>死定了；要倒大霉</td><td>If Mum finds out we broke the vase, we're dead meat.<br>要是妈发现花瓶是我们打碎的，我们就死定了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(in) the ˌdead of (the) ˈnight</td><td>深夜；夜深人静时</td><td>They loaded the van in the dead of night so nobody would notice.<br>他们趁夜深人静装车，免得被人看见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˌdead of ˈnight</td><td>在深夜；夜半时分</td><td>The phone rang at dead of night and everyone jumped out of bed.<br>半夜电话响起，所有人都从床上蹦起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a dead ˈringer for sb (informal)</td><td>酷似某人的人</td><td>Your cousin is a dead ringer for that actor in the crime series.<br>你表哥跟那部罪案剧里的演员长得一模一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dead to the ˈworld (informal)</td><td>睡得很沉；不省人事</td><td>After the long flight he was dead to the world by nine.<br>长途飞行之后，他九点就睡得不省人事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dead ˈwood (informal)</td><td>冗员；无用的人（或物）</td><td>The new manager wants to cut out the dead wood in our department.<br>新经理想清掉我们部门的冗员。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sb wouldn't be seen/caught ˈdead… (spoken)</td><td>打死也不会做（某事）</td><td>She wouldn't be seen dead in a pink dress at a wedding.<br>她打死也不会穿粉裙子去参加婚礼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>deaf</b></td><td>(as) deaf as a ˈpost (informal)</td><td>聋得什么也听不见</td><td>Speak up, Grandad's as deaf as a post without his hearing aid.<br>说大声点，爷爷不戴助听器什么都听不见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fall on deaf ˈears</td><td>被置若罔闻；没人理会</td><td>Her warnings about the budget fell on deaf ears at the board meeting.<br>她对预算的警告在董事会上没人听进去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn a deaf ˈear (to sth)</td><td>充耳不闻；不予理会</td><td>The landlord turned a deaf ear to our complaints about the heating.<br>房东对我们关于暖气的投诉充耳不闻。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>deal</b></td><td>cut a ˈdeal (with sb) • cut (sb) a ˈdeal (business)</td><td>（与某人）达成交易</td><td>They cut a deal with the supplier to keep prices fixed for two years.<br>他们和供应商谈成协议，两年内价格不变。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>deal sb/sth a ˈblow • deal a blow to sb/sth</td><td>给…以打击；使…受挫</td><td>The factory closure dealt a blow to the whole town's economy.<br>工厂关闭给全镇经济带来沉重打击。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a raw/rough ˈdeal</td><td>不公正的待遇</td><td>Part-time staff got a raw deal when the bonuses were handed out.<br>发奖金时，兼职员工受到了不公平的对待。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dear</b></td><td>dear ˈme • (dear,) oh ˈdear</td><td>哎呀；天哪（表示担忧或同情）</td><td>Dear me, you've spilt tea all over the new carpet.<br>哎呀，你把茶全洒在新地毯上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for dear ˈlife • for your ˈlife</td><td>拼命地；为了活命</td><td>The rope snapped and she hung on to the branch for dear life.<br>绳子断了，她死命抓住树枝不放。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold sb/sth ˈdear (formal)</td><td>珍视；珍爱</td><td>He holds his grandmother's letters dear and keeps them in a tin.<br>他很珍视祖母的信，放在一个铁盒里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>death</b></td><td>at death's ˈdoor (often ironic)</td><td>生命垂危；病得快不行了</td><td>He's got a slight cold but acts as if he's at death's door.<br>他就是有点感冒，却装得像快不行了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be the ˈdeath of sb (often humorous)</td><td>让某人操碎心；要了某人的命</td><td>These kids and their late-night parties will be the death of me.<br>这帮孩子天天开夜场派对，非把我折腾死不可。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌin at the ˈdeath/kill</td><td>亲眼目睹结局（或败局）</td><td>She stayed up all night to be in at the death of the election.<br>她熬了一整夜，就为亲眼看到选举尘埃落定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth to ˈdeath (informal)</td><td>做得过滥；讲腻了</td><td>That joke has been done to death; try something new tonight.<br>那个段子早被讲烂了，今晚换点新的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like death warmed ˈup (BrE) (AmE like death warmed ˈover) (informal)</td><td>面色极差；累（或病）得要命</td><td>You look like death warmed up — go home and get some sleep.<br>你脸色难看得要命，回家睡一觉吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb to ˈdeath</td><td>处死某人</td><td>Hundreds of prisoners were put to death during those two brutal years.<br>在那残酷的两年里，数百名囚犯被处死。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈdeath</td><td>极其；…得要命</td><td>I was bored to death during that three-hour lecture on tax law.<br>那场三小时的税法讲座把我闷死了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the ˈdeath</td><td>至死方休；战斗到底</td><td>They swore to defend their village to the death.<br>他们发誓要誓死保卫自己的村子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌwork yourself/sb to ˈdeath (informal)</td><td>把自己（或某人）累垮</td><td>He worked himself to death trying to finish the book before Christmas.<br>为了赶在圣诞前写完书，他把自己累垮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>debt</b></td><td>get/ˌrun into ˈdebt</td><td>负债；欠下债务</td><td>They ran into debt after both of them lost their jobs.<br>两人都失业后，他们欠了一屁股债。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>deep</b></td><td>deep ˈdown (informal)</td><td>内心深处；实际上</td><td>He acts confident, but deep down he's terrified of failing again.<br>他装得很自信，其实心底怕极了再失败。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go off the ˈdeep end (informal)</td><td>勃然大怒；情绪失控</td><td>Dad went off the deep end when he saw the scratch on the car.<br>爸看到车上的划痕，一下就炸了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in deep ˈwater(s)</td><td>陷入困境；麻烦缠身</td><td>The company is in deep water after losing its biggest client.<br>丢了最大的客户后，公司陷入了大麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jump in/be thrown in at the ˈdeep end</td><td>一上来就被推去做难事</td><td>On my first day I was thrown in at the deep end with angry customers.<br>上班第一天我就被推去应付发火的顾客。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>default</b></td><td>by deˈfault</td><td>因无人竞争而（获胜）；默认地</td><td>She became captain by default when nobody else wanted the job.<br>没人愿意干，她就顺理成章当上了队长。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in deˈfault of sth (formal)</td><td>因为没有；由于缺乏</td><td>In default of better evidence, the case against him was dropped.<br>因缺乏更有力的证据，对他的指控被撤销。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>defensive</b></td><td>on/onto the deˈfensive</td><td>处于守势；采取戒备姿态</td><td>Every question about the money put him on the defensive immediately.<br>一问到钱的事，他立刻就摆出防守的架势。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>degrees</b></td><td>by deˈgrees</td><td>逐渐地；一点点地</td><td>By degrees the noise died down and the children fell asleep.<br>声音渐渐小了，孩子们都睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>french</b></td><td>déjà ˈvu (from French)</td><td>似曾相识的感觉</td><td>Walking into that kitchen gave me a strange sense of déjà vu.<br>走进那间厨房，我有种奇怪的似曾相识感。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>delusions</b></td><td>delusions of ˈgrandeur (often humorous)</td><td>妄自尊大；自大狂想</td><td>He's got delusions of grandeur since they made him deputy manager.<br>自从当上副经理，他就有点自我膨胀。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>demand</b></td><td>in deˈmand</td><td>需求量大；很吃香</td><td>Good electricians are always in demand in this part of town.<br>这一带好电工总是很抢手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on deˈmand</td><td>一经要求就；按需</td><td>The new service lets you watch any episode on demand.<br>新服务让你随时点播任何一集。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by popular deˈmand</td><td>应大众要求</td><td>By popular demand, the band added a second night in Manchester.<br>应观众要求，乐队在曼彻斯特加演了一场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>demon</b></td><td>the demon ˈdrink (BrE, humorous)</td><td>酒；含酒精的饮料</td><td>He blames the demon drink for everything he said at the party.<br>派对上说的那些话，他全怪罪于酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>demur</b></td><td>without deˈmur (formal)</td><td>毫无异议地；毫不犹豫地</td><td>She paid the extra charge without demur and left quickly.<br>她二话没说付了附加费，很快就走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>den</b></td><td>a den of iniquity/vice (disapproving)</td><td>藏污纳垢之地；罪恶之所</td><td>Their parents called that little jazz club a den of iniquity.<br>他们的父母把那家小爵士俱乐部叫作藏污纳垢之地。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dent</b></td><td>make a ˈdent/ˈhole in sth (informal)</td><td>大大减少；耗掉一大块</td><td>The new roof made a serious dent in our savings this year.<br>换屋顶今年花掉了我们一大笔积蓄。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>department</b></td><td>be sb's deˈpartment (spoken)</td><td>是某人的职责（或专长）范围</td><td>Don't ask me about the wiring; that's really my brother's department.<br>别问我线路的事，那是我哥的专长。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>depth</b></td><td>in ˈdepth</td><td>深入地；彻底地</td><td>We need to discuss the safety report in depth before Friday.<br>周五之前我们得深入讨论这份安全报告。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>deserts</b></td><td>get your (just) deˈserts</td><td>得到应有的报应</td><td>The cheat finally got his just deserts when the club expelled him.<br>那个作弊的人终于遭了报应，被俱乐部开除了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave sb to their own deˈvices</td><td>听任某人自便；不加干涉</td><td>Left to his own devices, he'd eat crisps and play games all day.<br>没人管的话，他能整天吃薯片打游戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>devil</b></td><td>be a ˈdevil (BrE)</td><td>大胆试一次吧；放纵一下</td><td>Go on, be a devil and buy yourself that ridiculous red coat.<br>来吧，大胆点，把那件夸张的红大衣买下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>between the ˌdevil and the deep blue ˈsea</td><td>进退维谷；左右为难</td><td>Stay in a bad job or risk unemployment — between the devil and the deep blue sea.<br>是继续做烂工作还是冒险失业，真是进退两难。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈdevil (old-fashioned)</td><td>极难的事；极讨厌的事</td><td>That old lock is the devil to open in cold weather.<br>天冷的时候那把旧锁难开得要命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌdevil is in the ˈdetail(s)</td><td>细节最要命；魔鬼藏在细节里</td><td>The contract looks fine, but the devil is in the detail.<br>合同看着没问题，可细节最要命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌdevil looks after his ˈown (saying)</td><td>坏人反倒走运；恶人自有魔鬼护佑</td><td>He crashed the car and walked away unhurt — the devil looks after his own.<br>他撞了车却毫发无伤，真是坏人有坏福。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the devil makes work for idle ˈhands (saying)</td><td>游手好闲生是非</td><td>Give the boys a job — the devil makes work for idle hands.<br>给孩子们找点活干，闲着容易生事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˈdevil of a job, nuisance, fellow, etc.</td><td>极费劲的事；极难缠的人</td><td>It was a devil of a job getting the piano up those stairs.<br>把钢琴搬上那道楼梯真是费死劲了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the devil's ˈadvocate</td><td>故意唱反调的人</td><td>Let me play devil's advocate and argue against your plan for a minute.<br>我来唱个反调，暂且反驳一下你的方案。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(the) devil take the ˈhindmost (saying)</td><td>各人顾各人；落后者活该</td><td>In that market it's every trader for himself and devil take the hindmost.<br>在那个市场里人人自顾，落后的活该。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to the ˈdevil! (old-fashioned, spoken)</td><td>滚开；见鬼去吧</td><td>He told his landlord to go to the devil and slammed the door.<br>他叫房东见鬼去吧，然后摔上了门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like the ˈdevil (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>拼命地；飞快地</td><td>We ran like the devil to catch the last train home.<br>我们拼了命地跑，才赶上回家的末班车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>devoured</b></td><td>be devoured by sth</td><td>被（强烈情感）吞噬；心中充满</td><td>He was devoured by jealousy every time she mentioned her old boyfriend.<br>她一提起旧男友，他心里就被嫉妒吞噬。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dice</b></td><td>the ˌdice are loaded aˈgainst sb</td><td>形势对某人不利；毫无胜算</td><td>With no money and no contacts, the dice were loaded against her.<br>没钱没人脉，形势对她极为不利。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dice with ˈdeath (informal)</td><td>玩命；冒生命危险</td><td>Cycling through that junction without lights is dicing with death.<br>不开灯骑车穿那个路口简直是玩命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no ˈdice (spoken, especially AmE)</td><td>不行；没门</td><td>I asked for another week off, but the boss said no dice.<br>我想再请一周假，老板说没门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dicky</b></td><td>ˈdiddly • ˌdiddly-ˈsquat (AmE, informal)</td><td>（多用于否定）一点也没有；毫无</td><td>He knows diddly-squat about engines but insists on fixing the car.<br>他对发动机一窍不通，还非要修车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>die a/the ˈdeath (BrE, informal)</td><td>彻底失败；无疾而终</td><td>Our fundraising appeal died a death once the council withdrew support.<br>议会一撤支持，我们的募捐活动就彻底黄了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>die in your ˈbed</td><td>寿终正寝；善终</td><td>After all those wars he was lucky to die in his bed.<br>打了那么多仗，他能寿终正寝算是幸运。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the die is ˈcast (saying)</td><td>木已成舟；事已定局</td><td>We've signed the lease, so the die is cast now.<br>租约已经签了，木已成舟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>die ˈlaughing (informal)</td><td>笑死了；笑得不行</td><td>I nearly died laughing when he tried to dance at the wedding.<br>他在婚礼上跳舞那会儿，我差点笑死。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>difference</b></td><td>make a, no, some, etc. ˈdifference (to/in sb/sth)</td><td>有（或没有、有些）影响；起作用</td><td>Your age shouldn't make any difference to whether you get the job.<br>你能否得到这份工作，不该跟年龄有关。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>same ˈdifference (spoken)</td><td>还不都一样；没什么区别</td><td>Bus or train, same difference — we'll still be late.<br>坐公交还是坐火车，还不都一样，反正要迟到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>different</b></td><td>be in a different ˈleague</td><td>不是一个档次；高出一大截</td><td>Their new striker is in a different league from the rest of us.<br>他们的新前锋跟我们完全不是一个档次。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a different kettle of ˈfish (informal)</td><td>另一码事；截然不同的事</td><td>Cooking for two is one thing; feeding thirty is a different kettle of fish.<br>给两个人做饭是一回事，喂三十个人完全是另一码事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>different ˈstrokes (for different ˈfolks) (AmE)</td><td>人各有所好</td><td>He collects stamps and I collect records — different strokes for different folks.<br>他集邮我收唱片，各有各的爱好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>difficult</b></td><td>make life ˈdifficult (for sb)</td><td>给某人添麻烦；让某人日子难过</td><td>Losing the keys really made life difficult for everyone that weekend.<br>钥匙丢了，那个周末大家都被折腾惨了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dig</b></td><td>dig deep</td><td>深挖细查；（也指）慷慨解囊</td><td>You'll have to dig deep in the archives to find that letter.<br>你得在档案里深挖，才能找到那封信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dig your ˈheels in (informal)</td><td>拒不让步；固执己见</td><td>She dug her heels in and refused to change the deadline.<br>她死不松口，坚决不肯改截止日期。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dig your own ˈgrave • dig a ˈgrave for yourself</td><td>自掘坟墓；自取灭亡</td><td>By lying to the auditors he was digging his own grave.<br>对审计员撒谎，他这是在自掘坟墓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dig yourself (into) a ˈhole</td><td>使自己陷入难以脱身的困境</td><td>The more he explained, the deeper he dug himself into a hole.<br>他越解释，把自己陷得越深。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dignity</b></td><td>be beˈneath sb's ˈdignity (often ironic)</td><td>有失身份；有损尊严</td><td>Apparently washing his own coffee cup is beneath his dignity.<br>看来自己洗咖啡杯有失他的身份。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stand on your ˈdignity (formal)</td><td>摆架子；坚持要受到应有的礼遇</td><td>She stood on her dignity and refused to answer such a rude question.<br>她摆出架子，拒绝回答这么无礼的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dime</b></td><td>on a ˈdime (AmE) (BrE less frequent on a ˈsixpence)</td><td>在极小的范围内；说停就停</td><td>This little car can turn on a dime in a narrow street.<br>这辆小车在窄街上能原地掉头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌnickel-and-ˈdime (AmE, informal)</td><td>为小钱斤斤计较；微不足道的</td><td>Stop nickel-and-diming the staff over parking fees and coffee.<br>别在停车费和咖啡上跟员工斤斤计较了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get</b></td><td>get your ˈhands dirty</td><td>亲自动手干活；沾手不干净的事</td><td>A good manager isn't afraid to get their hands dirty on site.<br>好经理不怕到现场亲自动手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dirty</b></td><td>dirty great/big (BrE, informal)</td><td>极大的；大得不得了</td><td>There's a dirty great hole in the road outside our house.<br>我们家门口路上有个大得吓人的坑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a dirty ˈword</td><td>犯忌的字眼；忌讳的说法</td><td>In this office the word 'overtime' has become a dirty word.<br>在这间办公室里，「加班」成了忌讳的字眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do the ˈdirty on sb (BrE, informal)</td><td>对某人使坏；暗算某人</td><td>He did the dirty on his partner and took all the profits.<br>他暗算了合伙人，独吞了全部利润。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>disguise</b></td><td>a blessing in disˈguise</td><td>因祸得福；塞翁失马</td><td>Losing that job turned out to be a blessing in disguise.<br>丢了那份工作反倒因祸得福。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dish</b></td><td>ˌdish the ˈdirt (on sb) (informal)</td><td>揭某人的隐私；说人闲话</td><td>After a couple of drinks she started dishing the dirt on her boss.<br>几杯下肚，她开始爆老板的料。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>disposal</b></td><td>at your/sb's disˈposal</td><td>供某人随意使用；由某人支配</td><td>The car and driver are at your disposal for the whole weekend.<br>车和司机整个周末都由你随意支配。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>disservice</b></td><td>do sb a disˈservice</td><td>对某人不公；损害某人</td><td>You do her a disservice by calling her work amateurish.<br>你说她的作品业余，这对她不公平。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>distance</b></td><td>at/from a ˈdistance</td><td>从远处；隔着一段距离</td><td>From a distance the old barn still looks solid enough.<br>从远处看，那座旧谷仓还挺结实。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go the (full) ˈdistance</td><td>坚持到底；打满全场</td><td>Nobody thought the boxer would go the full distance against the champion.<br>没人想到那名拳手能跟冠军打满全场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/into the ˈdistance</td><td>在远处；向远方</td><td>We watched the ferry disappear into the distance from the harbour wall.<br>我们站在防波堤上看渡轮消失在远处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your ˈdistance (from sb/sth)</td><td>与…保持距离；疏远</td><td>Since the argument she's kept her distance from the whole family.<br>自那次争吵后，她一直和全家人保持距离。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep sb/sth at a ˈdistance</td><td>对某人冷淡；不与…亲近</td><td>He keeps new colleagues at a distance until he really trusts them.<br>他对新同事保持距离，直到真正信任对方。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>distraction</b></td><td>could ˈdo with sth (spoken)</td><td>想要；需要</td><td>I could do with a strong coffee before this afternoon's meeting.<br>下午开会前我真想来杯浓咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>could/can do withˈout sth (spoken)</td><td>用不着；不需要（表示厌烦）</td><td>I could do without him telling me what to say all the time.<br>我不需要他时时刻刻教我该怎么说话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>can do withˈout sth (spoken)</td><td>犯不着；巴不得没有</td><td>I can do without your sarcastic comments while I'm trying to concentrate.<br>我正专心呢，用不着你在旁边说风凉话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do's and ˈdon'ts (informal)</td><td>注意事项；须知与禁忌</td><td>The leaflet lists the do's and don'ts of driving in Italy.<br>这份传单列出了在意大利开车的注意事项。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the do's and ˈdon'ts of sth (informal)</td><td>做某事的规矩与忌讳</td><td>She explained the do's and don'ts of choosing and buying your first car.<br>她讲了挑选和购买第一辆车的注意事项。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈdo something for sb/sth (informal)</td><td>使某人（或某物）更好看</td><td>That blue jacket really does something for you.<br>那件蓝外套特别衬你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it/that (just) won't ˈdo • it/that will never ˈdo</td><td>那可不行；那不像话</td><td>Turning up late for every lesson simply won't do.<br>每节课都迟到，这可不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that ˈdoes it (informal)</td><td>够了；我受够了</td><td>Right, that does it — I'm not driving you anywhere again.<br>行了，够了，我再也不开车送你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not ˈdo anything/a lot/much for sb (informal)</td><td>并不使某人显得好看</td><td>That haircut really doesn't do much for you, if I'm honest.<br>说实话，那个发型真不怎么衬你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that will ˈdo (informal)</td><td>行啦；够啦（用于制止）</td><td>That will do, children — put the toys away and sit down.<br>行啦，孩子们，把玩具收好坐下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dog eat ˈdog (informal)</td><td>残酷竞争；你死我活</td><td>It's dog eat dog in this industry; nobody helps a rival.<br>这个行业里你死我活，没人会帮对手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dog sb's ˈfootsteps</td><td>（麻烦或霉运）一直缠着某人</td><td>Bad luck dogged his footsteps throughout that miserable season.<br>那个糟糕的赛季里，霉运一直缠着他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌdog in the ˈmanger</td><td>占着茅坑不拉屎的人</td><td>He won't use the garage himself but won't let us park there, a real dog in the manger.<br>他自己不用车库也不让我们停，真是占着茅坑不拉屎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the dog's ˈbollocks (BrE, taboo, slang)</td><td>顶呱呱的东西；棒极了</td><td>He thinks his new sound system is the dog's bollocks.<br>他觉得自己的新音响棒得不得了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a dog's ˈbreakfast/ˈdinner (BrE, informal)</td><td>一团糟；乱七八糟</td><td>They've made a complete dog's breakfast of the new timetable.<br>新时刻表被他们弄得一团糟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈdog's life (informal)</td><td>悲惨的生活；猪狗不如的日子</td><td>Working double shifts for that pay is a dog's life.<br>拿那点钱上两班倒，日子过得像狗一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>every dog has his/its ˈday (saying)</td><td>人人皆有得意时</td><td>Don't give up now — every dog has his day, remember.<br>现在别放弃，人人都有走运的时候。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give a dog a bad ˈname (and ˈhang him) (saying)</td><td>名声一坏，百口莫辩</td><td>One mistake and nobody trusts him — give a dog a bad name.<br>一次失误就没人信他了，名声坏了难翻身。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>why keep a ˌdog and bark yourˈself? (informal, saying)</td><td>既然有人代劳，何必事必躬亲</td><td>You hired an accountant, so why keep a dog and bark yourself?<br>你都请了会计，何必自己动手？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>doghouse</b></td><td>be in the ˈdoghouse (South African be in the ˈdogbox) (informal)</td><td>惹人生气而受冷落；失宠</td><td>I forgot our anniversary, so I'm in the doghouse again.<br>我忘了结婚纪念日，又要被冷落了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dogs</b></td><td>go to the ˈdogs (AmE also go to hell in a ˈhandbasket) (informal)</td><td>每况愈下；江河日下</td><td>Since the new owners took over, the club has gone to the dogs.<br>新老板接手后，俱乐部就一路衰败下去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>doing</b></td><td>can't be ˈdoing with sth (informal)</td><td>无法忍受；受不了</td><td>I can't be doing with all this paperwork before breakfast.<br>早饭前处理这一堆文件，我实在受不了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take some ˈdoing • take a lot of ˈdoing</td><td>很不容易；相当费事</td><td>Getting all three kids ready by seven takes some doing.<br>七点前把三个孩子都收拾好可真不容易。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what is sb/sth ˈdoing…?</td><td>某人（或某物）怎么会在…</td><td>What is my umbrella doing in the fridge, exactly?<br>我的伞到底怎么会在冰箱里？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>doldrums</b></td><td>in the ˈdoldrums</td><td>情绪低落；（生意）萧条</td><td>Sales have been in the doldrums since the shop moved.<br>搬店之后销售一直很萧条。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>done</b></td><td>be ˈdone for (informal)</td><td>完蛋了；没指望了</td><td>If the rain doesn't stop soon, the whole harvest is done for.<br>雨要是再不停，这一季庄稼就完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get ˈdone for sth/for doing sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>因轻微违法而受处罚</td><td>He got done for speeding on the motorway last Tuesday.<br>他上周二在高速上超速被罚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/have ˈdone with sb/sth (especially BrE)</td><td>与…断绝往来；把…了结</td><td>I've done with lending him money; he never pays it back.<br>我不再借钱给他了，他从来不还。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌover and ˈdone with done and ˈdusted (informal)</td><td>大功告成；全部搞定</td><td>The paperwork is done and dusted, so we can finally relax.<br>文件全部搞定，我们总算能歇口气了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a done ˈdeal (especially AmE)</td><td>板上钉钉的事；已定的安排</td><td>Don't celebrate yet; the transfer isn't a done deal.<br>先别庆祝，转会还没板上钉钉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>done ˈin (informal)</td><td>筋疲力尽</td><td>After moving furniture all day I'm completely done in.<br>搬了一天家具，我彻底累瘫了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the done ˈthing (BrE)</td><td>合乎礼数的做法；得体的举止</td><td>Arriving empty-handed at a dinner party isn't really the done thing.<br>空手去参加晚宴不太合规矩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>done to a ˈturn (BrE)</td><td>烹调得恰到火候</td><td>The lamb came out of the oven done to a turn.<br>羊肉出炉时火候恰到好处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>he, she, etc. has gone/been and ˈdone sth</td><td>竟然干出（蠢事）；怎么搞的</td><td>Now he's gone and told everyone about the surprise party.<br>他倒好，把惊喜派对的事跟所有人都说了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>donkey</b></td><td>ˈdonkey's years (BrE, informal)</td><td>很久很久；好多年</td><td>I haven't seen Maggie in donkey's years — how is she?<br>我好久没见玛吉了，她还好吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈdonkey's years (BrE, informal)</td><td>好多年；很长时间</td><td>She's been teaching at that school for donkey's years now.<br>她在那所学校教书已经好多年了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>doom</b></td><td>ˌdoom and ˈgloom • ˌgloom and ˈdoom</td><td>悲观失望；前景暗淡</td><td>It's not all doom and gloom; sales did rise last month.<br>也没那么悲观，上个月销量确实涨了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>doomsday</b></td><td>till ˈdoomsday (informal)</td><td>直到世界末日；永远</td><td>We could argue about this till doomsday and still not agree.<br>这事我们能吵到世界末日也谈不拢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>door</b></td><td>be on the ˈdoor</td><td>在门口把门（检票）</td><td>Tom's on the door tonight, so tell him you're with the band.<br>今晚汤姆把门，就说你是乐队的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by/through the back ˈdoor</td><td>走后门；通过不正当途径</td><td>He got the job through the back door because his uncle owns the firm.<br>他走后门拿到工作，他叔叔是公司老板。</td></tr>
