<tr><td></td><td>(from) ˌdoor to ˈdoor</td><td>从一处到另一处；挨家挨户</td><td>The journey takes two hours door to door if the traffic behaves.<br>路上不堵的话，门到门要两小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave the ˈdoor open (for/on sth)</td><td>留有余地；不把话说死</td><td>The manager left the door open for him to return next season.<br>经理留了余地，让他下赛季可以回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shut/close the ˈdoor on sth</td><td>拒绝考虑；把…的门堵死</td><td>Signing that contract closes the door on any further negotiation.<br>签了那份合同，就把再谈的门堵死了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>doors</b></td><td>out of ˈdoors</td><td>在户外；露天</td><td>The children spend all summer out of doors, whatever the weather.<br>不管天气如何，孩子们整个夏天都在户外。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>doorstep</b></td><td>on the/your ˈdoorstep</td><td>近在咫尺；就在家门口</td><td>We've got a beautiful park right on our doorstep.<br>我们家门口就有个漂亮的公园。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dose</b></td><td>like a dose of ˈsalts (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>又快又利落地；一下子</td><td>She went through the paperwork like a dose of salts.<br>她处理那堆文件又快又利索。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dot</b></td><td>dot the/your ˌi's and cross the/your ˈt's</td><td>一丝不苟；不放过细节</td><td>Before we sign, let's dot the i's and cross the t's.<br>签字前，咱们把细节都抠清楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈdot (informal)</td><td>准时；一分不差</td><td>She arrives at nine on the dot every single morning.<br>她每天早上九点整准时到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dotage</b></td><td>be in your ˈdotage (often humorous)</td><td>年老糊涂；老眼昏花</td><td>I'm not in my dotage yet — I can still read the timetable!<br>我还没老糊涂呢，时刻表我还看得懂！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in a ˌdouble ˈbind</td><td>进退两难；左右为难</td><td>Refusing puts her in a double bind with both her boss and her family.<br>一拒绝，她在老板和家人之间都难做人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at the ˈdouble (BrE) (AmE on the ˈdouble)</td><td>迅速地；马上</td><td>Get down to the office at the double; the inspector's already here.<br>快点到办公室来，检查员已经到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do a ˌdouble ˈtake</td><td>愣了一下才反应过来</td><td>I did a double take when I saw him wearing a suit.<br>看到他穿西装，我愣了一下才认出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>double ˈDutch (BrE, informal)</td><td>天书；莫名其妙的话</td><td>The instruction manual was complete double Dutch to me.<br>那本说明书对我来说就是天书。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>double or ˈquits (BrE) (AmE ˌdouble or ˈnothing)</td><td>赌注加倍或一笔勾销</td><td>He offered me double or quits on the next hand of cards.<br>他提议下一把牌赌注加倍或一笔勾销。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a double ˈwhammy (informal)</td><td>双重打击</td><td>Rising rents and falling wages were a double whammy for young families.<br>房租涨、工资跌，对年轻家庭是双重打击。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without/beyond (a) ˈdoubt</td><td>毫无疑问；确实无疑</td><td>She is without doubt the best cellist in the whole orchestra.<br>她无疑是整个乐团最好的大提琴手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb the benefit of the ˈdoubt</td><td>姑且相信某人；不妄下断语</td><td>I'll give him the benefit of the doubt and assume he simply forgot.<br>我姑且相信他，就当他是忘了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>doubting</b></td><td>a ˌdoubting ˈThomas</td><td>不见不信的人；多疑者</td><td>Don't be such a doubting Thomas; come and see the results yourself.<br>别这么疑神疑鬼，自己来看看结果。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>doubts</b></td><td>have your ˈdoubts (about sth)</td><td>对某事持怀疑态度</td><td>I have my doubts about whether that roof will survive the winter.<br>那屋顶能不能撑过冬天，我很怀疑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>down</b></td><td>be down to sb/sth (informal)</td><td>由…引起；归因于…</td><td>The team's success is largely down to their new goalkeeper.<br>球队的成功很大程度上归功于新门将。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be down to sth</td><td>只剩下（一点儿）</td><td>We're down to our last packet of coffee, so add it to the list.<br>咖啡只剩最后一包了，记到清单上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌdown and ˈout</td><td>穷困潦倒；流落街头</td><td>He was down and out for two years before the shelter took him in.<br>收容所收留他之前，他潦倒流浪了两年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>down through sth (written)</td><td>在（很长的）一段时间里</td><td>The recipe has been passed on down through the generations.<br>这道菜谱代代相传至今。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>down to sb/sth</td><td>直至；下至</td><td>Everyone came, down to the youngest child in the village.<br>所有人都来了，连村里最小的孩子都来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>down ˈunder (informal)</td><td>在（或去）澳大利亚和新西兰</td><td>My sister spent three years working down under before coming home.<br>我姐在澳洲工作了三年才回国。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>downhill</b></td><td>(all) downˈhill • ˌdownhill all the ˈway</td><td>此后就轻松多了</td><td>Once we passed the exam, it was all downhill from there.<br>考试一过，后面就轻松多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go downˈhill</td><td>每况愈下；走下坡路</td><td>The restaurant has gone downhill since the old chef left.<br>老厨师走后，这家餐厅一路下滑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>down-low</b></td><td>keep it on the ˈdown-low (AmE, slang)</td><td>对…保密；别声张</td><td>Keep it on the down-low, but they're getting engaged next month.<br>别声张，他们下个月要订婚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dozen</b></td><td>by the ˈdozen</td><td>许多；成打地</td><td>Complaints arrived by the dozen after the price increase.<br>涨价之后投诉成堆地涌来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌbaker's ˈdozen</td><td>十三个</td><td>The bakery gave us a baker's dozen instead of the twelve we ordered.<br>面包店给了我们十三个，我们只订了十二个。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drag your ˈfeet/ˈheels</td><td>故意拖延；磨洋工</td><td>The council keeps dragging its feet over repairing the footbridge.<br>议会在修人行桥的事上一直拖着不办。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull yourself up by your (own) ˈbootstraps</td><td>自力更生翻身；白手起家</td><td>He pulled himself up by his bootstraps and now owns three shops.<br>他白手起家，现在有三家店。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(go) down the ˈdrain (BrE also (go) down the ˈplughole) (informal)</td><td>付诸东流；白白浪费</td><td>Ten years of research went down the drain when the lab burned.<br>实验室一烧，十年研究付诸东流。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>draw</b></td><td>draw ˈstraws (for sth)</td><td>抽签（决定某事）</td><td>We drew straws for who had to tell the boss the bad news.<br>我们抽签决定谁去跟老板报坏消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>draught</b></td><td>on ˈdraught (BrE)</td><td>（啤酒）桶装的；散装的</td><td>They've got three local ales on draught at the pub tonight.<br>今晚酒吧有三种本地桶装啤酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be fast/quick on the ˈdraw</td><td>反应敏捷；出手迅速</td><td>He's quick on the draw with a joke whenever things get tense.<br>一有紧张气氛，他总能马上抖个包袱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>draw a ˈblank</td><td>毫无结果；一无所获</td><td>Police searched the woods all day but drew a blank.<br>警方搜了一整天树林，却一无所获。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈdrawing board</td><td>在筹划阶段；尚在考虑中</td><td>The new library is still on the drawing board, sadly.<br>可惜新图书馆还停留在图纸阶段。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dread</b></td><td>shudder/dread to ˈthink (how, what, etc.…)</td><td>不敢想象；想都不敢想</td><td>I dread to think what that repair is going to cost us.<br>我都不敢想那次维修要花我们多少钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dreaded</b></td><td>the ˌdreaded ˈlurgy (BrE, informal, humorous)</td><td>那要命的小毛病（如感冒）</td><td>Half the office is off with the dreaded lurgy this week.<br>这周办公室一半人都染上那要命的感冒请假了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dream</b></td><td>dream ˈon (spoken, informal)</td><td>别做梦了；想得美</td><td>You think he'll pay you back? Dream on!<br>你觉得他会还钱？别做梦了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like a bad ˈdream</td><td>像一场噩梦</td><td>The whole week felt like a bad dream I couldn't wake from.<br>那一整周像一场醒不来的噩梦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not ˈdream of sth/of doing sth</td><td>决不会做；从未想过</td><td>I wouldn't dream of asking her to work on a Sunday.<br>我绝不会叫她周日来上班。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>work/go like a ˈdream (informal)</td><td>十分顺利；性能极佳</td><td>The new engine goes like a dream on the motorway.<br>新发动机在高速上跑得棒极了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dreams</b></td><td>in your ˈdreams (spoken)</td><td>白日做梦；想得美</td><td>A pay rise this year? In your dreams!<br>今年加薪？你做梦吧！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beyond your wildest ˈdreams</td><td>远超想象；做梦也想不到</td><td>The book sold beyond her wildest dreams in the first month.<br>第一个月的销量远远超出她的想象。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dressed</b></td><td>dressed to ˈkill (informal)</td><td>打扮得极为惹眼；花枝招展</td><td>She arrived at the party dressed to kill in scarlet silk.<br>她一身猩红丝裙出现在派对上，惊艳全场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dressed (up) to the ˈnines (informal)</td><td>盛装打扮；穿得极讲究</td><td>Everyone turned up dressed to the nines for the awards dinner.<br>颁奖晚宴上人人都盛装出席。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dribs</b></td><td>in ˌdribs and ˈdrabs (informal)</td><td>零零星星地；一点一点地</td><td>Guests arrived in dribs and drabs all through the afternoon.<br>客人整个下午零零星星地陆续到来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dried</b></td><td>cut and ˈdried</td><td>已成定局；一成不变</td><td>Nothing about this case is cut and dried, so keep an open mind.<br>这案子没有定论，你先别下结论。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>drift</b></td><td>catch/get sb's/the ˈdrift (informal)</td><td>领会大意；抓住要点</td><td>I didn't hear every word, but I got the drift of his complaint.<br>我没听清每个字，但大概明白他在抱怨什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose the ˈdrift/ˈthread of sth</td><td>跟不上思路；找不着头绪</td><td>I lost the thread of the lecture about halfway through.<br>讲座讲到一半我就跟不上思路了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>drink</b></td><td>drink sb's ˈhealth</td><td>举杯祝某人健康</td><td>Let's raise our glasses and drink Anna's health on her birthday.<br>举杯，为安娜的生日祝她健康。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drink sb under the ˈtable (informal)</td><td>把某人喝倒；酒量胜过某人</td><td>She could drink most of the rugby team under the table.<br>橄榄球队大半人都能被她喝趴下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drive a coach and ˈhorses through sth</td><td>明目张胆地钻…的空子</td><td>Their lawyers drove a coach and horses through the new tax rules.<br>他们的律师把新税规的空子钻了个透。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what sb is ˈdriving at</td><td>某人想说的是；某人的言外之意</td><td>I'm not sure what you're driving at — just say it plainly.<br>我不太明白你想说什么，直说吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drive sb inˈsane</td><td>把某人逼疯；让人受不了</td><td>That dripping tap is driving me insane at night.<br>那个滴水的龙头晚上快把我逼疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drive sb out of their ˈmind/ˈwits (informal)</td><td>使某人发疯；让人焦虑万分</td><td>Waiting for the test results drove her out of her mind.<br>等检查结果快把她逼疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drive sb to ˈdrink (often humorous)</td><td>逼得某人借酒浇愁</td><td>These endless meetings will drive me to drink one day.<br>这没完没了的会，总有一天逼我借酒消愁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drive a wedge between A and B</td><td>离间；挑拨使不和</td><td>Gossip slowly drove a wedge between the two old friends.<br>流言渐渐离间了那两位老友。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>driving</b></td><td>the driving ˈforce (behind sth)</td><td>（某事背后的）推动力量；主要推手</td><td>She was the driving force behind the new road safety campaign.<br>她是新一轮道路安全运动的主要推手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈdriving seat (BrE) (AmE in the ˈdriver's seat)</td><td>掌控局面；当家做主</td><td>With the new contract signed, we're finally in the driving seat.<br>新合同一签，我们终于掌握了主动。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drop a ˈbombshell</td><td>抛出惊人消息；投下一颗炸弹</td><td>He dropped a bombshell by announcing his resignation at breakfast.<br>他在早餐时宣布辞职，扔了颗重磅炸弹。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drop a ˈbrick/ˈclanger (BrE, informal)</td><td>无意中失言；说错话闯祸</td><td>I dropped a clanger by asking about his wife — they divorced last year.<br>我一问他太太就说错话了，他们去年离婚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drop ˈdead</td><td>猝死；（也用于）滚开</td><td>He told the reporters to drop dead and walked off.<br>他叫记者们见鬼去，转身就走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drop a ˈhint (to sb) • drop sb a ˈhint</td><td>给某人暗示</td><td>She dropped a hint about wanting a bicycle for her birthday.<br>她暗示想要辆自行车当生日礼物。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drop ˈhints (about sth)</td><td>不断暗示；旁敲侧击</td><td>She's dropped me a few hints about what she'd like for her birthday.<br>她暗示过我几次她想要什么生日礼物。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drop sb ˈin it (BrE, informal)</td><td>害某人陷入尴尬（或麻烦）</td><td>Thanks for dropping me in it by telling Mum where I was.<br>谢谢你告诉我妈我在哪，把我给坑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌdrop in the ˈocean (BrE) (AmE a ˌdrop in the ˈbucket)</td><td>沧海一粟；杯水车薪</td><td>A hundred pounds is a drop in the ocean compared with the repair bill.<br>跟维修账单比，一百镑不过是杯水车薪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drop sb a ˈline/ˈnote (informal)</td><td>给某人写封短信（或便条）</td><td>Drop me a line when you get settled in the new flat.<br>在新公寓安顿好了就写封短信给我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drop ˈnames</td><td>提及名人以抬高自己</td><td>He drops names constantly, as if we care who he met.<br>他老提认识的名人，好像谁在乎似的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fit/ready to ˈdrop (informal)</td><td>累得要垮；筋疲力尽</td><td>After the double shift I was fit to drop.<br>连上两班之后我累得快垮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let sth ˈdrop</td><td>不再提及某事</td><td>Let it drop, will you? Nobody wants to argue tonight.<br>这事就别提了行吗？今晚谁也不想吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>drown</b></td><td>drown your ˈsorrows (informal, often humorous)</td><td>借酒浇愁</td><td>After the interview he went to the pub to drown his sorrows.<br>面试完他去酒吧借酒浇愁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>drowned</b></td><td>like a drowned ˈrat (informal)</td><td>湿得像落汤鸡</td><td>She came in from the storm looking like a drowned rat.<br>她冒着暴雨进来，活像只落汤鸡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>drugged</b></td><td>drugged up to the ˈeyeballs</td><td>用了大量药物（或毒品）</td><td>He was drugged up to the eyeballs after the operation.<br>手术后他被打了一身的药。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>drum</b></td><td>bang/beat the ˈdrum (for sb/sth) (especially BrE)</td><td>为…摇旗呐喊；大力鼓吹</td><td>She's been banging the drum for local libraries all year.<br>她整年都在为本地图书馆奔走呼吁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>drunk</b></td><td>(as) drunk as a ˈlord (BrE) (AmE (as) drunk as a ˈskunk) (informal)</td><td>烂醉如泥</td><td>He came home drunk as a lord and fell asleep on the stairs.<br>他烂醉如泥地回家，倒在楼梯上就睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dry</b></td><td>(as) dry as a ˈbone</td><td>十分干燥；干透了</td><td>The soil in these pots is as dry as a bone.<br>这些花盆里的土干得不能再干了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) dry as ˈdust</td><td>枯燥乏味</td><td>His lecture on drainage law was as dry as dust.<br>他那堂排水法的课枯燥得要命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>milk/suck sb/sth ˈdry</td><td>榨干某人（或某物）</td><td>The agents milked the young singer dry and then dropped her.<br>经纪人把那位年轻歌手榨干后就甩了她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˌdue ˈcourse</td><td>到适当的时候；届时</td><td>You'll receive a written reply in due course, probably next week.<br>你会在适当的时候收到书面答复，大概下周。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not a dry eye in the ˈhouse (humorous)</td><td>全场无不落泪</td><td>When she sang that last song there wasn't a dry eye in the house.<br>她唱最后一首时，全场无不落泪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run ˈdry</td><td>干涸；枯竭；告罄</td><td>The village well ran dry after that long, hot summer.<br>那个漫长炎热的夏天过后，村里的井干了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>duck</b></td><td>(take to sth) like a ˌduck to ˈwater</td><td>如鱼得水；毫不费力就上手</td><td>She took to teaching like a duck to water in her first week.<br>第一周她就把教书干得如鱼得水。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dust</b></td><td>leave sb/sth in the ˈdust (AmE)</td><td>把…远远甩在后面</td><td>Their new model leaves every competitor in the dust on price.<br>他们的新型号在价格上把对手全甩在了后面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let the ˈdust settle (also wait for the ˈdust to settle)</td><td>等尘埃落定；等局势明朗</td><td>Let the dust settle for a week before you talk to him again.<br>等一周尘埃落定，再去跟他谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not see sb for ˈdust (informal)</td><td>某人一溜烟就不见了</td><td>Mention washing up and you won't see him for dust.<br>一提洗碗，他立马就没影了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dusty</b></td><td>a dusty ˈanswer (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>生硬的答复；毫无帮助的回答</td><td>My request for more time got a dusty answer from the committee.<br>我要求延期，委员会给了个冷冰冰的回复。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dutch</b></td><td>ˌDutch ˈcourage (BrE, informal)</td><td>酒后之勇</td><td>He had two whiskies for Dutch courage before the speech.<br>演讲前他喝了两杯威士忌壮胆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈDutch (with sb) (informal)</td><td>各付各的账；平摊费用</td><td>We always go Dutch when the four of us eat out.<br>我们四个出去吃饭一向各付各的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>duty</b></td><td>duty ˈcalls</td><td>公事在身；正事要紧</td><td>I'd love to stay for another coffee, but duty calls now.<br>我真想留下再喝杯咖啡，可正事要紧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on/off ˈduty</td><td>值班；下班</td><td>The nurse goes off duty at eight and won't be back until Monday.<br>护士八点下班，要到周一才回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dying</b></td><td>be ˈdying for sth/to do sth (informal)</td><td>极想；渴望</td><td>I'm dying for a cold drink after that walk up the hill.<br>爬完那座山，我特别想来杯冷饮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈdying of sth (informal)</td><td>…得要死；难受极了</td><td>Open a window, I'm dying of heat in here.<br>开扇窗吧，我在这儿热死了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>till/to/until your ˌdying ˈday</td><td>至死；有生之年</td><td>He'll insist he was right until his dying day.<br>他到死都会坚称自己没错。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>eager</b></td><td>an eager ˈbeaver (informal)</td><td>干劲十足的人；工作热心的人</td><td>The new intern is a real eager beaver, always first in.<br>新来的实习生特别积极，总是第一个到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>eagle</b></td><td>an/sb's ˌeagle ˈeye (informal)</td><td>锐利的目光；火眼金睛</td><td>Nothing escapes the manager's eagle eye on the shop floor.<br>车间里什么也逃不过经理的火眼金睛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ear</b></td><td>be out on your ˈear (informal)</td><td>被突然解雇（或赶出去）</td><td>Turn up late once more and you'll be out on your ear.<br>再迟到一次，你就得卷铺盖走人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beam/grin/smile from ear to ˈear</td><td>笑得合不拢嘴；眉开眼笑</td><td>He was grinning from ear to ear when they announced his name.<br>报到他名字时，他笑得合不拢嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go in ˈone ear and out the ˈother (informal)</td><td>左耳进右耳出；当耳边风</td><td>Everything I say about tidying goes in one ear and out the other.<br>我说的收拾屋子的话，他左耳进右耳出。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have sb's ˈear • have the ear of sb (formal)</td><td>在某人那里说得上话</td><td>She has the ear of the minister, so her opinion carries weight.<br>她在部长那里说得上话，意见很有分量。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have an ˈear for sth</td><td>对…有辨别力；乐感好</td><td>He has a good ear for accents and mimics them perfectly.<br>他对口音很敏感，模仿得惟妙惟肖。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play (sth) by ˈear</td><td>不看乐谱凭听觉演奏；见机行事</td><td>We don't have a plan for the meeting, so let's just play it by ear.<br>会议没什么计划，咱们见机行事吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>earliest</b></td><td>at your earliest conˈvenience (written)</td><td>尽早；方便时尽快</td><td>Please return the signed contract to our office at your earliest convenience.<br>请尽早将签好的合同寄回我们办公室。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>early</b></td><td>the ˌearly bird catches the ˈworm (saying)</td><td>早起的鸟儿有虫吃；捷足先登</td><td>She queued at six to grab the sale item: the early bird catches the worm.<br>她六点就去排队抢特价品，真是早起的鸟儿有虫吃。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>early ˈon</td><td>在早期；在初期阶段</td><td>We realized early on that the software would never be ready by June.<br>我们很早就意识到这软件六月前根本做不完。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>earn</b></td><td>earn a/your ˈcrust (BrE, informal)</td><td>谋生；挣钱糊口</td><td>He drives a taxi at night to earn a crust while writing his novel.<br>他晚上开出租车糊口，白天写小说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌearn your ˈkeep</td><td>挣得自己的开销；值得雇用</td><td>Even the old cat earns his keep by scaring the mice out of the barn.<br>连那只老猫也靠赶走谷仓里的老鼠挣自己的口粮。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>earnest</b></td><td>in ˈearnest</td><td>认真地；郑重地；加紧地</td><td>After the holidays, work on the new bridge finally began in earnest.<br>假期一过，新桥的施工终于正式动了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ears</b></td><td>be all ˈears (informal)</td><td>洗耳恭听；专心地听</td><td>Tell me what happened at the party last night, I'm all ears.<br>快说说昨晚聚会上发生了什么，我洗耳恭听。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be up to your ˈears in sth</td><td>忙于；深陷于；埋头于</td><td>I can't come out tonight, I'm up to my ears in marking papers.<br>今晚我出不去，改卷子改得焦头烂额。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come to/reach sb's ˈears</td><td>传入某人耳中；终于让某人知道</td><td>News of the merger reached his ears long after everyone else knew.<br>合并的消息传到他耳朵里时，别人早都知道了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>his, her, etc. ˈears are burning</td><td>耳朵发热（觉得有人在议论自己）</td><td>We were talking about Tom all afternoon, so his ears must be burning.<br>我们整个下午都在说汤姆，他耳朵准发热了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>his, her, etc. ˈears are flapping (BrE, informal)</td><td>有人在竖着耳朵偷听；隔墙有耳</td><td>Lower your voice, the neighbour's ears are flapping over the garden fence.<br>小点声，隔壁正隔着篱笆竖着耳朵听呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shut/close your ˈears to sb/sth</td><td>对…充耳不闻；不理会</td><td>He simply shut his ears to every warning his colleagues gave him.<br>同事们的警告他一概充耳不闻。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>earshot</b></td><td>out of ˈearshot (of sb/sth)</td><td>在听力所及范围之外</td><td>She waited until the children were out of earshot before mentioning the divorce.<br>她等孩子们走远听不见了才提起离婚的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>within ˈearshot (of sb/sth)</td><td>在听力所及范围之内</td><td>Don't say anything about the surprise while Grandma is within earshot.<br>奶奶还听得见，别提惊喜的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>earth</b></td><td>bring sb/come (back) down to ˈearth (with a ˈbang, ˈbump, etc.)</td><td>（使）回到现实；（使）美梦破灭</td><td>The rejection letter brought him back down to earth with a bump.<br>那封拒信一下子把他打回了现实。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cost/pay/charge the ˈearth (BrE, informal)</td><td>花（或索要）一大笔钱</td><td>That little handbag looks plain but it must have cost the earth.<br>那只小包看着普通，肯定贵得吓人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to ˈearth/ˈground (BrE)</td><td>躲藏起来；藏匿避风头</td><td>After the robbery the gang went to ground in a farmhouse for weeks.<br>抢劫之后，那伙人在一处农舍躲了好几个星期。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how, what, why, etc. on ˈearth... (informal)</td><td>（表示惊讶或强调）究竟；到底</td><td>How on earth did you manage to lose your passport twice in one week?<br>你到底是怎么做到一周丢两次护照的？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like nothing on ˈearth</td><td>难看极了；难受极了</td><td>After three nights without sleep she looked like nothing on earth.<br>三夜没睡，她看上去糟糕透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nothing on ˈearth (informal)</td><td>任何东西都不；无论如何也不</td><td>Nothing on earth would persuade me to go back and work for him.<br>说什么我也不会回去给他干活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run sb/sth to ˈearth/ˈground (informal)</td><td>（长期搜寻后）终于找到</td><td>The reporter finally ran the missing witness to earth in a seaside hotel.<br>记者最终在一家海边旅馆找到了失踪的证人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ease</b></td><td>at (your) ˈease</td><td>自在；放松；不拘束</td><td>Her warm smile put the nervous candidates completely at their ease.<br>她温暖的笑容让紧张的应聘者彻底放松下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(stand) at ˈease</td><td>（军队口令）稍息</td><td>The sergeant barked at the recruits to stand at ease before the inspection.<br>检阅前，军士喝令新兵稍息。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>easier</b></td><td>easier said than ˈdone (saying)</td><td>说起来容易做起来难</td><td>Saving half your salary every month is easier said than done.<br>每月存下一半工资，说起来容易做起来难。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>easy</b></td><td>ˌeasy ˈgame</td><td>易受攻击的对象；容易上钩的人</td><td>Tourists with open backpacks are easy game for pickpockets in this square.<br>背着敞口背包的游客在这个广场上是扒手的活靶子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌeasy ˈmoney</td><td>来得容易的钱；不义之财</td><td>He thought reselling concert tickets was easy money until the police called.<br>他以为倒卖演唱会门票是轻松来钱，直到警察找上门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌeasy on the ˈeye, ˈear, etc.</td><td>悦目；悦耳</td><td>The new website is simple and very easy on the eye.<br>新网站简洁，看着很舒服。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈeasy on sb (informal)</td><td>对某人别太苛刻；温和对待某人</td><td>Go easy on him, it's only his second day behind the counter.<br>别太严厉，他站柜台才第二天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈeasy on sth</td><td>节约使用；少用一点</td><td>Go easy on the chilli, my parents can't handle spicy food at all.<br>辣椒少放点，我爸妈完全吃不了辣。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have an easy ˈtime of it (BrE, informal)</td><td>日子过得顺当；境况轻松</td><td>Nurses on the night shift certainly don't have an easy time of it.<br>上夜班的护士日子可真不轻松。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'm ˈeasy (BrE, informal)</td><td>（表示无所谓）我都可以</td><td>Pizza or noodles? I'm easy, you two decide tonight.<br>披萨还是面条？我都行，你俩定吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈeasy street (AmE)</td><td>生活优裕；不愁吃穿</td><td>One good patent and the whole family was suddenly on easy street.<br>一项好专利，全家一下子就衣食无忧了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the easy way ˈout</td><td>选择最省事的解决办法</td><td>Instead of apologizing, he took the easy way out and just quit.<br>他没道歉，图省事直接辞职了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take it/things ˈeasy (informal)</td><td>放松；别着急；别激动</td><td>The doctor told her to take things easy for at least two weeks.<br>医生让她至少休养两周，别太累。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>eat</b></td><td>eat sb aˈlive (informal)</td><td>严厉责骂某人；彻底击败某人</td><td>Walk into that debate unprepared and they will eat you alive.<br>毫无准备就上台辩论，他们会把你吃得连渣都不剩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌeat, drink and be ˈmerry (saying)</td><td>及时行乐</td><td>It's your last night in Rome, so eat, drink and be merry.<br>这是你在罗马的最后一晚，好好吃喝玩乐吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>eat your ˈheart out (spoken)</td><td>（夸自己更胜一筹）某某该羡慕了</td><td>Look at my homemade pasta. Eat your heart out, Italian chefs!<br>瞧我做的手擀意面，意大利大厨都得眼红。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>eat your ˈheart out (for sb/sth) (especially BrE)</td><td>因得不到而伤心；苦苦思念</td><td>She spent that whole winter eating her heart out for a man who never wrote.<br>那整个冬天她都在为一个从不来信的男人黯然神伤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌeat humble ˈpie (BrE) (AmE eat ˈcrow)</td><td>低头认错；忍辱道歉</td><td>When the figures proved him wrong, the manager had to eat humble pie.<br>数据证明他错了，经理只好低头认错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>eat like a ˈbird</td><td>吃得很少</td><td>She eats like a bird, half a sandwich and she's already full.<br>她吃得跟小鸟似的，半个三明治就饱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>eat like a ˈhorse</td><td>吃得很多；食量惊人</td><td>My teenage son is thin but he eats like a horse every evening.<br>我那十几岁的儿子很瘦，可每天晚上吃得像头牛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>eat sb out of ˌhouse and ˈhome (informal, often humorous)</td><td>把某人的食物吃个精光</td><td>Three hungry students stayed a week and ate us out of house and home.<br>三个饿坏了的学生住了一周，把我家吃了个精光。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>eat your ˈwords</td><td>收回前言；承认自己说错</td><td>You said I'd never finish the marathon, now eat your words.<br>你说我跑不完马拉松，现在收回你的话吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I could eat a ˈhorse (spoken)</td><td>我饿极了</td><td>Is dinner nearly ready? I skipped lunch and I could eat a horse.<br>饭快好了吗？我没吃午饭，饿得能吞下一头牛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'll eat my ˈhat! (spoken)</td><td>（表示几无可能）我才不信呢</td><td>If that lazy team wins the cup, I'll eat my hat.<br>那支懒散的队要是能夺冠，我把帽子吃了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>he, she, etc. won't ˈeat you (informal)</td><td>他（她）又不会吃了你</td><td>Just knock on the boss's door and ask, she won't eat you.<br>去敲老板的门问一声，她又不会吃了你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>eating</b></td><td>what's ˈeating sb? (spoken)</td><td>某人为何发愁（或不高兴）</td><td>He's been slamming doors all morning, what's eating him?<br>他一上午都在摔门，到底怎么了？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ebb</b></td><td>the ˌebb and ˈflow (of sb/sth)</td><td>潮起潮落；盛衰消长</td><td>The novel traces the ebb and flow of a marriage over thirty years.<br>这部小说描写了一段婚姻三十年的起起落落。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>economical</b></td><td>economical with the ˈtruth</td><td>说话有所隐瞒；不全说实话</td><td>The minister wasn't lying exactly, just being economical with the truth.<br>部长算不上撒谎，只是没把话说全。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈedge off sth</td><td>减轻；缓和；使不那么强烈</td><td>A hot bath took the edge off the pain in her shoulders.<br>洗个热水澡缓解了她肩膀的疼痛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>educated</b></td><td>an ˌeducated ˈguess</td><td>有根据的猜测；有把握的估计</td><td>I'd make an educated guess that the repairs will cost about two thousand.<br>我大致估摸修理费在两千左右。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>effect</b></td><td>bring/put sth into efˈfect</td><td>实施；使生效</td><td>The council will bring the new parking rules into effect next Monday.<br>市政会下周一起实施新的停车规定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come/go into efˈfect</td><td>（法律、规章等）开始生效</td><td>The ban on plastic bags comes into effect at the start of next year.<br>塑料袋禁令将于明年年初生效。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in efˈfect</td><td>事实上；实际上</td><td>He still signs the letters, but in effect his daughter runs the company.<br>信还是他签，可实际上是女儿在管公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of/to no efˈfect</td><td>无效；没有达到预期效果</td><td>She argued with the referee for ten minutes, but to no effect.<br>她跟裁判争了十分钟，一点用也没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take efˈfect</td><td>见效；开始起作用</td><td>Wait twenty minutes for the painkiller to take effect before you drive.<br>等二十分钟让止痛药起效再开车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the effect that... ◆ to this/that efˈfect</td><td>大意是；意思是说</td><td>He left a note to the effect that he would not be coming back.<br>他留了张条，大意是说他不回来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to good, little, etc. efˈfect</td><td>效果好（或不大等）</td><td>She used her three minutes to great effect and won the whole room over.<br>她把那三分钟用得极好，赢得了全场支持。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with effect from... ◆ with immediate efˈfect</td><td>自…起实行；立即生效</td><td>Ticket prices will rise with effect from the first of April.<br>票价自四月一日起上调。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>effing</b></td><td>effing and ˈblinding (BrE, informal)</td><td>骂骂咧咧；满嘴脏话</td><td>The driver got out effing and blinding about the dent in his bumper.<br>司机下了车，对着凹进去的保险杠骂骂咧咧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>egg</b></td><td>(have) ˈegg on your face (informal)</td><td>出丑；丢脸</td><td>The minister was left with egg on his face when the figures turned out wrong.<br>数据被证明是错的，部长丢尽了脸。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put all your eggs into one ˈbasket</td><td>孤注一掷；把全部希望寄托于一事</td><td>Apply to several universities, don't put all your eggs into one basket.<br>多申请几所大学，别在一棵树上吊死。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>eight</b></td><td>be/have one over the ˈeight (informal)</td><td>喝多了；微醉</td><td>Judging by his singing, Dave has had one over the eight tonight.<br>听他那唱腔，戴夫今晚是喝多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your ˌelders and ˈbetters</td><td>长辈；前辈</td><td>Grandma always said children should listen to their elders and betters.<br>奶奶总说小孩子该听长辈的话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>elbow</b></td><td>at your ˈelbow</td><td>在手边；在近旁</td><td>He writes with a strong coffee and an old dictionary at his elbow.<br>他写作时手边总放着浓咖啡和一本旧词典。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈelbow grease (informal)</td><td>（干活出的）力气；体力活</td><td>That old stove will shine again with soap and a bit of elbow grease.<br>那台旧炉子用肥皂加把力气擦擦还能亮起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈelbow room (informal)</td><td>活动余地；回旋空间</td><td>The new budget gives the department some elbow room for research.<br>新预算给这个部门留了些做研究的余地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb the ˈelbow (BrE, informal)</td><td>与某人绝交；甩掉某人</td><td>She finally gave him the elbow after he forgot her birthday again.<br>他又忘了她生日，她终于把他甩了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>elder</b></td><td>an ˌelder ˈstatesman</td><td>资深政治家；德高望重的元老</td><td>Now retired, he acts as an elder statesman for the younger members.<br>他已退休，如今给年轻成员当元老顾问。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>or ˈelse</td><td>否则；要不然（含威胁意味）</td><td>Hand in the report by Friday, or else you'll be explaining it to the boss.<br>周五前交报告，否则你自己跟老板解释去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>something ˈelse</td><td>了不起的人（或事物）；与众不同</td><td>You have to hear her sing live, that voice is really something else.<br>你得听她现场唱，那嗓子真是绝了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>embarrassment</b></td><td>an emˌbarrassment of ˈriches</td><td>好东西太多难以取舍</td><td>With four excellent candidates, the panel faced an embarrassment of riches.<br>四位候选人都很优秀，评委反倒难以取舍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>embryo</b></td><td>in ˈembryo</td><td>尚在萌芽阶段；处于初期</td><td>The festival existed only in embryo when we first discussed it.<br>我们最初谈起时，这个音乐节还只是个雏形。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>emperor</b></td><td>the ˌemperor's new ˈclothes</td><td>皇帝的新装（众人不敢说破的虚假）</td><td>Critics called the whole project a case of the emperor's new clothes.<br>评论家说整个项目就是一场皇帝的新装。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌemperor has no ˈclothes</td><td>皇帝没穿衣服（其实并不出色）</td><td>One junior analyst finally said the emperor has no clothes, and the room fell silent.<br>一个初级分析师终于说破了真相，全场鸦雀无声。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>empty</b></td><td>the ˌempty ˈnest</td><td>空巢（子女离家后的家庭）</td><td>They bought a puppy to fill the empty nest after their son left.<br>儿子走后，他们养了只小狗来填补空巢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on an empty ˈstomach</td><td>空腹；未进食</td><td>Never take these tablets on an empty stomach, they'll make you sick.<br>千万别空腹吃这些药，会难受的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>enchilada</b></td><td>the whole enchiˈlada (AmE, informal)</td><td>全部；一切</td><td>He wants the corner office, the car, the whole enchilada.<br>他要角落的办公室、要车，什么都想要。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>end</b></td><td>at the ˌend of the ˈday (BrE, spoken)</td><td>归根结底；说到底</td><td>At the end of the day, it's your money and your decision.<br>说到底，钱是你的，主意也该你拿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be at an ˈend (formal)</td><td>结束；告终</td><td>After forty years of service, his career at the bank was at an end.<br>在银行干了四十年，他的职业生涯到此结束。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be at the ˌend of your ˈtether (BrE) (AmE be at the ˌend of your ˈrope)</td><td>忍无可忍；筋疲力尽</td><td>With three sick children at home, she was at the end of her tether.<br>家里三个孩子都病了，她已经撑到极限。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be the ˈend (BrE, spoken)</td><td>让人无法忍受；讨厌至极</td><td>Honestly, that man is the end, he complains about everything.<br>说真的，那人烦死了，什么都要抱怨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈend</td><td>最后；终于</td><td>We argued for hours and in the end just tossed a coin.<br>我们争了几小时，最后干脆抛硬币决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>days, weeks, etc. on ˈend</td><td>连续数日（或数周等）</td><td>It rained for days on end and the campsite turned into mud.<br>连着下了好几天雨，营地成了一片泥浆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be the ˌend of the ˈworld (spoken)</td><td>不是世界末日；没那么糟</td><td>If you fail the test, it's not the end of the world, you can retake it.<br>考砸了也不是世界末日，还能重考。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌend of the ˈroad/line</td><td>穷途末路；最终结局</td><td>When the bank refused another loan, it was the end of the road for the shop.<br>银行拒绝再贷款，这家店也就走到头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ends</b></td><td>make (both) ends ˈmeet</td><td>使收支相抵；勉强维持生活</td><td>With rent this high, two salaries barely make ends meet.<br>房租这么贵，两份工资也就勉强够花。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the ˌends of the ˈearth</td><td>天涯海角；任何遥远的地方</td><td>He said he would follow her to the ends of the earth.<br>他说他愿意跟着她走到天涯海角。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>english</b></td><td>in plain ˈEnglish</td><td>用简单明了的话说</td><td>Can you explain the contract in plain English for the rest of us?<br>你能用大白话给我们解释一下合同吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>englishman</b></td><td>an ˌEnglishman's ˌhome is his ˈcastle (BrE) (saying)</td><td>英国人的家就是他的城堡</td><td>He locked the gate and muttered that an Englishman's home is his castle.<br>他锁上大门，嘟囔说自己的家就是自己的城堡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌman's ˌhome is his ˈcastle (AmE) (saying)</td><td>家是私人领地，不容他人干涉</td><td>You can't just walk in here, a man's home is his castle.<br>你不能就这么闯进来，家是人家的地盘。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>engraved</b></td><td>be engraved on/in your ˈheart/ˈmemory/ˈmind</td><td>铭记在心；刻骨难忘</td><td>That last summer by the lake is engraved on my memory forever.<br>湖边的最后一个夏天永远刻在我记忆里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>enough</b></td><td>ˌcuriously, ˌfunnily, ˌstrangely, etc. eˈnough</td><td>说来奇怪；有趣的是</td><td>Funnily enough, I was just thinking about you when you called.<br>说来也巧，你打来时我正想着你呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>eˌnough is eˈnough (saying)</td><td>够了；适可而止</td><td>I've covered his shifts three times this month, enough is enough.<br>这个月我替他值了三次班，够了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have had eˈnough (of sb/sth)</td><td>受够了；忍无可忍</td><td>I've had enough of these excuses, just finish the job.<br>这些借口我听够了，把活干完吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>enter</b></td><td>enter sb's ˈhead</td><td>被某人想到；进入某人脑中</td><td>It never entered my head that she might say no.<br>我压根没想过她会拒绝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>enter sb's/your ˈname (for sth)</td><td>为某人（或自己）报名参加</td><td>Her father entered her name for the piano competition without telling her.<br>她父亲没告诉她就给她报了钢琴比赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/enter into the ˈspirit of sth</td><td>全情投入；融入气氛</td><td>Even the shy new intern entered into the spirit of the office party.<br>连腼腆的新实习生也玩进了办公室派对的气氛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>entirety</b></td><td>in its/their enˈtirety</td><td>整个地；作为一个整体</td><td>The speech was broadcast in its entirety on the evening news.<br>这篇讲话在晚间新闻中全文播出。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>envy</b></td><td>be the ˈenvy of sb/sth</td><td>令…羡慕；是…羡慕的对象</td><td>Their public transport system is the envy of every neighbouring city.<br>他们的公共交通系统让周边城市都羡慕。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>equal</b></td><td>be without ˈequal ◆ have no ˈequal (formal)</td><td>无与伦比；无人能及</td><td>As a cellist of her generation, she is quite without equal.<br>在同代大提琴家中，她无人能及。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on equal ˈterms (with sb/sth)</td><td>与…平起平坐；地位平等</td><td>The small firm now competes on equal terms with the big studios.<br>这家小公司如今能和大制片厂平起平坐地竞争了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the same ˈterms (as sb/sth)</td><td>与…条件相同；待遇一样</td><td>Part-time staff are paid on the same terms as everyone else here.<br>这里的兼职员工和其他人待遇相同。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>some ˌanimals are more ˈequal than others (saying)</td><td>有些人比别人更享特权</td><td>The boss's nephew got the promotion; some animals are more equal than others.<br>老板的侄子升职了，有些人就是比别人更平等。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of the ˈessence</td><td>极其重要；必不可少</td><td>Speed is of the essence if we want to catch the last ferry.<br>想赶上末班渡轮，快是关键。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>even</b></td><td>ˌeven ˈnow/then</td><td>即使现在（那时）；尽管如此</td><td>He apologized twice, but even now she refuses to speak to him.<br>他道了两次歉，可她到现在还是不理他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌeven the ˈscore</td><td>扯平；报复</td><td>They beat us last season, so tonight we're here to even the score.<br>上赛季他们赢了我们，今晚我们是来扯平的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌeven ˈso</td><td>尽管如此；即便这样</td><td>The tickets were expensive; even so, the concert was worth every penny.<br>票很贵，尽管如此，这场音乐会还是很值。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have an even ˈchance (of doing sth)</td><td>有一半的机会；成败各半</td><td>The doctors say she has an even chance of making a full recovery.<br>医生说她完全康复的机会有一半。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>event</b></td><td>in the eˈvent</td><td>结果；到头来（与预期相反）</td><td>We feared a storm, but in the event the wedding day was sunny.<br>我们担心会有暴风雨，结果婚礼那天阳光明媚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the event of sth ◆ in the event that sth</td><td>如果发生…；万一…</td><td>In the event of a power cut, the emergency lights come on automatically.<br>万一停电，应急灯会自动亮起。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>money, winning, etc. isn't ˈeverything</td><td>金钱（或取胜等）并非最重要</td><td>He turned down the offer, saying money isn't everything at his age.<br>他拒绝了这份工作，说到他这年纪钱不是一切。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn King's/Queen's ˈevidence (BrE) (AmE turn State's ˈevidence)</td><td>指证同伙以求从轻发落</td><td>The youngest robber turned Queen's evidence and named the other three.<br>那个最年轻的劫匪转做污点证人，供出了另外三人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>evil</b></td><td>the evil ˈhour/ˈday/ˈmoment</td><td>难熬的时刻；不愉快的日子</td><td>He kept watching videos to put off the evil hour of writing his essay.<br>他一直看视频，好推迟写论文那个难熬的时刻。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb the evil ˈeye</td><td>恶狠狠地瞪某人一眼</td><td>The old woman gave the noisy boys the evil eye across the bus.<br>老太太隔着车厢恶狠狠地瞪了那几个吵闹的男孩一眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>example</b></td><td>make an exˈample of sb</td><td>惩罚某人以儆效尤</td><td>The head teacher made an example of him to stop others cheating.<br>校长拿他开刀，以免别人再作弊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the exˈception that proves the ˈrule (saying)</td><td>证明规律存在的例外</td><td>He's the one honest politician here, the exception that proves the rule.<br>他是这里唯一诚实的政客，正是那个证明通例的例外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take exˈception to sth</td><td>对…表示不满（或反对）</td><td>I take exception to your suggestion that I did it purely for money.<br>我不能接受你暗示我这么做纯粹是为了钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without exˈception</td><td>毫无例外；一律</td><td>Every essay, without exception, must be handed in before noon.<br>所有论文一律必须在中午前交。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>excuse</b></td><td>exˈcuse me</td><td>对不起；劳驾；打扰一下</td><td>Excuse me, is this seat taken or may I sit here?<br>劳驾，这位子有人吗，我可以坐吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>existence</b></td><td>the bane of sb's life/existence</td><td>某人的祸根；烦恼的根源</td><td>That leaking roof has been the bane of my life all winter.<br>那个漏雨的屋顶让我整个冬天不得安宁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>expect</b></td><td>what (else) do you exˈpect? (spoken)</td><td>你还指望什么呢</td><td>You left the door open all night, so what do you expect?<br>你整夜开着门，还能指望什么呢？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>against/contrary to (all) expecˈtations</td><td>出乎意料；与预期相反</td><td>Against all expectations, the little team reached the final that year.<br>出乎所有人意料，那支小球队那年打进了决赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>expected</b></td><td>be (only) to be exˈpected</td><td>是意料之中的；很正常</td><td>A few mistakes in the first week are only to be expected.<br>头一周出点差错是很正常的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>expecting</b></td><td>be exˈpecting (informal)</td><td>怀孕；有孕</td><td>She's expecting again, due some time around Christmas.<br>她又怀孕了，预产期在圣诞节前后。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>expense</b></td><td>at sb's exˈpense</td><td>由某人付账；拿某人取笑</td><td>The whole trip was arranged at the company's expense.<br>整趟旅行的费用都由公司承担。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at the expense of sb/sth</td><td>以牺牲…为代价</td><td>He built the business at the expense of his health and his marriage.<br>他把生意做起来，代价是健康和婚姻。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to the exˈpense of sth/of doing sth</td><td>破费做某事</td><td>They went to the expense of hiring a band for the anniversary party.<br>他们不惜花钱为周年派对请了乐队。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to a lot of, great, etc. exˈpense</td><td>花很多钱；大破费</td><td>Please don't go to a lot of expense, a simple dinner is fine.<br>别太破费了，简单吃顿饭就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb to the exˈpense of sth/of doing sth</td><td>使某人破费做某事</td><td>The delay put us to the expense of booking another hotel room.<br>延误害得我们又花钱订了一间旅馆房。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb to a lot of, great, etc. exˈpense</td><td>使某人花很多钱</td><td>Sending the piano abroad put her parents to considerable expense.<br>把钢琴运到国外让她父母花了不少钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>experience</b></td><td>put sth down to exˈperience (also chalk it up to exˈperience especially AmE)</td><td>吃一堑长一智；当作教训</td><td>We lost the deposit, so let's just put it down to experience.<br>定金打了水漂，就当买个教训吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>explain</b></td><td>exˈplain yourself</td><td>为自己的行为辩解</td><td>You came home at three in the morning, now explain yourself.<br>你凌晨三点才回家，说清楚是怎么回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>extreme</b></td><td>boring, silly, etc. in the exˈtreme</td><td>极其乏味（或愚蠢等）</td><td>His speech about tax forms was boring in the extreme.<br>他那篇讲报税表的发言无聊透顶。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>extremes</b></td><td>go to exˈtremes</td><td>走极端；做得过分</td><td>She goes to extremes, cleaning the kitchen floor three times a day.<br>她做事太极端，一天擦三遍厨房地板。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>carry/take sth to exˈtremes</td><td>把某事做得过火</td><td>Being careful is fine, but you're taking it to extremes by never going out.<br>谨慎是好事，可你从不出门就过头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>eye</b></td><td>an ˌeye for an ˈeye (and a ˌtooth for a ˈtooth) (saying)</td><td>以眼还眼，以牙还牙</td><td>Their whole feud runs on an eye for an eye and nobody ever wins.<br>他们这场世仇就是以眼还眼，谁也没赢过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈeye in (BrE)</td><td>（球类中）找到手感；目测变准</td><td>Once she got her eye in, she hit four boundaries in a row.<br>一找到手感，她连着打出四个边界球。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give your eye ˈteeth for sth/to do sth (informal)</td><td>极想得到某物；不惜代价想做某事</td><td>Any young pianist would give their eye teeth for a chance like this.<br>任何年轻钢琴家都会为这样的机会付出一切。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>formal</b></td><td>have an ˈeye for sth</td><td>对…有眼光；判断准确</td><td>She has a good eye for colour and puts outfits together beautifully.<br>她对色彩很有眼光，衣服搭得漂亮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your ˈeye on sb/sth</td><td>留意某人；看中某物</td><td>I've had my eye on that little flat by the river for months.<br>河边那套小公寓我已经惦记好几个月了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have an eye to/for the main ˈchance (BrE, disapproving)</td><td>善于抓住机会为己谋利</td><td>With an eye to the main chance, he bought the land before prices rose.<br>他很会算计，赶在涨价前买下了那块地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have one eye/half an eye on sth</td><td>分神留意某事</td><td>He listened to me with half an eye on the football match.<br>他一边听我说，一边分神看着球赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep an/your ˈeye on sb/sth</td><td>照看；留意；密切注意</td><td>Could you keep an eye on my bag while I buy the tickets?<br>我去买票，你帮我看一下包好吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your eye on the ˈball</td><td>专注要点；不分散注意力</td><td>Too many side projects, we need to keep our eye on the ball.<br>副业太多了，我们得盯紧正事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep an ˈeye out (for sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>留心寻找；仔细留意</td><td>Keep an eye out for a red van, that's the delivery man.<br>留意一辆红色面包车，那是送货的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>my ˈeye! (BrE, spoken)</td><td>（表示不相信）胡说；才怪呢</td><td>He says he forgot the meeting? Too busy at work, my eye!<br>他说他忘了开会？说什么工作太忙，胡扯！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one in the eye for sb/sth (informal)</td><td>对…的打击；令…难堪的挫折</td><td>The court ruling was one in the eye for the property developers.<br>这项判决给开发商当头一棒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) see eye to ˈeye (with sb)</td><td>与某人意见（不）一致</td><td>My brother and I have never seen eye to eye about money.<br>我和哥哥在钱的事上从来谈不拢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under the (watchful) eye of sb</td><td>在某人的注视（或监督）下</td><td>The apprentices worked under the watchful eye of an old carpenter.<br>学徒们在一位老木匠的注视下干活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what the eye doesn't ˈsee (the heart doesn't ˈgrieve over) (saying)</td><td>眼不见，心不烦</td><td>I never tell him how much the shoes cost; what the eye doesn't see.<br>我从不告诉他鞋子多少钱，眼不见心不烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with an eye to sth/to doing sth</td><td>着眼于…；意在…</td><td>She's taking an interpreting course with an eye to working abroad.<br>她在上口译课，想着以后到国外工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>eyeball</b></td><td>eyeball to ˈeyeball (with sb) (informal)</td><td>面对面对峙；针锋相对</td><td>The two managers stood eyeball to eyeball arguing about the referee's decision.<br>两位主教练面对面站着，为裁判的判罚争执不下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>eyeful</b></td><td>have/get an ˈeyeful (of sth) (BrE, spoken)</td><td>好好看一眼；大饱眼福</td><td>Come up to the roof and get an eyeful of that sunset.<br>上屋顶来，好好看看那片晚霞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>eyes</b></td><td>all eyes are on sb/sth</td><td>众目睽睽；万众瞩目</td><td>All eyes are on the young striker as he steps up to take the penalty.<br>年轻前锋走上前主罚点球，全场目光都盯着他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all ˈeyes</td><td>目不转睛；专注地看</td><td>The children were all eyes when the magician opened his box.<br>魔术师打开箱子时，孩子们看得目不转睛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be up to your ˈeyes/ˈeyeballs in sth</td><td>深陷于；忙得不可开交</td><td>She's up to her eyeballs in paperwork and can't take another case.<br>她被文书工作淹没了，接不了新案子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>before your (very) ˈeyes</td><td>就在眼前；当着…的面</td><td>The old cinema was torn down before our very eyes in a single morning.<br>那家老电影院一个上午就在我们眼前被拆掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>clap/lay/set ˈeyes on sb/sth (informal)</td><td>看见；见到</td><td>The moment I set eyes on the house, I knew I wanted to live there.<br>第一眼看见那房子，我就知道我想住那儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have eyes in the back of your ˈhead (informal)</td><td>脑后长眼；眼观六路</td><td>You can't fool that teacher, she has eyes in the back of her head.<br>别想骗那位老师，她后脑勺上都长着眼睛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have eyes like a ˈhawk</td><td>目光敏锐；明察秋毫</td><td>Our accountant has eyes like a hawk and spots every missing receipt.<br>我们的会计眼睛毒得很，少一张收据都逃不过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in your ˈface (informal)</td><td>（态度、风格）咄咄逼人；张扬</td><td>Her comedy is loud and in your face, but the audience loves it.<br>她的喜剧张扬又冲，可观众就吃这一套。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>disappear/vanish off the face of the ˈearth</td><td>彻底消失；无影无踪</td><td>After the trial he seemed to vanish off the face of the earth.<br>庭审之后，他好像从地球上消失了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your/sb's ˈface doesn't fit</td><td>不被接纳；不合某处的口味</td><td>He was well qualified, but in that office his face just didn't fit.<br>他条件很好，可在那家公司就是不受待见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your face ˈfalls</td><td>拉长了脸；面露失望</td><td>Her face fell when she saw the exam paper on the desk.<br>她看见桌上那张考卷，脸色一下子垮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>face the ˈmusic (informal)</td><td>承担后果；接受责难</td><td>He broke the window, so now he has to go and face the music.<br>窗户是他打破的，现在得去承担后果。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>face to ˈface (with sb/sth)</td><td>面对面；当面</td><td>We finally met face to face after three years of emails.<br>通了三年邮件，我们终于见了面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>face ˈup/ˈdown</td><td>面朝上；面朝下</td><td>Lay the cards face down on the table before you shuffle them.<br>洗牌前把牌面朝下放在桌上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get in sb's ˈface (AmE, informal)</td><td>纠缠某人；对某人穷追不舍</td><td>Stop getting in my face about the rent, I'll pay on Friday.<br>别老为房租烦我，我周五就付。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the face of sth</td><td>面对（危险、困难等）；不顾</td><td>She stayed remarkably calm in the face of all that criticism.<br>面对那么多批评，她异常镇定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let's ˈface it (informal)</td><td>面对现实吧；说实话</td><td>Let's face it, nobody is going to read a two hundred page report.<br>说实话吧，两百页的报告没人会看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a slap in the ˈface</td><td>一记耳光；公然的侮辱</td><td>Giving the award to an outsider was a slap in the face for the staff.<br>把奖颁给外人，对员工来说就是一记耳光。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>facelift</b></td><td>give sth a ˈfacelift</td><td>翻新；整修外观</td><td>A coat of paint gave the old shopfront a much-needed facelift.<br>刷了一层漆，这个旧店面焕然一新。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fact</b></td><td>ˌafter the ˈfact</td><td>事后；木已成舟之后</td><td>Telling me after the fact that you sold the car isn't much help.<br>车都卖了才告诉我，有什么用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌfact of life</td><td>无法改变（或避免）的事实</td><td>Traffic jams are simply a fact of life in this part of the city.<br>在城里这一带，堵车就是没法改变的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in (actual) ˈfact</td><td>事实上；其实（尤表相反）</td><td>He looks about forty, but in actual fact he's nearly sixty.<br>他看着四十来岁，其实快六十了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>is that a ˈfact? (spoken)</td><td>（表示惊讶或怀疑）真的吗</td><td>You climbed the mountain in four hours? Is that a fact?<br>你四小时就爬上山了？真的假的？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌfacts of ˈlife</td><td>性知识；生理常识</td><td>Her mother explained the facts of life to her when she turned eleven.<br>她十一岁时，母亲给她讲了生理常识。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the facts speak for themˈselves</td><td>事实不言自明</td><td>Three failed inspections in one year, the facts speak for themselves.<br>一年三次检查不合格，事实不言自明。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be set ˈfair (BrE)</td><td>（天气）持续晴好；形势看好</td><td>The forecast says the weather is set fair for the whole weekend.<br>天气预报说整个周末都会晴好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without ˈfail</td><td>必定；务必</td><td>He phones his mother every Sunday evening without fail.<br>他每个星期天晚上必给母亲打电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fair</b></td><td>fair ˈdinkum (AustralE, New Zealand, informal)</td><td>真的；确实；地道的</td><td>Fair dinkum, I saw a kangaroo right outside the shop this morning.<br>真的，今早我在店门口看见一只袋鼠。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fair eˈnough (informal)</td><td>（表示接受）有道理；行吧</td><td>You'd rather split the bill? Fair enough, let's do that.<br>你想各付各的？行吧，就这样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fair ˈgame</td><td>可任意取笑（或抨击）的对象</td><td>Once you're a politician, your private life becomes fair game.<br>一旦当了政客，私生活就任人评说了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a fair ˈhearing</td><td>充分申辩的机会</td><td>Every employee deserves a fair hearing before being dismissed.<br>每个员工在被解雇前都应有申辩的机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fair ˈplay</td><td>公平竞争；光明正大</td><td>The coach cares more about fair play than about winning trophies.<br>这位教练看重公平竞赛胜过拿奖杯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a fair ˈshake (AmE, informal)</td><td>公平的机会；公道的待遇</td><td>All the new applicants deserve a fair shake at the job.<br>所有新申请人都该得到公平的机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(more than) your fair ˈshare of sth</td><td>（超过）应得的一份</td><td>That family has had more than its fair share of bad luck this year.<br>那家人今年真是倒霉透顶。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>faith</b></td><td>bad ˈfaith</td><td>不诚实；无诚意</td><td>The union accused the company of bargaining in bad faith.<br>工会指责公司谈判缺乏诚意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>good ˈfaith</td><td>诚意；善意</td><td>They paid a deposit as a sign of good faith.<br>他们付了定金以示诚意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a false aˈlarm</td><td>虚惊一场；假警报</td><td>The smoke in the kitchen turned out to be a false alarm.<br>厨房冒烟原来只是虚惊一场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>false</b></td><td>(make) a false ˈstart</td><td>起步失误；开局不顺</td><td>After two false starts, the business finally began to make money.<br>两次失败的开头之后，这生意终于开始赚钱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sound/strike a false ˈnote</td><td>显得不恰当；给人不真诚之感</td><td>His cheerful joke struck a false note at such a sad occasion.<br>在这么悲伤的场合，他那个笑话显得很不合适。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>familiar</b></td><td>have a familiar ˈring (about/to it)</td><td>听起来耳熟</td><td>That excuse has a familiar ring to it, you used it last week.<br>这借口听着耳熟，你上周就用过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>familiarity</b></td><td>familiarity breeds conˈtempt (saying)</td><td>亲不敬，熟生蔑</td><td>They shared an office for years and, familiarity breeds contempt, ended up quarrelling.<br>他们同办公室多年，熟不拘礼，最后闹翻了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>family</b></td><td>in the ˈfamily way (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>怀孕；有孕</td><td>By the time they moved house, she was already in the family way.<br>他们搬家的时候，她已经有身孕了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run in the ˈfamily</td><td>是家族特征；世代相传</td><td>Red hair and stubbornness both run in that family.<br>红头发和倔脾气在他们家都是祖传的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>famous</b></td><td>ˌfamous ˌlast ˈwords (informal, humorous)</td><td>鬼才信的漂亮话；话说得太早</td><td>"This train is never late." Famous last words, we sat there an hour.<br>“这趟车从不晚点。”话说得太满，我们干坐了一小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>famously</b></td><td>get on/along ˈfamously (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>相处得极好</td><td>My mother and my new boyfriend got on famously over dinner.<br>我妈和我新男友吃饭时相处得极好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fan</b></td><td>fan the ˈflames (of sth)</td><td>煽风点火；火上浇油</td><td>His angry tweets only fanned the flames of an already ugly dispute.<br>他那些愤怒的推文只是给这场丑陋的争端火上浇油。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>when the ˈshit hits the fan (slang)</td><td>出大乱子；捅了大娄子</td><td>Delete nothing, when the shit hits the fan we'll need those emails.<br>什么都别删，出了事我们还得靠这些邮件。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>taney</b></td><td>as, whenever, etc. the fancy ˈtakes you</td><td>只要你高兴；随你的意</td><td>You can paint the walls whatever colour the fancy takes you.<br>墙想刷什么颜色随你高兴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch/take/tickle sb's ˈfancy (informal)</td><td>吸引某人；投某人所好</td><td>A little blue teapot in the window caught my fancy at once.<br>橱窗里一只蓝色小茶壶一下子把我迷住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fancy your/sb's ˈchances (informal)</td><td>自认为有胜算；看好…能成功</td><td>He fancies his chances against a player ranked twenty places above him.<br>他觉得自己能赢一个排名高二十位的选手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) fancy ˈthat! (old-fashioned, BrE, spoken)</td><td>（表示惊讶）真想不到</td><td>She's moving to Iceland to open a bakery. Just fancy that!<br>她要搬去冰岛开面包店，真想不到！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a ˈfancy to sb/sth (especially BrE)</td><td>喜欢上；看中</td><td>The cat took a fancy to our new neighbour and moved in with him.<br>那只猫看上了新邻居，索性搬去他家住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as/so ˈfar as...</td><td>就…而言；到…程度</td><td>As far as the money goes, we can manage until the end of the month.<br>就钱而言，我们撑到月底没问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as far as the eye can/could ˈsee</td><td>一望无际；视线所及之处</td><td>There were sunflower fields as far as the eye could see.<br>向日葵田一望无际。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as/so far as it ˈgoes</td><td>就其本身而言（暗指不够）</td><td>His plan is fine as far as it goes, but it ignores the cost.<br>他的方案就本身而言还行，可没考虑成本。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>carry/take sth too ˈfar</td><td>做得过分；超出常理</td><td>Teasing him about his accent is taking the joke too far.<br>拿他的口音开玩笑就过分了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(by) far and aˈway</td><td>远远地；大大地（最…）</td><td>She is far and away the best cook in the whole family.<br>她做菜远远胜过家里其他人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>far and ˈwide</td><td>到处；四面八方</td><td>People came from far and wide to hear the old singer one last time.<br>人们从四面八方赶来，听老歌手最后唱一次。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a far ˈcry from sth</td><td>与…相去甚远；大不相同</td><td>This tiny flat is a far cry from the house we had in the country.<br>这间小公寓和我们乡下那栋房子天差地别。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>far ˈfrom it (informal)</td><td>完全不是；恰恰相反</td><td>Is he generous? Far from it, he spends everything on himself.<br>他大方吗？才不呢，钱全花自己身上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in so ˈfar as (also insoˈfar as)</td><td>就…而言；在…范围内</td><td>The report is useful in so far as it shows what must be fixed.<br>就其指出需要修正之处而言，这份报告是有用的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not far ˈoff/ˈout/ˈwrong (informal)</td><td>差不太多；八九不离十</td><td>I guessed her age as thirty and I wasn't far off.<br>我猜她三十岁，还真差不太多。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not go ˈfar</td><td>（钱）不经花；买不了多少</td><td>Twenty pounds doesn't go far when you're feeding four children.<br>养四个孩子，二十镑根本不经花。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so far, so ˈgood (saying)</td><td>到目前为止一切顺利</td><td>Two exams down and both went well, so far so good.<br>两门考完都不错，目前为止一切顺利。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fashion</b></td><td>after a ˈfashion</td><td>勉强；马马虎虎</td><td>He speaks Japanese after a fashion, enough to order dinner.<br>他会点日语，勉强够点菜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>after the fashion of sb/sth (formal)</td><td>仿照…的方式；照…的风格</td><td>The chapel was built after the fashion of a Greek temple.<br>这座小教堂仿希腊神庙的样式建造。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in (a)... ˈfashion (formal)</td><td>以…方式；以…态度</td><td>He answered every question in a calm and careful fashion.<br>他以冷静谨慎的方式回答了每个问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like it's going out of ˈfashion (spoken)</td><td>（用于强调）没完没了地；毫无节制地</td><td>Since the diet ended he's been eating chocolate like it's going out of fashion.<br>节食一结束，他吃巧克力就没个节制。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fast</b></td><td>as fast as your legs can ˈcarry you</td><td>拼命地跑；飞奔</td><td>He ran home as fast as his legs could carry him when the storm started.<br>暴雨一来，他拔腿飞奔回家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fast and ˈfurious</td><td>（比赛、活动）激烈的；热火朝天的</td><td>The quiz got fast and furious in the final round.<br>最后一轮抢答变得又快又激烈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a fast ˈtalker</td><td>花言巧语的人；油嘴滑舌者</td><td>Don't sign anything, that salesman is a fast talker.<br>什么都别签，那个推销员太会忽悠。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a fast ˈworker (informal)</td><td>很快博得他人青睐的人</td><td>They met on Monday and he'd asked her out by Tuesday, what a fast worker.<br>他们周一认识，周二他就约她出去了，动作真快。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold ˈfast to sth</td><td>坚持（信念、原则等）不放弃</td><td>She held fast to her principles even when the whole board disagreed.<br>即便全体董事反对，她仍坚守自己的原则。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈfast lane (informal)</td><td>过着紧张刺激的生活</td><td>After ten years of life in the fast lane, he moved to a quiet village.<br>过了十年紧张刺激的日子，他搬到了安静的村子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈslow lane</td><td>进展缓慢；落在后面</td><td>Our region is still in the slow lane when it comes to broadband.<br>在宽带方面，我们这个地区还是慢半拍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fat</b></td><td>(a) ˈfat chance (of sth/doing sth) (spoken)</td><td>希望渺茫；没什么机会</td><td>Fat chance of getting a table there without booking weeks ahead.<br>不提前几周订位，别想在那儿有座。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the fat is in the ˈfire (informal)</td><td>要出乱子了；闯下大祸</td><td>Once she read those messages, the fat was in the fire.<br>她一看到那些短信，事情就闹大了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to a ˈfault (written)</td><td>过分地；（好得）过头</td><td>He is generous to a fault and often lends money he needs himself.<br>他慷慨得过了头，常把自己要用的钱借出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>faux</b></td><td>(make/commit) a ˌfaux ˈpas (from French)</td><td>失礼；说错话</td><td>Calling the host by the wrong name was an awkward faux pas.<br>把主人的名字叫错了，实在失礼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be (all) in ˈfavour of sth/of doing sth</td><td>完全赞成（做）某事</td><td>I'm all in favour of starting the meeting half an hour earlier.<br>我完全赞成把会议提前半小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do me a ˈfavour</td><td>帮我个忙；（表示不信）得了吧</td><td>Do me a favour and hold the ladder while I fix this light.<br>帮个忙，我修灯时扶着梯子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in sb's/sth's ˈfavour</td><td>对…有利</td><td>The referee's decision went in our favour for once.<br>裁判的判罚这回总算对我们有利。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/out of ˈfavour (with sb)</td><td>得宠（或失宠）；受（不受）青睐</td><td>Long coats are back in favour with young designers this winter.<br>今冬长外套又受年轻设计师青睐了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sb's favourite ˈson</td><td>家乡的名人；当地的骄傲</td><td>The town welcomed its favourite son home with a brass band.<br>小镇用铜管乐队迎接这位家乡名人归来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>return the ˈfavour</td><td>回报；还人情</td><td>You helped me move, so let me return the favour with dinner.<br>你帮我搬了家，让我请顿饭还个人情。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sb no ˈfavours ◆ not do sb any ˈfavours</td><td>对某人没好处；帮倒忙</td><td>Lending him money again does him no favours at all.<br>再借钱给他对他没有任何好处。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fear</b></td><td>be/go in fear of your ˈlife</td><td>整天担心性命不保</td><td>After the threats, the witness lived in fear of her life.<br>受到威胁后，那名证人整天担心性命难保。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for fear of sth/of doing sth ◆ for fear (that)...</td><td>唯恐；以免</td><td>She tiptoed upstairs for fear of waking the baby.<br>她踮着脚上楼，生怕吵醒宝宝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in fear and ˈtrembling (of sb/sth) (written)</td><td>惶恐不安；提心吊胆</td><td>The pupils waited in fear and trembling outside the headmaster's door.<br>学生们提心吊胆地等在校长门外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no ˈfear! (BrE, spoken)</td><td>才不呢；绝对不干</td><td>You want me to jump into that freezing lake? No fear!<br>你要我跳进那冰冷的湖里？才不干呢！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put the fear of ˈGod into sb (informal)</td><td>把某人吓坏；恐吓某人就范</td><td>One look at the exam timetable put the fear of God into us.<br>一看考试时间表，我们全吓坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no fear of sth</td><td>不会发生某事；不必担心</td><td>There's no fear of rain today, leave the umbrella at home.<br>今天不会下雨，伞就别带了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without ˌfear or ˈfavour (BrE) (AmE without ˌfear or ˈfavor) (formal)</td><td>不偏不倚；公正地</td><td>A judge must apply the law without fear or favour.<br>法官必须不偏不倚地适用法律。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>feast</b></td><td>feast your ˈeyes (on sb/sth)</td><td>大饱眼福；尽情欣赏</td><td>Come to the window and feast your eyes on that view.<br>到窗边来，好好欣赏一下那景色。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>feather</b></td><td>a ˈfeather in your cap</td><td>值得骄傲的成绩；荣誉</td><td>Winning that contract was a real feather in her cap.<br>拿下那份合同是她一大荣耀。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feather your (own) ˈnest</td><td>中饱私囊；营私自肥</td><td>He spent years on the board quietly feathering his own nest.<br>他在董事会多年，一直悄悄中饱私囊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>feathered</b></td><td>our feathered ˈfriends (informal, humorous)</td><td>鸟儿；我们的羽毛朋友</td><td>Put out some crumbs in winter for our feathered friends.<br>冬天撒些面包屑，给鸟儿们吃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fed</b></td><td>fed up to the back ˈteeth with sb/sth (also ˌsick to the back ˈteeth of sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>烦透了；受够了</td><td>I'm fed up to the back teeth with their broken promises.<br>他们一再食言，我真是烦透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>feeding</b></td><td>a ˈfeeding frenzy (especially AmE)</td><td>疯抢；（媒体等的）疯狂追逐</td><td>The scandal set off a media feeding frenzy outside her house.<br>这桩丑闻引来媒体在她家门外疯狂围堵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>feel</b></td><td>be/feel ˈout of it/things</td><td>感到被冷落；融不进去</td><td>Everyone spoke Spanish at dinner and I felt completely out of it.<br>晚饭时大家都说西班牙语，我完全插不上话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feel your ˈage</td><td>感到自己老了</td><td>After two hours of football with my nephews, I really felt my age.<br>和侄子们踢了两小时球，我真觉得自己老了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feel the ˈdraught (informal)</td><td>感到手头拮据；出现财政困难</td><td>Small shops on the high street are starting to feel the draught.<br>大街上的小店开始感到日子难过了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feel ˈfree (to do sth) (informal)</td><td>请便；尽管（做某事）</td><td>Feel free to help yourself to coffee while you wait.<br>等的时候请随意喝咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feel (it) in your ˈbones (informal)</td><td>有预感；凭直觉感到</td><td>I can feel it in my bones that she's going to call tonight.<br>我有预感，她今晚会打电话来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feel like sth/like doing sth</td><td>想要某物；想做某事</td><td>I feel like a long walk before it gets dark.<br>天黑前我想去好好走一段路。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feel the ˈpinch (informal)</td><td>手头紧；经济困难</td><td>With rents rising, young families are really feeling the pinch.<br>房租上涨，年轻家庭真的手头吃紧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feel ˈstrange</td><td>觉得不舒服；觉得别扭</td><td>I felt strange all morning, so I went home early.<br>我一上午都不太舒服，就提早回家了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feel your ˈway</td><td>摸索着走；谨慎行事</td><td>He felt his way down the dark corridor to find the switch.<br>他摸索着走过漆黑的走廊去找开关。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get the ˈfeel of sth (informal)</td><td>开始熟悉；逐渐适应</td><td>Give me a week to get the feel of the new software.<br>给我一周时间熟悉这个新软件。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈfeel for sth (informal)</td><td>对…有悟性；有做某事的天分</td><td>She has a real feel for languages and picks up accents quickly.<br>她对语言很有天分，口音学得很快。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not feel yourˈself</td><td>觉得身体（或心情）不如平时</td><td>I haven't felt myself since that long flight home.<br>自从坐了那趟长途飞机回来，我一直不太对劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>feelers</b></td><td>put out/have ˈfeelers</td><td>试探；打探口风</td><td>He's putting out feelers about a job in Berlin.<br>他正在打听柏林那边的工作机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get</b></td><td>get/have the ˈfeeling (that...)</td><td>觉得；有种感觉</td><td>I get the feeling that she isn't telling us the whole story.<br>我觉得她没把事情全说出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>feelings</b></td><td>no ˌhard ˈfeelings</td><td>别往心里去；不记仇</td><td>You got the promotion and I didn't, but no hard feelings.<br>你升职了我没有，不过我不往心里去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>feet</b></td><td>at sb's ˈfeet</td><td>拜倒在某人脚下；对某人倾倒</td><td>After that performance the whole city was at her feet.<br>那场演出之后，全城的人都为她倾倒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get ˌrun/ˌrushed off your ˈfeet</td><td>忙得团团转；忙得不可开交</td><td>The café was so busy we were run off our feet all afternoon.<br>咖啡馆太忙了，我们整个下午脚不沾地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fall/land on your ˈfeet (informal)</td><td>逢凶化吉；运气好脱身</td><td>He lost his job in May and landed on his feet with a better one.<br>他五月丢了工作，转头就找到个更好的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feet ˈfirst (informal)</td><td>死后被抬出去</td><td>He swears he'll only leave this old house feet first.<br>他发誓自己只有死了才会离开这栋老房子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>feet of ˈclay</td><td>（受敬仰者的）致命弱点</td><td>Fans were shocked to learn their hero had feet of clay.<br>得知偶像也有致命缺点，粉丝们大为震惊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/keep both/your feet on the ˈground</td><td>脚踏实地；讲求实际</td><td>Despite all the praise, she keeps both feet on the ground.<br>尽管备受赞誉，她依然脚踏实地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on your ˈfeet</td><td>站着；（病后）康复自立</td><td>Nurses are on their feet for twelve hours at a stretch.<br>护士一站就是连续十二个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put your ˈfeet up</td><td>坐下（或躺下）休息放松</td><td>Dinner's cooking, so put your feet up for half an hour.<br>饭在做着，你先歇半小时吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under sb's ˈfeet</td><td>碍某人的事；挡道</td><td>The kids are under my feet all day during the school holidays.<br>放假时孩子们整天在我脚边碍事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fetch</b></td><td>fetch and ˈcarry (for sb)</td><td>为某人跑腿打杂</td><td>She's tired of fetching and carrying for her lazy flatmates.<br>她受够了给懒室友跑腿伺候。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fettle</b></td><td>in fine/good ˈfettle (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>身心俱佳；状态良好</td><td>Grandad is ninety but still in fine fettle.<br>爷爷九十岁了，身子骨还硬朗。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fever</b></td><td>at ˈfever pitch</td><td>极度兴奋；白热化</td><td>Excitement was at fever pitch before the final whistle.<br>终场哨响前，气氛热烈到了顶点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>few</b></td><td>few and far beˈtween</td><td>稀少；不常发生</td><td>Buses out here are few and far between after eight.<br>八点以后这一带的公交车少得可怜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have had a few (too many) (informal)</td><td>喝多了；喝过头了</td><td>Don't let him drive, he's had a few too many.<br>别让他开车，他喝多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a man/woman of few ˈwords</td><td>少言寡语的人</td><td>Our coach is a man of few words but everyone listens to him.<br>我们教练话不多，可大家都听他的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fiddle</b></td><td>ˌfiddle while Rome ˈburns (saying)</td><td>大难临头仍无所事事</td><td>Arguing about the logo while sales collapse is fiddling while Rome burns.<br>销量都垮了还在争标志，简直是大难临头不着急。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈfiddle (BrE, informal)</td><td>（做假账等）骗钱</td><td>The manager had been on the fiddle for years before anyone noticed.<br>那位经理骗了好几年钱才被人发现。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>field</b></td><td>have a ˈfield day</td><td>大干一场；尽情发挥（尤指借机大做文章）</td><td>The newspapers had a field day with the mayor's leaked emails.<br>市长的邮件外泄，报纸大做文章。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave the field ˈclear for sb</td><td>为某人扫清障碍</td><td>Her withdrawal left the field clear for the younger candidate.<br>她的退出为那位年轻候选人扫清了障碍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave sb in possession of the ˈfield</td><td>让某人独占优势；使某人成为赢家</td><td>The rival firm's collapse left them in possession of the field.<br>竞争对手垮台，让他们独占了市场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play the ˈfield (informal)</td><td>广交异性；不固定交往</td><td>He wants to play the field for a few years before settling down.<br>他想先花几年到处交往，再安定下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fierce</b></td><td>something ˈfierce (AmE, spoken)</td><td>非常；厉害地</td><td>My knee has been aching something fierce since the game.<br>比赛之后我的膝盖疼得厉害。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fifth</b></td><td>take/plead the ˈfifth (AmE)</td><td>援引第五修正案拒绝作答</td><td>The witness took the fifth rather than name his business partners.<br>证人援引第五修正案，拒绝说出生意伙伴的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fight</b></td><td>fight ˌfire with ˈfire</td><td>以其人之道还治其人之身</td><td>They ran negative ads, so we decided to fight fire with fire.<br>他们打负面广告，我们就决定以牙还牙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fight for (your) ˈlife</td><td>拼命求生；奋力保命</td><td>The climber is in hospital fighting for his life after the fall.<br>那名登山者坠落后正在医院里与死神搏斗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fight it ˈout</td><td>一决高下；决出胜负</td><td>The two finalists will fight it out on Sunday afternoon.<br>两位决赛选手将在周日下午一决高下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fight like cat and ˈdog (informal)</td><td>像猫狗一样争吵不休</td><td>Those brothers fight like cat and dog but would defend each other anywhere.<br>那对兄弟成天吵架，可对外总是护着彼此。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fight a ˌlosing ˈbattle</td><td>打一场无望取胜的仗</td><td>Trying to keep the kitchen tidy with four kids is fighting a losing battle.<br>带着四个孩子想保持厨房整洁，纯属徒劳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fight your ˈown battles</td><td>自己解决问题；独立应对</td><td>She's old enough now to fight her own battles at school.<br>她已经大了，学校的事该自己应付。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fight ˈshy of sth/of doing sth</td><td>回避；避免（做）某事</td><td>The minister fought shy of answering questions about the budget.<br>部长回避了关于预算的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fight ˌtooth and ˈnail (for sb/sth/to do sth)</td><td>拼命抗争；全力争取</td><td>Local people fought tooth and nail to save the village school.<br>当地人拼尽全力保住了村里的学校。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put up a (good) ˈfight</td><td>奋力抵抗；顽强战斗</td><td>They lost in the end, but they put up a good fight.<br>他们最后输了，但打得很顽强。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fighting</b></td><td>a ˌfighting ˈchance</td><td>尚有希望的机会</td><td>With five minutes left, our team still has a fighting chance.<br>还剩五分钟，我们队仍有一线获胜的机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in with a ˈchance (of doing sth) (BrE, informal)</td><td>有获胜（或成功）的可能</td><td>John Brown is still in with a chance of winning the nomination.<br>约翰·布朗仍有机会拿到提名。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fighting ˈspirit</td><td>斗志；顽强的意志</td><td>What the team lacks in skill it makes up for in fighting spirit.<br>这支队伍技术不足，却靠斗志弥补。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fighting ˈtalk</td><td>挑战性的言论；豪言壮语</td><td>Beat them by ten points? That's fighting talk from a new captain.<br>赢他们十分？新队长口气可真不小。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>figment</b></td><td>a figment of sb's imagiˈnation</td><td>凭空想象的事物；虚构之事</td><td>The noises in the attic were just a figment of her imagination.<br>阁楼上的声响不过是她的想象罢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>figure</b></td><td>cut a fine, poor, sorry, etc. ˈfigure</td><td>显得出众（或狼狈、可怜等）</td><td>Soaked and muddy, he cut a sorry figure at the front door.<br>他浑身湿透沾满泥，站在门口显得十分狼狈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a figure of ˈfun</td><td>笑柄；被人取笑的对象</td><td>That silly hat made him a figure of fun in the whole office.<br>那顶滑稽的帽子让他成了全办公室的笑柄。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈfigure (AmE, informal)</td><td>真搞不懂；你说怪不怪</td><td>He hates the sea but bought a boat. Go figure.<br>他讨厌大海却买了条船，真搞不懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put a ˈfigure on sth</td><td>给出确切数字（或价值）</td><td>It's hard to put a figure on the damage before the survey.<br>勘查之前很难给损失定出个数字。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>figures</b></td><td>it/that ˈfigures (informal)</td><td>那就说得通了；不奇怪</td><td>He was late again? That figures, he missed the early train.<br>他又迟到了？不奇怪，他没赶上早班车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>file</b></td><td>(in) single/Indian ˈfile</td><td>排成一列纵队</td><td>The children walked in single file along the narrow mountain path.<br>孩子们排成一列走在狭窄的山路上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌrank and ˈfile</td><td>普通成员；基层群众</td><td>The leadership agreed, but the rank and file voted against the deal.<br>领导层同意了，可基层成员投票否决了这项协议。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fill</b></td><td>fill sb's ˈboots/ˈshoes</td><td>接替某人（并胜任其职）</td><td>It won't be easy to fill her shoes after twenty years of teaching here.<br>她在这儿教了二十年书，接她的班可不容易。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have had your ˈfill of sb/sth</td><td>受够了某人（或某事）</td><td>I've had my fill of meetings for this week.<br>这一周的会我算是开够了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>find</b></td><td>find ˈfault (with sb/sth)</td><td>挑毛病；找茬儿</td><td>He finds fault with everything I cook, however hard I try.<br>不管我多用心做饭，他总能挑出毛病。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>find your ˈfeet (informal)</td><td>适应新环境（或新工作）</td><td>Give the new nurse a month to find her feet on the ward.<br>给这位新护士一个月时间适应病房工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) find it in your heart to ˈdo sth (also (not) find it ˈin yourself to do sth) (literary)</td><td>（不）忍心做某事</td><td>She couldn't find it in her heart to tell the boy his dog had died.<br>她不忍心告诉那男孩他的狗死了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>find your ˈvoice/ˈtongue (informal)</td><td>终于开口说话；不再怯场</td><td>After a nervous silence, she finally found her voice and answered.<br>紧张地沉默片刻后，她终于开口作答。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>find your/its ˈway (to/into...)</td><td>辗转来到；无意间进入</td><td>Somehow my umbrella found its way into his car.<br>不知怎么，我的伞跑到他车里去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb as you ˈfind them</td><td>接受某人的本来面目</td><td>The house is a mess and so am I, you'll have to take me as you find me.<br>屋子乱，我也乱，你就将就着接受我这样吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌfinders ˈkeepers (saying)</td><td>谁捡到就归谁</td><td>He kept the coin he found in the park, finders keepers.<br>他把公园里捡到的硬币留下了，谁捡到归谁嘛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fine</b></td><td>have sth down to a fine ˈart (informal)</td><td>把某事做得炉火纯青</td><td>After six children, she has bedtime down to a fine art.<br>养了六个孩子，她把哄睡这事做得炉火纯青。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not to put too fine a ˈpoint on it</td><td>直截了当地说；不客气地说</td><td>Not to put too fine a point on it, the report is badly written.<br>不客气地说，这份报告写得很糟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>finger</b></td><td>work your ˌfingers to the ˈbone (informal)</td><td>拼命干活；不停手地干</td><td>She worked her fingers to the bone to send both sons to college.<br>她拼死拼活干活，供两个儿子上了大学。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fingertips</b></td><td>have sth at your ˈfingertips</td><td>对…了如指掌；随时可用</td><td>A good guide has the city's history at her fingertips.<br>好导游对这座城市的历史了如指掌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to your ˈfingertips (BrE)</td><td>彻头彻尾；十足地</td><td>He is a gentleman to his fingertips, even when provoked.<br>即便被激怒，他也是个十足的绅士。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>finish</b></td><td>be in at the ˈfinish</td><td>结束时在场；见证最后阶段</td><td>She joined the project late but was in at the finish.<br>她中途才加入项目，但坚持到了最后。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>finishing</b></td><td>the finishing ˈtouch(es)</td><td>最后的修饰；收尾工作</td><td>He was putting the finishing touches to the cake when we arrived.<br>我们到时他正在给蛋糕做最后的装饰。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fire</b></td><td>be/come under ˈfire</td><td>遭到攻击；受到抨击</td><td>The airline came under fire for cancelling flights without warning.<br>这家航空公司因无预警取消航班而遭到抨击。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fire ˈquestions, ˈinsults, etc. at sb</td><td>连珠炮般地发问（或辱骂）</td><td>Reporters fired questions at the coach as he left the stadium.<br>教练离开球场时，记者连珠炮般地向他发问。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold your ˈfire</td><td>暂不开火；先别发作</td><td>Hold your fire until we know what really happened.<br>先别急着发作，等弄清事情真相再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈfire</td><td>着火；火辣辣；状态火热</td><td>My throat is on fire after eating that chilli.<br>吃了那个辣椒，我嗓子火烧火燎的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play with ˈfire</td><td>玩火；冒不必要的危险</td><td>Lending money to that gambler is playing with fire.<br>借钱给那个赌徒简直是玩火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set sth on ˈfire</td><td>点燃；纵火焚烧</td><td>Someone set the rubbish bins on fire behind the school.<br>有人把学校后面的垃圾桶点着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>firing</b></td><td>be in the ˈfiring line (BrE) (AmE be on the ˈfiring line)</td><td>首当其冲；处于易受批评之位</td><td>As spokesman, he's always in the firing line when things go wrong.<br>作为发言人，一出事他总是首当其冲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>firm</b></td><td>be on firm ˈground</td><td>有把握；立场稳固</td><td>Ask about the history, that's where she's on firm ground.<br>问历史吧，那是她有把握的领域。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a firm ˈhand</td><td>严格的管教；铁腕</td><td>That class needs a firm hand from the very first lesson.<br>那个班从第一节课起就得严加管教。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold ˈfirm (to sth) (formal)</td><td>坚持；不动摇</td><td>The committee held firm to its decision despite the protests.<br>尽管有抗议，委员会仍坚持原来的决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a firm ˈline/stand (on/against sth)</td><td>对…采取坚定立场</td><td>The school takes a firm line on bullying of any kind.<br>学校对任何形式的欺凌都态度坚决。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be a great/firm beˈliever in sth</td><td>笃信…；坚信…有好处</td><td>My grandmother is a firm believer in a walk before breakfast.<br>我外婆坚信早饭前该散散步。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>first</b></td><td>at first ˈglance/ˈsight</td><td>乍看之下；初看起来</td><td>At first glance the twins look identical, but their voices differ.<br>乍一看这对双胞胎一模一样，声音却不同。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come ˈfirst</td><td>最重要；被放在首位</td><td>For her, the children's health always comes first.<br>对她来说，孩子的健康永远排第一。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>first among ˈequals</td><td>同级中居首位者</td><td>The chairman is really just first among equals on this board.<br>在董事会里，主席其实只是同僚中的第一人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌfirst and ˈforemost</td><td>首先；最重要的是</td><td>First and foremost, we need to make the building safe.<br>首要的是把这栋楼弄安全。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>first and ˈlast</td><td>归根到底；从头至尾就是</td><td>He is, first and last, a teacher, whatever titles they give him.<br>不管给他什么头衔，他归根到底是个老师。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(at) first ˈhand</td><td>第一手地；直接地</td><td>She learned about the flood at first hand, wading through the streets.<br>她蹚着水走过街道，亲身体验了那场洪水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>first ˈoff/ˈup (informal)</td><td>首先；第一件事</td><td>First off, let me thank everyone who stayed late last night.<br>首先，感谢昨晚留下加班的各位。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(give sb, have, etc.) (the) first reˈfusal</td><td>（给予或拥有）优先购买权</td><td>The landlord gave us first refusal on the flat downstairs.<br>房东给了我们优先租下楼下那套房的权利。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>first ˈthing (tomorrow, in the morning, etc.)</td><td>（明早等）一开始就；头一件事</td><td>I'll call the bank first thing tomorrow morning.<br>我明天一早就给银行打电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be) the ˈfirst/ˈlast (person) to do sth</td><td>（是）最（不）会做某事的人</td><td>I'd be the last person to criticize her, she saved the project.<br>我最不会去批评她，是她救了这个项目。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from the (very) ˈfirst</td><td>从一开始</td><td>From the very first, I knew this job wasn't right for me.<br>从一开始我就知道这份工作不适合我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from ˌfirst to ˈlast</td><td>从头到尾；自始至终</td><td>From first to last the whole trial took only three days.<br>整场审判从头到尾只用了三天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get to first ˈbase (with sb/sth)</td><td>迈出第一步；取得初步进展</td><td>We never even got to first base with the funding application.<br>我们的经费申请连第一步都没走成。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have first ˈcall (on sb/sth)</td><td>有优先权；须优先照顾</td><td>The children's school fees have first call on our savings.<br>孩子的学费在我们的存款里排第一位。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈfirst instance (formal)</td><td>首先；第一步</td><td>In the first instance, please write to the customer services team.<br>第一步请先写信给客服部。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈfirst place</td><td>首先；当初</td><td>Why did you lend him the car in the first place?<br>你当初为什么要把车借给他？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make the first ˈmove</td><td>采取主动；率先行动</td><td>After the quarrel, he finally made the first move and phoned her.<br>吵架之后，他终于主动打了电话给她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb/sth ˈfirst</td><td>把…放在首位</td><td>Good managers put their team first when things go wrong.<br>出了问题时，好经理会把团队放在第一位。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's a ˌfirst time for ˈeverything (saying, humorous)</td><td>凡事都有第一次</td><td>You cooked dinner? Well, there's a first time for everything.<br>你居然做饭了？凡事都有第一次嘛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fish</b></td><td>fish for compliments</td><td>转弯抹角地讨人恭维；沽名钓誉</td><td>She kept saying her cake was awful, obviously fishing for compliments from her guests.<br>她一个劲儿说自己的蛋糕难吃，明摆着是想让客人夸她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fish or cut ˈbait (AmE, informal)</td><td>要么动手要么拉倒；快作抉择</td><td>You've thought about this job offer for a month—time to fish or cut bait.<br>这份工作你考虑一个月了，是接是推，该拿主意了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌfish out of ˈwater (informal)</td><td>不适应环境的人；不得其所的人</td><td>At the fancy dinner party, wearing jeans, I felt like a fish out of water.<br>在那种高级晚宴上我穿着牛仔裤，浑身别扭得像条离水的鱼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have other/bigger fish to ˈfry (informal)</td><td>有更重要的事要做</td><td>He skipped the meeting because he had bigger fish to fry that afternoon.<br>他没去开会，那天下午他有更要紧的事得办。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>neither ˌfish nor ˈfowl</td><td>非驴非马；不伦不类</td><td>The new building is neither fish nor fowl—half office, half shopping mall.<br>这栋新楼不伦不类，一半是写字楼，一半是商场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌodd/a ˌqueer ˈfish (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>怪人；古怪的家伙</td><td>Our neighbour is an odd fish who only goes out after midnight.<br>我们邻居是个怪人，只在半夜之后才出门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there are plenty/lots more fish in the ˈsea</td><td>天涯何处无芳草；好对象多的是</td><td>Stop crying over him—there are plenty more fish in the sea, believe me.<br>别为他哭了，天涯何处无芳草，信我的。</td></tr>
