<tr><td></td><td>there are (plenty of) other fish in the ˈsea</td><td>还有很多同样好的人或物；天涯何处无芳草</td><td>She lost that contract, but there are plenty of other fish in the sea.<br>那份合同她丢了，不过好机会多的是。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fist</b></td><td>make a better/ˌgood, poor, etc. ˈfist of sth</td><td>某事做得较好；做得不错；做得糟糕</td><td>For a beginner, he made a pretty good fist of repairing the old bicycle.<br>作为新手，他把那辆旧自行车修得相当不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an iron fist/hand (in a velvet glove)</td><td>外柔内刚的强硬手腕；笑里藏刀</td><td>She runs the department with an iron fist in a velvet glove.<br>她管理这个部门是绵里藏针，看着温和其实极强硬。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fit</b></td><td>(as) ˌfit as a ˈfiddle (also ˌfighting ˈfit)</td><td>非常健康；身体棒极了</td><td>At eighty, my grandfather still swims daily and is as fit as a fiddle.<br>我爷爷八十岁了还天天游泳，身体棒得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fit the ˈbill (informal)</td><td>符合要求；正合适</td><td>We need someone patient and bilingual, and this candidate fits the bill perfectly.<br>我们要找有耐心又懂两门语言的人，这位应聘者正合适。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fit (sb) like a ˈglove</td><td>（衣服等）完全合身</td><td>The suit he borrowed from his brother fitted him like a glove.<br>他从哥哥那儿借的西装穿上正合身。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/throw a ˈfit (informal)</td><td>大发脾气；激动万分</td><td>My mum will have a fit when she sees the mess in the kitchen.<br>我妈看到厨房这么乱肯定要发飙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a pink/blue ˈfit (BrE, informal)</td><td>震怒；大发雷霆</td><td>Dad had a blue fit when he found out I'd scratched his new car.<br>我把爸的新车刮花了，他知道后大发雷霆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see/think ˈfit (to do sth) (formal, often disapproving)</td><td>认为做某事恰当（或合适）</td><td>The manager saw fit to cancel the trip without telling any of us.<br>经理自认为有理，取消了行程却谁也没通知。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fits</b></td><td>in ˌfits and ˈstarts</td><td>断断续续地；时停时续地</td><td>The old engine started in fits and starts before it finally settled down.<br>那台旧发动机断断续续地响了半天才终于平稳下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>five</b></td><td>give sb ˈfive (informal)</td><td>与某人击掌（问候或庆祝）</td><td>After scoring the winning goal, he ran over and gave his coach five.<br>他攻入制胜一球后跑过去和教练击了个掌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fix</b></td><td>be/get in a ˈfix (informal)</td><td>陷入困境；处境为难</td><td>I'm in a bit of a fix—I've locked my keys inside the flat again.<br>我有点麻烦，又把钥匙锁在屋里了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fixed</b></td><td>how are you, etc. ˈfixed (for sth)? (spoken)</td><td>你有多少；你有什么安排</td><td>How are you fixed for cash this weekend? I might need to borrow some.<br>这周末你手头钱宽裕吗？我可能得借点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flag</b></td><td>fly/show/wave the ˈflag</td><td>表示支持自己的国家（或组织、思想）</td><td>Someone from our office should go to the conference and fly the flag.<br>我们办公室得派个人去那个会议撑撑场面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fly/wave the ˈflag</td><td>为自己一方助威；公开表示支持</td><td>Even in the rain, the fans stayed to wave the flag for their team.<br>就算下着雨，球迷们还是留下来为球队呐喊助威。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈflag-waving (noun)</td><td>强烈民族情绪的表现；沙文主义作派</td><td>The speech was pure flag-waving, with almost no real policy in it.<br>那篇演讲全是煽情的爱国口号，几乎没有实质政策。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep the ˈflag flying</td><td>继续支持濒临消亡的思想或活动</td><td>Only three members are left, but they're keeping the flag flying for folk music.<br>只剩三个成员了，可他们还在为民谣音乐撑着这面旗。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flagrante</b></td><td>in flaˈgrante (delicto) (from Latin, literary or humorous)</td><td>（做坏事时）被当场捉住</td><td>The two thieves were caught in flagrante, stuffing watches into their pockets.<br>两个小偷正把手表往兜里塞时被当场抓获。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flap</b></td><td>be in/get into a ˈflap (informal)</td><td>慌乱；焦虑不安</td><td>Don't get into a flap—the guests aren't arriving for another two hours.<br>别慌，客人还要两个小时才到呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flapping</b></td><td>his, her, etc. ˈears are flapping (BrE, informal)</td><td>竖着耳朵偷听别人说话</td><td>Lower your voice—her ears are flapping and she'll tell everyone tomorrow.<br>小点声，她正竖着耳朵听呢，明天准传遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flash</b></td><td>a ˌflash in the ˈpan (informal)</td><td>昙花一现；短暂的成功</td><td>Their first album sold well, but the band turned out to be a flash in the pan.<br>他们首张专辑卖得不错，可这乐队终究只是昙花一现。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>flash sb a ˈsmile, ˈlook, etc.</td><td>向某人投以一笑（或一瞥等）</td><td>She flashed me a smile across the room and then went back to her book.<br>她隔着房间冲我一笑，又低头看书去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/like a ˈflash (informal)</td><td>转眼间；迅速地</td><td>I asked him to fetch the ladder and he was back in a flash.<br>我让他去搬梯子，他一转眼就回来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flat</b></td><td>and ˌthat's ˈflat! (BrE, spoken)</td><td>就这么定了；这是最后决定</td><td>You're not going to that party on a school night, and that's flat!<br>明天要上学，今晚你不许去那个派对，就这么定了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fall ˈflat</td><td>（笑话等）没能逗乐；未收到预期效果</td><td>His opening joke fell flat and the whole room went awkwardly silent.<br>他开场那个笑话没人笑，全场尴尬地安静下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fall ˌflat on your ˈface (informal)</td><td>彻底失败；栽跟头</td><td>He bragged for weeks about his business plan, then fell flat on his face.<br>他吹嘘自己的创业计划好几周，结果摔了个大跟头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be flat ˈbroke (BrE also be stony ˈbroke)</td><td>身无分文；一贫如洗</td><td>I can't join you for dinner tonight—I'm flat broke until payday.<br>今晚饭我不去了，发薪水前我身上一分钱没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) flat as a ˈpancake (informal)</td><td>非常平；平得像纸一样</td><td>The countryside here is as flat as a pancake for miles in every direction.<br>这一带的乡野方圆几英里平得像张饼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>flat ˈout (informal)</td><td>全力以赴地；开足马力地</td><td>We worked flat out all weekend to get the report finished on time.<br>我们整个周末拼命赶工，才按时把报告做完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in two minutes, ten seconds, etc. ˈflat</td><td>仅用两分钟（或十秒等）；极快</td><td>He changed the flat tyre in five minutes flat and we drove on.<br>他五分钟就换好了瘪胎，我们接着上路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flattery</b></td><td>flattery will get you ˈeverywhere/ˈnowhere</td><td>阿谀奉承会（不会）让你如愿</td><td>Flattery will get you nowhere—you still have to finish the dishes tonight.<br>拍马屁没用，今晚碗还是得你洗。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flaunt</b></td><td>if you've ˌgot it, ˈflaunt it (humorous, saying)</td><td>有本事就亮出来；有能耐别藏着</td><td>She wore the diamond earrings to the office—if you've got it, flaunt it.<br>她戴着钻石耳环上班，有就得显摆嘛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>flavour of the ˈmonth (especially BrE)</td><td>时下走红的人物；一时的宠儿</td><td>That young director is flavour of the month with every studio in town.<br>那个年轻导演眼下是各家制片厂争抢的红人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flea</b></td><td>with a ˈflea in your ear</td><td>被斥退；碰一鼻子灰</td><td>He asked for a raise and was sent away with a flea in his ear.<br>他去要求加薪，结果被训了一顿轰了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flesh</b></td><td>ˌflesh and ˈblood</td><td>血肉之躯；凡人的弱点</td><td>I'm only flesh and blood—I can't work eighteen hours a day forever.<br>我也是血肉之躯，不可能天天干十八个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your (own) ˌflesh and ˈblood</td><td>亲骨肉；亲人</td><td>How could you turn away your own flesh and blood on a night like this?<br>这样的夜里，你怎么忍心把自家亲人拒之门外？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈflesh</td><td>本人；亲自出现</td><td>I'd only seen her on television, so meeting her in the flesh was strange.<br>我只在电视上见过她，真人站在面前感觉挺奇妙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make your ˈflesh creep/crawl</td><td>使人毛骨悚然；令人起鸡皮疙瘩</td><td>The way that man stared at us made my flesh creep.<br>那男人盯着我们看的样子让我起了一身鸡皮疙瘩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>more than ˈflesh and blood can enˈdure, etc.</td><td>非血肉之躯所能承受</td><td>Three night shifts in a row is more than flesh and blood can endure.<br>连上三个夜班，血肉之躯实在扛不住。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put flesh on (the bones of) sth</td><td>充实内容；添加细节</td><td>The idea sounds promising, but you need to put flesh on the bones of it.<br>这个想法听着不错，但你得把细节填充起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flex</b></td><td>flex your ˈmuscles</td><td>跃跃欲试；摩拳擦掌显示实力</td><td>The new manager is flexing his muscles by rewriting all our procedures.<br>新经理正在大显身手，把我们的流程全改了一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flies</b></td><td>die/drop/fall like ˈflies</td><td>大批死掉；成片病倒</td><td>With the flu going round the office, people are dropping like flies.<br>办公室流感一传开，人一个接一个地倒下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(there are) no flies on sb (informal)</td><td>某人很精明；不容易上当</td><td>Don't try to overcharge her—there are no flies on that woman.<br>别想多收她钱，那女人精着呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flight</b></td><td>a flight of ˈfancy</td><td>异想天开；不切实际的想象</td><td>His plan to buy an island was just another flight of fancy.<br>他要买座岛的计划不过是又一次异想天开。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the first/top ˈflight</td><td>位居前列；属于佼佼者</td><td>She is now in the top flight of British tennis after that win.<br>赢下那场比赛后，她跻身英国网球一流选手之列。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈflight</td><td>逃走；仓皇而逃</td><td>The burglars took flight the moment the alarm started screaming.<br>警报一响，窃贼们立刻逃之夭夭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fling</b></td><td>have a ˈfling (informal)</td><td>尽情玩乐；短暂的风流韵事</td><td>Before settling down, he had one last fling travelling around Asia.<br>安定下来之前，他最后放纵了一回，跑遍了亚洲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flip</b></td><td>flip your ˈlid (AmE also flip your ˈwig) (informal)</td><td>勃然大怒；发火</td><td>Dad flipped his lid when he saw the phone bill this month.<br>我爸看到这个月的话费单时暴跳如雷。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>float</b></td><td>float sb's ˈboat (informal)</td><td>合某人心意；讨某人喜欢</td><td>Jazz doesn't really float my boat, but I'll come along anyway.<br>爵士乐我不太感冒，不过我还是跟你去吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flog</b></td><td>ˌflog a dead ˈhorse (BrE, informal)</td><td>白费力气；做无用功</td><td>Asking him to apologize again is flogging a dead horse, honestly.<br>说实话，再让他道歉纯属白费力气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>flog sth to ˈdeath (BrE, informal)</td><td>把某事说滥；反复使用以致乏味</td><td>That advertising slogan has been flogged to death over the past year.<br>那句广告语这一年被用滥了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flood</b></td><td>flood the ˈmarket</td><td>大量抛售商品；充斥市场</td><td>Cheap imported toys have flooded the market and hurt local makers.<br>廉价进口玩具充斥市场，把本地厂家挤垮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>floods</b></td><td>be in ˈfloods (of ˈtears) (informal)</td><td>泪如雨下；痛哭流涕</td><td>She was in floods of tears when she heard her dog had been found.<br>听说狗找到了，她哭得稀里哗啦。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>floor</b></td><td>hold the ˈfloor</td><td>长时间独自发言；垄断谈话</td><td>Uncle Bob held the floor for an hour telling stories about the war.<br>鲍勃叔叔滔滔不绝讲了一小时战争往事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈfloor</td><td>起立发言；步入舞池</td><td>The union representative took the floor and demanded better safety rules.<br>工会代表起身发言，要求改善安全规定。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flotsam</b></td><td>flotsam and ˈjetsam</td><td>漂浮的残骸杂物；社会上的流浪者</td><td>After the storm, the beach was covered with flotsam and jetsam.<br>暴风雨过后，海滩上满是漂来的杂物残骸。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flow</b></td><td>go with the ˈflow (informal)</td><td>顺其自然；随大流</td><td>Stop planning every minute of the trip and just go with the flow.<br>别把行程每分钟都排满，顺其自然就好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flower</b></td><td>the flower of sth (literary)</td><td>精华；最优秀的部分</td><td>The flower of a whole generation was lost in those four years.<br>整整一代人的精英都葬送在那四年里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fly</b></td><td>the ˌfeathers/ˌfur/ˌsparks will ˈfly (informal)</td><td>会大吵一架；会闹得不可开交</td><td>When she finds out he sold her car, the sparks will fly.<br>等她发现他把车卖了，非闹翻天不可。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fly the ˈcoop (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>溜走；逃离</td><td>By the time the police arrived, the suspect had already flown the coop.<br>警察赶到时，嫌疑人早就溜之大吉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fly ˈhigh</td><td>非常成功；事业兴旺</td><td>Her design studio is flying high after winning that international prize.<br>拿下那个国际奖之后，她的设计工作室风生水起。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fly in the face of ˈsth (written)</td><td>公然违抗；与……背道而驰</td><td>His claims fly in the face of everything the research has shown.<br>他的说法与所有研究结果完全相悖。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the fly in the ˈointment (informal)</td><td>美中不足之处；扫兴的因素</td><td>The hotel was lovely; the only fly in the ointment was the noisy road.<br>酒店很不错，唯一美中不足是马路太吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fly into a ˈrage, ˈtemper, etc.</td><td>突然大怒；勃然发火</td><td>He flew into a rage when the waiter brought the wrong order twice.<br>服务员两次上错菜，他一下子火冒三丈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fly a ˈkite (BrE, informal)</td><td>放风声试探反应</td><td>The minister flew a kite about raising taxes to see how voters reacted.<br>部长放出加税的风声，看看选民什么反应。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(go) fly a/your ˈkite (AmE, informal)</td><td>走开；别烦我</td><td>I told the pushy salesman to go fly a kite and shut the door.<br>我叫那个死缠烂打的推销员走开，然后关上了门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌfly the ˈnest</td><td>（子女）离家独立生活</td><td>Now that both kids have flown the nest, the house feels enormous.<br>两个孩子都离家了，屋子显得空荡荡的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fly off the ˈhandle (informal)</td><td>勃然大怒；大发雷霆</td><td>Try to explain calmly instead of flying off the handle at him.<br>好好跟他解释，别一上来就对他发火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a fly on the ˈwall</td><td>不为人察觉的旁观者</td><td>I'd love to be a fly on the wall during their negotiation tomorrow.<br>真想明天躲在他们谈判现场偷偷看一眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let ˈfly (at sb/sth) (with sth) (informal)</td><td>猛掷；破口大骂</td><td>The boy let fly at the window with a stone and ran off.<br>那男孩朝窗户猛掷一块石头就跑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈfly (informal)</td><td>匆匆地；同时忙别的事时</td><td>I edited the whole speech on the fly during the taxi ride there.<br>我在去那儿的出租车上匆匆把整篇讲稿改完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>he, she, etc. wouldn't harm/hurt a ˈfly</td><td>心地善良；连只苍蝇都不忍伤害</td><td>That huge dog looks scary but he wouldn't hurt a fly.<br>那条大狗看着吓人，其实连只苍蝇都不会伤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flying</b></td><td>a ˌflying ˈvisit</td><td>闪电式访问；短暂停留</td><td>She paid us a flying visit between two meetings and left after tea.<br>她在两个会之间来我们这儿坐了坐，喝完茶就走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get off to a ˌflying ˈstart • get off to a ˈflyer</td><td>开局良好；有个好开端</td><td>The charity appeal got off to a flying start with a huge first donation.<br>头一笔捐款数额巨大，这次募捐开局大好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈflying (BrE, informal)</td><td>摔倒；被绊倒</td><td>He tripped on the loose carpet and went flying across the hallway.<br>他被松脱的地毯绊了一下，在走廊上摔了个大跟头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with ˌflying ˈcolours (BrE) (AmE with ˌflying ˈcolors)</td><td>出色地；成绩优异地</td><td>She passed her driving test with flying colours on the first attempt.<br>她第一次考驾照就轻松高分通过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fog</b></td><td>in a ˈfog (informal)</td><td>一头雾水；迷惘糊涂</td><td>After the long flight I spent the whole day in a fog.<br>坐了那么久的飞机，我一整天都昏头昏脑的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>food for ˈthought</td><td>引人深思的事；发人深省的内容</td><td>Her talk on food waste gave us all plenty of food for thought.<br>她关于食物浪费的演讲让我们都陷入了思考。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fold sb in your ˈarms (literary)</td><td>把某人搂入怀中</td><td>He folded his daughter in his arms and told her not to cry.<br>他把女儿搂进怀里，叫她别哭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>follow in sb's ˈfootsteps</td><td>步某人后尘；继承某人的事业</td><td>She followed in her mother's footsteps and became a country doctor.<br>她追随母亲的脚步，也成了一名乡村医生。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>follow your ˈnose</td><td>一直往前走；凭直觉行事</td><td>Just follow your nose down this street and you'll see the market.<br>沿着这条街一直走，你就能看见市场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>follow ˈsuit</td><td>照着做；跟着仿效</td><td>One bank cut its rates and the others quickly followed suit.<br>一家银行降息，其他银行很快跟进。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>any fool can/could... (spoken)</td><td>傻子也能……（形容极其容易）</td><td>Any fool can criticize the plan; try writing a better one yourself.<br>谁都会挑毛病，你倒是自己写个更好的出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌno/ˌnobody's ˈfool</td><td>很精明；不易上当</td><td>Don't try that trick on Grandma—she's nobody's fool.<br>别拿那套糊弄奶奶，她精明着呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌfool's ˈerrand</td><td>徒劳无益的差事</td><td>Driving across town for a shop that closed years ago was a fool's errand.<br>开车穿城去一家早就关门的店，纯属白跑一趟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a fool's ˈparadise</td><td>虚幻的幸福；自欺欺人的美梦</td><td>They're living in a fool's paradise if they think the debt will vanish.<br>要是以为债务会自己消失，他们就是在做白日梦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈfool of sb/yourself</td><td>使出丑；出洋相</td><td>I made a complete fool of myself singing karaoke at the office party.<br>公司聚会上我唱卡拉OK，把自己丢人现眼了一回。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmore fool ˈyou, them, etc. (spoken)</td><td>（斥责）你真够蠢的；活该</td><td>You lent him money again? More fool you, he never pays anyone back.<br>你又借钱给他？你真够傻的，他从不还钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(there's) ˌno fool like an ˈold fool (saying)</td><td>老糊涂最糊涂；老年荒唐最可笑</td><td>He's sixty and buying a sports car—there's no fool like an old fool.<br>他六十了还买跑车，真是老糊涂最糊涂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fooled</b></td><td>you could have ˌfooled ˈme! (informal)</td><td>我可不信；你休想骗我</td><td>You say you cleaned the room? You could have fooled me!<br>你说你打扫过房间？我可不信！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fools</b></td><td>fools rush ˈin (where angels fear to ˈtread) (saying)</td><td>无知者无畏；莽汉闯入天使止步之地</td><td>He gave marriage advice to a couple he'd just met—fools rush in.<br>他给刚认识的一对夫妻出婚姻主意，真是无知者无畏。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>foot</b></td><td>foot the ˈbill (for sth)</td><td>付账；负担费用</td><td>Her parents footed the bill for the entire wedding reception.<br>婚宴的全部费用都是她父母出的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/have a/your ˌfoot in the ˈdoor</td><td>取得初步进入的机会</td><td>The internship was badly paid but it got her foot in the door.<br>那份实习工资很低，却让她敲开了行业的大门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/start off on the right/wrong ˈfoot (with sb) (informal)</td><td>（与某人）一开始就相处得好（或不好）</td><td>I got off on the wrong foot with my new boss by arriving late.<br>我第一天就迟到，跟新老板开局就不顺。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a foot in both ˈcamps (informal)</td><td>脚踏两只船；同时与对立双方有关系</td><td>As both a farmer and a conservationist, he has a foot in both camps.<br>他既是农场主又是环保人士，两边都沾着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>my foot! (informal, humorous)</td><td>胡说八道；才怪呢</td><td>He's too busy to help? Too busy my foot, he's watching football.<br>他忙得没空帮忙？忙个鬼，他在看球呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not/never put/set a foot ˈwrong (informal)</td><td>从不出错；从未走错一步</td><td>In thirty years at the firm she never put a foot wrong.<br>在公司三十年，她从来没出过一次差错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈfoot</td><td>步行；徒步</td><td>The bridge was closed, so we crossed the river on foot further upstream.<br>桥封了，我们只好从上游徒步过河。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put your ˈfoot down (informal)</td><td>坚决反对；踩油门加速</td><td>Mum finally put her foot down and banned phones at the dinner table.<br>妈妈终于坚决表态，吃饭时不许玩手机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put your ˈfoot in it (BrE) (also put your foot in your ˈmouth AmE, BrE) (informal)</td><td>说错话；无意中冒犯别人</td><td>I really put my foot in it by asking about his ex-wife.<br>我问起他前妻，真是说错话了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set ˈfoot in/on sth</td><td>踏入；进入某地</td><td>She swore she would never set foot in that restaurant again.<br>她发誓再也不踏进那家餐厅一步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put your best foot ˈforward</td><td>全力以赴；尽力表现好</td><td>It's your first day, so put your best foot forward and smile a lot.<br>今天是你第一天上班，好好表现，多笑笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>footloose</b></td><td>footloose and fancy-ˈfree</td><td>无牵无挂；自由自在</td><td>At twenty-two, footloose and fancy-free, he bought a one-way ticket to Peru.<br>二十二岁时他无牵无挂，买了张去秘鲁的单程票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>footsie</b></td><td>play ˈfootsie (with sb)</td><td>（桌下）用脚碰脚调情；暗中勾搭</td><td>She was playing footsie with him under the table all through dinner.<br>整顿饭她都在桌子底下用脚跟他调情。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>for</b></td><td>A for B</td><td>逐一对应；一项对一项地</td><td>They checked the two lists A for B and found three names missing.<br>他们把两份名单逐一对照，发现少了三个名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈall...</td><td>尽管；虽然</td><td>For all his money, he seems a rather lonely and unhappy man.<br>尽管他很有钱，看上去却孤单又不快乐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for all (the world) to ˈsee</td><td>众目睽睽之下；显而易见</td><td>Her disappointment was written on her face for all to see.<br>她脸上的失望之情谁都看得出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>forbid</b></td><td>God/Heaven forˈbid (that...) (also humorous)</td><td>但愿不会；千万别</td><td>God forbid that anything should happen to the children on that road.<br>但愿孩子们在那条路上别出什么事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Heaven forˈfend (that...) (old use)</td><td>但愿不会发生；上天保佑别这样</td><td>Heaven forfend that we should ever have to sell the family house.<br>但愿我们永远不必卖掉这套祖屋。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>forbidden</b></td><td>forˌbidden ˈfruit</td><td>禁果；因被禁而更诱人的事物</td><td>Sweets were forbidden fruit in our house, which made us want them more.<br>在我们家糖果是禁果，越不让吃越想吃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>force</b></td><td>bring sth into ˈforce • come into ˈforce</td><td>（使法律等）生效；开始实施</td><td>The new smoking ban comes into force at the beginning of next month.<br>新的禁烟规定从下月初开始生效。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>force sb's ˈhand</td><td>迫使某人提前或改变计划</td><td>The leaked email forced the company's hand and they announced the layoffs.<br>邮件泄露逼得公司不得不提前宣布裁员。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈforce the issue</td><td>迫使问题摊牌；逼人迅速决断</td><td>She forced the issue by asking him publicly whether he would resign.<br>她当众问他是否辞职，把问题挑明了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>force of ˈcircumstance</td><td>情势所迫；迫不得已</td><td>By force of circumstance, we ended up living with my parents for a year.<br>情势所迫，我们最后跟我父母同住了一年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>force of ˈhabit</td><td>习惯使然；出于习惯</td><td>I still reach for my keys at that door out of force of habit.<br>我还是会习惯性地在那扇门前掏钥匙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>force the ˈpace (especially BrE)</td><td>迫使加快速度；加紧推进</td><td>The younger runners forced the pace over the last two kilometres.<br>最后两公里几个年轻选手加快了节奏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a force to be ˈreckoned with a force to be ˈreckoned with</td><td>厉害角色；不容轻视的对手</td><td>Be very careful how you deal with her, because she's a force to be reckoned with.<br>跟她打交道千万小心，她可是个厉害人物。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈforce/ˈstrength</td><td>大批地；大量出动</td><td>Police turned out in force to control the crowd outside the stadium.<br>警察大批出动，维持体育场外的人群秩序。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>forces</b></td><td>the forces of ˈnature</td><td>大自然的威力（尤指破坏性的）</td><td>No sea wall can hold back the forces of nature for ever.<br>再坚固的海堤也挡不住大自然的力量。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>join/combine ˈforces (with sb)</td><td>（与某人）联手；通力合作</td><td>Two small charities joined forces to build the new children's library.<br>两家小慈善机构联手建起了这座儿童图书馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fore</b></td><td>be/come to the ˈfore (BrE) (AmE be at the ˈfore)</td><td>崭露头角；起重要作用</td><td>Young designers have come to the fore since the competition last spring.<br>自去年春天那场比赛后，年轻设计师纷纷崭露头角。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring sth to the ˈfore</td><td>使某事突出；使受到关注</td><td>The scandal brought the issue of factory safety to the fore.<br>这桩丑闻让工厂安全问题浮出水面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>forefront</b></td><td>at/in/to the ˈforefront (of sth)</td><td>在最前列；处于领先地位</td><td>This lab has been at the forefront of cancer research for a decade.<br>这个实验室十年来一直处在癌症研究的最前沿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>forelock</b></td><td>touch/tug your ˈforelock (disapproving)</td><td>卑躬屈膝；点头哈腰</td><td>He refuses to tug his forelock to anyone, however senior they are.<br>不管对方职位多高，他都不肯低三下四。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>foreseeable</b></td><td>ˌforewarned is foreˈarmed (saying)</td><td>有备无患；预先警告即预先武装</td><td>Read the contract before the meeting—forewarned is forearmed.<br>开会前先把合同看一遍，有备无患。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>God/Heaven forˈbid (that...)</td><td>但愿不会；上天保佑别这样</td><td>Heaven forbid that we should ever go through another winter like that.<br>但愿我们再也别过那样的冬天了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>forget</b></td><td>forˈget it (spoken)</td><td>算了；别提了；不用谢</td><td>You want me to drive four hours in this snow? Forget it.<br>你要我在这大雪天开四个小时车？别想了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>good</b></td><td>off ˈform (also out of ˈform)</td><td>状态不佳；发挥失常</td><td>The goalkeeper has been badly off form since he came back from injury.<br>这名门将伤愈复出后状态一直很差。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈform (also in (good) ˈform)</td><td>状态良好；发挥出色</td><td>Grandpa was on great form at dinner, telling one joke after another.<br>爷爷晚饭时状态极佳，一个接一个地讲笑话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈform (formal)</td><td>逐渐成形；渐渐形成</td><td>A plan for the new community garden slowly took form over the winter.<br>整个冬天，新社区花园的方案慢慢成形了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>former</b></td><td>be a shadow/ghost of your/its former ˈself</td><td>远不如从前；风光不再</td><td>After the factory closed, the town became a shadow of its former self.<br>工厂关闭后，这座小镇早已不复当年的模样。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fort</b></td><td>hold the ˈfort (BrE) (AmE hold down the ˈfort)</td><td>暂时代管；帮忙照看</td><td>Can you hold the fort in the shop while I take Mum to hospital?<br>我送我妈去医院，店里你先顶一下好吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>forth</b></td><td>be like painting the Forth ˈBridge (BrE)</td><td>永远做不完的活儿；没完没了</td><td>Cleaning up after three kids is like painting the Forth Bridge.<br>给三个孩子收拾屋子，永远也收拾不完。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>forth</b></td><td>and ˈso forth (also and ˈso on (and ˈso forth))</td><td>等等；诸如此类</td><td>Bring a towel, sunscreen, a hat and so forth—it'll be very hot.<br>带上毛巾、防晒霜、帽子等等，那边会很热。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>back and ˈforth (also ˌbackwards and ˈforwards)</td><td>来回地；反复地</td><td>The nurse walked back and forth in the corridor waiting for news.<br>护士在走廊里来回踱步，等着消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌbackwards and ˈforwards</td><td>来回；往返奔波</td><td>She travels backwards and forwards between the factory and head office.<br>她在工厂和总部之间来回奔波。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from that day/time ˈforth (literary)</td><td>从那天起；自那时起</td><td>From that day forth he never spoke his brother's name again.<br>从那天起，他再没提过他弟弟的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold ˈforth (about/on sth) (disapproving)</td><td>喋喋不休；发表冗长议论</td><td>He held forth about modern art for twenty minutes without pausing.<br>他滔滔不绝讲了二十分钟现代艺术，中间都没停。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be like/as safe as Fort ˈKnox</td><td>固若金汤；戒备森严</td><td>The new server room is as safe as Fort Knox, with three separate locks.<br>新机房固若金汤，装了三道独立的锁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fortune</b></td><td>fortune ˈsmiles on sb</td><td>某人交好运；时来运转</td><td>Fortune smiled on us and the rain stopped just before the ceremony.<br>我们运气不错，仪式开始前雨正好停了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈfortune</td><td>发财；赚大钱</td><td>He made a fortune selling bicycle parts online during the lockdown.<br>封控期间他在网上卖自行车配件发了财。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a hostage to ˈfortune</td><td>授人以柄的言行；招致风险的承诺</td><td>Promising zero delays was a hostage to fortune he later regretted.<br>承诺绝不延误成了他日后追悔的把柄。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a small ˈfortune</td><td>一大笔钱</td><td>That leaking roof has already cost us a small fortune this year.<br>今年那个漏雨的屋顶已经花了我们一大笔钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>forty</b></td><td>forty ˈwinks (informal)</td><td>小睡；打个盹</td><td>Dad always has forty winks in his armchair after Sunday lunch.<br>周日午饭后我爸总要在扶手椅上打个盹。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fall</b></td><td>fall foul of ˈsb/ˈsth</td><td>与某人发生冲突；触犯（规定等）</td><td>The company fell foul of the tax authorities and paid a huge fine.<br>这家公司触犯了税务部门，交了一大笔罚款。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>found</b></td><td>be in/out of the ˈframe (for sth)</td><td>有（或没有）资格参与；被列入或排除</td><td>After that win, our team is still in the frame for the championship.<br>赢下那场后，我们队仍有争夺冠军的资格。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nowhere to be ˈfound/ˈseen</td><td>遍寻不见；找不到</td><td>When the bill arrived, my generous friend was nowhere to be found.<br>账单一来，那位大方的朋友就不见人影了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nowhere in ˈsight</td><td>看不到；毫无踪影</td><td>We waited an hour, but the bus was still nowhere in sight.<br>我们等了一个小时，公交车还是连影子都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shake</b></td><td>rock sth to its ˈfoundations</td><td>从根本上动摇；撼动根基</td><td>The scandal rocked the whole sport to its foundations.<br>这桩丑闻从根基上撼动了整个体育项目。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌfounding ˈfather(s) of sth (formal)</td><td>（国家、组织、学科的）创始人；奠基者</td><td>He is regarded as one of the founding fathers of modern computing.<br>他被视为现代计算机科学的奠基人之一。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the four ˌcorners of the ˈearth</td><td>天涯海角；世界各地</td><td>Fans came from the four corners of the earth to see the final concert.<br>歌迷从世界各地赶来看那场告别演唱会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>free</b></td><td>be in/go into ˌfree ˈfall</td><td>急剧下跌；直线下滑</td><td>House prices in the region went into free fall after the factory closed.<br>工厂关闭后，这一带的房价直线下跌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈfree</td><td>免费</td><td>The café gives day-old bread to students for free every evening.<br>那家咖啡馆每天傍晚把隔夜面包免费送给学生。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>free and ˈeasy</td><td>随意轻松；无拘无束</td><td>The atmosphere in the studio is free and easy, and nobody wears a tie.<br>工作室气氛很随意，没人打领带。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) free as (the) ˈair/as a ˈbird</td><td>完全自由；无拘无束</td><td>With the exams over, I felt as free as a bird all summer.<br>考完试后，整个夏天我都自由得像只鸟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get, have, etc. a free ˈhand</td><td>有自主权；可自行决定</td><td>The new chef was given a free hand to redesign the whole menu.<br>新厨师获准自行决定，把整份菜单重新设计。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get, take, etc. a free ˈride</td><td>白占便宜；不出力而得好处</td><td>He's had a free ride for years while the rest of us do the work.<br>这些年活儿都是我们干，他一直白占便宜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's a free ˈcountry (spoken)</td><td>这是自由的国家（我爱怎样就怎样）</td><td>I'll sit here if I want to—it's a free country, isn't it?<br>我愿意坐这儿就坐这儿，这可是自由的国家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make free with sth (disapproving)</td><td>擅自使用（别人的东西）</td><td>He makes free with my tools and never puts any of them back.<br>他随便拿我的工具用，还从来不放回去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of your own ˌfree ˈwill</td><td>自愿地；出于本意</td><td>She signed the agreement of her own free will, with no pressure at all.<br>她完全出于自愿签了协议，没有受到任何压力。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>french</b></td><td>exˌcuse/ˌpardon my ˈFrench (informal, humorous)</td><td>请原谅我说粗话</td><td>The whole thing was a bloody disaster, pardon my French.<br>整件事糟透了，恕我说话难听。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take French ˈleave (BrE, old-fashioned or humorous)</td><td>不辞而别；擅离职守</td><td>Two of the workers took French leave and went fishing all afternoon.<br>有两个工人擅自溜号，钓了一下午鱼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fresh</b></td><td>(as) fresh as a ˈdaisy</td><td>精神饱满；容光焕发</td><td>After ten hours' sleep she came down as fresh as a daisy.<br>睡了十个小时后，她下楼时神清气爽。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fresh out of sth (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>刚刚用完（或卖完）</td><td>Sorry, we're fresh out of chocolate cake, but the apple pie is good.<br>抱歉，巧克力蛋糕刚卖完，不过苹果派不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get ˈfresh (with sb) (informal)</td><td>（对某人）放肆无礼；轻薄</td><td>The barman got fresh with a customer and was fired the next day.<br>那个酒保对顾客动手动脚，第二天就被辞退了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈfriends (with sb)</td><td>（与某人）交朋友</td><td>My son made friends with the boy next door on his very first day.<br>我儿子头一天就跟隔壁男孩交上了朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌFreudian ˈslip</td><td>说漏嘴；无意中泄露真实想法</td><td>Calling his wife by his ex's name was quite a Freudian slip.<br>他把妻子叫成前女友的名字，真是说漏了心里话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>friends</b></td><td>have ˌfriends in high ˈplaces</td><td>上面有人；有权贵朋友</td><td>The permit came through fast because he has friends in high places.<br>许可证办得飞快，因为他上面有人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>frog</b></td><td>have a ˈfrog in your throat (informal)</td><td>嗓子发哑；说话不清楚</td><td>Sorry, I've got a frog in my throat this morning—let me get some water.<br>抱歉，今早我嗓子哑了，我喝口水。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>front</b></td><td>ˌback to ˈfront</td><td>前后颠倒；穿反了</td><td>He rushed out with his sweater on back to front and didn't notice.<br>他匆匆出门，毛衣前后穿反了都没发现。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌfront and ˈcenter (AmE)</td><td>处于最重要的位置；备受关注</td><td>Housing costs are front and center in this year's local election.<br>住房成本是今年地方选举最受关注的议题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the front ˈline (of sth)</td><td>在第一线；身处要冲</td><td>Nurses were in the front line throughout the whole outbreak.<br>整个疫情期间护士都在第一线。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the front ˈburner (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>（问题等）受到重视；成为焦点</td><td>The bridge repairs are finally on the front burner at city hall.<br>修桥的事在市政厅终于被摆到了首要位置。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up ˈfront (informal)</td><td>（钱）预付；坦率地</td><td>The builder wants half the money up front before he starts work.<br>施工方要求开工前先付一半的钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>full</b></td><td>come to a full ˈstop (BrE)</td><td>完全停止；戛然而止</td><td>Talks between the two sides came to a full stop after the walkout.<br>一方退场后，双方的谈判彻底停了下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>full steam/speed aˈhead</td><td>全速前进；全力以赴</td><td>Now the permits are signed, it's full steam ahead with the new wing.<br>许可批下来了，新楼那边可以全速开工了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>full ˈmarks (to sb for doing sth) (BrE)</td><td>满分；大加赞扬</td><td>Full marks to the team for finishing the whole job in one weekend.<br>这个团队一个周末干完全部活儿，值得大大表扬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌfull ˈmonty (BrE, informal)</td><td>全套；应有尽有</td><td>For breakfast he ordered the full monty—eggs, bacon, beans, the lot.<br>早餐他点了全套：鸡蛋、培根、豆子，样样都有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>full of ˈbeans (informal)</td><td>精力充沛；生龙活虎</td><td>The puppy is full of beans again now that his leg has healed.<br>小狗的腿好了，又活蹦乱跳起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in full ˈswing</td><td>在高潮中；进行得热火朝天</td><td>By nine o'clock the street festival was in full swing.<br>到九点钟，街头庆典已经进入高潮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in full ˈview (of sb/sth)</td><td>在众目睽睽之下；一览无余</td><td>He dropped the tray in full view of the entire restaurant.<br>他当着整个餐厅的面把托盘摔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not the full ˈquid (AustralE, NZE, informal)</td><td>脑子不太灵光；不够聪明</td><td>People say the old man isn't the full quid, but he beats me at chess.<br>人家说那老头儿脑子不灵光，可下棋我下不过他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the ˈfull</td><td>尽情地；充分地</td><td>After his illness he decided to live life to the full.<br>生了那场病之后，他决定要尽情地活。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fullness</b></td><td>in the fullness of ˈtime (formal)</td><td>时机成熟时；到头来</td><td>In the fullness of time she will understand why we did this.<br>时候到了，她自会明白我们为什么这么做。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fun</b></td><td>for ˈfun • for the ˈfun of it</td><td>为了好玩；闹着玩</td><td>He learned to juggle just for the fun of it during the long winter.<br>漫长的冬天里，他纯粹为好玩学会了杂耍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>funeral</b></td><td>go ˈfurther</td><td>更进一步；说得更过分</td><td>I'd go further and say the whole system needs replacing.<br>我甚至想说，整个系统都该换掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go no ˈfurther • not go any ˈfurther</td><td>（秘密）到此为止；不再外传</td><td>I'll tell you, but this must go no further than this room.<br>我可以告诉你，但这话不能传出这个房间。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nothing could be further from the ˈtruth, etc.</td><td>根本不是这么回事；完全不对</td><td>People think he's arrogant, but nothing could be further from the truth.<br>人们觉得他傲慢，其实完全不是这么回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nothing could be further from the ˈtruth</td><td>绝无此事；完全是误会</td><td>You may think I'm judging your outfit, but nothing could be further from the truth.<br>你以为我在挑剔你的穿着，其实完全不是。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth ˈfurther</td><td>进一步追究；把某事继续推进</td><td>If the shop won't refund you, take it further with the ombudsman.<br>店里要是不退款，就找监察专员继续追究。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌgame is not worth the ˈcandle (old-fashioned, saying)</td><td>得不偿失；不值得费这个劲</td><td>Driving two hours to save five pounds—the game is not worth the candle.<br>开两小时车省五英镑，实在得不偿失。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the game is ˈup (BrE, informal)</td><td>阴谋败露；玩完了</td><td>When the police showed him the video, he knew the game was up.<br>警察给他看录像时，他知道自己完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give the ˈgame away (informal)</td><td>泄露秘密；露馅儿</td><td>Don't grin like that—you'll give the game away before she opens it.<br>别那么傻笑，她还没拆礼物你就露馅了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep sb ˈguessing (informal)</td><td>让某人捉摸不透；吊人胃口</td><td>The director keeps us guessing right up to the final scene.<br>导演一直吊着观众胃口，直到最后一幕才揭晓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be/go) on the ˈgame (BrE, slang)</td><td>卖淫；做妓女</td><td>She wrote a book about young women who go on the game to survive.<br>她写了本书，讲那些为了活下去而卖身的年轻女子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the only game in ˈtown (informal)</td><td>唯一的选择；同类中最重要者</td><td>For late-night food around here, that noodle shop is the only game in town.<br>这一带深夜想吃东西，只有那家面馆一个选择。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play the ˈgame</td><td>办事公道；按规矩行事</td><td>He may be tough, but he always plays the game with his suppliers.<br>他也许不好说话，但对供应商一向讲规矩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play sb's ˈgame • play the same ˈgame (as sb)</td><td>以对方的方式行事；跟着对方那一套来</td><td>If they leak stories, we'll play the same game and talk to reporters too.<br>他们放风，我们也照着来，同样找记者。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play sb at their own ˈgame</td><td>以其人之道还治其人之身</td><td>She undercut their prices and beat them at their own game.<br>她压低价格，用他们那一套把他们打败了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's sb's/your ˈgame? (BrE, spoken)</td><td>你搞什么鬼；你打什么算盘</td><td>You've been hanging round my shop all week—what's your game?<br>你在我店门口转悠了一星期，到底打什么主意？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>games</b></td><td>play (silly) ˈgames (with sb)</td><td>（与某人）耍花招；玩把戏</td><td>Stop playing games with me and tell me what you actually want.<br>别跟我兜圈子了，直说你到底想要什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gamut</b></td><td>run the ˈgamut of sth</td><td>经历全过程；涵盖各种情形</td><td>Her films run the gamut of human emotion, from joy to despair.<br>她的电影涵盖了从欢愉到绝望的各种情感。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your/the last ˈgasp</td><td>最后一刻；奄奄一息之时</td><td>They scored at the last gasp and stole the match from us.<br>他们在最后一刻进球，把比赛从我们手里抢走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/take a ˈgander (at sth) (informal)</td><td>看一看；瞧一眼</td><td>Come and take a gander at the old photos I found in the attic.<br>过来瞧瞧我在阁楼上找到的这些老照片。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gangbusters</b></td><td>like ˈgangbusters (AmE, informal)</td><td>势头强劲；干得热火朝天</td><td>Their little bakery is going like gangbusters since the article appeared.<br>那篇报道出来后，他们的小面包房生意火得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>garden</b></td><td>everything in the garden is ˈlovely/ˈrosy</td><td>一切顺利；万事如意</td><td>He talks as if everything in the garden is rosy, but the debts are huge.<br>他说得好像一切顺利，其实欠了一屁股债。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gates</b></td><td>the Pearly ˈGates (humorous)</td><td>天堂之门</td><td>Grandad joked that he'd argue his way through the Pearly Gates.<br>爷爷开玩笑说，他能靠嘴皮子混进天堂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gather</b></td><td>gather ˈdust</td><td>被束之高阁；无人问津</td><td>His report has been gathering dust on the director's desk for months.<br>他的报告在主任桌上搁了好几个月没人理。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gauntlet</b></td><td>run the ˈgauntlet</td><td>遭到众人攻击；受夹道责难</td><td>The players had to run the gauntlet of angry fans outside the stadium.<br>球员们不得不从愤怒的球迷夹道中穿过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take up the ˈgauntlet</td><td>接受挑战；应战</td><td>Nobody else would debate him, so she took up the gauntlet.<br>没人肯跟他辩论，于是她接下了这个挑战。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw down the ˈgauntlet</td><td>提出挑战；下战书</td><td>The small company threw down the gauntlet to the industry giants.<br>这家小公司向行业巨头发起了挑战。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gay</b></td><td>with gay aˈbandon (old-fashioned)</td><td>无所顾忌地；轻率地</td><td>He spent his bonus with gay abandon and regretted it a month later.<br>他把奖金花得毫无节制，一个月后就后悔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gear</b></td><td>get into ˈgear • get sth into ˈgear</td><td>（使）开始运转；进入状态</td><td>It takes me two coffees to get into gear on Monday mornings.<br>周一早上我得喝两杯咖啡才能进入状态。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(slip/be thrown) out of ˈgear</td><td>失去控制；乱了套</td><td>The whole schedule was thrown out of gear by the sudden strike.<br>突如其来的罢工把整个日程都打乱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>general</b></td><td>in ˈgeneral</td><td>通常；大体上</td><td>In general, the food here is good, though tonight was disappointing.<br>这里的饭菜总体不错，不过今晚让人失望。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in parˈticular</td><td>尤其；特别是</td><td>I liked the whole album, but the last song in particular stayed with me.<br>整张专辑我都喜欢，尤其最后那首一直在我脑子里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>genie</b></td><td>the ˌgenie is out of the ˈbottle</td><td>覆水难收；后果已无法收回</td><td>Once the files were leaked, the genie was out of the bottle.<br>文件一泄露，就再也收不回来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let the ˌgenie out of the ˈbottle</td><td>放出魔鬼；引发难以收拾的后果</td><td>Legalizing it now would let the genie out of the bottle, he warned.<br>他警告说，现在放开等于把魔鬼从瓶子里放出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gentleman</b></td><td>a ˌgentleman's aˈgreement (also a ˌgentlemen's aˈgreement)</td><td>君子协定；口头协议</td><td>There was no contract, just a gentleman's agreement sealed with a handshake.<br>没有合同，只有握手为凭的君子协定。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get</b></td><td>can't get ˈover sth (spoken)</td><td>对……感到十分惊讶（或好笑）</td><td>I can't get over how much your son has grown since last summer.<br>你儿子从去年夏天到现在长这么高，真让我吃惊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get aˈway from it all (informal)</td><td>躲个清静；抛开一切去休息</td><td>We rented a cabin in the hills to get away from it all for a week.<br>我们在山里租了间小屋，躲清静住了一周。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get ˈhold of sb/sth</td><td>联系上某人；弄到某物</td><td>I've been trying to get hold of the landlord since Friday morning.<br>从周五早上起我就一直想联系上房东。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈget it (in the ˈneck) (informal)</td><td>挨批；受责罚</td><td>If the report is late again, we'll all get it in the neck.<br>报告要是再晚交，我们都得挨骂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get it ˈon (with sb) (slang, especially AmE)</td><td>与某人发生性关系</td><td>The gossip is that those two got it on after the office party.<br>有传言说那两个人在公司聚会后好上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get sb ˈnowhere / not get sb ˈanywhere</td><td>对某人毫无帮助；没有好处</td><td>Shouting at the clerk will get you nowhere, so try being polite.<br>冲柜员嚷嚷没有用，客气点试试。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈget somewhere/anywhere/nowhere</td><td>有（或没有）进展</td><td>After three hours of talks we finally started to get somewhere.<br>谈了三个小时，我们终于开始有点进展了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈget there (informal)</td><td>达到目标；渐渐做成</td><td>My Spanish is still rough, but I'm getting there slowly.<br>我的西班牙语还很糟，不过在慢慢接近目标了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how selfish, stupid, ungrateful, etc. can you ˈget? (spoken)</td><td>怎么能这么自私（或愚蠢等）</td><td>He ate the whole cake alone—how selfish can you get?<br>他一个人把整个蛋糕吃了，怎么能这么自私？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>getting</b></td><td>be getting ˈon (informal)</td><td>上年纪了；上了岁数</td><td>Dad's getting on now and shouldn't be climbing ladders.<br>我爸上年纪了，不该再爬梯子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>getting on for... (especially BrE)</td><td>接近（某时刻、数目或年龄）</td><td>It's getting on for midnight, so we'd better call a taxi.<br>快到半夜了，我们最好叫辆出租车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no getting aˈway from it (informal)</td><td>这是躲不掉的事实；无法回避</td><td>There's no getting away from it—we simply can't afford this house.<br>这事躲不过去：这房子我们真买不起。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what are you, was he, etc. ˈgetting at?</td><td>你（他）到底想说什么</td><td>Just say it plainly—what exactly are you getting at?<br>你直说吧，到底想说什么？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ghost</b></td><td>give up the ˈghost</td><td>死去；（机器）报废停转</td><td>My old washing machine finally gave up the ghost last night.<br>我那台旧洗衣机昨晚终于彻底罢工了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have a ˈghost of a chance (of doing sth)</td><td>毫无机会；一点希望也没有</td><td>Without a lawyer he hasn't a ghost of a chance of winning the case.<br>没有律师，他打赢这场官司的机会等于零。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be a shadow/ghost of your/its former ˈself</td><td>远不如从前；风光不再</td><td>Since the injury, the striker is a ghost of his former self.<br>受伤之后，这名前锋早已不复当年之勇。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gift</b></td><td>the gift of the ˈgab (BrE) (AmE a gift of/for ˈgab) (informal, sometimes disapproving)</td><td>口才好；能说会道</td><td>With the gift of the gab, he could sell sand in the desert.<br>凭那张嘴，他在沙漠里都能把沙子卖出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) look a ˌgift horse in the ˈmouth</td><td>（不要）对馈赠挑三拣四</td><td>The car's free, so don't look a gift horse in the mouth.<br>车是白送的，就别挑三拣四了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gild</b></td><td>gild the ˈlily</td><td>画蛇添足；多此一举</td><td>Adding music to that beautiful film would be gilding the lily.<br>给那么美的片子再配乐纯属画蛇添足。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gills</b></td><td>to the ˈgills (informal)</td><td>满满当当；塞得很满</td><td>The little car was packed to the gills with camping equipment.<br>那辆小车里塞满了露营装备。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gilt</b></td><td>take the gilt off the ˈgingerbread (BrE)</td><td>使兴致大减；煞风景</td><td>The parking fine rather took the gilt off the gingerbread of our day out.<br>一张停车罚单把我们这天的兴致全毁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gird</b></td><td>gird (up) your ˈloins (literary or humorous)</td><td>准备行动；摩拳擦掌</td><td>Gird up your loins—we've got four hours of packing ahead.<br>打起精神来，还有四个小时的行李要收拾。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give</b></td><td>ˌdon't give me ˈthat (spoken, informal)</td><td>别跟我来这一套；我不信你那套</td><td>Don't give me that—you knew about the meeting all along.<br>别跟我来这套，你一直都知道有这个会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb a ˈbreak</td><td>给某人一次机会；宽容某人</td><td>Give the kid a break; it's only his second day on the job.<br>别难为这孩子了，他才上班第二天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌgive and ˈtake</td><td>互相让步；互谅互让</td><td>Any long marriage needs a lot of give and take from both sides.<br>长久的婚姻少不了双方的互相迁就。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give as good as you ˈget</td><td>针锋相对；不甘示弱</td><td>She's small, but in an argument she gives as good as she gets.<br>她个子小，吵起架来却从不吃亏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give me a ˈbreak! (spoken)</td><td>得了吧；饶了我吧</td><td>You finished the whole essay in an hour? Give me a break!<br>你一小时写完整篇论文？得了吧！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give or ˈtake (sth)</td><td>相差不过；出入不超过</td><td>The journey takes about two hours, give or take twenty minutes.<br>这趟路大约两小时，前后差个二十分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb what ˈfor • ˈgive it to sb (BrE, spoken)</td><td>狠狠训斥某人；严惩某人</td><td>Mum gave him what for when she saw the broken window.<br>妈妈看到打碎的窗户，把他狠狠骂了一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'll give you ˈthat (spoken)</td><td>这一点我承认；这话没错</td><td>He's lazy, but he's very funny, I'll give you that.<br>他是懒，不过挺逗的，这我承认。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gloves</b></td><td>the gloves are ˈoff (informal)</td><td>不再留情；开始激烈交锋</td><td>After that insult the gloves were off and the debate turned nasty.<br>那句羞辱之后双方就不再客气，辩论变得难看起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>handle/treat, etc. sb with kid ˈgloves</td><td>小心翼翼地对待某人</td><td>You'll have to handle the client with kid gloves after yesterday's mistake.<br>出了昨天那档子事，对这客户你得格外小心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>glowing</b></td><td>in glowing ˈterms/ˈcolours (BrE) (AmE in glowing ˈterms/ˈcolors)</td><td>热情赞美地；大加褒扬地</td><td>Her old boss described her in glowing terms to the interview panel.<br>她的老上司在面试小组面前对她大加称赞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>glued</b></td><td>be ˈglued to sth (informal)</td><td>目不转睛地盯着；紧贴着</td><td>The kids were glued to the screen all afternoon.<br>孩子们整个下午都盯着屏幕不放。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>glutton</b></td><td>a ˌglutton for ˈpunishment, ˈwork, etc. (informal)</td><td>自讨苦吃的人；工作狂</td><td>He's taken a second job—the man's a glutton for punishment.<br>他又找了份工作，真是个自讨苦吃的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gnash</b></td><td>gnash your ˈteeth</td><td>咬牙切齿；懊恼万分</td><td>He was gnashing his teeth after missing the penalty in the last minute.<br>最后一分钟点球罚丢，他懊恼得直咬牙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as things, people, etc. ˈgo</td><td>就一般情况而言；跟同类相比</td><td>As small hotels go, this one is remarkably comfortable and cheap.<br>就小旅馆而言，这家算相当舒服又便宜了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at/in one ˈgo (BrE)</td><td>一次；一举</td><td>He blew out all fifty candles in one go, to everyone's surprise.<br>他一口气吹灭了五十支蜡烛，大家都很惊讶。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be a ˈgo (AmE, informal)</td><td>已获批准；可以进行</td><td>The launch is a go—everyone report to the site at six.<br>发射照常进行，所有人六点到场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be on the ˈgo (informal)</td><td>忙个不停；一直奔忙</td><td>With three children and a job, she's on the go from dawn till midnight.<br>又要带三个孩子又要上班，她从早忙到半夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>don't go doing sth (spoken)</td><td>（告诫）可别去做某事</td><td>Don't go telling your mother about this before I've explained it.<br>在我解释清楚之前，你可别去跟你妈说这事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>first, second, etc. ˈgo (BrE)</td><td>第一次（或第二次等）尝试</td><td>She passed her driving test first go, which surprised everybody.<br>她第一次就考过了驾照，大家都很意外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go all ˈout for sth • go all out to ˈdo sth</td><td>全力以赴争取；竭尽全力做</td><td>The team went all out to win the cup in their captain's last season.<br>队长最后一个赛季，全队拼尽全力想夺冠。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈgo (at sth/at doing sth) (informal)</td><td>尝试做某事；试一试</td><td>I've never made bread before, but I'll have a go this weekend.<br>我从没做过面包，这周末打算试一试。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have sth on the ˈgo (informal)</td><td>手头正在进行某事</td><td>She's got three writing projects on the go at the same time.<br>她手头同时有三个写作项目在做。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not (even) ˈgo there (informal)</td><td>不想谈那个话题；别提了</td><td>His divorce? Let's not even go there tonight.<br>他离婚的事？今晚咱们就别提了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈgo</td><td>还剩；（食物）外带</td><td>Two exams down, one to go, and then I'm free for the summer.<br>考完两门还剩一门，考完暑假就自由了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>goat</b></td><td>act/play the ˈgoat (informal)</td><td>犯傻；出洋相</td><td>Stop playing the goat and help me carry these boxes upstairs.<br>别耍宝了，帮我把这些箱子搬上楼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get sb's ˈgoat (informal)</td><td>惹恼某人；让某人窝火</td><td>The way he chews his pen really gets my goat.<br>他咬笔的那副样子真让我火大。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>god</b></td><td>(good) ˈGod • God alˈmighty • God in ˈheaven (spoken)</td><td>（表示惊讶或愤怒）天哪；老天爷</td><td>Good God, what happened to the front of your car?<br>天哪，你车头怎么成这样了？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>my/oh ˈGod (spoken)</td><td>（表示惊讶、愤怒等）天哪</td><td>Oh my God, I've left the tickets on the kitchen table!<br>天哪，我把票落在厨房桌上了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>God ˈbless (spoken)</td><td>（道别时的祝福）愿上帝保佑你</td><td>Take care on the road tonight, and God bless.<br>今晚路上小心，愿上帝保佑你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>God's gift (to sb/sth) (ironic)</td><td>自以为是的天之骄子；上天的恩赐</td><td>He thinks he's God's gift to women, which is exhausting.<br>他自以为是女人心中的完美男人，真让人受不了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>God ˈwilling (spoken)</td><td>如果一切顺利；但愿如此</td><td>We'll be back home by Friday evening, God willing.<br>顺利的话，我们周五晚上就到家了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play ˈGod</td><td>自视全能；主宰他人命运</td><td>Doctors sometimes have to decide who gets the organ, but they hate playing God.<br>医生有时得决定器官给谁，但没人愿意扮演上帝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wish to ˈGod/ˈgoodness/ˈHeaven</td><td>（加强语气）真希望；巴不得</td><td>I wish to goodness you'd told me before I bought the tickets.<br>你要是在我买票之前告诉我就好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gods</b></td><td>in the lap of the ˈgods</td><td>听天由命；难以预料</td><td>We've done all we can; the result is in the lap of the gods now.<br>我们能做的都做了，结果只能听天由命。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>goes</b></td><td>what ˌgoes around ˈcomes around (saying)</td><td>善有善报，恶有恶报</td><td>He cheated everyone for years—what goes around comes around.<br>他骗了别人这么多年，善恶终有报。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>going</b></td><td>be going on (for) sth (BrE)</td><td>接近（某年龄、时刻或数目）</td><td>It must be going on for twenty years since we last met.<br>我们上次见面到现在快二十年了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>enough/something to be going ˈon with</td><td>暂时够用；先应付一阵</td><td>Here's fifty pounds—that should be enough to be going on with.<br>给你五十镑，暂时应该够用了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a lot, something, nothing, etc. ˈgoing for you</td><td>有很多（或一些）有利条件</td><td>She's young, clever and kind—she's got a lot going for her.<br>她年轻、聪明又善良，条件真不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get out while the ˌgoing/ˌgetting is ˈgood</td><td>趁形势尚可及早抽身</td><td>The market is still high, so sell up while the going is good.<br>行情还高，趁势好赶紧脱手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gold</b></td><td>ˌall that ˌglitters/ˌglistens/ˌglisters is not ˈgold (saying)</td><td>闪光的未必都是金子</td><td>The job sounded glamorous, but all that glitters is not gold.<br>那份工作听着光鲜，可闪光的未必都是金子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌall that ˌglitters is not ˈgold (saying)</td><td>发光的未必都是金子；表面好未必实在</td><td>That mansion is falling apart inside—all that glitters is not gold.<br>那座豪宅里面都快塌了，中看不中用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈgold mine</td><td>金矿；摇钱树</td><td>That little car park behind the stadium is an absolute gold mine.<br>体育场后面那个小停车场简直是棵摇钱树。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) good as ˈgold</td><td>（小孩）非常乖；很听话</td><td>The twins were as good as gold during the whole four-hour flight.<br>四个小时的飞行里，这对双胞胎乖得不得了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like ˈgold dust</td><td>极其稀缺；一票难求</td><td>Tickets for the final are like gold dust this year.<br>今年决赛的票简直一票难求。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>golden</b></td><td>the ˈgolden age (of sth)</td><td>黄金时代；全盛时期</td><td>The thirties are often called the golden age of Hollywood cinema.<br>三十年代常被称为好莱坞电影的黄金时代。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈgolden boy</td><td>红人；备受赏识的年轻人</td><td>He was the golden boy of British athletics until the injury.<br>受伤之前他一直是英国田径界的宠儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(kill) the golden ˈgoose (also (kill) the goose that lays the golden ˈegg/ˈeggs)</td><td>杀鸡取卵；自断财源</td><td>Raising rents that high would kill the goose that lays the golden eggs.<br>房租涨那么高，等于杀鸡取卵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(kill) the goose that lays the golden ˈeggs</td><td>自毁财源；杀鸡取卵</td><td>However, by killing the goose that lays the golden eggs, the farmer lost everything.<br>然而农夫杀了那只下金蛋的鹅，结果一无所有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a golden ˈhandshake</td><td>巨额退职金；高额解雇费</td><td>He left the bank with a golden handshake worth two years' salary.<br>他离开银行时拿到了相当于两年薪水的退职金。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the golden ˈrule</td><td>金科玉律；首要准则</td><td>The golden rule of hiking is to tell someone where you're going.<br>徒步的首要准则是告诉别人你要去哪儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the happy/golden ˈmean</td><td>中庸之道；折中之法</td><td>Between strict rules and total freedom, she found the happy mean.<br>在严规和放任之间，她找到了中庸之道。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>good</b></td><td>all to the ˈgood</td><td>那更好；有益无害</td><td>If the train arrives early, that's all to the good.<br>火车要是早到，那更好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as ˈgood as...</td><td>几乎；简直等于</td><td>The repair is as good as finished—just one screw left.<br>修理基本上完工了，只剩一颗螺丝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as ˌgood as it ˈgets</td><td>已经是最好的了</td><td>A hot shower after a long hike is as good as it gets.<br>长途徒步后洗个热水澡，没有比这更享受的了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈgood for sth</td><td>能提供（钱等）；能维持</td><td>The old van is still good for another two winters at least.<br>这辆旧货车至少还能再撑两个冬天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be no ˈgood • not be any/much ˈgood</td><td>没有用；不管用</td><td>It's no good arguing with him when he's this tired.<br>他这么累的时候跟他争没有用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do ˈgood</td><td>做好事；行善</td><td>She left the bank to do good in a rural health charity.<br>她离开银行，去一家乡村医疗慈善机构做善事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sb a good ˈturn</td><td>帮某人一个忙；做件好事</td><td>He did me a good turn once, so I owe him this favour.<br>他帮过我一次，这个忙我该还。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sb ˈgood</td><td>对某人有好处；有益于某人</td><td>A walk in the fresh air will do you good after all that studying.<br>学了这么久，出去走走对你有好处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈgood (BrE also for ˌgood and ˈall)</td><td>永久地；一劳永逸</td><td>He's moving to Canada for good next spring.<br>他明年春天就要永远搬去加拿大了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for your (ˌown) ˈgood</td><td>为了你好</td><td>I'm taking the car keys for your own good—you've been drinking.<br>我把车钥匙拿走是为你好，你喝酒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>good and... (informal)</td><td>完全地；十足地</td><td>Wait until the pan is good and hot before you add the oil.<br>等锅完全热了再倒油。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>good for ˈyou, ˈhim, etc. (especially AustralE good ˈon you, him, etc.) (informal)</td><td>（表扬）真棒；干得好</td><td>You finished the whole marathon? Good for you!<br>你跑完了全程马拉松？真棒！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the ˈgood</td><td>盈余；净赚</td><td>After paying for the stall, we were still forty pounds to the good.<br>付完摊位费，我们还净赚四十英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up to no ˈgood (informal)</td><td>不怀好意；在干坏事</td><td>Those lads hanging round the shed are clearly up to no good.<br>在棚子边转悠的那几个小子明显不怀好意。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>goodbye</b></td><td>kiss/say goodˈbye to sth • kiss sth goodˈbye</td><td>放弃（得到某物的）希望；就此告别</td><td>If you miss this deadline, you can kiss goodbye to the bonus.<br>错过这个截止日期，奖金你就别想了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>goodness</b></td><td>out of the ˌgoodness of your ˈheart</td><td>完全出于好心；不图回报</td><td>She fixed my fence out of the goodness of her heart and refused payment.<br>她纯粹出于好心帮我修了篱笆，还不肯收钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>goods</b></td><td>come up with/deliver/produce the ˈgoods</td><td>不负所望；兑现承诺</td><td>He talks a lot, but on match day he always delivers the goods.<br>他话是多，可到了比赛日总能拿出真本事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>goody-goody</b></td><td>a ˈgoody-goody • a goody ˈtwo-shoes (informal, disapproving)</td><td>装乖讨好的人；伪君子式的乖孩子</td><td>Nobody liked the goody two-shoes who reported us to the teacher.<br>没人喜欢那个跟老师告状的乖乖牌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>goose</b></td><td>what's sauce for the goose is sauce for the ˈgander (saying)</td><td>对甲适用的规矩对乙同样适用</td><td>If he can leave early, so can I—what's sauce for the goose is sauce for the gander.<br>他能早走我也能，一碗水得端平。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gooseberry</b></td><td>play ˈgooseberry (BrE)</td><td>当电灯泡；夹在情侣中间</td><td>I'm not coming to the cinema with those two—I'd just be playing gooseberry.<br>我才不跟他俩去看电影，纯粹当电灯泡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gordian</b></td><td>cut/untie the ˌGordian ˈknot</td><td>快刀斩乱麻；果断解决难题</td><td>She cut the Gordian knot by simply closing the loss-making branch.<br>她快刀斩乱麻，直接关掉了那家亏损的分店。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gospel</b></td><td>take sth as/for ˈgospel / ˌgospel ˈtruth (informal)</td><td>把某事当真理；对……信以为真</td><td>Don't take everything your cousin says as gospel.<br>你表哥说的话别句句都当真。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grab</b></td><td>how does...grab you? (spoken)</td><td>你觉得……怎么样；有兴趣吗</td><td>How does a weekend in the mountains grab you?<br>去山里过个周末，你觉得怎么样？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grabs</b></td><td>be up for ˈgrabs (informal)</td><td>可供争夺；谁都有机会得到</td><td>Three scholarships are up for grabs this year, so apply early.<br>今年有三个奖学金名额待争取，早点申请。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grace</b></td><td>fall from ˈgrace</td><td>失宠；名誉扫地</td><td>The minister's fall from grace came after a single leaked recording.<br>一段录音泄露，这位部长便身败名裂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have the (good) grace to do sth</td><td>有雅量做某事；通情达理地做某事</td><td>At least he had the good grace to admit he'd been wrong.<br>他至少还有点雅量，承认自己错了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there but for the grace of ˈGod (go ˈI) (saying)</td><td>若非侥幸，我也难逃此运</td><td>Seeing him lose everything, I thought: there but for the grace of God go I.<br>看着他一无所有，我心想：换作我未必强到哪去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with (a) good/bad ˈgrace</td><td>有风度地；不情愿地</td><td>He accepted the referee's decision with good grace and shook hands.<br>他大度地接受了裁判的判罚，还握了手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>graces</b></td><td>be in sb's good ˈgraces (formal)</td><td>得到某人的青睐；受某人赏识</td><td>Since the presentation, she's firmly in the director's good graces.<br>那次汇报之后，她很得主任赏识。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grade</b></td><td>make the ˈgrade (informal)</td><td>达到标准；合格</td><td>Only two of the twenty trainees made the grade this year.<br>今年二十名学员里只有两个达标。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grain</b></td><td>be/go against the ˈgrain</td><td>违背本性；不合常理</td><td>Asking strangers for money goes against the grain for her.<br>向陌生人开口要钱有违她的本性。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grand</b></td><td>a/the ˌgrand old ˈage</td><td>高龄</td><td>He was still gardening at the grand old age of ninety-four.<br>他九十四岁高龄还在打理花园。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˌgrand old ˈman (of sth)</td><td>元老；老前辈</td><td>He is the grand old man of British jazz and still tours.<br>他是英国爵士乐界的老前辈，如今仍在巡演。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>granted</b></td><td>take sb/sth for ˈgranted</td><td>不把……当回事；对……忽视</td><td>She left him because he took her for granted for years.<br>她离开他，是因为这些年他从没把她放在心上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth for ˈgranted (that...)</td><td>想当然地认为；视为理所当然</td><td>I took it for granted that someone had booked the hall.<br>我想当然地以为有人订好了礼堂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grapevine</b></td><td>on/through the ˈgrapevine</td><td>通过小道消息；听传闻</td><td>I heard through the grapevine that two managers are leaving.<br>我听小道消息说有两位经理要走。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grasp</b></td><td>grasp the ˈnettle (BrE)</td><td>果断处理棘手问题</td><td>It's time to grasp the nettle and tell the team about the cuts.<br>该硬着头皮把裁减的事告诉团队了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grass</b></td><td>the ˌgrass is (always) ˈgreener on the other ˌside (of the ˈfence) (saying)</td><td>这山望着那山高</td><td>He keeps changing jobs because the grass is always greener on the other side.<br>他老换工作，总觉得别处更好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌgrass ˈroots</td><td>基层；草根阶层</td><td>The campaign started at the grass roots, with volunteers knocking on doors.<br>这场运动从基层做起，靠志愿者挨家敲门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not let the ˌgrass grow under your ˈfeet</td><td>抓紧行动；不拖延</td><td>She doesn't let the grass grow under her feet—the shop opened in a month.<br>她一点不拖沓，一个月就把店开起来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/turn/send sb out to ˈgrass (informal, humorous)</td><td>让某人（因年老）退职</td><td>They put the old engineer out to grass after thirty years' service.<br>那位老工程师干了三十年后被打发退休了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grave</b></td><td>turn in his, her, etc. ˈgrave (BrE) (AmE roll in his, her, etc. ˈgrave)</td><td>（死者）九泉之下也不安宁</td><td>Grandma would turn in her grave if she saw what we did to the kitchen.<br>要是奶奶看见我们把厨房改成这样，准会气得在坟里翻身。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈgravy train (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>轻松赚钱的美差；肥缺</td><td>Consultants have been riding the gravy train on this project for years.<br>这个项目上的顾问们轻轻松松捞了好几年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/get the ˌgreen ˈlight (informal)</td><td>开绿灯；获得许可</td><td>The council finally gave us the green light to build the extension.<br>议会终于批准我们加建那部分了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>greased</b></td><td>like greased ˈlightning (informal)</td><td>快如闪电；飞快</td><td>The cat was out of the door like greased lightning when the vacuum started.<br>吸尘器一开，那猫像闪电一样窜出了门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be a ˈgreat one for sth/for doing sth</td><td>特别喜欢做某事；很擅长某事</td><td>My father is a great one for early morning walks in winter.<br>我父亲特别喜欢冬天一大早出去散步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be no great ˈshakes (informal)</td><td>不怎么样；平平</td><td>The food was no great shakes, but the view was worth the trip.<br>东西不怎么样，不过那景色值回票价。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go great ˈguns (informal)</td><td>干得起劲；进展神速</td><td>The new bakery is going great guns three months after opening.<br>这家新面包店开张三个月就红火得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's</b></td><td>it's all ˈGreek to me (informal, saying)</td><td>我完全看不懂；简直像天书</td><td>He explained the tax rules twice, but it's all Greek to me.<br>税务规定他解释了两遍，我还是听得云里雾里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>green</b></td><td>give sb/get the green ˈlight (informal)</td><td>批准；放行</td><td>We can't order materials until we get the green light from head office.<br>总部不点头，我们就不能订料。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>green ˈfingers (BrE) (AmE a ˌgreen ˈthumb)</td><td>精通园艺；擅长种花草</td><td>My aunt has green fingers—even her cactus flowers twice a year.<br>我姑姑特别会种花，连仙人掌一年都开两次花。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>green with ˈenvy</td><td>十分嫉妒；眼红</td><td>My colleagues were green with envy when they heard about the trip.<br>同事们听说这趟旅行，一个个眼红得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>green-eyed</b></td><td>the ˌgreen-eyed ˈmonster (humorous)</td><td>嫉妒心；醋意</td><td>The green-eyed monster appeared the moment she mentioned his new partner.<br>她一提他的新伴侣，醋意就冒了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>greetings</b></td><td>(the) season's ˈgreetings</td><td>（节日贺词）佳节问候</td><td>The card simply said 'Season's greetings from all of us at the office'.<br>卡片上只写着：办公室全体同仁恭祝佳节愉快。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌgrey ˈarea</td><td>灰色地带；界限不清的问题</td><td>Whether volunteers count as staff is a grey area in the contract.<br>志愿者算不算员工，在合同里是个灰色地带。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈgrey matter (informal)</td><td>脑力；智力</td><td>These puzzles are a good way to exercise your grey matter.<br>这些谜题挺能锻炼脑子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(men in) grey ˈsuits</td><td>幕后的当权者；不为人知的决策者</td><td>The men in grey suits decided the deal long before it was announced.<br>这笔交易早在宣布前就由幕后人物拍板了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grief</b></td><td>come to ˈgrief (informal)</td><td>遭遇失败；意外受伤</td><td>His bicycle came to grief on the icy corner near the school.<br>他的自行车在学校旁的结冰拐角出了事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb ˈgrief (about/over sth) (informal)</td><td>责怪某人；给某人添堵</td><td>My boss gave me grief about arriving five minutes late.<br>就因为迟到五分钟，老板没完没了地说我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>good ˈgrief! (informal)</td><td>（表示惊讶）哎呀；天哪</td><td>Good grief, have you really eaten the whole pizza already?<br>天哪，你真把整个披萨都吃完了？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grim</b></td><td>hang on/hold on (to sb/sth) like grim ˈdeath</td><td>死死抓住不放</td><td>The child hung on to the rope like grim death until we pulled her up.<br>那孩子死死抓着绳子，直到我们把她拉上来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grin</b></td><td>grin and ˈbear it (informal)</td><td>咬牙忍受；逆来顺受</td><td>Working with Ann isn't easy, but Tony knows he must grin and bear it.<br>跟安一起工作不轻松，但托尼知道只能忍着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>grin like a Cheshire ˈcat</td><td>咧嘴傻笑；笑得合不拢嘴</td><td>He came out of the interview grinning like a Cheshire cat.<br>他面试出来时笑得合不拢嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beam/grin/smile from ˌear to ˈear</td><td>笑得合不拢嘴；喜形于色</td><td>When she saw the puppy, she grinned from ear to ear.<br>看到那只小狗时，她笑得合不拢嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grind</b></td><td>grind to a ˈhalt/ˈstandstill</td><td>慢慢停下；陷入停顿</td><td>Traffic ground to a halt when the lorry blocked both lanes.<br>卡车堵住了两条车道，车流慢慢停了下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>grinding ˈhalt</td><td>慢慢停下；完全停顿</td><td>The strike brought the whole factory to a grinding halt within a few hours.<br>罢工几小时内就让整个工厂彻底停了下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grindstone</b></td><td>keep your ˈnose to the ˈgrindstone</td><td>埋头苦干；辛勤工作</td><td>She kept her nose to the grindstone all summer and finally passed the exam.<br>她整个夏天埋头苦读，最后终于通过了考试。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grip</b></td><td>get/take a ˈgrip/ˈhold on yourself (informal)</td><td>控制情绪；使自己镇定下来</td><td>Get a grip on yourself — crying won't help us find the missing keys.<br>振作点，哭也帮不了我们找到丢的钥匙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈgrip of sth</td><td>在…支配下；受制于…</td><td>The whole town was in the grip of panic after the second robbery.<br>第二起抢劫案之后，整座小镇陷入了恐慌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose your ˈgrip (on sth) (informal)</td><td>失去（对某事物的）控制</td><td>He's losing his grip on the business, and everyone in the office knows it.<br>他对生意的掌控力在下降，办公室里人人都看得出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grips</b></td><td>come/get to ˈgrips with sb/sth</td><td>着手处理；认真应对</td><td>It took me a month to come to grips with the new accounting software.<br>我花了一个月才摸清这套新会计软件。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grist</b></td><td>grist for/to sb's ˈmill</td><td>对某人有用的东西；有利可图的素材</td><td>Every celebrity divorce is grist to the mill for those cheap gossip magazines.<br>每一桩明星离婚案都是那些八卦杂志的好材料。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grit</b></td><td>grit your ˈteeth</td><td>咬紧牙关；下定决心忍耐</td><td>I gritted my teeth and finished the last three miles of the race.<br>我咬紧牙关跑完了比赛最后三英里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>groan</b></td><td>groan under the weight of sth (written)</td><td>在重压下发出嘎吱声；不堪重负</td><td>The table groaned under the weight of roast turkey, pies and three enormous cakes.<br>烤火鸡、派和三个大蛋糕压得桌子直响。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>groove</b></td><td>be (stuck) in a ˈgroove (BrE)</td><td>墨守成规；一成不变</td><td>After twenty years here he's stuck in a groove and refuses to try anything new.<br>在这儿干了二十年，他早已墨守成规，不肯尝试新东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ground</b></td><td>be, come, get, etc. in on the ground ˈfloor</td><td>一开始就参与（日后可能获利）</td><td>I got in on the ground floor of that startup and made a small fortune.<br>我在那家初创公司刚起步时就加入了，赚了一小笔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>break fresh/new ˈground</td><td>有新发现；开创新局面</td><td>Her research on sleep and memory really broke new ground in the field.<br>她关于睡眠与记忆的研究在这个领域真正开创了新局面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cut the ground from under sb/sb's ˈfeet</td><td>破坏某人的计划；拆某人的台</td><td>By cutting prices first, they cut the ground from under our feet completely.<br>他们抢先降价，把我们的路彻底堵死了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drive/run/work yourself into the ˈground</td><td>把自己累垮；过度劳累</td><td>You'll work yourself into the ground if you keep taking on extra shifts.<br>你要是老加班，非把自己累垮不可。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get (sth) off the ˈground</td><td>使（计划等）开始；顺利启动</td><td>We need more funding to get this project off the ground by the spring.<br>我们需要更多资金，才能在春天前把这个项目启动起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give/lose ˈground (to sb/sth)</td><td>让步退却；失去优势</td><td>The party lost ground to its rivals in almost every northern city.<br>该党在北方几乎每座城市都被对手抢去了地盘。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold/stand your ˈground</td><td>坚守立场；不让步</td><td>She stood her ground and refused to lower the price by a single cent.<br>她寸步不让，一分钱也不肯降。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈground</td><td>在基层；置身现场</td><td>Aid workers on the ground say the situation is far worse than reported.<br>身处一线的救援人员说，情况比报道的糟得多。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run sb/sth into the ˈground</td><td>过度使用；把…用垮累垮</td><td>He ran that poor van into the ground driving it across the country twice.<br>他开着那辆破面包车横穿全国两趟，彻底把它开报废了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>thick/thin on the ˈground (BrE)</td><td>遍地皆是；寥寥无几</td><td>Good plumbers are pretty thin on the ground in this part of town.<br>这一带的好水管工少得可怜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grow</b></td><td>grow like ˈTopsy</td><td>迅速增长；发展飞快</td><td>The little book club grew like Topsy until nearly two hundred people had joined.<br>这个小读书会飞速壮大，最后有近两百人加入。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>growing</b></td><td>ˈgrowing pains</td><td>初期的问题或困难</td><td>The restaurant had a few growing pains, but business is steady now.<br>这家餐馆经历了一些初期的磕碰，现在生意稳定了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an educated ˈguess</td><td>有根据的推测</td><td>At best I can make an educated guess about how long the repairs will take.<br>我最多只能凭经验估算一下修理要多久。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>guessing</b></td><td>keep sb ˈguessing (informal)</td><td>让某人捉摸不透；吊某人胃口</td><td>The writer keeps you guessing right up to the very last page.<br>这位作家吊足了读者胃口，直到最后一页才揭晓。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>guest</b></td><td>be my ˈguest (informal)</td><td>请便；随你的便</td><td>Do you mind if I borrow your bike? Sure, be my guest.<br>我能借下你的自行车吗？当然，请便。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>guilt</b></td><td>a ˈguilt trip (informal)</td><td>内疚感；负罪感</td><td>My mother laid a real guilt trip on me for missing Sunday dinner.<br>我没回家吃周日晚饭，我妈让我内疚得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>guinea</b></td><td>a ˈguinea pig</td><td>实验对象；试验品</td><td>They used first-year students as guinea pigs for the new online course.<br>他们拿大一学生给新的网课当试验品。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gum</b></td><td>gum up the ˈworks (informal)</td><td>把事情弄糟；使运转停滞</td><td>One missing signature gummed up the works for the entire department.<br>一个签名没签，整个部门的活儿都卡住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up a ˈgum tree (BrE, informal)</td><td>陷入困境；进退两难</td><td>Without a car and without money, we were well and truly up a gum tree.<br>没车又没钱，我们真是彻底陷进去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gun</b></td><td>have a ˈgun to your head (informal)</td><td>被迫做某事；受人胁迫</td><td>I signed the contract, but honestly I had a gun to my head.<br>我签了合同，但说实话我是被逼的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold/put a ˈgun to sb's head</td><td>胁迫某人就范</td><td>Nobody put a gun to your head — you chose this job all by yourself.<br>没人拿枪逼你，这份工作是你自己选的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under the ˈgun (AmE, informal)</td><td>承受巨大压力</td><td>The whole team is under the gun to ship the app by Friday.<br>整个团队压力巨大，周五前必须把应用上线。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jump the ˈgun (informal)</td><td>抢先行动；操之过急</td><td>Don't jump the gun and announce the deal before the contract is actually signed.<br>别操之过急，合同没签就别宣布这笔交易。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>guts</b></td><td>have the ˈguts (to do sth) (informal)</td><td>有胆量做某事</td><td>Nobody had the guts to tell the boss his presentation was boring.<br>没人有胆量告诉老板他的演示很无聊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have sb's ˌguts for ˈgarters (BrE, informal)</td><td>恨死某人；严惩某人</td><td>If you scratch my car again, I'll have your guts for garters.<br>你要是再刮花我的车，我饶不了你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>slog/sweat/work your ˈguts out (informal)</td><td>呕心沥血；拼命干活</td><td>She worked her guts out for that company and they let her go anyway.<br>她为那家公司拼死拼活，结果还是被辞退了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gutter</b></td><td>the ˌgutter ˈpress (disapproving)</td><td>市井小报；八卦小报</td><td>The gutter press hounded the actress for weeks after her sudden divorce.<br>她突然离婚后，八卦小报纠缠了这位女演员好几周。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>gyp</b></td><td>give sb ˈgyp (BrE, informal)</td><td>使某人疼痛难忍；折磨某人</td><td>My knee's been giving me gyp ever since that long walk on Sunday.<br>自从周日走了那么远，我的膝盖就一直疼得厉害。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hair</b></td><td>a ˌbad ˈhair day (informal)</td><td>诸事不顺的一天</td><td>Ignore her snapping at everyone; she's just having a bad hair day.<br>别理她冲人发火，她今天诸事不顺。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make sb's ˈhair curl (informal, humorous)</td><td>使某人震惊；令人毛骨悚然</td><td>Some of the stories he told about prison would make your hair curl.<br>他讲的一些监狱里的事能让你头皮发麻。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not a ˈhair out of place</td><td>仪容整洁；一丝不乱</td><td>After ten hours on a plane she stepped off with not a hair out of place.<br>坐了十小时飞机下来，她依然仪容整洁、纹丝不乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not harm/touch a hair of sb's ˈhead</td><td>丝毫不伤害某人</td><td>I promise nobody will touch a hair of your head while I am here.<br>我保证只要我在，没人能动你一根汗毛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not turn a ˈhair</td><td>不动声色；泰然自若</td><td>She didn't turn a hair when the waiter dropped the whole tray beside her.<br>服务员在她旁边摔了整盘东西，她连眉头都没皱一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hairs</b></td><td>put ˈhairs on your chest (informal, humorous)</td><td>（尤指酒）使人有男子汉气概</td><td>Drink this whisky, lad — it'll put hairs on your chest.<br>小子，把这杯威士忌喝了，长长男子汉气概。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/get sb by the short ˈhairs (informal)</td><td>抓住某人把柄；完全控制某人</td><td>The bank has us by the short hairs until the mortgage is finally paid off.<br>房贷还清之前，银行牢牢捏着我们的命门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hairy</b></td><td>give sb the hairy ˈeyeball (AmE, informal)</td><td>以怀疑或不以为然的眼神看人</td><td>The librarian gave me the hairy eyeball when my phone rang twice.<br>我手机响了两次，图书管理员用怀疑的眼神盯着我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hale</b></td><td>hale and ˈhearty</td><td>老当益壮；健壮矍铄</td><td>At ninety-two my grandfather is still hale and hearty and gardens every day.<br>我爷爷九十二了，依然精神矍铄，天天侍弄花园。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>half</b></td><td>and a ˈhalf (informal)</td><td>非同一般的；超乎寻常的</td><td>That was a meal and a half — I really couldn't eat another bite.<br>那顿饭真够丰盛的，我一口也吃不下了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your better/other ˈhalf (informal, humorous)</td><td>那口子；配偶</td><td>I'd love to come, but I'll have to check with my better half first.<br>我很想去，不过得先问问我那口子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb half a ˈchance (to do sth) (informal)</td><td>给某人一点机会</td><td>Give him half a chance and he'll talk about football all evening.<br>只要给他一点机会，他能聊一晚上足球。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>half the ˈbattle</td><td>最困难的部分；成功的一半</td><td>Getting the kids out of bed on time is half the battle.<br>按时把孩子们弄起床，事情就成功了一半。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>half the ˈfun, ˈtrouble, etc. of sth (informal)</td><td>乐趣（或麻烦等）的一大部分</td><td>Half the fun of camping is cooking badly over an open fire.<br>露营的乐趣有一半在于生着火胡乱做饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>half a ˌloaf is better than ˈnone/no ˈbread (saying)</td><td>有总比没有好；聊胜于无</td><td>They only offered part of the refund, but half a loaf is better than none.<br>他们只退了一部分钱，不过聊胜于无。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>half a ˈminute, ˈtick, ˈsecond, etc. (informal)</td><td>一小会儿；片刻</td><td>Hang on half a minute while I find my other shoe.<br>等一小会儿，我找找另一只鞋。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈhalf of it</td><td>（全部情况的）一部分</td><td>You've heard about the flood? Believe me, that's not the half of it.<br>你听说水灾了？信我，那还只是一部分呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈhalf the time (informal)</td><td>大部分时间；经常</td><td>Half the time he doesn't even bother answering his phone.<br>他多半时候连电话都懒得接。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how the other half ˈlives</td><td>另一阶层的人如何生活</td><td>Staying in that fancy hotel showed me how the other half lives.<br>住那家豪华酒店让我见识了另一个阶层是怎么生活的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈhalf the time</td><td>用比预期短得多的时间</td><td>With the new machine we finished the whole order in half the time.<br>用了新机器，我们用一半的时间就完成了整批订单。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no half ˈmeasures (BrE)</td><td>不打折扣；彻底做到</td><td>When my mother cleans the house there are no half measures at all.<br>我妈打扫房子从来都彻彻底底，绝不马虎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not ˈhalf (BrE, informal)</td><td>非常；实在是</td><td>Did you enjoy the concert? Not half — it was the best night ever.<br>演唱会好玩吗？太好玩了，这是最棒的一晚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not ˈhalf as good, nice, etc. as sb/sth</td><td>远不如…好；差得远</td><td>The sequel was not half as good as the original film.<br>续集远不如第一部好看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not half ˈbad (informal)</td><td>相当不错；出乎意料地好</td><td>I tried her homemade bread and honestly it was not half bad.<br>我尝了她自己烤的面包，说实话相当不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>too clever, quick, etc. by ˈhalf (BrE, informal, disapproving)</td><td>过于聪明（或迅速等）</td><td>That young lawyer is too clever by half, and everyone finds him irritating.<br>那个年轻律师聪明过头了，人人都嫌他讨厌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>half-cock</b></td><td>go off at ˌhalf-ˈcock (informal)</td><td>贸然为之；仓促行事</td><td>The campaign went off at half-cock because nobody had printed the posters.<br>这次活动仓促上马，因为没人把海报印出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>halfway</b></td><td>a ˌhalfway ˈhouse</td><td>折中办法；过渡安排</td><td>This arrangement is a halfway house between full-time work and complete retirement.<br>这种安排是全职工作与彻底退休之间的折中。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hallmarks</b></td><td>have all the ˈhallmarks of sb/sth</td><td>具有…的所有特点</td><td>The burglary has all the hallmarks of the gang that hit the bank.<br>这起入室盗窃完全是抢银行那伙人的手法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>halves</b></td><td>do nothing/not do anything by ˈhalves</td><td>做事彻底；全心全意</td><td>She never does anything by halves — the party took three months to plan.<br>她做事从不半途而废，这场派对筹备了三个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈhalves (with sb) • go ˌhalf and ˈhalf</td><td>（与某人）平摊费用</td><td>Let's go halves on the taxi since we're heading the same way.<br>我们顺路，打车费平摊吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ham</b></td><td>ˌham it ˈup (informal)</td><td>表演过火；故意夸张做作</td><td>The lead actor hammed it up so much that the audience started laughing.<br>男主角表演太夸张，观众都笑了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hammer</b></td><td>be/go at sb/sth ˌhammer and ˈtongs (informal)</td><td>激烈争吵；猛烈打斗</td><td>The neighbours were at it hammer and tongs again until well past midnight.<br>邻居们又吵得不可开交，一直闹到过了午夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come/go under the ˈhammer</td><td>被拍卖</td><td>Her grandmother's diamond ring goes under the hammer next Thursday morning.<br>她祖母的钻戒下周四上午将被拍卖。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hammering</b></td><td>give sb/get a ˈhammering (BrE, informal)</td><td>痛击；惨败；严厉惩罚</td><td>Our team got a real hammering in the second half of the match.<br>我们队在下半场被打得落花流水。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hand</b></td><td>ask for/win sb's hand (old-fashioned)</td><td>求婚；获准与某人结婚</td><td>He asked for her hand at Christmas and they married the following spring.<br>他在圣诞节向她求婚，第二年春天他们就结婚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(close/near) at ˈhand</td><td>近在手边；即将发生</td><td>Help was close at hand when the car broke down outside the village.<br>车在村外抛锚时，援手就在近旁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bind/tie sb hand and ˈfoot</td><td>束缚某人；限制某人行动</td><td>The new rules tie small shopkeepers hand and foot with endless paperwork.<br>新规定用没完没了的文书把小店主捆得死死的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by ˈhand</td><td>手工制作；由专人递送</td><td>The postmen are on strike, so we'll have to deliver these invitations by hand.<br>邮政工人罢工，这些请帖只好我们派人送了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get out of ˈhand</td><td>失去控制；难以驾驭</td><td>The party got out of hand once the neighbours' friends all turned up.<br>邻居的朋友一来，派对就失控了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb a hand (with sth)</td><td>帮助某人（做某事）</td><td>Could you give me a hand with these heavy boxes before you leave?<br>你走之前能帮我搬一下这些重箱子吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go hand in ˈhand (with sth)</td><td>与…密切相关；相伴而生</td><td>Poverty tends to go hand in hand with poor health and shorter lives.<br>贫困往往与健康差、寿命短相伴而生。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hand in ˈglove (with sb)</td><td>与某人密切勾结；狼狈为奸</td><td>The inspector had been working hand in glove with the smugglers for years.<br>这名检查员多年来一直与走私者狼狈为奸。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hand in ˈhand</td><td>手拉手；携手</td><td>The two little girls walked hand in hand all the way to school.<br>两个小女孩手拉着手一路走到学校。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hand sth to sb on a ˈplate • hand sb sth on a ˈplate (informal)</td><td>把某物拱手送给某人</td><td>He was handed that job on a plate because his uncle owns the firm.<br>这份工作是白送给他的，因为公司是他叔叔的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have to ˈhand it to sb (informal)</td><td>不得不佩服某人</td><td>You have to hand it to her — she organized the whole festival alone.<br>你不得不佩服她，整个音乐节都是她一个人办的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk to/tell it to the ˈhand (because/ˈcos the face ain't ˈlistening) (AmE, informal)</td><td>别说了；我不想听</td><td>Don't bother explaining again — talk to the hand, I've heard quite enough.<br>别再解释了，我不想听，真够了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw your ˈhand in (informal)</td><td>放弃；认输</td><td>After two failed auditions he threw his hand in and went back home.<br>两次试镜失败后，他放弃了，回了老家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(ready) to ˈhand</td><td>近在手边；便于取用</td><td>Keep a torch ready to hand in case the power goes out again.<br>手边备好手电筒，以防又停电。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn your ˈhand to sth</td><td>着手做；有能力做</td><td>Since retiring he has turned his hand to carpentry and repairs everyone's furniture.<br>退休后他做起了木工，帮大家修家具。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with your ˌhand on your ˈheart • ˌhand on ˈheart</td><td>诚恳地；发自内心地</td><td>Hand on heart, I never told anyone what you said that night.<br>我发誓，那晚你说的话我从没告诉过任何人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with one hand tied behind your ˈback</td><td>束手束脚地；不尽全力地</td><td>I could beat him at chess with one hand tied behind my back.<br>我下棋赢他，不费吹灰之力。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hands</b></td><td>at the hands of sb • at sb's ˈhands (written)</td><td>出自某人之手；由某人造成</td><td>The prisoners suffered terribly at the hands of their own guards.<br>囚犯在自己看守手里吃尽了苦头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wash your ˈhands of sb/sth</td><td>洗手不干；不再过问</td><td>After the third warning she washed her hands of the whole project.<br>第三次警告之后，她就撒手不管整个项目了。</td></tr>
