<tr><td></td><td>be good with your ˈhands</td><td>手巧；擅长做手工活</td><td>My brother is good with his hands and built that garden shed himself.<br>我哥哥手很巧，花园里那个棚子是他自己搭的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fall into sb's ˈhands/the ˈhands of sb</td><td>落入某人手中</td><td>If those letters fall into the hands of a journalist, the scandal will explode.<br>这些信要是落到记者手里，丑闻就会爆发。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈhands dirty</td><td>亲自动手干活；插手不正当勾当</td><td>A good manager isn't afraid to get his hands dirty on the factory floor.<br>好经理不怕在车间里亲自动手干活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/lay your ˈhands on sth</td><td>找到；弄到手</td><td>I can't lay my hands on the receipt, so they won't refund me.<br>我找不到收据，所以他们不给我退款。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/keep/take your ˈhands off (sb/sth)</td><td>别碰；放手；不许染指</td><td>Keep your hands off my sandwich — I've been saving it all morning.<br>别碰我的三明治，我留了一上午了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the hands of sb • in sb's ˈhands</td><td>由某人掌管；在某人控制下</td><td>The future of the industry is now in the hands of the government.<br>这个行业的未来现在掌握在政府手中。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in safe/good ˈhands</td><td>得到妥善照顾；交托可靠</td><td>Leave the cat with me; she'll be in safe hands for two weeks.<br>猫交给我吧，这两周包在我身上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>many hands make light ˈwork (saying)</td><td>人多好办事；众人拾柴火焰高</td><td>Come and help with the dishes — many hands make light work.<br>过来帮忙洗碗，人多好办事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>off sb's ˈhands</td><td>不再由某人负责</td><td>Once the twins start school, that's six hours a day off my hands.<br>双胞胎一上学，我每天就能省出六个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on sb's ˈhands</td><td>待某人处理；由某人负担</td><td>With the wedding cancelled, we had two hundred meals on our hands.<br>婚礼取消了，两百份餐食砸在我们手里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on your ˌhands and ˈknees</td><td>趴在地上；匍匐着</td><td>I spent an hour on my hands and knees looking for that lost earring.<br>我趴在地上找了一个小时那只丢的耳环。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌout of sb's ˈhands</td><td>不再由某人控制或负责</td><td>The decision is out of my hands now; head office will decide everything.<br>这事我已经做不了主了，一切由总部决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play (right) into sb's ˈhands</td><td>正中某人下怀；自投罗网</td><td>By resigning angrily, you would be playing right into your rival's hands.<br>你要是气得辞职，正中对手下怀。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth/sb off sb's ˈhands</td><td>替某人接手；代为承担</td><td>I'll take the children off your hands for the weekend so you can rest.<br>这周末孩子我来带，你们好好休息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw your ˈhands up in ˈhorror, etc. (often humorous)</td><td>极为震惊；强烈反对</td><td>My aunt threw her hands up in horror when she saw my new tattoo.<br>我姑妈看见我的新纹身，吓得直摆手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with your bare ˈhands</td><td>赤手空拳；徒手</td><td>He claims he caught that huge fish with his bare hands.<br>他说那条大鱼是他徒手抓到的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>handy</b></td><td>come in ˈhandy/ˈuseful (informal)</td><td>派上用场；有用</td><td>Take the spare rope — it might come in handy on the boat.<br>把备用绳带上，在船上说不定用得着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hang</b></td><td>get the hang of sth (informal)</td><td>掌握…的窍门；熟悉用法</td><td>It took me a week to get the hang of driving on the left.<br>我花了一周才掌握靠左行驶的窍门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈhang sth (BrE, spoken)</td><td>不去担心；管它呢</td><td>Oh, hang the expense — let's order the lobster and enjoy ourselves.<br>管它多贵呢，点龙虾，好好享受一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang by a ˈthread/hair</td><td>千钧一发；岌岌可危</td><td>After the second heart attack his life hung by a thread for days.<br>第二次心脏病发作后，他好几天命悬一线。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang ˈfire</td><td>延迟；暂缓行动</td><td>The council decided to hang fire on the new road until after the election.<br>议会决定把新路的事拖到选举之后再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang your ˈhead (in/for ˈshame)</td><td>羞愧地低下头</td><td>He hung his head in shame when the teacher read out his feeble excuse.<br>老师念出他蹩脚的借口时，他羞愧地低下了头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang (on) ˈin there (informal)</td><td>坚持住；别放弃</td><td>Hang in there — only two more weeks until the exams are over.<br>坚持住，再有两周考试就结束了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang a ˈleft/ˈright (AmE)</td><td>向左转；向右转</td><td>Hang a left at the traffic lights and the museum is straight ahead.<br>在红绿灯处左转，博物馆就在正前方。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang on sb's ˈwords/every ˈword</td><td>聚精会神地听；一字不漏</td><td>The children sat quietly, hanging on every word of the ghost story.<br>孩子们静静坐着，听鬼故事听得一字不落。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang out/up your ˈshingle (AmE, informal)</td><td>挂牌开业（尤指医生、律师）</td><td>After passing the bar exam she hung out her shingle in her home town.<br>通过律师考试后，她在家乡挂牌开业。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang sb out to ˈdry (AmE, informal)</td><td>弃之不管；袖手旁观</td><td>When the scandal broke, the company hung its own manager out to dry.<br>丑闻一曝光，公司就把自己的经理丢在一边不管了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang over sb's ˈhead • hang ˈover sb</td><td>（问题等）笼罩心头；令人担忧</td><td>The threat of redundancy has been hanging over my head since January.<br>裁员的威胁从一月起就一直压在我心头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang ˈtough (AmE)</td><td>坚持己见；寸步不让</td><td>The union told its members to hang tough and reject the latest offer.<br>工会让会员们坚持到底，拒绝最新的方案。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang up your ˈboots</td><td>挂靴；退役；停止工作</td><td>After twenty seasons the old striker finally hung up his boots.<br>踢了二十个赛季，这位老前锋终于挂靴了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˌhappy eˈvent (humorous)</td><td>喜事，指婴儿出世</td><td>They're expecting the happy event some time in early October.<br>他们预计十月初就要添丁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a happy ˈhunting ground (humorous)</td><td>淘宝乐园；能找到所需物之地</td><td>That flea market is a happy hunting ground for anyone who collects old records.<br>那个跳蚤市场是老唱片收藏者的淘宝乐园。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the happy ˈmedium</td><td>中庸之道；折中办法</td><td>We need a happy medium between strict rules and complete chaos.<br>我们需要在严规和彻底混乱之间找到折中。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>many happy reˈturns (of the ˈday)</td><td>祝生日快乐</td><td>Many happy returns of the day, Grandma — here's your birthday cake.<br>祝您生日快乐，奶奶，这是您的生日蛋糕。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hard</b></td><td>be hard ˈat it</td><td>拼命干活；埋头苦干</td><td>The builders have been hard at it since six o'clock this morning.<br>建筑工人从今早六点起就一直在拼命干。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/feel hard ˈdone by (informal)</td><td>受到不公平对待；感到委屈</td><td>She felt hard done by when everyone else in the office got a bonus.<br>办公室里别人都拿了奖金，她觉得很委屈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈhard on sb</td><td>严厉对待；苛责</td><td>Don't be too hard on him; it's only his second week here.<br>别对他太苛刻，他才来第二周。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be hard ˈup (informal)</td><td>缺钱；手头拮据</td><td>We were so hard up that winter that we sold the piano.<br>那年冬天我们太缺钱了，把钢琴都卖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be hard ˈup for sth</td><td>缺乏；缺少</td><td>The team is hard up for defenders after two injuries last month.<br>上个月两名球员受伤，球队后卫严重不足。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do/learn sth the ˈhard way</td><td>吃过苦头才学会</td><td>I learned the hard way that you should never lend friends money.<br>我吃了苦头才明白，千万别借钱给朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hard ˈluck/ˈlines (BrE)</td><td>真不走运；真倒霉</td><td>Hard luck about the interview — there'll be other chances very soon.<br>面试没成，真不走运，很快还会有机会的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hard of ˈhearing</td><td>耳背；听力不好</td><td>Speak up a bit — my grandfather is rather hard of hearing.<br>说话大声点，我爷爷有点耳背。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hard ˈput (to it) to do sth • hard ˈpressed/ˈpushed to do sth</td><td>很难做到；勉强能做某事</td><td>You'd be hard pushed to find a better mechanic anywhere in this town.<br>在这个镇上，你很难找到比他更好的技工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈhard stuff (informal)</td><td>烈酒，如威士忌、白兰地</td><td>He gave up the hard stuff and drinks nothing but beer now.<br>他把烈酒戒了，现在只喝啤酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make hard ˈwork of sth</td><td>把简单的事做得很费力</td><td>You're making hard work of that knot — let me untie it for you.<br>这个结你解得太费劲了，我来帮你解吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no hard ˈfeelings (spoken)</td><td>不计前嫌；别往心里去</td><td>You won fair and square, so no hard feelings from me.<br>你赢得光明正大，我不往心里去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play hard to ˈget (informal)</td><td>故意拿架子；欲擒故纵</td><td>Stop playing hard to get and just tell him that you'd like to go.<br>别再欲擒故纵了，直接告诉他你想去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth ˈhard</td><td>为某事伤心；难以承受</td><td>She took her father's death very hard and barely left the house.<br>父亲去世让她极为伤心，几乎足不出户。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>too much like hard ˈwork</td><td>太费劲而不愿去做</td><td>Cycling to work in winter is too much like hard work for me.<br>冬天骑车上班对我来说太累了，我不干。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of harm's ˈway</td><td>处境安全；不会受伤害</td><td>Put the scissors on the top shelf, well out of harm's way.<br>把剪刀放到最上层，免得伤着人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no harm in (sb's) doing sth • it does no ˈharm (for sb) to do sth</td><td>不会有坏处；无妨</td><td>There's no harm in asking whether they still have any tickets left.<br>问问他们还有没有余票，也没什么损失。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>he, she, etc. wouldn't harm/hurt a ˈfly</td><td>心地善良；连苍蝇都不忍伤害</td><td>My uncle looks fierce, but honestly he wouldn't hurt a fly.<br>我叔叔看着凶，其实连只苍蝇都不忍心伤害。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>harness</b></td><td>in ˈharness (BrE)</td><td>在日常工作中；重返岗位</td><td>It felt strange being back in harness after three weeks on the beach.<br>在海滩待了三周后重回工作岗位，感觉怪怪的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈharness (with sb) (BrE)</td><td>合作；共同工作</td><td>The two charities have worked in harness with each other for many years.<br>这两家慈善机构多年来一直携手合作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>haste</b></td><td>ˌmore ˈhaste, ˌless ˈspeed (BrE, saying)</td><td>欲速则不达</td><td>More haste, less speed — you'll finish sooner if you stop rushing.<br>欲速则不达，别慌反而更快做完。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hat</b></td><td>ˌkeep sth under your ˈhat (informal)</td><td>保守秘密；不声张</td><td>Keep this under your hat, but I'm leaving the company in June.<br>这事你别声张，我六月要离职了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take your ˈhat off to sb • hats ˈoff to sb (especially BrE) (informal)</td><td>向…表示钦佩；脱帽致敬</td><td>I take my hat off to anyone who can run a marathon barefoot.<br>谁能赤脚跑完马拉松，我真是佩服。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>old ˈhat (informal)</td><td>老一套；过时的东西</td><td>Those special effects looked amazing once, but they're all old hat now.<br>那些特效当年很惊艳，如今全是老一套了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw your ˈhat into the ring</td><td>宣布参加竞选或比赛</td><td>She threw her hat into the ring just two days before nominations closed.<br>提名截止前两天，她才宣布参选。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hatch</b></td><td>down the ˈhatch (informal)</td><td>干杯</td><td>Right, everyone raise your glasses and down the hatch!<br>好了，大家举杯，干了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>batten down the ˈhatches</td><td>严阵以待；准备应对困难</td><td>With budget cuts coming, we'd better batten down the hatches for a hard year.<br>预算要削减了，我们最好做好过苦日子的准备。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hatchet</b></td><td>a ˈhatchet job (on sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>恶意攻击；肆意诋毁</td><td>The reviewer did a real hatchet job on her first novel.<br>那位评论家把她的第一部小说批得一无是处。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>haul</b></td><td>haul sb over the ˈcoals (BrE) (AmE rake sb over the ˈcoals)</td><td>严厉训斥某人</td><td>The coach hauled us over the coals for turning up late to training.<br>我们训练迟到，教练把我们狠狠训了一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a long ˈhaul</td><td>长期艰苦的努力；长途运输</td><td>Rebuilding the business after the fire will be a long haul.<br>火灾后重建生意会是一场持久战。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have it ˈout with sb</td><td>与某人摊牌；争论清楚</td><td>I'm going to have it out with my flatmate about the unwashed dishes.<br>我要跟室友把没洗碗的事说清楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>and what ˈhave you (spoken)</td><td>诸如此类；等等</td><td>The drawer's full of pens, batteries, old keys and what have you.<br>抽屉里塞满了笔、电池、旧钥匙之类的东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have ˈhad it (informal)</td><td>坏透了无法修复；完蛋了</td><td>This kettle has had it — the element burned out this morning.<br>这水壶报废了，今早加热管烧坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>haves</b></td><td>the ˌhaves and the ˈhave-nots</td><td>富人和穷人</td><td>The gap between the haves and the have-nots keeps getting wider every year.<br>富人和穷人之间的差距一年比一年大。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>having</b></td><td>he, she, etc. isn't ˈhaving any (of it)</td><td>不愿听；不肯接受</td><td>I offered to explain everything, but she wasn't having any of it.<br>我想把一切解释清楚，可她根本不听。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>havoc</b></td><td>play/wreak ˈhavoc with sth</td><td>对…造成严重破坏或混乱</td><td>The snowstorm wreaked havoc with flights all along the east coast.<br>暴风雪把整个东海岸的航班搅得一团糟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hay</b></td><td>make hay while the ˈsun shines (saying)</td><td>抓紧时机；趁热打铁</td><td>Tourists are everywhere this month, so make hay while the sun shines.<br>这个月游客很多，趁热打铁多赚点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>haywire</b></td><td>go ˈhaywire (informal)</td><td>失去控制；出故障</td><td>The heating went haywire and the whole flat was boiling all night.<br>暖气失灵了，整间公寓热了一整夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>head</b></td><td>above/over sb's ˈhead</td><td>超出某人的理解能力</td><td>Most of that lecture went completely over my head, I'm afraid.<br>恐怕那堂课大部分我都听不懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be banging, etc. your head against a brick ˈwall (informal)</td><td>徒劳无益；白费口舌</td><td>Asking him to tidy his room is like banging your head against a brick wall.<br>让他收拾房间简直是白费口舌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>off the top of your ˈhead (informal)</td><td>未经细想；随口说出</td><td>Off the top of my head, I'd say about forty people came.<br>我随口一说，大概来了四十人吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bite/snap sb's ˈhead off (informal)</td><td>没好气地呵斥某人</td><td>I only asked about dinner and she bit my head off.<br>我不过问了一句晚饭，她就冲我发火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring sth/come to a ˈhead</td><td>到危急关头；必须解决</td><td>The argument over money finally came to a head at Christmas.<br>关于钱的争执在圣诞节终于到了摊牌的地步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>build up/work up, etc. a head of ˈsteam</td><td>蓄势；形成势头</td><td>The campaign is finally building up a head of steam in the northern towns.<br>这场运动终于在北方各镇形成了势头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bury/hide your ˌhead in the ˈsand</td><td>回避现实；采取鸵鸟政策</td><td>Stop burying your head in the sand and open those bank letters.<br>别再逃避现实了，把银行的信拆开看看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>can't make head or/nor ˈtail of sth (informal)</td><td>完全不明白；茫无头绪</td><td>I can't make head or tail of these assembly instructions.<br>这些组装说明我完全看不懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sb's ˈhead in (BrE, informal)</td><td>使某人烦躁；让人受不了</td><td>All this paperwork is really doing my head in this week.<br>这周这么多文书工作快把我逼疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from ˌhead to ˈfoot/ˈtoe</td><td>从头到脚；全身</td><td>He came in from the garden covered in mud from head to foot.<br>他从花园进来，从头到脚都是泥。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈhead down (informal)</td><td>埋头工作或学习</td><td>I'll get my head down and finish the report before lunch.<br>我埋头把报告在午饭前写完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈhead round sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>理解难懂的事；想明白</td><td>I still can't get my head round the fact that she's moving abroad.<br>她要移居国外，我到现在还想不明白。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get sth into your/sb's (thick) ˈhead (informal)</td><td>使充分理解；记牢</td><td>Get it into your thick head that the shop closes at five.<br>你给我记牢了，店里五点关门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/take it into your ˈhead that... (informal)</td><td>（常指错误地）认定；误以为</td><td>He got it into his head that everyone in the office was laughing at him.<br>他认定办公室里人人都在笑话他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb their ˈhead</td><td>放手让某人自主行事</td><td>Give the new designer her head and see what she comes up with.<br>放手让新设计师去做，看看她能拿出什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to your ˈhead</td><td>（酒）上头；（成功）冲昏头脑</td><td>That second glass of wine has gone straight to my head.<br>第二杯酒一下就让我上头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a good ˈhead on your shoulders</td><td>头脑清醒；明智</td><td>She's only nineteen but she has a good head on her shoulders.<br>她才十九岁，但很有头脑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a (good) head for ˈfigures</td><td>擅长计算；数字头脑好</td><td>You need a good head for figures to survive in this job.<br>干这行得有很强的数字头脑才行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a (good) head for ˈheights</td><td>不恐高</td><td>I don't have a head for heights, so you can clean the gutters.<br>我恐高，清理屋檐排水槽的活儿归你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your head in the ˈclouds (informal)</td><td>想入非非；不切实际</td><td>He has his head in the clouds and never notices what's happening around him.<br>他整天想入非非，从不留意周围的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your ˈhead screwed on (the right way)</td><td>头脑清楚；明白事理</td><td>Don't worry about her — that girl has her head screwed on.<br>别为她操心，那姑娘明白着呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/per ˈhead</td><td>每人；按人头计</td><td>Dinner worked out at about thirty pounds a head, including wine.<br>连酒算下来，晚饭人均三十英镑左右。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>head and ˈshoulders above sb/sth</td><td>远胜过；出类拔萃</td><td>Her design was head and shoulders above everything else we received.<br>她的设计比我们收到的其他作品高出一大截。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>head ˈnorth/ˈsouth (business)</td><td>（股价等）上升；下降</td><td>Share prices headed south the moment the results were announced.<br>业绩一公布，股价立刻下跌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>head over ˈheels (in ˈlove)</td><td>深深迷恋；爱得神魂颠倒</td><td>They met in March and by June were head over heels in love.<br>他们三月相识，到六月就爱得死去活来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌhead ˈstart (on/over sb)</td><td>先起步的优势；领先一步</td><td>Studying abroad gave her a head start over the other applicants.<br>留学经历让她比其他申请者抢先一步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold your ˈhead up (high)</td><td>昂首挺胸；不以为耻</td><td>You did nothing wrong, so hold your head up high in there.<br>你没做错事，进去时把头抬起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in over your ˈhead</td><td>力不从心；难以应付</td><td>I took the contract on and quickly realized I was in over my head.<br>我接下了这份合同，很快就发现自己力不从心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your ˈhead</td><td>保持镇静</td><td>She kept her head when the engine caught fire and led everyone out.<br>发动机着火时她保持镇静，把大家带了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your ˈhead above water</td><td>勉强维持；不致陷入困境</td><td>Two jobs are just enough to keep our heads above water.<br>打两份工才勉强让我们不至于入不敷出。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your ˈhead down (informal)</td><td>低调行事；避免引人注意</td><td>Just keep your head down for a week until the boss calms down.<br>低调一周，等老板消气再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose your ˈhead (informal)</td><td>失去理智；惊慌失措</td><td>Everyone else lost their heads, but the pilot stayed completely calm.<br>其他人都慌了神，只有飞行员十分镇定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>need, want, etc. your ˈhead examined</td><td>脑子有毛病；发疯</td><td>Anyone who swims in that river in January needs their head examined.<br>一月份还在那条河里游泳的人，脑子准有毛病。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on sb's (own) head ˈbe it</td><td>后果自负；由某人承担</td><td>If you go climbing in this weather, on your own head be it.<br>这种天气你还去爬山，后果自负。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of/off your ˈhead (BrE, informal)</td><td>疯了；神志不清</td><td>He was completely out of his head and kept shouting at the traffic.<br>他神志不清，一直冲着车流大喊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>over sb's ˈhead</td><td>越级；越过某人向上级反映</td><td>She went over her manager's head and emailed the director directly.<br>她越过经理，直接给总监发了邮件。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put your ˌhead in the lion's ˈmouth</td><td>身涉险境；铤而走险</td><td>Testifying against them is putting your head in the lion's mouth.<br>出庭指证他们等于把脑袋往狮子嘴里送。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sth out of your ˈhead</td><td>不再想；打消念头</td><td>Put the exam out of your head and get some proper sleep tonight.<br>别再想考试了，今晚好好睡一觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rear/raise its (ugly) ˈhead</td><td>（坏事）再次出现；重新抬头</td><td>Racism reared its ugly head again during last weekend's match.<br>上周末的比赛中，种族主义又露头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>scream, shout, etc. your ˈhead off (informal)</td><td>拼命尖叫；大喊大叫</td><td>The baby screamed her head off all the way to the airport.<br>一路到机场，宝宝哭喊个不停。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stand/turn sth on its ˈhead</td><td>彻底颠覆；使完全颠倒</td><td>Her new book stands the traditional theory of evolution on its head.<br>她的新书把传统进化论彻底颠覆了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take it into your head to do sth</td><td>心血来潮；突发奇想</td><td>He suddenly took it into his head to cycle to Scotland alone.<br>他忽然心血来潮，要独自骑车去苏格兰。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn sb's ˈhead</td><td>使某人得意忘形；冲昏头脑</td><td>All that praise from the critics has clearly turned his head.<br>评论家的那些赞扬显然让他飘飘然了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run around like a ˌheadless ˈchicken</td><td>没头没脑地瞎忙</td><td>I ran around like a headless chicken all morning and achieved nothing.<br>我一上午瞎忙一气，什么也没干成。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>headlines</b></td><td>grab/hit/make the ˈheadlines (informal)</td><td>成为头条新闻；被大肆报道</td><td>The scandal hit the headlines just two days before the general election.<br>丑闻在大选前两天登上了头条。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heads</b></td><td>bang/knock your/their ˈheads together (informal)</td><td>迫使人们停止争吵</td><td>I'd like to bang those two boys' heads together and end this stupid argument.<br>我真想把这两个小子拉过来，结束这场愚蠢的争吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>heads or ˈtails? (spoken)</td><td>正面还是反面</td><td>Heads or tails? The winner gets to choose tonight's film.<br>正面还是反面？赢的人挑今晚的电影。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈheads will roll (humorous)</td><td>有人将为此受到惩罚</td><td>If these figures reach the press, heads will roll in the accounts department.<br>这些数字要是让媒体知道了，财务部有人要倒霉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put your, their, etc. ˈheads together (informal)</td><td>集思广益；共同商量</td><td>Let's put our heads together and find a way out of this mess.<br>咱们集思广益，想办法摆脱这个烂摊子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not ˈhear of sth</td><td>不同意；不肯考虑</td><td>I offered to pay for dinner but she wouldn't hear of it.<br>我提出请客，可她根本不答应。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(do) you ˈhear me? (spoken)</td><td>听到我的话没有</td><td>You are not going out tonight — do you hear me?<br>你今晚不许出去，听见我说的没有？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not say/hear a ˌdicky ˈbird (BrE, informal)</td><td>一言不发；毫无音讯</td><td>I've written three times and haven't heard a dicky bird from them.<br>我写了三次信，他们那边一点音讯都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heard</b></td><td>you could have heard a ˈpin drop</td><td>鸦雀无声；静得出奇</td><td>When she announced her resignation, you could have heard a pin drop.<br>她宣布辞职时，全场鸦雀无声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the last I ˈheard</td><td>我最后一次听说时</td><td>The last I heard, they were still living somewhere near Leeds.<br>我最后一次听说时，他们还住在利兹附近。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hearing</b></td><td>in/within (sb's) ˈhearing</td><td>在某人听得见的范围内</td><td>Please don't discuss the diagnosis within the patient's hearing.<br>请不要在病人听得见的地方讨论诊断结果。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heart</b></td><td>at ˈheart</td><td>内心里；本质上</td><td>He shouts a lot, but at heart he is a very gentle man.<br>他常大声嚷嚷，但骨子里是个很温和的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be close/dear/near to sb's ˈheart</td><td>为某人所珍视关切</td><td>Animal welfare is a subject very close to my grandmother's heart.<br>动物福利是我奶奶特别关心的话题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by ˈheart (BrE also off by ˈheart)</td><td>背诵；牢记在心</td><td>She learned the whole poem by heart in a single evening.<br>她一个晚上就把整首诗背了下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>break sb's ˈheart</td><td>使某人心碎；令人极为伤心</td><td>It broke my heart to sell the piano my father gave me.<br>卖掉父亲送我的钢琴让我心碎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌheart-to-ˈheart (talk)</td><td>推心置腹的谈话</td><td>We finally had a heart-to-heart about why he wants to leave school.<br>我们终于推心置腹地聊了聊他为什么想退学。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sb's heart ˈgood (to do sth)</td><td>使某人欣慰高兴</td><td>It does my heart good to see the two of you laughing again.<br>看到你俩又有说有笑，我心里真高兴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(come) (straight) from the ˈheart</td><td>发自内心；真诚的</td><td>Her apology clearly came straight from the heart, and everyone forgave her.<br>她的道歉显然发自肺腑，大家都原谅了她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈheart (spoken)</td><td>发发善心吧；开开恩吧</td><td>Have a heart — the poor dog has been walking for hours.<br>发发善心吧，这可怜的狗都走了好几个小时了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a heart of ˈgold</td><td>心肠极好；有金子般的心</td><td>He looks grumpy but he has a heart of gold underneath.<br>他看着脾气坏，其实心肠特别好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a heart of ˈstone</td><td>铁石心肠；冷酷无情</td><td>You'd need a heart of stone not to cry at that film.<br>看那部电影不哭，除非你铁石心肠。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(your) heart and ˈsoul</td><td>全心全意；满腔热忱</td><td>She threw herself heart and soul into rebuilding the village school.<br>她全身心投入到重建村小学的工作中。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your heart ˈbleeds for sb (ironic)</td><td>才不同情你呢（反语）</td><td>So you had to fly business class? My heart bleeds for you.<br>这么说你只能坐商务舱？我可真同情你啊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in good ˈheart (BrE)</td><td>心情舒畅；兴致高</td><td>The team came back from the tour tired but in good heart.<br>球队巡回赛回来，虽然疲惫但情绪很好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your heart is in your ˈmouth (informal)</td><td>提心吊胆；紧张万分</td><td>My heart was in my mouth as the plane bumped through the storm.<br>飞机在风暴中颠簸时，我的心提到了嗓子眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your heart ˈleaps</td><td>心头一喜；欢欣雀跃</td><td>My heart leapt when I saw his name on the caller display.<br>看到来电显示上他的名字，我心头一喜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your heart misses a ˈbeat</td><td>（因惊恐或兴奋）心跳漏拍</td><td>My heart missed a beat when the headmaster called out my name.<br>校长叫我名字时，我心跳漏了一拍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in your ˌheart of ˈhearts</td><td>在内心深处</td><td>In my heart of hearts I knew the marriage was already over.<br>在内心深处，我知道这段婚姻已经结束了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let your ˌheart rule your ˈhead</td><td>感情用事；情感胜过理智</td><td>She let her heart rule her head and lent him the money anyway.<br>她感情用事，还是把钱借给了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose ˈheart</td><td>失去信心；灰心泄气</td><td>Don't lose heart — plenty of famous writers were rejected twenty times.<br>别灰心，很多名作家都被退过二十次稿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose your ˈheart (to sb/sth) (formal)</td><td>爱上；倾心于</td><td>He lost his heart to that scruffy little dog at the shelter.<br>他爱上了收容所里那只邋遢的小狗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a man, woman, etc. after your own ˈheart</td><td>合自己心意的人</td><td>Anyone who hates early mornings is a woman after my own heart.<br>讨厌早起的人正合我意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have the ˈheart (to do sth)</td><td>不忍心做某事</td><td>I didn't have the heart to tell her the puppy had died.<br>我不忍心告诉她小狗死了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rip/ˌtear the ˈheart out of sth</td><td>摧毁…的核心</td><td>Closing the mine tore the heart out of the whole town.<br>矿井关闭，把整个镇子的命脉都毁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set your ˈheart/ˈmind on sth/on doing sth</td><td>决心得到；一心想要</td><td>She set her heart on that flat the moment she saw the balcony.<br>她一看到那个阳台，就一门心思要买下那套房。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your heart/mind ˈset on sth/on doing sth</td><td>渴望得到；一心想做某事</td><td>He has his heart set on studying medicine in Edinburgh next year.<br>他一心想明年去爱丁堡学医。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈheart (from sth)</td><td>受到鼓舞；重树信心</td><td>Take heart from the fact that your last two interviews went well.<br>想想你上两次面试都不错，别泄气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth to ˈheart</td><td>十分介意；耿耿于怀</td><td>She took his criticism to heart and rewrote the entire chapter.<br>她把他的批评听进了心里，重写了整章。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to your heart's conˈtent</td><td>尽情地</td><td>The garden is huge, so the children can run around to their heart's content.<br>花园很大，孩子们可以尽情地奔跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with all your ˈheart/your whole ˈheart</td><td>全心全意地；衷心地</td><td>I thank you with all my heart for everything you did.<br>我衷心感谢你所做的一切。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with a ˌheavy/ˌsinking ˈheart</td><td>心情沉重地；忧虑地</td><td>With a heavy heart she posted the keys back to the landlord.<br>她怀着沉重的心情把钥匙寄还给了房东。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heartbeat</b></td><td>a ˈheartbeat away (from sth)</td><td>近在咫尺；只差一步</td><td>As vice-president, he was only a heartbeat away from the presidency.<br>身为副总统，他离总统之位只有一步之遥。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in a ˈheartbeat</td><td>立刻；瞬间</td><td>If they offered me that job again, I'd take it in a heartbeat.<br>他们要是再给我那份工作，我立马就接。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hearts</b></td><td>hearts and ˈminds</td><td>人心；民心向背</td><td>Cheap tickets alone won't win the hearts and minds of local football fans.<br>光靠低价票赢不了当地球迷的心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heat</b></td><td>if you can't stand the ˈheat (get out of the ˈkitchen) (informal)</td><td>受不了压力就别干</td><td>The kitchen is chaotic at lunchtime; if you can't stand the heat, leave.<br>午餐时厨房乱成一团，受不了就别待着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˌheat of the ˈmoment</td><td>一时冲动之下</td><td>I said some awful things in the heat of the moment and deeply regret them.<br>一时冲动我说了些难听的话，现在很后悔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈheat out of sth</td><td>缓和局势；降低紧张</td><td>The manager's apology took the heat out of a very tense meeting.<br>经理的道歉缓和了会议紧张的气氛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn on the ˈheat (informal)</td><td>施加压力；威逼</td><td>The bank turned on the heat and demanded repayment within thirty days.<br>银行开始施压，要求三十天内还款。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heave-ho</b></td><td>give sb the (old) ˌheave-ˈho (informal)</td><td>解雇某人；与某人断绝关系</td><td>After twelve years the club gave their manager the old heave-ho.<br>干了十二年，俱乐部把主教练炒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heaven</b></td><td>a heaven on ˈearth</td><td>人间天堂</td><td>That quiet beach at sunset was a heaven on earth for us.<br>日落时那片安静的沙滩对我们就是人间天堂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌmarriage/ˌmatch made in ˈheaven</td><td>天作之合；天生一对</td><td>They're both quiet, kind and love hiking — a match made in heaven.<br>他俩都安静善良又爱远足，真是天作之合。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heavens</b></td><td>(Good) ˈHeavens! • Heavens aˈbove! (spoken)</td><td>天哪；我的天</td><td>Good Heavens! I had no idea it was already past midnight.<br>天哪！我都不知道已经过了半夜了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the heavens ˈopen</td><td>大雨倾盆</td><td>We'd just lit the barbecue when the heavens opened and everyone ran inside.<br>我们刚点上烧烤炉就下起倾盆大雨，大家全跑进屋。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heavy</b></td><td>get ˈheavy (informal)</td><td>变得严重；气氛紧张</td><td>Things got heavy when he accused her of taking the money.<br>他指责她拿了钱，场面一下就紧张起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang/lie ˈheavy (on sb/sth)</td><td>沉重地笼罩；郁积不散</td><td>A smell of damp hung heavy on the empty rooms upstairs.<br>楼上空房间里弥漫着一股浓重的潮气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>heavy ˈgoing</td><td>费劲的；枯燥难懂的</td><td>The first hundred pages were heavy going, but the novel improves later.<br>头一百页读着很费劲，不过小说后面好多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a heavy ˈhand</td><td>高压手段；过于严厉的方式</td><td>The new principal runs the school with a heavy hand.<br>新校长用高压手段管理学校。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈheavy mob/brigade (BrE, informal)</td><td>打手；保镖团伙</td><td>When he refused to pay, the landlord sent in the heavy mob.<br>他不肯付钱，房东就派了打手来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a heavy ˈsilence/ˈatmosphere</td><td>令人不安的沉默或气氛</td><td>A heavy silence fell when she asked who had told the manager.<br>她问是谁告诉经理的，屋里顿时一片沉默。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make heavy ˈweather of sth/of doing sth</td><td>小题大做；把事情弄复杂</td><td>You're making heavy weather of a simple form — just tick the boxes.<br>一张简单的表格你搞得这么复杂，打勾就行了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heck</b></td><td>for the ˈheck of it (informal)</td><td>只是为了好玩</td><td>We drove to the coast at midnight just for the heck of it.<br>我们半夜开车去海边，纯粹是图个好玩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what the ˈheck! (informal)</td><td>管它呢；那又怎样</td><td>What the heck! It's a celebration, so let's order dessert too.<br>管它呢！今天是庆祝，甜点也点上吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hedge</b></td><td>ˌhedge your ˈbets (informal)</td><td>两面下注；分散风险</td><td>I applied to three universities in order to hedge my bets.<br>我申请了三所大学，多留几手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌheebie-ˈjeebies (informal)</td><td>紧张不安；心里发毛</td><td>That empty hospital corridor at night gives me the heebie-jeebies.<br>夜里那条空荡荡的医院走廊让我心里发毛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heed</b></td><td>give/pay ˈheed (to sb/sth) • take ˈheed (of sb/sth) (formal)</td><td>留心；注意；理会</td><td>Pay heed to the weather forecast before you set off up the mountain.<br>上山前留心一下天气预报。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heel</b></td><td>come to ˈheel • bring sb to ˈheel</td><td>使就范；服从</td><td>One sharp word from the chairman brought the whole committee to heel.<br>主席一句厉声，整个委员会就都服帖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌdown at ˈheel</td><td>衣衫褴褛；破败寒酸</td><td>The hotel looked rather down at heel, with peeling paint everywhere.<br>这家旅馆显得破败寒酸，到处都是剥落的油漆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌturn/ˌspin on your ˈheel</td><td>转身就走</td><td>She turned on her heel and walked out without saying goodbye.<br>她转身就走，连声再见都没说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under the ˈheel of sb (literary)</td><td>受某人压迫；受人践踏</td><td>The village lived for years under the heel of a brutal landlord.<br>这个村子多年来受一个残暴地主的压迫。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heels</b></td><td>at/on sb's ˈheels</td><td>紧随某人身后</td><td>The little dog trotted at his heels all the way home.<br>小狗一路小跑跟着他回家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hard/hot on sb's ˈheels</td><td>紧追不舍；紧随其后</td><td>The police were hot on his heels as he crossed the border.<br>他越过边境时，警察正紧追不舍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtake to your ˈheels</td><td>撒腿就跑；逃走</td><td>The boys took to their heels the moment the angry farmer shouted.<br>愤怒的农夫一喊，男孩们撒腿就跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hell</b></td><td>all ˈhell breaks/is let loose (informal)</td><td>顿时乱作一团</td><td>The referee blew for a penalty and all hell broke loose.<br>裁判判了点球，全场顿时乱作一团。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat/knock/kick the ˈhell out of sb/sth (informal)</td><td>猛揍；狠打</td><td>Two men beat the hell out of him and stole his phone.<br>两个人把他狠揍一顿，抢走了手机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb ˈhell (informal)</td><td>让某人吃苦头；痛骂某人</td><td>The sergeant gave the new recruits hell during their very first week.<br>第一周里，中士把新兵折腾得够呛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) for the ˈhell of it (informal)</td><td>只是闹着玩；没有目的</td><td>He learned Finnish just for the hell of it, with no plans to travel.<br>他纯粹为了好玩学了芬兰语，根本没打算去旅行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from ˈhell (informal)</td><td>糟糕透顶的；坏得要命的</td><td>We had the flight from hell — three delays and lost luggage.<br>我们坐了趟糟糕透顶的航班，延误三次还丢了行李。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get the hell ˈout (of...) (spoken)</td><td>赶紧离开</td><td>Grab your coat and let's get the hell out of here.<br>拿上外套，咱们赶紧离开这儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to ˈhell (spoken, offensive)</td><td>见你的鬼；滚开</td><td>Go to hell! I am not lending you any money again.<br>见你的鬼去！我不会再借钱给你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hell hath no ˈfury (like a woman ˈscorned)</td><td>被抛弃的女人怒火难挡</td><td>She burned all his letters — hell hath no fury like a woman scorned.<br>她烧光了他所有的信，女人翻脸真是不得了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a hell on ˈearth</td><td>人间地狱</td><td>The refugee camp in winter was a hell on earth.<br>冬天的难民营简直是人间地狱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Hell's ˈteeth (old-fashioned, BrE, spoken)</td><td>见鬼；天哪</td><td>Hell's teeth! Who left the freezer door wide open all night?<br>见鬼！谁把冰柜门整夜大敞着？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like ˈhell</td><td>拼命地；飞快地</td><td>We ran like hell to catch the last bus home.<br>我们拼命跑去赶末班车回家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play (merry) ˈhell with sb/sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>严重扰乱；搅得一团糟</td><td>The roadworks are playing merry hell with deliveries to the shop.<br>修路把送货到店的事搅得一团糟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>scare, annoy, etc. the ˈhell out of sb (informal)</td><td>把某人吓坏；使人极为恼火</td><td>That horror film scared the hell out of my little sister.<br>那部恐怖片把我妹妹吓得魂不附体。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see sb in ˈhell first (informal)</td><td>决不；死也不肯</td><td>Apologize to him? I'd see him in hell first.<br>向他道歉？我死也不干。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈhell and back (informal)</td><td>历尽磨难</td><td>She's been to hell and back this year, but she's still smiling.<br>她今年历尽劫难，可依然在笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈhell with sb/sth (spoken)</td><td>见鬼去吧；管它呢</td><td>To hell with the diet — pass me another slice of cake.<br>减肥去它的吧，再给我来块蛋糕。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what the ˈhell! (spoken)</td><td>没关系；我不在乎</td><td>What the hell! It's my birthday, so let's take a taxi.<br>管它呢！今天我生日，打车吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>when ˈhell freezes over (informal)</td><td>永远不可能</td><td>He'll apologize when hell freezes over, and not a moment before.<br>他要道歉，除非太阳从西边出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hell-bent</b></td><td>be ˌhell-ˈbent on sth/on doing sth</td><td>一意孤行；铁了心要做</td><td>She seems hell-bent on selling the house before anyone can stop her.<br>她像是铁了心要在别人阻止之前把房子卖掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>helm</b></td><td>at the ˈhelm/tiller</td><td>掌舵；掌管</td><td>With his daughter at the helm, the family firm doubled its profits.<br>在女儿掌舵下，这家家族企业利润翻了一番。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take (over) the ˈhelm</td><td>接管；开始掌管</td><td>She took over the helm of the company after her father's sudden death.<br>父亲突然去世后，她接管了公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>help</b></td><td>can't help (doing) sth • can't help but do sth</td><td>忍不住做某事；不可避免</td><td>I can't help laughing every time I watch that old comedy sketch.<br>每次看那个老喜剧小品我都忍不住笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>God/Heaven ˈhelp sb (spoken)</td><td>老天保佑；某人可要糟了</td><td>God help us if the boss finds out who broke the printer.<br>要是老板发现谁弄坏了打印机，那我们可就惨了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so ˈhelp me (God)</td><td>上帝作证；我发誓</td><td>I never touched your bike that evening, so help me God.<br>那天晚上我从没碰过你的自行车，我发誓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no ˈhelp for it (especially BrE)</td><td>没办法；别无选择</td><td>The last bus has gone; there's no help for it, we walk.<br>末班车走了，没办法，只能走路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rare</b></td><td>(as) rare/scarce as hen's ˈteeth (old-fashioned)</td><td>极为稀少；凤毛麟角</td><td>Parking spaces near the station are as rare as hen's teeth on Fridays.<br>周五车站附近的车位少得跟凤毛麟角一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hence</b></td><td>days, weeks, etc. ˈhence (formal)</td><td>自现在起…天（或周等）后</td><td>Three weeks hence we shall know whether the merger has been approved.<br>三周之后我们就知道合并有没有获批了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>here</b></td><td>here and ˈnow</td><td>此时此刻；立即</td><td>I want an answer here and now, not next week.<br>我现在就要答案，不是下周。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>here and ˈthere</td><td>到处；四下</td><td>Wild flowers grew here and there along the old railway line.<br>野花零星地开在废弃铁路沿线。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>here ˈgoes • here we ˈgo</td><td>开始了；来吧</td><td>Right, here goes — wish me luck with this interview.<br>好了，开始了，祝我面试顺利吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>here goes ˈnothing (AmE)</td><td>碰碰运气吧</td><td>I've never skied before in my life, so here goes nothing.<br>我这辈子没滑过雪，碰碰运气吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>here we go aˈgain</td><td>又来了；又是老一套</td><td>He's blaming the weather for the delay again — here we go again.<br>他又拿天气给延误当借口，又来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>here you ˈare • here you ˈgo (spoken)</td><td>给你</td><td>Here you are — one black coffee and a warm croissant.<br>给你，一杯黑咖啡和一个热羊角面包。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>neither ˌhere nor ˈthere</td><td>无关紧要；不相干</td><td>Whether he apologized or not is neither here nor there now.<br>他有没有道歉，现在都无关紧要了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>herring</b></td><td>a red ˈherring</td><td>转移注意力的事物；幌子</td><td>The missing passport turned out to be a red herring in the investigation.<br>那本丢失的护照结果只是调查中的一个幌子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hesitates</b></td><td>he who ˈhesitates (is ˈlost) (saying)</td><td>犹豫不决错失良机</td><td>Book the flight tonight — he who hesitates is lost.<br>今晚就订机票，犹豫就会错失良机。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hey</b></td><td>hey ˈpresto (BrE) (AmE ˈpresto)</td><td>说变就变；瞧，成了</td><td>Add a little butter, stir twice, and hey presto, perfect sauce.<br>加点黄油，搅两下，瞧，完美的酱汁就成了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what the ˈhey! (AmE, spoken)</td><td>没关系；我不在乎</td><td>What the hey! Let's stay another night at the beach.<br>管它呢！咱们在海边再住一晚。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hide</b></td><td>hide your ˌlight under a ˈbushel (BrE)</td><td>不露锋芒；埋没才能</td><td>Don't hide your light under a bushel — tell them you speak Japanese.<br>别藏着掖着，告诉他们你会日语。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not see ˌhide nor ˈhair of sb/sth (spoken)</td><td>不见…的踪影</td><td>We haven't seen hide nor hair of the cat since Tuesday morning.<br>从周二早上起我们就没见过那只猫的影子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hiding</b></td><td>be on a ˌhiding to ˈnothing (BrE, informal)</td><td>毫无成功机会</td><td>You're on a hiding to nothing trying to please both families at once.<br>你想同时让两家都满意，根本不可能成功。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>high</b></td><td>be for the ˈhigh jump (BrE, informal)</td><td>将受到惩罚或批评</td><td>If the manager sees this mess, you'll be for the high jump.<br>经理要是看到这么乱，你可要挨罚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get on your ˌhigh ˈhorse</td><td>自以为是；愤愤不平地训人</td><td>She got on her high horse about people not recycling properly.<br>她为别人不好好垃圾分类而摆出一副训人的架势。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈhigh old time (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>玩得很尽兴</td><td>We had a high old time at the village fair last Saturday.<br>上周六村里的集市我们玩得很尽兴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>high and ˈdry</td><td>孤立无援；陷入困境</td><td>The travel company folded and left two hundred tourists high and dry.<br>旅行社倒闭，把两百名游客晾在了那里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌhigh and ˈlow</td><td>到处（寻找）</td><td>I searched high and low for my glasses and found them upstairs.<br>我到处找眼镜，最后在楼上找到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌhigh and ˈmighty (informal)</td><td>趾高气扬；神气活现</td><td>Don't be so high and mighty — you were once a beginner too.<br>别那么神气，你当初也是新手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) high as a ˈkite (informal)</td><td>极度兴奋；醉醺醺的</td><td>By midnight half the guests were as high as a kite.<br>到半夜，一半的客人都嗨翻了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>high days and ˈholidays</td><td>节庆假日；特殊日子</td><td>Grandmother's silver only came out on high days and holidays.<br>奶奶的银餐具只在节庆日子才拿出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>high ˈfive (especially AmE)</td><td>击掌（表示庆祝）</td><td>The children gave each other a high five after scoring the winning goal.<br>打进制胜球后，孩子们互相击掌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈhigh point/spot of sth</td><td>最精彩的部分；顶点</td><td>Swimming with dolphins was definitely the high point of our holiday.<br>和海豚一起游泳绝对是这次假期最精彩的部分。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˌhigh ˈdudgeon (old-fashioned, written)</td><td>怒气冲冲地</td><td>He left the meeting in high dudgeon after his idea was rejected.<br>提议被否后，他怒气冲冲地离开了会议。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈhigh</td><td>在高处；来自上层</td><td>The order came from on high, so nobody dared question it.<br>命令是上头下的，没人敢质疑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˌhigh ˈseas</td><td>在公海上</td><td>The ship was still on the high seas when the storm hit.<br>风暴来袭时，船还在公海上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run ˈhigh</td><td>（情绪）高涨激动</td><td>Feelings ran high at the meeting about closing the local library.<br>关于关闭社区图书馆的会上，大家情绪激动。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>smell/stink to high ˈheaven (informal)</td><td>臭气熏天；十分可疑</td><td>That bin hasn't been emptied for weeks and stinks to high heaven.<br>那个垃圾桶几周没倒了，臭气熏天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈhigh road (in sth) (AmE)</td><td>采取正派积极的做法</td><td>She took the high road and refused to comment on the ugly rumours.<br>她选择了正派的做法，拒绝对那些难听的传言发表评论。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hightail</b></td><td>hightail it (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>飞奔；急忙离开</td><td>As soon as the alarm sounded, he hightailed it out the back door.<br>警报一响，他就从后门飞奔而出。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>highways</b></td><td>ˌhighways and ˈbyways</td><td>大大小小的道路</td><td>We cycled the highways and byways of Devon for two whole weeks.<br>我们骑车走遍了德文郡的大路小道，整整两周。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hike</b></td><td>take a ˈhike (AmE, informal)</td><td>滚开；走开</td><td>He asked her for money again and she told him to take a hike.<br>他又向她要钱，她让他滚开。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hill</b></td><td>a hill of ˈbeans (old-fashioned, AmE, informal)</td><td>毫无价值的东西</td><td>Without proper funding, our whole plan isn't worth a hill of beans.<br>没有像样的资金，我们整个计划一文不值。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>over the ˈhill (informal)</td><td>过了巅峰期；不再年轻</td><td>He thinks anyone over forty is over the hill, which is nonsense.<br>他觉得过了四十就走下坡路了，真是胡说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up ˌhill and down ˈdale</td><td>翻山越谷；到处</td><td>We chased that runaway pony up hill and down dale all afternoon.<br>我们追那匹跑掉的小马，翻山越谷追了一下午。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hilt</b></td><td>(up) to the ˈhilt</td><td>全力地；最大限度地</td><td>The whole family backed her decision to the hilt.<br>全家人全力支持她的决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hint</b></td><td>take a/the ˈhint</td><td>领会暗示；心领神会</td><td>He kept yawning, so I took the hint and went home.<br>他一直打哈欠，我便识趣地回家了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>history</b></td><td>go down in/make ˈhistory</td><td>载入史册；创造历史</td><td>Her run that morning went down in history as the fastest ever.<br>她那天早上的成绩作为史上最快载入了史册。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈhistory books</td><td>史册；重大成就的记载</td><td>That victory earned the little club a place in the history books.<br>那场胜利让这家小俱乐部名留史册。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hit</b></td><td>be/make a (big, etc.) ˈhit with sb</td><td>大受某人欢迎</td><td>Your chocolate cake was a big hit with all the neighbours.<br>你做的巧克力蛋糕大受邻居们欢迎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit (it) ˈbig (informal)</td><td>大获成功；一炮而红</td><td>The band hit it big after their song appeared in a film.<br>这支乐队的歌上了电影后一炮而红。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit the ˈbooks (AmE)</td><td>用功学习</td><td>I'd better hit the books; the exam is on Monday morning.<br>我得用功了，周一上午就考试。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit the ˈbottle (informal)</td><td>酗酒；贪杯</td><td>He hit the bottle badly after losing his job last spring.<br>去年春天丢了工作后，他开始酗酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit the ˈbuffers (informal)</td><td>（计划等）突然受挫</td><td>The plan to build a new stadium has finally hit the buffers.<br>建新体育场的计划最终受挫了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit the nail on the ˈhead (informal)</td><td>一针见血；说到点子上</td><td>You've hit the nail on the head — it's really a staffing problem.<br>你说到点子上了，这其实是人手问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit the ˈroad (also hit the ˈtrail especially AmE)</td><td>出发；上路；动身</td><td>We should hit the road early tomorrow if we want to beat the traffic.<br>如果想避开车流，我们明天得早点出发。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit the ˈroof/ˈceiling (informal)</td><td>勃然大怒；暴跳如雷</td><td>My boss hit the roof when he saw how much the party had cost.<br>老板看到聚会花了多少钱，气得暴跳如雷。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit the ˈsack/ˈhay (informal)</td><td>上床睡觉</td><td>I'm exhausted after that long drive, so I'm going to hit the sack.<br>开了这么久的车，我累坏了，这就去睡觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit the ˈskids (especially AmE)</td><td>开始衰退；迅速恶化</td><td>His career hit the skids after that scandal appeared in the papers.<br>报上曝出那桩丑闻后，他的事业一路下滑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit the ˈspot (informal)</td><td>正合需要；恰到好处</td><td>A cold beer after mowing the lawn really hits the spot.<br>割完草坪来杯冰啤酒，真是舒服到位。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit the ˈstreets ◆ hit the ˈshops/ˈstores</td><td>上市；大量发售</td><td>The new phone hits the stores next Friday and people are already queuing.<br>新手机下周五上市，已经有人在排队了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit sb when they're ˈdown</td><td>落井下石；乘人之危</td><td>Firing her right after the divorce was really hitting someone when they're down.<br>刚离婚就把她辞了，真是落井下石。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit sb where it ˈhurts</td><td>刺中痛处；击中要害</td><td>If you want him to listen, hit him where it hurts and cut his budget.<br>想让他听话，就砍他预算，直击痛处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a ˈhit</td><td>受到重创；遭受损失</td><td>Our sales took a hit when the factory closed for three weeks.<br>工厂停工三周，我们的销售额受到了重创。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hit-and-run</b></td><td>ˌhit-and-run</td><td>肇事逃逸的（交通事故）</td><td>The police are still looking for the driver in last night's hit-and-run accident.<br>警方仍在追查昨晚肇事逃逸的司机。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hitch</b></td><td>hitch your ˌwagon to a ˈstar</td><td>借他人之势；攀附成功者</td><td>She hitched her wagon to a star by joining the young senator's campaign team.<br>她加入那位年轻参议员的竞选团队，借势而上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hitched</b></td><td>get ˈhitched (informal)</td><td>结婚</td><td>After ten years together, they finally got hitched in a tiny country church.<br>在一起十年后，他们终于在乡下小教堂结了婚。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hither</b></td><td>hither and ˈthither (especially literary)</td><td>四处；各处</td><td>Leaves blew hither and thither across the empty playground all afternoon.<br>一整个下午，树叶在空荡的操场上四处飘飞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hobby</b></td><td>a ˈhobby horse</td><td>老生常谈的话题；热衷谈论的事</td><td>Don't mention taxes or he'll climb onto his hobby horse again.<br>别提税的事，不然他又要老调重弹了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hobson</b></td><td>ˌHobson's ˈchoice</td><td>无选择余地的选择</td><td>It was Hobson's choice: take the night shift or lose the job entirely.<br>这是别无选择：要么上夜班，要么丢饭碗。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hock</b></td><td>be in ˈhock (to sb) (informal)</td><td>欠（某人）钱；负债</td><td>After the renovation we were in hock to the bank for years.<br>装修之后，我们欠了银行好几年的债。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take (a) ˈhold</td><td>开始完全控制；扎下根来</td><td>Panic took hold in the crowd as soon as the lights went out.<br>灯一灭，人群里立刻陷入恐慌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go the ˌwhole ˈhog (informal)</td><td>干到底；一不做二不休</td><td>We were repainting the kitchen anyway, so we went the whole hog and retiled it.<br>反正要重刷厨房，我们索性一不做二不休，连瓷砖也换了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hog-wild</b></td><td>go ˈhog-wild (AmE, informal)</td><td>疯狂；兴奋得忘乎所以</td><td>The kids went hog-wild when they saw the pile of presents.<br>孩子们看到一堆礼物，兴奋得快疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hoist</b></td><td>be hoist/hoisted by/with your own peˈtard</td><td>搬起石头砸自己的脚；害人害己</td><td>He spread the rumour and was hoist with his own petard when nobody trusted him.<br>他造谣生事，结果没人信他，搬石头砸了自己的脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hold</b></td><td>hold your ˈfire</td><td>暂停射击；先别急着批评</td><td>Hold your fire until you've heard the whole story from her side.<br>先别急着开火，听完她那边的说法再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catch/get/grab/take (a) ˈhold of sb/sth</td><td>抓住；握住</td><td>Grab hold of the rope and don't let go until I say so.<br>抓住绳子，我不说放手就别松开。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold ˈgood/ˈtrue</td><td>依然有效；仍然适用</td><td>That old advice about saving early still holds true for young workers today.<br>尽早储蓄这个老建议，对今天的年轻人依然适用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈhold it (informal)</td><td>别动；稍等一下</td><td>Hold it, I think you've left your wallet on the kitchen table.<br>等一下，你的钱包好像落在厨房桌上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold your ˈown</td><td>不落下风；支撑得住</td><td>She's only nineteen but she holds her own against much older players.<br>她才十九岁，跟年长得多的选手打也毫不逊色。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈhold</td><td>搁置；推迟</td><td>The whole project is on hold until the funding comes through next spring.<br>整个项目暂时搁置，要等明年春天拨款到位。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>holding</b></td><td>leave sb holding the ˈbaby (AmE also leave sb holding the ˈbag) (informal)</td><td>把烂摊子丢给某人</td><td>My partner quit halfway and left me holding the baby on the whole project.<br>合伙人中途退出，把整个项目的烂摊子丢给了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no ˈholding/ˈstopping sb</td><td>某人势不可挡；拦也拦不住</td><td>Once she decides to learn something, there's no holding her.<br>她一旦决定要学什么，谁也拦不住。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>holds</b></td><td>(with) no ˌholds ˈbarred</td><td>不受约束；毫无限制</td><td>It was a debate with no holds barred, and both sides said exactly what they thought.<br>那是一场毫无顾忌的辩论，双方都把话说透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hole</b></td><td>in a ˈhole (informal)</td><td>处于困境</td><td>We're in a hole financially and the rent is due on Monday.<br>我们手头很紧，房租周一就要交了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈhole (AmE, informal)</td><td>负债；欠钱</td><td>The restaurant was fifty thousand dollars in the hole by December.<br>到十二月，那家餐馆已经欠了五万美元。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>need/want sb/sth like (you need/want) a ˌhole in the ˈhead (informal)</td><td>绝不需要；根本不想要</td><td>I need another meeting today like I need a hole in the head.<br>今天再来一场会，我可真是一点都不想要。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈdent/ˈhole in sth</td><td>大量消耗；花掉一大笔</td><td>Buying the new car made a serious hole in our savings.<br>买了新车，我们的存款被啃掉一大块。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>holiday</b></td><td>a ˌbusman's ˈholiday</td><td>照常干本行的假日</td><td>For a chef, cooking for friends on Sunday is a real busman's holiday.<br>对厨师来说，周日给朋友做饭简直是换汤不换药的假期。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>holy</b></td><td>ˌholy of ˈholies (humorous)</td><td>圣地；禁地</td><td>Nobody enters the director's office; it's the holy of holies around here.<br>没人能进主任办公室，那可是这里的禁地。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>home</b></td><td>at ˈhome</td><td>自在；不拘束；在主场</td><td>She was completely at home talking to strangers at the reception.<br>在招待会上跟陌生人聊天，她一点都不拘束。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring home the ˈbacon (informal)</td><td>养家糊口；旗开得胜</td><td>He works two jobs to bring home the bacon for his family.<br>他打两份工养活一家人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring sth ˈhome to sb</td><td>使某人深切体会到（重要性或严重性）</td><td>The photographs really brought home to us how bad the flooding was.<br>那些照片让我们真切感受到洪水有多严重。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come ˈhome (to sb)</td><td>（使）完全明白；深刻意识到</td><td>It finally came home to me that I'd been wrong about her all along.<br>我终于彻底明白，自己一直都误会了她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drive/hammer sth ˈhome (to sb)</td><td>反复强调使人透彻理解</td><td>The coach hammered home the point that discipline matters more than talent.<br>教练反复强调，纪律比天赋更重要。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit/strike ˈhome</td><td>正中要害；说到点子上</td><td>Her comment about my laziness struck home and I said nothing.<br>她说我懒的那句话戳中要害，我一句也没回。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈhome bird</td><td>恋家的人；喜欢待在家的人</td><td>My brother travels constantly, but I've always been a home bird.<br>我哥老在外面跑，我却一直是个恋家的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌhome from ˈhome (BrE) (AmE a ˌhome away from ˈhome)</td><td>像家一样舒适自在的地方</td><td>That little café by the station has become a home from home for us.<br>车站旁那家小咖啡馆成了我们的第二个家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set up ˈhouse/ˈhome (with sb/together)</td><td>（与某人）安家；建立家庭</td><td>They set up home together in a tiny flat above a bakery.<br>他们在一家面包店楼上的小公寓里安了家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌhome ˈtruth</td><td>逆耳忠言；当面的实话</td><td>It's time somebody told him a few home truths about his behaviour.<br>该有人当面跟他说说他那些行为的实话了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈhome front</td><td>在家里；在国内</td><td>Business is fine, but on the home front things have been rather tense.<br>生意还行，但家里最近气氛挺紧张。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˌhome ˈstraight/ˈstretch</td><td>接近终点；即将完成</td><td>One more chapter and I'll be on the home straight with this thesis.<br>再写一章，这篇论文就进入最后冲刺了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do your ˈhomework (on sth)</td><td>事先做足功课；做好准备</td><td>She'd done her homework on the company and asked very sharp questions.<br>她事先把这家公司研究透了，问题问得非常犀利。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>honest to ˈGod/ˈgoodness</td><td>老天作证；确确实实</td><td>Honest to God, I had no idea the tickets were fake when I bought them.<br>我发誓，买票的时候真不知道那是假的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>honesty</b></td><td>in all ˈhonesty</td><td>老实说；说实在的</td><td>In all honesty, I never expected the film to be that good.<br>老实说，我真没想到这部电影会这么好看。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>honeymoon</b></td><td>a/the ˈhoneymoon period</td><td>蜜月期；最初的和谐时期</td><td>The new manager's honeymoon period ended the moment sales started falling.<br>销售一下滑，新经理的蜜月期就结束了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a point of ˈhonour</td><td>事关名誉的原则问题</td><td>It was a point of honour with him never to borrow money from friends.<br>从不向朋友借钱，是他的名誉底线。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sb an ˈhonour ◆ do sb the ˈhonour (of doing sth) (formal)</td><td>使某人感到荣幸；给某人带来荣誉</td><td>Would you do me the honour of opening our new library next month?<br>下个月能否有幸请您为我们的新图书馆揭幕？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have the ˈhonour of sth/of doing sth (formal)</td><td>有幸做某事</td><td>I had the honour of introducing her at the awards ceremony last night.<br>昨晚颁奖典礼上，我有幸为她做了介绍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(there is) honour among ˈthieves (saying)</td><td>盗亦有道</td><td>Neither of them told the police anything — there's honour among thieves.<br>两人都没向警方透露半句，果然盗亦有道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈhonour of sb/sth ◆ in sb's/sth's ˈhonour</td><td>为纪念；为向…致敬</td><td>The town held a concert in honour of the doctor who saved so many lives.<br>镇上办了一场音乐会，纪念那位救人无数的医生。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on your ˈhonour (old-fashioned)</td><td>以名誉担保</td><td>You're on your honour not to look at the answers before Friday.<br>你得以名誉担保，周五之前不偷看答案。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/feel ˌduty/ˌhonour ˈbound to do sth</td><td>有义务做某事；理应做某事</td><td>She felt honour bound to tell him what his brother had said.<br>她觉得自己有义务把他弟弟说的话告诉他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with full ˈhonours</td><td>以隆重礼仪；备极哀荣</td><td>The old soldier was buried with full honours in his home village.<br>那位老兵在故乡以隆重的礼仪下葬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do the ˈhonours (often humorous)</td><td>代主人尽礼（如斟酒、切蛋糕）</td><td>There's the cake and the knife — would you like to do the honours?<br>蛋糕和刀都在这儿了，要不你来代劳？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>honours are ˈeven (BrE)</td><td>不分上下；势均力敌</td><td>After two draws and a win each, honours are even between the teams.<br>两平一胜各半，两队算是打成平手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hoof</b></td><td>ˈhoof it (informal)</td><td>步行；徒步走</td><td>We missed the last bus and had to hoof it three miles home.<br>我们错过了末班车，只好走三英里回家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈhoof (BrE, informal)</td><td>匆忙地；顺便处理</td><td>He makes most of his decisions on the hoof between meetings.<br>他大多数决定都是在会与会之间匆匆做出的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hook</b></td><td>by ˌhook or by ˈcrook</td><td>想方设法；不择手段</td><td>By hook or by crook, we'll get these tickets before the show sells out.<br>无论如何，我们都要在票卖光前弄到票。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get sb off the ˈhook (informal)</td><td>使某人摆脱困境（或责任）</td><td>Her honest apology got him off the hook with the angry customer.<br>她诚恳地道了歉，让他从那位怒气冲冲的顾客手里脱了身。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hook, line and ˈsinker</td><td>完全地（相信或上当）</td><td>He swallowed the whole story hook, line and sinker without asking questions.<br>他一句没问，把那套说辞全盘信了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let sb off the ˈhook (informal)</td><td>放某人一马；让某人脱身</td><td>The teacher let us off the hook and moved the deadline to Monday.<br>老师放了我们一马，把截止日期挪到了周一。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hooks</b></td><td>get your ˈhooks into sb</td><td>控制某人；把某人牢牢抓住</td><td>Once that agency gets its hooks into you, it's hard to leave.<br>那家中介一旦把你抓住，就很难脱身了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not care/give a ˈhoot (about sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>毫不在乎</td><td>He doesn't give a hoot about what the neighbours think of his garden.<br>邻居怎么看他的花园，他压根不在乎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not care/give two ˈhoots (about sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>满不在乎；一点也不在意</td><td>She doesn't care two hoots about fashion and wears the same coat daily.<br>她对时尚毫不在意，天天穿同一件外套。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hope</b></td><td>be beyond ˈhope (of sth)</td><td>无可救药；毫无希望</td><td>The old car was beyond hope of repair, so we finally sold it.<br>那辆旧车已经修不好了，我们最后把它卖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold out little, etc. ˈhope (of sth/that...)</td><td>不抱多大希望</td><td>Doctors hold out little hope that he will walk again this year.<br>医生对他今年能重新走路不抱多大希望。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not hold out any, much, etc. ˈhope</td><td>不抱任何（或多大）希望</td><td>The rescue team didn't hold out much hope after the third night.<br>第三个夜晚过后，救援队已不抱多大希望。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hope against ˈhope (that...)</td><td>抱着一线希望；仍存幻想</td><td>We hoped against hope that the letter had simply been delayed.<br>我们抱着一线希望，觉得信只是寄晚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hope springs eˈternal (saying)</td><td>希望长存；人总心怀期待</td><td>He's failed the test four times, but hope springs eternal and he's booked again.<br>他考挂了四次，可希望不灭，又报了名。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I should ˈhope so/not ◆ so I should ˈhope</td><td>希望如此；但愿不会如此</td><td>You mean he apologized at last? I should hope so, after all that.<br>你是说他终于道歉了？闹成那样，本该如此。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have a ˌhope in ˈhell (informal)</td><td>毫无机会；根本没戏</td><td>Without a passport he doesn't have a hope in hell of boarding that flight.<br>没有护照，他根本别想登上那班飞机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not a ˈhope ◆ some ˈhope(s)! (BrE, spoken)</td><td>毫无希望；休想</td><td>Him tidying his room by himself? Some hope!<br>指望他自己收拾房间？做梦吧！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hopes</b></td><td>build up/raise sb's ˈhopes</td><td>使某人满怀希望</td><td>Don't raise her hopes until the hospital confirms the appointment.<br>医院确认预约之前，别让她抱太大希望。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dash/shatter sb's ˈhopes</td><td>使某人的希望破灭</td><td>One bad injury shattered his hopes of playing in the World Cup.<br>一次重伤，让他参加世界杯的希望彻底破灭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hopping</b></td><td>ˌhopping ˈmad (about/over sth) (informal)</td><td>暴跳如雷；气得跳脚</td><td>Mum was hopping mad about the mess we'd left in the kitchen.<br>我们把厨房弄得一团糟，妈妈气得跳脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>horizon</b></td><td>on the hoˈrizon</td><td>即将发生；已露端倪</td><td>With big layoffs on the horizon, nobody in the office feels safe.<br>大裁员在即，办公室里谁都不觉得安稳。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hornet</b></td><td>a ˈhornet's nest</td><td>马蜂窝；一大堆麻烦</td><td>His article about the mayor stirred up a real hornet's nest.<br>他那篇写市长的文章，真捅了马蜂窝。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>horns</b></td><td>draw/pull in your ˈhorns</td><td>收敛；缩减开支</td><td>After the bad quarter, the company pulled in its horns and stopped hiring.<br>业绩糟糕的一季度后，公司开始收敛，停止了招聘。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(on) the horns of a diˈlemma</td><td>进退两难</td><td>She was on the horns of a dilemma: take the job or finish her degree.<br>她左右为难：是接受这份工作，还是读完学位。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈbull by the horns</td><td>迎难而上；果断处理难题</td><td>He took the bull by the horns and asked his boss for a raise.<br>他鼓起勇气，直接向老板提了加薪。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>horror</b></td><td>ˌhorror of ˈhorrors (BrE, humorous or ironic)</td><td>（用于强调）糟糕透顶</td><td>And then, horror of horrors, I realized I'd left the tickets at home.<br>接着，天哪，我发现票落在家里了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>horse</b></td><td>(straight) from the horse's ˈmouth (informal)</td><td>（消息）直接来自当事人；可靠</td><td>I heard it straight from the horse's mouth — she's leaving in June.<br>我是从当事人那儿听来的，她六月就走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you can ˌtake/ˌlead a horse to ˌwater, but you ˌcan't make it ˈdrink (saying)</td><td>牛不喝水不能强按头</td><td>I've offered him lessons twice; you can lead a horse to water, but you can't make it drink.<br>我给他找了两次课，牛不喝水强按头也没用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>close/shut the stable ˈdoor after the horse has bolted</td><td>亡羊补牢；为时已晚</td><td>Installing an alarm now is shutting the stable door after the horse has bolted.<br>现在才装警报器，早就为时已晚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>change/swap horses in midˈstream</td><td>中途换将；中途改变计划</td><td>We're halfway through the build, so let's not change horses in midstream.<br>工程都盖到一半了，别在这时候临阵换人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold your ˈhorses (informal)</td><td>且慢；沉住气</td><td>Hold your horses — we haven't even read the contract yet.<br>别急，合同我们还没看呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>horses for ˈcourses (BrE)</td><td>知人善任；因事择人</td><td>Put Ana on the phones and Sam on design — horses for courses.<br>让安娜接电话，山姆做设计，各尽所长。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hostage</b></td><td>a ˌhostage to ˈfortune</td><td>可能招致后患的言行</td><td>Promising to cut taxes twice was a hostage to fortune he later regretted.<br>两度承诺减税成了后患，他后来很后悔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌhot off the ˈpress (informal)</td><td>刚印出来的；最新出炉的</td><td>These figures are hot off the press, so nobody else has seen them.<br>这些数据刚刚出炉，别人都还没见过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hot on sb's/sth's ˈtracks/ˈtrail (informal)</td><td>紧追不舍；即将追上</td><td>The detectives were hot on his trail by the time he reached the border.<br>他到边境时，警探已紧追不舍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a hot poˈtato (informal)</td><td>棘手问题；烫手山芋</td><td>School closures are a political hot potato nobody wants to touch.<br>关闭学校是个烫手山芋，没有政客愿碰。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈhot spot (informal)</td><td>热门去处；动乱地区</td><td>That street is the city's newest hot spot for live music.<br>那条街是全城最新的现场音乐热门去处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hot ˈstuff (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>了不起的人（或事物）；性感的人</td><td>Her first novel was hot stuff and sold out in a week.<br>她的第一部小说非常抢眼，一周就卖光了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hot under the ˈcollar (informal)</td><td>恼火；气恼不安</td><td>Dad gets hot under the collar whenever anyone mentions parking fines.<br>一提到停车罚单，爸爸就火冒三丈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in hot purˈsuit (of sb/sth)</td><td>紧追不舍</td><td>The thief ran off with two officers in hot pursuit down the alley.<br>小偷跑掉了，两名警察沿小巷紧追不舍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈhot seat (informal)</td><td>身处要职；面临质询</td><td>As the new head coach, he's in the hot seat from day one.<br>作为新任主教练，他从第一天起就如坐针毡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in hot ˈwater (informal)</td><td>陷入麻烦；惹上事</td><td>He landed in hot water after posting those photos online.<br>他把那些照片发到网上后惹上了麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make it ˈhot for sb (informal)</td><td>刁难某人；让某人不好过</td><td>The union threatened to make it hot for any manager who ignored the rules.<br>工会扬言要让任何无视规定的经理不好过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>more ˌtimes than sb has had hot ˈdinners (informal, often humorous)</td><td>次数多得数不清</td><td>I've told him to lock the gate more times than he's had hot dinners.<br>我叫他锁门的次数多得数都数不清。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not so/too ˈhot (informal)</td><td>不太好；不太舒服</td><td>I'm feeling not so hot today, so I'll skip the run.<br>我今天不太舒服，就不去跑步了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sell/go like ˈhot cakes (informal)</td><td>畅销；热卖</td><td>Those umbrellas sold like hot cakes the moment it started raining.<br>一下雨，那些伞立刻卖疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>too ˈhot for sb (also too hot to ˈhandle)</td><td>太棘手；难以应付</td><td>The story was too hot to handle, so the editor pulled it.<br>这条报道太烫手，编辑把它撤了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hotfoot</b></td><td>ˈhotfoot it (informal)</td><td>疾走；急忙赶去</td><td>He hotfooted it to the station and just caught the last train.<br>他一路飞奔到车站，刚好赶上末班车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hots</b></td><td>get/have the ˈhots for sb (informal)</td><td>对某人有强烈的情欲</td><td>Everyone can tell he's got the hots for the new barista.<br>谁都看得出他迷上了新来的咖啡师。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hour</b></td><td>at an unˌearthly/unˌgodly ˈhour (informal)</td><td>在极早（或极晚）的时刻</td><td>The builders started drilling at some unearthly hour this morning.<br>今天一大早，工人们就开始钻墙了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in your ˌhour of ˈneed (often humorous)</td><td>在急需帮助的时候</td><td>She lent me her car in my hour of need and never mentioned it again.<br>我最急的时候她把车借给我，之后再没提过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈhour/ˈhalf-hour</td><td>在整点（或半点）</td><td>Buses to the airport leave on the hour from stand four.<br>去机场的班车每逢整点从四号站台发车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a house of ˈcards</td><td>纸牌屋；不牢靠的计划</td><td>His plans collapsed like a house of cards when the scholarship fell through.<br>奖学金没拿到，他的计划顿时土崩瓦解。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>after ˈhours</td><td>在营业（或工作）时间以外</td><td>The staff sometimes stay for a drink after hours on Fridays.<br>周五下班后，员工有时会留下喝一杯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈall hours</td><td>随时；不分昼夜</td><td>Their neighbours play music at all hours and nobody dares complain.<br>他们邻居不分昼夜地放音乐，没人敢抱怨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈsmall/ˈearly hours (also the ˌwee (small) ˈhours)</td><td>深夜；凌晨</td><td>They sat talking in the kitchen into the small hours of the morning.<br>他们在厨房里一直聊到凌晨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>work all the ˈhours God sends (BrE, informal)</td><td>没日没夜地干活</td><td>He works all the hours God sends just to pay the mortgage.<br>为了还房贷，他没日没夜地干。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>till/until ˈall hours</td><td>直到深夜（或次日凌晨）</td><td>The students stayed up until all hours revising for their exams.<br>学生们复习备考，熬到了深更半夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not give sb/sth ˈhouseroom (BrE)</td><td>绝不要；根本看不上</td><td>That ugly old sofa? I wouldn't give it houseroom.<br>那张丑沙发？白送我也不要。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get on/along like a ˈhouse on fire (informal)</td><td>一见如故；相处极为融洽</td><td>My mother and my girlfriend got on like a house on fire at dinner.<br>晚饭时我妈和我女友一见如故。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a household ˈname/ˈword</td><td>家喻户晓的人（或名称）</td><td>Within two years the little brand had become a household name.<br>短短两年，这个小品牌就变得家喻户晓。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>houses</b></td><td>go all round the ˈhouses (BrE, informal)</td><td>绕圈子；拐弯抹角</td><td>Stop going all round the houses and tell me what you actually want.<br>别再绕圈子了，直说你到底想要什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>housetops</b></td><td>shout, etc. sth from the ˈhousetops/ˈrooftops (informal)</td><td>到处张扬；大肆宣扬</td><td>He was so proud of the news he wanted to shout it from the rooftops.<br>这消息让他得意极了，恨不得昭告天下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>how</b></td><td>how ˈcan/ˈcould you! (spoken)</td><td>你怎么能这样（表示不满或吃惊）</td><td>You told her about the surprise party? How could you!<br>你把惊喜派对的事告诉她了？你怎么能这样！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how ˈcome (...)? (spoken)</td><td>为什么；怎么会</td><td>How come you're already home when the meeting was at five?<br>会议五点开，你怎么这么早就回来了？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌhow do you ˈdo (becoming old-fashioned)</td><td>你好（初次见面的正式问候）</td><td>He shook my hand and said, "How do you do," very formally.<br>他握着我的手，很正式地说了句“您好”。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how's ˈthis/ˈthat for a...? (informal)</td><td>这（那）个怎么样</td><td>How's this for a bargain — two jackets for the price of one.<br>这算不算便宜：两件夹克只收一件的钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>huddle</b></td><td>get/go into a ˈhuddle (with sb)</td><td>（与某人）交头接耳；凑近密谈</td><td>The lawyers went into a huddle in the corner before answering the judge.<br>律师们先在角落里密谈了一阵，才回答法官。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hue</b></td><td>a ˌhue and ˈcry</td><td>强烈抗议；一片责难声</td><td>There was a hue and cry when the council announced the library would close.<br>议会宣布关闭图书馆时，引起一片强烈抗议。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>huff</b></td><td>ˌhuff and ˈpuff</td><td>气喘吁吁；虚张声势</td><td>He huffed and puffed all the way up the stairs with the suitcase.<br>他提着行李箱上楼，一路气喘吁吁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in a ˈhuff (informal)</td><td>怒气冲冲；气呼呼</td><td>She walked out of the meeting in a huff without saying goodbye.<br>她气呼呼地退出会议，连招呼都没打。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>human</b></td><td>the milk of human ˈkindness</td><td>人的善良天性；恻隐之心</td><td>He's not exactly overflowing with the milk of human kindness these days.<br>他这阵子可算不上有多少善心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hump</b></td><td>give sb/get the ˈhump (BrE, informal)</td><td>（使）恼火；生闷气</td><td>Don't tease him about his haircut or he'll get the hump.<br>别拿他的发型开玩笑，不然他要生气了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>over the ˈhump (informal)</td><td>渡过最艰难的阶段</td><td>Once the exams are finished we'll be over the hump for the year.<br>考完试，今年最难的一关就算过去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a hundred per ˈcent</td><td>百分之百；完全地</td><td>I agree with her a hundred per cent about closing the road.<br>关于封路的事，我百分之百同意她的看法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hunkers</b></td><td>on your ˈhunkers (BrE, informal)</td><td>蹲着</td><td>He was down on his hunkers, fixing the bicycle chain in the rain.<br>他蹲在地上，冒着雨修自行车链条。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hurry</b></td><td>in a ˈhurry to do sth</td><td>急于做某事；等不及</td><td>She's in no hurry to move out of her parents' comfortable house.<br>她一点也不急着从父母舒服的家里搬出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ice</b></td><td>ˌbreak the ˈice</td><td>打破僵局；缓和气氛</td><td>He told a silly joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.<br>会议一开始，他讲了个傻笑话来暖场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˈice-breaker</td><td>打破僵局的话（或活动）</td><td>James told a very funny story as an ice-breaker and everyone relaxed.<br>詹姆斯讲了个很好笑的故事暖场，大家都放松了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cut no ˈice (with sb)</td><td>（对某人）不起作用；无效</td><td>His excuses cut no ice with the head teacher at all.<br>他那些借口在校长面前一点用都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sth on ˈice</td><td>把…暂时搁置</td><td>We've put the extension on ice until the loan is approved.<br>贷款批下来之前，扩建的事先搁着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>iceberg</b></td><td>be the tip of the ˈiceberg</td><td>冰山一角</td><td>These complaints are just the tip of the iceberg, believe me.<br>信我，这些投诉不过是冰山一角。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>icing</b></td><td>the icing on the ˈcake</td><td>锦上添花</td><td>Winning was great, and meeting the coach was the icing on the cake.<br>赢了球已经很棒，见到教练更是锦上添花。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>idea</b></td><td>get the iˈdea (informal)</td><td>明白过来；听懂了</td><td>Watch me do it twice and you'll soon get the idea.<br>看我做两遍，你很快就明白了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have the ˈfaintest/ˈfoggiest/ˈslightest, etc. iˈdea</td><td>一无所知；毫无头绪</td><td>I haven't the faintest idea where she put the spare keys.<br>她把备用钥匙放哪儿了，我一点头绪也没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you have no iˈdea... (spoken)</td><td>你根本想象不到</td><td>You have no idea how cold it was standing on that platform.<br>你根本想象不到站在那个站台上有多冷。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the (very) iˈdea! (old-fashioned, spoken)</td><td>亏你想得出；真是的</td><td>Charging children for a glass of tap water — the very idea!<br>连自来水都要收孩子的钱，亏他们想得出！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run aˈway with the idea/notion (spoken)</td><td>轻率地相信；产生误解</td><td>Don't run away with the idea that this job is easy money.<br>别以为这份工作是轻松来钱，那是误会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈthat's an idea! (spoken)</td><td>好主意</td><td>Order pizza and watch the match here? That's an idea!<br>叫披萨在这儿看比赛？这主意不错！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈthat's the idea! (spoken)</td><td>对，就是这样；做得对</td><td>Keep your elbow down when you swing — that's the idea!<br>挥拍时手肘压低，对，就是这样！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ideas</b></td><td>give sb iˈdeas (also put iˈdeas in/into sb's head)</td><td>让某人想入非非</td><td>Don't tell him about the bonus; you'll only give him ideas.<br>别跟他提奖金的事，那只会让他想入非非。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>idle</b></td><td>if and ˈwhen</td><td>如果真的；倘若到时</td><td>We'll discuss the budget if and when the project is approved.<br>项目一旦获批，我们再谈预算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if ˈanything</td><td>要说有什么不同的话；倒不如说</td><td>The weather isn't better today; if anything, it's worse.<br>今天天气没变好，要说有变化，反倒更糟了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if ˌI were ˈyou</td><td>要是我是你的话（用于提建议）</td><td>If I were you, I'd apologize before she hears it from someone else.<br>要是我，我会在她从别人那儿听说之前先道歉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if ˈnot</td><td>不然；要不（表示不同意见）</td><td>Business is good for the builders, if not for everybody else.<br>对建筑商来说生意不错，虽然别人未必如此。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if ˈonly...</td><td>要是…就好了</td><td>If only we had booked the tickets a week earlier.<br>要是我们早一周订票就好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ifs</b></td><td>ˌifs and/or ˈbuts</td><td>种种借口；这样那样的条件</td><td>I want the report on Monday, with no ifs and buts.<br>报告周一交，别跟我讲条件找借口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ignorance</b></td><td>ignorance is ˈbliss (saying)</td><td>无知是福；不知者不烦</td><td>She never reads the news before bed — ignorance is bliss.<br>她睡前从不看新闻，眼不见心不烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>impression</b></td><td>anything/nothing/something ˈin it for sb</td><td>对某人有（或没有）好处</td><td>I'll help with the move if there's something in it for me.<br>要是对我也有点好处，我就帮忙搬家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈin at sth</td><td>在场目睹；参与其中</td><td>She was in at the start of the company and still owns shares.<br>公司创立时她就在场，现在还持有股份。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈin for sth</td><td>即将经历（不愉快的事）</td><td>If you think the exam was hard, you're in for a shock next term.<br>你要觉得这次考试难，下学期还有得受呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈin for it (BrE also be ˈfor it) (informal)</td><td>要倒霉了；要挨罚了</td><td>You're in for it when Mum sees what happened to the carpet.<br>等妈妈看到地毯变成这样，你可要倒霉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get ˈin on sth (informal)</td><td>参与；知情</td><td>Everyone in the office was in on the plan except the birthday girl.<br>除了寿星本人，办公室里人人都知道这个计划。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/keep (well) ˈin with sb (informal)</td><td>与某人搞好关系（图好处）</td><td>He keeps well in with the boss by remembering everyone's birthday.<br>他记得每个人的生日，借此跟老板搞好关系。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in and ˈout (of sth)</td><td>进进出出；时常出入</td><td>The kids were in and out of the kitchen all afternoon looking for snacks.<br>孩子们整个下午在厨房进进出出找零食。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈin that (written)</td><td>因为；在于</td><td>The plan is risky in that it depends entirely on good weather.<br>这个计划有风险，因为它完全靠天气好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>industry</b></td><td>a ˌcaptain of ˈindustry</td><td>实业界巨头</td><td>The dinner was full of politicians and captains of industry.<br>那场晚宴上尽是政客和实业界大佬。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>influence</b></td><td>under the ˈinfluence</td><td>酒后（驾车）；醉酒</td><td>He lost his licence for driving under the influence last winter.<br>去年冬天他因醉驾被吊销了驾照。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>information</b></td><td>for your inforˈmation</td><td>供参考；需要说明的是</td><td>For your information, that meeting was cancelled two days ago.<br>提醒你一句，那个会两天前就取消了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>initiative</b></td><td>(do sth) on your own iˈnitiative</td><td>主动（做某事）；自作主张</td><td>She rewrote the whole proposal on her own initiative over the weekend.<br>周末她主动把整份方案重写了一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the iˈnitiative</td><td>采取主动；率先行动</td><td>Someone had to take the initiative, so I called the landlord myself.<br>总得有人主动，于是我自己给房东打了电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>injury</b></td><td>do sb/yourself an ˈinjury (often humorous)</td><td>弄伤某人（或自己）</td><td>Be careful with that ladder or you'll do yourself an injury.<br>小心那梯子，不然你要弄伤自己了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ink</b></td><td>much ˌink has been ˈspilled (on/over sth)</td><td>关于某事已有大量论述</td><td>Much ink has been spilled over whether the painting is genuine.<br>关于这幅画是否真迹，已有大量文章讨论。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>inner</b></td><td>the ˌinner ˈman/ˈwoman</td><td>内心；心灵；食欲</td><td>A long walk and a hot meal did wonders for the inner man.<br>走一趟长路再吃顿热饭，整个人从里到外舒服了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>innings</b></td><td>a good ˈinnings (BrE, informal)</td><td>享得高寿；干得够久了</td><td>He died at ninety-four, so he'd had a good innings.<br>他九十四岁去世，也算是享尽天年了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>inroads</b></td><td>make ˈinroads in/into sth</td><td>大量消耗；取得进展</td><td>The repairs made serious inroads into our holiday savings.<br>这些维修费大大侵蚀了我们的度假存款。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>inside</b></td><td>inside ˈout</td><td>里面朝外；彻底地</td><td>You've got your jumper on inside out again.<br>你的毛衣又穿反了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the inˈside</td><td>在内部；掌握内情</td><td>Someone on the inside must have told the press about the merger.<br>一定是内部有人把合并的事透给了媒体。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>instance</b></td><td>for ˈinstance</td><td>例如；比如</td><td>Take a cheap hobby, for instance running, and you'll save money.<br>找个便宜的爱好，比如跑步，就能省钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>instant</b></td><td>not for a/one ˈmoment/ˈinstant</td><td>一点也不；决不</td><td>I never for one instant doubted that she would come back.<br>我从未有一刻怀疑过她会回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>intents</b></td><td>to all intents and ˈpurposes (BrE) (AmE for all intents and ˈpurposes)</td><td>实际上；几乎完全</td><td>To all intents and purposes the deal was finished before lunch.<br>实际上这笔交易午饭前就谈成了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>interest</b></td><td>in the interest(s) of sth</td><td>为了；出于…的考虑</td><td>In the interests of safety, please keep the aisle clear.<br>为了安全起见，请保持通道畅通。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay sth back/return sth with ˈinterest</td><td>加倍回报（或报复）</td><td>They beat us last year and we returned the favour with interest.<br>去年他们赢了我们，今年我们加倍奉还。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>interests</b></td><td>have sb's (best) interests at ˈheart</td><td>真心为某人着想</td><td>Your parents nag because they have your best interests at heart.<br>父母唠叨，是因为真心为你着想。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>interference</b></td><td>run interˈference (AmE, informal)</td><td>为某人挡事；替某人开道</td><td>My assistant runs interference so I can finish the report in peace.<br>助理帮我挡下杂事，我才能安心写完报告。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>interim</b></td><td>in the ˈinterim</td><td>在此期间</td><td>The new manager starts in May; in the interim, Sara is in charge.<br>新经理五月上任，在此期间由萨拉负责。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>intervals</b></td><td>at (...) ˈintervals</td><td>每隔…时间；不时</td><td>Buses run at ten-minute intervals until the evening rush ends.<br>晚高峰结束前，公交车每十分钟一班。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>into</b></td><td>be ˈinto sb for sth (AmE, informal)</td><td>欠某人（钱）</td><td>He's into his brother for two thousand dollars already.<br>他已经欠他哥两千美元了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈinto sth (informal)</td><td>热衷于；对…很感兴趣</td><td>My sister is really into rock climbing these days.<br>我妹妹最近特别迷攀岩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>necessity is the mother of inˈvention (saying)</td><td>需要乃发明之母</td><td>He built a stove out of tin cans — necessity is the mother of invention.<br>他用铁罐子做了个炉子，需要真是发明之母。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in inverted ˈcommas (spoken)</td><td>所谓的（表示质疑）</td><td>His so-called friend, in inverted commas, never once visited him.<br>他那位“朋友”，加个引号，一次都没来看过他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>invitation</b></td><td>an iron ˈfist/ˈhand (in a velvet ˈglove)</td><td>外柔内刚；笑里藏刀</td><td>She runs the department with an iron fist in a velvet glove.<br>她管这个部门是绵里藏针，柔中带硬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have many/several irons in the ˈfire</td><td>同时进行多项计划</td><td>He's not worried about the rejection; he has plenty of irons in the fire.<br>被拒他并不担心，他手上还有不少别的路子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈissue</td><td>争论中的；关键所在的</td><td>What's at issue here is whether he was honest, not whether he was clever.<br>这里的关键是他是否诚实，而不是他聪不聪明。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make an ˈissue of/out of sth</td><td>小题大做；揪住不放</td><td>Who broke it doesn't matter; let's not make an issue out of it.<br>谁弄坏的不重要，咱们别揪着这事不放。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈissue with sb (about/on/over sth)</td><td>与某人争辩；表示异议</td><td>I must take issue with you over your description of that evening.<br>你对那天晚上的描述，我不得不提出异议。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>item</b></td><td>be an ˈitem (informal)</td><td>是一对（恋人）</td><td>Are those two an item, or just close friends?<br>他俩是在谈恋爱，还是只是好朋友？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>itself</b></td><td>be ˌpatience, ˌhonesty, simˌplicity, etc. itˈself</td><td>极有耐心（诚实、朴素等）</td><td>The nurse was patience itself with the frightened little boy.<br>那位护士对受惊的小男孩极有耐心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ivory</b></td><td>an ˌivory ˈtower (disapproving)</td><td>象牙塔；脱离现实之地</td><td>Come down from your ivory tower and talk to the people who use the system.<br>从象牙塔里下来，跟真正用这套系统的人聊聊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jack</b></td><td>a ˌJack the ˈLad (BrE, slang)</td><td>浪荡小子；吊儿郎当的年轻人</td><td>He was a bit of a Jack the Lad at twenty, always out until dawn.<br>他二十岁时挺浪荡的，老是玩到天亮。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jack</b></td><td>a jack of ˈall trades</td><td>万金油；样样通样样松</td><td>As a jack of all trades, he can fix the roof but not the wiring properly.<br>他是个万金油，屋顶能修，电路就不行了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jam</b></td><td>be in a ˈjam (informal)</td><td>陷入困境</td><td>I'm in a bit of a jam — could you lend me twenty pounds?<br>我有点周转不开，能借我二十镑吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jam on the ˈbrake(s) ◆ jam the ˈbrake(s) on</td><td>猛踩刹车</td><td>A dog ran out and he jammed on the brakes just in time.<br>一条狗窜出来，他及时猛踩了刹车。</td></tr>
