<tr><td></td><td>jam toˈmorrow (BrE, informal)</td><td>许而不予的好处；画饼充饥</td><td>Every year the boss promises jam tomorrow and nothing ever changes.<br>老板年年画大饼，什么都没变过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jaw</b></td><td>your ˈjaw drops</td><td>惊得目瞪口呆</td><td>Her jaw dropped when she saw the price on the tag.<br>她看到吊牌上的价格，惊得下巴都快掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈjaw-dropping</td><td>令人瞠目结舌的</td><td>Taking the desert road at night was a jaw-dropping experience.<br>夜里走那条沙漠公路是一次让人瞠目的经历。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jaws</b></td><td>the jaws of ˈdeath, deˈfeat, etc. (literary)</td><td>鬼门关；失败的边缘</td><td>The goalkeeper snatched victory from the jaws of defeat in the last minute.<br>守门员在最后一分钟把败局扳成了胜局。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jazz</b></td><td>and all that ˈjazz (spoken, informal)</td><td>诸如此类；等等</td><td>We had to fill in forms, show passports and all that jazz.<br>我们得填表、出示护照，诸如此类。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jekyll</b></td><td>a ˌJekyll and ˈHyde</td><td>双重人格的人</td><td>He's a Jekyll and Hyde: charming at parties, impossible at home.<br>他有双重人格：聚会上迷人，在家却难以相处。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jelly</b></td><td>be/feel like ˈjelly (also turn to ˈjelly)</td><td>（腿）发软；紧张得站不稳</td><td>My legs turned to jelly the moment I stepped onto the stage.<br>一走上舞台，我的腿就软了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jest</b></td><td>in ˈjest</td><td>开玩笑地</td><td>He said it in jest, but she took the remark seriously.<br>他是开玩笑说的，她却当了真。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jet</b></td><td>the ˈjet set</td><td>常乘飞机四处玩乐的富豪一族</td><td>The little island became a playground for the jet set in the sixties.<br>六十年代，这座小岛成了富豪一族的游乐场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jewel</b></td><td>the jewel in the ˈcrown</td><td>王冠上的明珠；最珍贵的部分</td><td>The old library is the jewel in the crown of this university.<br>这座老图书馆是这所大学的镇校之宝。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jitters</b></td><td>get/have the ˈjitters (informal)</td><td>紧张不安；焦躁</td><td>I always get the jitters the night before a big interview.<br>重要面试前一晚，我总是紧张得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>job</b></td><td>a ˌJob's ˈcomforter (old-fashioned)</td><td>越安慰越添愁的人</td><td>Don't ask him for sympathy; he's a real Job's comforter.<br>别指望他安慰你，他越劝你越难受。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the patience of a ˈsaint/of ˈJob</td><td>极大的耐心</td><td>Teaching that class needs the patience of a saint.<br>教那个班需要极大的耐心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>job</b></td><td>do a good, bad, etc. ˈjob (on sth) ◆ make a good, bad, etc. ˈjob of sth</td><td>（把某事）做得好（或差等）</td><td>The painters did a lovely job on the front of the house.<br>油漆工把房子正面刷得非常漂亮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do the ˈjob/ˈtrick (informal)</td><td>管用；奏效</td><td>A bit of tape should do the trick until you buy a new one.<br>你买新的之前，贴点胶带应该就管用了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/sth up as a bad ˈjob (informal)</td><td>对…不再抱希望；放弃</td><td>After three hours we gave the old printer up as a bad job.<br>折腾了三小时，我们放弃了那台旧打印机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>good ˈjob! (AmE, spoken)</td><td>干得好</td><td>Good job! You finished the whole wall by yourself.<br>干得漂亮！你一个人把整面墙弄完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(it's) a good job/thing (that)... (spoken)</td><td>幸好；好在</td><td>It's a good job you brought an umbrella, because it's pouring.<br>幸好你带了伞，外面下大了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(and) a ˌgood job/thing ˈtoo (spoken)</td><td>这样才好；太好了</td><td>They've banned cars from the square, and a good job too.<br>广场禁止通车了，这样才对。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a job of ˈwork (BrE, old-fashioned or formal)</td><td>一件正经活儿；分内的工作</td><td>Clearing that garden was a real job of work for two people.<br>清理那个花园，对两个人来说真是不小的活儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>more than your ˈjob's worth (to do sth) (BrE, spoken)</td><td>违反规定会丢饭碗</td><td>It's more than my job's worth to let you in without a pass.<br>没有通行证放你进去，我这饭碗可保不住。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jobs</b></td><td>jobs for the ˈboys (BrE, informal, disapproving)</td><td>给亲信安排的肥缺</td><td>Three of his cousins got contracts — pure jobs for the boys.<br>他三个表亲都拿到了合同，纯粹是安插亲信。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>joe</b></td><td>Joe ˈBloggs (BrE)</td><td>张三李四；普通老百姓</td><td>What does this tax cut really mean to Joe Bloggs and his family?<br>这项减税对普通老百姓一家到底意味着什么？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Joe ˈPublic (BrE) (AmE John Q. ˈPublic) (informal)</td><td>普通民众；一般公众</td><td>Joe Public doesn't care who designed the bridge, only that it works.<br>老百姓不在乎桥是谁设计的，能用就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jog sb's ˈmemory</td><td>唤起某人的记忆</td><td>Here's a photograph of you two — maybe it'll jog your memory.<br>这是你俩的合影，也许能帮你想起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>joined</b></td><td>joined at the ˈhip</td><td>形影不离</td><td>She and Scott were joined at the hip all evening.<br>整个晚上她和斯科特形影不离。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>joint</b></td><td>out of ˈjoint</td><td>脱臼；失序，不正常</td><td>He put his shoulder out of joint reaching for the top shelf.<br>他去够顶层架子，把肩膀弄脱臼了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>joke</b></td><td>be/get/go beyond a ˈjoke</td><td>过分了；不是闹着玩的</td><td>Being two hours late every day has gone beyond a joke.<br>天天迟到两小时，这已经不是开玩笑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be no ˈjoke</td><td>不是轻松的事；很不容易</td><td>It's no joke living on such a small income in this city.<br>在这座城市靠这点收入过日子可不轻松。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the joke's on ˈsb (informal)</td><td>反被自己捉弄了</td><td>He hid my keys, but the joke's on him — they were his own.<br>他藏了我的钥匙，结果笑话闹到自己头上，那是他自己的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈjoke of sth</td><td>拿（正经事）开玩笑</td><td>Stop making a joke of your health and see a doctor.<br>别拿身体开玩笑了，去看医生吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a ˈjoke</td><td>开得起玩笑</td><td>He's a good boss because he can take a joke about himself.<br>他是个好老板，因为拿他开玩笑他也不介意。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>joker</b></td><td>the joker in the ˈpack</td><td>难以捉摸的人；不可预料的因素</td><td>The weather is the joker in the pack for Saturday's race.<br>天气是周六比赛中最难预料的因素。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>joking</b></td><td>joking aˈpart/aˈside (BrE)</td><td>言归正传；说正经的</td><td>Joking apart, we really do need to fix that roof before winter.<br>说正经的，入冬前我们真得把屋顶修好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you're ˈjoking ◆ you must be ˈjoking (spoken)</td><td>你开玩笑吧；别逗了</td><td>The boss wants us to work Sunday too? You must be joking.<br>老板要我们周日也上班？别逗了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jolly</b></td><td>jolly ˈgood! (old-fashioned, BrE, spoken)</td><td>太棒了；好极了</td><td>You've finished the whole report already? Jolly good!<br>报告全写完了？太棒了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈjolly well (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>（表示生气）当然；就该</td><td>You made the mess, so you can jolly well clean it up.<br>是你弄乱的，就该你收拾。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>joneses</b></td><td>keep up with the ˈJoneses (informal, disapproving)</td><td>与邻里攀比；比阔气</td><td>They bought a second car just to keep up with the Joneses.<br>他们又买了辆车，纯粹是跟邻居攀比。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jot</b></td><td>not one/a ˈjot (or ˈtittle) (informal)</td><td>一点也没有；丝毫不</td><td>His attitude hasn't changed one jot since last year.<br>他的态度和去年比丝毫没变。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>joy</b></td><td>(get/have) no ˈjoy (from sb) (informal)</td><td>无功而返；没有结果</td><td>I asked the airline for a refund but got no joy from them.<br>我向航空公司要退款，结果什么也没要到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>judge</b></td><td>don't judge a ˌbook by its ˈcover (saying)</td><td>勿以貌取人</td><td>The café looks shabby, but don't judge a book by its cover.<br>这家咖啡馆看着破旧，可别以貌取人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>juggling</b></td><td>a ˌbalancing/ˌjuggling ˈact</td><td>需要兼顾多方的难事</td><td>Raising twins while studying is a constant juggling act.<br>一边带双胞胎一边读书，得时时刻刻两头兼顾。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jugular</b></td><td>go for the ˈjugular (informal)</td><td>直击要害；穷追猛打</td><td>In the debate she went for the jugular and asked about his expenses.<br>辩论中她直击要害，追问他的开销问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jump</b></td><td>be/stay one jump aˈhead (of sb/sth)</td><td>领先一步；抢先一着</td><td>Good sellers stay one jump ahead of what customers will want next.<br>好的销售总能比顾客的需求抢先一步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go (and) jump in a/the ˈlake (spoken)</td><td>走开；一边儿去</td><td>When he asked to borrow money again, I told him to go jump in a lake.<br>他又来借钱，我叫他一边儿去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jump down sb's ˈthroat (informal)</td><td>对某人发火；猛烈回击</td><td>I only asked a simple question and she jumped down my throat.<br>我只是问了个简单问题，她就冲我发火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jump the ˈgun (informal)</td><td>抢跑；操之过急</td><td>Don't jump the gun and book the hall before the date is confirmed.<br>日期没定下来就订场地，别操之过急。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jump the ˈlights (informal)</td><td>闯红灯</td><td>He jumped the lights at the crossroads and nearly hit a cyclist.<br>他在路口闯了红灯，差点撞到骑车人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jump out of your ˈskin (informal)</td><td>吓一大跳</td><td>I nearly jumped out of my skin when the balloon burst behind me.<br>身后气球一炸，我差点吓得跳起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jump the ˈqueue (BrE) (AmE jump the ˈline, cut in ˈline)</td><td>插队；加塞儿</td><td>That man just jumped the queue and everyone started complaining.<br>那人插了队，大家都开始抱怨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈjump the shark (AmE)</td><td>由盛转衰；开始走下坡路</td><td>The show jumped the shark when they added a talking dog.<br>剧里加了条会说话的狗，这剧就开始走下坡路了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jump ˈship</td><td>擅自离船；中途跳槽</td><td>Two of our best engineers jumped ship just before the launch.<br>产品发布前，我们两位最好的工程师跳了槽。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jump through ˈhoops</td><td>经受层层刁难；费尽周折</td><td>We had to jump through hoops to get the building permit approved.<br>为拿到建筑许可，我们费尽了周折。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>jump ˈto it (AmE also hop ˈto it) (informal)</td><td>赶快；马上行动</td><td>The train leaves in ten minutes, so jump to it!<br>火车十分钟后开，快点动起来！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jury</b></td><td>the jury is/are (still) ˈout (on sth)</td><td>尚无定论；悬而未决</td><td>The jury is still out on whether the new timetable actually helps.<br>新时刻表到底有没有用，现在还很难说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>just</b></td><td>could/might just as ˈwell</td><td>还不如；倒不如</td><td>The bus takes an hour, so we might just as well walk there.<br>坐车要一小时，我们还不如走过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>just aˈbout (informal)</td><td>几乎；差不多</td><td>I've just about finished packing, give me five more minutes.<br>我行李差不多收拾好了，再给我五分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>just like ˈthat</td><td>就这样；冷不防地</td><td>He handed in his notice and walked out, just like that.<br>他递了辞呈就走人，说走就走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>just a ˈminute/ˈmoment/ˈsecond (informal)</td><td>稍等一下</td><td>Just a second — I'll check whether we still have your size.<br>稍等一下，我看看还有没有你的尺码。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>just ˈnow</td><td>此刻；刚才</td><td>I can't talk just now; can I call you back after lunch?<br>我这会儿没空，午饭后回你电话行吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>just ˈso</td><td>井井有条；一丝不苟</td><td>Her desk is always just so, with every pen in its place.<br>她的桌子永远整整齐齐，每支笔都归位。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>just ˈthen</td><td>就在那时</td><td>I was about to leave, and just then the phone rang.<br>我正要出门，就在那时电话响了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not just ˈyet</td><td>现在还不；暂时还没</td><td>We're not moving house just yet, but probably in the spring.<br>我们暂时还不搬家，大概春天吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's just ˈit (also that's just the ˈtrouble)</td><td>问题就在这儿</td><td>That's just it — nobody told the neighbours about the roadworks.<br>问题就在这儿，谁都没通知邻居要修路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>justice</b></td><td>bring sb to ˈjustice</td><td>将某人绳之以法</td><td>The family waited twenty years to see the killer brought to justice.<br>这家人等了二十年，才见凶手被绳之以法。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do justice to ˈsb/ˈsth ◆ do sb/sth ˈjustice</td><td>公正评价；充分展现</td><td>These photos don't do the mountains justice at all.<br>这些照片完全拍不出那些山的气势。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do yourself ˈjustice</td><td>充分发挥自己的水平</td><td>He was too nervous in the interview to do himself justice.<br>面试时他太紧张，没能发挥出真实水平。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keen</b></td><td>(as) keen as ˈmustard (BrE, informal)</td><td>非常热心；干劲十足</td><td>The new intern is as keen as mustard and arrives before everyone.<br>新来的实习生干劲十足，总是最早到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep</b></td><td>ˌkeep sb ˈgoing (informal)</td><td>使某人支撑下去</td><td>A sandwich at noon should keep you going until dinner.<br>中午吃个三明治，撑到晚饭应该没问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌkeep it ˈup</td><td>坚持下去；继续努力</td><td>You've lost five kilos already — keep it up!<br>你已经瘦了五公斤，继续保持！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌkeep sth to yourˈself</td><td>对某事保密</td><td>I'll tell you the news, but please keep it to yourself for now.<br>我告诉你这消息，但暂时请你保密。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep yourˌself to yourˈself</td><td>离群索居；不与人来往</td><td>The old man next door keeps himself to himself and rarely speaks.<br>隔壁的老人独来独往，很少说话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keeping</b></td><td>in sb's ˈkeeping</td><td>由某人保管（或照料）</td><td>The documents are in my lawyer's keeping until the sale is complete.<br>交易完成前，这些文件由我的律师保管。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈkeeping (with sth)</td><td>与…协调一致</td><td>The new windows are in keeping with the rest of the old house.<br>新窗户和这栋老房子的其余部分很协调。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of ˈkeeping (with sth)</td><td>与…不协调；不相称</td><td>That glass tower is completely out of keeping with the old square.<br>那座玻璃塔楼与老广场极不协调。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keeps</b></td><td>for ˈkeeps (informal)</td><td>永远地；长久地</td><td>Take the bike — it's yours for keeps.<br>这车拿去吧，永远归你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ken</b></td><td>beyond/outside your ˈken (old-fashioned)</td><td>超出某人的理解范围</td><td>How the software actually works is completely beyond my ken.<br>这软件到底怎么运作，我完全搞不懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>key</b></td><td>under ˌlock and ˈkey</td><td>妥善锁藏；被关押</td><td>The paintings are kept under lock and key in the basement.<br>那些画锁在地下室里妥善保管。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kibosh</b></td><td>put the ˈkibosh on sth (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>阻止某事；使泡汤</td><td>The storm put the kibosh on our plans for a beach barbecue.<br>暴风雨让我们的海滩烧烤计划泡了汤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kick</b></td><td>get a ˈkick from/out of sth (informal)</td><td>从某事中获得乐趣（或刺激）</td><td>She gets a real kick out of teaching kids to swim.<br>教孩子游泳让她特别有成就感。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌkick against the ˈpricks</td><td>以卵击石；徒劳反抗</td><td>Complaining to head office is just kicking against the pricks.<br>向总部抱怨不过是以卵击石。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick (some/sb's) ˈass/ˈbutt (slang, AmE)</td><td>狠揍某人；表现强势</td><td>Our team went out there and kicked butt in the second half.<br>下半场我们队上场后打得非常凶猛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick the ˈbucket (BrE, informal or humorous)</td><td>翘辫子；死</td><td>He joked that he'd sell the boat before he kicked the bucket.<br>他开玩笑说，翘辫子前要把船卖掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick the ˈhabit, ˈdrug, ˈbooze, etc.</td><td>戒掉（恶习、毒品、酒等）</td><td>It took him two years to kick the habit for good.<br>他花了两年才彻底把这毛病戒掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick your ˈheels (BrE, informal)</td><td>无所事事地干等</td><td>I kicked my heels at the airport for four hours waiting for him.<br>我在机场干等了他四个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick sb in the ˈteeth (informal)</td><td>在困难时打击某人</td><td>Cutting her hours after all that overtime really kicked her in the teeth.<br>加了那么多班还砍她工时，真是狠狠打击了她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick sth into the long ˈgrass (BrE)</td><td>束之高阁；拖着不办</td><td>The council kicked the parking plan into the long grass again.<br>议会又把停车方案束之高阁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick sth into ˈtouch (BrE)</td><td>搁置不理；放弃某事</td><td>They kicked the whole proposal into touch after the first vote.<br>第一轮表决后，他们就把整个提案搁下了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌkick over the ˈtraces (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>不服管束；开始放纵</td><td>At eighteen he kicked over the traces and moved to the city.<br>十八岁那年他挣脱管束，搬去了城里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick the ˈtyres (BrE) (AmE kick the ˈtires)</td><td>验货；检验某物是否合适</td><td>Before signing, let's kick the tyres on this software for a week.<br>签约前，我们先把这软件试用一周看看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈtyrekicker (BrE) (AmE a ˈtirekicker)</td><td>只看不买的顾客</td><td>Most people at the car lot on Sundays are just tyrekickers.<br>周日来车行的人多半只看不买。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a kick up the ˈbackside (also a kick in the ˈpants) (informal)</td><td>鞭策；当头棒喝</td><td>That bad review was the kick up the backside he needed.<br>那篇差评正是他需要的当头一棒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick up a ˈfuss, ˈrow, etc. (informal)</td><td>大吵大闹；小题大做</td><td>She kicked up a fuss when the waiter brought the wrong bill.<br>服务员拿错账单，她大吵了一通。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick up your ˈheels (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>尽情玩乐；放松一下</td><td>After exams we all went out to kick up our heels downtown.<br>考完试我们都进城好好玩了一场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌkick sb upˈstairs (informal)</td><td>明升暗降</td><td>They kicked him upstairs to a title with no real power.<br>他们把他明升暗降，给了个没实权的头衔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>kick sb when they're ˈdown</td><td>落井下石；乘人之危</td><td>Mocking her after the layoff is just kicking someone when they're down.<br>她被裁了还嘲笑她，纯属落井下石。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈkick yourself (informal)</td><td>懊悔不已；自责</td><td>I could kick myself for not writing down her number.<br>没记下她的号码，我真想抽自己一巴掌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat/knock/kick the ˈhell out of sb/sth (informal)</td><td>狠揍；把…打得稀烂</td><td>The storm knocked the hell out of the fence along the back garden.<br>暴风雨把后花园的围栏打得稀烂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kicks</b></td><td>for ˈkicks (informal)</td><td>为了寻刺激；图个好玩</td><td>Some bored teenagers around here break windows and steal signs just for kicks.<br>这一带有些无聊的青少年砸玻璃、偷路牌纯粹是为了找刺激。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kid</b></td><td>handle, treat, etc. sb with kid ˈgloves</td><td>小心翼翼地对待某人</td><td>You'll have to handle the new client with kid gloves at first.<br>一开始你得小心翼翼地对待这位新客户。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like a kid in a ˈcandy store/shop (AmE)</td><td>兴奋得像进了糖果店的孩子</td><td>At the tool sale he was like a kid in a candy store.<br>在工具特卖会上，他兴奋得像个进了糖果店的孩子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kidding</b></td><td>no ˈkidding (spoken)</td><td>真的；可不是嘛</td><td>No kidding, I saw her win the whole tournament last year.<br>真的，我去年亲眼看她拿了整个锦标赛冠军。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you're ˈkidding ◆ you must be ˈkidding</td><td>你开玩笑吧；不会吧</td><td>They cancelled the flight again? You must be kidding.<br>航班又取消了？不会吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kids</b></td><td>ˈkids' stuff (BrE) (AmE ˈkid stuff)</td><td>小儿科；轻而易举的事</td><td>For a climber like her, that route is kids' stuff.<br>对她这样的攀岩者，那条线路简直是小儿科。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kill</b></td><td>ˌkill the fatted ˈcalf</td><td>设宴款待；隆重迎接归来的人</td><td>When their son came back from abroad, they killed the fatted calf.<br>儿子从国外回来，他们摆宴接风。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kilter</b></td><td>out of ˈkilter</td><td>失调；不正常</td><td>My sleep has been out of kilter since the trip to Japan.<br>自从去了日本，我的作息就一直乱着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kind</b></td><td>in ˈkind</td><td>以实物支付；以同样方式</td><td>The farmer paid the workers partly in kind, with milk and eggs.<br>农场主部分用牛奶和鸡蛋抵付工钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nothing of the ˈkind/ˈsort (informal)</td><td>完全不是那么回事</td><td>He said I'd agreed, but I did nothing of the kind.<br>他说我同意了，我根本没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of a ˈkind</td><td>同一类的；彼此相似的</td><td>Those two are very much of a kind — stubborn and generous.<br>这两人是一路货色：又倔又大方。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of a ˈkind/ˈsort (disapproving)</td><td>徒有其名的；勉强算得上的</td><td>They gave us a meal of a kind, mostly cold potatoes.<br>他们给了顿所谓的饭，主要是冷土豆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one of a ˈkind</td><td>独一无二</td><td>My grandmother's ring is one of a kind and can't be replaced.<br>奶奶的戒指独一无二，没法再配一个。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>something of the/that ˈkind/ˈsort</td><td>诸如此类的事；类似的东西</td><td>He mentioned a merger or something of the kind at lunch.<br>午饭时他提到合并之类的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kindly</b></td><td>look ˈkindly on/upon sb/sth (formal)</td><td>赞同；认可</td><td>The committee did not look kindly on our late application.<br>委员会对我们迟交的申请并不认可。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not take ˈkindly to sb/sth</td><td>不喜欢；难以接受</td><td>He doesn't take kindly to being told how to run his kitchen.<br>别人教他怎么管厨房，他很不高兴。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>king</b></td><td>a ˌking's ˈransom</td><td>一笔巨款</td><td>That little painting sold for a king's ransom at auction.<br>那幅小画在拍卖会上卖了一大笔钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kingdom</b></td><td>blow, send, etc. sb to kingdom ˈcome</td><td>把某人送上西天</td><td>One spark near that tank could blow us all to kingdom come.<br>那个油罐旁边一点火星就能把我们全送上西天。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kiss</b></td><td>ˌkiss and ˈtell</td><td>（为钱）泄露与名人的私情</td><td>She refused to kiss and tell, even when the papers offered money.<br>即便报社出钱，她也不肯把私情抖出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌkiss sth ˈbetter (spoken)</td><td>亲一亲就不疼了</td><td>Come here and let Mummy kiss your knee better.<br>过来，妈妈亲亲你的膝盖就不疼了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the kiss of ˈdeath (informal, often humorous)</td><td>死亡之吻；看似有利实则致命</td><td>His public support was the kiss of death for the candidate.<br>他的公开支持成了那位候选人的催命符。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the kiss of ˈlife (BrE)</td><td>口对口人工呼吸；起死回生之举</td><td>A lifeguard gave the boy the kiss of life on the beach.<br>一名救生员在沙滩上给男孩做了人工呼吸。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kit</b></td><td>get your ˈkit off (BrE, slang)</td><td>脱光衣服</td><td>The lads dared him to get his kit off and jump in the river.<br>几个小伙起哄让他脱光跳进河里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kitchen</b></td><td>everything but/bar the kitchen ˈsink (informal, humorous)</td><td>什么都带上；一大堆东西</td><td>For a two-day trip she packed everything but the kitchen sink.<br>才去两天，她却把家当都带上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kite</b></td><td>fly a ˈkite</td><td>试探反应；放试探气球</td><td>The minister flew a kite about raising the tax to see the reaction.<br>部长放风说要加税，试探各方反应。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kith</b></td><td>kith and ˈkin (old-fashioned)</td><td>亲友；亲朋</td><td>He left the village and all his kith and kin behind.<br>他离开了村子，也离开了所有亲友。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>kittens</b></td><td>have ˈkittens (BrE, informal)</td><td>焦虑不安；急得团团转</td><td>Mum was having kittens because we hadn't called all evening.<br>我们一晚上没打电话，妈妈急得团团转。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knee-high</b></td><td>knee-high to a ˈgrasshopper (informal, humorous)</td><td>（孩子）小不点儿；很小的时候</td><td>I've known Tom since he was knee-high to a grasshopper.<br>汤姆还是个小不点儿时我就认识他了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knees</b></td><td>bring sb to their ˈknees</td><td>使某人屈服；彻底击败某人</td><td>Two years of strikes brought the company to its knees.<br>两年的罢工让这家公司彻底屈服。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring sth to its ˈknees</td><td>使（组织等）瘫痪</td><td>The cyber attack brought the whole rail network to its knees.<br>那次网络攻击让整个铁路系统陷入瘫痪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your/sb's ˈknees are knocking (informal)</td><td>吓得双腿发抖</td><td>My knees were knocking as I walked up to give my speech.<br>上台演讲时，我腿肚子直打颤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on your ˈknees</td><td>跪着；筋疲力尽</td><td>He was on his knees in the garden pulling out weeds.<br>他跪在花园里拔草。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knickers</b></td><td>get/have your ˈknickers in a twist (BrE, informal)</td><td>慌乱；恼火</td><td>Don't get your knickers in a twist — the train is only ten minutes late.<br>别慌，火车才晚点十分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/have your ˈpanties in a knot (AmE, informal)</td><td>为小事着急上火</td><td>He got his panties in a knot over a tiny spelling mistake.<br>为一个小拼写错误，他就急得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knife</b></td><td>get your ˈknife into sb ◆ have your ˈknife in sb</td><td>跟某人过不去；屡屡刁难</td><td>The supervisor has had her knife in him since the argument.<br>自从那次争吵，主管就一直跟他过不去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go under the ˈknife (informal)</td><td>接受手术</td><td>She goes under the knife on Thursday for her shoulder.<br>她周四要做肩膀手术。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like a knife through ˈbutter</td><td>轻而易举；势如破竹</td><td>The new saw went through the log like a knife through butter.<br>这把新锯子切木头像切黄油一样轻松。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/stick the ˈknife in (BrE, informal)</td><td>故意伤人；落井下石</td><td>He waited until the meeting to put the knife in about my figures.<br>他专等开会时，拿我的数据狠狠捅了我一刀。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn/twist the ˈknife (in the wound)</td><td>往伤口上撒盐</td><td>Mentioning his ex at dinner really twisted the knife.<br>晚饭时提起他前妻，真是往他伤口上撒盐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you could cut the atmosphere with a ˈknife</td><td>气氛紧张得让人窒息</td><td>After the argument you could cut the atmosphere with a knife.<br>那场争吵之后，气氛紧张得让人窒息。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knife-edge</b></td><td>on a ˈknife-edge (also on a ˈrazor's edge)</td><td>处于危险（或难以预料）的境地</td><td>The whole election is on a knife-edge with two seats left.<br>只剩两个席位，整场选举悬在刀刃上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knifepoint</b></td><td>at ˈknifepoint</td><td>在刀子威胁下</td><td>The driver was robbed at knifepoint outside the station.<br>司机在车站外被人持刀抢劫。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knight</b></td><td>a knight in shining ˈarmour (BrE) (AmE a knight in shining ˈarmor) (usually humorous)</td><td>救人于危难的侠士；救星</td><td>My neighbour arrived like a knight in shining armour with jump leads.<br>邻居像救星一样，拿着搭电线赶来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌwhite ˈknight</td><td>白衣骑士；及时相助者</td><td>A white knight bought the failing bookshop and saved every job.<br>一位白衣骑士买下濒临倒闭的书店，保住了所有工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knit</b></td><td>knit your ˈbrows</td><td>皱眉（表示困惑或不快）</td><td>She knitted her brows as she read the strange letter again.<br>她又读了一遍那封奇怪的信，眉头紧锁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knives</b></td><td>the knives are ˈout (for sb)</td><td>（对某人）磨刀霍霍；群起而攻</td><td>After the third defeat, the knives are out for the manager.<br>三连败之后，众人对主教练磨刀霍霍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knobs</b></td><td>with ˈknobs on (BrE, slang)</td><td>有过之而无不及</td><td>It's the same old plan with knobs on, just a new name.<br>还是那套老计划，只是变本加厉换了个名。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knock</b></td><td>knock sb ˈdead (spoken)</td><td>使某人倾倒；令人惊艳</td><td>Wear the blue dress tonight — you'll knock them dead.<br>今晚穿那条蓝裙子，保证惊艳全场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>knock sb/sth into a cocked ˈhat (BrE)</td><td>远远胜过；使相形见绌</td><td>Her homemade bread knocks the supermarket stuff into a cocked hat.<br>她自己烤的面包把超市卖的比得一无是处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>knock it ˈoff! (spoken)</td><td>别闹了；住手</td><td>Knock it off, you two, I'm trying to work in here.<br>你俩别闹了，我这儿还在干活呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>knock sb off their ˈperch/ˈpedestal</td><td>把某人拉下神坛；灭某人威风</td><td>One bad season knocked the champion off his pedestal.<br>一个糟糕的赛季就把这位冠军拉下了神坛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>knock sth on the ˈhead (BrE, informal)</td><td>叫停某事；使泡汤</td><td>Let's knock the whole idea on the head before we waste more money.<br>趁没再浪费钱，咱们把这想法叫停吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>knock sb ˈsideways (informal)</td><td>使某人震惊得不知所措</td><td>The news of the closure knocked us all sideways.<br>关闭的消息让我们都懵了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>knock ˈspots off sb/sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>远胜过；使相形见绌</td><td>Her homemade pizza knocks spots off anything you can buy frozen.<br>她自己做的比萨比冷冻的强太多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>knock the ˈstuffing out of sb (informal)</td><td>挫某人锐气；使某人元气大伤</td><td>Losing the final really knocked the stuffing out of the whole team.<br>输掉决赛让整支队伍元气大伤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a (hard, nasty, etc.) ˈknock</td><td>遭受挫折；受到沉重打击</td><td>His confidence took a nasty knock after the interview went badly.<br>面试搞砸后，他的自信心受了重创。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knocked</b></td><td>you could have knocked me, etc. down with a ˈfeather</td><td>（表示极度惊讶）真让人大吃一惊</td><td>When she said she was quitting, you could have knocked me down with a feather.<br>她说要辞职时，我惊得半天说不出话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with a ˈfeather (informal)</td><td>（表示惊讶）令人大跌眼镜</td><td>You could have knocked him down with a feather when the prize was announced.<br>宣布获奖名单时，他惊得目瞪口呆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know</b></td><td>before you know where you ˈare</td><td>转眼间；瞬息之间</td><td>Start chatting online and before you know where you are it's two in the morning.<br>一上网聊天，转眼就到凌晨两点了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be not to ˈknow</td><td>无从知道；并不知情</td><td>Don't blame him for the mix-up—he wasn't to know the meeting had moved.<br>别怪他弄错了，他哪知道会议改期了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for all ˈI, ˈyou, etc. know (spoken)</td><td>（强调不知情）说不定；亦未可知</td><td>For all I know, she could be living in Australia by now.<br>说不定她现在已经住在澳大利亚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈknow (informal)</td><td>知道内情；熟悉内幕</td><td>People in the know say the factory will close before Christmas.<br>知情人士说这家工厂圣诞节前就要关门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it takes one to ˈknow one (informal, disapproving)</td><td>半斤八两；五十步笑百步</td><td>You're calling me lazy? Well, it takes one to know one.<br>你说我懒？彼此彼此吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know sb/sth ˈbackwards (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>对…了如指掌；背得滚瓜烂熟</td><td>She's played that part so often she knows the script backwards.<br>这个角色她演过太多次，剧本早已倒背如流。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know ˈbest</td><td>最懂得该怎么做；比谁都明白</td><td>Fine, do it your way—you always know best, apparently.<br>行，照你的来，反正你总是最懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know ˈbetter (than that/than to do sth)</td><td>明白事理；不至于糊涂到…</td><td>At your age you should know better than to believe every ad you see.<br>你这个岁数了，不该轻信每条广告。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know sb by ˈsight</td><td>与某人面熟；只认得脸</td><td>I know the man next door by sight, but we've never actually spoken.<br>隔壁那位我脸熟，但从没说过话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know ˈdifferent/ˈotherwise (informal)</td><td>知道并非如此；掌握的情况不同</td><td>He claims he was home all evening, but the neighbours know different.<br>他说自己整晚在家，邻居可知道不是这么回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know sb/sth inside ˈout (informal)</td><td>对…极为熟悉；了如指掌</td><td>After twenty years here, she knows this old building inside out.<br>在这儿待了二十年，这栋老楼她了如指掌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know sth like the back of your ˈhand (informal)</td><td>对…了如指掌；如数家珍</td><td>Ask the taxi driver—he knows these back streets like the back of his hand.<br>问司机吧，这些小巷他闭着眼都认得。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know no ˈbounds</td><td>无限；没有止境</td><td>When the baby finally arrived, their joy knew no bounds.<br>孩子终于降生，他们喜不自胜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know your own ˈmind</td><td>有主见；知道自己要什么</td><td>She's only sixteen, but she certainly knows her own mind.<br>她才十六岁，主意可正得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know your ˈplace</td><td>有自知之明；守本分</td><td>In those days a junior clerk was expected to know his place.<br>那年头，小职员得知道自己几斤几两。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know the ˈscore (informal)</td><td>了解实情；知道真相</td><td>Don't sugar-coat it—I've worked here long enough to know the score.<br>别粉饰了，我在这儿干这么久，什么情况都清楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know your ˈstuff (informal)</td><td>精通业务；很内行</td><td>Watch the way she fixes that engine—she really knows her stuff.<br>看她修发动机的手法，真是行家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know a thing or two (about sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>对…很在行；见多识广</td><td>Ask Grandad about roses—he knows a thing or two about growing them.<br>养玫瑰的事问爷爷，他挺有一套。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know your way aˈbout/aˈround (sth)</td><td>熟门熟路；熟悉情况</td><td>Give me a week and I'll know my way around the new office.<br>给我一周，我就熟悉新办公室了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know what it is to be/do sth</td><td>亲身经历过；深知其中滋味</td><td>She grew up poor, so she knows what it is to go hungry.<br>她穷苦出身，深知挨饿是什么滋味。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know what you're ˈdoing/aˈbout (informal)</td><td>有经验；老练在行</td><td>Relax, let him carry the ladder—he knows what he's doing.<br>放心让他扛梯子，他有经验。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know what you're ˈtalking about (informal)</td><td>熟知此事；作经验之谈</td><td>Listen to her on childcare—she's raised four kids and knows what she's talking about.<br>育儿的事听她的，她带大四个孩子，都是经验之谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know what's ˈgood for you</td><td>知道好歹；懂得趋利避害</td><td>You'll apologize to the boss tomorrow, if you know what's good for you.<br>你要是识相，明天就去跟老板道歉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know what's ˈwhat (informal)</td><td>是内行；有鉴别能力</td><td>Take the old mechanic with you—he knows what's what about used cars.<br>带上那位老技工，二手车的门道他门儿清。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know where you ˈare/ˈstand</td><td>知道自己的处境（或地位）</td><td>Just tell me straight, so at least I know where I stand.<br>直说吧，好歹让我知道自己是什么处境。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know where you're ˈgoing</td><td>目标明确；有清楚的追求</td><td>She's only twenty-two, but she clearly knows where she's going.<br>她才二十二岁，可目标非常清楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>know which side your ˈbread is buttered</td><td>知道利益所在；善于为自己打算</td><td>He never argues with the boss—he knows which side his bread is buttered.<br>他从不跟老板顶嘴，知道好处在哪边。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let sb ˈknow</td><td>告诉某人；通知某人</td><td>Let me know as soon as the delivery arrives at the shop.<br>货一到店里就通知我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know any ˈbetter</td><td>（因缺乏教养而）举止无礼</td><td>He grabbed the last cake without asking—he just doesn't know any better.<br>他没问就抓走最后一块蛋糕，实在是没教养。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know you're ˈborn (BrE, spoken)</td><td>身在福中不知福</td><td>Kids today with their heating and hot water don't know they're born.<br>如今的孩子有暖气有热水，身在福中不知福。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know your ˌarse from your ˈelbow (BrE)</td><td>蠢笨至极；什么都不懂</td><td>Don't let him wire the lamp—he doesn't know his arse from his elbow.<br>别让他接灯线，他啥也不懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(AmE not know your ˌass from your ˈelbow) (△, slang)</td><td>愚蠢之极；屁都不懂</td><td>The new manager doesn't know his ass from his elbow about scheduling.<br>新经理排班的事一窍不通。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know ˈbeans about sth (AmE, informal)</td><td>对…一窍不通；完全不懂行</td><td>I don't know beans about fixing cars, so I called a mechanic.<br>我修车一窍不通，就叫了技工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know the first thing aˈbout sb/sth</td><td>对…一无所知</td><td>He doesn't know the first thing about babies, yet he's giving advice.<br>他对带孩子一无所知，还在那儿指点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know sb from ˈAdam (informal)</td><td>根本不认识某人</td><td>A man waved at me in the street, but I didn't know him from Adam.<br>街上有人朝我挥手，我压根不认识他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know the ˈmeaning of the word (disapproving)</td><td>根本不懂；毫无这种概念</td><td>Patience? My brother doesn't know the meaning of the word.<br>耐心？我弟弟压根不知道这两个字怎么写。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know what ˈhit you (informal)</td><td>惊呆了；不知所措</td><td>The tackle came so fast the poor kid didn't know what hit him.<br>那一下铲球太快，那孩子完全懵了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know what you're ˈmissing</td><td>不知道错过了多好的事</td><td>You've never tried snorkelling? You don't know what you're missing.<br>你没浮潜过？你真是错过太多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know what to ˈdo with yourself</td><td>不知如何打发时间</td><td>With the kids away for a week, she didn't know what to do with herself.<br>孩子走了一周，她都不知道怎么打发时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know whether you're ˈcoming or ˈgoing</td><td>忙得晕头转向；理不清头绪</td><td>Between the new baby and the move, I don't know whether I'm coming or going.<br>又添了孩子又搬家，我忙得晕头转向。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know whether to ˈlaugh or ˈcry</td><td>哭笑不得</td><td>When the cake collapsed, I didn't know whether to laugh or cry.<br>蛋糕塌了的时候，我真是哭笑不得。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know which way/where to ˈlook</td><td>尴尬得不知所措；狼狈不堪</td><td>When he started singing in the restaurant, I didn't know where to look.<br>他在餐厅里唱起歌来，我尴尬得没处躲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know which way/where to ˈturn</td><td>（困境中）不知如何是好</td><td>After losing the job and the flat, he didn't know which way to turn.<br>丢了工作又丢了房子，他不知道该怎么办。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(well) what do you ˈknow (about ˈthat)?</td><td>（表示惊讶）真没想到</td><td>She passed the test first time—well, what do you know about that!<br>她一次就考过了，真没想到！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(informal) what do you ˈknow</td><td>（表示惊讶）你看，真没想到</td><td>And what do you know, the missing keys were in my coat pocket.<br>你猜怎么着，丢的钥匙就在我大衣口袋里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you ˈknow (informal) (1 used when you are thinking of what to say)</td><td>（考虑接着说什么时）嗯，那个</td><td>It was, you know, one of those days when nothing goes right.<br>就是那种，嗯，什么都不顺的日子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you know as well as ˈI do</td><td>（说服他人时）你我都清楚</td><td>You know as well as I do that he never returns anything he borrows.<br>你我都清楚，他借东西从不还。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you know ˈwho/ˈwhat (spoken)</td><td>（不点名）你知道是谁（或什么）</td><td>Careful what you say—you know who is standing right behind you.<br>说话当心，你知道谁就站在你后面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you never ˈknow (with sb/sth)</td><td>很难说；很难预料</td><td>Take an umbrella—you never know with the weather in April.<br>带把伞吧，四月的天气说不准。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you never ˈknow with him</td><td>他这人叫人捉摸不透</td><td>You never know with him; one day he's smiling and the next he ignores everyone.<br>他叫人捉摸不透，今天笑脸相迎，明天谁都不理。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knowing</b></td><td>there's no ˈknowing/ˈsaying/ˈtelling...</td><td>难以预料；无从知道</td><td>There's no knowing how long the repairs will take once they open the wall.<br>墙一拆开，修多久谁也说不准。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knowledge</b></td><td>be common/public ˈknowledge</td><td>尽人皆知；是公开的事</td><td>It's common knowledge in the office that the two of them are dating.<br>他们俩在谈恋爱，办公室里人尽皆知。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come to sb's ˈknowledge (formal)</td><td>为某人所知；被某人获悉</td><td>It has come to my knowledge that several files were removed last night.<br>我获悉昨晚有几份档案被人拿走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to your ˈknowledge</td><td>据某人所知</td><td>To my knowledge, nobody has ever complained about the noise before.<br>据我所知，从没人抱怨过噪音。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the best of your belief/knowledge</td><td>据某人所知（或所信）</td><td>To the best of my knowledge, the shop closes at six on Saturdays.<br>据我所知，这家店周六六点关门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a working knowledge of sth</td><td>对…有实用的了解；能应付日常使用</td><td>You'll need a working knowledge of Spanish to handle calls from Madrid.<br>接马德里的电话，你得会点日常西班牙语。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>known</b></td><td>let it be ˈknown/make it ˈknown that...</td><td>（设法让人）得知某事</td><td>The manager let it be known that late arrivals would no longer be tolerated.<br>经理放话出来，以后迟到概不容忍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make yourself ˈknown to sb</td><td>向某人作自我介绍</td><td>If you arrive early, make yourself known to the woman at the desk.<br>你要是早到，就先跟前台那位女士报个到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knows</b></td><td>God/goodness/Heaven knows (spoken)</td><td>天知道；谁知道呢</td><td>God knows why he painted the kitchen bright orange.<br>天知道他为什么把厨房刷成亮橙色。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(Some people may find the use of God knows offensive.)</td><td>（有人觉得此用法冒犯）</td><td>Some people may find the use of God knows offensive, so choose your words carefully.<br>有人会觉得这种说法冒犯，用词要留心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>knuckles</b></td><td>give sb, get, etc. a rap over the knuckles</td><td>斥责某人；受到申斥</td><td>The reporter got a rap over the knuckles for printing the family's address.<br>那记者因登出这家人的地址挨了训。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>labour</b></td><td>a ˌlabour of ˈlove</td><td>乐在其中的苦差；心甘情愿做的事</td><td>Restoring that old motorbike was a labour of love that took him three years.<br>修复那辆老摩托是他甘之如饴的苦差，干了三年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>labour the ˈpoint</td><td>反复解释；一再重复已明白的事</td><td>I don't want to labour the point, but we really cannot afford this.<br>我不想啰嗦，可我们真的负担不起。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ladder</b></td><td>(at) the top of the tree/ladder</td><td>处于顶层；居于最高位</td><td>After thirty years she finally reached the top of the tree in publishing.<br>干了三十年，她终于站上了出版界的顶端。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ladies</b></td><td>a ˈladies' ˈman</td><td>讨女人喜欢的男子；爱与女人厮混的男子</td><td>My uncle was a ladies' man in his youth and never missed a dance.<br>我叔叔年轻时是个情场高手，逢舞会必到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lager</b></td><td>a ˈlager lout (BrE)</td><td>酗酒闹事的年轻男子</td><td>The seaside town is tired of lager louts wrecking the place every summer.<br>这座海滨小城受够了每年夏天来撒酒疯的年轻人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lam</b></td><td>on the ˈlam (AmE, informal)</td><td>在逃；逃匿</td><td>The pair have been on the lam since the bank job last spring.<br>自去年春天抢银行后，这两人一直在逃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lamb</b></td><td>be mutton dressed (up) as lamb</td><td>老来俏；装嫩</td><td>She thinks that miniskirt suits her, but it's mutton dressed up as lamb.<br>她觉得那条超短裙很衬她，其实是老来俏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌlame ˈduck (informal)</td><td>跛脚鸭；处境艰难的人（或机构）</td><td>The government refused to keep pouring money into a lame duck airline.<br>政府拒绝继续给这家难以为继的航空公司砸钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>land</b></td><td>in the land of the ˈliving (humorous)</td><td>活着；在世</td><td>You're finally up? Good to see you back in the land of the living.<br>你总算起床了？欢迎回到人间。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˌland of ˈNod (old-fashioned, humorous)</td><td>在梦乡；睡着了</td><td>By nine o'clock both children were safely in the land of Nod.<br>九点钟，两个孩子都已进了梦乡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>land a ˈblow, ˈpunch, etc.</td><td>击中；打中对方</td><td>He barely landed a punch before the referee stopped the fight.<br>裁判叫停之前，他几乎没打中一拳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the land of ˌmilk and ˈhoney</td><td>富饶的乐土；丰裕之地</td><td>Their grandparents crossed the ocean expecting a land of milk and honey.<br>他们的祖辈漂洋过海，指望找到一片乐土。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see, etc. how the ˈland lies (BrE)</td><td>摸清形势；弄清情况</td><td>Let's have coffee with her first and see how the land lies.<br>先跟她喝杯咖啡，摸摸情况再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>landscape</b></td><td>a blot on the landscape</td><td>大煞风景的东西</td><td>That concrete car park is a real blot on the landscape here.<br>那座水泥停车场在这儿实在大煞风景。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>language</b></td><td>mind/watch your ˈlanguage</td><td>注意言辞；说话文明点</td><td>Watch your language—there are small children in the next room.<br>说话注意点，隔壁屋里有小孩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>speak/talk the same/a different ˈlanguage</td><td>谈得来（或谈不来）；有无共同语言</td><td>The engineers and the designers simply don't speak the same language.<br>工程师和设计师根本说不到一块儿去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lap</b></td><td>drop/dump sth in sb's ˈlap (informal)</td><td>把某事推给某人负责</td><td>He dumped the whole budget mess in my lap and went on holiday.<br>他把整摊预算烂事丢给我，自己度假去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>drop/fall into sb's ˈlap (informal)</td><td>轻易到手；从天上掉下来</td><td>A job like that doesn't just fall into your lap—you have to chase it.<br>这种工作不会从天上掉下来，得自己去争取。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the lap of the ˈgods</td><td>听天由命；非人力所能左右</td><td>We've done all we can; the result is in the lap of the gods now.<br>我们能做的都做了，结果就听天由命吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the lap of ˈluxury</td><td>生活优裕；养尊处优</td><td>He grew up in the lap of luxury and has never washed a dish.<br>他从小锦衣玉食，连碗都没洗过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the last lap</td><td>最后阶段；最后一圈</td><td>We're on the last lap of the project, so hang on for another week.<br>项目进入最后阶段了，再撑一周。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>large</b></td><td>at ˈlarge</td><td>（用于名词后）整体而言；一般大众</td><td>The proposal is popular with staff but society at large remains unconvinced.<br>这项提议员工欢迎，但整个社会仍不买账。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by and ˈlarge (informal)</td><td>大体上；总的说来</td><td>By and large, the new timetable has made the commute much easier.<br>总的来说，新时刻表让通勤轻松多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈlarge part • in ˌno small ˈpart (formal)</td><td>在很大程度上</td><td>The team's success is in large part due to their new goalkeeper.<br>球队的成功在很大程度上归功于新门将。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) large as ˈlife (humorous)</td><td>本人赫然在场；千真万确</td><td>I turned the corner and there he was, as large as life, selling flowers.<br>我一拐弯，他就赫然站在那儿卖花。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>larger</b></td><td>larger than ˈlife</td><td>超乎寻常；个性张扬</td><td>Her father was a larger than life character who filled any room he entered.<br>她父亲是个气场十足的人，走到哪儿都是焦点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lark</b></td><td>be ˌup/ˌrise with the ˈlark</td><td>一大早就起床；鸡鸣即起</td><td>Farmers here are up with the lark, even in the middle of winter.<br>这里的农民天不亮就起，隆冬也不例外。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>last</b></td><td>at (long) ˈlast</td><td>终于；最终</td><td>At long last the builders finished and we could move back in.<br>工人们总算完工，我们可以搬回去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at the last ˈcount</td><td>据最新统计；最新消息说</td><td>At the last count, over three hundred people had signed the petition.<br>据最新统计，已有三百多人在请愿书上签名。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at the last ˈminute/ˈmoment</td><td>在最后一刻；踩着点儿</td><td>She cancelled at the last minute and left us one player short.<br>她最后一刻取消，害我们少了一个人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the day, week, month, etc. before ˈlast</td><td>前天；上上周；上上月</td><td>I saw him at the market the week before last, looking perfectly well.<br>上上周我在市场见过他，气色好得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>every last...</td><td>每一个；全部</td><td>They ate every last crumb of the cake before I got home.<br>我到家前，蛋糕被他们吃得一点渣都不剩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have the last ˈlaugh (informal)</td><td>笑到最后；最终获胜</td><td>They mocked her little shop, but she had the last laugh when it expanded.<br>他们嘲笑她那家小店，可她最后笑到了最后。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have the last ˈword</td><td>作最后决定；说最后一句话</td><td>She always has to have the last word in an argument.<br>吵架时她总要说最后一句才罢休。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>last but not ˈleast • last but by no means ˈleast</td><td>最后但同样重要的是</td><td>Last but not least, I want to thank the volunteers who cooked for us.<br>最后但同样重要的，感谢为我们做饭的志愿者。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the last I ˈheard (spoken)</td><td>据我最后听到的消息</td><td>The last I heard, they were still living somewhere near Leeds.<br>我最后听说，他们还住在利兹附近。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>last ˈin, first ˈout</td><td>后进先出（裁员时最晚来的最先走）</td><td>The factory is cutting staff on a last in, first out basis.<br>工厂按后进先出的原则裁员。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌlast ˈword (in sth)</td><td>最新最先进的（事物）</td><td>This kitchen is the last word in gadgets, but nobody ever cooks here.<br>这厨房里的电器最先进，可从来没人做饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on your/its ˌlast ˈlegs</td><td>行将垮掉；奄奄一息</td><td>That old washing machine is on its last legs and floods the floor weekly.<br>那台旧洗衣机快散架了，每周都漏一地水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to/till the ˈlast</td><td>直到最后；直至死亡</td><td>He defended his brother's name to the last, even in court.<br>他至死都在维护弟弟的名声，连在法庭上也是。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>last-ditch</b></td><td>a ˌlast-ditch ˈstand/atˈtempt/ˈeffort</td><td>最后的努力；最后一搏</td><td>In a last-ditch attempt to save the shop, they started selling online.<br>为救下这家店，他们最后一搏，开始网上卖货。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>latch</b></td><td>on the ˈlatch (BrE)</td><td>（门）虚掩着未上锁</td><td>I'll leave the back door on the latch so you can get in.<br>我把后门虚掩着，你自己进来就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>late</b></td><td>late in the ˈday (disapproving)</td><td>为时已晚；错过时机</td><td>It's a bit late in the day to complain about the design now.<br>现在才抱怨设计，未免太迟了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>late of... (formal)</td><td>不久前在…工作（或居住）</td><td>The speaker was Dr Grant, late of the university's biology department.<br>演讲人是格兰特博士，不久前还在该校生物系任职。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of ˈlate (formal)</td><td>最近；近来</td><td>He has been noticeably quieter of late, which worries his mother.<br>他近来明显话少了，他母亲很担心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>later</b></td><td>later ˈon (informal)</td><td>后来；过些时候</td><td>Finish your homework now and we can watch a film later on.<br>先写完作业，过会儿我们看电影。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lather</b></td><td>get into a ˈlather • work yourself into a ˈlather</td><td>焦躁不安；急得团团转</td><td>Don't work yourself into a lather over one late email.<br>别为一封迟到的邮件急得团团转。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈlather (BrE, informal)</td><td>（不必要的）焦躁；恼火</td><td>He got into a right lather when the taxi failed to turn up.<br>出租车没来，他急得直冒火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in a ˈlather (BrE, informal)</td><td>紧张不安；激动恼火</td><td>She was in a lather about the inspection all weekend.<br>整个周末她都为检查的事紧张得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>don't make me ˈlaugh (spoken)</td><td>别逗了；别让我笑掉大牙</td><td>Him, run a marathon? Don't make me laugh.<br>他？跑马拉松？别逗了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for a ˈlaugh • for ˈlaughs</td><td>为了好玩；开个玩笑</td><td>They swapped name badges just for a laugh at the conference.<br>在会上他们换了胸牌，纯粹图个乐子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a (good) ˈlaugh (about sth)</td><td>觉得有趣；开怀一笑</td><td>We still have a good laugh about the day the tent blew away.<br>帐篷被风刮跑那天的事，我们至今笑个不停。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>laugh all the way to the ˈbank (informal)</td><td>大赚一笔；数钱数到手软</td><td>The critics hated the film, but the producers laughed all the way to the bank.<br>影评人骂惨了这部片，制片方却赚得盆满钵满。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈlaughing stock</td><td>笑柄；被人取笑的对象</td><td>Wearing this to the party would make me a laughing stock.<br>穿这个去派对我会成为笑柄的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no laughing ˈmatter</td><td>不是闹着玩的事；严肃的事</td><td>Losing your passport abroad is no laughing matter.<br>在国外弄丢护照可不是闹着玩的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>laughs</b></td><td>a barrel/bundle of ˈlaughs (informal, often ironic)</td><td>非常有趣的人（或事）</td><td>Three hours of safety training—what a barrel of laughs that was.<br>三小时安全培训，可真是「有趣」极了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>he who laughs last laughs ˈlongest (saying)</td><td>谁笑到最后谁笑得最好</td><td>They mocked his savings plan, but he who laughs last laughs longest.<br>他们笑话他的储蓄计划，可谁笑到最后谁笑得最好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>laurels</b></td><td>look to your ˈlaurels</td><td>谨防被人超越；力保荣誉</td><td>With that new bakery opening, the old shop must look to its laurels.<br>新面包店一开，老店可得当心自己的地位了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>law</b></td><td>go to ˈlaw (BrE)</td><td>诉诸法律；打官司</td><td>Rather than argue for months, they decided to go to law.<br>与其吵上几个月，他们决定打官司。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have the ˈlaw on sb (BrE, informal)</td><td>（常用作威胁）告发某人</td><td>Touch my fence again and I'll have the law on you.<br>再碰我的篱笆，我就报警告你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>law and ˈorder</td><td>法治；社会治安</td><td>The mayor promised to restore law and order in the town centre.<br>市长承诺恢复市中心的治安。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌlaw of ˈaverages</td><td>平均律；概率使然</td><td>By the law of averages, this team has to win a match eventually.<br>按概率算，这支队总该赢一场了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌlaw of the ˈjungle</td><td>丛林法则；弱肉强食</td><td>In that industry it's the law of the jungle—only the ruthless survive.<br>那个行业奉行丛林法则，只有狠角色能活下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a law unto himˈself, herˈself, etc.</td><td>我行我素的人；独断专行的人</td><td>The old caretaker is a law unto himself and ignores every memo.<br>老看门人我行我素，什么通知都不理。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a person who does what they want</td><td>独断专行的人；我行我素的人</td><td>She is a person who does what they want, whatever the rules say.<br>她是个我行我素的人，规矩管不住她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the law into your own ˈhands</td><td>私自处置；擅自治罪</td><td>When the police did nothing, the villagers took the law into their own hands.<br>警察不管，村民就自己动手处置了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no ˈlaw against sth (spoken)</td><td>这又不犯法；谁也管不着</td><td>I'm singing in my own garden—there's no law against it.<br>我在自家院子唱歌，又不犯法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lay</b></td><td>lay sth at sb's ˈdoor (formal)</td><td>把…归咎于某人</td><td>The failure of the merger was laid at the chairman's door.<br>合并失败的责任被归到了董事长头上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay sth ˈbare</td><td>揭露；暴露（隐情）</td><td>The diary lays bare the loneliness he hid from everyone.<br>这本日记揭示了他瞒着所有人的孤独。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay ˈclaim to sth</td><td>声称对…拥有权利</td><td>Two families now lay claim to the same patch of farmland.<br>两家人如今都声称这块农地归自己。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay down your ˈarms</td><td>放下武器；停止作战</td><td>The rebels agreed to lay down their arms in return for an amnesty.<br>叛军同意放下武器，换取特赦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay down the ˈlaw (informal, disapproving)</td><td>发号施令；指手画脚</td><td>He walked in and started laying down the law about parking spaces.<br>他一进来就对停车位的事发号施令。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay down your ˈlife (for sb/sth) (literary)</td><td>献身；捐躯</td><td>Thousands laid down their lives for a country they barely knew.<br>成千上万的人为一个他们几乎不了解的国家献出了生命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay an ˈegg (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>彻底失败；砸锅</td><td>His opening joke laid an egg and the room went silent.<br>他开场的笑话砸了锅，全场鸦雀无声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay a ˈfinger on sb (informal)</td><td>（常用于否定句）动某人一根手指头</td><td>If you lay a finger on my little brother, you'll answer to me.<br>你敢动我弟弟一根手指头，我跟你没完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay it on ˈthick/with a ˈtrowel (also pile it on ˈthick, pile it ˈon)</td><td>过分吹捧；言过其实</td><td>He laid it on thick about how brilliant her cooking was.<br>他把她的厨艺夸得天花乱坠。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay it on the ˈline (informal)</td><td>开诚布公；把话说明白</td><td>The coach laid it on the line: train harder or leave the squad.<br>教练把话挑明了：要么加练，要么走人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay sb ˈlow (informal)</td><td>（疾病）使卧床不起</td><td>A nasty chest infection laid him low for the whole of January.<br>一场严重的肺部感染让他整个一月都躺在床上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay ˈsiege to sth</td><td>围攻；包围（某地）</td><td>Reporters laid siege to the actor's house for a full week.<br>记者把这位演员的住所围了整整一周。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>speak to or question the people living there</td><td>向当地居民询问情况</td><td>Officers went door to door to speak to or question the people living there.<br>警员挨家挨户向当地居民了解情况。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an army tries to capture a town by surrounding it</td><td>（军队）围城；包围攻取城镇</td><td>For months an army tried to capture the town by surrounding it and waiting.<br>几个月里，军队围困该城，坐等其降。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lead (sb) ˈnowhere</td><td>（对某人）毫无成效；毫无结果</td><td>Arguing about who started it will lead us nowhere tonight.<br>今晚争论谁先挑事，一点用也没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay sb to ˈrest (formal)</td><td>安葬某人</td><td>She was laid to rest beside her husband in the village churchyard.<br>她被安葬在村里教堂墓地丈夫的身旁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay sth to ˈrest</td><td>平息（谣言等）；打消（疑虑）</td><td>The company's statement finally laid the takeover rumours to rest.<br>公司的声明终于平息了收购传闻。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay sth ˈwaste • lay ˈwaste to sth (formal)</td><td>摧毁；使荒芜</td><td>The fire laid waste to thousands of hectares of forest in two days.<br>大火两天内烧毁了数千公顷森林。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lead sb aˈstray</td><td>把某人引入歧途；把某人带坏</td><td>His parents blamed the older boys for leading him astray.<br>他父母怪那些大孩子把他带坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lead sb by the ˈnose</td><td>牵着某人鼻子走；完全控制某人</td><td>She lets her business partner lead her by the nose on every decision.<br>每件事她都让合伙人牵着鼻子走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make sb do everything you want; control sb</td><td>完全操控某人；牵着某人走</td><td>A good manager doesn't make sb do everything you want by fear alone.<br>好的管理者不会只靠威吓让人事事听命。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leading</b></td><td>a ˌleading ˈlight (in/of sth)</td><td>有影响的人物；头面人物</td><td>She was a leading light in the campaign to save the old cinema.<br>她是拯救老影院运动中的核心人物。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌleading ˈquestion</td><td>诱导性提问</td><td>The lawyer objected that it was a leading question and the judge agreed.<br>律师反对说这是诱导性提问，法官同意了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take</b></td><td>take a leaf out of sb's ˈbook</td><td>效仿某人；学某人的样</td><td>You should take a leaf out of your sister's book and start saving.<br>你该学学你姐姐，开始存点钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>league</b></td><td>be out of sb's ˈleague (informal)</td><td>非某人能力（或财力）所及</td><td>That flat by the river is way out of our league on one salary.<br>靠一份工资，河边那套公寓我们根本买不起。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈleague (with sb)</td><td>（与某人）串通；勾结</td><td>The guard turned out to be in league with the thieves all along.<br>原来那名保安一直和窃贼串通一气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be in the same ˈleague/ˈclass/ˈstreet</td><td>不是一个档次；差得远</td><td>He plays well, but he's not in the same league as his older brother.<br>他打得不错，可跟他哥比差着档次。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leak</b></td><td>take a ˈleak (slang)</td><td>撒尿</td><td>Pull over at the next services—I need to take a leak.<br>在下个服务区停一下，我要去撒尿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leap</b></td><td>a leap in the ˈdark</td><td>冒险之举；后果难料的行动</td><td>Quitting a steady job to open a café was a real leap in the dark.<br>辞掉稳定工作去开咖啡馆，实在是一场冒险。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌlook before you ˈleap (saying)</td><td>三思而后行</td><td>Read the whole contract first—look before you leap.<br>先把合同读完，三思而后行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leaps</b></td><td>by/in ˌleaps and ˈbounds</td><td>突飞猛进；飞快地</td><td>Her Chinese has improved by leaps and bounds since she moved to Beijing.<br>搬到北京后，她的中文突飞猛进。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>learn</b></td><td>learn your ˈlesson</td><td>吸取教训</td><td>He's learnt his lesson and never lends money to friends now.<br>他吸取了教训，如今再不借钱给朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lease</b></td><td>a (new) lease of ˈlife (BrE) (AmE a (ˌnew) lease on ˈlife)</td><td>新的活力；获得新生</td><td>The new knee gave my grandmother a whole new lease of life.<br>新换的膝关节让我奶奶像换了个人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>least</b></td><td>at the (very) ˈleast • ˌleave it ˈout (BrE, spoken)</td><td>至少；最少</td><td>The repairs will cost two thousand pounds at the very least.<br>修理费至少也要两千英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) in the ˈleast • leave sb ˈto it (informal)</td><td>丝毫不；一点也不</td><td>I'm not in the least bothered about who gets the credit.<br>功劳算谁的，我一点也不在意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not ˈleast (written) • without (so much as) a ˌby your ˈleave</td><td>特别；尤其</td><td>Everyone was exhausted, not least the driver who had done nine hours.<br>人人都累坏了，尤其是开了九小时车的司机。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leeway</b></td><td>make up ˈleeway (BrE)</td><td>赶上进度；挽回失去的时间</td><td>After the strike the factory worked weekends to make up leeway.<br>罢工过后，工厂周末加班赶进度。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>left</b></td><td>be (way out/over) in left ˈfield (AmE, informal)</td><td>十分离谱；显得古怪</td><td>His theory about the missing cat was way out in left field.<br>他关于那只走失猫的说法离谱得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌleft hand doesn't know what the ˌright hand's ˈdoing</td><td>左手不知右手在做什么；内部不通气</td><td>In that department the left hand doesn't know what the right hand's doing.<br>那个部门左手不知右手在干什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hand's ˈdoing (saying, informal)</td><td>（同一机构内）各自为政，互不通气</td><td>Two teams booked the same hall—clearly the left hand doesn't know what the right hand's doing.<br>两个组订了同一个厅，显然内部完全不通气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the left hand doesn't know what the right hand is doing</td><td>内部沟通不畅；各行其是</td><td>Obviously the left hand doesn't know what the right hand is doing at that bank.<br>显然那家银行内部完全不通气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>left ˌout in the ˈcold</td><td>被冷落；受排斥</td><td>The part-timers felt left out in the cold when the bonuses were announced.<br>发奖金时，兼职员工觉得自己被晾在一边。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌleft, right and ˈcentre • ˌright, left and ˈcentre</td><td>四面八方；到处</td><td>He was handing out business cards left, right and centre at the fair.<br>在展会上他四处发名片。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈcentre (BrE) (AmE ˌleft, right and ˈcenter, ˌright, left and ˈcenter) (informal)</td><td>四处；处处</td><td>The new café is being recommended left, right and center online.<br>网上到处都在推荐这家新咖啡馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leg</b></td><td>break a ˈleg! (spoken)</td><td>祝你好运（尤对演员）</td><td>Break a leg tonight—I'll be in the third row cheering.<br>今晚演出加油，我坐第三排给你鼓劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈleg over (BrE, informal)</td><td>（男子）与人性交</td><td>All he talked about that summer was getting his leg over.<br>那年夏天他张口闭口都是男女那点事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈleg it (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>快跑；逃跑</td><td>We legged it down the alley as soon as the alarm went off.<br>警报一响，我们撒腿沿小巷跑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have a ˌleg to ˈstand on (informal)</td><td>站不住脚；缺乏根据</td><td>Without a receipt you haven't got a leg to stand on in this dispute.<br>没有收据，你在这场纠纷里根本站不住脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>legs</b></td><td>have ˈlegs (informal)</td><td>（作品、话题）持久走红；有后劲</td><td>That documentary really has legs—people still discuss it a year later.<br>那部纪录片很有后劲，一年后大家还在讨论。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leg-up</b></td><td>give sb a ˈleg-up</td><td>托某人一把；助某人一臂之力</td><td>Give me a leg-up and I'll climb over and open the gate.<br>托我一把，我翻过去把门打开。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leisure</b></td><td>at (your) ˈleisure</td><td>有空时；从容不迫地</td><td>Take the brochure home and read it at your leisure.<br>把册子拿回家，有空慢慢看。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lend</b></td><td>lend ˈcolour to sth (BrE) (AmE lend ˈcolor to sth)</td><td>使…显得可信；增加可信度</td><td>The photographs lend colour to his story about the storm.<br>这些照片让他讲的暴风雨经历显得更可信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lend an ˈear (to sb/sth)</td><td>倾听；聆听</td><td>Thanks for lending an ear—I just needed to talk it through.<br>谢谢你听我说，我就是想倾诉一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lend (sb) a ˈhand (with sth)</td><td>帮某人一把</td><td>Could you lend me a hand with these boxes before you go?<br>走之前能帮我搬一下这些箱子吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lend your ˈname to sth (formal)</td><td>以名义支持；公开支持</td><td>Several actors lent their names to the campaign against the new road.<br>几位演员公开支持反对修新路的运动。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lend supˈport, ˈweight, ˈcredence, etc. to sth</td><td>为…提供支持（或佐证）</td><td>The new findings lend weight to her theory about early migration.<br>新发现为她关于早期迁徙的理论提供了佐证。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>length</b></td><td>at ˈlength</td><td>详尽地；良久之后</td><td>He spoke at length about the changes coming to the department.<br>他详详细细讲了部门即将发生的变化。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the length and ˈbreadth of sth</td><td>…的各个角落；到处</td><td>They cycled the length and breadth of Ireland one wet summer.<br>一个多雨的夏天，他们骑车走遍了爱尔兰。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lengths</b></td><td>go to any, great, etc. ˈlengths (to do sth)</td><td>不遗余力（做某事）</td><td>She went to great lengths to find the owner of the lost dog.<br>为找到走失狗的主人，她费尽了心思。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>try very hard (to do sth); do whatever is necessary</td><td>竭尽全力；无所不用其极</td><td>He will try very hard to do whatever is necessary to keep the shop open.<br>为保住这家店，他会想尽一切办法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leopard</b></td><td>a leopard cannot change its ˈspots (saying)</td><td>本性难移</td><td>He promised to stop gossiping, but a leopard cannot change its spots.<br>他保证不再说闲话，可本性难移。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>less</b></td><td>even/much/still ˈless</td><td>更不用说；更谈不上</td><td>He can't boil an egg, much less cook dinner for twelve.<br>他连鸡蛋都煮不好，更别提给十二个人做饭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>less is ˈmore</td><td>少即是多；简约为美</td><td>Take half the furniture out—with this room, less is more.<br>搬走一半家具吧，这屋子少即是多。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no ˈless (often ironic)</td><td>（表示惊讶）竟然；居然</td><td>She was invited to dinner by the ambassador, no less.<br>她竟然被大使请去吃饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no less than...</td><td>（强调数量大）多达；不少于</td><td>No less than four hundred people turned up for the free concert.<br>免费音乐会来了多达四百人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lesser</b></td><td>the ˌlesser of two ˈevils</td><td>两害相权取其轻</td><td>Taking the night train was the lesser of two evils, given the airport chaos.<br>机场一团糟，坐夜车算是两害相权取其轻。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>let</b></td><td>ˌlet ˈfall sth</td><td>（似）无意中说出；脱口而出</td><td>She let fall that the manager had already handed in his notice.<br>她无意中说漏，经理已经递了辞呈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌlet sb/sth ˈgo • ˌlet ˈgo (of sb/sth)</td><td>放开；松手</td><td>Don't let go of the rope until I say so.<br>我没喊之前别松开绳子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌlet yourself ˈgo</td><td>放松尽兴；不修边幅</td><td>It's your birthday—let yourself go for once and dance.<br>今天你生日，就放开一回跳跳舞吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let sb ˈhave it (spoken, informal)</td><td>狠狠教训某人；严厉斥责</td><td>When he finally came home at three, his father let him have it.<br>他凌晨三点才回家，被父亲狠狠训了一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let it ˈgo (at ˈthat)</td><td>到此为止；不再计较</td><td>He apologized, so let's let it go at that.<br>他道歉了，这事就到此为止吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let me ˈsee/ˈthink</td><td>（思考或回忆时）让我想想</td><td>Let me see—I think we last met at Kate's wedding.<br>让我想想，我们上次好像是在凯特婚礼上见的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>letter</b></td><td>the ˌletter of the ˈlaw (often disapproving)</td><td>法律条文（的字面规定）</td><td>He stuck to the letter of the law and ignored its purpose entirely.<br>他死抠法律条文，完全不顾立法本意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the ˈletter</td><td>不折不扣地；一丝不差地</td><td>Follow the recipe to the letter or the bread won't rise.<br>严格照食谱来，不然面包发不起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>level</b></td><td>do/try your level ˈbest (to do sth)</td><td>竭尽全力；全力以赴</td><td>I'll do my level best to get the report to you by Friday.<br>我一定尽全力周五前把报告交给你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep a level ˈhead</td><td>保持冷静；不慌不忙</td><td>She kept a level head while everyone else panicked about the fire.<br>别人为火灾慌成一团，她始终保持冷静。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>level ˈpegging (BrE)</td><td>不分胜负；势均力敌</td><td>The two candidates were level pegging right up to the final count.<br>两位候选人一直不分上下，直到最后计票。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌlevel ˈplaying field</td><td>公平竞争的环境</td><td>Small firms just want a level playing field when they bid for contracts.<br>小公司投标时只求一个公平的竞争环境。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌlevel the ˈplaying field</td><td>创造公平的竞争环境</td><td>Free school meals help level the playing field for poorer children.<br>免费校餐有助于让贫困孩子起点更公平。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈlevel (AmE also on the ˌup and ˈup)</td><td>诚实的；正当的</td><td>Is this deal really on the level, or should I ask a lawyer?<br>这笔交易真的正当吗，还是我该问问律师？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>liberties</b></td><td>take ˈliberties (with sb/sth)</td><td>放肆；过于随便</td><td>The film takes liberties with the facts of her early life.<br>这部电影对她早年经历的处理相当随意。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>liberty</b></td><td>at ˈliberty (to do sth) (formal)</td><td>有权做某事；不受约束</td><td>I'm not at liberty to discuss the details of the case.<br>案件细节我无权透露。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the liberty of doing sth (formal)</td><td>擅自做某事；冒昧行事</td><td>I took the liberty of booking you a table for eight o'clock.<br>我冒昧替你订了八点的位子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>artistic/poetic ˈlicence (often ironic)</td><td>艺术上的自由发挥；破格处理</td><td>The painter used a bit of artistic licence with the shape of the hills.<br>画家在山形上作了些艺术化处理。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>poetic ˈlicence</td><td>创作上的自由发挥</td><td>I used some poetic licence in describing that table as an antique.<br>我自由发挥了一下，把那张桌子说成了古董。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lick</b></td><td>show too much respect for sb in authority</td><td>阿谀奉承；拍马屁</td><td>He shows too much respect for anyone in authority and never disagrees.<br>他对上司一味逢迎，从不表示异议。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a lick of ˈpaint (informal)</td><td>刷一层新漆</td><td>The front door just needs a lick of paint and it'll look new.<br>前门刷层新漆就跟新的一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lick your ˈwounds</td><td>舔舐伤口；失败后恢复元气</td><td>After the election defeat he went home to lick his wounds.<br>竞选失利后，他回家舔舐伤口。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your confidence back after a defeat or disappointment</td><td>失败或失望后恢复信心</td><td>Give her a week to get her confidence back after a defeat like that.<br>输成那样，给她一周时间恢复信心吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lid</b></td><td>keep/put a/the ˈlid on sth</td><td>掩盖某事；控制住某事</td><td>The company tried to keep a lid on the safety report for months.<br>公司试图把那份安全报告压了好几个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lift, blow, etc. the ˈlid off sth (informal)</td><td>揭露内幕；曝光真相</td><td>Her book blows the lid off conditions inside the factories.<br>她的书揭开了这些工厂内部状况的盖子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lie</b></td><td>give the ˈlie to sth (formal)</td><td>证明…是假的；戳穿</td><td>These statistics give the lie to the claim that crime is falling.<br>这些统计数据戳穿了犯罪率下降的说法。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lie ˈdoggo (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>潜伏不动；隐匿不露面</td><td>He lay doggo in the barn until the search party had gone.<br>他躲在谷仓里一动不动，直到搜寻的人走远。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lie down on the ˈjob (informal)</td><td>消极怠工；磨洋工</td><td>I won't employ anyone who lies down on the job—I want workers.<br>我不会雇磨洋工的人，我只要肯干活的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lie in ˈstate</td><td>（遗体）供公众瞻仰</td><td>The former president will lie in state for two days before the funeral.<br>前总统的遗体将在葬礼前供公众瞻仰两天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lie in ˈwait</td><td>埋伏以待；伺机行动</td><td>Photographers lay in wait outside the hotel all night.<br>摄影师们在酒店外守了一整夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lie ˈlow (informal)</td><td>（暂时）躲藏；不露面</td><td>He's lying low at his cousin's until the fuss dies down.<br>风头过去之前，他躲在表哥家不露面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌlie of the ˈland (BrE) (AmE the ˌlay of the ˈland)</td><td>地形地势；目前的形势</td><td>Let me talk to a few people first and get the lie of the land.<br>我先找几个人聊聊，摸摸情况。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lie through your ˈteeth (informal)</td><td>睁眼说瞎话；满口谎言</td><td>He was lying through his teeth when he said he'd never met her.<br>他说从没见过她，纯属睁眼说瞎话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lie your way into/out of sth</td><td>靠撒谎陷入（或脱身）</td><td>He lied his way into the job and was found out within a month.<br>他靠撒谎得到这份工作，一个月就露馅了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lie your way out of sth</td><td>靠撒谎脱身</td><td>You can't lie your way out of it this time, I'm afraid.<br>恐怕你这次靠撒谎是过不了关了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lieu</b></td><td>in lieu (of sth) (formal)</td><td>代替；作为…的替代</td><td>Staff were given extra days off in lieu of a pay rise.<br>员工没加薪，改为多给了几天假。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>life</b></td><td>be sb's ˈlife</td><td>是某人的命根子；至关重要</td><td>That little bookshop was her life for nearly forty years.<br>那家小书店是她近四十年的命根子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring sb/sth to ˈlife</td><td>使生动起来；使有生气</td><td>A few old photographs really brought the story to life for the children.<br>几张老照片让这个故事在孩子们眼里活了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come to ˈlife</td><td>活跃起来；变得有生气</td><td>The square only comes to life after nine, when the bars open.<br>这个广场要到九点酒吧开门后才热闹起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>frighten/scare the ˈlife out of sb</td><td>把某人吓得魂飞魄散</td><td>Don't creep up like that—you scared the life out of me!<br>别这么悄悄摸过来，吓死我了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get a ˈlife (spoken)</td><td>别这么无聊；找点正事做</td><td>You're counting my typos again? Get a life.<br>你又在数我的错别字？找点正事干吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lead/live the life of Reilly/ˈRiley (informal)</td><td>过舒适无忧的生活</td><td>Since he retired he's been living the life of Riley by the sea.<br>退休后他在海边过着悠哉的日子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>life after ˈdeath</td><td>死后的生命；来世</td><td>She lost her faith in life after death when her brother died.<br>弟弟去世后，她不再相信有来世。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(a matter of) ˌlife and/or ˈdeath (informal)</td><td>性命攸关（的事）</td><td>Getting the medicine there tonight is a matter of life and death.<br>今晚把药送到，是人命关天的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the life and ˌsoul of the ˈparty (BrE)</td><td>全场最活跃的人；气氛担当</td><td>Give him a guitar and he's the life and soul of the party.<br>给他一把吉他，他就是全场的气氛担当。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>life is ˈcheap (disapproving)</td><td>人命不值钱</td><td>In those mines life was cheap and accidents were barely reported.<br>那些矿井里人命不值钱，出了事故都没人报道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(have) a life of its ˈown</td><td>（某物）像有生命一般；自行发展</td><td>The rumour took on a life of its own and reached the local paper.<br>这条传言像长了腿，一路传到了本地报纸上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose your ˈlife</td><td>丧生；遇难</td><td>Three firefighters lost their lives trying to reach the top floor.<br>三名消防员在试图冲上顶层时殉职。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>loss of ˈlife</td><td>人员伤亡；丧生</td><td>Fortunately there was no loss of life in the warehouse fire.<br>幸运的是这场仓库火灾没有人员死亡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make life ˈdifficult (for sb)</td><td>给某人找麻烦；使日子难过</td><td>Changing the rules midweek just makes life difficult for everyone.<br>周中改规则，只会让大家都难做。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make sb's life a ˈmisery</td><td>折磨某人；使某人痛苦不堪</td><td>The constant noise from upstairs made her life a misery.<br>楼上没完没了的噪音折磨得她苦不堪言。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈman/ˈwoman in your life (informal)</td><td>你生命中的那个男人（或女人）</td><td>So, is he the man in your life now, or just a good friend?<br>怎么，他现在是你的那位了，还是只是好朋友？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not for the ˈlife of me, etc.</td><td>无论如何也不能；怎么也想不起</td><td>I cannot for the life of me remember where I parked the car.<br>我怎么也想不起来车停在哪儿了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for the life of him</td><td>他无论如何也（不能）</td><td>He couldn't for the life of him understand why she was so annoyed.<br>他无论如何也不明白她为什么这么生气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not on your ˈlife (spoken)</td><td>（断然拒绝）绝不；没门儿</td><td>Lend him the van again? Not on your life.<br>再把货车借给他？没门儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see ˈlife</td><td>见世面；经历世事</td><td>Two years driving a taxi at night certainly made him see life.<br>开了两年夜班出租，他可真见了世面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>such is ˈlife (informal)</td><td>（表示无奈）这就是生活</td><td>The train was cancelled and I missed the wedding—such is life.<br>火车取消了，婚礼也错过了，这就是生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb's ˈlife (formal)</td><td>杀害某人；夺去某人性命</td><td>No argument over money can justify taking another person's life.<br>再大的金钱纠纷也不能成为杀人的理由。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take your ˌlife in your ˈhands</td><td>冒生命危险；豁出性命</td><td>You take your life in your hands crossing that road at rush hour.<br>高峰期过那条马路简直是玩命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take your own ˈlife (formal)</td><td>自杀</td><td>The poet took his own life at the age of thirty-two.<br>这位诗人三十二岁时自杀身亡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌthat's ˈlife (also ˌc'est la ˈvie from French)</td><td>（表示无奈）生活就是这样</td><td>I worked all weekend and someone else got the credit—that's life.<br>我干了整个周末，功劳算别人的，生活就是这样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's ˌlife in the old dog ˈyet (humorous)</td><td>人老心不老；老当益壮</td><td>Grandad won the fun run again—there's life in the old dog yet.<br>爷爷又赢了趣味长跑，真是老当益壮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>this is the ˈlife!</td><td>（表示满足）这才叫生活</td><td>Sun, a cold drink and no emails—this is the life!<br>阳光、冷饮、没有邮件，这才叫生活！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the ˈlife</td><td>（描摹）逼真；活灵活现</td><td>The old sailor in the painting is drawn to the life.<br>画里那位老水手画得活灵活现。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what a ˈlife!</td><td>这日子真难熬；人生太苦了</td><td>Two jobs, three kids and a leaking roof—what a life!<br>两份工作、三个孩子、屋顶还漏水，这日子真够呛！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>where there's ˈlife (ˌthere's ˈhope) (saying)</td><td>留得青山在，不怕没柴烧</td><td>The shop's barely surviving, but where there's life there's hope.<br>店勉强撑着，可留得青山在，不怕没柴烧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lifetime</b></td><td>the chance, etc. of a ˈlifetime</td><td>千载难逢的机会</td><td>Studying in Kyoto for a year was the chance of a lifetime.<br>去京都读一年书是千载难逢的机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lift</b></td><td>(not) lift a ˈfinger (to do sth) (informal)</td><td>（不）出一点力；（不）帮一点忙</td><td>He never lifts a finger to help with the washing-up.<br>洗碗的事他从来不搭把手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>thumb/hitch a ˈlift</td><td>搭便车；伸手拦车</td><td>We missed the last bus and had to thumb a lift into town.<br>我们错过末班车，只好搭便车进城。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>light</b></td><td>be in sb's ˈlight</td><td>挡住某人的光线</td><td>Move over a bit—you're in my light and I can't read.<br>挪一挪，你挡着光，我没法看书。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be light on sth</td><td>缺少某物；某方面不足</td><td>The report is a bit light on hard evidence, to be honest.<br>说实话，这份报告缺乏有力证据。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/go out like a ˈlight (informal)</td><td>很快睡着；突然失去知觉</td><td>He hit the pillow and went out like a light.<br>他头一沾枕头就睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring sth to ˈlight</td><td>揭露；使真相大白</td><td>The audit brought to light years of missing payments.<br>这次审计揭出了多年来的欠款问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cast/shed/throw (new) ˈlight on sth</td><td>阐明；使人对…有新认识</td><td>The letters shed new light on why she left the country.<br>这些信件让人重新理解她为何离开这个国家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come to ˈlight</td><td>被发现；为人所知</td><td>New details about the accident came to light this morning.<br>今早又有关于这起事故的新细节曝光。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in a ˌgood, ˌbad, ˌfavourable, etc. ˈlight</td><td>从好（或坏）的角度看</td><td>The interview showed the company in a very bad light.<br>这次采访把公司衬得很不堪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈlight of sth (BrE) (AmE in ˈlight of sth)</td><td>鉴于；考虑到</td><td>In the light of these new figures, we should redo the budget.<br>鉴于这些新数字，我们该重做预算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) light as ˈair/a ˈfeather</td><td>轻如鸿毛；非常轻</td><td>The little suitcase was as light as a feather when empty.<br>这只小行李箱空着时轻得像羽毛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(see the) ˌlight at the end of the ˈtunnel</td><td>（看到）苦尽甘来的希望；曙光在望</td><td>After three years of building work we can finally see light at the end of the tunnel.<br>施工三年，我们总算看到曙光了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the future, especially after a long period of difficulty</td><td>长期艰难后的希望；曙光在望</td><td>There's hope in the future, especially after a long period of difficulty like this.<br>熬过这么长一段苦日子，前面总算有盼头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(the) light ˈdawned (on sb)</td><td>恍然大悟；豁然开朗</td><td>Then the light dawned—she'd been reading the wrong timetable.<br>这时她恍然大悟，原来看错了时刻表。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(see) the light of ˈday</td><td>问世；公之于众</td><td>The novel he wrote at twenty never saw the light of day.<br>他二十岁写的那部小说从未面世。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the light of sb's ˈlife</td><td>某人的心肝宝贝</td><td>That scruffy little dog is the light of my father's life.<br>那只脏兮兮的小狗是我父亲的心肝宝贝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a light ˈtouch</td><td>灵活巧妙的处理方式</td><td>She handled the complaint with a light touch and nobody felt blamed.<br>她处理投诉举重若轻，谁都没觉得被指责。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈlight of sth</td><td>轻描淡写；不把…当回事</td><td>He made light of the injury, but he could hardly walk.<br>他对伤势轻描淡写，其实几乎走不了路。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make light ˈwork of sth (informal)</td><td>轻而易举地完成；轻松取胜</td><td>The two of them made light work of clearing the whole garden.<br>他们俩三下五除二就把整个花园清理干净了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see the ˈlight</td><td>恍然大悟；醒悟过来</td><td>After months of arguing, he finally saw the light and sold the car.<br>争了几个月，他终于想通，把车卖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set ˈlight to sth (especially BrE)</td><td>点燃；使着火</td><td>Someone set light to a pile of rubbish behind the shops.<br>有人点着了店铺后面的一堆垃圾。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with a light ˈheart</td><td>心情轻松地；欣然</td><td>She handed in the last exam paper with a light heart.<br>交上最后一份考卷时，她心情轻松。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lightly</b></td><td>get off/be let off ˈlightly (informal)</td><td>从轻发落；免受重罚</td><td>A warning? He got off lightly, if you ask me.<br>就一个警告？要我说他算是轻判了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lightning</b></td><td>at/with ˌlightning ˈspeed</td><td>以闪电般的速度；飞快地</td><td>News of the closure spread through the office at lightning speed.<br>关门的消息在办公室里飞快传开。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌlightning never strikes (in the same place) ˈtwice</td><td>同样的倒霉事不会重演</td><td>We were burgled last year, but lightning never strikes twice.<br>去年我们家被偷了，不过倒霉事不会连着来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈtwice (saying)</td><td>倒霉事不会在同一处（或同一人身上）重演</td><td>Relax—lightning never strikes in the same place twice.<br>放宽心吧，这种倒霉事不会再来一次。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lights</b></td><td>the lights are ˈon but nobody's ˈhome</td><td>（形容人）呆头呆脑；心不在焉</td><td>You can talk to him all day, but the lights are on and nobody's home.<br>你跟他说一天也没用，他压根没往心里去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>like</b></td><td>and the ˈlike (informal)</td><td>诸如此类；等等</td><td>Bring towels, sunscreen and the like—we'll be there all day.<br>带上毛巾、防晒霜之类的，我们要待一整天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>anything/nothing/something like that how would ˈyou like it?</td><td>换了你会怎么想呢</td><td>How would you like it if someone read your messages?<br>要是有人翻你的短信，你会怎么想？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I like your ˈnerve, ˈcheek, etc. • I like ˈthat!</td><td>亏你说得出口（或做得出来）</td><td>You want me to pay for the taxi too? I like that!<br>还要我付出租车钱？亏你说得出口！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if you ˈlike (spoken)</td><td>如果你愿意；你要是想的话</td><td>We can eat at home instead, if you like.<br>你要是愿意，我们可以改在家里吃。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) like as ˈnot • like eˈnough • most/very ˈlike</td><td>很可能；多半</td><td>As like as not he's stuck in traffic again on the ring road.<br>他多半又堵在环路上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈlike (informal)</td><td>很可能；大概</td><td>Most like he forgot the whole thing the moment you told him.<br>他八成你一说完就忘了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) like ˈthat</td><td>就那样；毫不犹豫地</td><td>She stood up, walked out and quit, just like that.<br>她站起来，走出去，就那么辞职了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>limelight</b></td><td>out of/in the ˈlimelight</td><td>（不）受公众关注；（不）引人注目</td><td>After the scandal he stayed out of the limelight for years.<br>丑闻之后，他多年不露面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>limit</b></td><td>be the (absolute) ˈlimit (old-fashioned, spoken)</td><td>实在令人受不了</td><td>Turning up two hours late is the absolute limit.<br>迟到两个小时，真是让人忍无可忍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈsky's the limit</td><td>前途无量；没有上限</td><td>With her talent and that scholarship, the sky's the limit.<br>凭她的天赋加上奖学金，前途不可限量。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>limits</b></td><td>within ˈlimits</td><td>在一定程度上；有限度地</td><td>You can decorate the room however you want, within limits.<br>房间随你怎么布置，但要有个限度。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>line</b></td><td>all along/down the ˈline • right down the ˈline</td><td>彻头彻尾；在每个环节</td><td>The project was badly managed all down the line.<br>这个项目从头到尾管理得一塌糊涂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈline (informal)</td><td>完全地；在每一点上</td><td>They supported her right down the line during the dispute.<br>纠纷期间他们自始至终支持她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring sb/sth into ˈline (with sb/sth)</td><td>使与…一致；使符合</td><td>The new rules bring our pay scales into line with the industry.<br>新规定使我们的薪级与行业水平接轨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in line for sth</td><td>有望获得某物</td><td>She's in line for promotion if the department expands next year.<br>如果明年部门扩编，她有望升职。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˌline of ˈduty</td><td>在执行公务时；在履行职责时</td><td>The officer was injured in the line of duty last Saturday.<br>这名警官上周六在执勤中受伤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be) in/out of ˈline with sb/sth</td><td>与…一致（或不一致）</td><td>His account of the meeting is completely out of line with mine.<br>他对会议的说法跟我的完全不一致。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(choose, follow, take, etc.) the line of least reˈsistance</td><td>走阻力最小的路；图省事</td><td>He took the line of least resistance and agreed to everything.<br>他图省事，什么都答应了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>reˈsistance</td><td>（采取）最省事的办法</td><td>Following the line of least resistance won't fix this problem.<br>一味图省事解决不了这个问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>line your (own)/sb's ˈpocket(s) (informal)</td><td>中饱私囊；发不义之财</td><td>The contractor was lining his own pockets with the repair money.<br>承包商把修缮款装进了自己腰包。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈline</td><td>（名誉、工作等）面临风险</td><td>His whole reputation is on the line with this one trial.<br>这一场官司关系到他的全部声誉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>somewhere, etc. along/down the ˈline</td><td>在某个时刻；在某个环节</td><td>Somewhere along the line the two files got mixed up.<br>不知在哪个环节，这两份档案弄混了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tread/walk a fine/thin ˈline</td><td>在两难间小心行事；如履薄冰</td><td>Comedians walk a fine line between funny and offensive.<br>喜剧演员在好笑和冒犯之间走钢丝。</td></tr>
