<tr><td></td><td>the bottom line</td><td>关键之处；最终结果</td><td>The bottom line is we can't afford another delay.<br>关键在于，我们再也拖不起了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lines</b></td><td>on/along the lines of...</td><td>按…的方式；类似于…</td><td>He said something along the lines of never wanting to see me again.<br>他说了句大概是再也不想见我之类的话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lines (spoken)</td><td>按…的方式；大致如此</td><td>We want a garden along the lines of the one in that magazine.<br>我们想要个跟杂志上那个差不多的花园。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lingua</b></td><td>a ˌlingua ˈfranca (from Italian)</td><td>（不同母语者共用的）通用语</td><td>English serves as a lingua franca among the engineers on this site.<br>英语是工地上这些工程师的通用语。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>link</b></td><td>a link in the ˈchain</td><td>链条中的一环；过程中的一个环节</td><td>Every delivery driver is an important link in the chain.<br>每个送货司机都是链条上重要的一环。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lion</b></td><td>the lion's ˈden</td><td>龙潭虎穴；难以应付的场合</td><td>Walking into that board meeting felt like entering the lion's den.<br>走进那场董事会，感觉像进了龙潭虎穴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈlion's share (of sth) (BrE)</td><td>最大的一份</td><td>Her brother took the lion's share of the inheritance.<br>遗产中最大的一份被她哥哥拿走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lips</b></td><td>lick/smack your ˈlips</td><td>舔嘴唇；急不可待</td><td>The kids were licking their lips as the cake came out of the oven.<br>蛋糕一出炉，孩子们就馋得直咂嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>my lips are ˈsealed (informal, humorous)</td><td>守口如瓶；绝不外传</td><td>Tell me the gossip—my lips are sealed, I promise.<br>跟我说说八卦吧，我保证守口如瓶。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on everyone's ˈlips</td><td>人人都在谈论</td><td>That singer's name was on everyone's lips after the final.<br>决赛之后，那位歌手的名字人人都在谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>list</b></td><td>be on/off the danger list</td><td>（病人）处于（或脱离）危险期</td><td>The doctors say he's off the danger list and can have visitors.<br>医生说他脱离危险了，可以探视。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>listen</b></td><td>listen with half an ˈear</td><td>心不在焉地听；半听不听</td><td>He listened with half an ear while scrolling through his phone.<br>他一边刷手机，一边心不在焉地听着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>little</b></td><td>a little ˈbird told me (that...) (spoken)</td><td>有人私下告诉我；小道消息说</td><td>A little bird told me you're moving to Shanghai next month.<br>有人偷偷告诉我，你下个月要搬去上海。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌlittle by ˈlittle</td><td>一点一点地；逐渐地</td><td>Little by little she taught herself to play the piano.<br>她一点一点自学会了弹钢琴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈlittle of sth</td><td>不重视；轻描淡写</td><td>He made little of the injury so his mother wouldn't worry.<br>他把伤说得轻描淡写，免得母亲担心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>more than a little exˈcited, ˈshocked, etc.</td><td>非常兴奋（或震惊等）</td><td>She was more than a little shocked to find the door wide open.<br>发现门大敞着，她着实吓了一跳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>little ˈfinger (informal)</td><td>任意摆布某人；玩弄于股掌之间</td><td>That child can twist his grandmother round his little finger.<br>那孩子把奶奶哄得团团转。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>live</b></td><td>live and ˈbreathe sth</td><td>全身心投入；痴迷于某事</td><td>He lives and breathes football, even on his wedding day.<br>他痴迷足球，连结婚那天也不例外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live and ˈlearn</td><td>活到老学到老；吃一堑长一智</td><td>I'll never buy a used phone online again—live and learn.<br>我再也不网购二手手机了，吃一堑长一智。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live and ˈlet live (saying)</td><td>自己活也让别人活；彼此宽容</td><td>My neighbours and I live and let live, and we get along fine.<br>我和邻居互不干涉，相处得挺好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live beyond/within your ˈmeans</td><td>入不敷出；量入为出</td><td>They lived beyond their means for years and ended up in debt.<br>他们多年入不敷出，最后欠了一身债。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live by/on your ˈwits</td><td>靠机智谋生；随机应变过活</td><td>He left home at sixteen and lived on his wits in the city.<br>他十六岁离家，在城里靠机灵劲儿讨生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live (from) ˌhand to ˈmouth</td><td>勉强糊口；挣一天吃一天</td><td>They lived hand to mouth all winter until the work picked up.<br>整个冬天他们勉强糊口，直到活儿多起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live in ˈhope</td><td>怀着希望；一直盼着</td><td>I live in hope that one day he'll return my ladder.<br>我一直盼着他哪天把梯子还我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live in ˈsin (old-fashioned or humorous)</td><td>未婚同居</td><td>Her grandmother still says the two of them are living in sin.<br>她奶奶至今还说他们俩是未婚同居。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live it ˈup (informal)</td><td>尽情享乐；纵情挥霍</td><td>They lived it up in Barcelona for a week on his bonus.<br>他们拿着奖金在巴塞罗那潇洒了一周。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep sth important about yourself a secret from others</td><td>过双面生活；为人虚伪</td><td>He kept something important about himself a secret from everyone for years.<br>多年来他向所有人隐瞒着自己的重要秘密。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live like a ˈking</td><td>过帝王般的生活；生活阔绰</td><td>On that salary you could live like a king in this town.<br>拿那份薪水，在这座小城你能过得像个国王。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live off/on the ˌfat of the ˈland (informal)</td><td>锦衣玉食；过奢侈生活</td><td>They sold the company and have lived off the fat of the land since.<br>他们卖了公司，从此过上了锦衣玉食的日子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live off the ˈland</td><td>靠土地为生；就地取食</td><td>For a whole summer they lived off the land in the hills.<br>整整一个夏天，他们在山里靠山吃山。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live to fight another ˈday (saying)</td><td>留得青山在；改日再战</td><td>We lost the vote, but we live to fight another day.<br>这次表决输了，但我们还有下回。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live to tell the ˈtale (informal, often humorous)</td><td>死里逃生；挺过难关</td><td>He fell off the roof and somehow lived to tell the tale.<br>他从屋顶摔下来，居然还活着讲这段经历。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live to tell the ˈtale</td><td>熬过来；幸存下来</td><td>It'll be a difficult trip, but I expect you'll live to tell the tale.<br>这趟不好走，不过我相信你能挺过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live up to your/its repuˈtation</td><td>名副其实；不负盛名</td><td>The restaurant certainly lived up to its reputation for slow service.<br>这家餐厅上菜慢的名声果然名不虚传。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a live ˈwire (informal)</td><td>生龙活虎的人；活跃分子</td><td>Our new receptionist is a real live wire and everyone loves her.<br>新来的前台特别有活力，人人都喜欢她。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lived</b></td><td>you haven't ˈlived</td><td>你算是白活了</td><td>You've never eaten hotpot in Chengdu? You haven't lived!<br>你没在成都吃过火锅？那你算白活了！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lively</b></td><td>look ˈlively/ˈsharp (BrE, informal)</td><td>快点；麻利些</td><td>Look lively, you two—the bus for town leaves in four minutes.<br>你俩快点，进城的车四分钟后就开。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>living</b></td><td>be ˌliving ˈproof of sth</td><td>是…的活证据</td><td>My uncle is living proof that you can start again at sixty.<br>我叔叔就是六十岁还能重新开始的活证据。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/within ˌliving ˈmemory</td><td>在当今人们的记忆中</td><td>It was the worst flood in living memory in this valley.<br>这是本地人记忆中这条山谷最严重的一次洪水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a living ˈlegend (also a ˌlegend in your own ˈlifetime)</td><td>在世的传奇人物</td><td>Among local fishermen the old skipper is a living legend.<br>在本地渔民中，那位老船长是个活着的传奇。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Io</b></td><td>lo and beˈhold (humorous)</td><td>（引出意外之事）你瞧，真想不到</td><td>I opened the cupboard and, lo and behold, there was the missing cat.<br>我打开橱柜，你瞧，走失的猫就在里面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get a load of ˈthis (spoken)</td><td>瞧瞧这个；听听这个</td><td>Get a load of this—they want us to work on Christmas Day.<br>听听这个，他们想让我们圣诞节上班。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a load of (old) ˈrubbish, ˈnonsense, etc.</td><td>一派胡言；净是废话</td><td>That article about the diet is a load of old rubbish.<br>那篇讲减肥的文章纯属一派胡言。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>loaded</b></td><td>loaded for ˈbear (AmE)</td><td>严阵以待；准备大干一场</td><td>She walked into the negotiation loaded for bear.<br>她带着一身火气走进谈判现场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lock</b></td><td>lock ˈhorns (with sb) (over sth)</td><td>（与某人）争执；发生冲突</td><td>The two directors locked horns over the budget again.<br>两位主管又为预算问题争执起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌlock, stock and ˈbarrel</td><td>全部；彻底地</td><td>They sold the farm lock, stock and barrel and moved abroad.<br>他们把农场连同一切全卖了，搬去了国外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under ˌlock and ˈkey</td><td>被严密锁藏；被囚禁</td><td>The old letters are kept under lock and key in the archive.<br>那些旧信件锁在档案室里严加保管。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>loco</b></td><td>in ˌloco paˈrentis (from Latin, formal)</td><td>代行父母之责</td><td>Teachers on the trip act in loco parentis for the whole week.<br>带队老师整整一周都代行父母职责。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>loggerheads</b></td><td>at ˈloggerheads (with sb) (over sth)</td><td>（与某人）不和；有严重分歧</td><td>The council is at loggerheads with residents over the new car park.<br>市政会与居民在新停车场问题上争执不下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lone</b></td><td>a ˌlone ˈwolf</td><td>独来独往的人；独行侠</td><td>He's always been a lone wolf and prefers to work nights alone.<br>他一向独来独往，喜欢一个人上夜班。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>long</b></td><td>as/so ˈlong as be in sth for the long ˈhaul</td><td>打持久战；愿意坚持到底</td><td>We're in this campaign for the long haul, not just one winter.<br>这场运动我们打算长期坚持，不止一个冬天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for (so) ˈlong</td><td>（这么）长时间；长久地</td><td>I haven't seen her for so long that I barely recognized her.<br>太久没见她了，我差点没认出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go back a long ˈway</td><td>（人之间）相识很久</td><td>Those two go back a long way—they were at school together.<br>他们俩交情很久了，是同学。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have come a long ˈway</td><td>取得很大进步；大有长进</td><td>Cancer treatment has come a long way since my grandmother was first diagnosed.<br>自我祖母初次确诊以来，癌症治疗已有了长足进步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a long way to ˈgo</td><td>还有很长的路要走；差距还很大</td><td>Her Spanish is improving, but she still has a long way to go before fluency.<br>她的西班牙语在进步，但离流利还差得远。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how long is a piece of ˈstring? (BrE, spoken)</td><td>说不准；这可没准数</td><td>You ask how much the repair will cost—well, how long is a piece of string?<br>你问修理要多少钱，这可真说不准。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈlong run</td><td>从长远来看；最终</td><td>Buying decent boots costs more now but saves you money in the long run.<br>买双好靴子眼下费钱，长远看反而省钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's a ˌlong ˈstory (informal)</td><td>说来话长；一言难尽</td><td>Why did I quit my job in Beijing? It's a long story, buy me a drink first.<br>我为什么辞掉北京的工作？说来话长，先请我喝一杯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the long and (the) ˈshort of it</td><td>总而言之；总的情况就是这样</td><td>The long and the short of it is that we can't afford the house.<br>总而言之，这房子我们买不起。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the long arm of the ˈlaw</td><td>法律的力量；法网恢恢</td><td>He hid in Thailand for years, but the long arm of the law finally reached him.<br>他在泰国躲了多年，最终还是没能逃出法网。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(pull, wear, etc.) a long ˈface</td><td>闷闷不乐；哭丧着脸</td><td>Don't pull a long face just because your team lost one match.<br>别只因球队输了一场就哭丧着脸。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a long ˈhaul (informal)</td><td>漫长而艰辛的事；长途跋涉</td><td>Getting the factory back to full production will be a long haul.<br>让工厂恢复满负荷生产会是件漫长又费劲的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be) ˌlong in the ˈtooth (humorous, especially BrE)</td><td>年事已高；上了年纪</td><td>I'm getting a bit long in the tooth for climbing mountains in winter.<br>我这把年纪，冬天爬山有点吃不消了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈlong shot (informal)</td><td>成功机会不大的尝试；胜算很小的猜测</td><td>Applying to Oxford was a long shot, but she got in anyway.<br>申请牛津本是碰碰运气，结果她真考上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>long time no ˈsee (spoken)</td><td>好久不见</td><td>Wei! Long time no see—how have you been these past three years?<br>阿伟！好久不见，这三年过得怎么样？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not by a ˈlong chalk (BrE) (also not by a ˈlong shot AmE, BrE) (informal)</td><td>差得远；绝不；一点也不</td><td>The job isn't finished, not by a long chalk—we've barely started.<br>活儿还差得远呢，我们才刚开了个头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not ˌlong for this ˈworld (old-fashioned)</td><td>不久于人世；活不了多久</td><td>The old dog can barely walk now; I'm afraid he's not long for this world.<br>这条老狗几乎走不动了，恐怕活不了多久。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>over the long ˈhaul</td><td>从长远看；在很长一段时间里</td><td>Over the long haul, small daily savings add up to a real cushion.<br>长远看来，每天省下的一点点会攒成一笔应急钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so ˈlong (for now) (informal)</td><td>再见；回头见</td><td>So long for now—I'll call you when I land in Shanghai.<br>先这样，等我落地上海再给你打电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a long (cool/hard) ˈlook at sth</td><td>慎重考虑；深思熟虑</td><td>You should take a long hard look at your spending before buying that car.<br>买那辆车之前，你该好好审视一下自己的开销。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈlong view (of sth)</td><td>从长计议；着眼长远</td><td>Good investors take the long view and ignore one bad quarter.<br>优秀的投资者着眼长远，不会在意一个季度的亏损。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to cut a long story ˈshort (BrE) (AmE to make a long story ˈshort) (spoken)</td><td>长话短说；简而言之</td><td>To cut a long story short, we missed the flight and drove instead.<br>长话短说，我们误了航班，改成开车了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>longer</b></td><td>no/any ˈlonger</td><td>不再；已不</td><td>She no longer answers his messages, and honestly I don't blame her.<br>她不再回他消息了，说实话我不怪她。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>look</b></td><td>by/from the ˈlook(s) of it/things (informal)</td><td>看样子；从表面看</td><td>By the look of things, this meeting is going to run past six.<br>看样子，这个会要开到六点以后了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look ˈbad • not look ˈgood</td><td>（行为）不得体；显得失礼</td><td>It would look bad if you skipped your own brother's wedding.<br>你要是缺席亲弟弟的婚礼，那可太说不过去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look ˈgood</td><td>看来充满希望；形势看好</td><td>Sales are up two months running—things are finally starting to look good.<br>销售连涨两个月，情况总算开始看好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌlook ˈhere! (old-fashioned)</td><td>喂，听着（用于引起注意）</td><td>Look here, I've paid on time every month and I won't be spoken to like that.<br>喂，听着，我每月都按时付款，不许这么跟我说话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look sb ˌup and ˈdown (informal)</td><td>上下打量（某人）</td><td>The doorman looked me up and down and decided my jacket wasn't smart enough.<br>门童把我上下打量一番，认定我的外套不够体面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) look yourˈself (informal)</td><td>气色（不）如常；看来（不）像平时那样</td><td>You don't look yourself today—did you sleep at all last night?<br>你今天气色不太对，昨晚睡了吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be much to ˈlook at (informal)</td><td>相貌平平；不起眼</td><td>The car isn't much to look at, but the engine runs like new.<br>这车外表不起眼，可发动机跟新的一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈlook at sb/sth • by the ˈlook of sb/sth</td><td>从外表看；看起来</td><td>To look at him, you'd never guess he once ran marathons.<br>从外表看，你绝想不到他当年跑过马拉松。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>look-in</b></td><td>not get/have a ˈlook-in (BrE, informal)</td><td>没有机会参与；没有得胜的希望</td><td>With three older brothers, he never got a look-in at the dinner table.<br>上头三个哥哥，饭桌上从来轮不到他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>looking</b></td><td>be just ˈlooking</td><td>（不想买）只是随便看看</td><td>Thanks, I'm just looking—I'll shout if I need help with sizes.<br>谢谢，我随便看看，要试尺码再叫你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be looking over your ˈshoulder</td><td>提心吊胆；时刻提防</td><td>Ever since the layoffs, everyone in the office is looking over their shoulder.<br>自从裁员以来，办公室里人人都提心吊胆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be looking to do sth</td><td>打算做某事；正想着做某事</td><td>We're looking to move somewhere quieter before the baby arrives.<br>我们打算在孩子出生前搬到清静点的地方。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lookout</b></td><td>be ˈsb's (own) lookout (BrE, informal)</td><td>是某人自己的事；后果自负</td><td>If he wants to invest his savings in crypto, that's his own lookout.<br>他要拿积蓄去炒币，那是他自己的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be on the ˈlookout (for sb/sth) • keep a ˈlookout (for sb/sth)</td><td>留心寻找；注意提防</td><td>Keep a lookout for a red door—the café is just behind it.<br>留心找一扇红门，咖啡馆就在门后面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>looks</b></td><td>if looks could ˈkill...</td><td>如果目光能杀人（形容目光极其愤怒）</td><td>If looks could kill, the waiter would have dropped dead on the spot.<br>要是目光能杀人，那服务员当场就没命了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>loom</b></td><td>loom ˈlarge</td><td>（问题、事件）迫近而令人忧虑；显得突出</td><td>With exams two weeks away, failure began to loom large in her mind.<br>考试还有两周，落榜的念头在她心里越来越沉重。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>loop</td><td>环；圈；循环</td><td>The road makes a wide loop around the lake before heading north.<br>这条路绕湖兜了一个大圈，然后向北去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in the ˈloop • be out of the ˈloop (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>属于（或不属于）知情圈子</td><td>Copy me on those emails so I stay in the loop about the merger.<br>那些邮件抄送我一份，好让我了解并购进展。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>knock/throw sb for a ˈloop (AmE, informal)</td><td>使某人大为震惊；打得某人措手不及</td><td>His sudden resignation really threw the whole team for a loop.<br>他突然辞职，把整个团队都搞蒙了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌloop the ˈloop</td><td>（飞机）做翻筋斗飞行</td><td>The old biplane looped the loop twice and the crowd went wild.<br>那架老双翼机连翻两个筋斗，观众都疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>loose</b></td><td>at a loose ˈend (BrE) (AmE at loose ˈends)</td><td>无所事事；闲得没事干</td><td>If you're at a loose end on Sunday, come and help me paint the fence.<br>你周日要是闲着没事，来帮我刷围栏吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>break/cut/tear (sth) ˈloose from sb/sth</td><td>（使）挣脱；摆脱</td><td>At eighteen he broke loose from his family and moved across the country.<br>十八岁时他挣脱家庭束缚，搬到了国家的另一头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hang/stay ˈloose (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>保持镇静；别紧张</td><td>Just hang loose—the results won't be posted until Friday anyway.<br>别急，反正成绩要到周五才公布。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a loose ˈtongue</td><td>嘴不严；口无遮拦</td><td>Don't tell him anything private; he has a very loose tongue.<br>别跟他说私事，他嘴太不严了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let ˈloose (BrE) (AmE cut ˈloose) (informal)</td><td>放开玩；无拘无束</td><td>After finals we all let loose and danced until three in the morning.<br>期末考完，我们彻底放开，跳舞跳到凌晨三点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let ˈloose sth</td><td>（突然大声）发出；喊出</td><td>When the goal went in, he let loose a yell that woke the neighbours.<br>球进的那一刻，他大吼一声，把邻居都吵醒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let sb/sth ˈloose</td><td>放开；释放；任其自由行动</td><td>Never let that dog loose in the park without checking the gate first.<br>没先检查大门，绝不要在公园里放开那条狗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌloose ˈcannon (disapproving)</td><td>言行难以预料的危险人物</td><td>The manager is talented but a loose cannon in front of reporters.<br>这位经理很有才，但面对记者时口无遮拦、难以掌控。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the loose ˈends/ˈthreads</td><td>尚待处理的枝节问题；未了结的细节</td><td>The film is fun, but it leaves far too many loose ends unexplained.<br>这部电影挺好看，可留下的伏笔太多没交代。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>You know who committed the murder, but there</td><td>凶手已知，细节却未交代清楚</td><td>You know who committed the murder, but there are still loose ends everywhere.<br>你知道凶手是谁，可到处都是没交代清楚的细节。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be) on the ˈloose</td><td>（囚犯、动物等）在逃；逍遥法外</td><td>Two bears are on the loose near the campsite, so keep food inside.<br>有两头熊在营地附近游荡，食物请收在屋里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play fast and ˈloose (with sb/sth)</td><td>玩弄；对待…不负责任</td><td>The company played fast and loose with safety rules until someone got hurt.<br>这家公司一直无视安全规定，直到出了工伤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>loosen</b></td><td>loosen sb's ˈtongue</td><td>使某人无拘无束地说话；使人说话没顾忌</td><td>Two glasses of wine loosened his tongue and out came the whole story.<br>两杯红酒下肚，他话匣子打开，全说了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(good) ˈLord! • oh ˈLord!</td><td>天哪；主啊（表示惊讶或懊恼）</td><td>Oh Lord, I've left my passport on the kitchen table again.<br>天哪，我又把护照落在厨房桌上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(Some people may find these idioms offensive.)</td><td>（有人可能认为这些习语含冒犯意）</td><td>Some people may find these idioms offensive, so use them carefully in class.<br>有人可能觉得这些习语冒犯，课堂上要慎用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈLord (only) knows (what, where, why, etc.)</td><td>天晓得；谁也不知道</td><td>Lord knows why he sold the flat right before prices doubled.<br>天晓得他为什么在房价翻倍前把房子卖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈlord it over sb (disapproving)</td><td>对某人盛气凌人；摆架子</td><td>Ever since her promotion she's been lording it over the rest of us.<br>自从升职以后，她就对我们其他人颐指气使。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lorry</b></td><td>off the ˌback of a ˈlorry (BrE, informal, humorous)</td><td>来路不明（通常指偷来的）</td><td>That watch was suspiciously cheap—it probably fell off the back of a lorry.<br>那块表便宜得可疑，八成是来路不明的货。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come ˈoff the back of a lorry (BrE, informal, humorous)</td><td>来路不明；（婉指）赃物</td><td>He never asks where the stock comes off the back of a lorry from.<br>他从不问那些来路不明的货究竟是哪儿来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lose</b></td><td>ˈlose it (spoken)</td><td>失控；情绪崩溃；发火</td><td>When the printer jammed for the fifth time, I completely lost it.<br>打印机第五次卡纸时，我彻底崩溃了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>loss</b></td><td>at a ˈloss (informal)</td><td>不知所措；困惑</td><td>I'm at a loss to explain why the server crashed again this morning.<br>我实在说不清今早服务器为什么又崩了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at a ˌloss for ˈwords</td><td>无言以对；不知说什么好</td><td>When she handed me the keys to the flat, I was at a loss for words.<br>她把公寓钥匙交给我时，我一时说不出话来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>losses</b></td><td>cut your ˈlosses</td><td>及时止损；趁早撒手</td><td>The shop lost money for two years, so we cut our losses and closed it.<br>店里亏了两年，我们只好止损关门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lost</b></td><td>ˌall is not ˈlost (saying)</td><td>尚有一线希望</td><td>We missed the deadline, but all is not lost—they'll accept late entries.<br>我们错过了截止日期，但还有希望，他们收迟交的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be lost for ˈwords</td><td>（惊讶得）不知说什么才好</td><td>He was lost for words when the whole street turned up to help.<br>整条街的人都来帮忙，他感动得说不出话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈlost in sth</td><td>全神贯注于；沉浸于</td><td>She was lost in her book and didn't hear the doorbell at all.<br>她看书入了神，压根没听见门铃。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈlost on sb</td><td>未被某人领会；对某人不起作用</td><td>The joke about the tax code was completely lost on the children.<br>那个关于税法的笑话，孩子们根本没听懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be lost to the ˈworld</td><td>浑然忘我；不理会周围一切</td><td>With his headphones on, he's lost to the world for hours at a time.<br>戴上耳机，他能一连几个小时与世隔绝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/feel ˈlost without sb/sth</td><td>没有…就不知所措</td><td>I'd be lost without my phone's calendar—I can't remember a single date.<br>没了手机日历我就抓瞎，什么日子都记不住。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get ˈlost! (informal)</td><td>走开；滚开</td><td>I told the guy selling fake tickets to get lost before I called security.<br>我叫那个卖假票的滚开，不然就叫保安。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/sth up for ˈlost (formal)</td><td>认定…已无望找回；认定某人已死</td><td>After ten days the rescuers had almost given the climbers up for lost.<br>十天过后，救援队几乎认定那些登山者已经遇难。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a lost ˈcause</td><td>注定失败的事；败局已定的目标</td><td>Teaching my father to use video calls is frankly a lost cause.<br>教我爸用视频通话，说实话是件没指望的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make up for lost ˈtime</td><td>把耽误的时间补回来</td><td>After a year apart, they travelled everywhere together to make up for lost time.<br>分开一年后，他们四处同游，把耽误的时光补回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lot</b></td><td>a bad ˈlot (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>坏家伙；不老实的人</td><td>Her second husband was a bad lot who ran off with her savings.<br>她的第二任丈夫不是好东西，卷走了她的积蓄。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by ˈlot</td><td>以抽签方式；用抓阄的办法</td><td>The last two tickets were given out by lot among the waiting fans.<br>最后两张票是在等候的粉丝中抽签发放的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from a container and the one whose paper has</td><td>从容器中抽签决定</td><td>Each name is drawn from a container and the one whose paper has a cross wins.<br>名字从容器里抽出，纸上画叉的那位获胜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw in your ˈlot with sb</td><td>与某人共命运；与某人同甘共苦</td><td>He threw in his lot with the strikers even though it cost him his job.<br>他和罢工者站到一起，哪怕因此丢了工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lots</b></td><td>cast/draw ˈlots (for sth/to do sth)</td><td>抽签决定；抓阄</td><td>We drew lots to decide who would sleep on the sofa that night.<br>我们抓阄决定那晚谁睡沙发。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>loud</b></td><td>loud and ˈclear (informal)</td><td>清清楚楚；十分明白</td><td>The message from the voters came through loud and clear last night.<br>昨晚选民传递的信号清清楚楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌout ˈloud</td><td>出声地；大声地</td><td>He read the letter out loud so everyone at the table could hear.<br>他把信念出声来，好让桌边的人都听见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>love</b></td><td>(just) for ˈlove/for the ˈlove of sth</td><td>出于爱好；无偿；不图回报</td><td>She coaches the village team just for love, not for a single penny.<br>她带村里的球队纯粹出于喜欢，一分钱不收。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for the love of ˈGod (old-fashioned, spoken)</td><td>看在上帝的份上（表示愤怒或不耐烦）</td><td>For the love of God, will someone turn that alarm off?<br>看在上帝的份上，谁去把那警报关了行吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give/send my love to sb (informal)</td><td>代我向某人问好</td><td>Give my love to your parents when you get home for the holiday.<br>放假回家时代我向你父母问好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>love at first ˈsight</td><td>一见钟情</td><td>It was love at first sight—he proposed six weeks after they met.<br>那是一见钟情，认识六周他就求婚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈlove from • lots of ˈlove (from) (written, informal)</td><td>（书信结尾）爱你的；此致爱意</td><td>She ended every postcard with 'lots of love from your silly aunt'.<br>她每张明信片都以“爱你的傻姑姑”结尾。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>love is ˈblind (saying)</td><td>情人眼里出西施；爱是盲目的</td><td>Everyone can see he's using her, but love is blind, I suppose.<br>谁都看得出他在利用她，可惜爱是盲目的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>love you and ˈleave you (spoken, humorous)</td><td>（想留却得走）我得先走了</td><td>This has been fun, but I must love you and leave you—last train's at eleven.<br>聊得真开心，可我得走了，末班车十一点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈlove (to sb)</td><td>（与某人）做爱</td><td>They made love for the first time in a freezing flat with no heating.<br>他们第一次做爱是在一间没暖气的冰冷公寓里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not for love or/nor ˈmoney (informal)</td><td>无论如何也不；说什么也不</td><td>You couldn't get a taxi that night for love nor money.<br>那天晚上你无论如何也叫不到出租车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no ˈlove lost between A and B (informal)</td><td>彼此厌恶；互无好感</td><td>There's no love lost between the two coaches since last season's final.<br>自上赛季决赛以来，两位教练彼此厌恶。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lovely</b></td><td>lovely and ˈwarm, ˈcold, ˈquiet, etc. (BrE, spoken)</td><td>非常暖和（或凉快、安静等）</td><td>Come inside, it's lovely and warm by the fire in here.<br>快进来，这儿炉火边可暖和了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>low</b></td><td>be/run ˈlow (on sth)</td><td>（某物）快用完了；所剩无几</td><td>We're running low on coffee, so add a jar to the shopping list.<br>咖啡快没了，购物单上加一罐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(at) a low ˈebb</td><td>处于低潮；状况不佳</td><td>Morale in the department was at a low ebb after the third round of cuts.<br>第三轮裁员后，部门士气跌到了谷底。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>low-down</b></td><td>give sb/get the ˈlow-down (on sb/sth)</td><td>告知（或得知）内情</td><td>Sit down and give me the low-down on your new boss.<br>坐下来，跟我讲讲你新上司的底细。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lower</b></td><td>lower the ˈtone (of sth)</td><td>降低（某场合、作品的）格调</td><td>One rude joke like that can lower the tone of the whole evening.<br>那样一个粗俗笑话就能把整晚的格调拉低。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈlower yourself (by doing sth)</td><td>降低身份；自贬人格</td><td>I won't lower myself by arguing with strangers in the comments.<br>我不会自降身份，去跟评论区的陌生人吵架。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>luck</b></td><td>any ˈluck? (spoken)</td><td>有戏吗；运气如何</td><td>Any luck with the job applications you sent out last week?<br>上周投的那些简历有消息了吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be down on your ˈluck (informal)</td><td>时运不济；穷困潦倒</td><td>He's been down on his luck since the restaurant closed last winter.<br>自从去年冬天餐馆关门，他就一直不走运。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth for ˈluck</td><td>为求吉利而做某事</td><td>She always touches the doorframe for luck before an exam.<br>她考试前总要摸一下门框讨个吉利。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>good ˈluck (with sth) (spoken)</td><td>祝好运；祝成功</td><td>Good luck with your driving test—remember to check the mirrors.<br>祝你路考顺利，记得看后视镜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>good ˈluck to sb (spoken)</td><td>祝某人走运；随他去吧</td><td>If he wants to cycle across Mongolia, good luck to him.<br>他要骑车穿越蒙古，那就祝他好运吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you're in ˈluck • your ˈluck is in</td><td>你走运了；运气来了</td><td>You're in luck—there's exactly one seat left on the evening train.<br>你走运了，晚班车刚好还剩一个座位。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the luck of the ˈdevil • the luck of the ˈIrish</td><td>运气好得出奇</td><td>He walked away from that crash with the luck of the devil.<br>那场车祸他毫发无伤，运气好得出奇。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌluck of the ˈdraw</td><td>全凭运气；碰运气的事</td><td>Which examiner you get is just the luck of the draw.<br>碰上哪个考官，全凭运气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no such ˈluck (informal)</td><td>没那么走运；可惜没有</td><td>I hoped the meeting was cancelled, but no such luck.<br>我盼着会议取消，可惜没那么走运。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tough/bad ˈluck (informal)</td><td>真不走运；活该（视语气而定）</td><td>Tough luck about the concert tickets—they sold out in four minutes.<br>演唱会门票四分钟就没了，真不走运。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ump</b></td><td>have a ˈlump in your throat</td><td>（激动得）喉咙哽住</td><td>I had a lump in my throat watching my daughter walk onto the stage.<br>看着女儿走上台，我喉咙一阵发哽。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>umps</b></td><td>take your ˈlumps (AmE, informal)</td><td>承受打击；甘愿挨批</td><td>He made the mistake, so he'll have to take his lumps at the meeting.<br>错是他犯的，会上挨批他就得受着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lunatic</b></td><td>the lunatic ˈfringe (disapproving)</td><td>（团体中的）极端分子；狂热的少数人</td><td>Most members are reasonable; it's the lunatic fringe that gets on television.<br>多数成员都很理性，上电视的偏偏是那帮极端分子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌout to ˈlunch (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>神志不清；糊里糊涂</td><td>Whoever priced this flat at two million is completely out to lunch.<br>把这套公寓标价两百万的人脑子进水了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lurch</b></td><td>leave sb in the ˈlurch (informal)</td><td>在危难时弃某人不顾</td><td>She quit two days before the show and left the whole cast in the lurch.<br>她在演出前两天辞演，把全组人晾在那里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lying</b></td><td>(not) take sth lying ˈdown (informal)</td><td>（不）甘心忍受；（不）逆来顺受</td><td>They cut his hours without warning, and he won't take it lying down.<br>他们不打招呼就减他工时，他可不会忍气吞声。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mad</b></td><td>be mad ˈkeen (on sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>对…极其着迷</td><td>My nephew is mad keen on dinosaurs and can name about forty.<br>我侄子对恐龙着迷得很，能说出四十来种。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) mad as a ˈhatter</td><td>疯疯癫癫；十足的疯子</td><td>The old man who feeds the crows is as mad as a hatter, but harmless.<br>那个喂乌鸦的老头疯疯癫癫，不过没有恶意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) mad as a March ˈhare (informal)</td><td>疯疯癫癫；举止怪异</td><td>She danced through the office in slippers, mad as a March hare.<br>她穿着拖鞋在办公室里跳舞，简直疯疯癫癫。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>made</b></td><td>be made ˈup (about/with sth) (BrE, informal)</td><td>对某事非常满意；乐坏了</td><td>He was made up about getting into his first-choice university.<br>考上第一志愿的大学，他乐坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have it ˈmade (informal)</td><td>稳操胜券；万事俱备</td><td>With a paid-off house and a pension like that, he's got it made.<br>房贷还清，还有那样的退休金，他这辈子不愁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be) ˈmade for sb/each other</td><td>非常般配；天生一对</td><td>Those two argue about films all night—they're made for each other.<br>那两个人整晚争论电影，真是天生一对。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what sb is ˈmade of (informal)</td><td>某人的真本事；某人有几分能耐</td><td>The final round will show us what this young boxer is made of.<br>最后一轮就能看出这个年轻拳手到底有几分能耐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Go out and show them what you're made of</td><td>出去让他们见识你的本事</td><td>Go out and show them what you're made of—you've trained all year for this.<br>出去让他们见识见识你的本事，你练了一整年就为这个。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>magic</b></td><td>(have) a/the magic ˈtouch</td><td>有过人的本领；有点石成金的本事</td><td>She has the magic touch with nervous dogs; they calm down instantly.<br>她对付胆小的狗有一手，狗一见她就安静了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>maid</b></td><td>an old ˈmaid</td><td>老处女；未婚的老姑娘</td><td>At thirty her aunts already called her an old maid, which infuriated her.<br>她三十岁时姑姑们就叫她老姑娘，把她气坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>main</b></td><td>in the ˈmain</td><td>大体上；基本上</td><td>In the main, the students were polite, though a few arrived late.<br>总体来说学生都很有礼貌，只有几个迟到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make</b></td><td>make as if to do sth (written)</td><td>做出要做某事的样子</td><td>He made as if to leave, then sat back down and ordered another beer.<br>他做出要走的样子，又坐下再要了一杯啤酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈbreak for it (informal)</td><td>趁机逃跑；夺路而逃</td><td>When the guard turned his back, the two men made a break for it.<br>警卫一转身，那两人就撒腿跑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈdo (with sth) • make sth ˈdo</td><td>凑合；将就着用</td><td>There's no rice left, so we'll make do with noodles tonight.<br>米没了，今晚就将就吃面吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈgo of sth (informal)</td><td>把某事做成功</td><td>They're determined to make a go of the bakery despite the rent.<br>尽管房租很高，他们还是决心把面包店做起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈgood (informal)</td><td>发家致富；白手起家获得成功</td><td>He left the village with nothing and made good in the shipping trade.<br>他身无分文离开村子，靠海运生意发了家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make good sth</td><td>赔偿；修复；兑现（诺言）</td><td>The builder promised to make good the damage to our garden wall.<br>建筑商答应把我们花园墙的损坏修好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>mechanic explained that they would have to ˈmake it</td><td>成功；赶到；活下来</td><td>Two of the three startups failed, but hers actually made it.<br>三家创业公司倒了两家，她那家真做成了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈmake it with sb (AmE, slang)</td><td>与某人发生性关系</td><td>He kept bragging that he'd made it with the singer, which nobody believed.<br>他一直吹嘘和那位歌手上过床，没人信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make the ˈmost of sth</td><td>充分利用；尽情享受</td><td>The sun's finally out—let's make the most of it and eat outside.<br>太阳总算出来了，咱们抓紧到外面吃饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make the ˈmost of yourself, himself, etc.</td><td>充分展示自己的长处</td><td>A decent haircut helps you make the most of yourself at interviews.<br>剪个像样的头发，面试时能更好地展现自己。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈmuch of sb/sth (written)</td><td>重视；大肆宣扬</td><td>The papers made much of his humble background during the campaign.<br>竞选期间报纸大肆渲染他出身寒微。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make nothing ˈof sth</td><td>不理解；不把…当回事</td><td>I read the contract twice and could make nothing of clause nine.<br>合同我读了两遍，第九条完全看不懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>The more he thought about it, the less he under-</td><td>越想越糊涂</td><td>The more he thought about it, the less he understood her sudden silence.<br>他越琢磨，越不明白她为何突然沉默。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make or ˈbreak (informal)</td><td>成败攸关；决定成败</td><td>This launch will make or break the company, so nobody's sleeping much.<br>这次发布决定公司成败，大家都睡不好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈmake something of yourself</td><td>有所成就；事业有成</td><td>His mother worked two jobs so he could make something of himself.<br>他母亲打两份工，就为了让他有出息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈmake (informal, disapproving)</td><td>一心谋私利；追名逐利</td><td>Half the people at that party were politicians on the make.<br>那场聚会上一半人是钻营名利的政客。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>making</b></td><td>be the ˈmaking of sb/sth</td><td>是某人（或某事）成功的关键</td><td>Two years in the countryside were the making of that spoiled boy.<br>在乡下的两年成就了那个被宠坏的男孩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈmaking</td><td>在形成中；在酝酿中</td><td>Watching her rehearse, you can see a fine violinist in the making.<br>看她排练就知道，一位出色的小提琴家正在成长。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of your own ˈmaking</td><td>自己造成的；自作自受</td><td>The debt crisis at the club was entirely of their own making.<br>俱乐部的债务危机完全是他们自己造成的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>makings</b></td><td>have the ˈmakings of sth</td><td>具备成为…的条件</td><td>That kid has the makings of a first-class goalkeeper if he keeps training.<br>那孩子要是坚持练，会成为一流门将。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>malice</b></td><td>with ˌmalice aˈforethought (law)</td><td>蓄意；预谋</td><td>The prosecution argued he acted with malice aforethought, not in panic.<br>控方主张他是蓄意行凶，而非惊慌失措。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>man</b></td><td>be sb's ˈman/ˈwoman</td><td>是（做某事）最合适的人选</td><td>If you need someone to fix that old boiler, Tom's your man.<br>要修那台老锅炉，找汤姆准没错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈman enough (to do sth/for sth)</td><td>有足够的勇气（做某事）</td><td>Be man enough to apologize to her in person, not by text.<br>拿出点担当，当面跟她道歉，别发短信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be no good/use to ˈman or ˈbeast (informal)</td><td>毫无用处；一无是处</td><td>This rusted old lawnmower is no use to man or beast now.<br>这台生锈的旧割草机现在一点用都没有了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be your own ˈman/woman</td><td>独立自主；有主见</td><td>Since going freelance she's finally her own woman again.<br>自从做了自由职业，她终于又能自己做主了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>every man has his ˈprice • everyone has</td><td>人皆有价；人人都可能被收买</td><td>The lawyer smiled and said every man has his price, including judges.<br>律师笑着说人皆有价，法官也不例外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>their ˈprice (saying)</td><td>人皆有价；重赏之下必有勇夫</td><td>Offer enough and everyone has their price, or so the cynics claim.<br>出价够高，人人都有价，愤世嫉俗者如是说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's every ˌman for himˈself (saying)</td><td>各人顾各人；人人自顾</td><td>When the funding was cut, it was every man for himself in that department.<br>经费一砍，那个部门就人人自顾了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈman of/out of sb</td><td>使某人成为男子汉；使人长大成人</td><td>His father thought two winters at sea would make a man of him.<br>他父亲认为在海上过两个冬天能让他成为男子汉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˌman about ˈtown</td><td>交际场上的活跃人物；社交名流</td><td>In his thirties he was a man about town who knew every club owner.<br>三十多岁时他是个社交场上的活跃人物，认识每家夜店老板。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>man and ˈboy</td><td>从小到大；一辈子</td><td>He worked at that mill man and boy for forty-two years.<br>他从小到大在那家工厂干了四十二年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌman (and/or ˌwoman) in the ˈstreet</td><td>普通人；老百姓</td><td>The man in the street cares about rent, not about party slogans.<br>老百姓关心的是房租，不是政党口号。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌClapham ˈomnibus (old-fashioned)</td><td>普通人；平民百姓</td><td>Would the man on the Clapham omnibus think this contract fair?<br>普通百姓会觉得这份合同公平吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌman of ˈGod/the ˈcloth (old-fashioned, formal)</td><td>神职人员；牧师</td><td>As a man of the cloth, he was expected to visit the sick weekly.<br>身为神职人员，他每周都要去探望病人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌman of the ˈmatch (BrE, sport)</td><td>（比赛的）最佳球员</td><td>The keeper saved two penalties and was named man of the match.<br>门将扑出两个点球，当选全场最佳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌman of the ˈpeople</td><td>体察民情的人；平民出身的领袖</td><td>He rides the bus to work and calls himself a man of the people.<br>他坐公交上班，自称是体察民情的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌman of ˈstraw</td><td>懦夫；无足轻重的人</td><td>The new chairman turned out to be a man of straw with no real authority.<br>新任主席原来是个没有实权的软弱角色。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>man to ˈman</td><td>（男人之间）坦诚地；开诚布公地</td><td>Let's talk man to man about why you've been avoiding the office.<br>咱们男人之间坦白讲，你为什么老躲着办公室。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>man's best ˈfriend</td><td>人类最好的朋友（指狗）</td><td>After the rescue, everyone agreed the dog was truly man's best friend.<br>救援之后，大家都说狗真是人类最好的朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈman's man</td><td>更受男人欢迎的男人</td><td>He's a man's man—football, beer and very little small talk.<br>他是那种典型的男人堆里的男人：足球、啤酒，很少闲聊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one man's ˌmeat is another man's ˈpoison (saying)</td><td>各人口味不同；甲之蜜糖，乙之砒霜</td><td>He loves durian and I can't stand it—one man's meat is another man's poison.<br>他爱吃榴莲我却受不了，真是各人口味不同。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to a ˈman (written)</td><td>一致地；无一例外</td><td>The committee voted, to a man, against selling the old library.<br>委员会一致投票反对出售那座旧图书馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you can't keep a good man ˈdown (saying)</td><td>有本事的人终会出头</td><td>He lost everything in the fire and reopened a year later—you can't keep a good man down.<br>一场火烧光了他的一切，一年后他又开张了，有能耐的人压不垮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rent</td><td>租金；房租</td><td>Half my salary goes on rent for a flat the size of a shoebox.<br>我半份工资都交了房租，房子却小得像鞋盒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>There are a great many places in the world I'd</td><td>世界上有许多地方我想去</td><td>There are a great many places in the world I'd like to visit before forty.<br>世界上有很多地方我想在四十岁前去看看。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>map</b></td><td>(be) off the ˈmap</td><td>偏僻；远离闹市</td><td>Their farmhouse is completely off the map—no signal, no neighbours.<br>他们的农舍偏僻得很，没信号，也没邻居。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb/sth on the ˈmap</td><td>使出名；使受到重视</td><td>One viral video put the tiny noodle shop on the map overnight.<br>一条爆红视频让这家小面馆一夜成名。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>marbles</b></td><td>lose your ˈmarbles (informal)</td><td>精神失常；发疯</td><td>Selling the car to buy a boat? Have you lost your marbles?<br>卖车买船？你是不是疯了？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>March</td><td>三月</td><td>We're moving house in March, right after the lease runs out.<br>我们三月搬家，正好租约到期。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>march</b></td><td>march to (the beat of) a different</td><td>特立独行；与众不同</td><td>She's always marched to a different beat, wearing red boots to funerals.<br>她从来特立独行，参加葬礼都穿红靴子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈdrummer/drum (also march to a different ˈtune less frequent)</td><td>与众不同；另有一套想法</td><td>He marches to a different drummer and refuses every trend going.<br>他自有一套，任何潮流都不跟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>marching</td><td>行进；行军</td><td>The band kept marching down the street despite the pouring rain.<br>尽管大雨倾盆，乐队仍沿街行进。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈmarching orders (BrE, informal)</td><td>被解雇；被赶走</td><td>After three warnings about lateness, he finally got his marching orders.<br>迟到被警告三次后，他终于被辞退了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb their ˈmarching orders (BrE, informal)</td><td>解雇某人；命令某人走人</td><td>She gave her business partner his marching orders after the audit.<br>审计之后，她让合伙人卷铺盖走人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mare</b></td><td>a ˈmare's nest</td><td>看似重大实则无用的发现；混乱局面</td><td>The investigation turned up a mare's nest of rumours and no facts.<br>调查挖出一堆传言，全无实据，白忙一场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mark</b></td><td>be close to/near the ˈmark</td><td>接近准确；八九不离十</td><td>Your guess of two thousand yuan was pretty close to the mark.<br>你猜两千块，已经八九不离十了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌquick/ˌslow off the ˈmark</td><td>反应快（或慢）；行动敏捷（或迟缓）</td><td>You have to be quick off the mark to get concert tickets these days.<br>现在抢演唱会门票，手慢就没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get off the ˈmark</td><td>开始得分；起步</td><td>The striker finally got off the mark in his eighth game for the club.<br>这名前锋加盟后第八场比赛终于开了张。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make your ˈmark</td><td>崭露头角；扬名</td><td>She made her mark as a designer before she turned twenty-five.<br>她二十五岁前就在设计界崭露头角。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmark my ˈwords (old-fashioned, spoken)</td><td>记住我的话；听我一句</td><td>Mark my words, that bridge will need repairs within five years.<br>记住我的话，那座桥不出五年就得修。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>mark ˈtime</td><td>原地踏步；等待时机</td><td>He's just marking time in that job until his visa comes through.<br>他在那份工作上原地踏步，就等签证下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>mark ˈyou (old-fashioned, spoken, especially BrE)</td><td>请注意；不过话说回来</td><td>He paid for dinner, mark you, which he's never done before.<br>他请了客，注意啊，这可是头一回。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌup to the ˈmark</td><td>达到标准；合格</td><td>The kitchen wasn't up to the mark, so the inspector closed the café.<br>厨房不达标，检查员把咖啡馆关了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>marked</b></td><td>a marked ˈman</td><td>被盯上的人；成为攻击目标的人</td><td>After testifying against the gang, he was a marked man in that city.<br>指证那伙人之后，他在那座城市就成了被盯上的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>market</b></td><td>in the ˈmarket for sth (informal)</td><td>有意购买；正想买</td><td>We're in the market for a used van big enough for the band.<br>我们想买辆二手面包车，得装得下乐队的家伙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈmarket</td><td>上市；有售；待售</td><td>Their house has been on the market since last spring with no offers.<br>他们的房子从去年春天挂到现在，无人出价。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play the ˈmarket</td><td>做股票投机；炒股</td><td>He started playing the market with his student loan, which ended badly.<br>他拿助学贷款去炒股，结果很惨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>marks</b></td><td>on your ˌmarks, get ˌset, ˈgo!</td><td>各就位，预备，跑！</td><td>The teacher shouted 'on your marks, get set, go!' and the children sprinted off.<br>老师喊“各就位，预备，跑！”，孩子们冲了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>marrow</b></td><td>chill sb to the ˈbone/ˈmarrow</td><td>使某人冷彻骨髓；使不寒而栗</td><td>The scream from the empty stairwell chilled us to the marrow.<br>空楼梯间传来的尖叫让我们不寒而栗。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>marry</b></td><td>marry in ˈhaste (, repent at ˈleisure) (saying)</td><td>结婚匆忙，后悔漫长</td><td>They married after six weeks—marry in haste, repent at leisure, as they say.<br>他们认识六周就结婚，正应了那句：结婚太急，后悔莫及。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>marry ˈmoney</td><td>嫁（或娶）有钱人</td><td>Her cousin married money and hasn't worked a day since.<br>她表姐嫁了个有钱人，从此一天班都没上过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mass</b></td><td>be a ˈmass of sth</td><td>布满；充满</td><td>By June the hillside is a mass of wild orange poppies.<br>到六月，山坡上开满了野生的橙色罂粟花。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>master</b></td><td>be your own ˈmaster/ˈmistress</td><td>自己作主；独立自主</td><td>Running the shop alone is hard, but at least I'm my own master.<br>一个人开店很辛苦，但至少我自己说了算。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mat</b></td><td>take sb/sth to the ˈmat (AmE, informal)</td><td>与…激烈争辩；与…较量到底</td><td>The union is ready to take management to the mat over overtime pay.<br>工会准备为加班费和资方斗到底。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lay, put, roll, etc. out the welcome ˈmat</td><td>热情欢迎；隆重接待</td><td>The village rolled out the welcome mat for the returning soldiers.<br>村里张灯结彩，热情迎接归来的士兵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be no ˈmatch for sb/sth</td><td>不是…的对手；比不上</td><td>Our little team was no match for the champions last Saturday.<br>上周六我们这支小队根本不是冠军队的对手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be as good, etc. as sb/sth; not be able to</td><td>不如；比不过</td><td>Cheap copies are not as good as the original and can't be repaired.<br>廉价仿品不如原版，还没法修。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>match for the Japanese when it comes to making</td><td>在制造方面比不上（日本人）</td><td>We're no match for the Japanese when it comes to making precision lenses.<br>论精密镜头制造，我们比不过日本人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>find/meet your ˈmatch (in sb)</td><td>遇到旗鼓相当的对手</td><td>The chess champion finally met his match in a twelve-year-old girl.<br>这位象棋冠军最终败给了一个十二岁的女孩。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>matter</b></td><td>as a matter of ˈcourse</td><td>作为常规；理所当然地</td><td>The hotel changes the towels daily as a matter of course.<br>酒店照例每天更换毛巾。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as a matter of ˈfact (spoken)</td><td>事实上；其实</td><td>As a matter of fact, today happens to be my fortieth birthday.<br>事实上，今天正好是我四十岁生日。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(do sth) as a matter of ˈform</td><td>作为例行公事</td><td>They asked for my ID as a matter of form, then waved me through.<br>他们例行公事查了我的证件，就放我过去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be another/a different ˈmatter</td><td>是另一回事；另当别论</td><td>Reading Chinese is fine; speaking it fluently is another matter entirely.<br>读中文没问题，但流利地说完全是另一回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be the ˈmatter (with sb/sth)</td><td>（某人或某物）出了问题</td><td>You look pale—what's the matter with you this morning?<br>你脸色发白，今天早上怎么了？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be a matter of oˈpinion</td><td>见仁见智；看法因人而异</td><td>Whether the film is a masterpiece is very much a matter of opinion.<br>这部电影算不算杰作，实在见仁见智。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈfact/ˈtruth of the matter</td><td>事实真相；实情是</td><td>The truth of the matter is that nobody checked the figures.<br>事实真相是，根本没人核对过数字。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈthat matter (spoken)</td><td>就此而言；其实也一样</td><td>I've never been to Paris, or to France for that matter.<br>我没去过巴黎，其实整个法国都没去过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a matter of ˈdays, ˈmiles, ˈpounds, etc.</td><td>只有几天（或几英里、几镑等）</td><td>The nearest hospital is a matter of miles away, luckily for us.<br>最近的医院不过几英里，我们算走运。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a particular number of days, miles, etc., espe-</td><td>只有若干天（或英里等）</td><td>It took a particular number of days, miles and arguments to get there.<br>到那儿花了整整几天、几百英里，还吵了不少架。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no matter who, what, where, when, etc.</td><td>无论谁（或什么、何处、何时）</td><td>No matter what she says, don't lend him money again.<br>不管她怎么说，都别再借钱给他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>matters</b></td><td>take matters into your own ˈhands</td><td>自己动手解决；自行处理</td><td>The council ignored the potholes, so residents took matters into their own hands.<br>市政不管坑洼路面，居民只好自己动手修。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>max</b></td><td>to the ˈmax</td><td>最大限度地；到极点</td><td>He pushed the old engine to the max and it finally gave out.<br>他把那台老发动机催到极限，它终于报废了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>may</b></td><td>be that as it ˈmay • that's</td><td>尽管如此；即便这样</td><td>Be that as it may, we still have to hand the report in tomorrow.<br>尽管如此，我们明天还是得交报告。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mccoy</b></td><td>the real McˈCoy (informal)</td><td>真货；货真价实的东西</td><td>This isn't a copy—the violin is the real McCoy, made in 1890.<br>这不是仿品，这把小提琴货真价实，1890年制。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mea</b></td><td>mea ˈculpa (from Latin, often humorous)</td><td>是我的错；我认错</td><td>Mea culpa—I booked the tickets for the wrong weekend entirely.<br>是我的错，我把票订到了另一个周末。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>meal</b></td><td>make a ˈmeal of/out of sth (informal)</td><td>小题大做；把事情弄得过于复杂</td><td>It's one email; don't make a meal of it and rewrite it six times.<br>就一封邮件，别小题大做改上六遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈmeal ticket (informal)</td><td>饭票；供养自己的人或物</td><td>He treated his older girlfriend as little more than a meal ticket.<br>他把年长的女友几乎只当成一张长期饭票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mean</b></td><td>be no mean... (approving)</td><td>是很了不起的…；相当出色的…</td><td>She's no mean cook—that dumpling stall of hers has queues every night.<br>她厨艺可不含糊，那个饺子摊每晚都排队。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/mean ˈnothing to sb</td><td>对某人不重要；某人毫不在意</td><td>Those old awards mean nothing to him now that his kids are grown.<br>孩子都大了，那些旧奖项对他已毫无意义。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the happy/golden ˈmean (approving)</td><td>中庸之道；折中之道</td><td>Between strict dieting and eating whatever, she found the golden mean.<br>在严格节食和放开吃之间，她找到了中庸之道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>mean ˈbusiness (informal)</td><td>是认真的；说到做到</td><td>When the landlord changed the locks, we knew he meant business.<br>房东把锁换了，我们就知道他是来真的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be serious about what you plan to do; be deter-</td><td>对计划认真；下定决心</td><td>You have to be serious about what you plan to do, or nobody will back you.<br>你得认真对待自己的计划，否则没人支持你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>mean to ˈsay</td><td>（强调）我是说；难道说</td><td>Do you mean to say you walked home twelve miles in the rain?<br>你是说你冒雨走了十二英里回家？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get sb's ˈmeaning (informal)</td><td>领会某人的意思</td><td>He glanced at the clock twice, and I got his meaning and left.<br>他看了两次钟，我明白了他的意思就走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know the meaning of the ˈword</td><td>根本不懂…；完全不知何为…</td><td>My brother works weekends—he doesn't know the meaning of the word rest.<br>我哥连周末都干活，他根本不懂什么叫休息。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>means</b></td><td>by ˈall means (spoken)</td><td>当然可以；请便</td><td>By all means borrow the car, just fill the tank before you return it.<br>车尽管借去开，还的时候把油加满就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by ˈno (manner of) means • not by ˈany</td><td>绝不；一点也不</td><td>The deal is by no means settled, so don't celebrate yet.<br>这笔交易远未敲定，先别庆祝。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>meant</b></td><td>be meant to be sth</td><td>据说是；本应是</td><td>That new ramen place is meant to be the best in the city.<br>那家新开的拉面店据说是全城最好的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>meantime</b></td><td>in the ˈmeantime/ˈmeanwhile</td><td>在此期间；与此同时</td><td>The doctor sees you at four; in the meantime, grab a coffee downstairs.<br>医生四点见你，这期间你先去楼下喝杯咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>measure</b></td><td>the whole of sth or less of sth than you expect</td><td>足量；或不足量</td><td>You may get the whole of something or less of something than you expect.<br>你可能拿到足量，也可能比预期的少。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/have/take the ˈmeasure of sb • get/</td><td>摸清某人的底细；掂出某人的分量</td><td>After two meetings she had the measure of her new boss completely.<br>开了两次会，她就把新上司摸透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/take sb's ˈmeasure (formal)</td><td>看透某人；估量某人的能力</td><td>The old coach took the boy's measure in a single training session.<br>老教练一堂训练课就看出了这男孩的斤两。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in great, large, etc. ˈmeasure (formal)</td><td>在很大程度上</td><td>The project's success was in large measure due to volunteers.<br>项目的成功在很大程度上要归功于志愿者。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in some, equal, etc. ˈmeasure (formal)</td><td>在某种（或同等）程度上</td><td>Both parents are in equal measure responsible for the mess.<br>这烂摊子父母双方要负同等责任。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make sth to ˈmeasure (BrE)</td><td>定做；量身定制</td><td>His suits are made to measure by a tailor in the old town.<br>他的西装是老城区一位裁缝量身定做的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>meat</b></td><td>be meat and ˈdrink (to sb)</td><td>是某人的一大乐事；正合某人胃口</td><td>Arguing about politics at dinner is meat and drink to my uncle.<br>饭桌上争论政治，正是我舅舅的一大乐事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>medicine</b></td><td>give sb a taste/dose of their own ˈmedicine</td><td>以其人之道还治其人之身</td><td>She ignored his calls for a week, giving him a dose of his own medicine.<br>她一周不接他电话，让他也尝尝被冷落的滋味。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take your ˈmedicine (like a ˈman) (usually humorous)</td><td>甘愿受罚；忍受不快</td><td>You broke the window, so take your medicine and tell your dad.<br>窗户是你打破的，认了吧，去告诉你爸。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>meet</b></td><td>meet the/your ˈeye(s)</td><td>映入眼帘；呈现在眼前</td><td>A sea of broken glass met our eyes when we opened the door.<br>门一开，满地碎玻璃映入眼帘。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>meet sb's ˈeyes (also meet sb's ˈgaze, ˈlook, etc.)</td><td>与某人目光相遇；直视某人</td><td>He couldn't meet her eyes when she asked where the money went.<br>她问钱去哪儿了，他不敢与她对视。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>meet sb halfˈway</td><td>与某人妥协；各让一步</td><td>I wanted eight thousand, he offered six, so we met halfway.<br>我要八千，他出六千，最后各让一步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>meet your ˈMaker (especially humorous)</td><td>去见上帝；死</td><td>If I eat one more of these chillies, I'll meet my Maker tonight.<br>再吃一个这种辣椒，我今晚就得去见上帝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmeet your Waterˈloo</td><td>遭遇滑铁卢；一败涂地</td><td>The unbeaten team met their Waterloo against a squad of amateurs.<br>这支不败之师栽在了一群业余选手手里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>melt</b></td><td>ˌmelt in your ˈmouth</td><td>（食物）入口即化</td><td>The braised pork was so tender it melted in your mouth.<br>那道红烧肉嫩得入口即化。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>melting</b></td><td>in the ˈmelting pot (especially BrE)</td><td>处于变化之中；尚未定型</td><td>The team's plans for next season are still in the melting pot.<br>球队下赛季的计划仍在变动之中。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>memory</b></td><td>if ˌmemory ˈserves</td><td>如果我没记错的话</td><td>If memory serves, we last met at that awful conference in Leeds.<br>如果我没记错，我们上次见面是在利兹那场糟糕的会议上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go down/take sb down ˌmemory ˈlane •</td><td>追忆往事；重温旧梦</td><td>Those old photographs took us all down memory lane for an hour.<br>那些老照片让我们追忆往事，聊了一个钟头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a trip down ˌmemory ˈlane</td><td>重温往昔；追忆旧事</td><td>Visiting my old school was a real trip down memory lane.<br>重回母校，真是一次难忘的回忆之旅。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>getting</b></td><td>be getting better after an illness or injury</td><td>（病后或伤后）正在康复</td><td>She's getting better after an illness that kept her in bed for weeks.<br>她大病一场卧床数周，如今正在康复。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mend</b></td><td>be on the ˈmend (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>正在康复；渐渐好转</td><td>Jane was very ill, but she's on the mend and eating properly again.<br>简曾病得很重，现在正在康复，也能好好吃饭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mention</b></td><td>don't ˈmention it (spoken)</td><td>不客气；别放在心上</td><td>Don't mention it—driving you to the airport was no trouble at all.<br>别客气，送你去机场根本不费事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>mention sb/sth in the same ˈbreath</td><td>相提并论；等量齐观</td><td>You can't mention that pub band and a symphony orchestra in the same breath.<br>你不能把那个酒吧乐队和交响乐团相提并论。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not to mention sth</td><td>更不用说；且不说</td><td>The flat is tiny and damp, not to mention the noise from the road.<br>这公寓又小又潮，更别提路上的噪音了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mercy</b></td><td>(be) at the ˈmercy of sb/sth</td><td>任由…摆布；受…支配</td><td>Small farmers here are at the mercy of the weather every single year.<br>这里的小农年年都得看老天爷脸色。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have sb at your ˈmercy</td><td>使某人任由自己摆布</td><td>With the only key in his pocket, he had us at his mercy.<br>唯一的钥匙在他兜里，我们只能任他摆布。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave sb/sth to the mercy/mercies of sb/sth</td><td>把…丢给…任其摆布</td><td>They left the old dog to the mercy of the winter streets.<br>他们把那条老狗丢在寒冬的街头自生自灭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw yourself on sb's ˈmercy (formal)</td><td>请求某人宽恕；乞求某人开恩</td><td>He threw himself on the judge's mercy and asked for one more chance.<br>他向法官求情，请求再给一次机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>merge</b></td><td>merge into the ˈbackground</td><td>低调不张扬；不引人注意</td><td>At parties he merges into the background and watches everyone else.<br>聚会上他总是低调地待在一旁看别人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>merrier</b></td><td>the ˌmore the ˈmerrier (saying)</td><td>人越多越热闹；多多益善</td><td>Bring your cousins to the barbecue—the more the merrier.<br>把你表亲们也带来烧烤吧，人越多越热闹。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>merry</b></td><td>make ˈmerry (old-fashioned)</td><td>寻欢作乐；饮酒作乐</td><td>The villagers made merry in the square until well past midnight.<br>村民们在广场上尽情欢闹，直到后半夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mess</b></td><td>make a ˈmess/ˈhash of sth/of doing sth</td><td>把某事搞砸；弄得一团糟</td><td>I made a complete hash of the interview by arriving twenty minutes late.<br>我迟到二十分钟，把面试彻底搞砸了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>message</b></td><td>get the ˈmessage (BrE, informal)</td><td>领会暗示；听明白了</td><td>She kept looking at her watch until he finally got the message.<br>她不停看表，他终于会意了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>messing</b></td><td>ˌno ˈmessing (informal)</td><td>干脆利落；不含糊</td><td>He fixed the leak in ten minutes, no messing.<br>他十分钟就把漏水修好了，干脆利落。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>metal</b></td><td>keep/put the ˈpedal to the ˈmetal (AmE, informal)</td><td>全速前进；油门踩到底</td><td>We put the pedal to the metal and still reached the airport late.<br>我们一路油门踩到底，到机场还是晚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mettle</b></td><td>be on, show, prove, etc. your ˈmettle</td><td>显示自己的勇气和能力</td><td>The young surgeon showed her mettle during that twelve-hour operation.<br>那台十二小时的手术让这位年轻外科医生展现了真本事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb on their ˈmettle</td><td>激励某人全力以赴</td><td>A tough opponent puts you on your mettle better than any coach.<br>强劲的对手比任何教练都更能激发你的斗志。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mickey</b></td><td>take the ˈmickey/ˈmick (out of sb/sth) (BrE, informal)</td><td>取笑；戏弄</td><td>The lads took the mickey out of his new haircut all afternoon.<br>伙计们拿他的新发型取笑了一下午。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>microcosm</b></td><td>in ˈmicrocosm</td><td>以缩影的形式；具体而微地</td><td>That noisy little street shows the whole country's changes in microcosm.<br>那条嘈杂的小街就是整个国家变迁的缩影。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>midas</b></td><td>the ˈMidas touch</td><td>点石成金的本领；赚钱的本事</td><td>Every shop she opens turns a profit; the woman has the Midas touch.<br>她开的每家店都赚钱，这女人真有点石成金的本事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>middle</b></td><td>be in the middle of sth/of doing sth</td><td>正在做某事；正忙于</td><td>I was in the middle of dinner when your call came through.<br>你打电话来的时候我正在吃饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be sb's middle ˈname (informal)</td><td>是某人的突出特点</td><td>Patience is my middle name—I once queued six hours for tickets.<br>耐心是我的招牌，我曾为买票排过六小时队。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the middle ˈway</td><td>中间道路；折中之道</td><td>The mayor is looking for a middle way between the two angry camps.<br>市长正在两个对立阵营之间寻求折中之道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be/live) in the middle of ˈnowhere (informal)</td><td>住在偏远的地方；荒郊野岭</td><td>They bought a cottage in the middle of nowhere with no phone signal.<br>他们在荒郊野岭买了间小屋，连手机信号都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be) pig/piggy in the ˈmiddle (informal)</td><td>夹在两方之间左右为难</td><td>When my parents argue, I'm always piggy in the middle.<br>父母吵架时，我总是夹在中间受夹板气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>midst</b></td><td>in our, their, its, etc. ˈmidst (formal)</td><td>在我们（他们）中间</td><td>We had no idea there was a famous novelist in our midst.<br>我们完全不知道当中还有一位著名小说家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈmidst of sth/of doing sth</td><td>在…过程中；正当…之时</td><td>In the midst of packing, she realized her passport had expired.<br>正收拾行李时，她发现护照过期了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>midstream</b></td><td>in midˈstream</td><td>中途；进行到一半</td><td>He stopped the speech in midstream and asked for a glass of water.<br>他讲到一半停下来，要了杯水。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>might</b></td><td>might is ˈright (saying)</td><td>强权即公理</td><td>In that office might is right, and the loudest voice always wins.<br>在那个办公室里强权即公理，嗓门大的总赢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mildly</b></td><td>put it ˈmildly</td><td>说得婉转些；说得客气点</td><td>The meal was disappointing, to put it mildly, and cost a fortune.<br>那顿饭说得客气点叫令人失望，还贵得要命。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mile</b></td><td>go the ˌextra ˈmile (for sb/sth)</td><td>多付出一份努力；再加把劲</td><td>Our nurse went the extra mile and phoned every family personally.<br>我们的护士格外用心，挨个给家属打了电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run a ˈmile (from sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>避之唯恐不及；吓得逃开</td><td>Mention commitment and he'd run a mile in the opposite direction.<br>一提承诺，他就躲得远远的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see, spot, smell, etc. sth a ˈmile off (informal)</td><td>一眼就能看出；老远就察觉</td><td>You could spot that fake designer bag a mile off.<br>那个假名牌包老远就能看出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stand/stick out a ˈmile (informal)</td><td>极其明显；一眼就看得出</td><td>His nerves stuck out a mile during the whole presentation.<br>整场演讲中他的紧张显而易见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>miles</b></td><td>be ˈmiles apart</td><td>（观点等）大相径庭</td><td>The two sides are still miles apart on the question of pay.<br>双方在薪酬问题上仍然分歧巨大。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>miles apart on our understanding of the problem.</td><td>对问题的理解大相径庭</td><td>We are miles apart on our understanding of the problem, which slows everything down.<br>我们对问题的理解大相径庭，这拖慢了一切。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈmiles away (informal)</td><td>心不在焉；走神</td><td>Sorry, what did you say? I was miles away just then.<br>抱歉，你说什么？我刚才走神了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>miles from ˈanywhere/ˈnowhere</td><td>在偏远地方；荒无人烟</td><td>The car broke down miles from anywhere on a dark country road.<br>车在漆黑的乡间路上抛锚，四周荒无人烟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not a hundred/thousand/million ˈmiles (from here)</td><td>就在附近（间接指称某人某事）</td><td>The person who leaked it is not a million miles from this room.<br>泄密的人就在这屋里，不用往远处找。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'm talking about is not a hundred miles from</td><td>我说的这个就在近旁</td><td>The factory I'm talking about is not a hundred miles from where we stand.<br>我说的那家工厂离我们站的地方并不远。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>milk</b></td><td>the milk of human ˈkindness</td><td>人的善良天性；恻隐之心</td><td>After that phone call, the milk of human kindness had quite dried up in me.<br>接完那通电话，我心里那点善意全没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mill</b></td><td>go through/put sb through the ˈmill</td><td>经受磨练；使某人吃苦头</td><td>The new recruits were put through the mill during their first fortnight.<br>新兵在头两周吃尽了苦头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>million</b></td><td>look/feel like a million ˈdollars/ˈbucks</td><td>看上去（感觉）棒极了</td><td>In that new suit he looked like a million dollars at the reception.<br>穿上那套新西装，他在招待会上看起来神气极了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one, etc. in a ˈmillion</td><td>万里挑一；难得的人（或物）</td><td>A neighbour who shovels your snow is one in a million.<br>会替你铲雪的邻居，真是万里挑一。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>millstone</b></td><td>a millstone around/round sb's ˈneck</td><td>沉重的负担；甩不掉的累赘</td><td>That empty second flat became a millstone around their necks.<br>那套空置的第二套房成了他们甩不掉的包袱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mince</b></td><td>not mince your ˈwords (also not ˈmince matters)</td><td>直言不讳；说话不绕弯子</td><td>The coach didn't mince his words about our defending last night.<br>教练对我们昨晚的防守直言不讳，毫不留情。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mincemeat</b></td><td>make ˈmincemeat of sb/sth (informal)</td><td>彻底击败；驳得体无完肤</td><td>The lawyer made mincemeat of the witness in ten minutes.<br>律师十分钟就把证人驳得体无完肤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mind</b></td><td>at/in the ˌback of your ˈmind</td><td>隐约地；在潜意识里</td><td>At the back of my mind I knew the trip was a mistake.<br>我心里隐隐知道，这趟旅行是个错误。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all in sb's/the ˈmind</td><td>纯属想象；是自己吓自己</td><td>The doctor said the pain was all in my mind, which annoyed me.<br>医生说疼痛纯属心理作用，这话让我恼火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be of one/the same ˈmind (about/on sb/sth)</td><td>看法一致；意见相同</td><td>For once my sister and I are of one mind about selling the house.<br>这次我和姐姐难得在卖房子上意见一致。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/go ˌout of your ˈmind</td><td>发疯；精神失常</td><td>Swimming in that river in February? You're out of your mind.<br>二月在那条河里游泳？你疯了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bear/keep sb/sth in ˈmind • bear/keep in</td><td>把…记在心上；牢记</td><td>Keep in mind that the last bus leaves at half past eleven.<br>记住，末班车十一点半发车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈmind that...</td><td>记住…；牢记…</td><td>Bear in mind that the museum closes early on public holidays.<br>记住，博物馆节假日提前闭馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring/call sb/sth to ˈmind</td><td>使想起；令人记起</td><td>That smell of wet wool brings my grandmother's kitchen to mind.<br>湿羊毛的味道让我想起外婆的厨房。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come/spring to ˈmind</td><td>浮上心头；想起来</td><td>No good excuse came to mind, so I just told her the truth.<br>一时想不出好借口，我就跟她说了实话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do you ˈmind (if...)?</td><td>你介意吗（用于征求许可）</td><td>Do you mind if I open the window? It's stifling in here.<br>我开下窗你介意吗？这里太闷了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>don't mind ˈme</td><td>别管我；不用招呼我</td><td>Don't mind me, just carry on with your rehearsal.<br>别管我，你们继续排练。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give your ˈmind to sth</td><td>专心于某事；认真考虑</td><td>If you gave your mind to it, you'd finish that essay by lunchtime.<br>你要是专心去写，午饭前就能写完那篇文章。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go over sth in your ˈmind</td><td>在心里反复琢磨</td><td>She went over the conversation in her mind all the way home.<br>回家的一路上，她都在心里反复回想那段对话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a good mind to ˈdo sth • have half a mind to ˈdo sth</td><td>有点想做某事（但不一定去做）</td><td>I've half a mind to quit and open a bookshop by the sea.<br>我有点想辞职，去海边开家书店。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have sb/sth in ˈmind (for sth)</td><td>心中已有人选（或打算）</td><td>We have someone in mind for the job, but nothing's confirmed.<br>这职位我们心里有人选，不过还没定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have it in mind to do sth • have sth in</td><td>打算做某事；有意做某事</td><td>He's had it in mind to learn the guitar since he was twelve.<br>他从十二岁起就想学吉他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a mind of your ˈown</td><td>有主见；自己拿主意</td><td>My daughter is six and already has a mind of her own about clothes.<br>我女儿六岁，穿什么衣服已经很有主见了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your ˌmind on other ˈthings • your ˌmind is on other ˈthings</td><td>心有旁骛；走神</td><td>Sorry I missed the turning; my mind was on other things.<br>抱歉走错了路口，我刚才走神了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a mind to do sth</td><td>想要做某事；有意做某事</td><td>I have a mind to sell this old piano before we move.<br>搬家前我想把这架旧钢琴卖掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have sth on your ˈmind • sth is on your</td><td>心里惦记着某事；为某事发愁</td><td>You've clearly got something on your mind—out with it.<br>你显然有心事，说出来吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(spoken) ˈmind</td><td>心里挂念着；惦记着</td><td>Her son's exams have been on her mind for weeks.<br>儿子的考试让她惦记了好几个星期。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I don't mind adˈmitting, ˈtelling you..., etc.</td><td>我不妨承认（告诉你）</td><td>I don't mind admitting I cried at the end of that film.<br>我不妨承认，那部电影结尾我哭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I don't mind if I ˈdo (spoken, informal)</td><td>那我就不客气了；好啊</td><td>Another slice of cake? I don't mind if I do.<br>再来块蛋糕？那我就不客气了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if you ˌdon't ˈmind • if you ˌwouldn't ˈmind</td><td>如果你不介意（用于礼貌请求）</td><td>I'll take the window seat, if you don't mind.<br>如果你不介意，我坐靠窗的位子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if you ˌdon't mind me/my ˈsaying so...</td><td>恕我直言；你别介意我这么说</td><td>If you don't mind my saying so, that colour really doesn't suit you.<br>恕我直言，那个颜色真的不适合你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in your ˌmind's ˈeye</td><td>在脑海中；在想象中</td><td>In my mind's eye I can still see the old bridge before the flood.<br>在我脑海里，还能看见洪水前的那座老桥。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I wouldn't mind... (spoken)</td><td>我倒挺想…；我不介意…</td><td>I wouldn't mind a cold beer after carrying boxes all afternoon.<br>搬了一下午箱子，来杯冰啤酒倒是不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I wouldn't mind living abroad for a few years.</td><td>我倒想到国外住几年</td><td>I wouldn't mind living abroad for a few years while the kids are small.<br>趁孩子还小，我倒想去国外住几年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your mind on sth • your mind is on</td><td>专心于；集中注意力于</td><td>Keep your mind on the road and stop fiddling with the radio.<br>专心开车，别老摆弄收音机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(take) a load/weight off sb's mind</td><td>使人如释重负；心里石头落地</td><td>Hearing the biopsy was clear took a huge weight off my mind.<br>听说活检结果没事，我心里的石头落了地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose your ˈmind</td><td>发疯；精神失常</td><td>If this printer jams once more I'm going to lose my mind.<br>这台打印机再卡一次纸，我就要疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make up your ˈmind • make your ˈmind up</td><td>下定决心；作出决定</td><td>She finally made up her mind to study medicine instead of law.<br>她最终决定学医而不是学法律。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>change it.</td><td>改变主意；改掉它</td><td>Make up your mind now, because tomorrow you can't change it.<br>现在就拿定主意，明天可就改不了了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the mind ˈboggles (at sth) • it boggles the ˈmind (informal)</td><td>令人难以置信；使人摸不着头脑</td><td>It boggles the mind that anyone approved such an ugly building.<br>居然有人批准这么丑的楼，真让人费解。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmind how you ˈgo (informal)</td><td>路上小心；慢走</td><td>Mind how you go—the pavement's icy near the corner.<br>路上小心，拐角那儿人行道结冰了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmind over ˈmatter</td><td>精神胜过物质；意志战胜身体</td><td>Finishing that marathon was pure mind over matter for her.<br>跑完那场马拉松，全靠她的意志力。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>mind your own ˈbusiness (spoken, informal)</td><td>别管闲事；管好你自己</td><td>How much I earn is my affair, so mind your own business.<br>我挣多少是我的事，你别多管闲事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sitting in a cafe minding my own business when a mind your ˌP's and ˈQ's (informal)</td><td>注意礼貌；谨言慎行</td><td>Mind your P's and Q's at your girlfriend's parents' house tonight.<br>今晚在你女友父母家要注意礼貌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>'please' and the pronunciation of ˈthank you.</td><td>指“请”和“谢谢”的说法</td><td>The phrase may come from 'please' and the pronunciation of thank you.<br>这个说法可能源自“请”和“谢谢”的发音。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>mind the ˈshop (BrE) (AmE mind the ˈstore)</td><td>临时照看店铺；代管事务</td><td>Can you mind the shop while I run to the bank?<br>我去趟银行，你能帮忙看会儿店吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmind ˈyou (spoken)</td><td>请注意；不过话说回来</td><td>He's always late. Mind you, the traffic here is genuinely awful.<br>他总迟到。不过话说回来，这儿的交通确实糟糕。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmind your ˈbacks! (informal)</td><td>劳驾让让；借过</td><td>Mind your backs, please—hot soup coming through!<br>劳驾让让，热汤过来了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>never ˈmind</td><td>没关系；别在意</td><td>Never mind about the broken glass, I'll sweep it up.<br>杯子碎了没关系，我来扫。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>never mind (about) (doing) sth</td><td>别管…；先不用管</td><td>Never mind washing up—sit down and eat your dinner first.<br>别管洗碗了，先坐下吃饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌnever you ˈmind (informal)</td><td>不关你的事；别问</td><td>Never you mind how I got the tickets; just be there at seven.<br>别问我票怎么弄来的，七点到就是了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put you in mind of sb/sth (old-fashioned)</td><td>使你想起某人（或某事）</td><td>That song puts me in mind of long car journeys as a child.<br>那首歌让我想起小时候漫长的汽车旅行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/set sb's ˈmind at ease/rest</td><td>使某人放心；宽慰某人</td><td>One text from her would put my mind at rest for the night.<br>她发条短信来，我今晚就能安心了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/set/turn your ˈmind to sth</td><td>专心做某事；下功夫去做</td><td>You could pass this exam easily if you set your mind to it.<br>你要是肯下功夫，这门考试轻松就过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/get sth out of your ˈmind</td><td>把某事抛在脑后；不再去想</td><td>Put that argument out of your mind and enjoy the weekend.<br>把那场争吵忘了吧，好好过个周末。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb's ˈmind off sth</td><td>让某人转移注意力；暂时忘掉某事</td><td>A long walk took my mind off the results for an hour.<br>长途散步让我把成绩的事忘了一个钟头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈmy mind (spoken)</td><td>依我看；在我看来</td><td>To my mind, the second candidate interviewed far better.<br>依我看，第二位候选人面试表现好得多。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a practical, scientific, etc. turn of ˈmind</td><td>务实（或科学等）的思维方式</td><td>With her practical turn of mind, she fixed the leak herself.<br>她思维务实，自己就把漏水修好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn sth over in your ˈmind</td><td>反复思量；仔细琢磨</td><td>He turned the offer over in his mind for three sleepless nights.<br>他把那个提议反复琢磨了三个不眠之夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with sth in mind</td><td>考虑到；为了…着想</td><td>We chose this flat with the children's school in mind.<br>我们选这套公寓，主要是考虑孩子上学。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mine</b></td><td>a mine of inforˈmation (about/on sb/sth)</td><td>知识宝库；消息灵通的人</td><td>Old Mr Chen is a mine of information about the neighbourhood.<br>老陈头对这一带的事情知道得比谁都多。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>minority</b></td><td>be in a/the miˈnority</td><td>占少数；属于少数派</td><td>Those who still prefer paper maps are in a small minority.<br>仍偏爱纸质地图的人只占极少数。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in a minority of ˈone (often humorous)</td><td>是唯一持此看法的人</td><td>I was in a minority of one in wanting pineapple on the pizza.<br>只有我一个人想在披萨上放菠萝。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mint</b></td><td>in mint conˈdition</td><td>崭新如初；完好无损</td><td>He sold me a 1970s camera in mint condition for very little.<br>他把一台崭新如初的七十年代相机低价卖给了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>exactly in mint condition so I really can't ask</td><td>并非全新，因此不能要价太高</td><td>My bike isn't exactly in mint condition so I really can't ask much.<br>我的自行车算不上全新，所以真不能要价太高。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make, etc. a ˈmint (of money) (informal)</td><td>赚大钱；发大财</td><td>He made a mint selling face masks during that first winter.<br>头一个冬天他靠卖口罩赚了大钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>minus</b></td><td>plus or ˈminus</td><td>上下；正负（表示误差范围）</td><td>The journey takes two hours, plus or minus twenty minutes.<br>路上要两小时，上下差个二十分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>minute</b></td><td>(at) any ˈminute/ˈmoment (ˈnow)</td><td>随时；马上</td><td>The delivery van should be here any minute now.<br>送货车马上就该到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the minute/moment (that)...</td><td>一…就…</td><td>Call me the minute you land, no matter how late it is.<br>你一落地就给我打电话，多晚都行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not for a/one ˈminute/ˈmoment/ˈsecond/</td><td>一点也不；决不</td><td>I didn't for one minute believe his story about the missing keys.<br>他说钥匙丢了的那套说辞我一点也不信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈinstant (informal)</td><td>一刻也不；决不</td><td>Not for an instant did she consider giving up the case.<br>她一刻也没想过放弃这个案子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>this ˈminute</td><td>立刻；马上</td><td>Come down here this minute and clean up the kitchen.<br>马上下来把厨房收拾干净。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the ˈminute</td><td>分秒不差；准时</td><td>The Shanghai train arrived at 6.02, to the minute.<br>上海来的火车六点零二分到站，分秒不差。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌup to the ˈminute (informal)</td><td>最新的；紧跟潮流的</td><td>The app gives you up to the minute scores from every match.<br>这款应用提供每场比赛的最新比分。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>miracles</b></td><td>work/do ˈwonders/ˈmiracles (for/on/with sb/sth)</td><td>产生奇效；创造奇迹</td><td>A week by the sea worked wonders for her mood.<br>在海边待一周，她的心情大为好转。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mischief</b></td><td>do sb/yourself a ˈmischief (BrE, informal or humorous)</td><td>伤到某人（或自己）</td><td>Lift that box properly or you'll do yourself a mischief.<br>抬箱子姿势要对，不然你会伤到自己。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈmischief</td><td>搬弄是非；挑拨离间</td><td>She loves making mischief between the two departments.<br>她就爱在两个部门之间挑拨离间。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>misery</b></td><td>(a) ˈmisery guts (informal)</td><td>牢骚鬼；老不高兴的人</td><td>Don't be such a misery guts—it's only a bit of rain.<br>别老拉着个脸，不过下点小雨罢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb/sth out of their/its ˈmisery</td><td>解除某人的悬念；结束（动物的）痛苦</td><td>Put me out of my misery and just tell me who won.<br>别吊我胃口了，直接说谁赢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>prolong the agony</td><td>延长痛苦；拖延折磨</td><td>Announce the results now and don't prolong the agony.<br>现在就公布结果吧，别再折磨大家了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>miss</b></td><td>he, she, etc. doesn't miss a ˈtrick (also he,</td><td>很机敏；从不错过机会</td><td>Our accountant doesn't miss a trick when it comes to expenses.<br>说到报销，我们的会计什么都逃不过她的眼睛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>she, etc. doesn't ˈmiss much) (spoken)</td><td>什么都看在眼里；很少疏漏</td><td>Grandma is ninety and still doesn't miss much around the house.<br>奶奶九十岁了，家里的事还是什么都瞒不过她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sth a ˈmiss (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>决定不做；避开某事</td><td>I'll give the gym a miss tonight; my knee is playing up.<br>今晚健身房我就不去了，膝盖不舒服。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>miss the ˈboat (informal)</td><td>错失良机；错过机会</td><td>We missed the boat on cheap flights and now they've doubled.<br>我们错过了便宜机票，现在价格翻倍了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌmiss is as ˌgood as a ˈmile (saying)</td><td>差之毫厘，谬以千里；小错也是错</td><td>He lost by two votes, but a miss is as good as a mile.<br>他只差两票落选，可差一点也是输。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>missing</b></td><td>not know what you're ˈmissing</td><td>不知道自己错过了什么好东西</td><td>You've never tried sushi? Honestly, you don't know what you're missing.<br>你从没吃过寿司？说真的，你不知道自己错过了什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mission</b></td><td>ˌmission acˈcomplished</td><td>任务已完成</td><td>Two hours of scrubbing later, the kitchen was spotless — mission accomplished.<br>刷了两个小时，厨房一尘不染，任务完成。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mistake</b></td><td>and ˈno mistake! (old-fashioned, especially BrE)</td><td>准确无误；毫无疑问</td><td>That was the coldest winter we've had in years, and no mistake!<br>那是我们多年来最冷的一个冬天，这是毫无疑问的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by miˈstake</td><td>错误地；无意地</td><td>I took someone else's umbrella by mistake and only noticed on the bus.<br>我错拿了别人的伞，上了公交车才发现。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in miˈstake for sth</td><td>误以为；错看成</td><td>He grabbed the salt in mistake for the sugar and ruined the whole cake.<br>他把盐错当成糖，整个蛋糕都毁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmake no miˈstake (about sth) (spoken)</td><td>毫无疑问；完全可以肯定</td><td>Make no mistake about it, this decision will cost the company millions.<br>毫无疑问，这个决定会让公司损失几百万。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mistaking</b></td><td>there's no miˈstaking sb/sth</td><td>不可能认错；很明显</td><td>There's no mistaking that laugh — Danny must be back from his trip.<br>那笑声绝不会认错，丹尼肯定旅行回来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mix</b></td><td>ˌmix and ˈmatch</td><td>混搭；重新组合</td><td>You can mix and match the plates; nobody expects a matching dinner set.<br>盘子可以随便混搭，没人指望你有整套餐具。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈmix it (with sb) (BrE) (AmE ˌmix it ˈup (with sb))</td><td>与某人吵架；找某人的茬</td><td>Don't mix it with the referee or you'll be off the pitch in seconds.<br>别跟裁判吵，不然你几秒钟就被罚下场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mixed</b></td><td>be/get mixed ˈup in sth</td><td>卷入（尤指非法或不正当的事）；与某事有牵连</td><td>His brother got mixed up in some shady business and ended up in court.<br>他哥哥卷进了一些见不得光的事，最后上了法庭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get mixed ˈup with sb</td><td>与（不正当的人）交往；和某人鬼混</td><td>She got mixed up with a bad crowd during her first year at college.<br>她大一那年跟一帮不三不四的人混在了一起。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have ˌmixed ˈfeelings (about sb/sth)</td><td>感情复杂；喜忧参半</td><td>I have mixed feelings about moving abroad — excited, but scared of losing friends.<br>对出国我心情复杂，既兴奋又怕失去朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌmixed ˈbag/ˈbunch (informal)</td><td>大杂烩；五花八门的人或物</td><td>The applicants were a mixed bag: two experts, three students and a retired chef.<br>应聘者五花八门：两个专家、三个学生和一个退休厨师。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌmixed ˈblessing</td><td>福祸参半的事物；利弊并存的事</td><td>Working from home is a mixed blessing — no commute, but no escape either.<br>在家办公利弊参半：不用通勤，却也无处可逃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mixer</b></td><td>a good/bad ˈmixer</td><td>善于（或不善于）交际的人</td><td>Tom's a good mixer; he knew half the room within ten minutes of arriving.<br>汤姆很会social，到场十分钟就认识了半屋子人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mockers</b></td><td>put the ˈmockers on sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>挫败；使落空；使成功无望</td><td>The rain really put the mockers on our barbecue plans for Saturday.<br>这场雨彻底毁了我们周六烧烤的计划。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mockery</b></td><td>make a ˈmockery of sth</td><td>使成为笑柄；嘲弄；使显得荒唐</td><td>Letting him off with a fine makes a mockery of the whole justice system.<br>只罚他点钱，简直是把整个司法制度当笑话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mod</b></td><td>(with) all mod ˈcons (BrE, informal)</td><td>（房屋）配备各种现代生活设施</td><td>The flat is tiny but comes with all mod cons, including a dishwasher.<br>这公寓虽小，但各种现代设施齐全，连洗碗机都有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>muhammad</b></td><td>if the mountain will not come to Muˈhammad, Muˌhammad must go to the ˈmountain (saying)</td><td>山不就我，我便就山；人要懂得变通</td><td>She won't visit, so I'll fly over — if the mountain will not come to Muhammad.<br>她不肯来，那我飞过去，山不就我我就山。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>moment</b></td><td>at the ˈmoment</td><td>此刻；目前</td><td>I can't talk at the moment — can I call you back in an hour?<br>我现在不方便讲话，一小时后回你电话行吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the man, woman, etc. of the ˈmoment</td><td>当前红极一时的人；最受关注的人</td><td>After that winning goal, he's the man of the moment in every newspaper.<br>那记制胜球之后，他成了各家报纸的头号风云人物。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌmoment of ˈtruth</td><td>关键时刻；见分晓的时刻</td><td>The envelope was in my hand — this was the moment of truth.<br>信封就在我手里，见分晓的时刻到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of ˈmoment</td><td>（用于名词后）非常重要的</td><td>The committee has several matters of moment to settle before Friday.<br>委员会周五前还有几件要紧事要解决。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick/choose your ˈmoment</td><td>慎重选择时机</td><td>If you want a pay rise, pick your moment — don't ask when she's stressed.<br>想加薪就挑好时机，别在她焦头烂额时开口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>moments</b></td><td>have your/its ˈmoments</td><td>也有精彩（或得意）的时候</td><td>The film drags in places, but it definitely has its moments.<br>这片子有些地方拖沓，但确实也有出彩的时候。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌMonday ˈmorning quarterback (AmE, informal, disapproving)</td><td>事后诸葛亮；马后炮的人</td><td>Every Monday morning quarterback in the office knew how to fix the deal.<br>办公室里每个马后炮都知道那笔交易该怎么救。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have ˌmoney to ˈburn</td><td>钱多得花不完；有用不完的钱</td><td>Only someone with money to burn would pay that much for a pair of shoes.<br>只有钱多得没处花的人才会花那么多买双鞋。</td></tr>
