<tr><td></td><td>ˌMonday morning ˈquarterbacking (AmE, informal, disapproving)</td><td>事后诸葛亮式的评论；马后炮</td><td>Enough Monday morning quarterbacking — nobody could have predicted that storm.<br>别再放马后炮了，那场暴风雨谁也预料不到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that Monday ˈmorning feeling</td><td>周一上午的低落情绪；假期后不想上班</td><td>I've got that Monday morning feeling and it's only nine o'clock.<br>我这会儿满是周一综合症，可才九点钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in the ˈmoney (informal)</td><td>有很多钱；发财了</td><td>If this contract goes through, we'll be in the money by Christmas.<br>这份合同要是签成，圣诞节前我们就发财了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈmade of money (informal)</td><td>极其富有；钱多得用不完</td><td>Another new phone? I'm not made of money, you know.<br>又要新手机？我可不是印钞机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈmy money (informal)</td><td>依我看；我认为</td><td>For my money, she's the best singer this competition has ever produced.<br>依我看，她是这个比赛出过的最好的歌手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>money</b></td><td>on the ˈmoney (AmE)</td><td>正确；准确</td><td>Your guess about the traffic was right on the money — we took two hours.<br>你对路况的判断完全准确，我们开了两小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put ˈmoney into sth</td><td>投资于；把钱投入</td><td>They put money into stocks and shares instead of leaving it in the bank.<br>他们把钱投进了股票，而不是放在银行里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put (your) ˈmoney on sb/sth</td><td>在…上下赌注；断定…会赢</td><td>I'd put my money on the grey horse — she's won her last three races.<br>我押那匹灰马，她前三场都赢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put your money where your ˈmouth is</td><td>说话算数；用行动兑现承诺</td><td>If you really believe in the project, put your money where your mouth is.<br>你要真看好这个项目，就拿钱出来证明。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a (good) run for your ˈmoney (informal)</td><td>物有所值的收获；有力的竞争</td><td>They lost, but they gave the champions a good run for their money.<br>他们输了，但让冠军队费了不少劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw good money after ˈbad (disapproving)</td><td>为挽回损失再砸钱；把钱扔进无底洞</td><td>Repairing that old van again would just be throwing good money after bad.<br>再修那辆破面包车就是往无底洞里扔钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw your ˈmoney about/around (informal)</td><td>大手大脚地花钱；挥霍</td><td>He throws his money around in bars to impress people he barely knows.<br>他在酒吧里挥金如土，就为了在半生不熟的人面前显摆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw ˈmoney at sth (disapproving)</td><td>只砸钱了事；往某事上白扔钱</td><td>You can't fix a broken school system just by throwing money at it.<br>光靠砸钱是修不好一个烂掉的教育体系的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>monkey</b></td><td>I don't/couldn't give a ˈmonkey's (BrE, slang)</td><td>我压根儿不在乎；无所谓</td><td>He can think what he likes — I couldn't give a monkey's.<br>他爱怎么想怎么想，我压根不在乎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈmonkey out of sb</td><td>拿某人当猴耍；使某人出洋相</td><td>They made a monkey out of him by sending him to a meeting that didn't exist.<br>他们让他去开一个根本不存在的会，把他耍得团团转。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈmonkey business (informal)</td><td>骗人的把戏；胡闹；捣鬼</td><td>I want no monkey business while I'm out — just finish your homework.<br>我出去这段时间不许胡闹，把作业写完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˌmonkey on sb's ˈback</td><td>难以摆脱的负担（或毒瘾、难题）</td><td>That unpaid loan has been a monkey on his back for three years.<br>那笔没还的贷款压了他三年，甩都甩不掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmonkey's ˈwedding (South African)</td><td>太阳雨；晴天下雨</td><td>The kids ran outside laughing at the monkey's wedding falling on the garden.<br>孩子们跑到院子里，笑着看这场太阳雨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>once</b></td><td>once in a ˌblue ˈmoon</td><td>千载难逢；极少发生</td><td>My cousin only calls once in a blue moon, usually when he needs a favour.<br>我表哥难得打一次电话，多半是有事求人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>month</b></td><td>month after ˈmonth</td><td>一连数月；月复一月</td><td>Month after month she saved a little, until she could afford the deposit.<br>她月复一月地攒钱，直到攒够首付。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmonth by ˈmonth</td><td>逐月；一月一月地</td><td>His health improved month by month after he finally quit smoking.<br>他戒烟之后，身体一个月比一个月好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not for/in) a ˌmonth of ˈSundays (spoken)</td><td>（用于强调）绝不会；遥遥无期</td><td>You won't get him to apologize, not in a month of Sundays.<br>想让他道歉？八辈子也不可能。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mood</b></td><td>be in the ˈmood for sth/for doing sth</td><td>有心情做某事；想做某事</td><td>I'm not in the mood for a party tonight; let's just order pizza.<br>今晚我没心情去派对，我们叫披萨吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in no ˈmood for sth/for doing sth</td><td>没心思做某事；无意做某事</td><td>After that phone call she was in no mood for jokes about her boss.<br>接完那通电话，她可没心情听关于她老板的玩笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be over the ˈmoon (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>欣喜若狂；乐翻了天</td><td>She was over the moon when the university finally sent her an offer.<br>大学终于发来录取通知时，她高兴得不得了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cry/ask for the ˈmoon (also want the ˈmoon)</td><td>想要办不到的事；异想天开</td><td>Asking for a pay rise and a shorter week is crying for the moon here.<br>在这里既要加薪又要减少工时，简直是异想天开。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>moonlight</b></td><td>do a moonlight ˈflit (BrE, informal)</td><td>（为躲债等）连夜潜逃</td><td>The tenants did a moonlight flit, leaving three months' rent unpaid.<br>那些租客连夜跑了，欠了三个月房租。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>moons</b></td><td>many ˈmoons ago (literary)</td><td>很久以前；许多年前</td><td>Many moons ago I could run a marathon without stopping once.<br>很久以前我能一口气跑完马拉松。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>moot</b></td><td>be a moot ˈpoint/ˈquestion</td><td>有争议的问题；尚无定论的事</td><td>Whether the new rule actually helps students is still a moot point.<br>新规定是否真对学生有帮助，仍然众说纷纭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>moral</b></td><td>(give sb) ˌmoral supˈport</td><td>（给某人）道义上的支持；精神支持</td><td>I can't fix the car, but I'll come along and give you moral support.<br>我修不了车，但我可以陪着你，给你打打气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take, claim, seize, etc. the moral ˈhigh ground</td><td>占据道德制高点；自居正义</td><td>He seized the moral high ground by refusing to take the company's money.<br>他拒收公司的钱，从而占据了道德制高点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>more</b></td><td>be ˈmore than glad, ready, etc. (to do sth)</td><td>非常乐意（做某事）</td><td>I'd be more than glad to look after your cat while you're away.<br>你不在的时候，我非常乐意帮你照看猫。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>more ˈlike (it) (informal)</td><td>这才像话；更令人满意</td><td>Now that's more like it — the soup's finally hot enough.<br>这才像话嘛，汤总算够烫了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmore or ˈless</td><td>差不多；大体上</td><td>The report is more or less finished; I just need to add the charts.<br>报告差不多写完了，我只要再加上图表。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>morning</b></td><td>the morning ˈafter (the night beˈfore) (informal)</td><td>宿醉；狂饮之后次日的难受</td><td>He staggered in at noon with a classic case of the morning after.<br>他中午晃进来，一副典型的宿醉模样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>morning, noon and ˈnight</td><td>从早到晚；一天到晚</td><td>She practises that violin morning, noon and night, and the neighbours complain.<br>她一天到晚拉小提琴，邻居都有意见了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈmortal enemy</td><td>死敌；不共戴天的仇人</td><td>The two families have been mortal enemies since a dispute over land.<br>这两家自从争地之后就成了死对头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>most</b></td><td>at (the) ˈmost</td><td>至多；充其量</td><td>The whole trip will take an hour at the most if the roads are clear.<br>路上要是不堵，全程最多一个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mother</b></td><td>at your ˌmother's ˈknee</td><td>年幼时；孩提时代</td><td>He learned those old fishing songs at his mother's knee.<br>那些古老的渔歌是他小时候在母亲膝下学会的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈmother (old-fashioned, informal or humorous)</td><td>（在餐桌上）负责倒茶分菜</td><td>Shall I be mother and pour the tea for everyone?<br>我来当东道，给大家倒茶吧？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈmother country</td><td>祖国；母国</td><td>After forty years abroad, he still calls Ireland the mother country.<br>在国外待了四十年，他仍然把爱尔兰称作祖国。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈmother (and ˈfather) of (all) sth (informal)</td><td>（强调）最大（或最厉害）的…</td><td>We got caught in the mother of all traffic jams on the way home.<br>回家路上我们碰上了史上最恐怖的大堵车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your ˌmother ˈtongue</td><td>母语；本族语</td><td>Even after years in Berlin, she counts money in her mother tongue.<br>在柏林待了这么多年，她数钱时还是用母语。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>motion</b></td><td>put/set sth in ˈmotion (also set the wheels in ˈmotion)</td><td>启动；使开始运作</td><td>One phone call set the wheels in motion for the whole rescue operation.<br>一通电话就启动了整个救援行动。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>motions</b></td><td>go through the ˈmotions (of doing sth)</td><td>走过场；敷衍了事</td><td>He's just going through the motions at work until his notice period ends.<br>离职期没结束前，他在公司只是应付差事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>break the ˈmould (of sth) (BrE) (AmE break the ˈmold (of sth))</td><td>打破常规；改变固有模式</td><td>Her first novel broke the mould of what a detective story could be.<br>她的第一部小说打破了侦探小说的固有套路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mount</b></td><td>if the mountain will not come to Muˈhammad, Muˌhammad must go to the ˈmountain (saying)</td><td>山不就我，我便就山；要懂变通</td><td>He never answers emails, so I flew there: if the mountain will not come to Muhammad.<br>他从不回邮件，我只好飞过去，山不就我我就山。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˌmountain out of a ˈmolehill (disapproving)</td><td>小题大做；大惊小怪</td><td>It's one late payment; don't make a mountain out of a molehill.<br>不过晚交了一次款，别小题大做。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mouse</b></td><td>get a ˈmove on (spoken)</td><td>赶快；快点</td><td>Get a move on — the train leaves in eleven minutes and we're still here.<br>快点，火车十一分钟后就开，我们还在这儿呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all ˈmouth (BrE also be all mouth and no ˈtrousers) (informal)</td><td>只说不练；光会吹牛</td><td>He swears he'll quit tomorrow, but he's all mouth and no trousers.<br>他发誓明天就辞职，其实光说不练。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all ˈmouth and no ˈtrousers (BrE, informal)</td><td>只说不做；嘴上厉害</td><td>Ignore his threats — the man is all mouth and no trousers.<br>别理他的威胁，那人就是嘴上厉害。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>down in the ˈmouth (informal)</td><td>闷闷不乐；情绪低落</td><td>You've looked down in the mouth all week — is something wrong at home?<br>你这一周都无精打采的，家里出事了吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make sb's ˈmouth water</td><td>使某人垂涎；令人流口水</td><td>The smell of garlic bread from the kitchen made my mouth water.<br>厨房飘来的蒜香面包味让我直流口水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run off at the ˈmouth (AmE, informal)</td><td>夸夸其谈；信口开河</td><td>He ran off at the mouth for twenty minutes and said absolutely nothing useful.<br>他滔滔不绝讲了二十分钟，一句有用的都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mouths</b></td><td>out of the ˌmouths of ˈbabes (and ˈsucklings) (saying)</td><td>童言有理；小孩说话常有道理</td><td>My six-year-old solved it instantly — out of the mouths of babes!<br>我六岁的孩子一下就说出答案了，童言有理啊！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>move</b></td><td>get a ˈmove on (spoken)</td><td>赶快；抓紧时间</td><td>If we don't get a move on, we'll miss the start of the film.<br>再不抓紧，我们就赶不上电影开头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈmove</td><td>动身；起身告辞</td><td>It's nearly midnight; I think we should make a move.<br>快半夜了，我看我们该走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈmove on sb (informal)</td><td>对某人示好；主动求欢</td><td>He made a move on her at the party and got politely turned down.<br>他在派对上向她示好，被客气地拒绝了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>move the ˈgoalposts (informal, disapproving, especially BrE)</td><td>中途改变规则（使人为难）</td><td>Every time we meet the target, management moves the goalposts again.<br>我们每次达标，管理层就又改一次标准。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Mr</b></td><td>Mr ˈBig (informal, disapproving)</td><td>（犯罪团伙的）头目；老大</td><td>Police finally arrested the Mr Big behind the whole smuggling network.<br>警方终于抓到了整个走私网络背后的老大。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Mr ˈNice Guy (informal)</td><td>好好先生；老好人</td><td>I've been Mr Nice Guy for months; from today I'm saying no.<br>我当了几个月好好先生，从今天起我要学会拒绝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Mr ˈRight (informal)</td><td>如意郎君；理想的结婚对象</td><td>She's still waiting for Mr Right and refuses to settle for less.<br>她还在等她的白马王子，不肯将就。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>much</b></td><td>as ˈmuch (as)</td><td>同样多；正是如此</td><td>I thought he'd forget, and he did as much — no card, no call.<br>我就知道他会忘，果然如此，没卡片也没电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as much as sb can/could ˈdo (not) to do sth</td><td>尽最大努力才（没有）做某事</td><td>It was as much as I could do not to laugh during his speech.<br>他讲话时我拼命忍着才没笑出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be not so much sth as sth</td><td>与其说是…不如说是…</td><td>She's not so much angry as deeply disappointed in all of us.<br>与其说她生气，不如说她对我们大失所望。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be too ˈmuch (for sb)</td><td>（对某人来说）承受不了；太过分</td><td>Three night shifts in a row was too much for him, so he quit.<br>连上三个夜班他实在吃不消，就辞职了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>much as/though</td><td>虽然；尽管</td><td>Much as I love the city, I couldn't live there all year round.<br>尽管我很爱这座城市，却没法常年住在那里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be much of a sth</td><td>算不上好的…；不怎么样</td><td>I'm not much of a cook, but I can manage scrambled eggs.<br>我算不上会做饭，但炒鸡蛋还行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not much ˈin it</td><td>（两者）相差无几；不相上下</td><td>Both offers are decent; honestly, there's not much in it.<br>两份工作都不错，说实话差别不大。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not ˈup to much (BrE)</td><td>不怎么样；质量不佳</td><td>The hotel was cheap, but the breakfast wasn't up to much.<br>酒店挺便宜，可早餐实在不怎么样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so much for ˈsb/ˈsth</td><td>…就说到这里；…不过如此</td><td>The car broke down again — so much for the mechanic's guarantee.<br>车又坏了，那修车师傅的保证也不过如此。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so much ˈso that ˈthis much</td><td>（引出要点）有一点是…</td><td>I'll say this much for him: he never once complained about the hours.<br>我得替他说句公道话：他从没抱怨过工时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>very ˈmuch so</td><td>确实如此；非常是</td><td>Was the concert worth the ticket price? Very much so.<br>演唱会值那个票价吗？太值了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without so much as sth/as doing sth</td><td>竟然连…都没有</td><td>He walked out without so much as a goodbye to anyone.<br>他就那么走了，连声再见都没跟人说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>muchness</b></td><td>be ˌmuch of a ˈmuchness</td><td>半斤八两；不相上下</td><td>The two hotels are much of a muchness, so pick the cheaper one.<br>两家酒店半斤八两，挑便宜的那家吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>muck</b></td><td>where there's ˌmuck there's ˈbrass (BrE, saying)</td><td>哪里活脏，哪里有钱赚</td><td>He cleans drains and drives a new car — where there's muck there's brass.<br>他通下水道却开新车，脏活儿才来钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mud</b></td><td>fling/sling/throw ˈmud (at sb) (informal)</td><td>诋毁；泼脏水；污蔑</td><td>Both candidates spent the debate throwing mud at each other.<br>两位候选人整场辩论都在互相泼脏水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>mud ˈsticks (also if you ˌthrow enough ˈmud, ˌsome of it will ˈstick) (saying)</td><td>污名难洗；谣言总会留下痕迹</td><td>He was cleared in court, but mud sticks and clients still avoid him.<br>他已被判无罪，可污名难洗，客户仍躲着他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>muddy</b></td><td>muddy the ˈwaters (disapproving)</td><td>把水搅浑；使问题更复杂</td><td>Bringing up last year's budget only muddies the waters in this discussion.<br>提去年的预算只会把这场讨论搅得更乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mug</b></td><td>be a ˈmug's game (disapproving, especially BrE)</td><td>傻子才干的事；徒劳无益的事</td><td>Buying lottery tickets every week is a mug's game, if you ask me.<br>要我说，每周买彩票是傻子才干的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cover</b></td><td>cover a multitude of ˈsins (humorous)</td><td>掩盖种种实情；遮住许多不足</td><td>The phrase 'cosy flat' can cover a multitude of sins in an advert.<br>广告里“温馨小屋”这几个字能掩盖一大堆问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mum</b></td><td>keep ˈmum (informal)</td><td>保持沉默；守口如瓶</td><td>Keep mum about the party — it's supposed to be a surprise for Jen.<br>派对的事别说出去，那是给珍的惊喜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌmum's the ˈword! (informal)</td><td>别声张；我会保密</td><td>You're getting engaged? Congratulations — and mum's the word!<br>你要订婚了？恭喜，我一定保密！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>munchies</b></td><td>have the ˈmunchies (informal)</td><td>突然特别想吃东西；嘴馋</td><td>It's midnight and I've got the munchies — is there any bread left?<br>半夜了我又嘴馋，还有面包吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>murder</b></td><td>get away with ˈmurder (informal, often humorous)</td><td>为所欲为而不受惩罚；无法无天</td><td>That kid gets away with murder because his grandmother never says no.<br>那孩子无法无天，因为他奶奶从不说不。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I could ˈmurder a... (spoken)</td><td>我非常想吃（或喝）…</td><td>After that long walk I could murder a cold beer right now.<br>走了那么远，我现在特别想来杯冰啤酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>he, she, etc. will ˈmurder you (spoken)</td><td>（警告）他（她）会宰了你的</td><td>Don't touch Dad's toolbox — he'll murder you if anything's missing.<br>别动爸的工具箱，少了东西他会宰了你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>murmur</b></td><td>(do sth) withˌout a ˈmurmur</td><td>毫无怨言地（做某事）</td><td>She worked two extra shifts without a murmur and went home smiling.<br>她一声不吭地多上了两班，回家时还笑着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>murphy</b></td><td>Murphy's ˈLaw (humorous)</td><td>墨菲定律（可能出错的事终会出错）</td><td>The printer died five minutes before the deadline — Murphy's Law again.<br>截止前五分钟打印机坏了，又是墨菲定律。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>music</b></td><td>be (like) ˌmusic to your ˈears</td><td>是好消息；听着让人高兴</td><td>Hearing that the loan was approved was music to my ears.<br>听说贷款批下来了，简直是天籁之音。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>must</b></td><td>if you ˈmust (do sth)</td><td>（虽不赞同但允许）你非要那样就…</td><td>Smoke outside if you must, but please don't do it in the kitchen.<br>你非抽不可就去外面抽，别在厨房里抽。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mustard</b></td><td>(not) cut the ˈmustard</td><td>（不）达到要求；（不）胜任</td><td>He's friendly enough, but he just doesn't cut the mustard as a manager.<br>他人挺好，可当经理实在不够格。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mutton</b></td><td>be mutton dressed (up) as ˈlamb (BrE, informal, disapproving)</td><td>（女子）扮嫩；老来俏</td><td>That miniskirt on her is mutton dressed as lamb, my aunt whispered.<br>我姑姑小声说，她穿那条超短裙就是老来俏。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nail</b></td><td>nail your colours to the ˈmast (especially BrE)</td><td>公开表明立场；明确表态</td><td>The mayor nailed her colours to the mast and backed the new hospital.<br>市长公开表态，支持修建这家新医院。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a nail in sb's/sth's ˈcoffin</td><td>促使失败的因素；致命一击</td><td>Losing the last big client was the final nail in the firm's coffin.<br>失去最后一个大客户，成了公司的致命一击。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nail sb to the ˈwall (informal)</td><td>严惩某人；狠狠教训某人</td><td>If the auditors find those receipts, they'll nail him to the wall.<br>审计员要是找到那些收据，会把他往死里整。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈnail (informal)</td><td>（付款）当场；立即</td><td>He bought the van and paid cash on the nail, no haggling at all.<br>他买下那辆车，当场付现，一点都没还价。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>naked</b></td><td>the naked ˈeye</td><td>肉眼</td><td>The comet is faint but still visible to the naked eye tonight.<br>这颗彗星很暗，但今晚肉眼仍能看到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the naked ˈtruth</td><td>赤裸裸的事实；真相</td><td>The naked truth is that we simply cannot afford another car.<br>赤裸裸的事实是，我们根本买不起第二辆车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>name</b></td><td>by ˈname</td><td>凭名字；指名地</td><td>The teacher knew every child by name within the first two weeks.<br>头两周内老师就叫得出每个孩子的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by the name of... (written)</td><td>名叫…</td><td>A young man by the name of Carter has been asking to see you.<br>一个名叫卡特的年轻人一直要见你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go by the name of...</td><td>自称…；以…之名为人所知</td><td>He writes crime novels and goes by the name of J. L. Frost.<br>他写犯罪小说，笔名叫 J. L. 弗罗斯特。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have (sb's) ˈname on it • with your ˈname on it (informal)</td><td>注定属于某人的；命中注定的</td><td>That corner house has your name on it — you'll love the garden.<br>那栋角落的房子简直就是为你留的，你会爱死那个花园。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) have sth to your ˈname (informal)</td><td>（不）拥有；名下（没）有</td><td>He arrived in London without a penny to his name.<br>他到伦敦时身无分文。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˌall but ˈname</td><td>实际上是；只差名分</td><td>She's been running the department in all but name for two years.<br>这两年她实际上一直在管这个部门，只是没名分。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈGod's/ˈHeaven's name • in the name of ˈGod/ˈHeaven</td><td>（表愤怒或惊讶）究竟；到底</td><td>What in God's name were you thinking when you signed that?<br>你签那玩意儿的时候到底在想什么？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the name of ˈsb/ˈsth • in sb's/sth's ˈname</td><td>以…的名义；凭…的权威</td><td>Terrible things have been done in the name of progress.<br>多少可怕的事都是以进步的名义干出来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˌname ˈonly</td><td>名义上；有名无实</td><td>He's the boss in name only; his deputy makes all the decisions.<br>他只是名义上的老板，一切都由副手拍板。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈname for yourself • make your ˈname</td><td>成名；扬名</td><td>She made a name for herself photographing storms across the Midwest.<br>她靠拍摄中西部的风暴打出了名气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>name the ˈday</td><td>确定婚期</td><td>They've been engaged for years but still haven't named the day.<br>他们订婚好几年了，婚期却一直没定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your, his, etc. name is ˈmud (informal, usually humorous)</td><td>名声扫地；不受待见</td><td>After he forgot her birthday again, his name is mud in that house.<br>他又忘了她生日，如今在那个家里臭名昭著。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>name ˈnames</td><td>指名道姓；公开点名</td><td>The witness refused to name names, even under pressure from the court.<br>即便法庭施压，证人仍拒绝指名道姓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the name of the ˈgame (informal)</td><td>关键所在；最重要的事</td><td>In this business, patience is the name of the game.<br>干这行，耐心才是关键。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a name to ˈconjure with put a ˈname to sb/sth</td><td>说得出…的名字；认得出</td><td>I know that actor's face but I can't put a name to him.<br>那演员的脸我认得，就是叫不出名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb's name in ˈvain</td><td>妄称某人之名；背后议论某人</td><td>Were you two taking my name in vain while I was out?<br>我不在的时候你俩是不是在背后编排我？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you ˌname it, sb's ˈgot it (informal)</td><td>凡是你说得出的，应有尽有</td><td>Screwdrivers, drills, saws — you name it, my dad's got it.<br>螺丝刀、电钻、锯子，只要你说得出，我爸都有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nameless</b></td><td>somebody, who will/shall remain/be ˈnameless (humorous)</td><td>某位不便点名的人</td><td>Somebody who shall remain nameless ate the last slice of cake.<br>某位就不点名了的人，吃掉了最后一块蛋糕。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nanny</b></td><td>the ˈnanny state (BrE, disapproving)</td><td>保姆式国家（政府管得太多）</td><td>Banning salt in restaurants is the nanny state gone too far.<br>禁止餐馆放盐，这保姆式管理未免管得太宽。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>narrow</b></td><td>a narrow eˈscape/ˈsqueak</td><td>死里逃生；侥幸脱险</td><td>The van missed us by inches — that was a narrow escape.<br>那辆面包车差几厘米就撞上我们，真是死里逃生。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nasty</b></td><td>get/turn ˈnasty</td><td>翻脸；变得凶狠</td><td>The argument turned nasty when someone mentioned the money.<br>有人提到钱之后，争吵一下子就变难看了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a nasty piece of ˈwork (BrE, informal)</td><td>卑鄙的家伙；讨厌的人</td><td>Steer clear of the landlord; he's a nasty piece of work.<br>离那房东远点，他不是什么好东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>native</b></td><td>go ˈnative (often humorous)</td><td>入乡随俗；完全本地化</td><td>After a year in Naples he's gone native — espresso standing at the bar.<br>在那不勒斯待了一年，他彻底本地化了，站在吧台喝浓缩咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>naturally</b></td><td>come ˈnaturally (to sb/sth)</td><td>对某人来说不费力；是天生的本事</td><td>Talking to strangers comes naturally to her, which is why she sells so much.<br>跟陌生人搭话是她的天分，所以她业绩才这么好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nature</b></td><td>against ˈnature</td><td>违反自然；有违天性</td><td>Getting up before five feels completely against nature to me.<br>五点前起床对我来说完全违背天性。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(get, go, etc.) back to ˈnature</td><td>回归自然；返璞归真</td><td>They sold the flat and went back to nature on a small farm.<br>他们卖掉公寓，搬到小农场回归自然。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the nature of ˈsth</td><td>类似于…；具有…性质</td><td>His remark was in the nature of a warning rather than a joke.<br>他那句话与其说是玩笑，不如说是警告。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈnature of things</td><td>理所当然；事物本该如此</td><td>In the nature of things, children eventually leave home.<br>照事物的常理，孩子终归要离家的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let ˌnature take its ˈcourse</td><td>顺其自然；任其发展</td><td>The vet said to stop worrying and let nature take its course.<br>兽医说别担心了，顺其自然吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>near</b></td><td>as ˌnear as ˈdammit (also as ˌnear as makes no ˈdifference) (BrE, spoken)</td><td>几乎；差不多一样</td><td>The bill came to fifty pounds, as near as dammit.<br>账单差不多正好五十镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>near eˈnough (BrE, spoken)</td><td>差不多；几乎</td><td>We've been waiting an hour, near enough, and nobody has come.<br>我们差不多等了一个钟头，一个人也没来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a near ˈmiss</td><td>险些相撞；差一点击中</td><td>Two planes had a near miss above the airport this morning.<br>今早两架飞机在机场上空险些相撞。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>near the ˈknuckle (BrE, informal)</td><td>（言语、玩笑）近乎下流</td><td>Some of his jokes at the wedding were a bit near the knuckle.<br>他在婚礼上讲的有些笑话有点儿荤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nowhere/not anywhere ˈnear</td><td>远远不；差得远</td><td>The repairs are nowhere near finished, and the money has run out.<br>修缮工作离完工还远着呢，钱却花光了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so ˌnear and ˌyet so ˈfar</td><td>功亏一篑；差一点就成了</td><td>We lost in the final minute — so near and yet so far.<br>我们在最后一分钟输了，功亏一篑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nearest</b></td><td>your ˌnearest and ˈdearest (informal, often humorous)</td><td>至亲；最亲近的家人</td><td>At Christmas we squeeze all our nearest and dearest round one table.<br>圣诞节我们把所有至亲都挤在一张桌子边。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nearly</b></td><td>not nearly</td><td>远非；差得远</td><td>This coat is not nearly warm enough for a Moscow winter.<br>这件外套对莫斯科的冬天来说远远不够暖和。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>necessarily</b></td><td>not necesˈsarily</td><td>未必；不见得</td><td>Being busy does not necessarily mean you are getting anything done.<br>忙碌未必意味着你真做成了什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>necessary</b></td><td>a ˌnecessary ˈevil</td><td>必要之恶；不得已而为之的坏事</td><td>For most freelancers, chasing unpaid invoices is a necessary evil.<br>对多数自由职业者来说，催欠款是不得不干的苦差。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>necessity</b></td><td>neˌcessity is the ˌmother of inˈvention (saying)</td><td>需要是发明之母</td><td>We built a stove from a tin can — necessity is the mother of invention.<br>我们用铁罐做了个炉子，需要真是发明之母。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a virtue of neˈcessity</td><td>将无奈之举说成美德；变被动为主动</td><td>Stuck at home, he made a virtue of necessity and finally learned to bake.<br>困在家里，他索性顺势而为，终于学会了烘焙。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>neck</b></td><td>be up to your ˈneck in sth • be in sth up to your ˈneck</td><td>深陷于；忙得不可开交</td><td>I'm up to my neck in paperwork, so lunch will have to wait.<br>我埋在文件堆里，午饭只能往后拖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>break your ˈneck (doing sth/to do sth)</td><td>拼命（做某事）；竭尽全力</td><td>I broke my neck to finish the report and nobody even read it.<br>我拼了命赶完报告，结果没人看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by a ˈneck</td><td>（比赛中）以微弱优势</td><td>Our team won by a neck after a photo finish.<br>经过终点摄影判定，我们队以微弱优势获胜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get it in the ˈneck (BrE, informal)</td><td>挨骂；受重罚</td><td>If the shop opens late again, you'll get it in the neck from the manager.<br>店里再晚开门，你就要挨经理骂了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in your, this, etc. ˌneck of the ˈwoods (informal)</td><td>在某地一带；在这一片地区</td><td>What brings you to this neck of the woods on a Tuesday?<br>周二这天什么风把你吹到我们这一带了？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌneck and ˈneck (with sb/sth) (also ˌnip and ˈtuck (with sb) especially AmE)</td><td>势均力敌；不分上下</td><td>The two candidates were neck and neck right up to the final count.<br>两位候选人一直到最后计票都难分伯仲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>need</b></td><td>if need(s) ˈbe</td><td>如果需要的话；必要时</td><td>I'll sleep on the sofa if need be; just don't book a hotel.<br>必要的话我睡沙发，别订酒店了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's ˈall I need (informal)</td><td>这下可好；真是雪上加霜</td><td>A flat tyre in the rain — that's all I need!<br>下着雨还爆胎，这下可好！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>needle</b></td><td>like looking for/trying to find a ˌneedle in a ˈhaystack</td><td>大海捞针</td><td>Finding one file on that laptop is like looking for a needle in a haystack.<br>在那台笔记本上找一个文件简直是大海捞针。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>needles</b></td><td>have ˌpins and ˈneedles</td><td>（肢体）发麻；针刺般的麻感</td><td>I sat cross-legged too long and now I have pins and needles.<br>我盘腿坐太久，现在腿麻得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>needless</b></td><td>ˌneedless to ˈsay</td><td>不用说；当然</td><td>Needless to say, he arrived twenty minutes after the interview started.<br>不用说，他在面试开始二十分钟后才到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>needs</b></td><td>needs ˈmust (when the devil drives) (saying)</td><td>形势所迫，不得不为</td><td>I hate night shifts, but needs must when the devil drives.<br>我讨厌上夜班，可形势所迫也没办法。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈneighbourhood of sth (BrE) (AmE in the ˈneighborhood of sth)</td><td>大约；…上下</td><td>The repairs will cost in the neighbourhood of two thousand pounds.<br>修理费大约在两千英镑上下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nelly</b></td><td>not on your ˈnelly (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>绝对不行；休想</td><td>Lend him the car again? Not on your nelly.<br>再把车借他？门儿都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nerve</b></td><td>have a ˈnerve (informal)</td><td>厚颜无耻；好大的胆子</td><td>You've got a nerve, asking for a lift after what you said.<br>你说了那种话还敢让我捎你，脸皮真厚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit/touch a (raw) ˈnerve</td><td>触及痛处；戳到要害</td><td>Mentioning his old job clearly touched a raw nerve.<br>提到他从前的工作，显然戳到了他的痛处。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nerves</b></td><td>a bag/bundle of ˈnerves (informal)</td><td>非常紧张的人；焦虑不安的人</td><td>She was a bundle of nerves the morning of her driving test.<br>路考那天早上她紧张得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get on sb's ˈnerves (informal)</td><td>使某人心烦；惹某人厌烦</td><td>That dripping tap is really getting on my nerves tonight.<br>今晚那滴水的龙头真让我心烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have nerves of ˈsteel</td><td>意志坚强；沉着冷静</td><td>You need nerves of steel to land a plane in that wind.<br>这种风里降落飞机，得有钢铁般的胆量。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nest</b></td><td>a ˈnest egg (informal)</td><td>储备金；为将来攒的钱</td><td>They built up a decent nest egg before their first child arrived.<br>第一个孩子出生前，他们攒下了一笔不错的积蓄。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌempty ˈnest</td><td>空巢（子女离家后的家庭）</td><td>After the twins left for university, they had to get used to the empty nest.<br>双胞胎上大学后，他们得慢慢适应空巢生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>net</b></td><td>cast/spread your net ˈwide</td><td>广撒网；扩大搜寻范围</td><td>Cast your net wide when job-hunting; don't apply to just one city.<br>找工作要广撒网，别只投一个城市。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>neutral</b></td><td>on neutral ˈground/territory</td><td>在中立地点；在第三方场所</td><td>Let's meet on neutral ground — a café rather than either office.<br>我们找个中立地点见吧，去咖啡馆，别在谁的办公室。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>new</b></td><td>(as) good as ˈnew • like ˈnew</td><td>完好如新</td><td>A bit of polish and the old table looked as good as new.<br>稍一打蜡，这张旧桌子看起来就跟新的一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>... is the ˈnew ... (BrE, informal)</td><td>…是新的…（取代旧潮流）</td><td>Everyone keeps saying that fifty is the new thirty these days.<br>如今人人都说五十岁就是新的三十岁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a new ˈbroom (sweeps clean) (BrE, saying)</td><td>新官上任三把火</td><td>The new head teacher changed everything in a month — a new broom sweeps clean.<br>新校长一个月内改了个遍，新官上任三把火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˌnew kid on the ˈblock (informal)</td><td>新来的人；新手</td><td>As the new kid on the block, he ate lunch alone for a week.<br>作为新来的，他独自吃了一星期午饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌnew ˈman (BrE)</td><td>新好男人（分担家务育儿的男性）</td><td>He cooks, cleans and does the school run — a proper new man.<br>他做饭、打扫、接送孩子，是个标准的新好男人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌnew one on ˈme</td><td>头一回听说；闻所未闻</td><td>Coffee with butter in it? That's a new one on me.<br>咖啡里加黄油？我还是头一回听说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn over a new ˈleaf</td><td>改过自新；开始新生活</td><td>He's turned over a new leaf and hasn't missed a shift since January.<br>他已痛改前非，一月以来一天班都没缺过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's ˈnew? (spoken, informal)</td><td>（问候语）最近怎么样</td><td>Hey, long time no see — what's new?<br>嘿，好久不见，最近怎么样？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>news</b></td><td>be bad ˈnews (for sb/sth)</td><td>对…不利；是坏消息</td><td>A wet summer is bad news for farmers around here.<br>多雨的夏天对这一带的农民来说是个坏消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be good ˈnews (for sb/sth)</td><td>对…有利；是好消息</td><td>Lower interest rates are good news for anyone with a mortgage.<br>利率下调对所有背房贷的人都是好消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>break the ˈnews (to sb)</td><td>（向某人）透露坏消息</td><td>Nobody wanted to break the news to her that the dog had died.<br>谁也不愿告诉她狗死了的消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's/that's ˌnews to ˈme</td><td>我可从没听说；这我倒是头一回知道</td><td>The office is closing on Friday? That's news to me.<br>周五办公室要关门？我怎么不知道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌno news is ˈgood news (saying)</td><td>没有消息就是好消息</td><td>She hasn't rung from the hospital, but no news is good news.<br>她还没从医院打电话来，不过没消息就是好消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>new</b></td><td>a New York ˈminute (AmE)</td><td>极短的时间；一瞬间</td><td>He'd take that job in a New York minute if they offered it.<br>他们要是给他那份工作，他一秒钟都不会犹豫。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>next</b></td><td>as good, well, etc. as the ˈnext person</td><td>和一般人一样（好）；不比别人差</td><td>I enjoy a lazy Sunday as much as the next person.<br>懒散的周日我和谁一样喜欢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the next best ˈthing</td><td>仅次于最佳的选择；退而求其次</td><td>We couldn't get tickets, so watching it in the pub was the next best thing.<br>我们没买到票，去酒吧看算是退而求其次。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your ˌnext of ˈkin (formal)</td><td>最近的亲属；直系亲属</td><td>The hospital needs the name of your next of kin on this form.<br>医院要在这张表上填你的直系亲属姓名。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌnice ˈwork if you can get it (informal)</td><td>轻松的好差事；这活儿谁不想干</td><td>He gets paid to taste chocolate — nice work if you can get it.<br>他靠试吃巧克力赚钱，这好差事谁不想要。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nicely</b></td><td>do ˈnicely</td><td>进展良好；干得不错</td><td>The new café is doing nicely, even in its first winter.<br>这家新咖啡馆生意不错，头一个冬天就挺好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nick</b></td><td>in good, bad, etc. ˈnick (BrE, informal)</td><td>状况良好（或不佳）</td><td>The bike's twenty years old but still in good nick.<br>这车有二十年了，可状况还很好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˌnick of ˈtime (informal)</td><td>在紧要关头；恰好赶上</td><td>The ambulance arrived in the nick of time and saved him.<br>救护车在紧要关头赶到，救了他一命。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>night</b></td><td>have an early/a late ˈnight</td><td>（比平时）早睡（或晚睡）</td><td>I'm having an early night; the alarm goes off at five.<br>我今晚早点睡，闹钟五点就响。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a good/bad ˈnight</td><td>夜里睡得好（或不好）</td><td>The baby had a bad night, so nobody in the house slept.<br>宝宝夜里不安生，全家都没睡好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈnight of it (informal)</td><td>尽兴玩个通宵</td><td>We only meant to have one drink, but we made a night of it.<br>本来只想喝一杯，结果玩了个通宵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌnight and ˈday • ˌday and ˈnight</td><td>夜以继日；日夜不停</td><td>The builders worked night and day to finish before the rain came.<br>工人们日夜赶工，要在下雨前完工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>night ˈnight</td><td>（儿语）晚安</td><td>Night night, sweetheart — I'll leave the hall light on.<br>晚安，宝贝，我把走廊的灯留着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>night</b></td><td>a night ˈout</td><td>外出玩乐的一晚</td><td>They haven't had a night out together since the twins were born.<br>自从双胞胎出生，他俩就没一起出去玩过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈnight owl (informal)</td><td>夜猫子；习惯熬夜的人</td><td>She's a night owl and does her best writing after midnight.<br>她是个夜猫子，午夜后写得最好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nine</b></td><td>have nine ˈlives</td><td>命大；有九条命</td><td>That cat has nine lives — it fell three floors and walked away.<br>那猫命真大，从三楼摔下来还能自己走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a nine days ˈwonder</td><td>昙花一现；轰动一时的人或事</td><td>His scandal was a nine days wonder and then everyone forgot.<br>他那桩丑闻热闹了几天，之后就没人记得了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nine times out of ˈten (also ˌninety-nine ˌtimes out of a ˈhundred)</td><td>十有八九；几乎总是</td><td>Nine times out of ten the printer jams the moment I'm late.<br>十有八九我一赶时间打印机就卡纸。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌnine to ˈfive</td><td>朝九晚五（的工作）</td><td>After ten years of nine to five, he quit and opened a bakery.<br>朝九晚五干了十年，他辞职开了家面包店。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌwhole ˌnine ˈyards (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>全套；应有尽有</td><td>They had a marquee, a band, fireworks — the whole nine yards.<br>他们搭了篷子、请了乐队、放了烟花，全套都来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ninepins</b></td><td>go down, drop, etc. like ˈninepins (informal)</td><td>（许多人）纷纷倒下（病倒或死亡）</td><td>The flu hit the office and people went down like ninepins.<br>流感袭击了办公室，同事一个接一个地倒下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nineteen</b></td><td>talk, etc. nineteen to the ˈdozen (BrE, informal)</td><td>喋喋不休；说个不停</td><td>The two of them were talking nineteen to the dozen in the kitchen.<br>她俩在厨房里说个没完。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nip</b></td><td>nip sth in the ˈbud</td><td>把…扼杀在萌芽状态；防患未然</td><td>Nip that rumour in the bud before the whole school hears it.<br>趁全校还没传开，赶紧把那谣言掐灭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nitty-gritty</b></td><td>get down to the ˌnitty-ˈgritty (informal)</td><td>谈实质问题；讨论关键细节</td><td>Enough small talk — let's get down to the nitty-gritty of the contract.<br>客套够了，我们来谈合同的实质内容吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nod</b></td><td>get the ˈnod (informal)</td><td>获准；被选中</td><td>Her design finally got the nod from the planning committee.<br>她的设计终于得到了规划委员会的首肯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb the ˈnod (informal)</td><td>点头同意；批准</td><td>As soon as the boss gives us the nod, we'll start printing.<br>老板一点头，我们就开印。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌnod is as good as a ˈwink (to a ˈblind man) (saying)</td><td>一点就透；不必明说</td><td>Say no more — a nod is as good as a wink.<br>别说了，我懂，一点就明白。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈnod (BrE, informal)</td><td>（提案）无异议获通过</td><td>The budget went through on the nod in under two minutes.<br>预算案不到两分钟就无异议通过了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nodding</b></td><td>be on ˈnodding terms with sb</td><td>与某人有点头之交</td><td>I'm only on nodding terms with my neighbours after five years here.<br>住了五年，我跟邻居也就是点头之交。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a nodding acˈquaintance with sb/sth</td><td>与…是泛泛之交；对…略知一二</td><td>I have a nodding acquaintance with Spanish, enough to order dinner.<br>我西班牙语略懂一点，够点个晚餐。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>noise</b></td><td>make a (lot of) ˈnoise (about sth) (informal)</td><td>大声抱怨；大肆张扬</td><td>Residents made a lot of noise about the new car park and won.<br>居民对新停车场大闹了一通，最后赢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nook</b></td><td>(in) every ˌnook and ˈcranny (informal)</td><td>每个角落；到处</td><td>We searched every nook and cranny and still couldn't find the keys.<br>我们把每个角落都翻遍了，还是没找到钥匙。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>normal</b></td><td>as per ˈusual/ˈnormal (informal)</td><td>像往常一样；照例</td><td>As per usual, he turned up late and without his notes.<br>照例，他又迟到了，笔记也没带。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nose</b></td><td>cut off your ˈnose to spite your ˈface (informal)</td><td>为泄愤反害自己；损人不利己</td><td>Quitting to annoy your boss is cutting off your nose to spite your face.<br>为气老板而辞职，纯粹是害自己。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get up sb's ˈnose (BrE, informal)</td><td>惹恼某人；让人心烦</td><td>His constant humming really gets up my nose during meetings.<br>开会时他老哼小曲，真让我烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈnose for sth (informal)</td><td>对…很敏感；有发现…的本事</td><td>She has a nose for a bargain and never pays full price.<br>她对便宜货特别敏感，从不付全价。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your nose in a ˈbook, magaˈzine, etc. (informal)</td><td>埋头读书（或看杂志）</td><td>He sat all afternoon with his nose in a book about volcanoes.<br>他整个下午都埋头看一本讲火山的书。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a nose ˈround (BrE, informal)</td><td>四处看看；到处打量</td><td>The estate agent let us have a nose round the empty flat.<br>中介让我们在空公寓里四处看了看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your ˈnose clean (informal)</td><td>循规蹈矩；不惹麻烦</td><td>Keep your nose clean for six months and you'll get the promotion.<br>安分守己半年，升职就是你的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your ˈnose out of sth (informal)</td><td>不插手；别管闲事</td><td>Keep your nose out of my finances, thanks very much.<br>我的钱怎么花不劳你操心，谢谢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your ˌnose to the ˈgrindstone (informal)</td><td>埋头苦干；持续努力</td><td>Keep your nose to the grindstone this term and the exams will look easy.<br>这学期埋头苦读，考试就不难了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look down your ˈnose (at sb/sth) (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>看不起；对…嗤之以鼻</td><td>She looks down her nose at anyone who shops in the market.<br>她瞧不起任何在集市买东西的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌnose to ˈtail (BrE)</td><td>（车辆）首尾相接；一辆接一辆</td><td>The traffic was nose to tail all the way to the tunnel.<br>车辆首尾相接，一直堵到隧道口。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈnose (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>准确地；分毫不差</td><td>Her estimate of the crowd size was right on the nose.<br>她对人数的估计分毫不差。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb's ˈnose out of joint (informal)</td><td>使某人难堪；让某人不痛快</td><td>Giving the office to the newcomer put a few noses out of joint.<br>把办公室给了新人，惹得几个人心里不痛快。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn your ˈnose up at sth (informal)</td><td>看不起；对…嗤之以鼻</td><td>He turned his nose up at the sandwiches and ordered a steak instead.<br>他嫌那些三明治不上档次，改点了牛排。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(right) under sb's ˈnose (informal)</td><td>就在某人眼皮底下</td><td>The keys were right under my nose on the hall table all along.<br>钥匙一直就在门厅桌上，我眼皮底下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with your ˈnose in the air (informal, disapproving)</td><td>目中无人；趾高气扬</td><td>She walks past the whole team with her nose in the air.<br>她从全队面前走过，一副目中无人的样子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not see beyond/past the end of your ˈnose</td><td>目光短浅；只顾眼前</td><td>Politicians who can't see beyond the end of their noses ruin long-term plans.<br>目光短浅的政客会毁掉长远规划。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nosy</b></td><td>a ˌnosy ˈparker (BrE, informal, becoming old-fashioned)</td><td>爱管闲事的人；好打听的人</td><td>The nosy parker next door counts how many visitors we get.<br>隔壁那个爱管闲事的还数我们家来几个客人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>note</b></td><td>hit/strike the right/wrong ˈnote (especially BrE)</td><td>（说话或做事）得体（或不得体）</td><td>His speech struck exactly the right note at such a sad occasion.<br>在那样悲伤的场合，他的致辞分寸拿捏得刚好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of ˈnote</td><td>（用于名词后）重要的；知名的</td><td>Nothing of note happened at the meeting apart from the free biscuits.<br>会上除了有免费饼干，没什么值得一提的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sound/strike a ˈnote (of ˈsth)</td><td>表露某种情绪（或态度）</td><td>The manager struck a note of caution about next year's sales.<br>经理对明年的销售表达了一丝谨慎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈnote of sth</td><td>注意到；留意</td><td>Take note of the exit doors before the film starts.<br>电影开演前先留意一下安全出口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nothing</b></td><td>be/have nothing to ˈdo with sb/sth</td><td>与…无关；与…毫不相干</td><td>Where I spend my weekends has nothing to do with my colleagues.<br>我周末去哪儿跟同事没有半点关系。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈnothing</td><td>免费；不花钱</td><td>My neighbour fixed the bike for nothing and refused a cup of tea.<br>邻居免费帮我修好了车，连茶都不肯喝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have nothing on sb (informal)</td><td>远比不上某人；相形见绌</td><td>My cooking has nothing on my grandmother's, and everyone knows it.<br>我做的菜远不如我外婆，大家都清楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not for ˈnothing do I, will they, etc.</td><td>并非没有理由；不是没道理</td><td>Not for nothing is this street called the coldest place in town.<br>这条街被叫作全城最冷的地方，不是没道理的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈnothing but</td><td>只有；仅仅</td><td>For a week he ate nothing but rice and boiled eggs.<br>他整整一周只吃米饭和水煮蛋。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nothing ˈdoing (informal)</td><td>（拒绝请求）不行；办不到</td><td>Borrow the car for the whole weekend? Nothing doing.<br>借车用一整个周末？不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nothing if not sth (informal)</td><td>（强调）极其；十足</td><td>His plan is nothing if not ambitious, whatever else you say about it.<br>不管别的怎么说，他的计划野心十足。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(there's) nothing ˈin it</td><td>（两者）不相上下；难分高下</td><td>Both runners finished together; there was nothing in it at all.<br>两名选手同时冲线，完全难分高下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈnothing less than</td><td>（强调）简直是；不亚于</td><td>Her recovery after the crash was nothing less than a miracle.<br>车祸后她的康复简直就是奇迹。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nothing ˈlike (informal)</td><td>完全不像；根本不及</td><td>The film is nothing like the book I read as a child.<br>这部电影跟我小时候读的那本书完全不一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>nothing ˈmore than</td><td>（强调）只不过是</td><td>The whole argument was nothing more than a misunderstanding about money.<br>整场争吵只不过是钱上的一场误会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌnothing ˈmuch</td><td>没什么；不多；不重要</td><td>There's nothing much in the fridge except half a lemon.<br>冰箱里没什么东西，就剩半个柠檬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's nothing (else) ˈfor it (but to do sth)</td><td>除此之外别无他法</td><td>The lift was broken, so there was nothing for it but to climb.<br>电梯坏了，只好爬楼梯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's nothing like sth</td><td>没有什么比得上…；…最好不过</td><td>There's nothing like a hot shower after a day on the mountain.<br>在山上跑一天后，没什么比热水澡更舒服了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's nothing ˈto it (informal)</td><td>这事很简单；轻而易举</td><td>Once you've done it twice, there's nothing to it.<br>做过两次以后，这活儿一点都不难。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nouveau</b></td><td>the ˌnouveau ˈriche (from French, disapproving)</td><td>暴发户；新富阶层</td><td>The old villas are being bought up by the nouveau riche.<br>那些老别墅正被暴发户们买下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>now</b></td><td>any minute, day, time, etc. ˈnow</td><td>随时；马上；很快</td><td>The results will be up on the website any minute now.<br>成绩随时会公布在网站上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as of ˈnow</td><td>从现在起；从此刻起</td><td>As of now, nobody uses the back entrance without a pass.<br>从现在起，没有通行证谁都不许走后门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's ˌnow or ˈnever</td><td>机不可失；就这一次机会</td><td>The gallery closes on Sunday, so it's now or never.<br>画廊周日就闭馆了，机不可失。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(every) now and aˈgain/ˈthen</td><td>偶尔；时不时地</td><td>Every now and then we drive out to the coast for the day.<br>我们偶尔会开车去海边玩一天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>now for ˈsb/ˈsth</td><td>（转入新话题）下面轮到；接下来</td><td>That's the weather done — and now for the sports headlines.<br>天气就说到这儿，接下来是体育要闻。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>now... now...</td><td>时而…时而…</td><td>The music was now loud, now barely a whisper, all evening long.<br>那音乐整晚时而高亢，时而轻若耳语。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈnow what? (spoken)</td><td>现在又怎么了；接下来该怎么办</td><td>The engine's dead and the phone's flat — now what?<br>发动机熄火，手机也没电了，现在怎么办？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nth</b></td><td>for the nth ˈtime (informal)</td><td>不知第多少次；说过无数遍</td><td>For the nth time, please take your boots off at the door.<br>第无数次说了，请在门口脱靴子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the nth deˈgree (informal)</td><td>极度地；到了极点</td><td>She plans every trip to the nth degree, right down to snacks.<br>她把每次旅行都规划到极致，连零食都算好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nude</b></td><td>in the ˈnude</td><td>裸体；赤身</td><td>The artist prefers to paint her subjects in the nude.<br>这位画家更喜欢画裸体模特。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nudge</b></td><td>ˌnudge ˈnudge, ˌwink ˈwink • a ˌnudge and a ˈwink</td><td>（暗指男女之事）挤眉弄眼</td><td>He mentioned their 'business trip' with a nudge nudge, wink wink.<br>他提起他俩的“出差”时挤眉弄眼的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>null</b></td><td>ˌnull and ˈvoid (formal)</td><td>无效的；无法律效力的</td><td>Without both signatures the contract is null and void.<br>少了任何一方签字，合同就无效。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>number</b></td><td>do a ˈnumber on sb/sth (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>严重伤害；狠狠整治</td><td>That storm really did a number on our garden fence.<br>那场风暴把我们家院墙折腾得够呛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have sb's ˈnumber (informal)</td><td>看透某人；摸清某人底细</td><td>You can't fool her twice; she's had your number since day one.<br>你骗不了她第二次，她第一天就把你看透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your/sb's (lucky) ˈnumber comes up (informal)</td><td>走运；交好运</td><td>His lucky number came up and he finally got the flat he wanted.<br>他时来运转，终于买到了心仪的公寓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your/sb's number is ˈup (informal)</td><td>死期已到；大限将至</td><td>When the engine caught fire, he thought his number was up.<br>发动机着火时，他以为自己完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌnumber ˈone (informal)</td><td>头号人物；最重要的人或事</td><td>In this house, the dog is number one and everyone knows it.<br>在这个家里，狗是老大，人人都知道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your/sb's number ˈtwo (informal)</td><td>二把手；第二重要的人</td><td>While the director travels, her number two runs the whole office.<br>主任出差时，整个办公室由她的二把手管。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>numbers</b></td><td>by ˈnumbers</td><td>照本宣科；按部就班</td><td>He teaches by numbers and never answers an interesting question.<br>他上课照本宣科，从不回答有意思的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by the ˈnumbers (AmE)</td><td>严格照规矩办；一板一眼</td><td>The inspection was done by the numbers, with no shortcuts anywhere.<br>这次检查完全照章办事，没有任何变通。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˈnumbers game</td><td>数字游戏（只看数量不问实质）</td><td>Hiring has become a numbers game rather than a search for talent.<br>招聘变成了数字游戏，而不是真的找人才。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nut</b></td><td>do your ˈnut (BrE, informal, spoken)</td><td>暴跳如雷；急得发疯</td><td>Dad will do his nut when he sees the scratch on the car.<br>爸看到车上的划痕会气炸的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a hard/tough ˈnut (to ˈcrack) (informal)</td><td>棘手的难题；难对付的人</td><td>Getting him to change his mind is a tough nut to crack.<br>想让他改主意可是块难啃的骨头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>off your ˈnut (BrE, informal, spoken)</td><td>发疯；脑子不正常</td><td>Swimming in that river in January? You're off your nut.<br>一月份还去那条河里游泳？你疯了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nuts</b></td><td>the ˌnuts and ˈbolts (of sth) (informal)</td><td>基本要点；具体细节</td><td>She understands the nuts and bolts of running a restaurant kitchen.<br>她懂得经营餐厅后厨的各种实际门道。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nutshell</b></td><td>(put sth) in a ˈnutshell (informal)</td><td>简而言之；一言以蔽之</td><td>In a nutshell, we spent too much and sold too little.<br>简而言之，我们花得太多，卖得太少。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nutty</b></td><td>(as) nutty as a ˈfruitcake (informal, humorous)</td><td>疯疯癫癫；神经兮兮</td><td>Her uncle is as nutty as a fruitcake, but everyone adores him.<br>她叔叔疯疯癫癫的，可人人都喜欢他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>oaks</b></td><td>great/tall ˌoaks from little acorns ˈgrow (saying)</td><td>合抱之木生于毫末；万事起于微末</td><td>The shop began in her kitchen — great oaks from little acorns grow.<br>这家店最早只是她的厨房，万丈高楼平地起。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>oar</b></td><td>put/stick your ˈoar in (BrE, informal)</td><td>多管闲事；横插一杠</td><td>We nearly agreed until his brother stuck his oar in.<br>我们差点谈妥了，结果他哥来横插一杠。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>oath</b></td><td>on/under ˈoath (law)</td><td>宣誓（保证说实话）</td><td>The witness admitted under oath that he had lied to police.<br>证人在宣誓后承认曾向警方撒谎。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>oats</b></td><td>get your ˈoats (BrE, informal)</td><td>有规律的性生活</td><td>He's been in a much better mood since he started getting his oats.<br>自从他有了固定的性生活，脾气好多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>object</b></td><td>money, ˌexpense, etc. is no ˈobject</td><td>钱不成问题；费用不在话下</td><td>Money is no object for that family when it comes to holidays.<br>在度假这件事上，那家人从来不心疼钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˈobject lesson</td><td>可供借鉴的实例；活生生的教训</td><td>His failed shop is an object lesson in ignoring your customers.<br>他倒闭的店铺是无视顾客的活教材。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>occasion</b></td><td>have occasion to do sth (formal)</td><td>有理由做某事；有必要做</td><td>I have had occasion to complain about that driver twice this month.<br>这个月我已经有两次不得不投诉那位司机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ocˈcasion(s)</td><td>偶尔；有时</td><td>On occasion he still cooks the Sunday roast for the whole family.<br>他偶尔还会给全家做周日烤肉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ocean</b></td><td>an ocean of sth (BrE also oceans of sth)</td><td>大量；无数</td><td>There's an ocean of paperwork waiting on my desk tomorrow.<br>明天我桌上等着一大堆文件。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>odd</b></td><td>odd ˈjobs</td><td>零活；杂活</td><td>He does odd jobs around the village for a bit of extra cash.<br>他在村里干点零活，赚些外快。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the odd man/one ˈout</td><td>与众不同的人（或物）；多余的一个</td><td>In a family of doctors, the musician was always the odd one out.<br>在一家子医生里，那个搞音乐的总显得格格不入。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an odd/a queer ˈfish (BrE, becoming old-fashioned)</td><td>怪人；行为古怪的人</td><td>The new caretaker is an odd fish, but he keeps the place spotless.<br>新来的管理员是个怪人，不过把楼里打理得一尘不染。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>odds</b></td><td>against all (the) ˈodds</td><td>尽管困难重重；出人意料地</td><td>Against all the odds, the little team reached the national final.<br>这支小球队克服重重困难打进了全国决赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be at ˈodds (with sb/sth) (about/over sth)</td><td>与…意见不合；与…相矛盾</td><td>His account of the evening is at odds with what the neighbours saw.<br>他对那晚的说法与邻居所见不符。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it makes no ˈodds (to sb/sth) (spoken, especially BrE)</td><td>没关系；无所谓</td><td>Tea or coffee — it makes no odds to me.<br>茶还是咖啡，我都无所谓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌodds and ˈends (BrE also ˌodds and ˈsods)</td><td>零碎物品；杂七杂八的东西</td><td>The drawer is full of odds and ends we never use.<br>抽屉里塞满了我们从不用的零碎东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the odds ˈare (that...) (also (it's) ˌodds-ˈon (that...))</td><td>很有可能；十有八九</td><td>The odds are that she'll be late again, so order without her.<br>她十有八九又要迟到，别等她点吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the odds are aˈgainst sth/sb doing sth</td><td>…不大可能发生；希望不大</td><td>The odds are against us finishing the roof before winter.<br>我们赶在冬天前修好屋顶希望不大。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>over the ˈodds (informal)</td><td>（价钱）高于常价；出价过高</td><td>We paid well over the odds for the flat because of the location.<br>因为地段好，我们买这套公寓多花了不少钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's the ˈodds? (BrE, informal)</td><td>那有什么关系；有什么要紧</td><td>So we arrive an hour late — what's the odds?<br>就算晚到一小时，那又怎么样？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>good</b></td><td>be in good/bad ˈodour (with sb) (formal)</td><td>得（或不得）某人青睐</td><td>He's in bad odour with the head after missing three deadlines.<br>连误三次期限后，他在主管那儿很不受待见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>off</b></td><td>be ˌoff for ˈsth (informal)</td><td>某物有…数量；某物的储备情况</td><td>How are we off for milk before I go to the shop?<br>我去商店前问一下，牛奶还剩多少？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌoff and ˈon • ˌon and ˈoff</td><td>断断续续地；时有时无</td><td>It rained off and on all afternoon, so we stayed indoors.<br>整个下午断断续续下雨，我们就待在屋里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ofˈfence (at sth) (BrE) (AmE take ofˈfense (at sth))</td><td>生气；见怪；感到被冒犯</td><td>Don't take offence, but that jacket really doesn't suit you.<br>别生气啊，那件夹克真的不适合你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no ofˈfence (spoken)</td><td>无意冒犯；别见怪</td><td>No offence, but your singing woke the whole street.<br>无意冒犯，可你的歌声吵醒了整条街。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>offensive</b></td><td>be on the ofˈfensive</td><td>采取攻势；主动出击</td><td>The company has been on the offensive since the story broke.<br>消息曝光后，公司一直在主动反击。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go on(to) the ofˈfensive • take the ofˈfensive</td><td>转入进攻；先发制人</td><td>After half-time the team went on the offensive and scored twice.<br>下半场球队转守为攻，连进两球。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>offer</b></td><td>have sth to ˈoffer</td><td>能提供…；有…可供选择</td><td>The town has plenty to offer families with young children.<br>这座小城为有小孩的家庭提供了不少去处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈoffer</td><td>可买到的；提供的；在特价出售</td><td>There were three jobs on offer, all of them badly paid.<br>有三份工作可选，但薪水都很低。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under ˈoffer (BrE)</td><td>（房产）已有买主出价</td><td>The cottage went under offer within a week of being listed.<br>那栋小屋挂牌一周内就有人出价了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>offices</b></td><td>through sb's good ˈoffices (formal)</td><td>经某人斡旋；承某人帮忙</td><td>Through the good offices of a friend, we got a table at the restaurant.<br>多亏一位朋友帮忙，我们在那家餐厅订到了位子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>offing</b></td><td>in the ˈoffing (informal)</td><td>即将发生；可能出现</td><td>There are big changes in the offing at head office.<br>总部即将有大变动。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>often</b></td><td>every so ˈoften</td><td>偶尔；时不时</td><td>Every so often she rings just to check that we're all right.<br>她时不时打个电话来，看看我们好不好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) ˌoften as ˈnot • more ˌoften than ˈnot</td><td>通常；多半</td><td>More often than not, the bus arrives before I reach the stop.<br>多半情况下，我还没到站公交就先到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>oil</b></td><td>be no ˈoil painting (BrE, humorous)</td><td>相貌平平；长得不好看</td><td>He's no oil painting, but he's the kindest man I know.<br>他长得一般，却是我认识的最善良的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>oil the ˈwheels (BrE) (AmE grease the ˈwheels)</td><td>疏通关系；使事情顺利进行</td><td>A good lunch can oil the wheels of any difficult negotiation.<br>一顿好饭能让再难的谈判都顺畅些。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>okay</b></td><td>be doing OˈK/oˈkay (informal)</td><td>过得不错；赚得挺好</td><td>Since the second shop opened, they're doing okay for money.<br>第二家店开张后，他们经济上过得挺宽裕。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/get the OˈK/oˈkay (informal)</td><td>批准；获得同意</td><td>We can start digging as soon as the council gives us the okay.<br>市政厅一批准，我们就能开挖。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>old</b></td><td>the Old ˈBill (BrE, informal)</td><td>警察；警方</td><td>Someone called the Old Bill when the shouting started.<br>一开始吵嚷，就有人报了警。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>old</b></td><td>any old ˈhow (spoken)</td><td>随随便便；马马虎虎</td><td>He'd thrown his clothes into the case any old how.<br>他把衣服胡乱塞进了箱子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈany old thing, time, place, etc. (spoken)</td><td>随便哪个（或何时、何处）</td><td>Come round any old time; there's always someone at home.<br>你随时来都行，家里总有人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈold times' sake</td><td>看在旧日情分上；念及老交情</td><td>Let's walk home the long way, for old times' sake.<br>看在从前的份上，我们绕远路走回去吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈgood/ˈbad old days</td><td>从前的好（或苦）日子</td><td>Grandad still talks about the good old days before the mine closed.<br>爷爷还常说起矿场关闭前的好日子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's the (same) old ˈstory</td><td>又是老一套；老问题又来了</td><td>It's the same old story: big promises and no funding.<br>又是老一套：大话说尽，钱一分没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of ˈold (formal or literary)</td><td>往昔；从前</td><td>The knights of old would have ridden through this very valley.<br>昔日的骑士想必就是穿过这道山谷的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of the ˈold school</td><td>老派的；守旧的</td><td>He's a teacher of the old school and still marks in red ink.<br>他是位老派教师，至今还用红笔批改。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) old as the ˈhills</td><td>非常古老；由来已久</td><td>That joke is as old as the hills and still nobody laughs.<br>那个笑话老掉牙了，还是没人笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an old ˈbag (disapproving, offensive)</td><td>讨厌的老女人</td><td>Don't call her an old bag; she's only sixty and very sharp.<br>别叫她老婆子，她才六十，脑子灵光得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌold ˈbat (BrE, informal, disapproving)</td><td>讨厌（或愚蠢）的老太婆</td><td>The old bat next door complains every time we play music.<br>隔壁那老太太一听我们放音乐就投诉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>old ˈboy/girl (informal)</td><td>老兄；老姐；年长的男子或妇女</td><td>The old boy next door still cycles to the market every single morning.<br>隔壁那位老先生每天早上还骑车去市场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌold ˈboy network (BrE, informal)</td><td>校友关系网；老同学之间的互相关照</td><td>He got that job through the old boy network, not because of his skills.<br>他靠校友关系拿到那份工作，根本不是凭本事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an/that old ˈchestnut (informal)</td><td>老掉牙的笑话或故事</td><td>Not that old chestnut about your fishing trip again — we've heard it twice.<br>别又讲你钓鱼那个老段子了，我们都听两遍了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an old ˈdear (informal)</td><td>老太太</td><td>An old dear on the bus insisted on giving my daughter a boiled sweet.<br>公交车上一位老太太非要给我女儿一颗水果糖。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an old ˈflame (informal)</td><td>旧情人；老相好</td><td>She bumped into an old flame at the wedding and blushed all evening.<br>她在婚礼上碰见旧情人，整晚脸都红着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌold ˈfogey/fogy (usually disapproving)</td><td>守旧的人；老顽固</td><td>My dad calls himself an old fogey because he refuses to use a smartphone.<br>我爸不肯用智能手机，自称是个老顽固。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌold ˈguard</td><td>保守派；元老派；保守势力</td><td>The old guard on the committee blocked every idea the new members proposed.<br>委员会里的元老派否决了新成员提出的每个想法。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an old ˈhand (at sth/at doing sth)</td><td>老手；行家；有经验的人</td><td>Ask Wei to fix it — he's an old hand at repairing these old engines.<br>找小魏修吧，他修这种老发动机是老手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>old ˈhat</td><td>过时的；陈腐的事物</td><td>Fax machines are old hat now; nobody in this office uses one.<br>传真机早就过时了，办公室里没人再用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(have) an ˌold head on young ˈshoulders</td><td>少年老成；年轻而有见识</td><td>At sixteen she handled the crisis calmly — an old head on young shoulders.<br>才十六岁就能冷静处理危机，真是少年老成。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌold ˈmaid (old-fashioned, disapproving)</td><td>老处女；老姑娘</td><td>In those days people cruelly called any unmarried woman over thirty an old maid.<br>那年头，过了三十还没结婚的女人都被刻薄地叫作老姑娘。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>old ˈman (informal)</td><td>老爸；老公；老头儿</td><td>My old man taught me to drive in an empty car park one Sunday.<br>我老爸在一个周日的空停车场里教我开车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌold school ˈtie (BrE)</td><td>私立学校校友之间的互助情谊</td><td>Promotion here still depends on the old school tie rather than actual results.<br>这里的升迁靠的还是校友关系，不是实际业绩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌold wives' ˈtale (disapproving)</td><td>无稽之谈；迷信说法</td><td>Going out with wet hair causes colds? That's just an old wives' tale.<br>湿着头发出门会感冒？那不过是无稽之谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>old ˈwoman (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>老婆；老妈；婆婆妈妈的人</td><td>Stop fussing about the curtains — you're being a real old woman today.<br>别为窗帘瞎操心了，你今天真够婆婆妈妈的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a chip off the old ˈblock (informal)</td><td>酷似父母的人；一个模子刻出来的</td><td>He argues about football just like his dad — a chip off the old block.<br>他争论足球的样子活脱脱他爸，真是一个模子刻出来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>olive</b></td><td>hold out/offer an ˈolive branch (to sb)</td><td>伸出橄榄枝；表示愿意和好</td><td>After weeks of silence, she offered an olive branch by inviting him to dinner.<br>沉默数周后，她请他吃饭，算是伸出了橄榄枝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>omelette (AmE also omelet)</td><td>煎蛋饼；摊鸡蛋</td><td>He made a cheese omelette for supper because the fridge was almost empty.<br>冰箱快空了，他就做了个奶酪蛋饼当晚饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you can't make an omelette without breaking ˈeggs (saying)</td><td>不花代价难成大事；有得必有失</td><td>Layoffs are painful, but you can't make an omelette without breaking eggs.<br>裁员很痛苦，但不破不立，总得付出代价。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on</b></td><td>be ˈon about sth (informal)</td><td>谈论某事；意指</td><td>What on earth are you on about? I can't follow your story at all.<br>你到底在说什么？我完全听不懂你讲的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/go/keep ˈon about sth (informal, disapproving)</td><td>唠叨没完；喋喋不休地抱怨</td><td>He keeps on about the noisy neighbours every time we visit his flat.<br>我们每次去他家，他都唠叨邻居太吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/go/keep ˈon at sb (to do sth) (informal, disapproving)</td><td>对某人唠叨；喋喋不休地催促</td><td>My mum keeps on at me to tidy my room before the guests arrive.<br>我妈一直唠叨要我在客人来之前收拾房间。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) not ˈon (informal)</td><td>不行；不能接受；没门儿</td><td>Turning up two hours late without calling is just not on.<br>迟到两小时还不打个电话，这实在不能接受。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌon and ˈon</td><td>连续不停地；没完没了地</td><td>The lecturer talked on and on while half the students quietly dozed off.<br>那讲师没完没了地讲，一半学生悄悄睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>once</b></td><td>ˌall at ˈonce</td><td>突然；忽然；同时</td><td>All at once the lights went out and the whole street fell silent.<br>忽然间灯全灭了，整条街都安静下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈonce</td><td>立即；马上；同时</td><td>Put the phone down and come here at once — this is urgent.<br>放下电话马上过来，这事很急。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) for ˈonce ◆ just this ˈonce (spoken)</td><td>就这一次；仅此一次</td><td>For once, let me pay the bill — you've treated me all month.<br>就这一次让我买单吧，你请了我一个月了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>once aˈgain ◆ once ˈmore</td><td>又一次；再次</td><td>Once again the train was delayed, and we missed the connecting flight.<br>火车又一次晚点，我们错过了转机航班。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>once a..., always a...</td><td>一次为…便永远是…（本性难改）</td><td>Once a cheat, always a cheat — I wouldn't trust him with money.<br>一次骗人，终身骗人，钱的事我不会信他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>once and for ˈall</td><td>一劳永逸地；彻底地；最终</td><td>Let's settle this argument once and for all and never mention it again.<br>咱们一劳永逸地了结这场争论，以后别再提。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>once ˈbitten, ˌtwice ˈshy (saying)</td><td>一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳</td><td>He won't lend money to friends now — once bitten, twice shy.<br>他现在不借钱给朋友了，一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌonce in a blue ˈmoon (informal)</td><td>千载难逢；极难得；偶尔</td><td>My brother phones home once in a blue moon, usually when he needs money.<br>我弟弟难得往家里打电话，通常是缺钱的时候。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(every) ˌonce in a ˈwhile</td><td>偶尔；间或</td><td>Every once in a while we drive to the coast just to see the sea.<br>我们偶尔开车去海边，就为看看大海。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌonce or ˈtwice</td><td>一两次；几次</td><td>I've met her once or twice at conferences, but we never really talked.<br>我在会上见过她一两次，但没真正聊过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌonce too ˈoften</td><td>屡犯而终遭报应；这次没能幸免</td><td>He cheated on the test once too often and was finally expelled.<br>他考试作弊次数太多，终于被开除了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌonce upon a ˈtime</td><td>从前；很久以前</td><td>Once upon a time this quiet village had three pubs and a cinema.<br>很久以前，这个安静的村子有三家酒馆和一间电影院。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>once-over</b></td><td>give sb/sth a/the ˈonce-over (informal)</td><td>匆匆打量；草草过目</td><td>The mechanic gave my car the once-over and said the brakes needed work.<br>修理工把我的车草草检查了一遍，说刹车得修。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>one</b></td><td>as ˈone (also as one ˈman) (formal)</td><td>一致地；全体同时</td><td>The crowd rose as one when the injured player walked back onto the pitch.<br>受伤球员重回球场时，观众齐刷刷地站了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be) at ˈone (with sb/sth) (formal)</td><td>与…完全一致；融为一体</td><td>Sitting by the lake at dawn, he felt completely at one with nature.<br>黎明时坐在湖边，他觉得自己与自然融为一体。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be (a) one for sth/for doing sth (informal)</td><td>喜欢或善于做某事</td><td>She's a great one for organizing surprise parties at the last minute.<br>她特别喜欢临时张罗惊喜派对。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get/have one ˈup on sb (informal)</td><td>胜过某人一筹；占上风</td><td>Finishing the report early got her one up on the rest of the team.<br>提前交报告让她比组里其他人略胜一筹。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈupmanship noun (disapproving)</td><td>胜人一筹的伎俩；争强好胜</td><td>Their constant upmanship about holidays and cars makes dinner parties exhausting.<br>他们总在假期和车子上比来比去，饭局累人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I, you, etc. for ˈone</td><td>我（或你等）就是其中之一</td><td>I for one think the new schedule is far better than the old mess.<br>我个人认为新排班比原先那一团乱强多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/put one ˈover on sb/sth (informal)</td><td>占某人便宜；捉弄某人；胜过</td><td>He loves getting one over on his brother at cards every Christmas.<br>他每年圣诞打牌都爱赢他哥一把。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(you've, he's, etc.) got it in ˈone (informal)</td><td>一下子就猜到；一下子明白</td><td>You think she's quitting to travel? You've got it in one.<br>你猜她辞职是想去旅行？一下就猜中了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have had ˌone too ˈmany (informal)</td><td>酒喝多了</td><td>He'd clearly had one too many, so we took his car keys away.<br>他显然喝多了，我们就把他车钥匙收走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈone</td><td>集于一身；合为一体</td><td>This gadget is a torch, radio and phone charger in one.<br>这个小玩意儿集手电、收音机和充电器于一身。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's a hundred, etc. to ˈone that sb/sth will (not) do sth</td><td>几乎可以肯定会（或不会）发生</td><td>It's a hundred to one that he'll forget her birthday again this year.<br>几乎可以肯定他今年又会忘了她的生日。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one after aˈnother/the ˈother</td><td>一个接一个地；相继</td><td>One after another the guests made excuses and slipped quietly out.<br>客人们一个接一个找借口悄悄溜走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌone and ˈall (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>各位；大家；每一个人</td><td>Good evening one and all, and welcome to our little village concert.<br>各位晚上好，欢迎来到我们的小村音乐会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌone and ˈonly</td><td>唯一的；独一无二的；大名鼎鼎的</td><td>Please welcome the one and only Amy Chen to the stage tonight.<br>今晚请欢迎独一无二的陈艾米登台。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one and the ˈsame</td><td>同一个；一模一样</td><td>The quiet gardener and the famous poet turned out to be one and the same.<br>那个安静的园丁和著名诗人原来是同一个人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one by ˈone</td><td>一个接一个；逐一</td><td>One by one the candles went out until the room was dark.<br>蜡烛一根接一根熄灭，房间终于全黑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>when you've seen, heard, etc. ˈone, you've seen, heard, etc. them ˈall (saying)</td><td>见过一个就等于都见过；大同小异</td><td>When you've seen one of these shopping malls, you've seen them all.<br>这种商场看过一个，其余的也就都一样了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>one-horse</b></td><td>a ˌone-horse ˈrace</td><td>毫无悬念的比赛；只有一方可能获胜</td><td>With their star striker back, the league became a one-horse race.<br>头号前锋回归后，联赛就成了毫无悬念的角逐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌone-horse ˈtown (informal)</td><td>偏僻沉闷的小镇</td><td>He grew up in a one-horse town with a single shop and no cinema.<br>他在一个只有一家小店、没有影院的偏僻小镇长大。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>one-night</b></td><td>a ˌone-night ˈstand</td><td>一夜情；一夜情人</td><td>She insisted it was just a one-night stand and nothing more serious.<br>她坚称那只是一夜情，没什么别的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>one-off</b></td><td>a ˌone-ˈoff (BrE)</td><td>一次性的事物；绝无仅有的事物</td><td>This discount is a one-off, so don't expect it again next month.<br>这个折扣只有一次，别指望下个月还有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>one-track</b></td><td>have a ˌone-track ˈmind</td><td>一门心思只想一件事；思路狭隘</td><td>During exam season he has a one-track mind and talks only about revision.<br>考试季他一门心思只想复习，别的什么都不聊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>only</b></td><td>not only... but (also)...</td><td>不但…而且…</td><td>She not only cooked dinner but also cleaned the whole kitchen afterwards.<br>她不但做了晚饭，之后还把厨房全打扫了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈonly if</td><td>只有…才…</td><td>I'll go to the party only if you promise to drive me home.<br>只有你答应送我回家，我才去这个派对。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌonly ˈjust</td><td>刚刚；勉强</td><td>We only just caught the last bus home after the concert ended.<br>音乐会散场后，我们刚好赶上末班车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>only to do sth (written)</td><td>结果却；不料竟</td><td>He rushed to the station only to find the train had already left.<br>他赶到车站，结果发现火车已经开走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>only too ˈglad, ˈready, etc. (to do sth)</td><td>非常乐意做某事</td><td>She was only too glad to lend us her flat for the weekend.<br>她非常乐意把公寓借给我们过周末。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>onside</b></td><td>get/keep sb onˈside</td><td>得到某人的支持；争取某人站在自己一边</td><td>We need to get the finance team onside before we present the plan.<br>提交方案前我们得先争取到财务部门的支持。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>onto</b></td><td>be ˈonto sb</td><td>察觉某人的错事；盯上某人</td><td>The police are onto him after that suspicious bank transfer last week.<br>上周那笔可疑转账之后，警方已经盯上他了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈonto sth</td><td>发现有价值的东西；有了眉目</td><td>I think we're onto something big with this new battery design.<br>我觉得这个新电池设计让我们有了重大发现。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>open</b></td><td>be ˈopen to sth</td><td>愿意考虑某事；易受…影响</td><td>The boss says she's open to suggestions about changing our working hours.<br>老板说她愿意听取关于调整工时的建议。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/keep an ˌopen ˈmind (on/about sth)</td><td>不怀成见；思想开明</td><td>Keep an open mind about the new manager until you've actually worked with him.<br>在真正共事之前，对新经理别抱成见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(out) in(to) the ˈopen</td><td>公开；公之于众</td><td>The scandal finally came out into the open when a nurse spoke to reporters.<br>一名护士向记者开口后，丑闻终于公之于众。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˌopen ˈair</td><td>户外；露天</td><td>We ate breakfast in the open air, watching mist rise off the lake.<br>我们在户外吃早饭，看着湖面升起薄雾。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˌopen ˈmarket</td><td>在公开市场上</td><td>The painting would fetch millions if it were sold on the open market.<br>这幅画若在公开市场出售，能卖到几百万。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌopen ˈbook</td><td>极坦率的人；一目了然的事</td><td>My little sister is an open book — you can read her face instantly.<br>我妹妹是本打开的书，看脸就知道她想什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>open the ˈdoor to/for sb/sth</td><td>为…敞开大门；提供良机</td><td>That internship opened the door to a career in publishing for her.<br>那次实习为她打开了出版业的职业大门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>open your/sb's ˈeyes (to sth)</td><td>使认清事实；使开眼界</td><td>Working in the shelter opened my eyes to how many families struggle.<br>在收容所工作让我看清有多少家庭在苦苦挣扎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>open ˈfire (on sb/sth)</td><td>开火；开枪射击</td><td>The soldiers were ordered not to open fire unless they were attacked first.<br>士兵接到命令，除非先遭攻击否则不得开火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>open the ˈfloodgates (to sth)</td><td>打开闸门；放开限制引发大量涌入</td><td>Cutting the fee would open the floodgates to thousands of new applicants.<br>降低费用会引来成千上万的新申请者。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>open your ˈheart (to sb)</td><td>向某人倾诉衷肠</td><td>After a second glass of wine she opened her heart to me about her divorce.<br>喝到第二杯酒，她向我倾诉了离婚的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(keep) open ˈhouse</td><td>热情好客；随时欢迎客人来访</td><td>My grandparents kept open house every Sunday, and neighbours just walked in.<br>我祖父母每周日都门户大开，邻居们径直就进来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌopen inviˈtation (to sb)</td><td>随时欢迎来访的邀请；诱人犯罪的可乘之机</td><td>Leaving your laptop on the seat is an open invitation to thieves.<br>把笔记本电脑放在座位上等于给小偷发请帖。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌopen ˈletter</td><td>公开信</td><td>Hundreds of scientists signed an open letter urging the government to act.<br>数百名科学家联署公开信，敦促政府采取行动。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>open your (big) ˈmouth (informal)</td><td>多嘴；乱说话</td><td>Why did you open your big mouth about the surprise party?<br>你干嘛多嘴把惊喜派对说出去？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌopen ˈquestion (also ˌopen to ˈquestion)</td><td>悬而未决的问题；有待商榷</td><td>Whether the policy actually saves money remains an open question.<br>这项政策是否真能省钱，仍是个悬而未决的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌopen ˈsecret</td><td>公开的秘密</td><td>It's an open secret that the two managers can't stand each other.<br>那两位经理互相看不顺眼，这是公开的秘密。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>open ˈsesame (humorous)</td><td>芝麻开门；打开门路的法宝</td><td>A good reference from her seems to be the open sesame in this industry.<br>在这行，她的一封推荐信似乎就是芝麻开门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>open the ˈway for sb/sth (to do sth)</td><td>为…开辟道路；开方便之门</td><td>The treaty opened the way for trade between the two countries to resume.<br>这项条约为两国恢复贸易铺平了道路。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with ˌopen ˈarms</td><td>张开双臂热情欢迎；诚挚地</td><td>The village welcomed the new doctor with open arms and homemade cakes.<br>村里张开双臂欢迎新医生，还端来自制蛋糕。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>open-and-shut</b></td><td>ˌopen-and-ˈshut</td><td>一目了然的；显而易见的</td><td>The lawyer said the dispute was open-and-shut and would not reach court.<br>律师说这场纠纷一目了然，不会闹上法庭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌopen-and-shut ˈcase</td><td>（案件等）一目了然的案子</td><td>With three witnesses and a video, it's an open-and-shut case.<br>有三名证人加一段录像，这案子一目了然。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>openers</b></td><td>for ˈopeners (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>首先；作为开始</td><td>For openers, tell me exactly where you were on Friday night.<br>首先，告诉我周五晚上你到底在哪里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>operation</b></td><td>come into opeˈration</td><td>开始运转；开始生效</td><td>The new parking rules come into operation at the start of next month.<br>新的停车规定将于下月初开始生效。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in opeˈration</td><td>在运转中；在使用中；有效</td><td>Only two of the four lifts are in operation while repairs continue.<br>维修期间四部电梯只有两部在运行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sth into opeˈration</td><td>实施；使运转；启用</td><td>The council will put the recycling scheme into operation in June.<br>市政会将于六月启动这项回收计划。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>operative</b></td><td>the ˌoperative ˈword</td><td>关键词；最重要的字眼</td><td>He said he'd try to help — and 'try' is the operative word here.<br>他说会尽量帮忙，这里的关键词是「尽量」。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>opinion</b></td><td>be of the opinion that... (formal)</td><td>认为…；相信…</td><td>The committee is of the opinion that the current rules need urgent revision.<br>委员会认为现行规则亟需修订。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a good, bad, high, low, etc. oˈpinion of sb/sth</td><td>对…评价好（或差、高、低等）</td><td>She has a very high opinion of her new assistant's writing skills.<br>她对新助理的写作能力评价很高。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your considered oˈpinion</td><td>深思熟虑后的看法</td><td>In my considered opinion, we should delay the launch until spring.<br>依我深思熟虑后的看法，我们该把发布推迟到春天。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>opposed</b></td><td>as opˈposed to (written)</td><td>而不是；相对于</td><td>We want steady growth, as opposed to a quick profit this quarter.<br>我们要的是稳定增长，而不是这个季度的快钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>opposite</b></td><td>your ˌopposite ˈnumber</td><td>职位对等的人；对口人员</td><td>Our sales director met her opposite number from the Japanese firm.<br>我们的销售总监会见了那家日企的对口负责人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌopposite ˈsex</td><td>异性</td><td>At fourteen he was suddenly shy around members of the opposite sex.<br>十四岁那年，他在异性面前忽然变得腼腆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>opposites</b></td><td>ˌopposites atˈtract</td><td>异性相吸；性格相反的人互相吸引</td><td>She's loud and he's quiet, but opposites attract, I suppose.<br>她外向他内向，不过大概真是性格相反才互相吸引吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>opposition</b></td><td>in oppoˈsition to sb/sth</td><td>反对某人或某事物</td><td>Thousands marched in opposition to the plan to close the hospital.<br>数千人游行，反对关闭医院的计划。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>option</b></td><td>the ˌsoft/ˌeasy ˈoption (often disapproving)</td><td>轻松的选择；避重就轻的做法</td><td>Dropping the difficult module would be the easy option, but you'd regret it.<br>放弃那门难课是省事的选择，但你会后悔。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>options</b></td><td>keep/leave (all) your ˈoptions open</td><td>保留选择余地；暂不作决定</td><td>He's applied to three universities to keep his options open.<br>他申请了三所大学，好保留选择余地。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>order</b></td><td>in ˈorder</td><td>（文件）有效合法；井然有序；适宜</td><td>The inspector checked our passports and said everything was in order.<br>检查员查了护照，说一切都没问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/of the ˈorder of (BrE) (AmE on the ˈorder of) (formal)</td><td>大约；数量在…左右</td><td>Repairs will cost something in the order of five thousand pounds.<br>修理费大约在五千英镑上下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈorder that (formal)</td><td>为了；以便</td><td>We left at dawn in order that we might reach the border by noon.<br>我们黎明出发，以便中午前抵达边境。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈorder to do sth</td><td>为了；以便</td><td>She took a second job in order to pay off her student loan.<br>为了还清助学贷款，她又找了份兼职。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of the highest/first ˈorder ◆ of a high ˈorder</td><td>最高级别的；第一流的</td><td>His performance last night was showmanship of the highest order.<br>他昨晚的表演是第一流的舞台功夫。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈorder</td><td>已订购而尚未交货</td><td>The parts are on order and should arrive by the end of the week.<br>零件已经订了，本周末前应该能到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌorder of the ˈday</td><td>当时盛行的做法；应时之举</td><td>During the heatwave, cold drinks and short meetings were the order of the day.<br>热浪期间，冷饮和短会成了常态。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of ˈorder</td><td>出故障；不合规矩；次序颠倒</td><td>The coffee machine is out of order again, so we walked to the café.<br>咖啡机又坏了，我们只好走去咖啡馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>orders</b></td><td>be in/take (holy) ˈorders</td><td>担任圣职；成为神职人员</td><td>He gave up law and took holy orders at the age of forty.<br>他四十岁放弃律师工作，接受了圣职。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be under ˈorders (to do sth)</td><td>奉命做某事</td><td>The guards were under orders to let nobody past the gate.<br>卫兵奉命不许任何人通过大门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈmarching orders (BrE, informal)</td><td>被解雇；被撵走</td><td>After turning up drunk twice, he finally got his marching orders.<br>醉着上了两次班后，他终于被炒了鱿鱼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ordinary</b></td><td>in the ˌordinary ˈway (BrE)</td><td>一般；通常</td><td>In the ordinary way I'd walk, but the rain is far too heavy.<br>换作平常我会走路，可今天雨太大了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of the ˈordinary</td><td>不寻常；特殊</td><td>Did you notice anything out of the ordinary on the night of the fire?<br>失火那晚你有没有注意到什么反常的事？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>other</b></td><td>every ˈother (person/thing)</td><td>每隔一个（人或物）</td><td>She goes to the gym every other day, usually before breakfast.<br>她每隔一天去一次健身房，通常在早饭前。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌother ˈday, ˈmorning, etc.</td><td>前不久的一天（或一个上午等）</td><td>I ran into your cousin at the market the other day.<br>前几天我在市场上碰见你表弟了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>other than</td><td>除…以外；不同于</td><td>Nobody other than the manager can unlock the safe in here.<br>除了经理，这里没人能打开保险柜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈsomebody/ˈsomething/ˈsomewhere or ˈother</td><td>某个人（或事物、地方）</td><td>She's gone off to Spain or somewhere or other for the winter.<br>她跑去西班牙还是哪儿过冬了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>otherwise</b></td><td>or ˈotherwise</td><td>或相反；或其他情况</td><td>Her calmness, real or otherwise, kept the whole team from panicking.<br>她的镇定，无论真假，让整个团队没有慌乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>out</b></td><td>be (all) out to do sth ◆ be (all) out for sth</td><td>一心想做某事；全力以赴争取</td><td>That newspaper is all out to ruin his reputation before the election.<br>那家报纸一心想在选举前毁掉他的名声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌout and aˈbout (BrE)</td><td>（病后）能外出走动；四处走动</td><td>After three weeks in bed she's finally out and about again.<br>卧床三周后，她终于又能出门走动了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈout of it (informal)</td><td>神志不清；昏昏然；被冷落</td><td>He was completely out of it after the painkillers and slept all afternoon.<br>吃了止痛药他整个人昏昏沉沉，睡了一下午。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈout there (informal)</td><td>怪异的；不合常规的</td><td>Her fashion ideas are a bit out there, but the crowd loved them.<br>她的时装想法有点怪，但观众很喜欢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈout with it!</td><td>有话直说！说出来吧！</td><td>You've been sulking all morning — come on, out with it!<br>你整个上午都绷着脸，快说出来吧！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>outset</b></td><td>at/from the ˈoutset (of sth)</td><td>一开始；起初</td><td>From the outset of the trip we knew the weather would be terrible.<br>旅行一开始我们就知道天气会很糟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>outside</b></td><td>at the outˈside</td><td>至多；充其量</td><td>The whole job will take three hours at the outside.<br>这活儿最多也就三个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the outˈside</td><td>表面上；外表上</td><td>On the outside he seemed calm, but his hands were shaking badly.<br>他表面镇定，可双手抖得厉害。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌoutside ˈworld ◆ the world outˈside</td><td>外界；外面的世界</td><td>The monks have almost no contact with the outside world all winter.<br>整个冬天，僧侣们几乎与外界没有联系。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beyond/outside your ˈken</td><td>非某人所能理解；超出某人的知识范围</td><td>How the software actually works is completely beyond my ken.<br>这软件到底怎么运作，我完全搞不懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>over</b></td><td>(all) over aˈgain</td><td>再一次；从头重来</td><td>The file was deleted, so I had to type the whole report over again.<br>文件被删了，我只好把报告从头再打一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>over and aˈbove sth</td><td>除…之外；在…之上</td><td>He gets a big annual bonus over and above his basic salary.<br>除了基本工资，他每年还有一笔丰厚的年终奖。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>overshoot</b></td><td>overshoot the ˈmark</td><td>言过其实；做过了头</td><td>He overshot the mark by promising results nobody could possibly deliver.<br>他许诺了根本没人做得到的结果，说得太过了。</td></tr>
