<tr><td><b>overstep</b></td><td>overstep the ˈmark/ˈline</td><td>越轨；言行过分</td><td>Joking about her weight really overstepped the mark this time.<br>拿她的体重开玩笑，这次真的过分了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>overtime</b></td><td>be working ˈovertime</td><td>（想象力等）异常活跃；超负荷运转</td><td>Her imagination was working overtime after she heard those strange noises.<br>听到那些怪声后，她的想象力就开始过度活跃了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈovertures</td><td>序曲；主动的表示</td><td>The company's friendly overtures were met with complete silence from the union.<br>公司友好的表示换来了工会的沉默。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈovertures (to sb)</td><td>主动接近某人；向某人示好</td><td>The rebels made overtures to the government about a possible ceasefire.<br>叛军主动向政府示好，商谈停火的可能。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>own</b></td><td>come ˌinto your/its ˈown</td><td>得以充分发挥；有用武之地</td><td>A four-wheel drive really comes into its own on these muddy tracks.<br>在这些泥泞小路上，四驱车才真正派上用场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈown back (on sb) (informal)</td><td>报复；复仇</td><td>She got her own back on him by telling everyone his embarrassing nickname.<br>她把他难堪的绰号说给所有人听，算是报了仇。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(all) on your ˈown</td><td>独自；单独；独立地</td><td>He built that whole shed on his own in a single weekend.<br>那整间小棚子是他一个周末独自搭起来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>oyster</b></td><td>the world is your ˈoyster</td><td>一切皆有可能；天地任你闯</td><td>You're twenty-two with a degree — the world is your oyster.<br>你二十二岁又有学位，天地任你闯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb/sth through their/its ˈpaces</td><td>考验某人的能力；测试某物的性能</td><td>The coach put the new goalkeeper through his paces for two hours.<br>教练把新守门员操练了整整两小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pack</b></td><td>ahead of the ˈpack</td><td>处于领先位置；抢先于对手</td><td>Investing in solar early kept the firm ahead of the pack.<br>早早投资太阳能让这家公司领先同行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pack your ˈbags (informal)</td><td>收拾东西走人；永远离开</td><td>After that row with his boss he packed his bags and quit.<br>和老板大吵一架后，他收拾东西辞职了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pack it ˈin (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>停止做某事；别闹了</td><td>Pack it in, you two — I can't hear the phone over your shouting.<br>你们俩别闹了，你们一嚷我听不见电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌpack of ˈlies (informal)</td><td>一派谎言；谎话连篇</td><td>His story about missing the train was a pack of lies.<br>他说错过火车那套说辞完全是一派谎言。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pack a (hard, etc.) ˈpunch (informal)</td><td>能重拳出击；很有力量</td><td>For such a small speaker, this thing really packs a punch.<br>这么小的音箱，声音出奇地有劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌpack them ˈin ◆ ˌpack the ˈhouse</td><td>吸引大批观众；场场爆满</td><td>That comedian still packs them in at theatres across the country.<br>那位喜剧演员在全国各地剧场依然场场爆满。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>packed</b></td><td>packed (together) like sarˈdines (informal)</td><td>挤得像沙丁鱼罐头；拥挤不堪</td><td>We stood packed like sardines on the last train out of the city.<br>我们挤在末班车上，像沙丁鱼罐头一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>packet</b></td><td>make, lose, spend, etc. a ˈpacket (informal)</td><td>赚（或赔、花）一大笔钱</td><td>He made a packet selling his flat just before prices dropped.<br>他赶在房价跌前卖掉公寓，赚了一大笔。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>page</b></td><td>be on the same ˈpage (especially AmE)</td><td>想法一致；达成共识</td><td>Let's meet Monday to make sure everyone is on the same page.<br>周一碰个头，确保大家想法一致。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>paid</b></td><td>put ˈpaid to sth (informal)</td><td>了结；使…成为泡影</td><td>A broken ankle put paid to his hopes of running the marathon.<br>脚踝骨折让他跑马拉松的希望化为泡影。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>paid-up</b></td><td>a (fully) ˌpaid-up ˈmember, etc.</td><td>已缴费的会员；铁杆成员</td><td>She's a fully paid-up member of the local cycling club now.<br>她现在是本地骑行俱乐部的正式会员了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pain</b></td><td>on/under ˌpain of sth (formal)</td><td>违则受罚；违者以…论处</td><td>Workers were forbidden to discuss the case on pain of dismissal.<br>员工不得讨论此案，违者解雇。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌpain in the ˈneck (BrE also a ˌpain in the ˈarse△/ˈbum/ˈbackside) (AmE also a ˌpain in the ˈass△/ˈbutt) (informal)</td><td>极讨厌的人或事</td><td>Filling in these forms every month is a real pain in the neck.<br>每月填这些表格实在烦人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pains</b></td><td>be at (great) ˈpains to do sth</td><td>煞费苦心地做某事；竭力</td><td>He was at great pains to explain that the delay wasn't his fault.<br>他费尽口舌解释延误不是他的错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for your ˈpains (especially BrE, often ironic)</td><td>作为回报；作为答谢</td><td>I helped him move house all weekend and got a cold coffee for my pains.<br>我帮他搬了整个周末的家，回报是一杯凉咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take (great) ˈpains with sth/to do sth</td><td>煞费苦心；尽心竭力做某事</td><td>She took great pains with the wedding invitations, writing each one by hand.<br>她在婚礼请柬上下足功夫，每张都手写。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to great ˈpains to do sth</td><td>尽心竭力地做某事；小心谨慎地做</td><td>The chef goes to great pains to source every vegetable locally.<br>这位厨师费尽心思，所有蔬菜都从本地采购。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>paint</b></td><td>paint a terrible, depressing, rosy, etc. ˈpicture (of sb/sth)</td><td>把…描绘得很糟糕（或美好）</td><td>The report paints a depressing picture of housing conditions in the city.<br>报告把这座城市的住房状况描绘得十分令人沮丧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>paint the town ˈred (informal)</td><td>尽情狂欢；花天酒地</td><td>After finals we painted the town red and stumbled home at dawn.<br>期末考完我们出去尽情狂欢，天亮才跌跌撞撞回家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>paint sth with a ˌbroad ˈbrush</td><td>粗线条描绘；大致地描述</td><td>The minister painted the reforms with a broad brush and dodged details.<br>部长只是粗线条地讲了改革，回避了细节。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>painting</b></td><td>be like painting the Forth ˈBridge (BrE)</td><td>（工作）没完没了；做完又得重来</td><td>Tidying up after three kids is like painting the Forth Bridge.<br>给三个孩子收拾东西，简直没完没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pair</b></td><td>I've only got one pair of ˈhands (spoken)</td><td>我只有一双手；实在忙不过来</td><td>Wait your turn — I've only got one pair of hands here!<br>等等，我只有一双手，忙不过来！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a pair of ˈhands (informal)</td><td>帮手；人手</td><td>We need an extra pair of hands in the kitchen on Saturday nights.<br>周六晚上厨房需要多一个帮手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pairs</b></td><td>in ˈpairs</td><td>成对地；成双地</td><td>The children walked to the museum in pairs, holding hands tightly.<br>孩子们两人一组紧牵着手走去博物馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pajamas (AmE)</td><td>睡衣裤</td><td>He answered the door in his pajamas at two in the afternoon.<br>下午两点他还穿着睡衣去开门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pale</b></td><td>be beˌyond the ˈpale</td><td>出格；越轨；令人无法容忍</td><td>Shouting at the waiter like that was completely beyond the pale.<br>那样冲服务员吼叫实在太过分了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈpale beside/next to sth ◆ ˈpale in/by comparison (with sth)</td><td>相形见绌；相比之下逊色</td><td>My cooking pales beside my grandmother's, but I keep practising.<br>我的厨艺跟奶奶比相形见绌，但我一直在练。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>palm</b></td><td>have sb in the ˌpalm of your ˈhand</td><td>完全控制某人；把某人攥在手心</td><td>Within ten minutes the speaker had the audience in the palm of her hand.<br>不到十分钟，演讲者就把听众牢牢抓住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pan</b></td><td>go down the ˈpan (BrE, slang)</td><td>付诸东流；被糟蹋掉</td><td>Two years of research went down the pan when the funding stopped.<br>资金一断，两年的研究全打了水漂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌflash in the ˈpan</td><td>昙花一现；一时的成功</td><td>Their first hit turned out to be a flash in the pan.<br>他们的首支热门歌曲结果只是昙花一现。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pandora</b></td><td>Pandora's ˈbox</td><td>潘多拉的盒子；灾祸之源</td><td>Asking about their family history opened a real Pandora's box.<br>一问起他们的家史，等于打开了潘多拉的盒子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>panic</b></td><td>ˈpanic stations (BrE, informal)</td><td>手忙脚乱的状态；乱套</td><td>It was panic stations in the kitchen when forty guests arrived early.<br>四十位客人提早到，厨房里顿时乱成一团。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>press/push the ˈpanic button (BrE)</td><td>惊慌失措；仓促行事</td><td>Don't push the panic button just because sales dipped for one month.<br>只不过一个月销量下滑，别慌了手脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pants</b></td><td>scare, bore, etc. the ˈpants off sb (informal)</td><td>把某人吓坏（或烦死等）</td><td>That horror film scared the pants off my little brother.<br>那部恐怖片把我弟弟吓坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>paper</b></td><td>on ˈpaper</td><td>书面上；理论上</td><td>On paper the plan looks perfect, but nobody has tested it yet.<br>这计划纸面上很完美，可还没人试过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>paper over the ˈcracks</td><td>掩饰问题或分歧；权且遮掩</td><td>The apology just papered over the cracks in their friendship.<br>那句道歉不过是掩盖了他们友情中的裂痕。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌpaper ˈtiger</td><td>纸老虎；外强中干的人或事物</td><td>Their new competitor turned out to be a paper tiger with no real funding.<br>他们的新对手原来是只纸老虎，根本没有资金。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>par</b></td><td>be below/under ˈpar</td><td>低于标准；不如平常</td><td>His performance was below par all season after that knee injury.<br>膝伤之后，他整个赛季状态都不如平常。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be on a ˈpar with sb/sth</td><td>与…不相上下；与…相当</td><td>The local bakery's bread is on a par with anything in Paris.<br>这家本地面包店的面包不输巴黎的任何一家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be (about) ˌpar for the ˈcourse (disapproving)</td><td>意料之中；不足为奇</td><td>Waiting an hour at that clinic is about par for the course.<br>在那家诊所等一小时算是家常便饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be up to/above ˈpar</td><td>达到或超过标准</td><td>Her latest essay is well above par for a first-year student.<br>她这篇论文对大一学生来说远超水准。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>par ˈexcellence (from French)</td><td>杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的</td><td>He is a storyteller par excellence, holding children spellbound for hours.<br>他是个出类拔萃的故事家，能让孩子听上几个钟头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>paragon</b></td><td>a ˌparagon of ˈvirtue</td><td>道德楷模；完美无缺的人</td><td>She's no paragon of virtue, but she'd never steal from a friend.<br>她算不上什么道德楷模，但绝不会偷朋友的东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>parallel</b></td><td>in ˈparallel (with sb/sth)</td><td>与…同时；并行</td><td>The two investigations ran in parallel with each other for six months.<br>这两项调查并行了六个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>parcel</b></td><td>be ˌpart and ˈparcel of sth</td><td>是…的重要组成部分</td><td>Late nights are part and parcel of working in a busy newsroom.<br>熬夜是在繁忙新闻编辑室工作的一部分。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pardon</b></td><td>ˌpardon ˈme (spoken)</td><td>对不起；请再说一遍</td><td>Pardon me, did you say the meeting starts at eight or nine?<br>对不起，你是说会议八点还是九点开始？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌpardon me for ˈdoing sth (informal)</td><td>请原谅我…（表示不满）</td><td>Pardon me for asking, but who exactly invited you here tonight?<br>恕我多问一句，今晚到底是谁请你来的？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>parkinson</b></td><td>ˈParkinson's law (humorous)</td><td>帕金森定律；工作总会拖满时限</td><td>Give them a month and they'll take a month — Parkinson's law again.<br>给他们一个月他们就用满一个月，又是帕金森定律。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>parrot-fashion</b></td><td>(learn, repeat, etc. sth) ˈparrot-fashion (BrE, disapproving)</td><td>鹦鹉学舌般地；机械模仿地</td><td>He learned the poem parrot-fashion without understanding a single line.<br>他鹦鹉学舌般背下那首诗，一句也没懂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>part</b></td><td>be ˌpart and ˈparcel of sth</td><td>是…的基本组成部分；不可分割</td><td>Rejection is part and parcel of being an actor, sadly.<br>遗憾的是，被拒绝是当演员必然要经历的一部分。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the better/best part of sth</td><td>大部分；多半</td><td>We waited the better part of three hours for a table.<br>我们为了等位子等了将近三个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈmy, ˈhis, etc. (own) part</td><td>就我（或他等）而言</td><td>For my part, I'd rather stay home than sit in traffic all day.<br>就我而言，我宁愿待在家也不想堵一天车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈpart</td><td>部分地；在某种程度上</td><td>The delay was caused in part by the storm and in part by staff shortages.<br>延误一部分因风暴，一部分因人手不足。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look/dress the ˈpart</td><td>外表或穿着与身份相称</td><td>In that tailored suit he really looks the part of a lawyer.<br>穿上那套定制西装，他看着还真像个律师。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>part of the ˈfurniture (informal)</td><td>习以为常的人；不为人注意的老面孔</td><td>After thirty years here, old Tom is part of the furniture.<br>在这儿干了三十年，老汤姆早成了固定风景。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play a/your ˈpart (in sth)</td><td>起作用；参与其中</td><td>Bad weather certainly played a part in the team's poor result.<br>恶劣天气无疑对球队的糟糕成绩起了作用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth in good ˈpart (BrE)</td><td>不介意；从容接受（玩笑等）</td><td>They teased him about his haircut, but he took it in good part.<br>大家取笑他的发型，他倒毫不介意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈpart (in sth)</td><td>参加；参与</td><td>Over two hundred runners took part in the charity race yesterday.<br>昨天有两百多名跑者参加了慈善赛跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb's ˈpart (BrE)</td><td>支持某人；站在某人一边</td><td>My sister always takes my mother's part whenever we argue.<br>我们一吵架，我姐姐总是站在我妈那边。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>particular</b></td><td>in parˈticular</td><td>尤其；特别</td><td>I enjoyed the whole trip, but the mountain hike in particular.<br>整趟旅行我都喜欢，尤其是那次登山。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>parting</b></td><td>a/the ˌparting of the ˈways</td><td>分道扬镳；各奔前程之时</td><td>After ten years together, the band reached a parting of the ways.<br>合作十年后，乐队走到了分道扬镳的时刻。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌparting ˈshot (also a ˌParthian ˈshot)</td><td>临别时不友好的话或举动</td><td>As a parting shot, she said the office had never respected her.<br>临走时她撂下一句：这办公室从没尊重过她。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>parts</b></td><td>a ˌman/ˌwoman of (many) ˈparts</td><td>多才多艺的人；多面手</td><td>He farms, teaches piano and writes poetry — a man of many parts.<br>他种地、教钢琴、写诗，是个多面手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>party</b></td><td>be (a) ˈparty to sth (formal)</td><td>参与某事；与…有牵连</td><td>She refused to be a party to any deal involving the company's rivals.<br>她拒绝参与任何牵涉到公司对手的交易。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌparty ˈline</td><td>党的路线；官方立场</td><td>Every spokesman repeated the party line without answering our questions.<br>每位发言人都在重复官方口径，不回答我们的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your ˈparty piece (BrE, informal)</td><td>聚会上的拿手戏；表演节目</td><td>After dinner Uncle Ray did his party piece on the old piano.<br>饭后雷叔叔在旧钢琴上表演了他的拿手节目。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the party's ˈover</td><td>好日子到头了；该干正事了</td><td>Funding has been cut, so I'm afraid the party's over for us.<br>经费被砍了，恐怕我们的好日子到头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pass</b></td><td>come to such a ˈpass ◆ come to a pretty ˈpass</td><td>落到这步田地；陷入困境</td><td>Things have come to a pretty pass when neighbours won't even say hello.<br>连邻居都不打招呼了，真是落到这步田地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let sth ˈpass</td><td>放过不理会；不予计较</td><td>He made a rude remark, but I decided to let it pass.<br>他说了句难听的话，我决定不去计较。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈpass at sb (informal)</td><td>调情；挑逗；勾引</td><td>He made a pass at her during the office party and she left early.<br>他在公司派对上挑逗她，她提早就走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not pass your ˈlips</td><td>不说出口；不入口</td><td>Not a word of complaint passed his lips throughout the long journey.<br>整趟长途旅程他一句抱怨都没说过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pass the ˈbuck (informal)</td><td>推卸责任；把难题推给别人</td><td>Stop passing the buck and admit the mistake was yours.<br>别推卸责任了，承认错在你自己。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈbuck-passing noun</td><td>推诿责任；踢皮球</td><td>The public is tired of all the buck-passing between the two departments.<br>民众受够了两个部门之间互相推诿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pass the ˈhat round/around ◆ pass round/around the ˈhat (informal)</td><td>凑份子；募捐</td><td>We passed the hat round to buy the caretaker a leaving present.<br>我们凑份子给门卫买了份离别礼物。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pass ˈjudgement (on/about sb/sth) (especially BrE) (AmE usually pass ˈjudgment (on/about sb/sth))</td><td>对…妄加评判；作出评判</td><td>Don't pass judgement on her until you know the whole story.<br>在了解全部情况前别对她妄下评判。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sb</b></td><td>pass ˈmuster</td><td>符合要求；勉强合格</td><td>My handwriting barely passes muster, but at least it's readable.<br>我的字勉强过关，好歹还认得出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pass the/your ˈtime (doing sth)</td><td>消磨时间</td><td>We passed the time playing cards while waiting for the delayed flight.<br>等晚点航班时，我们打牌消磨时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pass the time of ˈday (with sb)</td><td>与某人寒暄；打招呼闲聊</td><td>She stopped to pass the time of day with the woman in the flower shop.<br>她停下来和花店的女人寒暄了几句。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pass ˈwater (formal)</td><td>排尿；小便</td><td>The doctor asked whether it hurt when he passed water.<br>医生问他小便时是否疼痛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>passage</b></td><td>a ˌbird of ˈpassage</td><td>过客；漂泊不定的人</td><td>He's a bird of passage who never stays in one city long.<br>他是个过客，从不在一个城市久留。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>passing</b></td><td>in ˈpassing</td><td>顺便地；附带地</td><td>She mentioned in passing that she might move to Berlin.<br>她顺口提了一句可能会搬去柏林。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>past</b></td><td>be/look ˈpast it (BrE, informal)</td><td>年老无用；力不从心</td><td>At forty he was told he was past it for professional football.<br>四十岁时人家就说他踢职业足球太老了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be past your/its ˈbest</td><td>过了鼎盛期；不如从前</td><td>These strawberries are past their best, but they'll do for jam.<br>这些草莓已经不新鲜了，做果酱还行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be past its ˈsell-by date (informal)</td><td>过时了；不再管用</td><td>That management theory is well past its sell-by date now.<br>那套管理理论早就过时了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I wouldn't put it ˈpast sb (to do sth)</td><td>相信某人干得出这种事</td><td>I wouldn't put it past him to read your emails while you're out.<br>我相信他趁你不在偷看你邮件这种事干得出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌpast ˈmaster (in/of/at sth)</td><td>老手；行家；大师</td><td>She's a past master at getting difficult customers to calm down.<br>她是安抚难缠客户的老手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pasting</b></td><td>give sb/get a ˈpasting (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>痛打或痛击；惨败</td><td>Our team got a real pasting in the second half on Saturday.<br>周六下半场我们队被打得很惨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pasture</b></td><td>put sb out to ˈpasture (informal, humorous)</td><td>让某人（因年老）退休</td><td>They put him out to pasture at sixty, though he was still sharp.<br>他六十岁就被劝退了，其实脑子还很灵光。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pastures</b></td><td>ˌpastures ˈnew</td><td>新的工作或生活环境</td><td>After eight years here she's off to pastures new in Canada.<br>在这儿干了八年后，她要去加拿大另谋新天地了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pat</b></td><td>give sb/yourself a ˌpat on the ˈback ◆ pat sb/yourself on the ˈback (for doing sth)</td><td>表扬；夸奖某人或自己</td><td>Give yourself a pat on the back — that presentation went brilliantly.<br>该给自己点个赞，那场演示做得棒极了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/know/get sth off ˈpat (BrE) (AmE have/know sth down ˈpat)</td><td>熟记于心；对答如流</td><td>She had her whole speech off pat before she even reached the hall.<br>还没到会场，她整篇讲稿就已经烂熟于心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stand ˈpat (especially AmE)</td><td>坚持原有决定；固执己见</td><td>The board decided to stand pat and keep the current pricing.<br>董事会决定按兵不动，维持现行定价。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>patch</b></td><td>go through, hit, etc. a ˈbad/ˈsticky patch</td><td>遇到难关；处于困难时期</td><td>Their marriage hit a bad patch after he lost his job.<br>他失业后，他们的婚姻遇到了难关。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be a ˈpatch on sb/sth (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>远不如；相比之下差得多</td><td>This café isn't a patch on the one that used to be here.<br>这家咖啡馆远不如从前那家。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>patience</b></td><td>the patience of a ˈsaint/of ˈJob</td><td>极大的耐心；圣人般的耐性</td><td>Teaching that class needs the patience of a saint.<br>教那个班需要圣人般的耐心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>patter</b></td><td>the patter of tiny ˈfeet (informal or humorous)</td><td>小孩子的脚步声；指要有孩子了</td><td>They're hoping for the patter of tiny feet before next Christmas.<br>他们盼着明年圣诞前家里能添个小宝宝。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pause</b></td><td>give (sb) pause for ˈthought ◆ give (sb) ˈpause (formal)</td><td>使认真思考；使犹豫</td><td>The doctor's warning about his blood pressure gave him pause for thought.<br>医生对他血压的警告让他认真思量起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌpregnant ˈpause/ˈsilence</td><td>意味深长的停顿；耐人寻味的沉默</td><td>There was a pregnant pause before she finally answered his question.<br>她终于回答他的问题前，出现了一段意味深长的沉默。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pave</b></td><td>pave the ˈway (for sb/sth)</td><td>为…铺平道路；作好准备</td><td>Her research paved the way for a much cheaper vaccine.<br>她的研究为一种廉价得多的疫苗铺平了道路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pay</b></td><td>be in the pay of sb/sth ◆ be in sb's/sth's ˈpay</td><td>受雇于（常指秘密地）；被…豢养</td><td>The journalist claimed two officials were in the pay of the company.<br>这名记者称有两名官员受雇于该公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈhell/the ˈdevil to pay (informal)</td><td>大麻烦；严重后果</td><td>There'll be hell to pay if your father finds the car scratched.<br>要是你爸发现车被刮了，可有大麻烦了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hit/strike ˈpay dirt (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>突然发财；意外获得成功</td><td>They struck pay dirt with their third app, which sold millions.<br>他们的第三款应用大卖，一举发了财。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay ˈdividends</td><td>带来好处；产生效益</td><td>Learning Spanish before the trip really paid dividends in every village.<br>出发前学西班牙语，在每个村子都派上了大用场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay for itˈself</td><td>（花费）自行收回；够本</td><td>The solar panels will pay for themselves within about six years.<br>这些太阳能板大约六年就能收回成本。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay ˈlip-service to sth</td><td>口惠而实不至；嘴上说说而已</td><td>The firm pays lip-service to equality but promotes only its old friends.<br>这家公司口头讲平等，提拔的却全是老熟人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay the ˈprice/ˈpenalty (for sth/for doing sth)</td><td>付出代价；自食其果</td><td>He partied all week and paid the price in Friday's exam.<br>他玩了一星期，周五考试自食其果。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay your reˈspects (to sb) (formal)</td><td>向某人致敬；作礼节性拜访</td><td>Hundreds came to pay their respects to the old headmaster.<br>数百人前来向老校长致敬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay through the ˈnose (for sth) (informal)</td><td>付出过高价钱；被敲竹杠</td><td>We paid through the nose for a hotel room with no window.<br>我们花了大价钱订了间没窗户的酒店房。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay ˈtribute to sb/sth</td><td>向…致敬；赞颂</td><td>The mayor paid tribute to the volunteers who cleared the flooded streets.<br>市长向清理水淹街道的志愿者致敬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay sb/sth a ˈvisit ◆ pay a ˈvisit to sb/sth</td><td>拜访；探望</td><td>We should pay Grandma a visit before the weather gets worse.<br>趁天气变坏前，我们该去看看奶奶。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay your/its (own) ˈway</td><td>自食其力；自负盈亏</td><td>He's been paying his own way since he was seventeen.<br>他从十七岁起就自食其力了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>payback</b></td><td>it's ˈpayback time (especially AmE, informal)</td><td>该报复了；该遭报应了</td><td>They humiliated us last season — now it's payback time.<br>上赛季他们让我们难堪，现在该我们讨回来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pays</b></td><td>he who pays the ˌpiper calls the ˈtune (saying)</td><td>谁出钱谁说了算</td><td>Her father funded the shop, so he who pays the piper calls the tune.<br>店是她父亲出的钱，自然是他说了算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it always/never pays to do sth</td><td>做某事总是明智（或不明智）的</td><td>It always pays to read the contract before you sign anything.<br>签字前先读合同，永远是明智之举。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you ˌpays your ˌmoney and you ˌtakes your ˈchoice (saying)</td><td>全凭个人喜好；选哪个都差不多</td><td>Both phones are much the same — you pays your money and you takes your choice.<br>两款手机差不多，全看你自己喜欢哪个。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>peace</b></td><td>be at ˈpeace</td><td>处于和平状态；内心平静；安息</td><td>After the treaty was signed, the region was at peace for a decade.<br>条约签署后，这个地区太平了十年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌhold your ˈpeace/ˈtongue (old-fashioned)</td><td>不作声；保持缄默</td><td>I wanted to argue, but I held my peace for my mother's sake.<br>我本想争辩，但为了我母亲还是没吭声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌkeep the ˈpeace</td><td>维持秩序；息事宁人</td><td>Two officers stood by the gate to keep the peace during the march.<br>游行期间两名警察守在门口维持秩序。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make (your) ˈpeace with sb</td><td>与某人和解；言归于好</td><td>He finally made his peace with his brother after twelve silent years.<br>沉默十二年后，他终于和哥哥和解了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌpeace and ˈquiet</td><td>安宁；清静</td><td>All I want this weekend is a bit of peace and quiet.<br>这个周末我只想要一点清静。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˈpeace dividend</td><td>和平红利（削减军费省下的钱）</td><td>The government promised to spend the peace dividend on schools and hospitals.<br>政府承诺把和平红利用在学校和医院上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌpeace of ˈmind</td><td>内心的安宁；安心</td><td>Buying good insurance gave my parents real peace of mind.<br>买了好保险让我父母真正安了心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈpeace offering</td><td>和解的礼物；谢罪礼</td><td>He arrived with flowers as a peace offering after their silly argument.<br>那场无聊争吵之后，他带着花来赔罪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no ˌpeace/ˌrest for the ˈwicked (humorous)</td><td>忙个不停；不得清闲</td><td>Another shift tonight? No rest for the wicked, I suppose.<br>今晚又要值班？看来是不得清闲了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pearls</b></td><td>ˌpearls of ˈwisdom (usually ironic)</td><td>金玉良言；睿智之语</td><td>Thanks for those pearls of wisdom, but I've already booked the flight.<br>多谢您的金玉良言，不过机票我已经订了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pearly</b></td><td>the ˌPearly ˈGates (humorous)</td><td>天国之门</td><td>He joked that he'd be arguing with St Peter at the Pearly Gates.<br>他打趣说自己会在天国之门跟圣彼得争辩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌpear-ˈshaped</td><td>梨形的；情况变糟的</td><td>The whole evening turned pear-shaped when the power went out.<br>停电之后，整个晚上就全乱套了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈpear-shaped (BrE, informal)</td><td>出岔子；搞砸</td><td>Our camping trip went pear-shaped when the tent leaked in the storm.<br>暴雨中帐篷漏水，我们的露营就搞砸了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>peas</b></td><td>as alike/like as (two) ˈpeas in a pod (informal)</td><td>一模一样；极为相似</td><td>The twins are as like as two peas in a pod, even their laughs.<br>这对双胞胎一模一样，连笑声都像。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pebble</b></td><td>not the ˈonly pebble on the beach (informal, disapproving)</td><td>并非绝无仅有；大有人在</td><td>Remind him he's not the only pebble on the beach around here.<br>提醒他一句，这地方少了他照样转。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌPeeping ˈTom (disapproving)</td><td>偷窥者；窥淫癖者</td><td>Neighbours called the police about a Peeping Tom in the back lane.<br>邻居报警说后巷有个偷窥狂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pecking</b></td><td>a/the ˈpecking order (informal, often humorous)</td><td>等级次序；尊卑排序</td><td>In this newsroom the pecking order is obvious within about five minutes.<br>在这间编辑室，五分钟就能看出谁大谁小。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep</b></td><td>keep your ˈpecker up (BrE, informal)</td><td>振作起来；别灰心</td><td>Keep your pecker up — there'll be other job interviews soon.<br>打起精神来，很快还会有别的面试。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/set/place sb on a ˈpedestal</td><td>把某人捧上神坛；过分崇拜某人</td><td>Don't put your teachers on a pedestal; they make mistakes too.<br>别把老师捧上神坛，他们也会犯错。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>peg</b></td><td>ˌbring/ˌtake sb ˈdown a peg (or two) (informal)</td><td>挫某人的锐气；杀某人威风</td><td>Losing to a junior player took him down a peg or two.<br>输给一名年轻选手挫了挫他的锐气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>off the ˈpeg (BrE) (AmE ˌoff the ˈrack)</td><td>（衣服）成品的；非定做的</td><td>He bought the suit off the peg and had the trousers shortened.<br>他买了套成衣，把裤子改短了些。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a peg to ˈhang sth on ◆ a peg on which to ˈhang sth</td><td>借口；由头；话头</td><td>The anniversary gave reporters a peg to hang the story on.<br>周年纪念给了记者做这篇报道的由头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be a ˌsquare ˈpeg (in a ˌround ˈhole)</td><td>不称职的人；格格不入的人</td><td>In that formal bank he was a square peg in a round hole.<br>在那家刻板的银行里，他显得格格不入。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pen</b></td><td>the ˌpen is ˌmightier than the ˈsword (saying)</td><td>笔杆胜过刀剑；文胜于武</td><td>Her articles toppled the minister, proving the pen is mightier than the sword.<br>她的文章扳倒了部长，证明笔杆胜过刀剑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put pen to ˈpaper (formal)</td><td>动笔；开始写</td><td>He thought about the novel for years before he put pen to paper.<br>这部小说他想了好几年才真正动笔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌpoison ˈpen letter</td><td>匿名恶意信；诽谤信</td><td>The vicar received a poison pen letter accusing him of stealing funds.<br>牧师收到一封匿名信，指控他挪用资金。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pennies</b></td><td>a ˈpennyworth (also ˈpenn'orth)</td><td>一便士的量；极少量</td><td>Let me add my pennyworth before you finalize the plan.<br>在你定案之前，让我也说两句浅见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>penny</b></td><td>ˌin for a ˈpenny, ˌin for a ˈpound (saying)</td><td>一不做二不休；既已开始就干到底</td><td>We've repainted two rooms, so in for a penny, in for a pound.<br>两间屋子都刷了，索性一不做二不休。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌpenny ˈdrops (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>恍然大悟；终于明白</td><td>He stared at the photo, and then suddenly the penny dropped.<br>他盯着照片看，忽然恍然大悟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌpenny for your ˈthoughts (also a ˈpenny for them) (saying)</td><td>你在想什么呢</td><td>You've been quiet all evening — a penny for your thoughts.<br>你一晚上没说话，在想什么呢？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌpenny ˌwise (and) pound ˈfoolish</td><td>小事精明，大事糊涂</td><td>Skipping the survey to save money was penny wise and pound foolish.<br>为省钱不做房屋检测，真是因小失大。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn up like a bad ˈpenny (informal)</td><td>不请自来；老是冒出来</td><td>Every family party, that cousin turns up like a bad penny.<br>每次家庭聚会，那个表亲总是不请自来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtwo/ˌten a ˈpenny (BrE) (AmE a ˌdime a ˈdozen)</td><td>多得不值钱；廉价而常见</td><td>Cafés like this are ten a penny in the city centre.<br>这种咖啡馆在市中心多得是。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>people</b></td><td>of ˈall people/places/things</td><td>偏偏是（某人、某地、某事）</td><td>You took a lift from Mike, of all people, in this weather?<br>这种天气，你偏偏搭了迈克的车？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>people who live in glass houses shouldn't throw ˈstones (saying)</td><td>自身有短，勿责他人；五十步莫笑百步</td><td>You criticize his spelling? People who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.<br>你还笑他拼写？自己也好不到哪儿去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pep</b></td><td>a ˈpep talk (informal)</td><td>鼓舞士气的话；打气的动员</td><td>The captain gave the team a short pep talk before extra time.<br>加时赛前队长给全队打了打气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>peril</b></td><td>(do sth) at your (own) ˈperil</td><td>自担风险地做某事；后果自负</td><td>You ignore the safety instructions at your own peril.<br>你不理会安全须知，后果自负。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>perish</b></td><td>perish the ˈthought! (spoken, often humorous)</td><td>但愿别发生；想都别想</td><td>Me, run a marathon in the desert? Perish the thought, I'd collapse!<br>让我去沙漠跑马拉松？想都别想，我准趴下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>perpetuity</b></td><td>in perpeˈtuity (formal)</td><td>永久地；永远</td><td>The land was given to the village in perpetuity by its former owner.<br>这块地由前主人永久赠予村庄。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>person</b></td><td>about/on your ˈperson (formal or humorous)</td><td>随身携带；身上带着</td><td>He always carries a small notebook about his person.<br>他随身总带着一个小本子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈperson</td><td>亲自；亲身</td><td>You'll have to collect the documents in person and bring your passport.<br>你得亲自来取文件，还要带上护照。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the person of sb (formal)</td><td>以某人为代表；由某人体现</td><td>Help arrived in the person of a passing nurse.<br>一位路过的护士出现，成了及时的援手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>persona</b></td><td>perˌsona non ˈgrata (from Latin)</td><td>不受欢迎的人</td><td>After leaking the memo he became persona non grata in the office.<br>泄露备忘录后，他在办公室成了不受欢迎的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>personally</b></td><td>take sth ˈpersonally</td><td>把泛泛之言当成针对自己而不悦</td><td>It's a general reminder, so please don't take it personally.<br>这只是普遍提醒，请别往心里去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>perspective</b></td><td>get, put, etc. sth in/out of perˈspective</td><td>正确（或不正确）地看待事物</td><td>Losing one client hurts, but let's get it in perspective.<br>丢一个客户是难受，但要放在大局里看。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>persuasion</b></td><td>of a/the... persuasion (formal or humorous)</td><td>属于…类型的；某派别的</td><td>Guests of every political persuasion argued cheerfully round the dinner table.<br>各种政治立场的客人围着餐桌高高兴兴地争论。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pervert</b></td><td>perˌvert the course of ˈjustice (law)</td><td>妨碍司法公正；扰乱司法程序</td><td>He was jailed for trying to pervert the course of justice by hiding evidence.<br>他因藏匿证据妨碍司法公正而入狱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pet</b></td><td>your, his, etc. pet ˈhate (BrE) (AmE your, his, etc. pet ˈpeeve)</td><td>特别厌恶的东西；最烦的事</td><td>People chewing loudly on trains is my pet hate.<br>我最烦的就是有人在火车上大声咀嚼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>petard</b></td><td>be hoist/hoisted by/with your own peˈtard</td><td>作茧自缚；搬起石头砸自己的脚</td><td>He banned phones in meetings and was hoist by his own petard.<br>他禁止开会用手机，结果自己也被这规矩绊住。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pete</b></td><td>for ˌPete's ˈsake (BrE)</td><td>看在老天的份上；拜托（表示不耐烦）</td><td>For Pete's sake, close the window before the rain soaks everything.<br>拜托，趁雨没把东西淋透赶紧关窗。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pew</b></td><td>take a ˈpew (BrE, spoken, humorous)</td><td>请坐</td><td>Come in and take a pew — the kettle's just boiled.<br>进来坐吧，水刚烧开。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>phase</b></td><td>in ˈphase/out of ˈphase (with sth) (BrE)</td><td>协调；不协调；同步或不同步</td><td>The traffic lights are out of phase, so the junction is chaotic.<br>红绿灯不同步，路口一片混乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>phone</b></td><td>be on the ˈtelephone/ˈphone</td><td>在通电话；装有电话</td><td>She's been on the phone to her sister for over an hour.<br>她跟她姐姐通电话已经一个多小时了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>phrase</b></td><td>a ˌturn of ˈphrase</td><td>措辞方式；某种说法</td><td>He has a lovely turn of phrase that makes dull topics interesting.<br>他措辞漂亮，能把枯燥的话题讲得有趣。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˌcoin a ˈphrase</td><td>套用一句老话；恕我杜撰一词</td><td>To coin a phrase, we're all in the same leaky boat here.<br>套句老话，咱们都在同一条漏水的船上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pick</b></td><td>pick and ˈchoose</td><td>挑挑拣拣；精挑细选</td><td>With so few offers, you can't afford to pick and choose.<br>机会这么少，你没资格挑三拣四。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick sb's ˈbrains (informal)</td><td>向某人讨教；请教某人的想法</td><td>Can I pick your brains about which laptop to buy?<br>能向你请教一下买哪款笔记本吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick a ˈfight/ˈquarrel (with sb)</td><td>找茬儿；寻衅吵架</td><td>He'd had too much to drink and started picking a fight with strangers.<br>他喝多了，开始跟陌生人找茬儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick ˈholes (in sth) (informal)</td><td>挑毛病；找漏洞</td><td>She picked holes in my plan without suggesting anything better.<br>她把我的方案挑得一无是处，却拿不出更好的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick a ˈlock</td><td>撬锁；用工具捅开锁</td><td>He locked himself out and had to pay someone to pick the lock.<br>他把自己锁在门外，只好花钱请人撬锁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the pick of the ˈbunch (informal)</td><td>其中最好的；佼佼者</td><td>Of all the applicants, that young engineer was the pick of the bunch.<br>所有应聘者中，那位年轻工程师最出色。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick sb's ˈpocket</td><td>扒窃；掏某人的口袋</td><td>Someone picked his pocket on the crowded metro platform.<br>有人在拥挤的地铁站台上扒了他的口袋。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick up the ˈpieces</td><td>收拾残局；重整旗鼓</td><td>After the fire, the family had to pick up the pieces alone.<br>火灾之后，这家人只能自己收拾残局。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick up ˈspeed</td><td>加速；加快速度</td><td>The train picked up speed once it left the station behind.<br>火车驶离车站后就加快了速度。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick up the ˈtab (for sth) (informal)</td><td>付账；买单</td><td>Her uncle insisted on picking up the tab for the whole meal.<br>她叔叔坚持要为整顿饭买单。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick up the ˈthreads</td><td>中断后重新开始；恢复原状</td><td>After a year abroad she came home and picked up the threads quickly.<br>在国外待了一年后，她回家很快就恢复了原来的生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick your ˈway (across, over, etc. sth)</td><td>择路而行；小心地走</td><td>We picked our way across the rocks to reach the little beach.<br>我们小心地在礁石间择路，走到那片小沙滩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pick a ˈwinner</td><td>选中赢家；挑得很准</td><td>You certainly picked a winner when you hired that new designer.<br>你雇那位新设计师，眼光真准。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take/have your ˈpick (of sth)</td><td>随意挑选</td><td>There are five spare rooms upstairs, so take your pick.<br>楼上有五间空房，随你挑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pickle</b></td><td>in a (real, right, etc.) ˈpickle (informal)</td><td>处于困境；遇上麻烦</td><td>We were in a real pickle when the car broke down miles from town.<br>车在离镇几英里处抛锚，我们真是麻烦大了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>picnic</b></td><td>be no ˈpicnic (informal)</td><td>不轻松；不好办</td><td>Raising three kids on one salary is no picnic.<br>靠一份工资养三个孩子可不轻松。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>picture</b></td><td>be/look a ˈpicture</td><td>美如画；好看悦目</td><td>The garden looks a picture now that the roses are out.<br>玫瑰开了，花园现在美得像画一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be the ˌpicture of ˈhealth, ˈhappiness, etc.</td><td>显得非常健康（或幸福等）</td><td>At eighty my grandfather is still the picture of health.<br>我祖父八十岁了，看上去依然十分硬朗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get the ˈpicture (spoken)</td><td>明白了；了解情况</td><td>She's not answering his calls — I think you get the picture.<br>她不接他电话，我想你明白是怎么回事了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/out of the ˈpicture (informal)</td><td>参与其中；置身局外</td><td>Since the merger, the old management is completely out of the picture.<br>合并之后，原来的管理层彻底出局了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/keep sb in the ˈpicture (informal)</td><td>向某人介绍情况；让某人了解进展</td><td>Email me weekly to keep me in the picture while I'm away.<br>我不在时，每周发邮件让我了解情况。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pie</b></td><td>pie in the ˈsky (informal)</td><td>空中楼阁；不切实际的空想</td><td>A high-speed line to this village is pie in the sky.<br>往这个村子修高铁纯属空中楼阁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>piece</b></td><td>give sb a piece of your ˈmind (informal)</td><td>直言斥责；把某人痛骂一顿</td><td>If he parks across my gate again, I'll give him a piece of my mind.<br>他要再堵我家大门，我非说他一顿不可。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(all) in one ˈpiece (informal)</td><td>安然无恙；完好无损</td><td>The bike is scratched, but at least you got home in one piece.<br>自行车刮花了，好在你人平安到家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(all) of a ˈpiece (with sth) (formal)</td><td>与…一致；与…如出一辙</td><td>His rudeness tonight is all of a piece with his behaviour last year.<br>他今晚的无礼跟他去年的表现如出一辙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>piece by ˈpiece</td><td>一点一点地；逐件地</td><td>He rebuilt the old motorbike piece by piece over two winters.<br>他用两个冬天把那辆旧摩托一件件重装起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a piece of ˈcake (informal) (BrE also a piece of ˈpiss△, slang)</td><td>小菜一碟；轻而易举的事</td><td>Once you've done it twice, the whole process is a piece of cake.<br>做过两次之后，整个流程就是小菜一碟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sistance</b></td><td>your/the ˌpièce de réˈsistance (from French)</td><td>最精彩的作品；压轴之作</td><td>The chocolate tart was the pièce de résistance of the whole meal.<br>巧克力挞是整顿饭的压轴之作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pieces</b></td><td>fall to ˈpieces</td><td>破旧不堪；散架；垮掉</td><td>That armchair is falling to pieces, but Dad refuses to throw it out.<br>那把扶手椅都快散架了，我爸还是不肯扔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go (all) to ˈpieces (informal)</td><td>崩溃；垮掉；沮丧至极</td><td>She went to pieces when she heard the news about her brother.<br>听到她弟弟的消息，她整个人垮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pig</b></td><td>in a pig's ˈeye (AmE, informal)</td><td>才不是呢；绝无可能</td><td>He says he'll pay me back tomorrow — in a pig's eye!<br>他说明天还我钱，鬼才信呢！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈpig of yourself (informal)</td><td>大吃大喝；吃相难看</td><td>I made a pig of myself at the buffet and regretted it later.<br>我在自助餐上吃撑了，后来很后悔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a pig's ˈear (out) of sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>把事情办砸；弄得一团糟</td><td>He made a pig's ear of painting the door and had to start again.<br>他把门刷得一塌糊涂，只好重来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(buy) a pig in a ˈpoke</td><td>隔山买牛；盲目购买</td><td>Buying a car online without seeing it is buying a pig in a poke.<br>网上买车不看实物，等于隔山买牛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a pig of a sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>麻烦事；苦差事</td><td>It's been a pig of a week, with two deadlines and a broken boiler.<br>这周真够呛，两个截稿期还赶上锅炉坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pigeon</b></td><td>be sb's ˈpigeon (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>是某人的分内事；由某人负责</td><td>Timetables aren't my pigeon — ask the office downstairs.<br>排课表不归我管，去楼下办公室问。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pigs</b></td><td>pigs might ˈfly (BrE) (AmE when ˌpigs ˈfly)</td><td>太阳打西边出来；绝无可能</td><td>He'll tidy his room on time? Yes, and pigs might fly.<br>他会按时收拾房间？太阳打西边出来吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pike</b></td><td>come down the ˈpike (AmE, informal)</td><td>出现；发生</td><td>New rules on data privacy are coming down the pike this year.<br>今年会出台新的数据隐私规定。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pile</b></td><td>make a/your ˈpile (informal)</td><td>赚一大笔钱；发财</td><td>He made his pile in shipping and retired at forty-five.<br>他做航运发了财，四十五岁就退休了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pile on the ˈagony/ˈgloom (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>大肆渲染痛苦；添油加醋博同情</td><td>Stop piling on the agony — it was only a scratch.<br>别再夸大其词了，就是擦破点皮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at the ˈbottom/ˈtop of the pile/heap</td><td>处于最底层；处于最上层</td><td>Part-time cleaners are still at the bottom of the pile here.<br>在这里，兼职清洁工仍处在最底层。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pill</b></td><td>be on the ˈpill</td><td>服用口服避孕药</td><td>She's been on the pill since she was at university.<br>她从大学时起就一直在服避孕药。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sugar/sweeten the ˈpill</td><td>使不愉快的事较易接受；给苦药裹糖衣</td><td>They sweetened the pill of relocation with a generous moving allowance.<br>他们用一笔丰厚的搬迁补贴让调职不那么难接受。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pillar</b></td><td>be driven, pushed, etc. from ˌpillar to ˈpost</td><td>被迫四处奔走；到处碰壁</td><td>She was sent from pillar to post before anyone answered her question.<br>她被推来推去，才终于有人回答她的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a pillar of soˈciety, etc.</td><td>社会中坚；栋梁人物</td><td>The old doctor was regarded as a pillar of society in this town.<br>这位老医生被视为镇上的中坚人物。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈpillar of soˈciety/the comˈmunity</td><td>社会栋梁；中流砥柱</td><td>Everyone was shocked when a pillar of the community was arrested for fraud.<br>当社区栋梁因诈骗被捕时，所有人都惊呆了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pillow</b></td><td>ˈpillow talk (informal)</td><td>枕边私房话；枕边悄悄话</td><td>He admitted he had leaked the company secret during pillow talk with his girlfriend.<br>他承认自己在和女友说枕边话时泄露了公司机密。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pin</b></td><td>pin your ˈfaith/ˈhopes on sb/sth</td><td>寄希望于；指望</td><td>She's pinning her hopes on that scholarship, because she can't afford the tuition otherwise.<br>她把希望全押在那笔奖学金上，不然她根本付不起学费。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pinch</b></td><td>at a ˈpinch/ˈpush (BrE) (AmE in a ˈpinch)</td><td>必要时；不得已时</td><td>This sofa sleeps two people comfortably, and three at a pinch.<br>这张沙发睡两个人很舒服，挤一挤三个人也行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pinch ˈpennies (informal)</td><td>省吃俭用；一分钱掰两半花</td><td>We had to pinch pennies for a year to save up for the wedding.<br>为了攒下婚礼的钱，我们省吃俭用了整整一年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈpenny-pinching noun • ˈpenny-pincher noun</td><td>小气；吝啬鬼</td><td>His penny-pinching finally paid off when he bought the flat with cash.<br>他的精打细算终于有了回报，他全款买下了那套公寓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth with a pinch of ˈsalt (informal)</td><td>不完全相信；半信半疑</td><td>Take his stories about meeting film stars with a pinch of salt.<br>他那些见过影星的故事，你听听就好，别当真。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pink</b></td><td>in the ˈpink (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>非常健康；满面红光</td><td>After two weeks by the sea, Grandpa came back in the pink.<br>在海边住了两周，爷爷回来时红光满面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see pink ˈelephants (informal)</td><td>（因醉酒等）看到幻象</td><td>One more whisky and you'll be seeing pink elephants, my friend.<br>朋友，再来一杯威士忌你就要出现幻觉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pins</b></td><td>have ˌpins and ˈneedles</td><td>（手脚）发麻；有针刺感</td><td>I sat cross-legged too long and now I have pins and needles in my left foot.<br>我盘腿坐太久了，现在左脚一阵发麻。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on your ˈpins (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>靠自己的腿站立（或行走）</td><td>At ninety-two she's still steady on her pins and walks to the shops daily.<br>九十二岁了她腿脚还很稳，每天都走着去商店。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pip</b></td><td>pip sb at/to the ˈpost (BrE, informal)</td><td>以微弱优势险胜；最后关头击败</td><td>Our team was pipped at the post by a single goal in the final minute.<br>我们队在最后一分钟被一个进球险胜，功亏一篑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pipe</b></td><td>a ˈpipe dream</td><td>白日梦；幻想</td><td>Owning a house in this city is a pipe dream on my current salary.<br>就我现在的工资，在这座城市买房纯属白日梦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put ˈthat in your pipe and smoke it (informal)</td><td>不管爱不爱听你都得接受</td><td>I got the promotion instead of you, so put that in your pipe and smoke it.<br>升职的是我不是你，你就好好受着吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pipeline</b></td><td>in the ˈpipeline</td><td>在酝酿中；在筹备中</td><td>There are two new albums in the pipeline, but nothing has been announced yet.<br>有两张新专辑正在筹备中，不过还没有正式公布。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pique</b></td><td>pique sb's ˈinterest, curiˈosity, etc. (especially AmE)</td><td>引起某人的兴趣（或好奇）</td><td>The strange title on the cover immediately piqued my curiosity.<br>封面上那个古怪的标题一下子勾起了我的好奇心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>piss</b></td><td>be on the ˈpiss (BrE, △, slang)</td><td>（在酒吧等）狂饮；豪饮</td><td>The whole team was on the piss all weekend after winning the cup.<br>夺冠之后，全队整个周末都在拼命喝酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>piss yourself (laughing) (BrE, △, slang)</td><td>笑得不能自制；笑破肚皮</td><td>We were pissing ourselves laughing at his impression of the boss.<br>他模仿老板的样子，把我们笑得直不起腰。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈpiss (out of sb/sth) (BrE, △, slang)</td><td>取笑；拿…寻开心</td><td>Stop taking the piss out of my accent — I've only been here a month.<br>别拿我的口音开涮了，我才来一个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pissed</b></td><td>(as) pissed as a ˈnewt (BrE, △, slang)</td><td>烂醉如泥；酩酊大醉</td><td>By midnight he was as pissed as a newt and singing on the table.<br>到了午夜他已经烂醉如泥，还站在桌上唱歌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pit</b></td><td>make a ˈpit stop (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>（旅途中）短暂停留；歇脚</td><td>Let's make a pit stop at the next services — I need coffee badly.<br>我们在下个服务区歇一下吧，我特别需要来杯咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the pit of your/the ˈstomach</td><td>心窝；心底</td><td>When I saw the police car outside, I felt sick in the pit of my stomach.<br>看到门外的警车，我心窝里一阵发慌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pit your ˈwits (against sb/sth)</td><td>（与…）斗智</td><td>Every Sunday he pits his wits against the newspaper's hardest crossword.<br>每个周日他都要和报纸上最难的填字游戏斗一斗智。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈbottomless pit (of sth)</td><td>无底洞；无穷无尽的东西</td><td>That old house has become a bottomless pit for our savings.<br>那栋老房子成了吞掉我们积蓄的无底洞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pitch</b></td><td>make a ˈpitch for sb/sth • make a ˈpitch to do sth</td><td>极力争取；竭力游说</td><td>Three agencies will make a pitch for the contract on Friday morning.<br>周五上午会有三家公司来竞标这份合同。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pitch a ˈline/ˈstory/ˈyarn (to sb) (informal)</td><td>（向某人）编瞎话；找借口</td><td>He pitched me some line about his car breaking down again.<br>他又跟我编了套车子抛锚的说辞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pitched</b></td><td>a ˌpitched ˈbattle</td><td>激战；大规模冲突</td><td>The protest turned into a pitched battle between demonstrators and riot police.<br>抗议演变成示威者与防暴警察之间的一场激战。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pits</b></td><td>be the ˈpits (informal)</td><td>糟透了；差到极点</td><td>The food was fine but the service was absolutely the pits.<br>东西还行，可服务简直糟透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pity</b></td><td>ˌmore's the ˈpity (BrE, informal)</td><td>很遗憾；不幸的是</td><td>She won't be joining us tonight, more's the pity.<br>她今晚不能和我们一起了，真是遗憾。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>place</b></td><td>all ˈover the place (informal)</td><td>到处都是；乱七八糟</td><td>His notes were all over the place, so nobody could follow the argument.<br>他的笔记乱七八糟，谁也看不懂他的论证。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) be sb's ˈplace to do sth</td><td>（不）是某人分内的事</td><td>It's not my place to tell your parents what you did last night.<br>你昨晚干了什么，轮不到我去告诉你父母。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fall, drop, etc. into ˈplace</td><td>（因新信息而）变得清楚明朗</td><td>Once she mentioned the missing key, everything fell into place.<br>她一提到那把不见的钥匙，一切就都说得通了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give ˈplace to sb/sth (formal)</td><td>让位于；被…取代</td><td>The old market gave place to a shopping centre in the nineties.<br>九十年代，老市场让位给了一座购物中心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if ˌI was/were in ˈyour place</td><td>如果我是你；换了我的话</td><td>If I were in your place, I'd take the job and move to Berlin.<br>如果我是你，我会接下这份工作，搬去柏林。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈmy, ˈyour, etc. place</td><td>处在我（或你等）的境况</td><td>In her place, I doubt anyone would have stayed so calm.<br>换作她那种处境，我想没几个人能这么冷静。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈplace</td><td>准备就绪；安排妥当</td><td>All the safety measures are in place, so we can start tomorrow.<br>各项安全措施都已就位，我们明天就能开工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in place of sb/sth • in sb's/sth's ˈplace</td><td>代替；顶替</td><td>Use honey in place of sugar if you want a milder taste.<br>想要味道柔和些的话，可以用蜂蜜代替糖。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of ˈplace</td><td>位置不当；不合时宜；格格不入</td><td>In my old jeans I felt completely out of place at the gala dinner.<br>穿着旧牛仔裤，我在那场晚宴上觉得格格不入。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a place in the ˈsun</td><td>有发展前途的地位；出头之日</td><td>After years of small roles, she finally found her place in the sun.<br>演了多年小角色后，她终于熬出了头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb in their ˈplace</td><td>灭某人威风；让某人识相</td><td>One cool sentence from the chairman put the young manager in his place.<br>董事长一句冷冷的话就让那位年轻经理老实了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈplace</td><td>发生；举行</td><td>The wedding will take place in a small church outside town.<br>婚礼将在城外一座小教堂举行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb's ˈplace • take the place of sb</td><td>代替；接替</td><td>No one can really take the place of a friend you grew up with.<br>一起长大的朋友，谁也真的替代不了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take your ˈplace</td><td>就位；入座</td><td>Please take your places, everyone — the performance starts in two minutes.<br>请各位就座，演出两分钟后开始。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>placed</b></td><td>be well, ideally, better, etc. ˈplaced (for sth/to do sth)</td><td>处于有利地位；有良好条件</td><td>With her contacts, she's ideally placed to launch the new campaign.<br>凭她的人脉，她最适合来发起这场新活动。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>places</b></td><td>change/swap ˈplaces (with sb)</td><td>交换位置；互换处境</td><td>I wouldn't change places with him for all the money in the world.<br>给我全世界的钱，我也不愿和他换个位置。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈgo places (informal)</td><td>飞黄腾达；前途无量</td><td>That girl really knows how to sell — she's going to go places.<br>那姑娘太会卖东西了，将来肯定有出息。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>plain</b></td><td>be (all) plain ˈsailing (AmE also be clear ˈsailing)</td><td>一帆风顺；非常顺利</td><td>Once we got the permit, the rest of the project was plain sailing.<br>拿到许可证之后，项目剩下的部分就一帆风顺了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in plain ˈEnglish</td><td>用简单易懂的话说</td><td>Could you explain the contract in plain English for once?<br>你能不能就这一次用大白话解释一下这份合同？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) plain as a ˈpikestaff • (as) plain as ˈday</td><td>一清二楚；显而易见</td><td>It was as plain as day that he had never read the report.<br>他压根没读过那份报告，这一点显而易见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) plain as the nose on your ˈface (informal)</td><td>一目了然；显而易见</td><td>The mistake was as plain as the nose on your face, yet nobody spotted it.<br>这个错误明摆着的，却没有一个人发现。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a plain ˈJane (disapproving)</td><td>相貌平平的女子</td><td>In the film she plays a plain Jane who turns out to be a genius hacker.<br>片中她演一个其貌不扬、却是天才黑客的姑娘。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>planet</b></td><td>be on another ˈplanet • what ˈplanet is sb on?</td><td>异想天开；不知在想什么</td><td>If he thinks we can finish this by Friday, what planet is he on?<br>他要是觉得我们周五就能做完，那他脑子里想的是什么呀？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>plant</b></td><td>plant/sow the ˈseeds of sth</td><td>埋下…的种子；播下…的祸根</td><td>That summer trip planted the seeds of her lifelong love of the sea.<br>那年夏天的旅行埋下了她一生爱海的种子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>plate</b></td><td>have enough, a lot, etc. on your ˈplate</td><td>手头事情一大堆；忙得不可开交</td><td>Don't ask her for favours — she's got enough on her plate already.<br>别再麻烦她了，她手头的事已经够多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>play</b></td><td>bring/call/put sth into ˈplay</td><td>使起作用；使发挥作用</td><td>The new rules bring several safety checks into play before every flight.<br>新规定让每次飞行前都要启动好几项安全检查。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come into ˈplay</td><td>开始起作用；开始有影响</td><td>Luck comes into play far more often than most investors like to admit.<br>运气起作用的时候，比多数投资者愿意承认的多得多。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have money, time, etc. to ˈplay with (informal)</td><td>有充裕的钱（或时间等）可用</td><td>We've got two hours to play with before the train leaves.<br>火车开车前我们还有两个小时可以随便安排。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/out of ˈplay</td><td>（球）在界内；在界外</td><td>The referee shouted that the ball was still in play, so nobody stopped.<br>裁判喊球还在界内，所以没人停下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make great, much, etc. ˈplay of/with sth</td><td>大肆渲染；着重强调</td><td>The minister made great play of the falling unemployment figures.<br>部长对失业率下降的数字大做文章。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈplay for sb/sth (especially AmE)</td><td>极力谋取；追求某人</td><td>He's clearly making a play for her job while she's on leave.<br>她休假期间，他明显在想方设法谋她的职位。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>playing</b></td><td>what's sb ˈplaying at?</td><td>在搞什么名堂（表示气愤）</td><td>What on earth is he playing at, parking right across our driveway?<br>他到底在搞什么鬼，车正好停在我们车道口？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>please</b></td><td>if you ˈplease</td><td>请；劳驾</td><td>Two coffees and a glass of water, if you please.<br>劳驾，两杯咖啡和一杯水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>please the ˈeye</td><td>悦目；养眼</td><td>The garden was designed to please the eye in every single season.<br>这座花园的设计让人一年四季看着都赏心悦目。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌplease ˈGod</td><td>但愿；上帝保佑</td><td>Please God, the rain will stop before the wedding starts tomorrow.<br>但愿明天婚礼开始前雨能停。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌplease yourˈself (spoken)</td><td>随你的便；悉听尊便</td><td>You don't want to come? Fine, please yourself.<br>你不想来？行啊，随你的便。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌplease yourˈself • ˌdo as you ˈplease</td><td>随心所欲；想怎样就怎样</td><td>Once the kids move out, you can finally do as you please on Sundays.<br>等孩子们搬出去，你周日总算可以想怎么过就怎么过了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pleased</b></td><td>I'm (very) pleased to ˈmeet you (formal)</td><td>很高兴认识您</td><td>I'm very pleased to meet you — I've heard so much about your research.<br>很高兴认识您，久闻您的研究大名。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>none too ˈpleased</td><td>很不高兴；相当气愤</td><td>Dad was none too pleased when he saw the scratch on his new car.<br>爸爸看到新车上的划痕，非常不高兴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>only too ˈpleased (to do sth)</td><td>十分乐意（做某事）</td><td>I'd be only too pleased to look after the cat while you're away.<br>你不在的时候，我非常乐意帮你照看猫。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) pleased as ˈPunch (BrE)</td><td>非常高兴；称心如意</td><td>Grandma was as pleased as Punch when we all turned up for her birthday.<br>我们全都来给奶奶过生日，她高兴得合不拢嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pleased with yourself (often disapproving)</td><td>自鸣得意；沾沾自喜</td><td>He looked very pleased with himself after beating me at chess.<br>下棋赢了我之后，他一脸得意。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pleasure</b></td><td>at your/sb's ˈpleasure (formal)</td><td>按某人的意愿；随某人高兴</td><td>The room is available at your pleasure for as long as you need it.<br>这间房随您的意愿使用，需要多久都行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have had the ˈpleasure (formal)</td><td>有幸认识（已被引见）</td><td>I don't believe I've had the pleasure — I'm Daniel, her brother.<br>我想我们还没被介绍过吧，我是丹尼尔，她哥哥。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's a ˈpleasure</td><td>别客气；不用谢</td><td>Thanks for driving me to the airport. It's a pleasure, really.<br>谢谢你送我去机场。别客气，真的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with ˈpleasure (formal)</td><td>很愿意；乐意之至</td><td>Could you say a few words at the ceremony? With pleasure.<br>典礼上您能讲几句吗？我很乐意。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pledge</b></td><td>sign/take the ˈpledge (old-fashioned)</td><td>发誓戒酒</td><td>After that awful night, he took the pledge and hasn't touched a drop since.<br>那个糟糕的晚上之后，他发誓戒酒，从此滴酒未沾。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>plot</b></td><td>lose the ˈplot (BrE, informal)</td><td>乱了方寸；不知所云</td><td>Halfway through the meeting the chairman completely lost the plot.<br>会开到一半，主席就完全乱了套。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the plot ˈthickens (often humorous)</td><td>情节（或情况）变得复杂起来</td><td>So her ex-husband was there too? The plot thickens.<br>这么说她前夫也在场？情况越来越复杂了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put your hand to the ˈplough (old-fashioned)</td><td>着手做事；开始动手干</td><td>Once you put your hand to the plough, there's no turning back.<br>一旦动手干起来，就没有回头路了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌplough a lonely, your own, etc. ˈfurrow</td><td>独自干；自行其是</td><td>She's ploughed her own furrow for years, ignoring every trend in fashion.<br>多年来她一直我行我素，对时尚潮流毫不理会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beat/turn ˈswords into ˈploughshares (BrE) (AmE plowshares)</td><td>化干戈为玉帛；变武器为农具</td><td>After the treaty, both sides promised to beat swords into ploughshares.<br>条约签订后，双方都承诺化干戈为玉帛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pluck</b></td><td>pluck sth out of the ˈair</td><td>随口说出；不加思索地说</td><td>He plucked a number out of the air and hoped nobody would check it.<br>他随口报了个数字，指望没人去核对。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>plumb</b></td><td>plumb the ˈdepths of sth</td><td>陷入…的深渊；到了…的极点</td><td>That documentary plumbs the depths of human cruelty during the war.<br>那部纪录片揭示了战争中人性残忍的极致。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>plunge</b></td><td>take the ˈplunge (informal)</td><td>果断行动；下决心冒险一试</td><td>After months of hesitating, they finally took the plunge and opened a bakery.<br>犹豫了几个月后，他们终于下定决心开了家面包店。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>plus</b></td><td>plus or ˈminus</td><td>上下；正负；大约</td><td>The trip takes about six hours, plus or minus thirty minutes.<br>这趟路程大约六小时，上下差个半小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>plus ça ˈchange (, plus c'est la même ˈchose) (from French, saying)</td><td>万变不离其宗；换汤不换药</td><td>New boss, same old rules — plus ça change, as my father used to say.<br>新老板，还是那套老规矩，正如我父亲常说的，万变不离其宗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the more it ˈchanges, the more it stays the ˈsame</td><td>变来变去还是老样子</td><td>They renamed every department, but the more it changes, the more it stays the same.<br>他们把每个部门都改了名，可越变越是老样子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ply</b></td><td>ply for ˈhire/ˈtrade/ˈbusiness (BrE)</td><td>招揽生意；候客</td><td>Dozens of taxis ply for hire outside the station until well past midnight.<br>几十辆出租车在车站外候客，一直到后半夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ply your ˈtrade (written)</td><td>从事本行；做自己的营生</td><td>For thirty years he has plied his trade as a shoemaker on this corner.<br>三十年来他一直在这个街角做鞋匠营生。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>poacher</b></td><td>poacher turned ˈgamekeeper (BrE)</td><td>由偷猎者变成护猎人；角色反转的人</td><td>As a former hacker now advising banks, he's a classic poacher turned gamekeeper.<br>他从前是黑客，如今给银行当顾问，典型的角色反转。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pocket</b></td><td>be ˌin/ˌout of ˈpocket (especially BrE)</td><td>赚了钱；赔了钱</td><td>After the repairs, I'm about three hundred pounds out of pocket.<br>修完之后，我大概倒贴了三百英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in sb's ˈpocket (informal)</td><td>受某人控制；被某人操纵</td><td>Everyone knew the inspector was in the developer's pocket.<br>谁都知道那个督察早被开发商收买了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of your own ˈpocket</td><td>自掏腰包；用自己的钱</td><td>She paid for the students' tickets out of her own pocket.<br>她自掏腰包给学生们买了票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pockets</b></td><td>be/live in each other's ˈpockets (BrE)</td><td>形影不离；过从甚密</td><td>Those two have lived in each other's pockets since primary school.<br>那两个人从小学起就形影不离。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>poetic</b></td><td>poetic ˈjustice</td><td>报应；善有善报，恶有恶报</td><td>It was poetic justice that the thief's own car got stolen that night.<br>那晚小偷自己的车被偷了，真是报应。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>point</b></td><td>ask, tell, etc. sb point ˈblank</td><td>直截了当地问（或说）</td><td>I asked him point blank whether he had taken the money.<br>我直截了当地问他是不是拿了那笔钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be on the ˈpoint of doing sth</td><td>正要做某事；即将</td><td>I was on the point of leaving when she finally called back.<br>我正要出门，她终于回了电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beside the ˈpoint</td><td>离题；不相干</td><td>Whether you like him is beside the point; he's the best candidate.<br>你喜不喜欢他不是重点，他是最合适的人选。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come/get (straight) to the ˈpoint</td><td>开门见山；直入正题</td><td>Let me get straight to the point: we can't afford another delay.<br>我就直说了，我们再拖不起了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get the ˈpoint (of sth)</td><td>理解要点；明白意思</td><td>I still don't get the point of these endless weekly reports.<br>我到现在也不明白这些没完没了的周报有什么意义。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈpoint (there)</td><td>说得有道理</td><td>You have a point there — we really should test it before launching.<br>你说得有道理，我们上线前确实该测一测。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if/when it ˌcomes to the ˈpoint</td><td>到了必须作决定的时候</td><td>He talks tough, but when it comes to the point he always backs down.<br>他嘴上很硬，可真到了紧要关头总是退缩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in point of ˈfact</td><td>实际上；事实上</td><td>In point of fact, she had already resigned two weeks before the scandal.<br>事实上，在丑闻爆发前两周她就已经辞职了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make your ˈpoint</td><td>阐明自己的观点</td><td>You've made your point, so let's move on to the next item.<br>你的意思已经说清楚了，我们继续下一项吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈpoint of doing sth</td><td>特意做某事；务必做到</td><td>She makes a point of calling her mother every Sunday evening.<br>她每周日晚上都特意给母亲打电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>more to the ˈpoint</td><td>更重要的是；更中肯的是</td><td>It's expensive and, more to the point, it doesn't even work properly.<br>它很贵，更要命的是，它根本用不好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>point a/the ˈfinger (at sb)</td><td>指责；指控</td><td>Before you point a finger at me, check who left the door unlocked.<br>在你指责我之前，先查查是谁没锁门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>point of ˈcontact</td><td>联络人；联系点</td><td>Sarah will be your main point of contact while the project runs.<br>项目期间莎拉是你的主要联络人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a point of deˈparture</td><td>出发点；（讨论的）起点</td><td>Her essay uses that old photograph as its point of departure.<br>她的文章以那张老照片作为出发点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌpoint of ˈhonour (BrE) (AmE a ˌpoint of ˈhonor)</td><td>事关名节的事；关乎荣誉之举</td><td>It was a point of honour for him to pay back every penny he owed.<br>把欠的每一分钱都还清，对他来说是事关名节的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(get to, reach, etc.) the ˌpoint of ˌno reˈturn</td><td>（到了）无法回头的地步</td><td>Once we sign this lease, we've reached the point of no return.<br>一旦签下这份租约，我们就没有退路了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌpoint of ˈview</td><td>观点；看法</td><td>From a parent's point of view, the new timetable is a nightmare.<br>从家长的角度看，新的时间表简直是噩梦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>point the ˈway (to/towards sth)</td><td>指明方向；预示发展趋势</td><td>This small trial may point the way towards a cheaper treatment.<br>这项小规模试验可能为更便宜的疗法指明方向。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb's ˈpoint</td><td>理解并接受某人的观点</td><td>I take your point about the cost, but safety has to come first.<br>你说的成本问题我接受，但安全必须放在第一位。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the ˈpoint</td><td>中肯；切题</td><td>Her answers were short, honest and very much to the point.<br>她的回答简短、坦诚，而且非常切中要害。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the ˈpoint of sth/of doing sth</td><td>达到…的程度；近乎</td><td>He was blunt to the point of rudeness during the whole interview.<br>整场面试他都直白得近乎无礼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up to a (certain) ˈpoint</td><td>在某种程度上</td><td>I agree with you up to a point, but the data tells a different story.<br>我在一定程度上同意你，但数据说的是另一回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>points</b></td><td>have your ˈgood, ˈplus, etc. points</td><td>有其长处；也有优点</td><td>The old flat was cold, but it had its good points, like the huge windows.<br>那套老公寓很冷，但也有好处，比如窗户特别大。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>poison</b></td><td>a ˌpoison ˈpen letter</td><td>恶意匿名信；匿名诽谤信</td><td>She received a poison pen letter accusing her husband of stealing.<br>她收到一封匿名信，指控她丈夫偷东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's your ˈpoison? (spoken, humorous)</td><td>你想喝点什么（酒）</td><td>Come in and sit down — right, what's your poison tonight?<br>进来坐吧，说说，今晚想喝点什么？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>poisoned</b></td><td>a poisoned ˈchalice (especially BrE)</td><td>金杯毒酒；看似诱人实则棘手的事</td><td>That promotion turned out to be a poisoned chalice for the young manager.<br>那次升职对这位年轻经理来说成了金杯毒酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>poke</b></td><td>have a ˌpoke aˈround (informal)</td><td>四处翻找；到处打探</td><td>I had a poke around in the attic and found Dad's old records.<br>我在阁楼里翻了翻，找到了爸爸的旧唱片。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a ˈpoke at sb/sth (old-fashioned, AmE, informal)</td><td>嘲弄；奚落</td><td>The comedian took a poke at politicians on both sides of the aisle.<br>那位喜剧演员把两党的政客都调侃了一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pole</b></td><td>be up the ˈpole (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>疯疯癫癫；发狂</td><td>If you think I'll work three weekends in a row, you're up the pole.<br>你要是以为我会连上三个周末的班，那你是疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>political</b></td><td>a poˌlitical ˈfootball</td><td>被政客当作争斗工具的问题</td><td>School funding has become a political football again this election year.<br>在今年的选举年，学校拨款又成了政治斗争的筹码。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pomp</b></td><td>pomp and ˈcircumstance</td><td>盛大隆重的仪式</td><td>The coronation was staged with all the pomp and circumstance you'd expect.<br>加冕典礼办得极尽隆重，正如人们预料的那样。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pond</b></td><td>across the ˈpond (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>在大西洋彼岸</td><td>My cousin has been living across the pond in Chicago for a decade.<br>我表哥在大西洋彼岸的芝加哥住了十年。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>poor</b></td><td>be a/the ˌpoor man's ˈsb/ˈsth</td><td>…的廉价替代品；逊色的仿版</td><td>Critics called the film a poor man's Godfather with worse dialogue.<br>影评人说这部片子是廉价版《教父》，台词还更差。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) poor as a church ˈmouse</td><td>一贫如洗；穷得叮当响</td><td>When they married they were as poor as church mice, sharing one small room.<br>他们结婚时一贫如洗，挤在一间小屋里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a poor reˈlation</td><td>受冷落的一方；无足轻重的角色</td><td>In this company, marketing has always been the poor relation of sales.<br>在这家公司，市场部一直是销售部的陪衬。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pop</b></td><td>pop your ˈclogs (BrE, humorous)</td><td>翘辫子；一命呜呼</td><td>He joked that he'd leave the cottage to me when he popped his clogs.<br>他开玩笑说等他翘辫子了就把那间小屋留给我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pop the ˈquestion (informal)</td><td>开口求婚</td><td>He finally popped the question on the beach at sunset.<br>他终于在日落时的海滩上开口求婚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>popular</b></td><td>by popular deˈmand</td><td>应大众要求</td><td>By popular demand, the exhibition will stay open another two weeks.<br>应观众要求，展览将再延长两周。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>porridge</b></td><td>do ˈporridge (BrE, old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>坐牢；蹲监狱</td><td>He did porridge for two years before turning his life around.<br>他坐了两年牢，之后彻底改变了自己的人生。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>port</b></td><td>any port in a ˈstorm (saying)</td><td>慌不择路；饥不择食</td><td>The hostel was filthy, but any port in a storm at two in the morning.<br>那家旅舍很脏，可凌晨两点了，也只能将就。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌport of ˈcall (informal)</td><td>中途停留处；落脚点</td><td>Our first port of call in Rome was a tiny café near the station.<br>我们到罗马的第一站是车站附近的一家小咖啡馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>possessed</b></td><td>like a man/woman posˈsessed</td><td>着了魔似地；拼命地</td><td>She cleaned the whole house like a woman possessed before her in-laws arrived.<br>公婆来之前，她像着了魔一样把整间屋子打扫了一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like one posˈsessed</td><td>着了魔似地；发狂似地</td><td>He wrote like one possessed and finished the novel in six weeks.<br>他像着了魔一样写作，六周就写完了这部小说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what(ever) posˈsessed sb to do sth?</td><td>究竟为什么会那样做；鬼迷心窍</td><td>Whatever possessed you to tell the boss what we said at lunch?<br>你究竟是鬼迷心窍了，把午饭时说的话告诉老板？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>possession</b></td><td>possession is nine points of the ˈlaw (saying)</td><td>现实占有，败一胜九</td><td>He won't return the trailer, and possession is nine points of the law.<br>他不肯还那辆拖车，而现实占有者往往占上风。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>possession is nine tenths/parts of the ˈlaw (saying)</td><td>占有者在争讼中占上风</td><td>She's living in the house already, and possession is nine tenths of the law.<br>她已经住进那房子了，占着的人总是占便宜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take posˈsession (of sth) (formal)</td><td>占有；取得…的所有权</td><td>He couldn't pay the tax, so the state took possession of his land.<br>他交不起税，于是政府没收了他的土地。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>possible</b></td><td>as quickly, much, soon, etc. as ˈpossible</td><td>尽可能快（或多、早等）</td><td>Send me the figures as soon as possible — the meeting is at nine.<br>尽快把数字发给我，会议九点开始。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>possum</b></td><td>play ˈpossum (informal)</td><td>装睡；装糊涂</td><td>The kids played possum when their mother came to check on them.<br>妈妈来查看时，孩子们全都装睡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>postal</b></td><td>go ˈpostal (AmE, informal)</td><td>大发雷霆；暴跳如雷</td><td>Dad will go postal if he sees what you did to the garage door.<br>爸爸要是看到你把车库门弄成这样，肯定暴跳如雷。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>posted</b></td><td>keep sb ˈposted (on/of/about sth) (informal)</td><td>随时向某人通报情况</td><td>Keep me posted on how your mother's operation goes.<br>你母亲手术的情况随时告诉我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>poster</b></td><td>poster child/boy/girl (AmE)</td><td>典型代表；标志性人物</td><td>That startup became the poster child for reckless spending.<br>那家创业公司成了乱花钱的典型。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>post-haste</b></td><td>post-ˈhaste (literary)</td><td>火速；急速</td><td>The messenger rode post-haste to the castle with the king's orders.<br>信使带着国王的命令火速赶往城堡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pot</b></td><td>go (all) to ˈpot (informal)</td><td>荒废；衰败；垮掉</td><td>The garden has gone to pot since Grandpa stopped looking after it.<br>自从爷爷不再打理，这园子就荒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌpot calling the kettle ˈblack (saying, informal)</td><td>五十步笑百步；锅笑壶黑</td><td>You calling me lazy is the pot calling the kettle black.<br>你说我懒，真是五十步笑百步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˌpot ˈluck (informal)</td><td>碰运气；有什么吃什么</td><td>We didn't book anywhere, so we'll just take pot luck tonight.<br>我们没订地方，今晚就碰碰运气吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈmelting pot (BrE)</td><td>在变动之中；前途未定</td><td>The whole schedule is in the melting pot until the funding is confirmed.<br>在资金落实之前，整个日程都还没定下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>potshot</b></td><td>take a ˈpotshot/ˈpotshots (at sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>冷不防射击；随意抨击</td><td>Journalists took potshots at the mayor throughout the entire press conference.<br>整场记者会上，记者们不断向市长发难。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pound</b></td><td>(have, demand, claim, etc.) your pound of ˈflesh</td><td>（不顾情面）索取全部欠款</td><td>The landlord wanted his pound of flesh, right down to the last day's rent.<br>房东连最后一天的租金都要算清，一分不让。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your pound of ˈflesh</td><td>死要讨回的欠债；应得却苛刻的索取</td><td>They lent us the money, but they'll want their pound of flesh eventually.<br>他们借了钱给我们，但迟早会连本带利讨回去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>demand your pound of ˈflesh</td><td>不顾情面地索取应得之物</td><td>I didn't know work here was this hard — they really demand their pound of flesh.<br>我不知道在这里工作这么辛苦，他们简直不顾别人死活。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>practice</b></td><td>in ˈpractice</td><td>实际上；事实上</td><td>In theory it's a great idea, but in practice nobody has the time.<br>理论上这主意很好，可实际上谁都没那个时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/ˌout of ˈpractice</td><td>勤于练习；久疏练习</td><td>I'm badly out of practice — I haven't touched the piano in years.<br>我手生得厉害，好几年没碰钢琴了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>practice makes ˈperfect (saying)</td><td>熟能生巧</td><td>Your serve is getting better already; practice makes perfect.<br>你的发球已经有进步了，熟能生巧嘛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sth into ˈpractice</td><td>付诸实践；付诸实施</td><td>It's time to put all that theory into practice on a real project.<br>该把那些理论放到真实项目里去实践了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈhabit/ˈpractice of sth</td><td>养成…的习惯；经常做某事</td><td>Don't make a habit of borrowing money from your colleagues.<br>别养成向同事借钱的习惯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌpractise what you ˈpreach (saying)</td><td>身体力行；言行一致</td><td>If you want the team to arrive early, practise what you preach.<br>想让团队早到，你自己得先做到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>praise</b></td><td>praise sb/sth to the ˈskies</td><td>把…捧上天；极力赞扬</td><td>The critics praised her first novel to the skies.<br>评论家把她的第一部小说捧上了天。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prayer</b></td><td>not have a ˈprayer (of doing sth)</td><td>毫无希望；根本不可能</td><td>Without a lawyer, he doesn't have a prayer of winning this case.<br>没有律师，他打赢这场官司毫无希望。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prayers</b></td><td>the answer to sb's ˈprayers</td><td>正是某人求之不得的东西</td><td>A cheap flat near the office was the answer to my prayers.<br>办公室附近有间便宜公寓，正是我求之不得的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>preach to the conˈverted (AmE also preach to the ˈchoir)</td><td>对已信服的人说教；多此一举</td><td>Telling me to recycle is preaching to the converted — I've done it for years.<br>跟我说要回收利用纯属多余，我做了好多年了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>precious</b></td><td>precious ˈfew/little (informal)</td><td>极少；少得可怜</td><td>There's precious little food left in the fridge before payday.<br>发工资前，冰箱里剩下的吃的少得可怜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>precise</b></td><td>to be (more) preˈcise (also more preˈcisely)</td><td>确切地说；更准确地说</td><td>It happened last week — on Thursday evening, to be more precise.<br>这事发生在上周，更确切地说，是周四晚上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>preference</b></td><td>give (a) ˈpreference to sb/sth</td><td>给予优先；优待</td><td>The school gives preference to children living within a mile.<br>这所学校优先录取一英里内居住的孩子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈpreference to sb/sth</td><td>宁愿…而不是</td><td>She chose the small college in preference to a famous university.<br>她宁愿选那所小学院，也不去名牌大学。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pregnant</b></td><td>a pregnant ˈpause/ˈsilence</td><td>意味深长的停顿（或沉默）</td><td>After his question there was a pregnant pause that made everyone uneasy.<br>他问完之后是一阵意味深长的沉默，弄得大家都不自在。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prejudice</b></td><td>without ˈprejudice (to sth) (law)</td><td>不损害（其他权益）</td><td>The offer is made without prejudice to any future claim.<br>此项提议不影响今后提出任何索赔。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>premium</b></td><td>at a ˈpremium</td><td>奇缺；难得；珍贵</td><td>Parking spaces are at a premium in this part of town.<br>在城里这一带，停车位一位难求。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/place a ˈpremium on sth</td><td>高度重视；珍视</td><td>This company puts a premium on honesty rather than clever sales talk.<br>这家公司看重的是诚实，而不是花哨的推销话术。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prepare</b></td><td>prepare the ˈground (for sth)</td><td>为…铺路；打下基础</td><td>Her early research prepared the ground for today's vaccines.<br>她早期的研究为如今的疫苗打下了基础。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>presence</b></td><td>in sb's ˈpresence • in the presence of sb</td><td>当着某人的面；在某人在场时</td><td>He never swears in the presence of his grandmother.<br>他从不当着祖母的面说粗话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make your ˈpresence felt</td><td>让人感受到自己的存在（或影响）</td><td>The new coach made his presence felt within the first week.<br>新教练第一周就让大家感受到了他的存在。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>presence of ˈmind</td><td>临危不乱；遇事镇定</td><td>She had the presence of mind to switch off the gas before running out.<br>她临危不乱，跑出去前先关掉了煤气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>present</b></td><td>all ˌpresent and corˈrect (BrE) (spoken)</td><td>全都到齐；一个不缺</td><td>Twelve chairs, twelve name cards — all present and correct.<br>十二把椅子，十二张名牌，全都齐了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>all ˌpresent and acˈcounted for (AmE) (spoken)</td><td>应到的都到了；如数到齐</td><td>I've checked the list twice: all present and accounted for.<br>名单我核对了两遍，人全都到齐了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈpresent</td><td>目前；现在</td><td>At present we have no plans to open a second shop.<br>目前我们没有开第二家店的打算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈpresent of sth (to sb)</td><td>（因大意而）把…白白送人</td><td>By leaving the gate open, we made a present of the bikes to any passing thief.<br>门开着没关，等于把自行车白送给过路的小偷。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈpresent form</td><td>就目前的表现看</td><td>On present form, they'll be lucky to finish in the top ten.<br>就目前的状态看，他们能进前十就算走运。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>present company exˈcepted (also excepting present ˈcompany)</td><td>在场诸位除外</td><td>Most managers here are useless — present company excepted, of course.<br>这里多数经理都不顶用，当然，在座各位除外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌpresent ˈday</td><td>当今；如今</td><td>The museum traces the city's story from Roman times to the present day.<br>博物馆讲述了这座城市从罗马时代至今的历史。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>press</b></td><td>get/have a good, bad, etc. ˈpress</td><td>受到好评（或恶评）</td><td>The new tax has had a very bad press since it was announced.<br>这项新税自公布以来一直恶评如潮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌpress (the) ˈflesh</td><td>（政客等）与选民握手拉票</td><td>The candidate spent all morning pressing the flesh in the market square.<br>候选人整个上午都在集市广场上与选民握手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>press sth ˈhome</td><td>坚持（论点）；乘势推进</td><td>She pressed her argument home until the committee finally agreed.<br>她一再强调自己的论点，直到委员会最终同意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>press ˌhome your adˈvantage</td><td>乘胜追击；充分利用优势</td><td>Two goals up, they pressed home their advantage in the second half.<br>领先两球后，他们在下半场乘胜追击。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>press sb/sth into ˈservice</td><td>临时征用；应急使用</td><td>We pressed an old door into service as a table for the party.<br>我们把一扇旧门临时拿来当聚会的桌子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈgutter press (BrE, disapproving)</td><td>低俗小报</td><td>The gutter press hounded the family for weeks after the trial.<br>庭审后，低俗小报追着这家人纠缠了好几个星期。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pressed</b></td><td>be pressed for ˈmoney, ˈspace, ˈtime, etc.</td><td>缺钱（或地方、时间等）</td><td>I'm rather pressed for time, so let's keep this short.<br>我时间比较紧，咱们长话短说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pressure</b></td><td>put ˈpressure on sb (to do sth)</td><td>向某人施加压力（要其做某事）</td><td>They're putting pressure on him to resign before the report comes out.<br>他们正施压要他在报告公布前辞职。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring pressure to ˈbear (on sb) (to do sth)</td><td>对某人施加压力；迫使</td><td>Local residents brought pressure to bear on the council to save the library.<br>当地居民向议会施压，要求保住图书馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under ˈpressure</td><td>在压力下；被迫</td><td>He makes silly mistakes when he's working under pressure.<br>他在压力下工作时会犯些低级错误。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pretty</b></td><td>not just a pretty ˈface (humorous)</td><td>不只有漂亮脸蛋；并非徒有其表</td><td>She fixed the engine in ten minutes — not just a pretty face, then.<br>她十分钟就修好了发动机，看来可不只是长得好看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌnot a pretty ˈsight (humorous)</td><td>不堪入目；有碍观瞻</td><td>The kitchen after their cooking lesson was not a pretty sight.<br>上完烹饪课后的厨房，那场面惨不忍睹。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) ˌpretty as a ˈpicture</td><td>美丽如画；漂亮极了</td><td>The village in the snow was as pretty as a picture.<br>雪中的村庄美得像一幅画。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pretty ˈmuch/ˈwell</td><td>几乎；差不多</td><td>I've pretty much finished the report; just the conclusion is left.<br>报告我差不多写完了，只剩结论部分。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pretty ˈnearly (BrE) (AmE also pretty ˈnear) (spoken)</td><td>几乎；将近</td><td>We were pretty near giving up when the rescue team arrived.<br>救援队赶到时，我们几乎已经要放弃了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a pretty ˈpenny (old-fashioned)</td><td>一大笔钱</td><td>That antique clock must have cost him a pretty penny.<br>那座古董钟一定花了他不少钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prevention</b></td><td>preˌvention is better than ˈcure (BrE) (saying)</td><td>预防胜于治疗；防患于未然</td><td>Get the boiler serviced now — prevention is better than cure.<br>现在就把锅炉检修了吧，预防胜于补救。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˌounce of preˈvention is worth a ˌpound of ˈcure (AmE) (saying)</td><td>防患于未然胜过事后补救</td><td>Back up your files today; an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.<br>今天就把文件备份了吧，防患于未然胜过事后补救。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>preview</b></td><td>a sneak ˈpreview</td><td>先睹为快；提前预览</td><td>The director gave us a sneak preview of the final scene.<br>导演让我们提前看了最后一场戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prey</b></td><td>be/fall ˈprey to sth (formal)</td><td>成为…的牺牲品；受…之害</td><td>Elderly people often fall prey to phone scams like this one.<br>老年人常常成为这类电话诈骗的受害者。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>prey on sb's ˈmind (also ˌplay on sb's ˈmind)</td><td>萦绕心头；使耿耿于怀</td><td>That argument with my sister has been preying on my mind all week.<br>和妹妹的那场争吵让我一整周都放不下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>price</b></td><td>at ˈany price</td><td>不惜任何代价</td><td>She wanted that gallery job at any price.<br>她不惜一切代价也要得到画廊那份工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at a ˈprice</td><td>代价高昂；要付出很大代价</td><td>You can get a table on Saturday night, but at a price.<br>周六晚上是能订到桌，不过价钱不便宜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beyond/without ˈprice (formal or literary)</td><td>无价的；极其珍贵</td><td>To a refugee, a passport can be beyond price.<br>对难民来说，一本护照可能是无价之宝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not at ˈany price</td><td>无论如何也不；给多少钱也不干</td><td>I wouldn't work for that man again, not at any price.<br>我不会再给那个人干活了，给多少钱也不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈprice on sb's head</td><td>悬赏捉拿某人的赏金</td><td>The outlaw fled north with a price on his head.<br>那名逃犯带着悬赏令逃往北方。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>price yourself/sth out of the ˈmarket</td><td>因要价过高而失去市场</td><td>They priced themselves out of the market and lost every regular client.<br>他们要价太高，把市场做丢了，老客户全跑光了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put a ˈprice on sth</td><td>为…定价；估价</td><td>It's hard to put a price on a good night's sleep.<br>一夜好眠的价值很难用钱衡量。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what ˈprice...? (BrE, spoken)</td><td>…又有什么用呢；值得吗</td><td>What price fame if you can't walk down the street in peace?<br>要是连安静走在街上都做不到，出名又有什么用？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prick</b></td><td>prick your ˈconscience • your ˈconscience pricks you</td><td>良心不安；受良心谴责</td><td>His conscience pricked him every time he walked past the beggar.<br>每次走过那个乞丐身边，他都会良心不安。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌprick up your ˈears • your ˈears prick up</td><td>竖起耳朵；侧耳倾听</td><td>The dog pricked up its ears the moment it heard the car outside.<br>一听到外面的车声，狗立刻竖起了耳朵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pride</b></td><td>your ˌpride and ˈjoy</td><td>引以为傲的人（或物）</td><td>That vintage motorbike in the garage is his pride and joy.<br>车库里那辆老式摩托车是他的心头宝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pride comes before a ˈfall (saying)</td><td>骄兵必败；骄者必衰</td><td>He bragged all week about winning, and then lost badly — pride comes before a fall.<br>他吹了一周要赢，结果输得很惨，真是骄兵必败。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(give sth) pride of ˈplace</td><td>（把…放在）最显要的位置</td><td>Her grandmother's clock has pride of place on the mantelpiece.<br>祖母那座钟摆在壁炉台最显眼的位置。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈpride in sb/sth</td><td>为…感到自豪；用心做好</td><td>He takes real pride in keeping the old bookshop spotless.<br>他把那家旧书店打理得一尘不染，很以此为傲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prim</b></td><td>prim and ˈproper</td><td>一本正经；循规蹈矩</td><td>Our new neighbour is far too prim and proper to enjoy a party like that.<br>我们的新邻居太一本正经了，不会喜欢那样的派对。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prima</b></td><td>(a) ˌprima ˈdonna (from Italian, disapproving)</td><td>自负的人；耍大牌的人</td><td>The lead singer is a complete prima donna about hotel rooms.<br>那位主唱在酒店房间上简直是个难伺候的大牌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prime</b></td><td>in the prime of (your) ˈlife</td><td>在壮年；风华正茂时</td><td>He gave up racing in the prime of his life to look after his father.<br>他在风华正茂时放弃了赛车，去照顾父亲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a prime ˈmover</td><td>原动力；主要发起人</td><td>She was the prime mover behind the campaign to clean up the river.<br>她是这场治河运动背后的主要推动者。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>prime the ˈpump</td><td>注资刺激（经济或行业）</td><td>The government cut taxes to prime the pump during the downturn.<br>政府在经济下行时减税以刺激市场。</td></tr>
