<tr><td><b>primrose</b></td><td>the primrose ˈpath (to ruin, destruction, etc.) (literary)</td><td>享乐之路；通向堕落的道路</td><td>Easy money led the young star down the primrose path to ruin.<br>轻易得来的钱把这位年轻明星引上了毁灭之路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prince</b></td><td>ˌPrince ˈCharming (usually humorous)</td><td>白马王子；理想情人</td><td>She's still waiting for Prince Charming to turn up at the bus stop.<br>她还在等着白马王子出现在公交站呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>principle</b></td><td>in ˈprinciple</td><td>原则上；理论上</td><td>They agreed in principle, but the details will take months.<br>他们原则上同意了，但细节还要谈上几个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈprinciple</td><td>出于原则；根据道德准则</td><td>He refuses to fly on principle because of the pollution.<br>出于原则，他因为污染问题拒绝坐飞机。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>print</b></td><td>get into ˈprint</td><td>付印；得以发表</td><td>It took her four years to get her poems into print.<br>她的诗歌用了四年才得以出版。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈprint</td><td>（书）仍在发行；已印行</td><td>Amazingly, that cookbook has stayed in print since 1962.<br>令人惊讶的是，那本菜谱从1962年起一直在印。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of ˈprint</td><td>（书）绝版；停印</td><td>The novel is out of print, so I hunted for it in second-hand shops.<br>这本小说已经绝版，我只好去二手书店找。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>printed</b></td><td>the printed ˈword/ˈpage</td><td>印刷文字；出版的书刊</td><td>My grandfather still trusts the printed word more than any website.<br>我祖父至今仍更相信白纸黑字，而不是网站。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>priorities</b></td><td>get your priˈorities right/straight</td><td>分清轻重缓急</td><td>Get your priorities straight — sleep first, emails later.<br>分清主次吧，先睡觉，邮件晚点再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prisoners</b></td><td>take no ˈprisoners</td><td>咄咄逼人；毫不留情</td><td>In negotiations she takes no prisoners and everyone knows it.<br>谈判桌上她毫不留情，这一点人尽皆知。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>private</b></td><td>a ˌprivate ˈeye (informal)</td><td>私家侦探</td><td>They hired a private eye to find out where the money had gone.<br>他们请了个私家侦探去查那笔钱的去向。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>private ˈparts</td><td>私处；生殖器官</td><td>The doctor asked politely whether he had any pain in his private parts.<br>医生客气地问他私处有没有疼痛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>probability</b></td><td>in ˌall probaˈbility (written)</td><td>很可能；十有八九</td><td>In all probability the train will be delayed again this evening.<br>今晚这趟车十有八九又要晚点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>problem</b></td><td>do you have a ˈproblem with that? (spoken)</td><td>你对此有意见吗</td><td>I'm taking Friday off. Do you have a problem with that?<br>我周五要请假，你对此有意见吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's/ˌthat's not ˈmy problem (spoken, informal)</td><td>那不关我的事</td><td>If he forgot to book the room, that's not my problem.<br>他忘了订房间，那不关我的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no ˈproblem (spoken, informal)</td><td>没问题；不客气</td><td>Could you pick me up at seven? No problem, see you then.<br>你能七点来接我吗？没问题，到时见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's ˈyour, ˈhis, etc. problem (spoken, informal)</td><td>那是你（或他等）自己的事</td><td>You spent all your wages on shoes? That's your problem.<br>你把工资全花在鞋上了？那是你自己的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's your ˈproblem? (spoken, informal)</td><td>你到底怎么了（表示不满）</td><td>You've been snapping at everyone all morning — what's your problem?<br>你一上午对谁都没好气，你到底怎么了？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>problems</b></td><td>have ˈteething problems/troubles</td><td>有初期的小毛病；遇到起步困难</td><td>The new app still has a few teething problems on older phones.<br>这款新应用在旧手机上还有些初期小毛病。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>probs</b></td><td>no ˈprobs (spoken)</td><td>没问题；小事一桩</td><td>Can you swap shifts with me on Tuesday? No probs.<br>周二能和我换个班吗？没问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>process</b></td><td>in the ˈprocess (of doing sth)</td><td>在（做某事）的过程中；同时</td><td>He fixed the tap and flooded the kitchen in the process.<br>他修好了水龙头，同时也把厨房淹了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prodigal</b></td><td>a/the prodigal ˈson (formal, disapproving or humorous)</td><td>回头的浪子；改过自新的人</td><td>The prodigal son returned after five years with no money and no job.<br>这位浪子五年后回来了，身无分文，也没工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>production</b></td><td>on production of sth (formal)</td><td>凭出示（某物）</td><td>Students get half-price tickets on production of a valid card.<br>学生凭有效证件可买半价票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>profile</b></td><td>adopt, keep, etc. a ˌhigh/ˌlow ˈprofile</td><td>保持高（或低）姿态；张扬（或低调）</td><td>After the scandal he kept a low profile for almost a year.<br>丑闻之后，他低调了将近一年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈprofile</td><td>从侧面看（脸）</td><td>In profile she looks exactly like her mother at that age.<br>从侧面看，她和她母亲那个年纪时一模一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get with the ˈprogram (AmE, informal)</td><td>跟上进度；按要求行事</td><td>Get with the program, Dave — everyone else filed their reports yesterday.<br>戴夫，跟上节奏吧，别人昨天就交报告了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get with the ˈprogramme (informal)</td><td>改变态度；做该做的事</td><td>The coach told the players to get with the programme or leave.<br>教练告诉队员们要么照做，要么走人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prolong</b></td><td>proˌlong the ˈagony</td><td>延长痛苦；拖延难熬的局面</td><td>Just tell me the result and don't prolong the agony.<br>直接告诉我结果吧，别再折磨我了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>promise</b></td><td>I (can) ˈpromise you (informal)</td><td>我向你保证；我敢担保</td><td>You'll regret selling that guitar, I can promise you.<br>卖掉那把吉他你会后悔的，我敢保证。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>promise (sb) the ˈmoon/the ˈearth/the ˈworld (informal)</td><td>许下无法兑现的承诺</td><td>The salesman promised us the earth and delivered almost nothing.<br>那个推销员对我们许下天大的承诺，结果几乎什么都没做到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>promised</b></td><td>the promised ˈland</td><td>希望之乡；理想的乐土</td><td>For many migrants that city was the promised land of steady work.<br>对许多移民来说，那座城市就是有稳定工作的希望之乡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>promises</b></td><td>he, it, etc. promises ˈwell</td><td>很有希望；前景看好</td><td>The first chapter promises well, though the ending is weak.<br>第一章很有看头，只是结尾差了些。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>proof</b></td><td>the proof of the ˈpudding (is in the ˈeating) (saying)</td><td>空谈不如实践；实践出真知</td><td>The design looks clever, but the proof of the pudding is in the eating.<br>设计看着很巧妙，不过好不好用还得试了才知道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>proof ˈpositive</td><td>确凿的证据；铁证</td><td>The video was proof positive that he had never left the building.<br>这段视频铁证如山，说明他根本没离开过大楼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prop</b></td><td>prop up the ˈbar (informal, disapproving)</td><td>整天泡在酒吧喝酒</td><td>He props up the bar every evening instead of looking for work.<br>他每天晚上都泡在酒吧里，也不去找工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>proper</b></td><td>good and ˈproper (BrE, spoken)</td><td>彻底地；完完全全</td><td>We got soaked good and proper walking home in that storm.<br>在那场暴雨里走回家，我们被淋了个透。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prophet</b></td><td>a ˌprophet of ˈdoom • a ˈdoom merchant</td><td>悲观论者；末日预言者</td><td>Ignore the prophets of doom; the shop is doing better every month.<br>别理那些唱衰的人，店里生意一个月比一个月好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>proportion</b></td><td>ˌkeep sth in proˈportion</td><td>理性看待；不夸大问题</td><td>It's one bad review — let's keep this in proportion.<br>不过是一条差评，咱们别小题大做。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of (all) proˈportion (to sth)</td><td>与…不成比例；不相称</td><td>His anger was completely out of all proportion to the mistake.<br>他发的火跟这点小错完全不成比例。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>propose</b></td><td>propose a ˈtoast (to sb)</td><td>提议为（某人）干杯</td><td>I'd like to propose a toast to the happy couple.<br>我提议为这对新人干杯。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pros</b></td><td>the ˌpros and ˈcons (of sth)</td><td>利与弊；正反两方面</td><td>We spent the evening weighing up the pros and cons of moving abroad.<br>我们花了一晚上权衡出国的利弊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>protest</b></td><td>under ˈprotest</td><td>不情愿地；抗议着</td><td>She signed the new contract under protest and told everyone so.<br>她很不情愿地签了新合同，还逢人便说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>proud</b></td><td>do sb ˈproud (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>盛情款待某人</td><td>Her parents did us proud with a huge Sunday lunch.<br>她父母做了一大桌周日午餐，把我们招待得非常周到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do yourself/sb ˈproud</td><td>为自己（或某人）争光</td><td>The choir did the school proud at the national competition.<br>合唱团在全国比赛上为学校争了光。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>proves</b></td><td>the exˈception that proves the ˈrule</td><td>例外恰恰证明规律的存在</td><td>He's never late, so today is the exception that proves the rule.<br>他从不迟到，所以今天算是那个证明规律的例外。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>prowl</b></td><td>be/go on the ˈprowl</td><td>（伺机）潜行；四处搜寻</td><td>A fox was on the prowl behind the bins again last night.<br>昨晚又有只狐狸在垃圾桶后面转悠。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pub</b></td><td>a ˈpub crawl (BrE, informal)</td><td>逐家酒吧喝酒；串酒吧</td><td>They went on a pub crawl through the old town on his birthday.<br>他生日那天，他们在老城区一家家酒吧喝了过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>public</b></td><td>be ˌpublic ˈproperty</td><td>人人皆知；成为公众话题</td><td>Once you're famous, your private life becomes public property.<br>一旦出了名，你的私生活就成了公众谈资。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈpublic</td><td>（公司）上市；公开宣布</td><td>The company went public last spring and the shares doubled.<br>这家公司去年春天上市，股价翻了一番。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the public ˈeye</td><td>受公众关注；广为人知</td><td>Raising children in the public eye can't be easy for them.<br>在公众目光下养育孩子对他们来说肯定不容易。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>public ˌenemy number ˈone</td><td>头号公敌；危害最大的人（或事物）</td><td>Sugar has become public enemy number one for many nutritionists.<br>在许多营养学家眼中，糖已成为头号公敌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>puff</b></td><td>puff and ˈpant/ˈblow (informal)</td><td>气喘吁吁；直喘粗气</td><td>He came up the last flight of stairs puffing and panting.<br>他爬上最后一段楼梯时已经气喘吁吁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>puffed</b></td><td>be puffed up with ˈpride, etc.</td><td>洋洋自得；趾高气扬</td><td>The boy was puffed up with pride after scoring the winning goal.<br>打进制胜球后，那男孩得意得不得了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pull</b></td><td>on the ˈpull (BrE, slang)</td><td>出去猎艳；找对象</td><td>The lads were clearly on the pull in that nightclub on Friday.<br>周五在那家夜店，几个小伙子明显是去找姑娘的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull the ˌcarpet/ˌrug out from under sb's ˈfeet (informal)</td><td>突然停止对某人的支持</td><td>The sponsors pulled the rug out from under our feet three weeks before opening.<br>开幕前三周，赞助方突然撤了对我们的支持。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull the ˈrug out from under sb's feet (informal)</td><td>突然撤走支持；釜底抽薪</td><td>Cutting the budget now pulls the rug out from under the whole research team.<br>现在砍预算等于把整个研究团队的支撑抽走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull the ˈcarpet out from under sb's feet (informal)</td><td>突然不再帮助（或支持）某人</td><td>The bank has pulled the carpet out from under his feet, so he must sell the business.<br>银行突然停止支持他，他只能卖掉企业了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull/make ˈfaces/a ˈface (at sb/sth)</td><td>做鬼脸；扮怪相</td><td>Stop pulling faces at your brother and eat your dinner.<br>别对你弟弟做鬼脸了，快吃饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull a ˈfast one (on sb) (slang)</td><td>欺骗；耍花招</td><td>The dealer pulled a fast one on us with the mileage.<br>那个车商在里程数上把我们给骗了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull sb's ˈleg (informal)</td><td>开某人的玩笑；捉弄某人</td><td>Relax, nobody's been fired — I was only pulling your leg.<br>别紧张，没人被解雇，我只是逗你玩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull the ˈother one (— it's got ˈbells on!) (BrE, informal)</td><td>别逗了；我才不信呢</td><td>You cooked this yourself? Pull the other one, it's got bells on.<br>这是你自己做的？别逗了，我才不信。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌpull the ˈother one! (BrE, informal)</td><td>别骗我了；别开玩笑了</td><td>I've been offered a job in New York. Pull the other one!<br>我在纽约找到工作了。别逗了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull out all the ˈstops (informal)</td><td>竭尽全力；使出浑身解数</td><td>The staff pulled out all the stops to get the shop open on time.<br>员工们使出了浑身解数，让店铺按时开张。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull the ˈplug on sth (informal)</td><td>终止；叫停（计划等）</td><td>Head office pulled the plug on the project after two bad quarters.<br>两个季度业绩糟糕后，总部叫停了这个项目。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull your ˈpunches (informal)</td><td>手下留情；言辞委婉</td><td>The review didn't pull any punches about the film's terrible script.<br>这篇影评对片子糟糕的剧本毫不留情。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull sth/a ˌrabbit out of the ˈhat (informal)</td><td>突然想出妙计；出奇制胜</td><td>With ten minutes left, the coach pulled a rabbit out of the hat.<br>比赛还剩十分钟，教练突然使出了一招妙棋。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull ˈrank (on sb)</td><td>以势压人；摆官架子</td><td>He pulled rank and took the only window office for himself.<br>他仗着职位高，把唯一那间靠窗的办公室占为己有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull your ˈsocks up (BrE, informal)</td><td>振作起来；加把劲</td><td>You'd better pull your socks up before the exams next month.<br>下个月就要考试了，你最好赶紧振作起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull ˈstrings (for sb) (AmE also pull ˈwires)</td><td>暗中疏通；走后门</td><td>His uncle pulled strings to get him an interview at the ministry.<br>他叔叔走后门给他弄了个部里的面试机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull the ˈstrings</td><td>幕后操纵；暗中控制</td><td>The chairman may be new, but his father still pulls the strings.<br>董事长虽然是新的，可幕后掌权的还是他父亲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull up ˈstakes (AmE)</td><td>迁居；举家搬走</td><td>They pulled up stakes in Ohio and started over in Texas.<br>他们离开俄亥俄，搬到得州重新开始。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull your ˈweight</td><td>尽自己的一份力；做好分内事</td><td>Everyone shares the rent, so everyone has to pull their weight.<br>房租大家分摊，所以每个人都得出力。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull the ˈwool over sb's eyes (informal)</td><td>蒙蔽某人；掩人耳目</td><td>Don't try to pull the wool over my eyes — I saw the receipt.<br>别想蒙我，我看到收据了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull yourself toˈgether</td><td>振作起来；恢复镇定</td><td>Pull yourself together — the interview starts in five minutes.<br>振作点，面试五分钟后就开始了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pulling</b></td><td>like pulling ˈteeth</td><td>极其困难；难如登天</td><td>Getting a straight answer out of him is like pulling teeth.<br>想从他嘴里得到一句实话，比登天还难。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pump</b></td><td>pump sb full of sth</td><td>给某人大量注射（或灌输）</td><td>They pumped him full of painkillers before moving him.<br>搬动他之前，他们给他打了大量止痛药。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pump ˈiron (informal)</td><td>举重健身；练器械</td><td>He pumps iron at the gym every morning before work.<br>他每天上班前都在健身房练器械。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pump sb's ˈstomach</td><td>给某人洗胃</td><td>Doctors had to pump the child's stomach after she swallowed the pills.<br>孩子吞了药片后，医生只好给她洗胃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>punch</b></td><td>he, she, etc. couldn't ˌpunch his, her, etc. way out of a paper ˈbag (informal, humorous)</td><td>软弱无能；不堪一击</td><td>Their new striker couldn't punch his way out of a paper bag.<br>他们新来的前锋简直是软脚虾。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>couldn't ˌpunch your way out of a paper ˈbag (informal, humorous)</td><td>毫无本事；窝囊</td><td>He talks tough but couldn't punch his way out of a paper bag.<br>他嘴上很横，其实一点本事也没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>punch above/below your ˈweight</td><td>做超出（或低于）自身能力的事</td><td>The little bakery punches well above its weight in national awards.<br>这家小面包店在全国评奖中的表现远超其规模。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pup</b></td><td>sell sb/buy a ˈpup (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>把次货卖给某人；买到次货</td><td>That second-hand laptop died in a week — I've been sold a pup.<br>那台二手笔记本一周就坏了，我买到次品了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pure</b></td><td>pure and ˈsimple</td><td>纯粹是；不折不扣</td><td>What happened at the border was theft, pure and simple.<br>边境上发生的事就是抢劫，不折不扣。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) pure as the driven ˈsnow (often humorous)</td><td>洁白无瑕；品行高洁</td><td>He acts as pure as the driven snow, but I know about the expenses.<br>他装得一尘不染，可我知道那些报销的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>purpose</b></td><td>on ˈpurpose</td><td>故意；有意</td><td>She spilled the drink on his shirt on purpose, I'm certain of it.<br>我敢肯定，她是故意把饮料洒在他衬衫上的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to little/good/some/no ˈpurpose (formal)</td><td>收效甚微（或很大、有些、毫无）</td><td>We argued with the officials for hours, to no purpose at all.<br>我们和官员们争了几个小时，一点用也没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>purse</b></td><td>control/hold the ˈpurse strings (informal)</td><td>掌管钱财；握有财权</td><td>In that family it's the grandmother who holds the purse strings.<br>在那个家里，管钱的是奶奶。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a silk ˈpurse out of a ˈsow's ear (saying)</td><td>化腐朽为神奇（通常指办不到）</td><td>With that script, even a great cast can't make a silk purse out of a sow's ear.<br>就那个剧本，再好的演员也无法化腐朽为神奇。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>push</b></td><td>give sb/get the ˈpush (BrE, informal)</td><td>解雇；被解雇</td><td>He got the push after arguing with a customer in front of everyone.<br>他当众和顾客吵架，结果被炒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if/when ˌpush comes to ˈshove (informal)</td><td>迫不得已时；到了关键时刻</td><td>If push comes to shove, we can always sleep in the car.<br>实在不行，我们还可以睡车里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>push the ˈboat out (BrE, informal)</td><td>大手笔庆祝；不惜花钱</td><td>They really pushed the boat out for their daughter's wedding.<br>女儿结婚，他们真是花了大钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌpush sb's ˈbuttons (also ˌpress sb's ˈbuttons especially in BrE) (informal)</td><td>触动某人情绪；惹某人发作</td><td>My brother knows exactly how to push my buttons at dinner.<br>我弟弟最清楚吃饭时怎么惹毛我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>push the ˈenvelope</td><td>挑战极限；突破界限</td><td>The band keeps pushing the envelope with every new album.<br>这支乐队每出一张新专辑都在突破边界。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>push your ˈluck • ˈpush it/things (informal)</td><td>得寸进尺；继续冒险</td><td>You got away with it once; don't push your luck again.<br>你侥幸过了一次，别再冒险了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>push sth to the ˌback of your ˈmind</td><td>把…抛到脑后；刻意不去想</td><td>She pushed the diagnosis to the back of her mind and went to work.<br>她把诊断结果抛到脑后，照常去上班。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>press/push the ˈpanic button (informal)</td><td>惊慌失措；仓促求救</td><td>Sales dipped for one month and management pressed the panic button.<br>销售额只降了一个月，管理层就慌了神。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pushing</b></td><td>be ˌpushing ˈforty, ˈfifty, etc. (informal)</td><td>年近四十（或五十等）</td><td>He's pushing fifty but still plays football every Sunday morning.<br>他快五十了，还是每周日上午踢球。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌpushing up (the) ˈdaisies (old-fashioned, humorous)</td><td>已经入土；死了</td><td>By the time that law changes, I'll be pushing up the daisies.<br>等那条法律改了，我坟头草都长高了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put</b></td><td>put it aˈbout (BrE, informal)</td><td>私生活不检点；到处乱搞</td><td>There were nasty rumours at work that he put it about a lot.<br>单位里有难听的传言，说他私生活很乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put it ˈon (informal)</td><td>装腔作势；故意夸张</td><td>She isn't really that upset — she's putting it on for sympathy.<br>她其实没那么难过，是装出来博同情的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌput it ˈthere!</td><td>来握握手吧（表示同意或赞赏）</td><td>You agree we should split the profit fifty-fifty? Put it there!<br>你同意利润五五分？来，握个手！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb ˈthrough it (especially BrE, informal)</td><td>使某人吃苦头；让某人经受考验</td><td>The interview panel really put me through it for two hours.<br>面试小组足足折腾了我两个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put toˈgether</td><td>（与…相比）加起来；总共</td><td>She earns more than the rest of the department put together.<br>她挣的比部门其他人加起来还多。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>putty</b></td><td>(like) putty in sb's ˈhands (informal)</td><td>任人摆布；对某人百依百顺</td><td>One smile from his granddaughter and he's putty in her hands.<br>孙女一笑，他就任由她摆布了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put-up</b></td><td>a ˌput-up ˈjob (BrE, informal)</td><td>骗局；预先设好的圈套</td><td>The whole auction was a put-up job to raise the price.<br>整场拍卖就是个抬价的局。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pyrrhic</b></td><td>a ˌPyrrhic ˈvictory</td><td>得不偿失的胜利</td><td>They won the case but lost their savings — a Pyrrhic victory.<br>他们赢了官司却赔光积蓄，实在是得不偿失。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Q</b></td><td>QEˈD</td><td>证明完毕；由此可见</td><td>Nobody complained, nobody left early, QED: the talk was good.<br>没人抱怨，没人早退，可见这场讲座不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quandary</b></td><td>in a ˈquandary</td><td>左右为难；进退两难</td><td>I'm in a quandary about whether to tell her the truth.<br>要不要告诉她实情，我实在左右为难。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quantum</b></td><td>a quantum ˈleap (also a quantum ˈjump less frequent)</td><td>巨大飞跃；重大进展</td><td>This treatment represents a quantum leap in cancer care.<br>这种疗法是癌症治疗上的一次巨大飞跃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quart</b></td><td>get/pour/put a ˌquart into a pint ˈpot (BrE)</td><td>强做办不到的事；硬塞</td><td>Fitting six people in that car is putting a quart into a pint pot.<br>那车里塞六个人，简直是强人所难。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quarters</b></td><td>at close ˈquarters</td><td>近距离地；紧挨着</td><td>You only notice the cracks when you see the painting at close quarters.<br>只有近距离看这幅画，才会注意到那些裂纹。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>queen</b></td><td>ˈqueen it over sb</td><td>对某人摆架子；盛气凌人</td><td>She queens it over the junior staff whenever the manager is away.<br>经理一不在，她就对新员工颐指气使。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>queer</b></td><td>queer sb's ˈpitch • queer the ˈpitch (for sb) (BrE, informal)</td><td>破坏某人的计划；从中作梗</td><td>Announcing his own plan early really queered the pitch for us.<br>他提前公布自己的方案，把我们的计划搅黄了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>an ˈodd/a ˈqueer fish (BrE, informal)</td><td>怪人；性情古怪的人</td><td>The caretaker is a queer fish, but he's kind to the children.<br>那位看门人是个怪人，不过对孩子们很好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>question</b></td><td>beyond/without ˈquestion</td><td>毫无疑问；确定无疑</td><td>She is beyond question the best pianist in the school.<br>她无疑是全校最好的钢琴手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring/call/throw sth into ˈquestion</td><td>使…受到质疑</td><td>The missing receipts call his honesty into question.<br>丢失的收据让人怀疑他是否诚实。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>good ˈquestion! (spoken)</td><td>问得好（表示答不上来）</td><td>Why is the deadline a Friday? Good question — nobody knows.<br>为什么截止日定在周五？问得好，没人知道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈquestion (formal)</td><td>正在讨论的；所提到的</td><td>The evening in question, he was three hundred miles away.<br>在所说的那个晚上，他在三百英里之外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's (just, etc.) a ˈquestion of sth</td><td>（只不过）是…的问题</td><td>It's just a question of finding the right person for the job.<br>这只不过是找到合适人选的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of the ˈquestion</td><td>不可能；不予考虑</td><td>Another loan is out of the question until you clear this one.<br>在你还清这笔之前，再贷一笔想都别想。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈquestion mark hangs over sb/sth</td><td>对…存有疑问；前景不明</td><td>A question mark hangs over the future of the whole department.<br>整个部门的前途都还是个问号。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's a ˈquestion mark (hanging) over sb/sth</td><td>对…打上问号；有疑问</td><td>There's a question mark hanging over whether the stadium will be finished.<br>体育场能否完工还是个问号。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's a ˈquestion mark over sth</td><td>对…存疑</td><td>There's a question mark over his loyalty to the company.<br>他对公司是否忠诚还是个问号。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's some/no question of sth/of doing sth</td><td>有（或没有）可能做某事</td><td>There's no question of us moving house before the baby arrives.<br>在孩子出生前，我们不可能搬家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without ˈquestion</td><td>毫无异议地；不加质疑地</td><td>The young soldiers followed every one of his orders without question.<br>年轻士兵们不加质疑地执行了他的每一道命令。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quick</b></td><td>cut sb to the ˈquick</td><td>深深刺痛某人；伤到某人痛处</td><td>Her remark about his cooking cut him to the quick.<br>她那句关于他厨艺的话深深刺伤了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a quick ˈtemper</td><td>脾气暴躁；易发火</td><td>My uncle has a quick temper but he calms down just as fast.<br>我叔叔脾气挺急，不过消气也快。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌquick and ˈdirty (informal)</td><td>权宜的；应急凑合的</td><td>I'll do a quick and dirty fix now and rewrite it properly later.<br>我先临时补一下，回头再好好重写。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) quick as a ˈflash</td><td>快如闪电；转眼之间</td><td>Quick as a flash, she caught the glass before it hit the floor.<br>说时迟那时快，她在杯子落地前一把接住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌquick ˈmarch</td><td>快走；赶紧行动</td><td>Right, quick march everyone, the bus leaves in three minutes.<br>好了，大家快走，公交三分钟后就开。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌquick ˈmarch! (military)</td><td>（口令）齐步走</td><td>The sergeant shouted 'Quick march!' and the whole line moved off.<br>中士喊了一声“齐步走”，整队人马就出发了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈquick one (BrE, informal)</td><td>匆匆喝的一杯（酒）</td><td>Fancy a quick one at the pub before your train?<br>火车前去酒吧快喝一杯怎么样？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈfast/ˈquick buck (informal)</td><td>捞快钱；赚快钱</td><td>He's only in this business to make a fast buck.<br>他做这行只是为了捞快钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quid</b></td><td>quid pro ˈquo (from Latin)</td><td>交换物；报偿</td><td>They'll help with the paperwork, but expect a quid pro quo later.<br>他们会帮着办手续，但以后会要回报的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not the full ˈquid (AustralE, NZE, informal)</td><td>脑子不太灵光；缺心眼</td><td>People say he's not the full quid, but he's sharper than he looks.<br>人家说他脑子不太灵光，其实他精着呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quids</b></td><td>quids ˈin (BrE, informal)</td><td>大赚一笔；获利颇丰</td><td>If the flat sells at that price, we're quids in.<br>房子要是能卖到那个价，我们就赚翻了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quiet</b></td><td>keep ˈquiet about sth • keep sth ˈquiet</td><td>对…保密；守口如瓶</td><td>Let's keep the party quiet until her birthday morning.<br>聚会的事先保密，到她生日那天早上再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈquiet (also on the ˈq.t. old-fashioned)</td><td>悄悄地；私下里</td><td>He'd been taking Spanish lessons on the quiet for months.<br>他偷偷学了好几个月西班牙语。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) quiet as a ˈmouse</td><td>非常安静；一声不吭</td><td>The children were as quiet as mice while the baby slept.<br>宝宝睡觉时，孩子们安静得像小老鼠。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quite</b></td><td>not ˌquite the ˈthing</td><td>不太得体；不合规矩</td><td>Wearing trainers to the funeral was not quite the thing.<br>穿运动鞋去参加葬礼不太得体。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈquite a/some sb/sth (informal)</td><td>了不起的；不同寻常的</td><td>That was quite a speech — half the room was in tears.<br>那真是一场了不起的演讲，半屋子人都哭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>quite the ˈbest, the ˈworst, etc. sth (informal)</td><td>绝对是最好（或最差等）的</td><td>That was quite the worst meal I've eaten all year.<br>那绝对是我今年吃过的最难吃的一顿饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>quite a ˈfew (BrE also a good ˈfew)</td><td>相当多；不少</td><td>Quite a few of my classmates have already moved abroad.<br>我不少同学都已经移居国外了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>quite ˈso (BrE, formal)</td><td>正是；一点不错</td><td>So the whole plan depends on the weather? Quite so.<br>这么说整个计划全看天气？正是如此。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>quite some ˈtime</td><td>相当长的一段时间</td><td>We waited quite some time before anyone came to the desk.<br>我们等了好一阵子才有人到柜台来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quits</b></td><td>be ˈquits (with sb) (informal)</td><td>互不相欠；两清</td><td>You bought lunch and I paid for the taxi, so we're quits.<br>你请了午饭，我付了车费，咱俩两清了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>quote</b></td><td>quote (... ˈunquote) (spoken)</td><td>引文起…引文止；所谓的</td><td>He called it a quote friendly discussion unquote, which it definitely wasn't.<br>他说那是场所谓的“友好讨论”，其实根本不是。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>race</b></td><td>a ˌrace against ˈtime/the ˈclock</td><td>与时间赛跑；争分夺秒</td><td>It was a race against time to get the roof on before the storm.<br>要在暴风雨来临前把屋顶盖好，真是一场与时间的赛跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˌrace to the ˈbottom (business)</td><td>竞相逐底；恶性竞争</td><td>Cutting wages again would only start a race to the bottom.<br>再降工资只会引发一场恶性的逐底竞争。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rack</b></td><td>go to ˌrack and ˈruin</td><td>破败不堪；日渐荒废</td><td>The old farmhouse has gone to rack and ruin since they left.<br>他们搬走后，那栋老农舍已经破败不堪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈrack</td><td>极度焦虑；十分痛苦</td><td>He was on the rack all weekend waiting for the biopsy results to arrive.<br>整个周末他都在焦灼不安地等活检结果。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rack your ˈbrains (also wrack your ˈbrains less frequent) (informal)</td><td>绞尽脑汁；冥思苦想</td><td>I racked my brains for an hour but still couldn't remember her name.<br>我绞尽脑汁想了一个小时，还是想不起她的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>radar</b></td><td>below/under the ˈradar (screen)</td><td>不为人所知；未受关注</td><td>The startup grew below the radar for two years before anyone really noticed.<br>这家初创公司低调发展了两年才被人注意到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on/off the ˈradar (screen)</td><td>受关注；被考虑（或反之）</td><td>Climate change is finally on the radar of every major political party here.<br>气候变化终于进入了这里各大政党的视野。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>remain off the ˈradar</td><td>一直不受关注；始终无人留意</td><td>Eastern Europe has remained off the radar of most British investors until quite recently.<br>直到最近，东欧仍不在多数英国投资者的视野内。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rag</b></td><td>lose your ˈrag (BrE, informal)</td><td>大发雷霆；行为失控</td><td>Dad completely lost his rag when he saw the scratch on his new car.<br>爸爸看到新车上的划痕，一下就火了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈrag trade (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>服装业；成衣业</td><td>She spent thirty years in the rag trade before opening her own boutique.<br>她在服装业干了三十年，后来开了自己的精品店。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rage</b></td><td>all the ˈrage (informal)</td><td>十分流行；风靡一时</td><td>Those chunky white trainers were all the rage when I was at university.<br>我上大学那会儿，那种厚底白运动鞋特别火。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ragged</b></td><td>ˌrun sb ˈragged (informal)</td><td>使精疲力竭；使过度操劳</td><td>The twins run me ragged from breakfast until bedtime every single day.<br>这对双胞胎每天从早到晚把我折腾得筋疲力尽。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a ˈrain check (on sth) (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>改天再说；下次吧</td><td>Can I take a rain check on dinner? I'm swamped with work tonight.<br>晚饭能改天吗？我今晚忙得不可开交。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rains</b></td><td>it never ˌrains but it ˈpours (BrE) (AmE when it ˌrains, it ˈpours) (saying)</td><td>祸不单行；不雨则已，一雨倾盆</td><td>My car broke down, then the boiler died — it never rains but it pours.<br>车坏了，锅炉又罢工，真是祸不单行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rainy</b></td><td>save, keep, etc. it for a ˌrainy ˈday (informal)</td><td>储蓄以备不时之需；未雨绸缪</td><td>Put some of that bonus aside and save it for a rainy day.<br>把奖金存下一部分，以备不时之需。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>raise</b></td><td>raise ˈCain/hell (informal)</td><td>大吵大闹；强烈抗议</td><td>Residents raised hell at the meeting about the new motorway through their village.<br>居民在会上为穿村而过的新高速公路大闹了一场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>raise your ˈeyebrows (at sth)</td><td>扬眉（表示惊讶或不赞同）</td><td>She raised her eyebrows at the price but paid for the coat anyway.<br>她看到价格扬了扬眉，但还是买下了那件大衣。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>raise your ˈglass (to sb)</td><td>举杯（向某人）祝酒</td><td>Let's raise our glasses to the happy couple and wish them many good years.<br>让我们举杯祝这对新人幸福长久。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>raise a ˈlaugh/ˈsmile</td><td>逗人发笑；引人一笑</td><td>Even his oldest jokes still raise a laugh at the family dinner table.<br>他那些老掉牙的笑话在家庭餐桌上仍能逗乐大家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>raise the ˈspectre of sth (BrE) (AmE raise the ˈspecter of sth)</td><td>引起对…的恐惧；使人担忧</td><td>The factory closure raises the spectre of mass unemployment across the whole region.<br>工厂关闭让人担心整个地区会出现大规模失业。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>raise sb's ˈspirits</td><td>使精神振奋；使高兴起来</td><td>A phone call from her grandson always raises her spirits on a gloomy day.<br>孙子的一通电话总能在阴郁的日子里让她开心起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>raise your ˈvoice</td><td>提高嗓门；大声说话</td><td>Don't raise your voice at me — it wasn't my fault the train was late.<br>别冲我嚷，火车晚点又不是我的错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>raise a/your voice aˈgainst sb/sth</td><td>公开反对；大声疾呼抗议</td><td>Only one councillor raised her voice against the plan to sell the park.<br>只有一位议员公开反对出售公园的计划。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rake</b></td><td>rake over the ˈashes/the ˈpast (informal, disapproving)</td><td>翻旧账；重提往事</td><td>There's no point raking over the past every time we have an argument.<br>每次吵架都翻旧账，毫无意义。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ram</b></td><td>ram sth ˈhome (especially BrE)</td><td>使充分明白；反复强调</td><td>The coach rammed home the point that fitness matters more than raw talent.<br>教练反复强调，体能比天赋更重要。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rampage</b></td><td>be/go on the ˈrampage</td><td>横冲直撞；到处撒野搞破坏</td><td>A group of fans went on the rampage through the town after the match.<br>一群球迷赛后在镇上到处闹事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ramrod</b></td><td>ˌramrod ˈstraight • (as) ˌstraight as a ˈramrod</td><td>腰板笔挺；站（坐）得笔直</td><td>The old sergeant stood ramrod straight even while waiting in the supermarket queue.<br>这位老军士连在超市排队时都站得笔直。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) ˌstraight as a ˈramrod</td><td>背挺得直直的；神情严肃郑重</td><td>She sat as straight as a ramrod through the entire three-hour interview.<br>整整三小时的面试，她都坐得笔直。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>range</b></td><td>in/within ˈrange (of sth)</td><td>在可及（可视、可听）的范围内</td><td>Stay within range of the wifi or the video call will keep dropping.<br>待在无线网范围内，不然视频通话会一直断。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of ˈrange (of sth)</td><td>在可及（可视、可听）的范围之外</td><td>The deer was out of range, so the photographer never got his shot.<br>那只鹿超出了距离，摄影师始终没拍到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rank</b></td><td>(the) ˌrank and ˈfile</td><td>（团体或组织中的）普通成员</td><td>The rank and file voted against the deal their union leaders had negotiated.<br>普通会员投票否决了工会领导谈成的协议。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ranks</b></td><td>break ˈranks</td><td>拒绝支持本团体；公开唱反调</td><td>Two ministers broke ranks and criticised the policy in public last night.<br>两位大臣昨晚公开批评该政策，与内阁唱了反调。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come up/rise through the ˈranks</td><td>从底层干起升至高位；行伍出身</td><td>She rose through the ranks from cashier to regional manager in just eight years.<br>她八年间从收银员一路升到大区经理。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>close ˈranks</td><td>（对外）团结一致；结成一气</td><td>The department closed ranks and refused to say anything to the waiting reporters.<br>该部门上下一心，拒绝对守候的记者透露任何情况。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ransom</b></td><td>hold sb to ˈransom</td><td>绑架某人索取赎金；要挟</td><td>A handful of rebels are holding the whole peace process to ransom.<br>少数反对者正在挟持整个和平进程。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a king's ˈransom</td><td>巨款；一大笔钱</td><td>That little painting in the hallway is apparently worth a king's ransom.<br>走廊里那幅小画据说值一大笔钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rant</b></td><td>ˌrant and ˈrave (disapproving)</td><td>大叫大嚷；不停地大声抱怨</td><td>He ranted and raved about the noise for twenty minutes before finally calming down.<br>他为噪音大吵大嚷了二十分钟才平静下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rap</b></td><td>a ˌrap over the ˈknuckles (informal)</td><td>批评；训斥</td><td>The paper got a rap over the knuckles for printing the leaked memo.<br>这家报纸因刊登泄露的备忘录而受到了批评。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈrap (for sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>（为他人）受罚；背黑锅</td><td>Why should I take the rap for a mistake the whole team made?<br>凭什么全队犯的错要我来背黑锅？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>raptures</b></td><td>be in/go into ˈraptures (about/over sb/sth)</td><td>为…狂喜；对…赞不绝口</td><td>The critics went into raptures over her first novel and its strange ending.<br>评论家们对她的处女作及其古怪结尾赞不绝口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rare</b></td><td>a rare ˈbird</td><td>罕见的人（或物）；珍品</td><td>A politician who happily admits mistakes is a rare bird these days.<br>如今肯痛快承认错误的政客实属罕见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>raring</b></td><td>ˌraring to ˈgo (informal)</td><td>跃跃欲试；急不可待</td><td>The kids were up at six, dressed and raring to go to the beach.<br>孩子们六点就起床穿好衣服，急着要去海边。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rat</b></td><td>the ˈrat race (disapproving)</td><td>（大城市里的）激烈竞争；疯狂角逐</td><td>He quit the rat race at forty and now grows vegetables in Wales.<br>他四十岁退出职场角逐，如今在威尔士种菜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rate</b></td><td>at ˈany rate (spoken)</td><td>无论如何；不管怎样</td><td>The flight might be delayed; at any rate, don't wait up for me.<br>航班可能晚点；不管怎样，别等我了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at a rate of ˈknots (BrE, informal)</td><td>飞快地；迅速地</td><td>He got through the paperwork at a rate of knots and left early.<br>他飞快地处理完文件，提早走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈthis/ˈthat rate (spoken)</td><td>照此速度；照这样下去</td><td>At this rate we won't finish painting the kitchen before Christmas arrives.<br>照这个速度，圣诞节前我们刷不完厨房。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌgoing ˈrate (for sth)</td><td>现行价格；通行收费标准</td><td>What's the going rate for babysitting round here on a Saturday night?<br>这一带周六晚上看孩子的行情价是多少？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rather</b></td><td>rather than</td><td>而不是</td><td>We took the train rather than driving, which saved us a lot of stress.<br>我们坐火车而不是开车，省了不少心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rather you, etc. than ˈme (also sooner you, etc. than ˈme) (especially BrE)</td><td>幸亏不是我；这事儿我可不干</td><td>You're swimming in the sea in January? Rather you than me, honestly.<br>一月还下海游泳？说实话，幸亏不是我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be a bit/rather ˈsteep (informal)</td><td>（价格）偏高；太贵</td><td>Forty pounds for a taxi to the airport seems a bit steep.<br>打车去机场四十镑，似乎贵了点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rattle</b></td><td>rattle sb's ˈcage (informal)</td><td>惹恼；触怒</td><td>Don't mention the referee's decision — it really rattles his cage every time.<br>别提裁判那个判罚，每次都能把他惹毛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>raving</b></td><td>(stark) raving ˈmad/ˈbonkers (informal)</td><td>彻底疯了的；疯疯癫癫的</td><td>You'd have to be stark raving mad to swim across that freezing river.<br>游过那条冰冷的河，你得是彻底疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>raw</b></td><td>catch/touch sb on the ˈraw (BrE)</td><td>触到某人痛处；揭某人伤疤</td><td>His joke about her divorce clearly caught her on the raw.<br>他拿她离婚开玩笑，显然戳到了她的痛处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈraw</td><td>自然状态下的；不加掩饰的</td><td>This documentary shows life in the raw for families on the city's edge.<br>这部纪录片真实呈现了城郊家庭的生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ray</b></td><td>the one/a ray of ˈhope</td><td>（困境中的）一线希望</td><td>The new treatment is the only ray of hope for patients like him.<br>新疗法是像他这样的病人唯一的一线希望。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ray of ˈsunshine (informal)</td><td>带来快乐的人（或事物）；一缕阳光</td><td>My little niece is a ray of sunshine on even the darkest days.<br>我的小侄女在最阴郁的日子里也是一缕阳光。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>razzle</b></td><td>be/go out on the ˈrazzle (BrE, informal)</td><td>外出寻欢作乐；出去纵饮狂欢</td><td>The lads went out on the razzle on Friday and stumbled home at dawn.<br>小伙子们周五出去疯玩，天亮才踉跄回家。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reach</b></td><td>reach for the ˈstars</td><td>志向远大；胸怀雄心壮志</td><td>My grandmother always told me to reach for the stars and ignore the doubters.<br>奶奶总叫我志存高远，别理会那些唱衰的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>within (easy) ˈreach (of sth)</td><td>近在咫尺；容易到达</td><td>The cottage is within easy reach of both the beach and the station.<br>那间小屋离海滩和车站都很近。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>read</b></td><td>ˌread between the ˈlines</td><td>领悟言外之意；看出弦外之音</td><td>Reading between the lines, I'd say she's not very happy in that job.<br>从字里行间看，我觉得她并不喜欢那份工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌread sb like a ˈbook (informal)</td><td>对某人了如指掌；看透某人</td><td>After twenty years of marriage she can read me like a book.<br>结婚二十年了，她把我看得透透的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌread sb's ˈmind/ˈthoughts (informal)</td><td>看出某人的心思；猜透某人的想法</td><td>I was just about to make tea — you read my mind!<br>我正想去泡茶，你真会猜我的心思！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>read my ˈlips (spoken)</td><td>听清楚了；给我听好了</td><td>Read my lips: I am not lending you the car again.<br>给我听好了，我不会再把车借给你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>read (sb) the ˈRiot Act (BrE)</td><td>严厉警告某人收敛；狠狠训斥</td><td>The head teacher read the whole class the Riot Act about the graffiti.<br>校长就涂鸦的事把全班狠狠训了一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth/it as ˈread (BrE)</td><td>认定某事不必再讨论；视为当然</td><td>We can take it as read that everyone here supports the new proposal.<br>可以认定在座各位都支持这项新提议。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ready</b></td><td>at the ˈready</td><td>准备停当；随时可用</td><td>She stood quietly by the door with her camera at the ready.<br>她静静守在门口，相机随时准备好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈready (for sth) (formal)</td><td>（为…）作准备</td><td>The whole village made ready for the storm that was forecast overnight.<br>全村都为预报中夜间来袭的风暴做好了准备。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ready, steady, ˈgo! (BrE) (also (get) ready, (get) set, ˈgo! AmE, BrE)</td><td>各就位，预备，跑！；准备开始</td><td>Ready, steady, go! The children raced across the field towards the finish line.<br>各就位，预备，跑！孩子们冲过田野奔向终点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ready when ˈyou are</td><td>我已准备就绪，就等你了</td><td>Ready when you are — the car's warmed up and the bags are in.<br>我这边好了，就等你，车热好了，行李也装上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>real</b></td><td>for ˈreal</td><td>真正地；确实地；认真地</td><td>Is this offer for real, or is somebody playing a joke on me?<br>这个报价是真的吗，还是有人在跟我开玩笑？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get ˈreal (informal)</td><td>别做梦了；面对现实吧</td><td>You want to buy a house on that salary? Get real.<br>就那点工资还想买房？醒醒吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in real ˈlife</td><td>在现实生活中</td><td>He seems shy online but in real life he never stops talking.<br>他网上看着腼腆，现实中却话多得停不下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌreal McˈCoy (informal)</td><td>真货；正品；地道的东西</td><td>This isn't a copy — the dealer swears it's the real McCoy.<br>这不是仿品，卖家发誓说是真货。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the real ˈthing (informal)</td><td>真品；货真价实的东西</td><td>Instant coffee is fine, but nothing beats the real thing in the morning.<br>速溶咖啡凑合，但早上还是真咖啡最好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reality</b></td><td>in reˈality</td><td>实际上；事实上</td><td>He looks confident on stage, but in reality he's terrified every single time.<br>他台上看着自信，其实每次都怕得要命。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>realms</b></td><td>beyond/within the realms of possiˈbility</td><td>没有可能；有可能</td><td>A February heatwave isn't beyond the realms of possibility these days.<br>如今二月出现热浪也并非没有可能。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reap</b></td><td>reap a/the ˈharvest (BrE)</td><td>收获成果；尝到苦果</td><td>After years of careful training, the team is finally reaping the harvest.<br>经过多年精心训练，这支队伍终于收获了成果。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you ˌreap what you ˈsow (saying)</td><td>种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆；自食其果</td><td>He cheated everyone for years, and now he's learning you reap what you sow.<br>他骗了大家多年，现在明白了什么叫自食其果。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(sow the wind,) reap the ˈwhirlwind (especially AmE)</td><td>自作自受；遭到报应</td><td>The company sowed the wind with those layoffs and is now reaping the whirlwind.<br>公司当初大裁员，如今自食恶果。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rear</b></td><td>ˌbring up the ˈrear</td><td>殿后；走在队伍最后</td><td>Grandad brought up the rear, stopping every few minutes to catch his breath.<br>爷爷走在最后，每隔几分钟就停下喘口气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rearrange</b></td><td>rearrange the ˌdeckchairs on the Tiˈtanic</td><td>做无用功；于事无补</td><td>Repainting the office while sales collapse is just rearranging the deckchairs on the Titanic.<br>销量崩盘还给办公室刷漆，纯属做无用功。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reason</b></td><td>within ˈreason</td><td>合情合理；在合理范围内</td><td>You can order whatever you like, within reason — I'm not made of money.<br>你想点什么都行，别太离谱，我可不是有钱人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rebound</b></td><td>on the ˈrebound</td><td>感情受挫后心灰意懒之际；反弹时</td><td>She married him on the rebound and regretted it within a year.<br>她失恋后草率嫁给了他，不到一年就后悔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>recall</b></td><td>beyond reˈcall</td><td>无法挽回；想不起来</td><td>The old village is gone beyond recall, buried under the new reservoir.<br>那个老村庄已无法找回，淹没在新水库下面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>receiving</b></td><td>be on/at the reˈceiving end (of sth) (informal)</td><td>成为（不快之事的）承受者</td><td>Nobody wants to be on the receiving end of one of his lectures.<br>谁都不想成为他训人的对象。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>recharge</b></td><td>recharge your ˈbatteries (informal)</td><td>养精蓄锐；休整恢复精力</td><td>A week by the sea should help you recharge your batteries properly.<br>在海边待一周应该能让你好好恢复精力。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>recipe</b></td><td>a recipe for diˈsaster, sucˈcess, etc.</td><td>招致灾难（或成功等）的做法</td><td>Cheap parts and a rushed deadline are a recipe for disaster.<br>劣质零件加上赶工期，是招致灾难的组合。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reckoning</b></td><td>in/into/out of the ˈreckoning (especially BrE)</td><td>有（或没有）获胜的可能</td><td>Two more wins would put us back in the reckoning for the title.<br>再赢两场，我们就重新有望争冠。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the day of ˈreckoning</td><td>算总账的日子；清算之日</td><td>The day of reckoning came when the auditors opened the second set of books.<br>审计员翻开第二套账本时，清算的日子到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>recognition</b></td><td>change, alter, etc. beyond/out of (all) recogˈnition</td><td>变得认不出来；面目全非</td><td>The waterfront has changed beyond all recognition since I last visited fifteen years ago.<br>自我十五年前上次来，滨水区已面目全非。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beyond/out of (all) recogˈnition</td><td>面目全非；认不出来</td><td>The old mill was altered out of all recognition when they turned it into flats.<br>老磨坊改成公寓后完全变了样。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>record</b></td><td>be/go on ˈrecord • put sth on ˈrecord</td><td>公开表态；把…记录在案</td><td>The mayor went on record saying he would never raise local taxes.<br>市长公开表示绝不会提高地方税。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) for the ˈrecord</td><td>仅供记录在案；为准确起见</td><td>Just for the record, I never agreed to pay for the repairs.<br>说明一下，我从没答应过承担修理费。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌoff the ˈrecord</td><td>私下说的；不得公开的</td><td>Off the record, the minister admitted the whole scheme was in serious trouble.<br>私下里，那位大臣承认整个方案陷入了大麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈrecord</td><td>记录在案的；有正式记载的</td><td>That was the hottest summer on record since measurements began in this city.<br>那是本市有记录以来最热的夏天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/set the ˈrecord straight (informal)</td><td>澄清误解；说明事实真相</td><td>Let me set the record straight: I resigned, I wasn't sacked.<br>我澄清一下，我是辞职，不是被开除。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>red</b></td><td>in the ˈred (informal)</td><td>亏损；有赤字；欠债</td><td>The shop has been in the red every month since the new supermarket opened.<br>自从新超市开业，这家店月月亏损。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have a red ˈcent (AmE, informal)</td><td>一文不名；身无分文</td><td>By the end of the trip I didn't have a red cent left.<br>旅行结束时我身上一分钱都没剩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˌred aˈlert</td><td>处于紧急戒备状态</td><td>Hospitals across the county were on red alert as the blizzard moved in.<br>暴风雪来袭时，全郡医院都进入了紧急戒备。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) red as a ˈbeetroot (BrE) (AmE (as) red as a ˈbeet) (informal)</td><td>满脸通红（因难堪、生气或觉得热）</td><td>He went as red as a beetroot when she mentioned his old nickname.<br>她一提他的旧外号，他脸就红得发烫。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the red ˈcarpet</td><td>红地毯；隆重的欢迎</td><td>They rolled out the red carpet for the visiting delegation from Japan.<br>他们隆重接待了来访的日本代表团。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a red ˈface (informal)</td><td>尴尬；窘迫相</td><td>There were plenty of red faces when the mistake appeared on the front page.<br>错误上了头版，不少人都很尴尬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a red ˈherring</td><td>转移注意力的话题（或事物）</td><td>The missing key turned out to be a red herring in the investigation.<br>那把丢失的钥匙原来是调查中的一个幌子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>red ˈink (business)</td><td>赤字；亏损</td><td>Another quarter of red ink and the board will start closing branches.<br>再亏一个季度，董事会就要关闭分店了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>red in ˌtooth and ˈclaw</td><td>血淋淋的；残酷无情的</td><td>Publishing looks genteel, but it's red in tooth and claw underneath.<br>出版业看着斯文，骨子里却残酷无情。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(like) a red rag to a ˈbull (BrE)</td><td>肯定会激怒某人的事物</td><td>Mentioning the referee to my uncle is like a red rag to a bull.<br>在我叔叔面前提裁判，无异于火上浇油。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(AmE like waving a red flag in front of/at a ˈbull)</td><td>必定激怒某人的事物；火上浇油</td><td>Bringing up her ex is like waving a red flag at a bull.<br>提她前男友就像拿红布逗牛，准惹她发火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>red ˈtape (disapproving)</td><td>繁文缛节；官僚作风</td><td>We waited eight months for the permit, buried in bureaucratic red tape.<br>我们等许可证等了八个月，全被繁文缛节耽误了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see ˈred (informal)</td><td>勃然大怒；火冒三丈</td><td>I saw red when he blamed the accident on my daughter.<br>他把事故怪到我女儿头上，我一下就火了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>redeeming</b></td><td>a redeeming ˈfeature</td><td>可弥补缺点的优点；可取之处</td><td>The flat is tiny, but the huge balcony is its one redeeming feature.<br>房子很小，但大阳台是它唯一的可取之处。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>red-letter</b></td><td>a ˌred-ˈletter day</td><td>值得纪念的日子；有特殊意义的一天</td><td>The day her son graduated was a real red-letter day for the family.<br>儿子毕业那天对全家来说是个值得纪念的日子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>red-light</b></td><td>the ˌred-ˈlight district</td><td>红灯区；烟花巷</td><td>Their hotel turned out to be right in the middle of the red-light district.<br>他们的酒店竟然就在红灯区正中间。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>redress</b></td><td>redress the ˈbalance</td><td>恢复平衡；重新做到公平合理</td><td>Hiring more women engineers would help redress the balance in the department.<br>多招些女工程师有助于扭转部门的失衡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reduced</b></td><td>reˌduced ˈcircumstances</td><td>境况拮据；家道中落</td><td>The old actress lived out her final years in reduced circumstances near Brighton.<br>这位老演员晚年在布莱顿附近过着拮据的生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live in reˌduced ˈcircumstances</td><td>生活拮据；穷困潦倒</td><td>After the business failed they had to live in reduced circumstances for years.<br>生意失败后，他们过了好些年的拮据日子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reference</b></td><td>in/with ˈreference to (formal or written)</td><td>关于；就…而言</td><td>I'm writing with reference to your advertisement in Saturday's local paper.<br>我来信是关于贵方在周六本地报纸上的广告。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reflect</b></td><td>reflect well, badly, etc. on sb/sth</td><td>使显得好（或坏）；给人某种印象</td><td>The way the staff handled the complaint reflects well on the whole company.<br>员工处理投诉的方式给整个公司加了分。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reflected</b></td><td>bathe/bask in reflected ˈglory</td><td>沾光；仰仗他人的荣耀</td><td>He basks in reflected glory every time his daughter wins another swimming medal.<br>女儿每次拿游泳奖牌，他都跟着沾光。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reflection</b></td><td>a sad, poor, etc. reflection on sth</td><td>有损…名誉的事；反映出…的不足</td><td>The state of these classrooms is a sad reflection on our education budget.<br>这些教室的状况反映出我们的教育经费有多可怜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on mature reˈflection/consideˈration</td><td>经过深思熟虑之后</td><td>On mature reflection, I've decided not to accept the job in Berlin.<br>经过慎重考虑，我决定不接受柏林那份工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>refresh</b></td><td>reˌfresh sb's/your ˈmemory</td><td>唤起记忆；帮助想起</td><td>Let me refresh your memory — you promised to return the ladder last spring.<br>我提醒你一下，你答应去年春天还梯子的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>regard</b></td><td>have reˈgard to sth (law)</td><td>考虑到；顾及</td><td>The court must have regard to the child's welfare above everything else.<br>法院必须首先顾及孩子的福祉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/with reˈgard to sb/sth (formal)</td><td>关于；对于</td><td>With regard to your complaint, we have already contacted the delivery company.<br>关于您的投诉，我们已联系了配送公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in this/that reˈgard (formal)</td><td>在这一点上；与此相关</td><td>Sales have improved, and in this regard the new website has helped enormously.<br>销售有所好转，在这一点上新网站帮了大忙。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>regards</b></td><td>as regards sb/sth (formal)</td><td>关于；至于</td><td>As regards pay, the union and the management are still far apart.<br>至于薪酬，工会和资方分歧仍然很大。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>region</b></td><td>in the region of</td><td>大约；…左右</td><td>Repairing the roof will cost somewhere in the region of five thousand pounds.<br>修屋顶大概要花五千英镑左右。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>regular</b></td><td>(as) regular as ˈclockwork</td><td>极有规律；准时可靠</td><td>He walks his dog past our window at seven, regular as clockwork.<br>他七点准时遛狗经过我们窗前，从不例外。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rein</b></td><td>give/allow sb/sth free/full ˈrein</td><td>对…不加约束；放手让…去做</td><td>The editor gave her free rein to write about whatever she liked.<br>编辑放手让她想写什么就写什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give/allow free/full ˈrein to sb/sth</td><td>对…放任自由；任其发挥</td><td>Try giving full rein to your imagination instead of just following the instructions.<br>试着放开想象力，别只照着说明走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep a tight ˈrein on sb/sth</td><td>严格控制；管得很紧</td><td>The new manager keeps a tight rein on spending in every single department.<br>新经理对各部门开支管得很紧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reinvent</b></td><td>reinvent the ˈwheel</td><td>重复劳动做无用功；重新发明轮子</td><td>Use the template we already have; there's no need to reinvent the wheel.<br>用现成的模板吧，没必要重复造轮子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>relatively</b></td><td>ˈrelatively speaking</td><td>相对来说；比较而言</td><td>Relatively speaking, this winter has been mild compared with the last one.<br>相对而言，今年冬天比去年暖和。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>religion</b></td><td>get reˈligion (informal, often disapproving)</td><td>突然变得虔诚；皈依宗教</td><td>My cousin got religion after his accident and now volunteers at the church.<br>我表哥出事后突然信教，现在在教堂做义工。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>remember</b></td><td>something to reˈmember sb by (informal)</td><td>给点厉害瞧瞧；惩罚（尤指体罚）</td><td>The bouncer gave him something to remember him by outside the club.<br>保安在夜店门口给了他点厉害瞧瞧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>remembered</b></td><td>be reˈmembered as/for sth</td><td>因…而被人铭记；因…出名</td><td>She will be remembered as the teacher who changed how we taught reading.<br>她会作为改变我们阅读教学方式的老师被人铭记。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>removed</b></td><td>be far/further/furthest reˈmoved from sth</td><td>与…大相径庭；与…毫不相干</td><td>His version of events is far removed from what the witnesses actually saw.<br>他的说法与目击者所见大相径庭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reopen</b></td><td>reopen old ˈwounds</td><td>揭旧疮疤；重提伤心事</td><td>Talking about the trial again would only reopen old wounds for her family.<br>再谈那场官司只会让她家人重揭旧伤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>repair</b></td><td>beyond reˈpair</td><td>无法修复；破损不堪</td><td>The flood damaged the piano beyond repair, so we finally gave it away.<br>洪水把钢琴泡得无法修复，我们最后送人了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in good, bad, etc. reˈpair (also in a good, bad, etc. state of reˈpair) (formal)</td><td>状况良好（或不佳等）；保养得如何</td><td>The cottage is old but the roof and windows are in good repair.<br>这小屋虽旧，但屋顶和窗户保养得不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reserve</b></td><td>in reˈserve</td><td>备用；储备着</td><td>Always keep a bit of cash in reserve for emergencies like this one.<br>总要留点现金备用，以应对这种急事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>residence</b></td><td>in ˈresidence</td><td>驻留的；（在大学等）有正式职位的</td><td>The flag shows that the Queen is in residence at the castle today.<br>旗帜表明女王今天正驻跸城堡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>respect</b></td><td>in reˈspect of sth (formal)</td><td>关于；就…而言</td><td>The company is liable in respect of all damage caused by its lorries.<br>公司须对其卡车造成的一切损失负责。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with (all due) reˈspect (formal)</td><td>恕我直言（委婉表示不同意）</td><td>With all due respect, minister, that figure simply doesn't match our own data.<br>恕我直言，部长，那个数字与我们的数据对不上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with respect to sth (formal)</td><td>关于；至于</td><td>With respect to delivery times, we can offer a same-day service locally.<br>关于送达时间，本地我们可提供当日送达服务。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>respecter</b></td><td>be no respecter of ˈpersons</td><td>一视同仁；不分高低贵贱</td><td>Illness is no respecter of persons; it strikes rich and poor alike.<br>疾病不分贵贱，穷人富人都难幸免。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rest</b></td><td>and the ˈrest (spoken)</td><td>还不止这些；远不止此</td><td>He says the repairs cost two hundred pounds — and the rest!<br>他说修车花了两百镑，远不止吧！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>and (all) the ˈrest (of it) (spoken)</td><td>诸如此类；等等</td><td>She brought maps, snacks, spare socks and all the rest of it.<br>她带了地图、零食、备用袜子等等一大堆东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈrest</td><td>静止不动；安息</td><td>The pendulum finally came to a stop and hung completely at rest.<br>钟摆终于停了下来，一动不动地垂着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come to ˈrest</td><td>停下来；不再移动</td><td>The runaway trolley rolled downhill and came to rest against a lamp post.<br>失控的手推车滑下坡，撞在路灯柱上停住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for the ˈrest (BrE, formal)</td><td>至于其他；除此之外</td><td>The kitchen needs work; for the rest, the house is in decent shape.<br>厨房需要整修，除此之外房子状况还不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(why don't you) give it a ˈrest! (BrE, spoken)</td><td>别再提了；消停会儿吧</td><td>Give it a rest! You've complained about that neighbour all evening.<br>消停会儿吧，你抱怨那个邻居一整晚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sth a ˈrest (informal)</td><td>暂停；暂时不做</td><td>I'm giving running a rest until my knee stops hurting properly.<br>膝盖不疼了我再跑步，先歇一阵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I ˌrest my ˈcase (spoken, law or humorous)</td><td>我陈述完毕；我的话说完了</td><td>He arrived late again — I rest my case about his timekeeping.<br>他又迟到了，关于他守不守时，我不必多说了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rest asˈsured (that...) (formal)</td><td>尽管放心；请相信</td><td>Rest assured that your parcel will arrive well before the weekend.<br>请放心，您的包裹周末前肯定送到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the rest is ˈhistory</td><td>后来的事大家都知道了</td><td>We met at a bus stop in the rain, and the rest is history.<br>我们在雨中的公交站相遇，后来的事就不用说了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌrest on your ˈlaurels (usually disapproving)</td><td>吃老本；躺在功劳簿上不思进取</td><td>One good season is no reason to rest on your laurels.<br>一个赛季打得好，不是躺平吃老本的理由。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>return</b></td><td>by reˈturn (of ˈpost) (BrE)</td><td>立即回复；下一班邮件即回</td><td>Please send the signed contract back to us by return of post.<br>请在收到后立即将签好的合同寄回。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in reˈturn (for sth)</td><td>作为回报；作为交换</td><td>She fed their cat and got a bottle of wine in return.<br>她帮忙喂猫，得到了一瓶葡萄酒作为回报。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>reˌturn the ˈcompliment</td><td>回敬称赞；报答恩惠</td><td>He praised my cooking, so I returned the compliment about his garden.<br>他夸我做饭好，我就回夸他的花园。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>reˌturn to the ˈfold (literary)</td><td>重返原团体（尤指宗教或政治团体）</td><td>After ten years abroad, the old striker has returned to the fold.<br>在国外踢了十年后，这位老前锋回归了母队。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay sth back/return sth with ˈinterest</td><td>加倍偿还；加倍回敬</td><td>They humiliated him last season, and yesterday he returned it with interest.<br>上赛季他们羞辱了他，昨天他加倍奉还。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>revelation</b></td><td>come as/be a reveˈlation (to sb)</td><td>令人大开眼界；出乎意料</td><td>Living without a car for a year came as a revelation to me.<br>一年不开车的生活让我大开眼界。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>reverse</b></td><td>go/put sth into reˈverse</td><td>（使）发生逆转；扭转局面</td><td>The government has put its own housing policy into reverse this month.<br>政府本月把自己的住房政策来了个大转向。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in reˈverse</td><td>相反地；反过来</td><td>Just do the same steps in reverse and the shelf comes apart easily.<br>把步骤倒过来做，架子很容易就拆开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>revert</b></td><td>revert to ˈtype (formal)</td><td>故态复萌；恢复本性</td><td>He behaved for a fortnight, then reverted to type and skipped training again.<br>他老实了两周，就故态复萌，又翘了训练。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rhinoceros</b></td><td>have a hide/skin like a rhiˈnoceros (informal)</td><td>脸皮极厚；不怕别人批评</td><td>You need a skin like a rhinoceros to survive in this newsroom.<br>在这个新闻编辑室待下去，你得脸皮厚得像犀牛皮。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rhyme</b></td><td>there's no ˌrhyme or ˈreason to/for sth</td><td>毫无道理可言；莫名其妙</td><td>There's no rhyme or reason to the way this office allocates parking spaces.<br>这家公司分配车位毫无道理可言。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without ˌrhyme or ˈreason</td><td>毫无缘由；莫名其妙</td><td>She stopped speaking to me without rhyme or reason halfway through the term.<br>学期过半时她莫名其妙就不跟我说话了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ribbons</b></td><td>cut, tear, etc. sth to ˈribbons</td><td>把…撕成碎片；驳得体无完肤</td><td>The wind tore our old tent to ribbons during the night.<br>夜里大风把我们的旧帐篷撕成了碎片。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rich</b></td><td>(as) rich as ˈCroesus (informal)</td><td>极其富有；富可敌国</td><td>His uncle is as rich as Croesus but still drives a rusty van.<br>他叔叔富得流油，却还开着辆生锈的货车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's ˈrich (spoken, especially BrE)</td><td>真是荒唐；亏你说得出口</td><td>He's calling me lazy? That's rich, coming from someone who naps daily.<br>他说我懒？他天天睡午觉，真好意思。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rid</b></td><td>be ˈrid of sb/sth (formal)</td><td>摆脱；除掉</td><td>I'll be glad to be rid of this cough before the holidays.<br>假期前能摆脱这咳嗽，我就谢天谢地了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get ˈrid of sb/sth</td><td>摆脱；丢弃</td><td>We finally got rid of that broken sofa in the spare room.<br>我们终于把客房那张破沙发处理掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>riddance</b></td><td>good ˈriddance (to sb/sth)</td><td>总算摆脱了；谢天谢地走了</td><td>The noisy tenants upstairs have moved out at last — good riddance!<br>楼上吵闹的租客终于搬走了，真是谢天谢地！</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>riddled</b></td><td>be ˈriddled with sth</td><td>充斥；布满（尤指不好的东西）</td><td>The report was riddled with errors and had to be written all over again.<br>报告错误百出，只好重写。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ride</b></td><td>be/go along for the ˈride (informal)</td><td>随大溜；只是凑热闹</td><td>I don't really care who wins; I'm just along for the ride.<br>我其实不在乎谁赢，只是来凑个热闹。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/give sb a rough/an easy ˈride (informal)</td><td>（使）日子难过；（使）一帆风顺</td><td>The new coach had a rough ride from the fans all season.<br>新教练整个赛季都被球迷刁难。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let sth ˈride (informal)</td><td>暂且不管；先放一放</td><td>I noticed the mistake but decided to let it ride for now.<br>我发现了错误，但决定暂时先不追究。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ride the ˈcrest of sth</td><td>处于鼎盛时期；趁势大获成功</td><td>The band is riding the crest of a wave after that festival performance.<br>那场音乐节演出后，乐队正处在事业顶峰。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ride ˈherd on sb/sth (AmE, informal)</td><td>严加监管；盯着管着</td><td>Someone has to ride herd on these interns or nothing ever gets finished.<br>得有人盯着这些实习生，不然什么都做不完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ride ˈroughshod over sb/sth (especially BrE)</td><td>对…横行霸道；轻蔑对待</td><td>The developers rode roughshod over every objection the local residents raised.<br>开发商对当地居民的反对意见全然不顾。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(AmE usually run ˈroughshod over sb/sth)</td><td>对…专横霸道；不予理会</td><td>The manager ran roughshod over the committee and signed the contract himself.<br>经理无视委员会，自己把合同签了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ride ˈshotgun (AmE, informal)</td><td>坐在副驾驶座上</td><td>My little brother always shouts that he gets to ride shotgun.<br>我弟弟总抢着喊要坐副驾驶。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ride a/the ˈwave of sth</td><td>趁…之势；受益于某种潮流</td><td>She rode a wave of public sympathy all the way into the mayor's office.<br>她借着一股民意同情的浪潮当上了市长。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb for a ˈride (informal)</td><td>欺骗；愚弄（某人）</td><td>That mechanic took us for a ride and charged for parts he never fitted.<br>那修车师傅骗了我们，收了根本没装的零件钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/have a ˌbumpy ˈride</td><td>（使）历经波折；日子不好过</td><td>The bill will have a bumpy ride through parliament next month.<br>这项法案下月在议会将历经波折。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>riding</b></td><td>be riding for a ˈfall</td><td>自讨苦吃；蛮干招祸</td><td>Borrowing that much to open a second shop, he's riding for a fall.<br>借那么多钱开第二家店，他这是自找麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>riding ˈhigh</td><td>春风得意；很成功很自信</td><td>The team is riding high after four straight wins away from home.<br>客场四连胜后，球队正春风得意。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>right</b></td><td>as of ˈright (also by ˈright) (formal)</td><td>依法有权；作为合法权利</td><td>Every employee here gets four weeks' paid holiday as of right.<br>这里每位员工依法享有四周带薪假。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's/that's all ˈright</td><td>不用谢；没关系</td><td>That's all right — anyone could have knocked that glass over.<br>没关系，谁都可能碰倒那个杯子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's ˌall right for ˈsome</td><td>有些人就是走运（表示羡慕）</td><td>Three weeks in Italy? It's all right for some, isn't it?<br>去意大利三周？有些人可真走运啊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make (all) the right ˈnoises (informal)</td><td>随声附和；口头上表示支持</td><td>The minister made all the right noises but promised no extra money.<br>部长说得很好听，却没承诺增加一分钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sth ˈright</td><td>纠正；修好</td><td>The plumber came back the next day and put everything right.<br>水管工第二天回来把问题都修好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/set sb ˈright</td><td>纠正某人的错误看法；澄清事实</td><td>I thought the museum opened on Mondays, but she soon put me right.<br>我以为博物馆周一开门，她很快纠正了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>right you ˈare! (BrE, informal)</td><td>好的；就这么办</td><td>Right you are, I'll pick the kids up at four then.<br>好的，那我四点去接孩子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>right and ˈleft • left and ˈright</td><td>到处；处处</td><td>He was handing out free samples right and left outside the station.<br>他在车站外到处派发免费样品。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) right as ˈrain (informal)</td><td>十分健康；恢复如常</td><td>A night's sleep and a hot meal and he'll be right as rain.<br>睡一觉再吃顿热饭，他就好利索了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>right aˈway/ˈoff</td><td>立刻；马上</td><td>Tell the driver to turn round and come back here right away.<br>叫司机马上掉头回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>right eˈnough (spoken)</td><td>的确；不可否认</td><td>It's cold right enough, but at least the rain has finally stopped.<br>确实挺冷，不过雨总算停了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>right ˈnow</td><td>此刻；眼下；立刻</td><td>I can't talk right now — I'm halfway through a job interview.<br>我现在没法说话，正在面试中。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>right ˈon (spoken)</td><td>说得对，好极了；政治观点激进的</td><td>Right on! That's exactly what this neighbourhood has needed for years.<br>说得好！这正是这个社区多年来需要的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌright side ˈup (AmE)</td><td>正面朝上；位置摆正</td><td>Make sure the box stays right side up or the cake will collapse.<br>务必让盒子正面朝上，不然蛋糕会塌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>right a ˈwrong</td><td>纠正错误；弥补过失；平反</td><td>The apology came thirty years late, but it did right an old wrong.<br>道歉迟了三十年，但总算弥补了旧日的过失。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see sb (all) ˈright (AmE also do sb ˈright)</td><td>不亏待某人；保证某人得到应得的</td><td>Help me move the piano and I'll see you right afterwards.<br>帮我搬钢琴，事后我不会亏待你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈshe'll be right (AustralE, informal)</td><td>没事的；一切都会好起来</td><td>The tyre's a bit flat, but she'll be right for the drive home.<br>轮胎有点瘪，不过开回家没问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>too ˈright/ˈtrue (informal)</td><td>太对了；一点不假</td><td>Too right the tickets are overpriced — I'm not paying that again.<br>票价确实太贵了，我不会再花这钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>would ˌgive your right ˈarm for sth/to do sth</td><td>为…不惜一切代价</td><td>I'd give my right arm for a quiet weekend with no phone calls.<br>我愿付出一切换一个没有电话打扰的周末。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in the same/right ˈballpark</td><td>数额（或水平）大致相当</td><td>Their offer and ours are at least in the same ballpark now.<br>他们的报价和我们的现在总算差不多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>right-hand</b></td><td>your ˌright-hand ˈman (informal)</td><td>得力助手；左右手</td><td>For twenty years he was the director's right-hand man at the theatre.<br>二十年来，他一直是剧院院长的得力助手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rights</b></td><td>by ˈrights</td><td>按理说；理应</td><td>By rights that promotion should have gone to someone with more experience.<br>按理说，那次升职应该给更有经验的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/set sth to ˈrights</td><td>纠正（不公）；收拾整顿</td><td>It took the new head two years to put the school to rights.<br>新校长花了两年才把学校整顿好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>within your ˈrights</td><td>有权（这样做）</td><td>You're perfectly within your rights to ask for a written receipt.<br>你完全有权索要书面收据。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>riled</b></td><td>be/get (all) ˌriled ˈup (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>十分生气；非常恼火</td><td>Don't get all riled up about a parking ticket; just pay it.<br>别为一张罚单气成这样，交了就是。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ring</b></td><td>give sb a ˈring (BrE, informal)</td><td>给某人打电话</td><td>Give me a ring when you get home so I stop worrying.<br>你到家给我打个电话，我好放心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ring a ˈbell (informal)</td><td>听起来耳熟；引起模糊的回忆</td><td>That name rings a bell, but I can't picture his face at all.<br>这名字听着耳熟，可我完全想不起他长什么样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ring the ˈchanges (on sth) (BrE)</td><td>变换花样；使更多样</td><td>She rings the changes on the same three recipes all winter long.<br>整个冬天她就靠那三个菜谱变着花样做。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ring in your ˈears/ˈhead</td><td>在耳边回响；言犹在耳</td><td>His warning about the deadline was still ringing in my ears.<br>他关于截止日期的警告仍在我耳边回响。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ring off the ˈhook (AmE)</td><td>（电话）铃声不断；被打爆</td><td>The phone has been ringing off the hook since the story went online.<br>报道上线后，电话就没停过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ring out the ˌold (year) and ˌring in the ˈnew</td><td>辞旧迎新</td><td>We gather on the hill each December to ring out the old and ring in the new.<br>每年十二月我们都聚在山上辞旧迎新。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌring in the ˈnew</td><td>迎新；迎接新的一年</td><td>Fireworks over the harbour will ring in the new year at midnight.<br>午夜港口的烟花将迎来新年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ring ˈtrue/ˈfalse/ˈhollow</td><td>听起来真实（或虚假、空洞）</td><td>His apology didn't ring true to anyone who had heard the recording.<br>听过录音的人都觉得他的道歉不真诚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the brass ˈring (AmE)</td><td>成功的良机；难得的机会</td><td>She grabbed the brass ring and moved to New York at twenty-two.<br>她抓住良机，二十二岁就搬去了纽约。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rings</b></td><td>run ˈrings around/round sb/sth (informal)</td><td>远胜于；使相形见绌</td><td>The young winger ran rings around their defence for ninety minutes.<br>这位年轻边锋九十分钟里把对方后防耍得团团转。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ringside</b></td><td>have a ringside ˈseat/ˈview (informal)</td><td>处于绝佳观看位置；近距离目睹</td><td>Living opposite the town hall, we had a ringside seat for the protest.<br>住在市政厅对面，我们近距离目睹了这场抗议。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>riot</b></td><td>run ˈriot</td><td>撒野失控；（想象等）放任驰骋</td><td>The children ran riot in the garden while their parents chatted indoors.<br>父母在屋里聊天，孩子们在花园里撒了欢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rip</b></td><td>let sth ˈrip (informal)</td><td>使（车、船等）全速前进</td><td>Once we hit the motorway he let the old van rip.<br>一上高速，他就让那辆旧货车撒开了跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let ˈrip (at sb) (with sth) (informal)</td><td>尽情发泄；毫无顾忌地大讲（或大干）</td><td>She let rip at the council about the terrible state of the roads.<br>她对着议会大吐苦水，痛批路况糟糕。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rip sb/sth aˈpart/to ˈshreds, ˈbits, etc.</td><td>撕碎；猛烈抨击</td><td>The reviewers ripped his second album to shreds within a single day.<br>乐评人一天之内就把他的第二张专辑批得体无完肤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ripe</b></td><td>at/to a ˈripe old age • at/to the ripe old age of...</td><td>活到高龄</td><td>Her grandfather kept cycling to market to a ripe old age.<br>她祖父到了高龄还骑车去赶集。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ripple</b></td><td>a ˈripple effect</td><td>涟漪效应；连锁反应</td><td>One factory closing had a ripple effect on shops across the whole town.<br>一家工厂关闭，对全镇商铺产生了连锁反应。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rise</b></td><td>get a ˈrise out of sb</td><td>故意惹恼某人；逗某人发火</td><td>He only says that to get a rise out of his sister.<br>他那么说只是为了逗他姐姐上火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get a ˈrise out of sb (informal)</td><td>把某人惹火；逗某人急眼</td><td>She always got a rise out of him by copying his strong accent.<br>她总学他的口音说话，把他惹得发火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give ˈrise to sth (formal)</td><td>引起；导致</td><td>The delay gave rise to rumours that the project had been cancelled.<br>延期引发了项目已被取消的传言。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rise and ˈshine (old-fashioned)</td><td>快起床；起来活动啦</td><td>Rise and shine! The bus to the airport leaves in forty minutes.<br>快起床！去机场的车四十分钟后就走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌrise from the ˈashes</td><td>东山再起；浴火重生</td><td>The club rose from the ashes of bankruptcy and won promotion twice.<br>俱乐部从破产中重生，两次冲级成功。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rise to the ˈbait</td><td>上钩；中圈套</td><td>He teased her about her cooking, but she refused to rise to the bait.<br>他拿她做的饭打趣，她却不上他的当。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rise to the ocˈcasion/ˈchallenge</td><td>从容应对难局；不负所望</td><td>The understudy rose to the occasion and got a standing ovation.<br>替补演员临场发挥出色，赢得全场起立鼓掌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rising</b></td><td>a rising ˌtide lifts all ˈboats (saying, especially AmE) (politics)</td><td>水涨船高；经济向好人人受益</td><td>The mayor argued that a rising tide lifts all boats in the local economy.<br>市长认为地方经济好转会让所有人受益。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>risk</b></td><td>at ˈrisk (from/of sth)</td><td>处境危险；面临…的风险</td><td>Thousands of homes are at risk of flooding along this stretch of coast.<br>这段海岸沿线有数千户住宅面临水淹风险。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at the ˈrisk of doing sth</td><td>冒着…的风险（引出可能冒犯的话）</td><td>At the risk of sounding rude, that shirt really doesn't suit you.<br>恕我直言，那件衬衫真的不适合你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at risk to yourself/sb/sth</td><td>冒着伤害自己（或他人）的危险</td><td>He pulled the driver out at considerable risk to himself.<br>他冒着极大危险把司机拖了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth at your ˌown ˈrisk</td><td>风险自担；后果自负</td><td>You can swim beyond the buoys, but you do so at your own risk.<br>你可以游到浮标外，但风险自担。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>risk life and limb</td><td>冒生命危险；不惜受伤</td><td>Firefighters risk life and limb every time that alarm goes off.<br>每次警铃响起，消防员都冒着生命危险。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>risk your ˈneck (informal)</td><td>冒极大的风险</td><td>I'm not risking my neck climbing that ladder in this wind.<br>这么大风，我可不冒险爬那梯子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run the ˈrisk (of doing sth) • run ˈrisks</td><td>冒…的风险；冒险行事</td><td>Post it today or you run the risk of missing her birthday.<br>今天就寄，不然可能赶不上她的生日。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run the ˈrisk (of sth)</td><td>冒…的风险；担…的危险</td><td>We don't want to run the risk of losing their business over this.<br>我们不想冒因此丢掉这笔生意的风险。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a ˈrisk • take ˈrisks</td><td>冒险（做某事）</td><td>Every investor has to take risks; the trick is choosing which ones.<br>投资人都得冒险，关键是选对哪些险值得冒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>riveted</b></td><td>be ˌriveted to the ˈspot/ˈground</td><td>呆立不动；吓得挪不开步</td><td>I was riveted to the spot when the bear stepped onto the path.<br>熊走上小路时，我吓得动弹不得。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>road</b></td><td>off the ˈroad</td><td>（汽车）不能上路；需要送修</td><td>My car's been off the road for a fortnight waiting for a part.<br>我的车等零件已经趴窝两周了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈroad</td><td>在途中；（尤指）在长途巡演旅行中</td><td>The band has been on the road for eight months without a break.<br>乐队已连续巡演了八个月没休息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˌroad to reˈcovery, ˈstardom, etc.</td><td>走在康复（或成名等）的路上</td><td>After the operation she's firmly on the road to recovery now.<br>手术后她正稳步走向康复。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˌroad to ˈruin, diˈsaster, etc.</td><td>走向毁灭（或灾难等）</td><td>Borrowing more to cover old debts puts you on the road to ruin.<br>借新债还旧债只会把你推向毁灭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one for the ˈroad (spoken)</td><td>（临走前的）最后一杯酒</td><td>Stay for one for the road before you head off into the snow.<br>走进雪地前，再喝一杯上路酒吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈroad hog (informal, disapproving)</td><td>占道行驶的莽撞司机</td><td>Some road hog overtook us on the bend and nearly caused a crash.<br>有个莽撞司机在弯道超车，差点撞上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the road to ˌhell is paved with good inˈtentions (saying)</td><td>光有善意无用；好心未必办成好事</td><td>He meant to help, but the road to hell is paved with good intentions.<br>他本想帮忙，可空有好意于事无补。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>good inˈtentions</td><td>良好的意愿；未付诸行动的善意</td><td>The charity was built on good intentions but almost no practical planning.<br>这家慈善机构全凭一腔善意，几乎没有实际规划。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>roaring</b></td><td>do a roaring ˈtrade (in sth) (informal)</td><td>生意兴隆；买卖火爆</td><td>The umbrella sellers did a roaring trade during yesterday's sudden downpour.<br>昨天突降暴雨，卖伞的生意火爆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌroaring ˈdrunk</td><td>酩酊大醉；醉后撒酒疯</td><td>He came home roaring drunk and woke the entire street singing.<br>他烂醉如泥地回家，唱歌吵醒了整条街。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>roasting</b></td><td>give sb/get a ˈroasting (informal)</td><td>严厉批评；挨一顿臭骂</td><td>The goalkeeper got a roasting from his manager at half-time.<br>守门员中场休息时被主教练痛骂了一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rob</b></td><td>ˌrob sb ˈblind (informal)</td><td>骗取某人大量钱财；向某人漫天要价</td><td>That garage robbed us blind over a simple exhaust repair.<br>那家修车行修个排气管就把我们宰惨了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌrob the ˈcradle (AmE, informal)</td><td>老牛吃嫩草（与年龄小很多的人交往）</td><td>His new girlfriend is twenty-three — everyone says he's robbing the cradle.<br>他新女友才二十三，大家都说他老牛吃嫩草。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈcradle-rob (AmE) (BrE ˈcradle-snatch) verb</td><td>与比自己年轻很多的人恋爱</td><td>Stop teasing me about cradle-robbing; she's only four years younger.<br>别再拿老牛吃嫩草打趣我了，她才小四岁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈcradle-robber (AmE) (BrE ˈcradle-snatcher)</td><td>与年轻得多的人恋爱的人</td><td>His friends jokingly call him a cradle-robber whenever she picks him up.<br>每次她来接他，朋友们都开玩笑叫他老牛吃嫩草。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌrob Peter to pay ˈPaul (saying)</td><td>拆东墙补西墙；借新债还旧账</td><td>Paying the credit card with another loan is just robbing Peter to pay Paul.<br>用另一笔贷款还信用卡，纯属拆东墙补西墙。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>robinson</b></td><td>before you can say Jack ˈRobinson (old-fashioned)</td><td>转眼之间；一眨眼工夫</td><td>Before you could say Jack Robinson, the whole cake had disappeared.<br>一眨眼工夫，整个蛋糕就没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rock</b></td><td>(caught/stuck) between a ˌrock and a ˈhard place</td><td>左右为难；进退维谷</td><td>Caught between a rock and a hard place, she resigned rather than choose.<br>进退两难之下，她索性辞职了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hit</b></td><td>hit ˌrock ˈbottom</td><td>跌至谷底；降到最低水平</td><td>House prices in the village hit rock bottom two winters ago.<br>村里的房价在两个冬天前跌到了谷底。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌrock ˈbottom</td><td>谷底；最低点</td><td>I really hit rock bottom after my marriage broke up last spring.<br>去年春天婚姻破裂后，我的人生跌到了谷底。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌrock-ˈbottom adj.</td><td>（价格等）最低的</td><td>For rock-bottom prices on sofas, come to MacArthur's Furniture this weekend.<br>要买最便宜的沙发，本周末来麦克阿瑟家具店。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rock the ˈboat (informal)</td><td>捣乱惹事；打破现状</td><td>Nobody wanted to rock the boat so close to the merger.<br>合并在即，谁也不想惹事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rocker</b></td><td>ˌoff your ˈrocker (informal, spoken, especially BrE)</td><td>疯了；精神失常</td><td>You're off your rocker if you think I'm cycling home in this.<br>这种天气你以为我会骑车回家？你疯了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rocket</b></td><td>give sb a ˈrocket (BrE, informal)</td><td>严厉批评；痛骂</td><td>The editor gave the whole team a rocket over that front-page mistake.<br>编辑因头版那个错误把全组痛骂了一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's not ˈrocket science</td><td>这并不难；没那么复杂</td><td>Changing a tyre isn't rocket science; I'll show you in five minutes.<br>换轮胎不难，我五分钟就能教会你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you don't have to be a ˈrocket scientist (to do sth)</td><td>用不着多聪明就懂；显而易见</td><td>You don't have to be a rocket scientist to see this plan will fail.<br>用不着多聪明也能看出这个计划会失败。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it doesn't take a ˈrocket scientist (to do sth)</td><td>谁都能明白；不需要什么高智商</td><td>It doesn't take a rocket scientist to work out why the shop closed.<br>谁都能想明白那家店为什么关门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rocks</b></td><td>on the ˈrocks</td><td>陷于困境；濒临破裂</td><td>Their marriage was on the rocks long before he moved to Leeds.<br>他搬去利兹之前，他们的婚姻早就摇摇欲坠了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rod</b></td><td>make a rod for your own ˈback</td><td>自讨苦吃；自惹麻烦</td><td>By doing his homework for him you're making a rod for your own back.<br>替他写作业，你这是自找麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rogues</b></td><td>a ˌrogues' ˈgallery (informal, humorous)</td><td>罪犯照片档案；一群坏家伙</td><td>The pub wall was covered with a rogues' gallery of old regulars.<br>酒吧墙上贴满了老主顾们的搞怪照片。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>roll</b></td><td>be on a ˈroll (informal)</td><td>接连获胜；连交好运</td><td>Don't stop her now — she's on a roll with these sales calls.<br>别打断她，她这几通销售电话正顺风顺水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈroll on...! (BrE, spoken)</td><td>…快点到来吧</td><td>Roll on Friday — I've had quite enough of this week already.<br>周五快来吧，这一周我已经受够了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>roll up your ˈsleeves (informal)</td><td>摩拳擦掌；准备大干一场</td><td>We rolled up our sleeves and cleared the flooded cellar before lunch.<br>我们撸起袖子，午饭前把淹水的地窖清理干净了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>roll with the ˈpunches</td><td>顺势应对；随机应变挺过困境</td><td>Freelancing teaches you to roll with the punches when clients suddenly disappear.<br>做自由职业让你学会在客户突然消失时随机应变。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rolled</b></td><td>(all) rolled into ˈone</td><td>集于一身；合为一体</td><td>She's our accountant, receptionist and marketing team all rolled into one.<br>她一个人兼任会计、前台和市场部。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rolling</b></td><td>ˌrolling in the ˈaisles (informal)</td><td>笑得前仰后合</td><td>His impression of the head teacher had us rolling in the aisles.<br>他模仿校长，把我们笑得前仰后合。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be) ˈrolling in it/money (informal)</td><td>非常富有；财源滚滚</td><td>They're absolutely rolling in it since they sold that patent last year.<br>自从去年卖掉那项专利，他们富得流油。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a rolling ˈstone (gathers no ˈmoss) (saying)</td><td>滚石不生苔；转业不聚财</td><td>He's changed jobs six times — a rolling stone gathers no moss.<br>他换了六份工作，真是滚石不生苔。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rooftops</b></td><td>shout, etc. sth from the ˈrooftops/ˈhousetops</td><td>到处张扬；大肆宣扬</td><td>She got the job and wanted to shout it from the rooftops.<br>她拿到了工作，恨不得四处宣扬。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>room</b></td><td>no room to swing a ˈcat (informal)</td><td>地方极其狭小；转不开身</td><td>The kitchen in that flat has no room to swing a cat.<br>那套公寓的厨房小得转不开身。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈcat-o'-nine-tails</td><td>九尾鞭（旧时鞭打水手的刑具）</td><td>Sailors who stole from the stores were flogged with a cat-o'-nine-tails.<br>偷仓库东西的水手会被九尾鞭抽打。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>root</b></td><td>get to the ˈroot of sth</td><td>追根溯源；查明根本原因</td><td>The engineer spent all morning getting to the root of the heating problem.<br>工程师花了一上午查明供暖问题的根源。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>root and ˈbranch</td><td>彻底地；连根拔除地</td><td>The new director reformed the department root and branch within a year.<br>新主任一年内对部门进行了彻底改革。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌroot ˈcause (of sth)</td><td>（…的）根本原因；起因</td><td>Poor drainage was the root cause of the damp in these old houses.<br>排水不畅是这些老房子潮湿的根本原因。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈroot</td><td>扎根；确立；深入人心</td><td>The idea of a village library slowly took root over several years.<br>办村图书馆的想法几年间慢慢扎下了根。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>roots</b></td><td>put down (new) ˈroots</td><td>扎根；安顿下来</td><td>After years of moving, they finally put down roots in a seaside town.<br>漂泊多年后，他们终于在一个海边小镇安顿下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pull up ˈstakes (AmE) (BrE up ˈsticks)</td><td>拔营迁居；举家搬走</td><td>They pulled up stakes and drove west with everything in one van.<br>他们举家迁走，一辆货车装下全部家当，一路西行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rope</b></td><td>give sb enough ˈrope (and he'll/she'll ˈhang himself/herself) (saying)</td><td>任其自作自受；听任自取灭亡</td><td>Say nothing and give him enough rope — he'll expose himself soon enough.<br>什么都别说，由着他去，他很快会露馅。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈropes (informal)</td><td>濒于失败；处境岌岌可危</td><td>The company was on the ropes until that unexpected order finally arrived.<br>在那笔意外订单到来前，公司几乎撑不下去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>show sb/learn/know the ˈropes (informal)</td><td>指点门道；学会（或掌握）诀窍</td><td>Sam will show you the ropes during your first week here.<br>第一周山姆会带你熟悉门道。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rose</b></td><td>a ˈrose by any other name (would smell as ˈsweet) (saying)</td><td>名称无关紧要，本质才重要</td><td>Call it a cottage or a shack — a rose by any other name.<br>管它叫小屋还是棚子，叫法不重要。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>roses</b></td><td>be all ˈroses • be a bed of ˈroses (also be ˌroses, ˌroses all the ˈway) (informal)</td><td>一帆风顺；称心如意</td><td>Running your own café is not a bed of roses, believe me.<br>自己开咖啡馆可不是什么美差，相信我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>everything's coming up ˈroses (informal)</td><td>一切顺利；事事如意</td><td>Since she started that course, everything's coming up roses for her.<br>自从上了那门课，她事事顺心。</td></tr>
