<tr><td></td><td>put the ˈroses back in your cheeks (BrE, informal)</td><td>使脸色红润；使恢复气色</td><td>A fortnight in the mountains will put the roses back in your cheeks.<br>在山里待两周会让你恢复好气色。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rosy</b></td><td>everything in the ˈgarden is lovely/rosy (BrE, saying)</td><td>一切都很美好；诸事顺遂</td><td>They smile for photographs as if everything in the garden is rosy.<br>他们对着镜头微笑，好像一切都很美好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rot</b></td><td>the rot sets ˈin</td><td>情况开始变坏</td><td>The rot set in when their best two players left the club.<br>两名主力离队后，情况就开始一路下滑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rotten</b></td><td>a bad/rotten ˈapple</td><td>害群之马；坏分子</td><td>One rotten apple in the team can spoil the mood for everyone.<br>队里一个害群之马就能坏了所有人的心情。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rough</b></td><td>cut up ˈrough/ˈnasty (informal)</td><td>发怒；翻脸；露出凶相</td><td>The landlord cut up rough when we asked about the broken boiler.<br>我们一问锅炉坏了的事，房东就翻了脸。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈrough (especially BrE)</td><td>粗略地；打草稿地</td><td>Sketch the layout in rough first, then we'll decide on the colours.<br>先粗略画出布局，然后再定颜色。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>live/sleep ˈrough</td><td>露宿街头；过流浪生活</td><td>He slept rough for two winters before the charity found him a flat.<br>慈善机构给他找到公寓前，他露宿了两个冬天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌrough and ˈready</td><td>粗陋但实用的；将就能用的</td><td>The shelter was rough and ready but it kept us completely dry.<br>那个棚子简陋，却让我们一点没淋着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rough and ˈtumble</td><td>混战；激烈无序的竞争</td><td>He enjoys the rough and tumble of local politics far too much.<br>他太享受地方政治的这种混战了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌrough ˈdiamond (BrE) (AmE a ˌdiamond in the ˈrough)</td><td>外粗内秀的人；未经雕琢的璞玉</td><td>Our foreman is a rough diamond — blunt, but kinder than anyone here.<br>我们工头外粗内秀，说话冲，心却最善。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rough ˈedges</td><td>瑕疵；美中不足之处</td><td>The performance still has a few rough edges, but the energy is wonderful.<br>演出还有些瑕疵，但活力十足。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌrough end of the ˈpineapple (AustralE, informal)</td><td>受到不公正对待；吃亏的一方</td><td>Casual workers always get the rough end of the pineapple in these deals.<br>这类协议里，临时工总是吃亏的一方。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈrough it (informal)</td><td>将就着过；暂时过艰苦生活</td><td>We roughed it in a tent for a fortnight and loved every minute.<br>我们在帐篷里将就了两周，却乐在其中。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˌrough with the ˈsmooth</td><td>甘苦与共；好坏都能接受</td><td>Farming means taking the rough with the smooth, year after year.<br>务农就得年复一年地承受好年景和坏年景。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>round</b></td><td>in round ˈfigures/ˈnumbers</td><td>以整数计；大约</td><td>In round figures, the repairs will cost us about three thousand pounds.<br>取整来说，修理大概要花三千英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌround aˈbout</td><td>在附近；在周围</td><td>There are three good pubs round about, all within ten minutes' walk.<br>附近有三家不错的酒馆，走十分钟都能到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌround ˈhere</td><td>在这附近；这一带</td><td>Nobody locks their bikes round here, which surprised me at first.<br>这一带没人锁自行车，起初让我很吃惊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌround ˈrobin</td><td>圆形联名信；循环赛</td><td>The staff sent a round robin asking for the canteen to reopen.<br>员工联名递交请愿书，要求食堂重新开放。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stand a ˈround (of drinks)</td><td>请一轮酒；做东请大家喝一杯</td><td>It's my birthday, so I'll stand a round for everyone at the bar.<br>今天我生日，吧台这边我请一轮。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rounds</b></td><td>do the ˈrounds (of sth) (BrE) (also make the ˈrounds AmE, BrE)</td><td>巡视；逐一走访；四处流传</td><td>The nurse does the rounds of every ward before the doctors arrive.<br>护士在医生到来前会巡视每个病房。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>route</b></td><td>en ˈroute (from French)</td><td>在途中；在路上</td><td>We stopped for coffee en route to the airport and nearly missed check-in.<br>去机场路上我们停下喝咖啡，差点误了值机。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>row</b></td><td>in a ˈrow</td><td>连续地；接连地</td><td>That's the fourth Monday in a row he's turned up late.<br>这是他连续第四个周一迟到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rub</b></td><td>rub sb's ˈnose in it (also rub it ˈin) (informal)</td><td>老揭人短处；反复提及某人的过失</td><td>Yes, I got the answer wrong — do you have to rub it in?<br>是，我答错了，你非得反复提吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rub ˈsalt into the wound/into sb's wounds</td><td>往伤口上撒盐；使雪上加霜</td><td>Losing was bad enough; his laughing rubbed salt into the wound.<br>输了就够难受了，他还笑，简直是往伤口上撒盐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rub ˈshoulders with sb (AmE also rub ˈelbows with sb) (informal)</td><td>与（名人、富人等）交往接触</td><td>At that gallery opening she rubbed shoulders with three famous novelists.<br>在那次画廊开幕式上，她与三位著名小说家有了交往。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rub sb up the ˈwrong way (BrE) (AmE rub sb the wrong ˈway) (informal)</td><td>无意中惹恼某人；让人不舒服</td><td>Something about his cheerful voice rubs me up the wrong way.<br>他那副欢快的声音总让我莫名不爽。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there is/lies the ˈrub (formal or humorous)</td><td>问题就在这里；难处正在于此</td><td>We need money to make money — and there lies the rub.<br>要赚钱先得有钱，难处就在这儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rude</b></td><td>a rude aˈwakening (written)</td><td>猛然醒悟；残酷的现实教训</td><td>First-year students get a rude awakening when the exam results appear.<br>考试成绩一出来，大一新生就猛然清醒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ruffle</b></td><td>ruffle sb's/a few ˈfeathers (informal)</td><td>惹恼某人；引起不安</td><td>Her blunt speech ruffled a few feathers among the older committee members.<br>她直言不讳的发言惹恼了几位年长的委员。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ruins</b></td><td>in ˈruins</td><td>成为废墟；彻底垮掉</td><td>One careless email left his twenty-year career completely in ruins.<br>一封粗心的邮件毁了他二十年的职业生涯。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rule</b></td><td>as a (general) ˈrule</td><td>通常；一般来说</td><td>As a general rule, we don't answer emails after seven in the evening.<br>一般来说，我们晚上七点后不回邮件。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make it a ˈrule to do sth</td><td>总是做某事；使之成为习惯</td><td>I make it a rule to walk the dog before breakfast every day.<br>我总是坚持早饭前遛狗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a rule of ˈthumb</td><td>经验法则；粗略的估算方法</td><td>As a rule of thumb, allow one hour of cooking per kilo.<br>按经验法则，每公斤肉烤一小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rule the ˈroost (informal)</td><td>当家作主；主宰一切</td><td>In that kitchen the head chef's mother still rules the roost.<br>在那间厨房里，主厨的母亲仍然说了算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>rule (sb/sth) with a rod of ˈiron/with an ˈiron hand</td><td>实行铁腕统治；严格管制</td><td>The old headmaster ruled the school with a rod of iron.<br>老校长以铁腕手段管理学校。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rules</b></td><td>bend/stretch the ˈrules</td><td>变通规则；通融一下</td><td>The librarian bent the rules and let me keep the book longer.<br>图书管理员通融了一下，让我多借几天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play by sb's ˈrules • play by your own ˈrules</td><td>按某人的规矩办事；自行其是</td><td>If you join his company, you play by his rules or leave.<br>进了他的公司，要么按他的规矩来，要么走人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play by your own ˈrules</td><td>自定规矩；我行我素</td><td>That director plays by her own rules and still wins every award.<br>那位导演我行我素，却照样拿遍大奖。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play by the ˈrules</td><td>按规则办事；处事公正诚实</td><td>He played by the rules his whole career and never once cheated.<br>他整个职业生涯都按规矩办事，从没作过弊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the rules of the ˈgame</td><td>游戏规则；公认的行为准则</td><td>Late payment is just part of the rules of the game in publishing.<br>拖延付款在出版界就是游戏规则的一部分。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>run</b></td><td>give sb/get/have the ˈrun of sth (informal)</td><td>获准随意使用；可自由出入</td><td>While they're away we have the run of their entire house.<br>他们不在的时候，整栋房子随我们用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈrun</td><td>在逃；被追捕</td><td>The pair were on the run for six weeks before police caught them.<br>两人在逃六周后被警方抓获。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈrun for it (informal)</td><td>快跑；赶紧逃</td><td>When the alarm went off we grabbed our coats and ran for it.<br>警报一响，我们抓起外套就跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>runaround</b></td><td>give sb the ˈrunaround (informal)</td><td>敷衍搪塞；踢皮球</td><td>The insurance company gave me the runaround for three whole months.<br>保险公司跟我踢了整整三个月皮球。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>run-in</b></td><td>have a ˈrun-in with sb (informal)</td><td>与某人争执；发生冲突</td><td>I had a run-in with the traffic warden about parking on Tuesday.<br>周二我为停车的事跟交警吵了一架。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>runner</b></td><td>do a ˈrunner (BrE, informal)</td><td>溜之大吉；（干坏事后）逃走</td><td>Two of them did a runner without paying for the meal.<br>他们中两个没付饭钱就溜了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>running</b></td><td>come ˈrunning</td><td>立刻赶来；欣然从命</td><td>He only has to whistle and she comes running every single time.<br>他一声招呼，她每次都马上跑来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/out of the ˈrunning (for sth) (informal)</td><td>有（或没有）获胜的机会</td><td>Two more goals and we're back in the running for the cup.<br>再进两球，我们就重新有望夺杯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make the ˈrunning (BrE, informal)</td><td>带头；引领节奏</td><td>Small local firms are making the running in solar panel installation.<br>在太阳能板安装方面，本地小公司走在了前头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a running ˈbattle</td><td>持续的争斗；旷日持久的争论</td><td>The council and residents have fought a running battle over the car park.<br>议会与居民为停车场问题长期争执不下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a running ˈjump (old-fashioned, spoken)</td><td>滚开；一边儿待着去</td><td>He asked to borrow money again, so I told him to take a running jump.<br>他又来借钱，我叫他哪儿凉快哪儿待着去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌup and ˈrunning</td><td>正常运转；顺利运行起来</td><td>The new website should be up and running by the end of March.<br>新网站三月底前应该就能正常运行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>run-of-the-mill</b></td><td>ˌrun-of-the-ˈmill (often disapproving)</td><td>普通的；平庸乏味的</td><td>It was a run-of-the-mill hotel with tiny rooms and weak coffee.<br>那是家普通的酒店，房间很小，咖啡很淡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rush</b></td><td>have a rush of blood to the ˈhead (humorous)</td><td>一时冲动；头脑发热</td><td>He had a rush of blood to the head and bought the motorbike.<br>他头脑一热，把那辆摩托车买下了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/get the ˌbum's ˈrush (informal)</td><td>被撵走；被草草打发</td><td>They gave the heckler the bum's rush before the speech even started.<br>演讲还没开始，起哄的人就被轰了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rushed</b></td><td>be/get run/rushed off your ˈfeet</td><td>忙得团团转；忙得脚不沾地</td><td>The café staff were run off their feet all through the bank holiday.<br>整个公休假期，咖啡馆员工都忙得脚不沾地。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rut</b></td><td>in a ˈrut</td><td>墨守成规；一成不变</td><td>Ten years in the same office and I'm stuck in a rut.<br>在同一间办公室待了十年，我的生活一成不变。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in a ˈrut</td><td>生活刻板无变化；停滞不前</td><td>I suddenly realised I'd been in a rut for years: same job, same everything.<br>我忽然意识到自己多年一成不变：同样的工作，同样的一切。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sack</b></td><td>give sb/get the ˈsack (informal)</td><td>解雇；被炒鱿鱼</td><td>He got the sack for turning up drunk on a Monday morning.<br>他因周一早上醉醺醺来上班被炒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sackcloth</b></td><td>put on, wear, etc. ˌsackcloth and ˈashes</td><td>忏悔；痛悔认错</td><td>There's no need for sackcloth and ashes; just apologise and move on.<br>用不着痛哭流涕地忏悔，道个歉往前走就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sacred</b></td><td>nothing is ˈsacred</td><td>毫无禁忌；什么都敢拿来开玩笑</td><td>In this comedy club nothing is sacred, not even the mayor's funeral.<br>在这家喜剧俱乐部没有禁忌，连市长的葬礼都能拿来说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a sacred ˈcow (disapproving)</td><td>神圣不可冒犯的人（或制度、信念）</td><td>The free bus pass has become a sacred cow no politician dares touch.<br>免费公交卡成了没有政客敢碰的神圣之物。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>saddle</b></td><td>be in the ˈsaddle</td><td>在位掌权；当家负责</td><td>With the founder back in the saddle, the company changed direction quickly.<br>创始人重新掌权后，公司很快改变了方向。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>safe</b></td><td>play (it) ˈsafe</td><td>稳妥行事；谨慎不冒险</td><td>Let's play it safe and book the earlier train to Manchester.<br>我们稳妥点，订去曼彻斯特那趟早一些的火车吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsafe and ˈsound</td><td>安然无恙；平安无事</td><td>All four climbers were found safe and sound the following morning.<br>四名登山者第二天早上都被安然找到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) safe as ˈhouses (BrE)</td><td>非常安全；毫无风险</td><td>He said the investment was as safe as houses, and it wasn't.<br>他说这项投资绝对安全，结果并非如此。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a safe ˈbet (informal)</td><td>十拿九稳的事；有把握的选择</td><td>Ordering the fish here is always a safe bet on a Friday.<br>周五在这儿点鱼总是没错的选择。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>safe in the knowledge that...</td><td>因确知…而放心；确信…</td><td>She slept well, safe in the knowledge that the tickets were already booked.<br>她睡得很香，因为确信票已经订好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to be on the ˈsafe side</td><td>谨慎起见；以防万一</td><td>Take an umbrella to be on the safe side; the forecast keeps changing.<br>带把伞以防万一，天气预报老在变。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>safety</b></td><td>there's ˌsafety in ˈnumbers (saying)</td><td>人多保险；人多势众</td><td>We walked home together because there's safety in numbers after midnight.<br>我们结伴回家，午夜之后人多才安全。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>said</b></td><td>eˌnough ˈsaid</td><td>无须多讲；不必多言</td><td>He's late again and hasn't called — enough said, really.<br>他又迟到，还不打电话，不必多说了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the less/least said, the ˈbetter (saying)</td><td>少说为妙</td><td>About last night's argument, the less said the better, I think.<br>关于昨晚那场争吵，我看还是少说为妙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's something, not much, etc. to be ˈsaid for sth/for doing sth</td><td>（做）某事有（或没有）好处</td><td>There's something to be said for arriving early and choosing your own seat.<br>早点到、自己挑座位还是有好处的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sth has something, not much, etc. to be ˈsaid for it</td><td>某事有（或没有）可取之处</td><td>Living above the shop has quite a lot to be said for it.<br>住在店铺楼上其实有不少好处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>something, not much, etc. to be ˈsaid for it</td><td>有（或没有）多少可取之处</td><td>The plan is cheap, and there's not much else to be said for it.<br>这方案便宜，除此之外没什么可取之处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not much to be ˈsaid for sth</td><td>某事物没什么可取之处</td><td>There's not much to be said for this book; it's the worst I've read.<br>这本书没什么可标榜的，是我读过最糟的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>when ˌall is said and ˈdone</td><td>说到底；毕竟</td><td>When all is said and done, she did far more good than harm.<br>说到底，她做的好事远多过坏事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you ˈsaid it! (informal)</td><td>一点没错；千真万确</td><td>You said it! This job is way harder than anyone warned us about.<br>可不是嘛！这活儿比谁说的都难得多。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sail</b></td><td>sail close to the ˈwind</td><td>打擦边球；冒险行事（近乎违法）</td><td>He sails close to the wind with his taxes, and one day he'll get caught.<br>他在报税上老打擦边球，早晚得栽跟头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>saint</b></td><td>the patience of a ˈsaint/of ˈJob</td><td>极大的耐心；圣人般的耐性</td><td>You need the patience of a saint to teach thirty toddlers all day.<br>带三十个小娃娃上一整天课，得有圣人般的耐性。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sais</b></td><td>je ne sais quoi /ˌʒə nə seɪ ˈkwɑː/ (from French, often humorous)</td><td>难以言传的独特魅力</td><td>Her cooking has a certain je ne sais quoi that restaurant chefs can never copy.<br>她做的菜有种说不清的味道，大厨都学不来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sake</b></td><td>for God's, heaven's, pity's, etc. ˈsake</td><td>看在上帝的分上；天哪；行行好</td><td>For God's sake, turn that music down, I'm trying to sleep here!<br>行行好，把音乐关小点，我还想睡觉呢！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(Some people find the use of God here offensive.)</td><td>有人认为这里用 God 一词含冒犯意</td><td>For heaven's sake, watch your language in front of my grandmother.<br>拜托，在我奶奶面前说话注意点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for its ˈown sake</td><td>为其本身的缘故；因其自身价值</td><td>He studies history for its own sake, not to pass any exam.<br>他学历史纯粹是喜欢，不是为了考试。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for the sake of sb/sth • for sb's/sth's sake</td><td>为了…的缘故；为了…着想</td><td>They stayed together for the sake of the children, though both were miserable.<br>两人都过得难受，却为了孩子勉强没分开。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for the sake of ˈargument</td><td>为了便于讨论；姑且假定</td><td>For the sake of argument, let's say the train is delayed by two hours.<br>姑且假定火车晚点两个小时吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>salad</b></td><td>your ˈsalad days (old-fashioned)</td><td>年少不谙世事的岁月；青葱年华</td><td>In my salad days I thought I could change the world overnight.<br>年轻不懂事那会儿，我以为一夜之间就能改变世界。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sale</b></td><td>for ˈsale</td><td>待售；供出售（尤指由物主出售）</td><td>The house next door has been for sale for almost a year now.<br>隔壁那房子挂牌卖了快一年了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈsale</td><td>上市；有售；（美）减价出售</td><td>Tickets go on sale this Friday, so set an alarm on your phone.<br>票周五开售，手机上定个闹钟吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>salt</b></td><td>the salt of the ˈearth</td><td>诚实可靠的人；社会中坚</td><td>Our neighbours drove me to hospital at midnight — they're the salt of the earth.<br>邻居半夜开车送我去医院，真是难得的好人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth with a pinch of ˈsalt</td><td>对…半信半疑；不可全信</td><td>Take his fishing stories with a pinch of salt; he always exaggerates the size.<br>他那些钓鱼故事听听就好，鱼多大他从来都往大了说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>samaritan</b></td><td>a good Saˈmaritan</td><td>乐善好施的人；见义勇为者</td><td>Some good Samaritan found my wallet and posted it back to me.<br>有位好心人捡到我的钱包，还寄了回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>same</b></td><td>all/ˌjust the ˈsame</td><td>尽管如此；仍然</td><td>It rained all weekend, but we had a great time all the same.<br>整个周末都在下雨，可我们还是玩得很开心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(the) ˌsame aˈgain (spoken)</td><td>再来一份同样的（饮料）</td><td>Same again, please, and get one for yourself while you're there.<br>照旧再来一杯，你也给自己来一杯吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsame ˈhere (spoken)</td><td>我也一样；我也是</td><td>'I hate Mondays.' 'Same here, especially when the alarm goes off early.'<br>“我讨厌星期一。”“我也是，尤其闹钟还响得早。”</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(the) ˌsame to ˈyou</td><td>你也一样（回应问候或辱骂）</td><td>'Merry Christmas!' 'And the same to you, love — see you next year.'<br>“圣诞快乐！”“也祝你快乐，明年见。”</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>satisfaction</b></td><td>to sb's satisˈfaction</td><td>令某人满意地</td><td>The builder fixed the leak to my satisfaction, so I paid him immediately.<br>师傅把漏水修得让我很满意，我当场就付了钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈface-saving adj.: face-saving measures</td><td>保全面子的</td><td>The minister announced a face-saving compromise minutes before the vote was due.<br>部长在表决前几分钟宣布了一个保全面子的折中方案。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>save sb's/your (own) ˈneck/ˈskin/ˈhide (informal)</td><td>救某人（或自己）一命；使摆脱困境</td><td>He lied to the boss just to save his own skin.<br>他为了自保，居然对老板撒谎。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>save</b></td><td>save sb or yourself from a dangerous or difficult situation</td><td>使某人（或自己）脱离危险或困境</td><td>She testified against her partner to save her own neck in court.<br>她在法庭上指证同伙，就是为了保住自己。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>saving</b></td><td>a ˌsaving ˈgrace</td><td>唯一可取之处；可弥补缺点的优点</td><td>The film was dull, but the soundtrack was its one saving grace.<br>电影很闷，配乐算是唯一的亮点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>savoir</b></td><td>savoir ˈfaire (from French, approving)</td><td>处世机敏；应付裕如的本领</td><td>He handled the angry customers with real savoir faire and everyone left smiling.<br>他应付那些恼火的顾客游刃有余，人人都是笑着走的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>say</b></td><td>as they ˈsay (also as the saying ˈgoes)</td><td>俗话说；常言道</td><td>Money can't buy happiness, as they say, but it certainly helps a lot.<br>常言道钱买不来幸福，不过确实帮得上大忙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>before you can say Jack ˈRobinson (old-fashioned)</td><td>转瞬间；说时迟那时快</td><td>She grabbed the last cake before you could say Jack Robinson.<br>说时迟那时快，最后一块蛋糕就被她抢走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your ˈsay (informal)</td><td>发表意见；表达看法</td><td>Let everyone have their say before we vote on the new schedule.<br>在表决新排班之前，让大家都说说自己的看法。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have something, nothing, etc. to ˈsay for yourself</td><td>能（或不能）为自己的行为辩解</td><td>You're three hours late — have you nothing to say for yourself?<br>你迟到了三个小时，就没什么话要说吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I ˈmust say (spoken)</td><td>我得说（用于强调看法）</td><td>I must say, that was the best curry I've eaten in years.<br>我得说，这是我这几年吃过最好的咖喱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I ˌwouldn't say ˈno (to sth) (spoken)</td><td>我不反对；乐意来一份</td><td>I wouldn't say no to a cold beer after all that digging.<br>挖了这么半天，来杯冰啤酒我可不会拒绝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>never say ˈdie (saying)</td><td>别气馁；决不放弃</td><td>We're two goals down, but never say die — there's still half an hour.<br>我们落后两球，可别泄气，还有半小时呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈnot to say</td><td>即便不说…；虽不能说…</td><td>His plan was ambitious, not to say completely impossible for a small team.<br>他的计划很有野心，对小团队来说甚至可以说是天方夜谭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>say ˈcheese!</td><td>笑一笑（拍照时用语）</td><td>Everyone squeeze in and say cheese — I want one photo without blinking.<br>大家挤紧点，笑一个，我想拍张没人眨眼的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>say no ˈmore (spoken)</td><td>不用再说了；我明白了</td><td>You want to leave early because of the match? Say no more, mate.<br>你要为看球早走？不用说了，明白。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>say your ˈpiece (informal)</td><td>说出心里话；表明看法</td><td>Let him say his piece, then we can all go home.<br>让他把话说完，然后大家就能回家了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>say ˈwhat? (AmE, spoken)</td><td>你说什么（表示惊讶）</td><td>Say what? You drove all the way to Chicago without a map?<br>你说什么？你没带地图就一路开到芝加哥？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>say ˈwhen</td><td>够了请说一声（倒饮料时用）</td><td>I'm pouring the wine now, so say when and I'll stop.<br>我在倒酒了，够了你就说一声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) say the ˈword</td><td>只要说一声；一声令下</td><td>Just say the word and I'll drive over to help you move.<br>你只要说一声，我就开车过去帮你搬家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that is to ˈsay</td><td>也就是说；换句话说</td><td>He's a night owl, that is to say he never wakes before noon.<br>他是个夜猫子，也就是说中午前从不起床。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˌsay the (very) ˈleast</td><td>至少可以说；说得客气些</td><td>The hotel was disappointing, to say the least, and the staff were rude.<br>那家酒店说得客气些也让人失望，服务员还没礼貌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to say ˈnothing of sth</td><td>更不用说；何况</td><td>The trip cost a fortune, to say nothing of the time we wasted.<br>这趟旅行花了一大笔钱，更别提浪费的时间了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌwhat would/do you ˈsay (to sth/doing sth)?</td><td>你觉得…怎么样；你愿意吗</td><td>What do you say to a walk along the river before dinner tonight?<br>今晚饭前沿河边走走，你觉得怎么样？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>whatever you ˈsay (spoken)</td><td>随你；由你（不想争论）</td><td>Whatever you say — I'm too tired to argue about paint colours tonight.<br>随你吧，今晚我累得懒得为墙漆颜色争。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>who can ˈsay (...)? (spoken)</td><td>谁知道呢；说不准</td><td>Who can say how long this rain will last in the mountains?<br>谁知道山里这场雨要下多久呢？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>who's to ˈsay (...)? (spoken)</td><td>谁说得准呢</td><td>Who's to say she wouldn't have won if she'd trained a bit harder?<br>谁说得准呢，她要是再多练点也许就赢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>he, she, etc. wouldn't say ˌboo to a ˈgoose</td><td>极为羞怯；胆小怕事</td><td>My brother wouldn't say boo to a goose, yet he became a lawyer.<br>我弟弟胆小得不敢跟人红脸，却当上了律师。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you can say ˈthat again! (spoken)</td><td>说得太对了；我完全同意</td><td>'This queue is ridiculous.' 'You can say that again — we've waited an hour.'<br>“这队排得离谱。”“可不是嘛，都等一小时了。”</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you can't say ˈfairer (than ˈthat) (BrE, spoken)</td><td>再公道不过了</td><td>I'll knock fifty pounds off — you can't say fairer than that, mate.<br>我给你便宜五十镑，这够公道了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you don't ˈsay! (spoken, often ironic)</td><td>不会吧；真的吗（亦表毫不意外）</td><td>You don't say! I'd never have guessed he was afraid of heights.<br>真的吗？我可看不出他还恐高。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>saying</b></td><td>it ˌgoes without ˈsaying (that...)</td><td>不言而喻；不用说</td><td>It goes without saying that we'll cover your travel costs for the interview.<br>不用说，面试的路费我们会给你报销。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that ˌgoes without ˈsaying</td><td>那是当然的；不言而喻</td><td>'Will you keep this confidential?' 'That goes without saying, obviously.'<br>“这事你会保密吧？”“那还用说。”</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's/that's not ˈsaying much, etc.</td><td>这说明不了什么；没什么了不起</td><td>He's the tallest in the family, but that's not saying much really.<br>他是家里最高的，不过这也说明不了什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>says /sez/</td><td>say 的第三人称单数，读作 /sez/</td><td>She says the shop opens at nine, so we should leave right now.<br>她说店里九点开门，我们现在就该走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(it) does (eˈxactly) what it says on the ˈtin</td><td>名副其实；与宣传的一样</td><td>This app does exactly what it says on the tin — no ads, no nonsense.<br>这个应用完全名副其实：没广告，不啰嗦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it, etc. says a ˈlot, ˈmuch, etc. about/for sb/sth</td><td>很能说明…的品质（或特点）</td><td>It says a lot about him that he drove four hours to help.<br>他开了四个小时车来帮忙，这很说明他的为人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>who ˈsays (...)? (spoken)</td><td>谁说的（表示不同意）</td><td>Who says men can't dance? Watch my dad at a wedding sometime.<br>谁说男人不会跳舞？改天看看我爸在婚礼上的样子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>say-so</b></td><td>on sb's ˈsay-so</td><td>仅凭某人一句话；经某人许可</td><td>I'm not spending that much on his say-so without seeing the figures.<br>没看到数据，我不会光凭他一句话就花这么多钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scales</b></td><td>the ˌscales fall from sb's ˈeyes (literary)</td><td>恍然大悟；看清真相</td><td>The scales fell from her eyes when she read his old letters.<br>读了他从前的信，她才恍然大悟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scarce</b></td><td>ˌmake yourself ˈscarce (informal)</td><td>躲开；回避；不露面</td><td>Dad's in a foul mood, so make yourself scarce until dinner is ready.<br>老爸心情很差，开饭前你还是躲远点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scare</b></td><td>scare the ˈshit out of sb • scare sb ˈshitless (△, slang)</td><td>把某人吓得屁滚尿流</td><td>That horror film scared the shit out of me and I slept badly.<br>那部恐怖片把我吓得半死，一晚上没睡好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scene</b></td><td>arrive/come on the ˈscene</td><td>到达现场；出现；露面</td><td>Police arrived on the scene minutes after the alarm started ringing.<br>警报响起几分钟后警察就赶到了现场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>create/make a ˈscene</td><td>大吵大闹（尤在公共场合）</td><td>Please don't make a scene in the restaurant over a cold soup.<br>别为一碗凉汤在餐厅里大吵大闹。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) sb's ˈscene (informal)</td><td>（不）合某人口味；（非）某人所好</td><td>Loud nightclubs really aren't my scene; I'd rather find a quiet pub.<br>吵闹的夜店真不合我口味，我宁愿找家安静的酒吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set the ˈscene/ˈstage (for sth)</td><td>为…作铺垫；交代背景</td><td>The opening chapter sets the scene for everything that goes wrong later.<br>开篇一章为后面的所有变故作了铺垫。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scenes</b></td><td>behind the ˈscenes</td><td>幕后；暗中；秘密地</td><td>A lot of negotiating went on behind the scenes before the deal closed.<br>交易达成前，幕后进行了大量谈判。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scent</b></td><td>be on the ˈscent (of sb/sth)</td><td>追踪…的踪迹；获得线索</td><td>Reporters were on the scent of the story long before it broke.<br>这条新闻爆出来之前，记者早就嗅到味儿了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/throw sb off the ˈscent</td><td>使某人失去线索；引某人走偏</td><td>He booked a fake flight to throw the detectives off the scent.<br>他订了张假机票，好把警探引到岔路上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scheme</b></td><td>the/sb's ˈscheme of things</td><td>事物的格局；总体安排</td><td>In the grand scheme of things, a late train hardly matters at all.<br>从大局来看，火车晚点根本算不上什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>school</b></td><td>a school of ˈthought</td><td>学派；某种观点</td><td>There's a school of thought that says children learn best through play.<br>有一种观点认为孩子在玩耍中学得最好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep ˈschtum/ˈshtum (BrE, informal)</td><td>保持沉默；什么也不说</td><td>Keep schtum about the party — it's meant to be a surprise.<br>聚会的事你可别说漏嘴，本来是个惊喜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>science</b></td><td>have/get sth down to a ˈscience (especially AmE, often humorous)</td><td>把某事做得又准又高效</td><td>She has packing for holidays down to a science, never forgetting anything.<br>她收拾行李已经练成一门学问，从来不会漏东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>score</b></td><td>on ˈthat/ˈthis score</td><td>就那（这）一点而言</td><td>The car's cheap to run, so don't worry on that score at all.<br>这车养起来便宜，这方面你完全不用操心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>score a ˈpoint/ˈpoints (off/over/against sb)</td><td>驳倒某人；令某人出丑</td><td>He kept trying to score points off his brother during the whole dinner.<br>整顿饭他都在想办法把哥哥比下去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scorn</b></td><td>heap/pour ˈscorn on sb/sth</td><td>嘲笑；对…嗤之以鼻</td><td>Critics poured scorn on the plan before they had even read it.<br>评论者连方案都没看就大加嘲讽。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scot-free</b></td><td>get off/go ˌscot-ˈfree (informal)</td><td>逃脱惩罚；逍遥法外</td><td>He crashed the van and somehow got off scot-free with a warning.<br>他把货车撞了，居然只挨了个警告就没事了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(from Old English sceot, meaning 'a tax')</td><td>源自古英语 sceot（税），指不用纳税</td><td>In those days landowners went scot-free while the poor paid every tax.<br>那时候地主不用纳税，穷人却什么税都得交。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scrap</b></td><td>on the ˈscrap heap (informal)</td><td>被抛弃；遭淘汰</td><td>After the factory closed, hundreds of skilled workers were on the scrap heap.<br>工厂一关，几百名熟练工人就被扔在了一边。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scrape</b></td><td>scrape (up) an acˈquaintance with sb (informal)</td><td>设法结识某人</td><td>He scraped an acquaintance with the manager hoping it would land him work.<br>他想方设法结识了经理，指望能弄到活干。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>scrape (the bottom of) the ˈbarrel (disapproving)</td><td>勉强凑合；降格以求</td><td>Casting him as the hero really is scraping the bottom of the barrel.<br>让他演男主角，实在是没人可选了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scratch</b></td><td>do sth from ˈscratch</td><td>从零开始；白手起家</td><td>We lost the file and had to write the report from scratch.<br>文件丢了，报告只能从头再写。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>scratch ˌA and you'll find ˈB</td><td>剥开表象，某类人骨子里是…</td><td>Scratch a cynic and you'll find a disappointed idealist underneath.<br>剥开愤世嫉俗的外壳，里头是个失望的理想主义者。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>scratch your ˈhead (over sth)</td><td>苦思冥想；大惑不解</td><td>Engineers are still scratching their heads over why the engine keeps stalling.<br>发动机老熄火，工程师们到现在还摸不着头脑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>scratch the ˈsurface (of sth)</td><td>浅尝辄止；只触及皮毛</td><td>Two weeks in India only scratches the surface of such a huge country.<br>在印度待两周，对这么大的国家不过是走马观花。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up to ˈscratch</td><td>达到标准；合格</td><td>Your essay isn't up to scratch yet, so rewrite the middle section.<br>你这篇文章还不合格，中间那部分重写。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈback-scratching noun</td><td>互相吹捧；互开方便之门</td><td>There's far too much back-scratching between the council and local builders.<br>市政厅和本地建筑商之间的互相关照实在太多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scream</b></td><td>scream blue ˈmurder (BrE) (AmE scream bloody ˈmurder) (informal)</td><td>大声抗议；不停叫嚷</td><td>Residents screamed blue murder when the council announced the parking charges.<br>市政厅一宣布停车收费，居民们就闹翻了天。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>screw</b></td><td>have a ˈscrew loose</td><td>有点疯癫；脑子不正常</td><td>Anyone who swims in that river in January has a screw loose.<br>一月份还下那条河游泳的人，脑子准是有点毛病。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>screw ˈhim, ˈyou, ˈthat, etc. (△, slang)</td><td>去他（你）的；见鬼去吧</td><td>Screw him — if he can't apologise, I'm not going to his wedding.<br>去他的，他要是不肯道歉，他的婚礼我不去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌturn of the ˈscrew</td><td>雪上加霜；变本加厉的施压</td><td>The new tax was another turn of the screw for struggling small shops.<br>新税对本就艰难的小店来说又是一次加压。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>screws</b></td><td>put the ˈscrews on (sb) (informal)</td><td>胁迫；威逼；施压</td><td>The bank put the screws on us when we missed two payments.<br>我们漏还了两期，银行就开始逼债了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scrounge</b></td><td>be/go on the ˈscrounge (for sth) (BrE, informal, disapproving)</td><td>讨要（钱财、食物等）；伸手索要</td><td>He's always on the scrounge for cigarettes instead of buying his own.<br>他从来不自己买烟，总是四处讨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scruff</b></td><td>by the scruff of sb's/the ˈneck</td><td>揪住…的颈背</td><td>She grabbed the puppy by the scruff of the neck and carried him inside.<br>她揪住小狗的后颈皮，把它抱进了屋。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scum</b></td><td>the ˌscum of the ˈearth (informal)</td><td>人渣；社会渣滓</td><td>People who steal from the elderly are the scum of the earth.<br>偷老人东西的人真是人渣。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sea</b></td><td>all, completely, etc. at ˈsea</td><td>茫然；不知所措</td><td>I was completely at sea during the maths lecture this morning.<br>今天上午的数学课我完全听懵了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seal</b></td><td>a ˌseal of apˈproval</td><td>正式认可；批准</td><td>The recipe finally got my grandmother's seal of approval last Sunday.<br>上周日这个菜谱总算得到了我奶奶的认可。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set the ˈseal on sth (formal)</td><td>使…圆满收官；为…画上句号</td><td>Winning the cup set the seal on a remarkable season for them.<br>夺杯为他们精彩的一个赛季画上了圆满句号。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sealed</b></td><td>my ˈlips are sealed</td><td>我守口如瓶；决不外传</td><td>Don't worry about the surprise party — my lips are sealed.<br>惊喜派对的事你放心，我守口如瓶。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seams</b></td><td>be bursting/bulging at the ˈseams (with sth)</td><td>挤得满满的；人满为患</td><td>The little classroom was bursting at the seams with thirty-five children.<br>三十五个孩子把那间小教室挤得满满当当。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(also be full to ˈbursting (with sth)) (informal)</td><td>太满；胀得要爆开</td><td>My suitcase was full to bursting with presents for the whole family.<br>我的行李箱塞满了给全家人的礼物，快撑爆了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seamy</b></td><td>the ˈseamy side (of life, etc.)</td><td>（生活等的）阴暗面</td><td>The novel shows the seamy side of city life in the eighties.<br>这部小说写的是八十年代城市生活的阴暗面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>search</b></td><td>search your ˈheart/ˈsoul/ˈconscience (formal)</td><td>反躬自问；扪心自问</td><td>Search your conscience before you accuse a colleague of stealing anything.<br>指控同事偷东西之前，先扪心自问一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈheart-searching, ˈsoul-searching nouns</td><td>反省；自我拷问</td><td>The divorce forced him into months of painful soul-searching about everything.<br>这场离婚让他痛苦地反省了好几个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>search ˈme (spoken)</td><td>我怎么知道；我不清楚</td><td>'Where's the corkscrew?' 'Search me — I haven't touched it all week.'<br>“开瓶器呢？”“我哪知道，我一周都没碰过。”</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>season</b></td><td>ˌin/ˌout of ˈseason</td><td>当令；不当令；旺季；淡季</td><td>Strawberries taste far better in season and cost half as much too.<br>草莓当令时好吃得多，价钱还便宜一半。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(the) season's ˈgreetings (written)</td><td>节日问候（尤用于圣诞贺卡）</td><td>Season's greetings to you and all the family from everyone at the office.<br>办公室全体同人向你和家人致以节日问候。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seat</b></td><td>(fly) by the seat of your ˈpants</td><td>凭直觉行事；无计划地瞎闯</td><td>We had no budget and flew by the seat of our pants for months.<br>我们没有预算，好几个月都是走一步看一步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a back ˈseat</td><td>退居次要地位；不起主导作用</td><td>Since her promotion, hobbies have taken a back seat to work entirely.<br>自从升职以后，她的爱好就完全给工作让路了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>second</b></td><td>be second ˈnature (to sb)</td><td>成为第二天性；习以为常</td><td>After twenty years of driving, changing gear is second nature to him.<br>开了二十年车，换挡对他来说完全是本能。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be second only to sb/sth</td><td>仅次于…</td><td>In terms of size, this lake is second only to Lake Superior.<br>论面积，这个湖仅次于苏必利尔湖。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your second ˈwind (informal)</td><td>恢复精力；重振干劲</td><td>I got my second wind around midnight and finished the whole essay.<br>半夜前后我又来了精神，把整篇论文写完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have second ˈthoughts</td><td>改变主意；重新考虑；心生疑虑</td><td>She's having second thoughts about moving abroad now that winter is coming.<br>眼看冬天要到了，她对出国的事又犹豫起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈsecond thoughts (BrE) (AmE on ˈsecond thought)</td><td>转念一想；再一想</td><td>On second thoughts, let's take the train instead of driving through town.<br>再想想，我们还是坐火车吧，别开车穿城了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play second ˈfiddle</td><td>充当副手；居次要地位</td><td>He got tired of playing second fiddle to his more famous brother.<br>给名气更大的哥哥当陪衬，他早就厌烦了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsecond ˈbest</td><td>次好的；退而求其次</td><td>I refuse to settle for second best when it comes to safety.<br>在安全问题上，我绝不肯将就。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/your second ˈchildhood</td><td>第二童年；老小孩</td><td>Grandad bought a skateboard — he's clearly enjoying his second childhood.<br>爷爷买了块滑板，显然是返老还童了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>second ˈsight</td><td>预见力；千里眼</td><td>My aunt claims she has second sight and knew about the accident.<br>我姑妈说她有预见力，早就知道会出事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>second to ˈnone</td><td>首屈一指；不亚于任何人</td><td>Their after-sales service is second to none in the whole industry.<br>他们的售后服务在整个行业里首屈一指。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>without a second ˈthought</td><td>毫不犹豫；不假思索</td><td>She jumped into the freezing canal without a second thought to save him.<br>她想都没想就跳进冰冷的运河去救他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a second/another bite at/of the ˈcherry</td><td>第二次机会；再试一次的机会</td><td>Losing the tender hurt, but we got a second bite of the cherry.<br>丢了那个标很心疼，好在我们又有了一次机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>secret</b></td><td>an ˌopen ˈsecret</td><td>公开的秘密</td><td>It's an open secret that the manager is leaving at Christmas.<br>经理圣诞节要走，这已经是公开的秘密了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>see</b></td><td>be glad, etc. to see the ˈback of sb/sth</td><td>庆幸摆脱某人（或某事）</td><td>I'll be glad to see the back of this cold, wet February.<br>这个又冷又湿的二月总算要过去了，真好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see a lot, nothing, etc. of sb</td><td>常（或从不）与某人来往</td><td>We've seen a lot of the neighbours since our kids started school.<br>孩子上学以后，我们和邻居来往多了不少。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see sb/sth for what they ˈare/it ˈis</td><td>看清…的真面目；识破</td><td>Eventually she saw the offer for what it was — a cheap trick.<br>她终于看清那个提议不过是个廉价的把戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsee for yourˈself</td><td>亲自去看；自己核实</td><td>Don't take my word for it; come and see for yourself tomorrow.<br>别光听我说，明天你自己来看看。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈsee to it (that...)</td><td>确保；务必做到</td><td>See to it that the doors are locked before you leave tonight.<br>今晚走之前，务必把门都锁好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsee you (aˈround) • ˌsee you ˈlater (also (Iˈll) be ˈseeing you) (spoken)</td><td>再见；回见</td><td>See you around, then — I'll message you when I'm back in town.<br>那回头见，我回城了给你发消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so I ˈsee!</td><td>我看出来了（多用于回应不快之事）</td><td>You've spilled paint on the carpet — so I see, unfortunately.<br>你把油漆洒到地毯上了。可不是嘛，我看到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you ˈsee (spoken)</td><td>你知道；要知道（作解释时说）</td><td>I can't come tonight; you see, my mother is arriving from Spain.<br>今晚我去不了，你知道，我妈从西班牙过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seed</b></td><td>go/run to ˈseed (informal)</td><td>（人）变得邋遢懒散；（地方）荒废</td><td>The old tennis club has really gone to seed since the owner died.<br>老板去世后，那家老网球俱乐部彻底荒废了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seeds</b></td><td>plant/sow the ˈseeds of sth</td><td>播下…的种子；埋下…的根源</td><td>That summer job planted the seeds of her interest in medicine.<br>那份暑期工作播下了她对医学感兴趣的种子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seeing</b></td><td>seeing as/that...</td><td>因为；鉴于；既然</td><td>Seeing as it's your birthday, dinner tonight is definitely on me.<br>既然今天你生日，晚饭肯定我请。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>seeing is beˈlieving (saying)</td><td>眼见为实</td><td>I doubted the trick worked until he showed me — seeing is believing.<br>他演示之前我一直不信，果然眼见为实。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seek</b></td><td>seek your ˈfortune (literary)</td><td>外出闯天下；寻求发财之路</td><td>At eighteen he left the village to seek his fortune in London.<br>十八岁那年他离开村子，去伦敦闯天下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈfortune seeker noun</td><td>淘金者；碰运气发财的人</td><td>The gold rush drew fortune seekers from every corner of the country.<br>淘金热把全国各地想发财的人都吸引来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>self</b></td><td>be a shadow/ghost of your/its former ˈself</td><td>远不如从前；今非昔比</td><td>After the illness he was a shadow of his former self.<br>生了那场病以后，他整个人都大不如前了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sell</b></td><td>sell sb down the ˈriver (informal)</td><td>出卖；背叛</td><td>He sold his colleagues down the river to save his own job.<br>为了保住饭碗，他把同事全出卖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sell sb ˈshort</td><td>缺斤短两；给某人的东西不足</td><td>That market stall sold me short by nearly half a kilo.<br>那个市场摊位缺了我将近半公斤的秤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sell your ˈsoul (informal, often humorous)</td><td>出卖灵魂（为好处不择手段）</td><td>He'd sell his soul for a seat in the front row.<br>为了坐第一排，他什么都干得出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sell yourself/sb/sth ˈshort</td><td>低估自己（或某人、某物）</td><td>Don't sell yourself short — you're the best candidate they've interviewed.<br>别小看自己，你是他们面试过最合适的人选。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seller</b></td><td>a ˌseller's ˈmarket</td><td>卖方市场</td><td>It's a seller's market right now, so houses go within days.<br>现在是卖方市场，房子几天就卖掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>send</b></td><td>send sb ˈpacking (informal)</td><td>打发某人走；叫某人卷铺盖</td><td>The landlord sent the noisy tenants packing after only two months.<br>才住了两个月，房东就把那些吵闹的租客赶走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>send sb to ˈCoventry (BrE)</td><td>不理睬某人；孤立某人</td><td>The whole team sent him to Coventry after he criticised the coach.<br>他批评了教练，全队都不再理他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sends</b></td><td>work all the ˌhours God ˈsends</td><td>拼命工作；没日没夜地干</td><td>She works all the hours God sends to keep the little café going.<br>为了撑住这家小咖啡馆，她没日没夜地干。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sense</b></td><td>in ˈno sense</td><td>决不；无论如何都不</td><td>This is in no sense an admission that we made a mistake.<br>这绝不表示我们承认犯了错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in a ˈsense • in ˈone sense</td><td>在某种意义上</td><td>In a sense we were lucky the storm hit before the roof was finished.<br>从某种意义上说，暴雨在屋顶完工前来还算走运。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sense</b></td><td>make ˈsense</td><td>有道理；讲得通</td><td>Your plan makes sense, but we'll need more money to pull it off.<br>你的方案有道理，只是要办成还得再加钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈsense of sth</td><td>弄懂；理解（难懂之事）</td><td>I can't make sense of these instructions; they must be badly translated.<br>这说明书我看不懂，八成是翻译得太差。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(make sb) see ˈsense/ˈreason</td><td>（使某人）明白事理</td><td>Her father finally saw sense and agreed to sell the old car.<br>她父亲总算想通了，同意把那辆旧车卖掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a sense of ocˈcasion</td><td>隆重感；场合意识</td><td>The candles and live music gave the evening a real sense of occasion.<br>烛光加现场音乐，让那一晚很有仪式感。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have more ˌmoney than ˈsense</td><td>有钱没脑子；乱花钱</td><td>Buying a third sports car? He has more money than sense.<br>又买第三辆跑车？他真是钱多得没处花。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>senses</b></td><td>come to your ˈsenses</td><td>恢复理智；醒悟过来</td><td>I hope he comes to his senses before he sells the family farm.<br>但愿他在卖掉家里农场之前能清醒过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˌleave of your ˈsenses (informal, humorous)</td><td>失去理智；发疯</td><td>Have you taken leave of your senses, cycling home in this blizzard?<br>你疯了吧，这么大的暴风雪还骑车回家？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>these things are ˌsent to ˈtry us</td><td>这类倒霉事是对人的考验</td><td>The boiler's broken again — well, these things are sent to try us.<br>锅炉又坏了，唉，这也是老天在考验人吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go your separate ˈways</td><td>各奔前程；分道扬镳</td><td>After graduation we went our separate ways and rarely spoke again.<br>毕业后我们各奔东西，几乎不再联系。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sort out/separate the ˌsheep from the ˈgoats</td><td>区分良莠；辨别优劣</td><td>The first exam will sort out the sheep from the goats quickly.<br>第一场考试很快就能把好坏分出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sequitur</b></td><td>a ˌnon ˈsequitur (from Latin, formal)</td><td>不合逻辑的推论；前言不搭后语</td><td>Saying it's cold so taxes must rise is a complete non sequitur.<br>说天冷所以得加税，完全是不合逻辑的推论。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb/sth ˈseriously</td><td>认真对待某人（或某事）</td><td>Nobody took his warning seriously until the river burst its banks.<br>直到河水决堤，才有人把他的警告当回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seriousness</b></td><td>in all ˈseriousness</td><td>非常严肃地；说实在的</td><td>In all seriousness, you should see a doctor about that cough.<br>说正经的，你这咳嗽该去看医生了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>serve a, his, its, etc. ˈpurpose</td><td>起作用；派上用场</td><td>This old crate serves its purpose as a table for now.<br>这只旧木箱暂时当桌子用也够了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>serve the ˈpurpose (of doing sth)</td><td>起到（做某事的）作用</td><td>The meeting served the purpose of getting everyone talking to each other.<br>这次会议起到了让大家彼此交流的作用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>press sb/sth into ˈservice</td><td>临时征用；紧急启用</td><td>Every spare van was pressed into service to deliver the flood supplies.<br>所有闲置的货车都被调来运送救灾物资。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>serve two ˈmasters</td><td>一仆二主；同时效忠两方</td><td>You can't serve two masters — pick a side and stick with it.<br>你不能一仆二主，选一边站稳了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>service</b></td><td>be at sb's ˈservice (formal)</td><td>听候某人吩咐；为某人效劳</td><td>Our driver is at your service for the whole weekend, sir.<br>先生，整个周末司机都听您差遣。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sb a/no ˈservice (formal)</td><td>对某人有益；对某人并无好处</td><td>You do him no service by finishing his homework every single night.<br>你天天替他把作业写完，这对他没有半点好处。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>seventh</b></td><td>be in (your) seventh ˈheaven</td><td>欣喜若狂；快活似神仙</td><td>Give her a garden and a dog and she's in seventh heaven.<br>给她一个院子加一条狗，她就快活似神仙。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shade</b></td><td>put sb/sth in the ˈshade (informal)</td><td>使…相形见绌；使黯然失色</td><td>Her homemade bread puts every bakery in town in the shade.<br>她自己烤的面包让全城面包店都相形见绌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shadow</b></td><td>be frightened/nervous/scared of your own ˈshadow</td><td>胆小如鼠；非常紧张</td><td>Since the burglary he's been scared of his own shadow at night.<br>自从家里遭贼，他晚上连自己的影子都怕。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be scared of your own ˈshadow</td><td>胆小怕事；草木皆兵</td><td>That dog is scared of his own shadow, let alone the postman.<br>那条狗连自己的影子都怕，更别说邮递员了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>beyond/without a ˌshadow of (a) ˈdoubt</td><td>毫无疑问；确凿无疑</td><td>Beyond a shadow of a doubt, this is the best team we've had.<br>毫无疑问，这是我们有过的最好的一支队伍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there isn't a ˌshadow of a ˈdoubt (that...)</td><td>毫无疑问；毋庸置疑</td><td>There isn't a shadow of a doubt that he took the money.<br>钱是他拿的，这一点毫无疑问。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there isn't a ˌshadow of ˈdoubt in my mind</td><td>我心中毫无疑虑；我深信不疑</td><td>There isn't a shadow of doubt in my mind that she's telling the truth.<br>我一点也不怀疑她说的是实话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/under the ˈshadow of be a shadow/ghost of your/its former ˈself</td><td>大不如前；今非昔比</td><td>The high street is a shadow of its former self these days.<br>如今这条商业街早已不复当年的热闹。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shaft</b></td><td>give sb the ˈshaft (AmE, informal)</td><td>亏待某人；不公正地对待某人</td><td>The company gave him the shaft after fifteen years of loyal work.<br>他忠心干了十五年，公司却亏待了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shaggy-dog</b></td><td>a ˌshaggy-ˈdog story (informal)</td><td>冗长无趣的故事（或笑话）</td><td>Uncle Ray told another shaggy-dog story that lasted the entire car journey.<br>雷叔又讲了个又臭又长的故事，一路上没停。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shake</b></td><td>shake your ˈfist (at sb)</td><td>（向某人）挥拳（表示愤怒或威胁）</td><td>The old man shook his fist at the boys racing past his gate.<br>那些男孩从他家门口飞奔而过，老头儿冲他们挥了挥拳头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shake ˈhands (with sb) • shake sb's ˈhand</td><td>与某人握手</td><td>The two leaders shook hands for the cameras and then said nothing.<br>两位领导人对着镜头握了握手，之后一言未发。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shake sb by the ˈhand</td><td>握某人的手；与某人握手</td><td>He shook me by the hand and thanked me for coming so far.<br>他握着我的手，谢我跑这么远过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shake your ˈhead</td><td>摇头（表示拒绝、难过、不同意等）</td><td>She just shook her head and walked out without saying another word.<br>她只是摇了摇头，一句话没说就走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shake a ˈleg (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>快点；动作麻利些</td><td>Shake a leg, you two, or we'll miss the last bus home.<br>你们俩快点，不然赶不上末班车了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shake like a ˈjelly/ˈleaf (informal)</td><td>（因害怕或紧张）浑身发抖</td><td>He was shaking like a leaf before his driving test this morning.<br>今早路考前他抖得像片叶子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shake (hands) on it/on sth</td><td>握手成交；击掌为约</td><td>We agreed a price and shook hands on it right there.<br>我们谈好价钱，当场就握手成交了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shame</b></td><td>put sb/sth to ˈshame</td><td>使…相形见绌；使某人自愧不如</td><td>Her garden puts mine to shame, and she barely spends anything on it.<br>她的花园让我的相形见绌，可她几乎没花什么钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈshame on you, him, etc. (spoken)</td><td>真丢脸；真不害臊</td><td>Shame on you for laughing when the poor kid dropped his ice cream.<br>那孩子冰淇淋掉了你还笑，真不害臊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be a ˌcrying ˈshame</td><td>太遗憾了；真是造孽</td><td>It's a crying shame they knocked down that beautiful old cinema.<br>把那座漂亮的老电影院拆了，实在太可惜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shanks</b></td><td>(on) Shanks's ˈpony (BrE, informal)</td><td>步行；徒步</td><td>The buses had stopped, so we got home on Shanks's pony.<br>公交停运了，我们只好走着回家。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shape</b></td><td>be in (good, bad, etc.) ˈshape</td><td>身体（或状况）良好；状况不佳</td><td>For a man of seventy, Dad is in remarkably good shape.<br>七十岁的人了，我爸身体好得出奇。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be out of ˈshape</td><td>变形走样；（人）体力差</td><td>Two flights of stairs left me gasping — I'm badly out of shape.<br>爬两层楼就喘，我这体能真是差透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌtaste of ˌthings to ˈcome</td><td>未来情形的预兆</td><td>That freak storm was a taste of things to come, scientists warn.<br>科学家警告说，那场怪异的风暴只是个开头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get (yourself) (back) into ˈshape</td><td>恢复体形；强身健体</td><td>I've started swimming to get myself back into shape before the wedding.<br>为了婚礼前恢复身材，我开始游泳了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/knock/lick sb/sth into ˈshape</td><td>使…像样；使达到标准</td><td>Give me a month to knock this sales team into shape.<br>给我一个月，把这支销售团队整顿像样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give ˈshape to sth (formal)</td><td>使…成形；表达（想法、计划）</td><td>These sketches finally give shape to an idea I've had for years.<br>这些草图总算让我多年的想法有了形状。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in any (way,) shape or ˈform (informal)</td><td>以任何形式；无论如何</td><td>I won't support this project in any way, shape or form.<br>这个项目我以任何形式都不会支持。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the shape/form of sb/sth</td><td>以…的形式；即…</td><td>Help arrived in the shape of a neighbour with a tow rope.<br>帮手来了，是位带着拖车绳的邻居。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈshape up or ship ˈout (AmE, informal)</td><td>要么好好干，要么走人</td><td>The coach told the players to shape up or ship out.<br>教练告诉队员们，要么拿出状态，要么走人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈshape</td><td>成形；初具规模</td><td>After weeks of talking, the plan is finally starting to take shape.<br>谈了好几周，方案总算开始成形了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shapes</b></td><td>come in all ˌshapes and ˈsizes</td><td>形状（或种类）各异</td><td>Good teachers come in all shapes and sizes, as my old head said.<br>好老师什么样的都有，我以前的校长这么说过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>share</b></td><td>share and share aˈlike (saying)</td><td>平摊；有福同享</td><td>There's one pizza left, so share and share alike, you two.<br>只剩一张比萨了，你们俩平分。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shared</b></td><td>a trouble ˈshared is a trouble ˈhalved (saying)</td><td>有人分担，愁苦减半</td><td>Tell me what's wrong — a trouble shared is a trouble halved.<br>跟我说说怎么了，说出来就轻松一半。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sharp</b></td><td>have a sharp ˈtongue (informal)</td><td>说话尖刻；牙尖嘴利</td><td>My aunt has a sharp tongue but a very generous heart underneath.<br>我姑妈嘴上厉害，心肠却极好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a sharp ˈtongue</td><td>尖刻的言辞；刻薄的口舌</td><td>Her sharp tongue has cost her more than one close friendship.<br>她嘴太毒，害得不止一个好朋友跟她断了交。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsharp-ˈtongued adj.: a sharp-tongued old man</td><td>说话尖刻的</td><td>A sharp-tongued old man runs the corner shop and frightens all the children.<br>街角小店的老头嘴巴刻薄，孩子们都怕他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) sharp as a ˈtack (AmE)</td><td>非常机敏；头脑灵活</td><td>At ninety-two, Grandma is still as sharp as a tack.<br>九十二岁的奶奶脑子还是特别清楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈsharp end (of sth) (BrE, informal)</td><td>最艰难的一线工作</td><td>Nurses are at the sharp end of every crisis in the health service.<br>医疗系统一有危机，护士总是顶在最前线。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sharp ˈpractice</td><td>不诚实的手段；欺诈行径</td><td>The regulator fined the firm for sharp practice in selling pensions.<br>监管机构因该公司在卖养老金时耍花招而处以罚款。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look ˈlively/ˈsharp</td><td>快点；动作利索些</td><td>Look lively, lads — the delivery van arrives in ten minutes.<br>伙计们麻利点，送货车十分钟后就到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sharpest</b></td><td>not the sharpest knife in the ˈdrawer</td><td>不太聪明；脑子不灵光</td><td>He's kind, but he's not the sharpest knife in the drawer.<br>他人很好，就是脑子不太灵光。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(also not the sharpest tool in the ˈbox) (humorous)</td><td>不够聪明；不太机灵</td><td>Bless him, he's not the sharpest tool in the box, is he?<br>这孩子人不坏，就是不太开窍，是吧？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shave</b></td><td>a ˌclose ˈshave/ˈcall</td><td>侥幸脱险；死里逃生</td><td>That was a close shave — the lorry missed us by inches.<br>真是好险，那辆卡车擦着我们过去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shebang</b></td><td>the ˌwhole sheˈbang (informal)</td><td>全部；整个这一套</td><td>Tent, sleeping bags, stove — she packed the whole shebang in one rucksack.<br>帐篷、睡袋、炉子，她把全套家什塞进了一个背包。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sheep</b></td><td>like ˈsheep (disapproving)</td><td>盲从地；随大溜地</td><td>The crowd followed the guide like sheep, nobody asking a single question.<br>人群像羊群一样跟着导游，没人问一句话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sort out/separate the ˌsheep from the ˈgoats</td><td>区分良莠；分辨优劣</td><td>The final round will separate the sheep from the goats once and for all.<br>最后一轮会彻底把高下分出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>separate the ˌsheep from the ˈgoats</td><td>辨别好坏；区分优劣</td><td>This tough interview separates the sheep from the goats very quickly indeed.<br>这种硬碰硬的面试很快就能分出优劣。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˌblack ˈsheep (of the family)</td><td>害群之马；家中的败家子</td><td>Uncle Joe was the black sheep of the family and moved abroad.<br>乔叔是家里的败家子，后来搬到了国外。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shelf</b></td><td>buy, get, etc. sth off the ˈshelf</td><td>买现成的（非定做的）</td><td>We bought the software off the shelf instead of paying for custom work.<br>我们买了现成的软件，没花钱做定制。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈshelf (informal)</td><td>被搁置；（女子）年岁大嫁不出去</td><td>The project has been on the shelf since the funding was cut.<br>经费一砍，这个项目就搁置到现在。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shell</b></td><td>come out of your ˈshell</td><td>不再羞怯；变得活跃开朗</td><td>She came out of her shell once she joined the hiking club.<br>加入徒步俱乐部以后，她整个人开朗了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring sb out of their ˈshell (informal)</td><td>使某人不再羞怯；使活跃起来</td><td>A summer job in a café brought him out of his shell.<br>在咖啡馆干了个暑期工，他变得放得开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go, retreat, withdraw, etc. into your ˈshell</td><td>变得孤僻内向；不愿与人接触</td><td>After the divorce he retreated into his shell and stopped calling friends.<br>离婚后他把自己封闭起来，也不再给朋友打电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shift</b></td><td>shift your ˈground (usually disapproving)</td><td>改变立场；改变说法</td><td>Every time we corner him in debate, he shifts his ground again.<br>每次辩论把他逼到墙角，他就又换个说法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shifting</b></td><td>(the) ˌshifting ˈsands (of sth)</td><td>变幻不定的局势；不牢靠的基础</td><td>Investors hate the shifting sands of government policy on renewable energy.<br>政府在可再生能源上的政策变来变去，投资者很反感。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shine</b></td><td>take the ˈshine off sth (informal)</td><td>使…失色；使兴致大减</td><td>The rain took the shine off our first day at the beach.<br>一场雨让我们在海边的第一天大打折扣。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a ˈshine to sb/sth (informal)</td><td>对…一见倾心；喜欢上</td><td>The boss has taken a shine to you, so ask for that raise.<br>老板挺看好你，去提加薪的事吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shines</b></td><td>make ˈhay while the sun ˈshines (saying)</td><td>抓紧时机；勿失良机</td><td>Orders are pouring in, so make hay while the sun shines.<br>订单源源不断，趁着行情好赶紧干。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shining</b></td><td>be a shining eˈxample (of sb/sth) (also be a shining ˈlight)</td><td>光辉榜样；楷模</td><td>That little library is a shining example of what volunteers can achieve.<br>那间小图书馆是志愿者能做成什么事的典范。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ship</b></td><td>when your ˈship/ˈboat comes in (informal)</td><td>等到发财（或成功）时</td><td>When my ship comes in, I'll buy us a cottage by the sea.<br>等我发达了，就给咱们在海边买栋小屋。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ships</b></td><td>be (like) ˌships that ˌpass in the ˈnight (informal)</td><td>萍水相逢；擦肩而过</td><td>We work opposite shifts and are like ships that pass in the night.<br>我们班次相反，就像夜里错身而过的两条船。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not give a ˈshit (about sb/sth) (△, slang)</td><td>毫不在乎；完全不关心</td><td>He doesn't give a shit about deadlines, which drives the whole team mad.<br>他压根不在乎截止日期，全组都被他气疯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shit all over sb/sth (△, slang, especially AmE)</td><td>极其恶劣地对待某人（或某事）</td><td>They shit all over their staff and then wonder why everybody leaves.<br>他们把员工往死里糟践，还纳闷人为什么都跑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shit ˈhappens (△, slang)</td><td>倒霉事难免；天有不测风云</td><td>Shit happens; you just pick yourself up and carry on regardless.<br>倒霉事总会有，爬起来接着走就是了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(when) the ˌshit hits the ˈfan (△, slang)</td><td>麻烦爆发；东窗事发</td><td>When the shit hits the fan, don't expect the manager to defend you.<br>真出了事，别指望经理会替你说话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shiver</b></td><td>a ˈshiver runs/goes down sb's spine</td><td>脊背发凉；不寒而栗</td><td>A shiver ran down my spine when I heard footsteps upstairs.<br>听到楼上的脚步声，我脊背一阵发凉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>send a ˈshiver up/down sb's spine</td><td>使人脊背发凉；令人战栗</td><td>His calm description of the crash sent a shiver down my spine.<br>他平静地讲述那场车祸，听得我脊背发凉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shivers</b></td><td>give sb/get the ˈshivers (informal)</td><td>使人（或感到）不寒而栗</td><td>That empty hospital corridor gives me the shivers every single time.<br>那条空荡荡的医院走廊，我每次走都发怵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shock</b></td><td>shock ˈhorror (BrE, informal, often humorous)</td><td>吓死人了（假装震惊）</td><td>Shock horror — the teenager actually tidied his bedroom without being asked.<br>天大的新闻，这小子居然没人催就收拾了房间。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shoes</b></td><td>be in sb's shoes (informal)</td><td>处于某人的境地</td><td>I wouldn't want to be in his shoes when the auditors arrive.<br>审计的人一来，我可不想站在他那个位置上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put yourself in sb's shoes/place</td><td>设身处地为某人着想</td><td>Put yourself in her shoes before you judge how she handled it.<br>在评价她的做法之前，先设身处地想一想。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shoestring</b></td><td>(do sth) on a ˈshoestring (informal)</td><td>以极少的钱（做某事）</td><td>They filmed the whole documentary on a shoestring using borrowed cameras.<br>他们借来摄影机，用极少的钱拍完了整部纪录片。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shoo-in</b></td><td>be a ˈshoo-in (AmE, informal)</td><td>稳操胜券；十拿九稳</td><td>With that record, she's a shoo-in for the manager's job.<br>凭这样的业绩，经理的位子非她莫属。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shoot</b></td><td>shoot your ˈbolt (informal)</td><td>已竭尽全力（尤指过早发力）</td><td>He shot his bolt in the first mile and faded badly afterwards.<br>他头一英里就把力气使光了，后面掉得很厉害。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shoot the ˈbreeze (also shoot the ˈbull/ˈshit △)</td><td>闲聊；侃大山</td><td>We sat on the porch shooting the breeze until well past midnight.<br>我们坐在门廊上闲聊，一直聊到后半夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shoot sb/sth ˈdown (in ˈflames) (informal)</td><td>彻底驳倒；把…批得一无是处</td><td>The committee shot our proposal down in flames within about five minutes.<br>委员会五分钟就把我们的提案批得体无完肤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌshoot from the ˈhip</td><td>鲁莽行事；不假思索地开口</td><td>The new director shoots from the hip and upsets people constantly.<br>新主管说话不过脑子，老是得罪人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shoot ˈhoops (AmE, informal)</td><td>打篮球</td><td>We used to shoot hoops in the driveway until it got dark.<br>我们以前在车道上打篮球，一直打到天黑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌshoot it ˈout (with sb) (informal)</td><td>决一死战；开枪对决</td><td>The robbers shot it out with police outside the bank.<br>劫匪在银行门外和警察展开了枪战。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shoot the ˈlights (informal)</td><td>闯红灯</td><td>He shot the lights on Main Street and got a hefty fine.<br>他在主街闯了红灯，被重罚了一笔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shoot the ˈmessenger</td><td>迁怒于报信人</td><td>Don't shoot the messenger — I only passed on what the boss said.<br>别拿我撒气，我只是转达老板的话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shoot your ˈmouth off (about sth)</td><td>信口开河；乱说（不该说的事）</td><td>Someone shot their mouth off about the merger before it was announced.<br>合并还没公布，就有人把消息说漏了嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shoot yourself in the ˈfoot (informal)</td><td>弄巧成拙；自找麻烦</td><td>He shot himself in the foot by insulting the client's hometown.<br>他嘲笑客户的家乡，纯属自毁前程。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shooting</b></td><td>the ˌwhole ˈshooting match (BrE, informal)</td><td>全部；所有的一切</td><td>She sold the shop, the van, the whole shooting match, last spring.<br>去年春天她把店、车，所有家当全卖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shop</b></td><td>all ˈover the shop (AmE also all ˈover the lot)</td><td>到处；乱七八糟</td><td>His notes were all over the shop, so nobody could follow the argument.<br>他的笔记乱七八糟，谁也理不清他的思路。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set up ˈshop (especially BrE)</td><td>开业；开始营业</td><td>They set up shop in a tiny unit behind the railway station.<br>他们在火车站后头一间小铺面开了张。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>short</b></td><td>at (very) short ˈnotice (also at a moment's ˈnotice)</td><td>临时通知；随时</td><td>She found us a hotel at very short notice on Christmas Eve.<br>平安夜她临时给我们找到了酒店。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be caught/taken ˈshort (BrE, informal)</td><td>突然内急（附近却没厕所）</td><td>I was caught short halfway up the mountain with no toilet anywhere.<br>爬到半山腰我突然内急，四下连个厕所都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in ˌshort supˈply</td><td>供应不足；短缺</td><td>Patience was in short supply after four hours on the motorway.<br>在高速上堵了四小时，谁都没耐心了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be on/have a short ˈfuse (informal)</td><td>脾气暴躁；动辄发火</td><td>Dad's on a short fuse today, so don't mention the car.<br>老爸今天火气大，别提车的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌshort and ˈsweet (informal)</td><td>简短明快；简明扼要</td><td>Keep the speech short and sweet; everyone wants to start eating.<br>致辞简短点，大家都等着开饭呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/run short of sth</td><td>缺乏；所剩不多</td><td>We're running short of milk, so grab some on your way home.<br>牛奶快没了，你回来的路上买点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring/pull sb up ˈshort</td><td>使某人猛然止步；使一下子怔住</td><td>Her question brought me up short and I forgot my whole argument.<br>她一句话把我问住了，我把要说的全忘了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come ˈshort (South African, informal)</td><td>出事；陷入麻烦</td><td>Drive carefully on that road or you'll come short one dark night.<br>那条路开车小心点，不然哪个黑夜就出事了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cut sb ˈshort</td><td>打断某人的话</td><td>The chairman cut her short before she could finish the second point.<br>她第二点还没讲完，主席就把她打断了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cut sth ˈshort</td><td>中断；提前结束</td><td>We cut our holiday short when Mum was taken into hospital.<br>妈妈住院了，我们提前结束了假期。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fall ˈshort of sth</td><td>未达到；不符合（标准）</td><td>The building falls short of the new fire safety standards.<br>这栋楼达不到新的消防安全标准。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈshort</td><td>简称；缩写为</td><td>His name is Bartholomew, but everyone calls him Bart for short.<br>他叫巴塞洛缪，大家都简称他巴特。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/have sb by the short and ˈcurlies (informal)</td><td>完全掌控某人；使某人任其摆布</td><td>With that contract, the supplier has us by the short and curlies.<br>有那份合同在手，供应商把我们捏得死死的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/sth short ˈshrift • get short ˈshrift</td><td>不予重视；遭到冷遇</td><td>My complaint got short shrift from the manager, who barely looked up.<br>经理头都没抬，把我的投诉打发了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go short (of sth)</td><td>缺少；短缺</td><td>The children never went short of food, whatever else we lacked.<br>不管别的多缺，孩子们从没饿过肚子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈshort</td><td>简言之；总之</td><td>In short, we need more money and a lot more time.<br>简言之，我们需要更多钱和更多时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˌshort ˈorder</td><td>迅速地；毫不拖延地</td><td>The plumber arrived and fixed the leak in short order.<br>水管工赶到后，很快就把漏水修好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shot</b></td><td>be (all) ˈshot (to ˈpieces) (informal)</td><td>被彻底毁坏；（神经）垮掉</td><td>My nerves were shot to pieces after two nights without any sleep.<br>两晚没合眼，我的神经彻底垮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get ˈshot of sb/sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>摆脱；除掉</td><td>I'll be glad to get shot of this leaky old van.<br>能把这辆漏雨的破车处理掉，我求之不得。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/take a ˈshot (at sth/at doing sth) (also give sth a ˈshot) (informal)</td><td>试一试；尝试（做某事）</td><td>I've never baked bread, but I'll have a shot at it tonight.<br>我从没烤过面包，今晚打算试一把。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(do sth) like a ˈshot (informal)</td><td>立刻；飞快地；毫不犹豫地</td><td>If they offered me that job, I'd take it like a shot.<br>他们要是给我那份工作，我二话不说就答应。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(fire) a (warning) shot across sb's ˈbows</td><td>发出警告；先行示警</td><td>The email was a warning shot across the bows of every late payer.<br>那封邮件是对所有拖欠者的一记警告。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a shot in the ˈarm (informal)</td><td>一针强心剂；有力的鼓舞</td><td>The grant was a real shot in the arm for our little theatre.<br>这笔拨款对我们这家小剧场来说是一针强心剂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌshotgun ˈwedding/ˈmarriage (old-fashioned)</td><td>奉子成婚；被迫成婚</td><td>It was a shotgun wedding, but they stayed happily married for decades.<br>那是场奉子成婚，可两人恩爱了几十年。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shoulder</b></td><td>put your shoulder to the ˈwheel</td><td>奋力干起来；开始拼命工作</td><td>Everyone put their shoulder to the wheel and we finished by Friday.<br>大家一齐使劲，周五前就干完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a shoulder to ˈcry on</td><td>可倾诉的对象；可依靠的肩膀</td><td>After the breakup she just needed a shoulder to cry on.<br>分手之后，她只想找个人诉诉苦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth/be for ˈshow</td><td>装样子；做给别人看</td><td>The apology was just for show; nothing about his behaviour actually changed.<br>那句道歉不过是做样子，他的行为一点没变。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/get the ˌcold ˈshoulder</td><td>冷落某人；遭到冷遇</td><td>They gave the new neighbour the cold shoulder for a whole year.<br>他们冷落了那位新邻居整整一年。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>show</b></td><td>have something, nothing, etc. to ˈshow for sth</td><td>在…方面有（或没有）成果</td><td>Ten years of work and he has nothing to show for it.<br>干了十年，他却什么成果都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it (just/only) goes to ˈshow (that...)</td><td>这就说明；这足以证明</td><td>It just goes to show that hard work sometimes beats raw talent.<br>这就说明，苦干有时候胜过天赋。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put on a good, poor, wonderful, etc. ˈshow</td><td>表现得好（或差等）</td><td>The youth team put on a good show against far stronger opponents.<br>面对强得多的对手，青年队表现不俗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run the ˈshow (sometimes disapproving)</td><td>掌管；操纵；说了算</td><td>Officially she's the deputy, but everyone knows she runs the show.<br>名义上她是副手，可谁都知道是她说了算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>show (sb) a clean pair of ˈheels (informal)</td><td>逃之夭夭；把人远远甩开</td><td>The thief showed the guards a clean pair of heels down the alley.<br>小偷顺着巷子跑得没影，保安只能干瞪眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>show sb the ˈdoor (informal)</td><td>下逐客令；把某人赶出去</td><td>When he started shouting, the landlord showed him the door immediately.<br>他一开始嚷嚷，老板立刻请他出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>show your ˈface</td><td>露面（尤指不受欢迎时）</td><td>After that argument, I doubt he'll show his face here again.<br>吵成那样，我看他不会再来这儿露面了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>show good ˈcause (for sth/for doing sth)</td><td>说明正当理由</td><td>You must show good cause for missing three weeks of lectures.<br>你得说明缺课三周的正当理由。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a show of ˈforce</td><td>武力示威；显示实力</td><td>Tanks rolled through the square in an obvious show of force.<br>坦克开过广场，明显是在示威。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a show of ˈhands</td><td>举手表决</td><td>Let's settle this by a show of hands rather than another debate.<br>这事举手表决吧，别再辩了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>show your ˈteeth (BrE)</td><td>张牙舞爪；亮出厉害</td><td>The union finally showed its teeth and called a one-day strike.<br>工会终于亮出了獠牙，发起了一天的罢工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>show the ˈway</td><td>带路；示范；引领</td><td>Their small factory showed the way on recycling long before it was fashionable.<br>早在回收还没流行时，他们那家小厂就带了个好头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>show sb who's ˈboss</td><td>让某人知道谁说了算</td><td>Train the puppy early and show him who's boss from day one.<br>小狗要早训，第一天就让它知道谁说了算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>show ˈwilling (BrE)</td><td>表示乐意帮忙</td><td>Even peeling a few potatoes would show willing at his mother's house.<br>在他妈家哪怕削几个土豆，也算是有个态度。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shreds</b></td><td>in ˈshreds</td><td>被撕成碎片；被彻底摧毁</td><td>My confidence was in shreds after that awful performance review.<br>那次糟糕的绩效面谈把我的信心撕得粉碎。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shrinking</b></td><td>a ˌshrinking ˈviolet (humorous)</td><td>极腼腆的人；羞怯的人</td><td>She's no shrinking violet; she'll argue with anyone about football.<br>她可不是害羞的人，谈起足球跟谁都能吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shtum</b></td><td>keep ˈschtum/ˈshtum</td><td>保持沉默；守口如瓶</td><td>Keep shtum about the bonus until everyone has been told officially.<br>奖金的事先别声张，等正式通知了再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shuffle</b></td><td>lose sb/sth in the ˈshuffle (AmE)</td><td>在忙乱中被忽略</td><td>Her application got lost in the shuffle when the office moved buildings.<br>办公室搬家那阵，她的申请被忙乱中漏掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shuffle off this mortal ˈcoil (old-fashioned or humorous)</td><td>撒手人寰；离开人世</td><td>Before I shuffle off this mortal coil, I'd like to see Japan.<br>在我两腿一蹬之前，我想去趟日本。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shufti</b></td><td>have/take a ˈshufti (at sb/sth) (BrE, informal)</td><td>看一眼；瞥一眼</td><td>Have a shufti at this photo and tell me who that is.<br>瞧一眼这张照片，告诉我那是谁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shut</b></td><td>put up or ˈshut up (especially BrE)</td><td>要么拿出行动，要么闭嘴</td><td>If you think you can do better, put up or shut up.<br>你要觉得自己更行，就拿出真本事，否则闭嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shut sb's ˈmouth</td><td>封住某人的嘴（不让说出秘密）</td><td>They paid him well to shut his mouth about the accident.<br>他们出了大价钱，让他把事故的事咽回去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your ˈmouth/ˈtrap shut (slang)</td><td>住口；闭嘴；保守秘密</td><td>Keep your mouth shut and nobody will ever know we were here.<br>你把嘴闭紧，没人会知道我们来过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>shut up ˈshop (BrE, informal)</td><td>打烊；停业</td><td>The bakery shuts up shop at two on a Saturday afternoon.<br>这家面包店周六下午两点就打烊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shutters</b></td><td>bring/ˌput down the ˈshutters</td><td>封闭内心；不再理会某事</td><td>Whenever I mention his father, he brings down the shutters completely.<br>一提他父亲，他就彻底把心门关上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sick</b></td><td>be off ˈsick</td><td>请病假；因病缺勤</td><td>Three of the drivers are off sick, so buses will run late.<br>有三个司机请了病假，公交会晚点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈsick (BrE)</td><td>呕吐</td><td>The child was sick twice on the coach before we reached Dover.<br>还没到多佛，那孩子在大巴上就吐了两回。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bre</b></td><td>make sb ˈsick (informal)</td><td>使某人厌恶（或生气）</td><td>It makes me sick to see food thrown away like that.<br>看着这么扔食物，我心里堵得慌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) sick as a ˈdog (informal)</td><td>病得很重；吐得厉害</td><td>I was as sick as a dog after that dodgy prawn curry.<br>吃了那份不新鲜的虾咖喱，我吐得死去活来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/keep on the right/wrong ˈside of sb</td><td>讨好某人；得罪某人</td><td>Get on the right side of the caretaker and life becomes much easier.<br>和门卫处好关系，日子会好过得多。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have sth on your ˈside</td><td>在某方面占优势</td><td>We lost the vote, but we have time on our side.<br>投票输了，可时间站在我们这边。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave/put sth on/to one ˈside</td><td>把…搁在一边；留待以后处理</td><td>Let's put that question to one side and finish the budget first.<br>这个问题先放一放，先把预算做完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let the ˈside down (especially BrE)</td><td>让自己人失望；拖后腿</td><td>Turn up on time — don't let the side down again tomorrow.<br>准时到，明天别再给大家掉链子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not leave sb's ˈside</td><td>寸步不离某人左右</td><td>The dog didn't leave her side for the whole week she was ill.<br>她病的那一周，狗一步都没离开过她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the other side of the ˈcoin</td><td>事情的另一面</td><td>Cheap flights are great, but pollution is the other side of the coin.<br>廉价机票是好事，可污染是硬币的另一面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>side by ˈside (with sb/sth)</td><td>并排；肩并肩</td><td>The two old churches stand side by side at the end of the lane.<br>两座老教堂并排立在巷子尽头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>my, her, the other, the same, etc. side of the ˈfence</td><td>我方（或对方、同一方）的立场</td><td>It's easy to judge from the other side of the fence, isn't it?<br>站在对面说风凉话总是容易的，对吧？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the other side of the ˈfence</td><td>站在对立的一方</td><td>Last year he was on the other side of the fence, defending the company.<br>去年他还站在对面，替公司辩护呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/one side of the ˈstory/ˈpicture</td><td>一面之词；片面的说法</td><td>That's only one side of the story; ask her brother what happened.<br>那只是一面之词，问问她哥哥到底怎么回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take/draw sb to one ˈside</td><td>把某人拉到一边（悄悄说话）</td><td>The coach took me to one side and asked about my knee.<br>教练把我拉到一边，问我膝盖怎么样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>this side of...</td><td>在…之前</td><td>We won't finish this side of Christmas at the rate we're going.<br>照这个速度，圣诞节前是干不完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sidelines</b></td><td>on the ˈsidelines</td><td>作壁上观；置身局外</td><td>He spent the whole crisis on the sidelines, offering advice to nobody.<br>整场危机他都袖手旁观，一句建议也没给。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from/on all ˈsides • from/on every ˈside</td><td>从四面八方；来自各方</td><td>Criticism came from all sides after the council announced the cuts.<br>市政厅一宣布削减开支，批评声就从四面八方涌来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see both ˈsides (of the question, problem, etc.)</td><td>看到问题的两个方面</td><td>A good mediator can see both sides of a family argument.<br>好的调解人能看清家庭争吵中双方的道理。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈsides • take sb's ˈside</td><td>偏袒一方；支持某人</td><td>I refuse to take sides when my two best friends are arguing.<br>两个最要好的朋友吵架，我不站队。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under ˈsiege</td><td>被围困；被围攻</td><td>The embassy was under siege for three days before help arrived.<br>救援到来之前，使馆被围困了三天。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sieve</b></td><td>have a mind/memory like a ˈsieve (informal)</td><td>记性极差；丢三落四</td><td>Write it down for me; I've got a memory like a sieve.<br>给我写下来吧，我这记性跟筛子似的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sight</b></td><td>be in/within ˈsight</td><td>看得见；在望</td><td>After six hours of walking, the village was finally in sight.<br>走了六个小时，村子终于出现在眼前。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be a ˌsight for sore ˈeyes (spoken)</td><td>见了就让人高兴；养眼的人（或物）</td><td>A hot bath after that hike was a sight for sore eyes.<br>徒步回来能泡个热水澡，简直太让人舒心了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth on ˈsight</td><td>一看见就（做某事）</td><td>The guards had orders to arrest him on sight at the border.<br>卫兵接到命令，在边境一见到他就抓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hate, be sick of, etc. the ˈsight of sb/sth</td><td>非常厌恶；一见就烦</td><td>I'm sick of the sight of this kitchen after painting it twice.<br>这厨房刷了两遍漆，我看见就烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep sight of sb/sth • keep sb/sth in sight</td><td>紧盯着；使不离视线</td><td>Keep the children in sight while the tide is coming in.<br>涨潮的时候，别让孩子离开你的视线。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look a ˈsight (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>样子难看；狼狈不堪</td><td>I looked a sight after cycling home through the rain and mud.<br>冒着雨踩着泥骑车回家，我狼狈极了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose ˈsight of sth</td><td>忽略；忘记（目标等）</td><td>We mustn't lose sight of why we started this charity ten years ago.<br>别忘了十年前我们办这个慈善机构是为了什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of ˈsight, ˌout of ˈmind (saying)</td><td>眼不见，心不想</td><td>He never writes now — out of sight, out of mind, I suppose.<br>他现在从不来信，大概就是眼不见心不想吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a (damn, etc.) sight ˈbetter, ˈworse, etc.</td><td>好（或坏等）得多</td><td>This coffee is a damn sight better than the stuff at work.<br>这咖啡比单位那玩意儿强多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a sight ˈbetter/ˈworse (than sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>比…好（或差）得多</td><td>My old bike was a sight better than this expensive rusty thing.<br>我那辆旧自行车比这贵价锈货强多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sight unˈseen</td><td>未经过目（就买等）</td><td>They bought the flat sight unseen and regretted it within a month.<br>他们没看房就买下了那套公寓，一个月不到就后悔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sights</b></td><td>raise/lower your ˈsights</td><td>提高（或降低）期望</td><td>After three rejections he lowered his sights and applied to smaller firms.<br>被拒了三次后，他放低了目标，改投小公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see the ˈsights</td><td>观光；游览名胜</td><td>We had one free day in Rome to see the sights properly.<br>在罗马我们有一整天空闲，好好逛了逛景点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set your sights ˈhigh/ˈlow</td><td>志向远大；目标不高</td><td>She set her sights high and applied to study medicine at Oxford.<br>她志向很高，申请去牛津读医学。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set your ˈsights on sth/on doing sth</td><td>立志要得到（或实现）某事</td><td>He's set his sights on running a marathon before he turns forty.<br>他立志要在四十岁前跑一次马拉松。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your sights ˈset on sth/on doing sth</td><td>一心想要得到（或做）某事</td><td>She has her sights set on a job with the United Nations.<br>她一心想进联合国工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sign</b></td><td>(be) a ˌsign of the ˈtimes</td><td>时代的特征；时势使然</td><td>Empty shops on the high street are a sign of the times.<br>商业街上空置的店铺就是这个时代的写照。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sign on the dotted ˈline (informal)</td><td>签字；正式同意</td><td>Read the contract twice before you sign on the dotted line.<br>签字之前，把合同看两遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sign your own ˈdeath warrant</td><td>自寻死路；自取灭亡</td><td>By insulting the investors he signed his own death warrant that evening.<br>那天晚上他得罪了投资人，等于自寻死路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>signed</b></td><td>ˌsigned, ˌsealed and deˈlivered</td><td>一切办妥；已成定局</td><td>The deal is signed, sealed and delivered, so we can celebrate tonight.<br>交易全部办妥，今晚可以庆祝了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsigned and ˈsealed</td><td>已签字盖章；板上钉钉</td><td>The contract is signed and sealed, so nobody can back out now.<br>合同已经签字盖章，谁也别想反悔。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>silence</b></td><td>ˌsilence is ˈgolden (saying)</td><td>沉默是金</td><td>In a meeting like that, silence is golden — say nothing at all.<br>那种会上沉默是金，一句都别说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>silent</b></td><td>give sb/get the ˈsilent treatment</td><td>对某人不理不睬；遭到冷落</td><td>She gave me the silent treatment for a week after our row.<br>吵完架她整整一周没理我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) ˌsilent as the ˈgrave</td><td>寂静无声；鸦雀无声</td><td>At three in the morning the whole village is silent as the grave.<br>凌晨三点，整个村子静得像坟场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌsilent maˈjority</td><td>沉默的大多数</td><td>Politicians love to claim they speak for the silent majority.<br>政客总爱说自己代表沉默的大多数。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>silk</b></td><td>make a silk ˌpurse out of a sow's ˈear</td><td>化腐朽为神奇；用劣材做精品</td><td>Renovating that ruin is making a silk purse out of a sow's ear.<br>把那片废墟翻新，简直是化腐朽为神奇。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>silly</b></td><td>ˌdrink, ˌlaugh, ˌshout, etc. yourself ˈsilly</td><td>喝（笑、喊等）得没了分寸</td><td>The kids laughed themselves silly at the clown's enormous flapping shoes.<br>小丑那双又大又晃的鞋逗得孩子们笑翻了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play ˈsilly buggers (with sth) (BrE, informal)</td><td>胡闹；瞎折腾</td><td>Stop playing silly buggers with the thermostat and let me work.<br>别再瞎捣鼓恒温器了，让我干活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈsilly season (BrE)</td><td>新闻淡季（多指夏季）</td><td>It must be the silly season; the front page is about a duck.<br>肯定是新闻淡季了，头版居然是只鸭子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>silver</b></td><td>(hand sth to sb) on a silver ˈplatter</td><td>拱手奉上；轻易给予</td><td>Nobody handed him success on a silver platter; he worked nights for years.<br>没人把成功端到他面前，他熬了好些年的夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the silver ˈscreen (old-fashioned)</td><td>银幕；电影业</td><td>Her grandmother was a star of the silver screen in the fifties.<br>她奶奶是五十年代的银幕明星。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sin</b></td><td>(as) miserable/ugly as ˈsin (spoken)</td><td>极其难看；愁眉苦脸</td><td>The old dog is ugly as sin but everybody in the street loves him.<br>那条老狗丑得要命，可整条街的人都喜欢它。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sincerely</b></td><td>Yours sinˈcerely (BrE) (AmE Sincerely (yours))</td><td>谨启；敬上（正式信函结尾语）</td><td>End the letter with 'Yours sincerely' when you know the person's name.<br>知道对方姓名时，信末用“谨启”收尾。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sine</b></td><td>a ˌsine qua ˈnon /ˌsɪneɪ kwɑː ˈnəʊn/ (from Latin, formal)</td><td>必要条件；必不可少的前提</td><td>Trust is a sine qua non of any lasting business partnership.<br>信任是任何长久商业合作的必要前提。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sing</b></td><td>sing a different ˈsong/ˈtune</td><td>改变论调；改弦更张</td><td>He'll sing a different tune once he sees the repair bill.<br>等他看到修车账单，调子就会变了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sing for your ˈsupper (old-fashioned)</td><td>先付出后受惠；为报答而效劳</td><td>Free tickets, but we had to sing for our supper by helping backstage.<br>票是免费的，可我们得去后台帮忙才算数。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sing from the same ˈsong/ˈhymn sheet</td><td>口径一致；步调统一</td><td>Before the press conference, make sure we're singing from the same hymn sheet.<br>开发布会前，先保证咱们口径一致。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sing sb's/sth's ˈpraises (informal)</td><td>大加赞扬；盛赞</td><td>My dentist keeps singing the praises of that electric toothbrush.<br>我的牙医一个劲儿地夸那款电动牙刷。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>singing</b></td><td>all ˈsinging, all ˈdancing (BrE, informal)</td><td>功能齐全的；花样繁多的</td><td>They installed an all-singing, all-dancing coffee machine nobody knows how to use.<br>他们装了台功能全得没人会用的咖啡机。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sink</b></td><td>sink your ˈdifferences</td><td>摒弃分歧；搁置争议</td><td>The two parties sank their differences long enough to pass the budget.<br>两党暂时放下分歧，把预算通过了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sink or ˈswim (saying)</td><td>不沉即浮；成败全靠自己</td><td>They threw me into the job and left me to sink or swim.<br>他们把我扔上岗位，是死是活全看自己。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sink so ˈlow • sink to sth</td><td>堕落到如此地步</td><td>I never thought he'd sink so low as to steal from friends.<br>我没想到他会堕落到偷朋友东西的地步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sink to sb's ˈlevel</td><td>自降身份，与某人一般见识</td><td>Don't sink to his level by shouting insults across the car park.<br>别隔着停车场骂回去，跟他一般见识。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sinking</b></td><td>(like rats) deserting/leaving a sinking ˈship</td><td>（如老鼠）弃船逃生；见势不妙就溜</td><td>Senior staff are leaving a sinking ship, and everyone can see it.<br>高层纷纷弃船而逃，明眼人都看得出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(get/have) a/that ˈsinking feeling (informal)</td><td>不祥的预感；心里发沉</td><td>I got that sinking feeling when I saw the exam paper.<br>一看到卷子，我心里就凉了半截。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sins</b></td><td>(do/be sth) for your sins (spoken, humorous, especially BrE)</td><td>算是报应；活该；倒霉</td><td>I coach the under-tens on Sundays, for my sins, every single week.<br>我每个周日都得带十岁以下的队，算我倒霉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sir</b></td><td>ˌno ˈsir! • ˌno sir ˈree! (spoken, especially AmE)</td><td>决不；绝对不行</td><td>No sir, I'm not lending him my car after last time.<br>绝对不行，上次之后我不会再借车给他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌyes ˈsir! • ˌyes sir ˈree! (spoken, especially AmE)</td><td>没错；的确如此</td><td>Yes sirree, that's the biggest pumpkin I've ever seen at the fair.<br>没错，这是我在集市上见过最大的南瓜。</td></tr>
