<tr><td><b>sisters</b></td><td>be (all) ˌbrothers/ˌsisters under the ˈskin</td><td>本质上都是一样的人</td><td>Rich or poor, we're all brothers under the skin when disaster strikes.<br>灾难来时，无论贫富，我们本质上都是一样的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sit</b></td><td>sit comfortably/easily/well (with sth)</td><td>与…相称；显得自然合适</td><td>His new job title doesn't sit comfortably with the way he actually behaves.<br>他的新头衔跟他的实际做派实在不搭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sit in ˈjudgement (on/over sb) (especially BrE)</td><td>对某人妄加评判</td><td>Who are you to sit in judgement on how I raise my own kids?<br>你凭什么对我怎么带孩子指手画脚？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(AmE usually sit in ˈjudgment (on/over sb))</td><td>对某人妄加评判；褒贬某人</td><td>The committee loves to sit in judgment over people who never asked for advice.<br>委员会最爱对没求教的人评头论足。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sit on the ˈfence</td><td>骑墙；持观望态度</td><td>Stop sitting on the fence and tell us which candidate you actually support.<br>别再骑墙了，说说你到底支持哪个候选人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sit ˈtight</td><td>原地不动；静观事态变化</td><td>Just sit tight until the storm passes and the roads reopen again.<br>先待着别动，等风暴过去道路重开。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sitting</b></td><td>be sitting pretty (informal)</td><td>处境优越；财运亨通</td><td>With two job offers in hand, she's sitting pretty for the first time.<br>手握两个录用通知，她头一回这么有底气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth in/at one ˈsitting</td><td>一口气做完某事</td><td>He finished the whole novel in one sitting and forgot to eat dinner.<br>他一口气读完整本小说，晚饭都忘了吃。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌsitting ˈduck/ˈtarget</td><td>易受攻击的人或物；活靶子</td><td>Parked out in the open, the old truck was a sitting duck for thieves.<br>停在空地上，那辆旧卡车成了小偷的活靶子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>situ</b></td><td>in ˈsitu (from Latin)</td><td>在原处；在原来位置</td><td>The archaeologists left the pottery in situ and photographed everything before digging.<br>考古队让陶器留在原处，开挖前先全部拍照。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>six</b></td><td>hit/knock sb/sth for ˈsix (BrE)</td><td>使某人大受打击；令某人震惊</td><td>The news of the layoffs knocked the whole department for six.<br>裁员的消息把整个部门打懵了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's six of ˌone and half a dozen of the ˈother (saying)</td><td>半斤八两；两者没什么两样</td><td>Bus or train? It's six of one and half a dozen of the other.<br>坐大巴还是火车？反正半斤八两。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>six feet ˈunder (informal, humorous)</td><td>已入土；死了</td><td>I'll be six feet under before I ever agree to that deal.<br>我死也不会答应那笔交易。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sixes</b></td><td>be at ˌsixes and ˈsevens (informal)</td><td>乱七八糟；不知所措</td><td>The office was at sixes and sevens the week after the move.<br>搬完家那一周，办公室里乱成一团。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sixth</b></td><td>a sixth ˈsense</td><td>第六感；直觉</td><td>Some sixth sense told her not to get into that car.<br>某种第六感告诉她别上那辆车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sixty-four</b></td><td>the sixty-four thousand dollar ˈquestion</td><td>难以回答的关键问题</td><td>Who's going to pay for all this? That's the sixty-four thousand dollar question.<br>这钱谁出？这才是最难回答的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(also the million dollar ˈquestion)</td><td>难以回答的重量级问题</td><td>Whether he'll actually show up is the million dollar question tonight.<br>他到底会不会来，这才是今晚的头号悬念。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sand dollar question for modern astronomy is ˈIs</td><td>当代天文学的重大难题</td><td>The sixty-four thousand dollar question for modern astronomy is: is anybody else out there?<br>当代天文学的头号难题是：宇宙别处还有生命吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>This phrase originated in the 1940s as ˈthe</td><td>该说法源于二十世纪四十年代</td><td>This phrase originated in the 1940s as the title of a popular American radio quiz.<br>这个说法源于四十年代一档美国热门广播问答节目。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>size</b></td><td>cut sb down to ˈsize</td><td>挫某人锐气；使有自知之明</td><td>One bad review was enough to cut the young director down to size.<br>一篇差评就把这位年轻导演的傲气打没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's about the ˈsize of it (spoken)</td><td>情况大致就是这样</td><td>So we're broke until payday? Yeah, that's about the size of it.<br>所以发薪前我们没钱了？对，大概就这样。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>skates</b></td><td>get/put your ˈskates on (BrE, informal)</td><td>赶快；抓紧时间</td><td>Get your skates on, the last train leaves in twelve minutes.<br>快点儿，末班车十二分钟后就开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>skeleton</b></td><td>a skeleton ˈcrew/ˈstaff/ˈservice</td><td>最低限度的人员；基本运转的服务</td><td>The hospital runs on a skeleton staff over the New Year holiday.<br>元旦假期医院只留最低限度的值班人员。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a skeleton in the ˈcupboard/ˈcloset</td><td>家丑；不可外扬的隐情</td><td>Every respectable family has a skeleton in the closet somewhere.<br>再体面的家庭也总有点不可外扬的隐情。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>skid</b></td><td>(on) skid row (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>潦倒落魄；住在贫民区</td><td>After the divorce he drank himself onto skid row within two years.<br>离婚后他酗酒，两年就沦落街头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>skids</b></td><td>on the ˈskids (informal)</td><td>逐渐衰落；走下坡路</td><td>Their marriage has been on the skids since he lost the business.<br>自从生意垮了，他们的婚姻就一直在走下坡路。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put the ˈskids under sb/sth (informal)</td><td>使失败；使停止</td><td>One leaked email put the skids under the entire merger plan.<br>一封外泄邮件就让整个并购计划泡了汤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>skin</b></td><td>be (all) brothers/sisters under the ˈskin</td><td>内心本质相同；同类人</td><td>Rich or poor, we're all brothers under the skin when disaster strikes.<br>灾难当头，不论贫富，人心都是一样的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be (all/just/nothing but) skin and ˈbone(s)</td><td>瘦得皮包骨</td><td>The stray dog was nothing but skin and bone when we found him.<br>我们发现那只流浪狗时，它瘦得只剩皮包骨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth by the ˌskin of your ˈteeth (informal)</td><td>勉强做成；险些没成</td><td>She passed the driving test by the skin of her teeth.<br>她驾照考试险险过关。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get under sb's ˈskin (informal)</td><td>惹恼某人；让某人念念不忘</td><td>His constant humming really gets under my skin during meetings.<br>他开会时不停哼歌，真把我惹毛了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/put skin in the ˈgame (AmE, especially business)</td><td>有切身利害；亲自投入风险</td><td>Investors trust founders who have real skin in the game.<br>投资人信任那些自己也押上身家的创始人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's no skin off ˈmy, ˈyour, ˈhis, etc. nose</td><td>与某人无关；对某人没损失</td><td>If they want to walk home in the rain, it's no skin off my nose.<br>他们想淋雨走回去，反正跟我没关系。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make your ˈskin crawl</td><td>使人毛骨悚然；让人起鸡皮疙瘩</td><td>The way he stared at us made my skin crawl.<br>他那样盯着我们看，让我浑身发毛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>skin sb aˈlive</td><td>严惩某人；扒了某人的皮</td><td>My mum will skin me alive if she finds out I skipped class.<br>我妈要是发现我逃课，非扒了我的皮不可。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(have) a thick/thin ˈskin (informal)</td><td>脸皮厚；脸皮薄</td><td>You need a thick skin to survive a year in customer service.<br>干一年客服，你得有副厚脸皮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>thin-ˈskinned adj.</td><td>脸皮薄的；敏感易怒的</td><td>He's too thin-skinned to work in politics for very long.<br>他脸皮太薄，在政坛待不长久。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>skinned</b></td><td>eyes keep your eyes open/peeled/skinned (for sb/sth)</td><td>留心察看；密切注意</td><td>Keep your eyes peeled for a red van parked near the gate.<br>留意一下门口附近停着的红色面包车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>skip</b></td><td>ˈskip it (spoken, informal)</td><td>别提了；不说这个了</td><td>Skip it, I don't want to argue about money again tonight.<br>算了，今晚我不想再为钱吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sky</b></td><td>the sky's the ˈlimit (spoken, informal)</td><td>前途无量；没有止境</td><td>With her talent and drive, the sky's the limit.<br>凭她的天赋和拼劲，前途不可限量。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slack</b></td><td>cut sb some ˈslack (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>对某人网开一面；宽容些</td><td>Cut him some slack, it's only his second day on the job.<br>别太苛刻，他才上班第二天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take up the ˈslack</td><td>补上空缺；充分利用闲置人力</td><td>When two colleagues quit, the rest of us took up the slack.<br>两个同事辞职后，剩下的人把活儿补上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slam</b></td><td>be a ˈslam dunk (AmE)</td><td>是十拿九稳的事</td><td>With that evidence, winning the case should be a slam dunk.<br>有那份证据，这官司赢定了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slanging</b></td><td>a ˈslanging match (BrE, informal)</td><td>互相谩骂；对骂</td><td>The debate turned into a slanging match within about ten minutes.<br>辩论不到十分钟就变成了对骂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slap</b></td><td>(a bit of) slap and ˈtickle (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>打情骂俏；亲昵嬉闹</td><td>They snuck off for a bit of slap and tickle behind the shed.<br>他们溜到棚子后面卿卿我我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a slap in the ˈface</td><td>一记耳光；侮辱与打击</td><td>Being passed over for promotion again was a real slap in the face.<br>又一次没能升职，真是狠狠一记耳光。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a slap on the ˈwrist (informal)</td><td>轻微惩罚；小小警告</td><td>He crashed the company car and got only a slap on the wrist.<br>他撞了公司的车，却只挨了轻描淡写的一句批评。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slate</b></td><td>(put sth) on the ˈslate (informal (put sth) on your account in a shop, a bar, etc.)</td><td>赊账；记账</td><td>Put the drinks on the slate and I'll settle up on Friday.<br>酒钱先记账，周五我一起结。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slaughter</b></td><td>(like) a lamb/lambs to the ˈslaughter</td><td>像待宰羔羊；不知危险地前往</td><td>The new recruits walked into that meeting like lambs to the slaughter.<br>新来的几个人像待宰羔羊一样进了会议室。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slave</b></td><td>be a slave to/of sth</td><td>是…的奴隶；受…支配</td><td>He's become a slave to his phone and checks it every minute.<br>他成了手机的奴隶，一分钟看一次。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sleep</b></td><td>be able to do sth in your ˈsleep (informal)</td><td>闭着眼也会做；轻车熟路</td><td>After ten years here, I could do this paperwork in my sleep.<br>干了十年，这些表格我闭着眼都能填。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to ˈsleep (informal)</td><td>手脚发麻；肢体麻木</td><td>I sat cross-legged too long and my left foot went to sleep.<br>盘腿坐太久，我左脚麻了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not sleep a ˈwink ◆ not get a ˈwink of sleep</td><td>一夜没合眼</td><td>The neighbours' party meant I didn't sleep a wink last night.<br>邻居开派对，我昨晚一眼没合。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb/sth to ˈsleep</td><td>使麻醉；给动物实施安乐死</td><td>The vet gently explained that we'd have to put the old dog to sleep.<br>兽医委婉地说，得让这条老狗安乐死了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sleep like a ˈlog/ˈtop (also sleep like a ˈbaby)</td><td>睡得很沉</td><td>After that ten-mile hike I slept like a log all night.<br>走了十英里山路，我一夜睡得像死猪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈsleep on it</td><td>把某事留到第二天再决定</td><td>Don't answer them tonight; sleep on it and call back tomorrow morning.<br>今晚别答复，睡一觉明早再回电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sleep ˈtight! (informal, spoken)</td><td>睡个好觉</td><td>Goodnight, kiddo, sleep tight and don't let the bedbugs bite.<br>晚安，小家伙，睡个好觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sleeping</b></td><td>let ˌsleeping dogs ˈlie (saying)</td><td>别惹麻烦；不要旧事重提</td><td>She's finally calmed down, so let sleeping dogs lie for now.<br>她好不容易消气了，这事就别再提了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sleeve</b></td><td>have an ˌace/a ˌtrick up your ˈsleeve (BrE)</td><td>留有一手；有锦囊妙计</td><td>Don't count him out; he always has an ace up his sleeve.<br>别以为他输定了，他总留着一手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(AmE have an ˌace in the ˈhole) (informal)</td><td>暗藏王牌；留有后招</td><td>The coach had an ace in the hole: a striker nobody had scouted.<br>教练藏着张王牌：一个没人考察过的前锋。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/keep sth up your ˈsleeve (informal)</td><td>暗中留着后手以备不时之需</td><td>I've got one more argument up my sleeve if they refuse.<br>他们要是拒绝，我还留着一个理由。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sleight</b></td><td>ˌsleight of ˈhand</td><td>巧妙的手法；障眼法</td><td>The budget balances only through some clever sleight of hand with the numbers.<br>这预算能平衡，全靠在数字上耍了点花招。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slice</b></td><td>a ˌslice of ˈlife</td><td>现实生活的一个侧面</td><td>The film is a quiet slice of life about three taxi drivers.<br>这部电影平静地截取了三个出租车司机的生活片段。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sliced</b></td><td>best the best thing since sliced bread</td><td>极好的东西；了不起的发明</td><td>He thinks his new coffee machine is the best thing since sliced bread.<br>他觉得他的新咖啡机简直是伟大发明。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slightest</b></td><td>not in the ˈslightest</td><td>一点也不；毫不</td><td>No, her comments didn't bother me in the slightest.<br>不，她那些话我一点都不介意。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sling</b></td><td>sling your ˈhook (BrE, informal)</td><td>走开；滚蛋</td><td>He told the reporters to sling their hook and slammed the door.<br>他叫记者们滚开，砰地关上了门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slings</b></td><td>the ˌslings and ˈarrows (of sth)</td><td>某事带来的种种磨难</td><td>She endured the slings and arrows of tabloid gossip for years.<br>她多年忍受小报流言的种种中伤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈthe slings and arrows of outrageous fortune'.</td><td>命运无情的摧残（出自《哈姆雷特》）</td><td>Hamlet asks whether to suffer the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune.<br>哈姆雷特问，是否该忍受命运无情的摧残。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slip</b></td><td>give sb the ˈslip (informal)</td><td>甩掉追踪者；摆脱某人</td><td>The thief gave the police the slip in the crowded market.<br>小偷在拥挤的市场里甩掉了警察。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let ˈslip sth</td><td>说漏嘴；无意中泄露</td><td>She let slip that they'd already chosen someone else for the job.<br>她说漏了嘴，他们已经另选了人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>slip sb's ˈmemory/ˈmind</td><td>忘记；想不起来</td><td>Sorry I missed your birthday, it completely slipped my mind.<br>抱歉错过你生日，我全给忘了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈslip of a boy, girl, etc. (old-fashioned)</td><td>瘦小的男孩或女孩；小不点儿</td><td>She was just a slip of a girl when she left the village.<br>她离开村子时还是个瘦小的小姑娘。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a slip of the ˈtongue/ˈpen</td><td>口误；笔误</td><td>Calling her by his ex's name was an unfortunate slip of the tongue.<br>把她叫成前女友的名字，真是要命的口误。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>slip on a baˈnana skin (informal)</td><td>当众出丑；犯低级错误</td><td>The minister slipped on a banana skin by misquoting his own report.<br>部长引错了自己的报告，当众出了洋相。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>slip through sb's ˈfingers</td><td>从手中溜走；被错过</td><td>He let a golden opportunity slip through his fingers last spring.<br>去年春天他让一个大好机会白白溜走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>slip through the ˈnet</td><td>漏网；被疏漏</td><td>A few faulty batteries slipped through the net during inspection.<br>几块次品电池在检验中漏了网。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's ˌmany a ˈslip (ˈtwixt ˌcup and ˈlip)</td><td>事情难料；万事难十拿九稳</td><td>The deal looks certain, but there's many a slip twixt cup and lip.<br>交易看着十拿九稳，可变数总是难免。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>before 7 oˈclock, but there's many a slip ˈtwixt cup</td><td>还没到手就别高兴太早</td><td>We should arrive before 7 o'clock, but there's many a slip twixt cup and lip.<br>我们应该七点前能到，不过意外总难免。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slippery</b></td><td>(as) slippery as an ˈeel (informal)</td><td>滑头；狡猾难缠</td><td>Ask him a direct question and he's as slippery as an eel.<br>你直接问他，他就滑得像条泥鳅。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>straight as a die (2)</td><td>笔直的；正直诚实的</td><td>You can trust old Frank, he's as straight as a die.<br>老弗兰克你尽管信，他为人正派得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the slippery ˈslope</td><td>危险的下坡路；每况愈下的开端</td><td>One skipped payment can start you down the slippery slope into debt.<br>漏还一期，就可能滑向负债的深渊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slipping</b></td><td>be ˈslipping (informal)</td><td>水平下降；不如从前</td><td>You forgot the passwords again? You must be slipping.<br>你又忘了密码？看来你是退步了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slouch</b></td><td>be no ˈslouch (at sth/at doing sth) (informal)</td><td>很在行；干得很出色</td><td>She's no slouch at fixing engines, despite what the guys assume.<br>别看那些人小瞧她，修发动机她可是行家。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slow</b></td><td>do a slow ˈburn (AmE, informal)</td><td>慢慢冒火；越想越气</td><td>He said nothing but did a slow burn all through dinner.<br>他一声没吭，整顿饭都在暗自窝火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈslow (on sth)</td><td>放慢速度；怠工</td><td>Management asked us to go slow on hiring until spring.<br>管理层要求春天前放慢招聘节奏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈslow lane</td><td>落在后面；处于慢车道</td><td>Their factory is stuck in the slow lane while rivals automate everything.<br>对手全面自动化，他们的工厂却还在慢车道上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slowly</b></td><td>slowly but ˈsurely</td><td>缓慢而稳步地</td><td>Slowly but surely, she paid off every penny of the loan.<br>她慢慢地却踏实地把贷款一分不差还清了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slum</b></td><td>ˈslum it (informal, often humorous)</td><td>将就过简陋日子</td><td>We slummed it in a tiny hostel to save money for flights.<br>我们挤在小旅舍将就，把钱省下来买机票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sly</b></td><td>do sth on the ˈsly</td><td>偷偷做某事</td><td>He's been smoking on the sly behind the garage for months.<br>他在车库后面偷偷抽了好几个月烟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>small</b></td><td>be grateful/thankful for small ˈmercies</td><td>庆幸情况没有更糟</td><td>The car's damaged but nobody was hurt, so be thankful for small mercies.<br>车坏了但没人受伤，该知足了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's a ˌsmall ˈworld (saying)</td><td>世界真小</td><td>You know my cousin too? It's a small world.<br>你也认识我表哥？世界真小。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look/feel ˈsmall (also feel ˈthat high)</td><td>感到难堪；觉得自己渺小</td><td>His sarcastic reply in front of everyone made me feel small.<br>他当众那句挖苦，让我抬不起头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>small ˈbeer (BrE) (AmE small poˈtatoes)</td><td>无足轻重的事物</td><td>A hundred pounds is small beer compared with what they lost.<br>跟他们的损失比，一百英镑不值一提。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌsmall ˈfortune (informal)</td><td>一大笔钱</td><td>That wedding must have cost them a small fortune.<br>那场婚礼准花了他们一大笔钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈsmall fry (informal)</td><td>小人物；无关紧要的小公司</td><td>The police caught the small fry but the ringleaders escaped.<br>警方抓到的都是小喽啰，头目跑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈsmall print (BrE) (AmE the ˈfine print)</td><td>合同中的附属细则</td><td>Always read the small print before you sign a rental agreement.<br>签租房合同前一定要看清附加条款。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the small ˈscreen</td><td>电视屏幕（相对电影而言）</td><td>After three blockbusters, the actor returned to the small screen.<br>拍完三部大片后，这位演员重回电视荧屏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(make) ˈsmall talk</td><td>闲聊；寒暄</td><td>I'm terrible at making small talk with strangers at parties.<br>在派对上跟陌生人寒暄，我特别不在行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hours the small/early hours</td><td>凌晨时分；后半夜</td><td>They argued into the small hours and woke the whole building.<br>他们吵到后半夜，把整栋楼都吵醒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smart</b></td><td>a ˈsmart alec/aleck (informal, disapproving)</td><td>自作聪明的人</td><td>Some smart alec at the back kept correcting the teacher's grammar.<br>后排有个自作聪明的家伙老纠正老师的语法。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a smart ˈcookie (AmE, informal)</td><td>机灵的人；聪明人</td><td>Give her the case, she's one smart cookie under pressure.<br>这案子交给她，她压力下特别机灵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˈsmart money is on sb/sth</td><td>内行看好某人或某事</td><td>The smart money is on the underdog winning tonight's final.<br>内行都看好弱队赢下今晚的决赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smash</b></td><td>smash sb's ˈface/head in (BrE, informal)</td><td>把某人打得头破血流</td><td>He threatened to smash my face in over a parking space.<br>为个车位，他扬言要打得我满脸开花。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌsmash ˈhit (informal)</td><td>轰动之作；一炮而红的作品</td><td>Her debut album was a smash hit across three continents.<br>她的首张专辑在三大洲都火得一塌糊涂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smell</b></td><td>smell a ˈrat (informal)</td><td>觉得可疑；察觉有诈</td><td>When he offered to pay in cash upfront, I smelled a rat.<br>他提出预付现金时，我就觉得不对劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smelling</b></td><td>come up/out of sth smelling of ˈroses (informal)</td><td>全身而退；名声无损</td><td>Somehow he came out of the scandal smelling of roses.<br>不知怎的，他从丑闻里全身而退。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smile</b></td><td>ear beam/grin/smile from ear to ear</td><td>笑得合不拢嘴</td><td>She was grinning from ear to ear when they handed her the trophy.<br>他们把奖杯递给她时，她笑得合不拢嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smiles</b></td><td>be all ˈsmiles</td><td>满面笑容；喜笑颜开</td><td>He was all smiles after hearing the test results.<br>听到检查结果后，他一脸笑容。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smithereens</b></td><td>blow, smash, etc. sth to smitheˈreens (informal)</td><td>把某物炸得或砸得粉碎</td><td>The old chimney was blown to smithereens in about three seconds.<br>那根老烟囱三秒钟就被炸得粉碎。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smoke</b></td><td>go up in ˈsmoke</td><td>被烧毁；化为泡影</td><td>Twenty years of savings went up in smoke when the business failed.<br>生意一垮，二十年积蓄化为乌有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>smoke and ˈmirrors</td><td>障眼法；掩人耳目的手段</td><td>The company's growth figures turned out to be pure smoke and mirrors.<br>这家公司的增长数字纯属障眼法。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>smoke like a ˈchimney (informal)</td><td>烟抽得极凶</td><td>My grandfather smoked like a chimney right up to his eightieth birthday.<br>我爷爷一直抽烟抽得凶，直到八十岁生日。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no ˌsmoke without ˈfire (BrE) (AmE)</td><td>无风不起浪</td><td>I don't believe every rumour, but there's no smoke without fire.<br>我不是全信谣言，可无风不起浪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>where there's smoke, there's ˈfire) (saying)</td><td>无火不生烟；事出必有因</td><td>Three people complained about him, and where there's smoke, there's fire.<br>三个人投诉他，无火不生烟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smokescreen</b></td><td>a ˈsmokescreen</td><td>烟幕；掩饰真实意图的说辞</td><td>His jokes are a smokescreen to hide how nervous he really is.<br>他开玩笑只是烟幕，掩饰他有多紧张。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smoking</b></td><td>a/the ˌsmoking ˈgun</td><td>确凿证据；铁证</td><td>The auditors finally found the smoking gun in an old email thread.<br>审计人员终于在一串旧邮件里找到了铁证。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>smooth</b></td><td>(as) smooth as ˈsilk (also (as) smooth as a baby's ˈbottom humorous)</td><td>光滑如丝；极其顺滑</td><td>After sanding and two coats, the tabletop was as smooth as silk.<br>打磨加两遍漆后，桌面光滑如丝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>smooth the ˈpath/ˈway</td><td>铺平道路；扫清障碍</td><td>Her introduction smoothed the way for our meeting with the mayor.<br>她的引荐为我们见市长铺平了路。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>smooth (sb's) ruffled ˈfeathers</td><td>使某人息怒；安抚情绪</td><td>It took two apologies to smooth the client's ruffled feathers.<br>道了两次歉才把客户的火气压下去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snail</b></td><td>at a ˈsnail's pace (informal)</td><td>慢吞吞地；像蜗牛爬</td><td>Traffic crawled along the motorway at a snail's pace all morning.<br>整个上午高速上的车都在蜗牛似地爬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈsnail mail (informal, humorous)</td><td>蜗牛邮递；普通邮寄</td><td>Just email it, snail mail would take another five days.<br>发邮件吧，寄信还得再等五天。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snake</b></td><td>a ˌsnake in the ˈgrass (disapproving)</td><td>笑面虎；伪装成朋友的阴险小人</td><td>He smiled at us all week, the snake in the grass.<br>他笑了整整一周，真是个笑面虎。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snap</b></td><td>be a ˈsnap (AmE, informal)</td><td>轻而易举的事</td><td>With the new software, filing taxes is a snap.<br>用了新软件，报税轻而易举。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>snap your ˈfingers</td><td>打响指</td><td>He snapped his fingers at the waiter, which everyone found rude.<br>他冲服务员打响指，大家都觉得没礼貌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsnap ˈout of it ◆ ˌsnap sb ˈout of it (informal)</td><td>使摆脱郁闷；振作起来</td><td>You've been moping for a week, snap out of it.<br>你都消沉一星期了，振作点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>snap ˈto it (informal)</td><td>赶快；加把劲</td><td>Snap to it, those boxes won't load themselves.<br>快点儿，那些箱子不会自己上车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snappy</b></td><td>ˌmake it ˈsnappy (informal)</td><td>快点；抓紧</td><td>Order whatever you want, but make it snappy, we're late.<br>想点什么随你，但快点，我们迟到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snatches</b></td><td>in ˈsnatches</td><td>断断续续地</td><td>With a newborn at home, I only sleep in snatches.<br>家里有新生儿，我只能断断续续地睡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sneak</b></td><td>a ˌsneak ˈpreview</td><td>内部预映；抢先预览</td><td>Fans got a sneak preview of the film two weeks before release.<br>影迷在上映前两周看了内部试映。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sneezed</b></td><td>not to be ˈsneezed/ˈsniffed at (informal)</td><td>不可小看；值得认真对待</td><td>A ten per cent discount is not to be sneezed at.<br>九折优惠可不能小看。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sneezes</b></td><td>when A ˈsneezes, B catches a ˈcold (also if A)</td><td>甲有风吹草动，乙就跟着遭殃</td><td>When Wall Street sneezes, the rest of the world catches a cold.<br>华尔街一打喷嚏，全世界就感冒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>catches a ˈcold, B gets pneuˈmonia less frequent)</td><td>甲感冒，乙就得肺炎；牵连更重</td><td>If America catches a cold, smaller economies get pneumonia.<br>美国一感冒，小经济体就得肺炎。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sniff</b></td><td>have a (good) ˌsniff aˈround</td><td>四处打探；仔细察看</td><td>Let me have a good sniff around the garage before we buy it.<br>买之前让我把这车库仔细看一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not get a ˈsniff of sth (informal)</td><td>连边都沾不上；根本得不到</td><td>The reserves never got a sniff of the ball all afternoon.<br>整个下午替补球员连球都没碰到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sniffles</b></td><td>get, have, etc. the ˈsniffles (informal)</td><td>患轻感冒；伤风</td><td>Half the class has the sniffles this week.<br>这周班里一半人都感冒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snit</b></td><td>be in a ˈsnit (AmE)</td><td>生闷气；闹脾气</td><td>She's been in a snit since I forgot to call back.<br>自我忘了回电话，她就一直闹别扭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snow</b></td><td>a ˈsnow job (AmE, informal)</td><td>花言巧语的蒙骗</td><td>That sales pitch was a total snow job from start to finish.<br>那套推销说辞从头到尾都是蒙人的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snowball</b></td><td>not have a ˌsnowball's chance in ˈhell (of doing sth) (informal)</td><td>毫无可能；机会渺茫</td><td>We don't have a snowball's chance in hell of finishing by Friday.<br>我们周五前完工是绝无可能的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sporting chance</td><td>取胜的可能；公平的机会</td><td>Give the kid a sporting chance and let him try the audition.<br>给这孩子个机会，让他去试镜吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snowed</b></td><td>be snowed ˈunder (with sth)</td><td>忙得不可开交；应接不暇</td><td>I'm snowed under with marking until the end of term.<br>期末前我被批作业埋得喘不过气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snuff</b></td><td>ˈsnuff it (BrE, slang, humorous)</td><td>咽气；蹬腿</td><td>The old cat finally snuffed it at the age of twenty.<br>那只老猫活到二十岁终于走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up to ˈsnuff (informal)</td><td>达到标准；身体状况良好</td><td>The kitchen wasn't up to snuff, so the inspector closed it.<br>厨房不达标，检查员把它关了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snuffles</b></td><td>get, have, etc. the ˈsnuffles (informal)</td><td>患感冒；鼻塞流涕</td><td>The baby's had the snuffles since the weather turned.<br>天一变，宝宝就一直鼻塞流涕。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>snug</b></td><td>(as) snug as a bug (in a rug) (informal, humorous)</td><td>非常温暖舒适</td><td>Wrapped in two blankets, she was as snug as a bug in a rug.<br>裹着两条毯子，她舒服得不得了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>SO</b></td><td>be so much/many sth</td><td>完全是；不过是</td><td>His promises were so much hot air, as everyone soon discovered.<br>他的承诺不过是空话，大家很快就看出来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>or ˈso</td><td>大约；左右</td><td>The whole repair should take an hour or so.<br>整个维修大概要一小时左右。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈso much/many (sth)</td><td>若干；一定数量的</td><td>Each guest is allowed so many drinks and no more.<br>每位客人只能喝规定杯数，不能再多。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>soaked</b></td><td>be/get ˌsoaked to the ˈskin</td><td>浑身湿透</td><td>We got soaked to the skin waiting twenty minutes for the bus.<br>等了二十分钟公交，我们浑身湿透。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>soapbox</b></td><td>be/get on your ˈsoapbox (informal)</td><td>大发议论；发表长篇高论</td><td>Don't mention taxes or he'll get on his soapbox again.<br>别提税的事，不然他又要长篇大论了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sob</b></td><td>sob your ˈheart out</td><td>伤心痛哭</td><td>She sobbed her heart out in the car after the funeral.<br>葬礼后她在车里哭得死去活来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈsob story (informal, disapproving)</td><td>博取同情的伤感故事</td><td>He turned up with another sob story about needing rent money.<br>他又编了套没钱交房租的苦情故事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sober</b></td><td>(as) sober as a judge</td><td>十分清醒；滴酒未沾</td><td>I only had juice all night; I'm as sober as a judge.<br>我整晚只喝了果汁，清醒得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>OPP (as) drunk as a lord</td><td>烂醉如泥</td><td>He came home as drunk as a lord and fell over the doormat.<br>他烂醉如泥地回家，绊在门垫上摔倒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sock</b></td><td>put a ˈsock in it (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>住嘴；别出声</td><td>Put a sock in it, some of us are trying to sleep.<br>闭嘴吧，有人还想睡觉呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>To play records more quietly, people used to ˈsock it to sb (informal or humorous)</td><td>痛快地说给某人听；狠狠还击</td><td>Get up there and sock it to them, they won't know what hit them.<br>上去给他们点厉害瞧瞧，让他们发懵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>socks</b></td><td>blow/knock sb's ˈsocks off (informal)</td><td>让某人大为惊叹</td><td>Her performance in the second act knocked our socks off.<br>她第二幕的表演把我们震住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sod</b></td><td>ˌSod's ˈLaw (BrE, humorous)</td><td>墨菲定律；越怕什么越来什么</td><td>Sod's Law says it'll rain the one day I forget my umbrella.<br>按墨菲定律，我忘带伞那天准下雨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>soft</b></td><td>be/go soft in the ˈhead (informal, disapproving)</td><td>脑子不正常；犯傻</td><td>Lending him money again? You must be going soft in the head.<br>又借钱给他？你脑子是不是坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a soft ˈspot for sb/sth (informal)</td><td>对某人或某物情有独钟</td><td>She's tough with everyone but has a soft spot for the youngest apprentice.<br>她对谁都严，唯独偏爱最小的学徒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>option the soft/easy option</td><td>省事的选择；轻松的出路</td><td>Quitting now would be the easy option, but I'd regret it.<br>现在放弃是省事，可我会后悔。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sold</b></td><td>be ˈsold on sth (informal)</td><td>热衷于；深信不疑</td><td>I'm not sold on the new logo, honestly.<br>说实话，新标志我不太买账。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>solid</b></td><td>(as) solid as a ˈrock</td><td>坚如磐石；十分可靠</td><td>Through all the chaos, her support was as solid as a rock.<br>在一片混乱中，她的支持坚如磐石。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>some</b></td><td>ˈsome such</td><td>诸如此类的；类似的</td><td>He said he was a consultant or some such thing.<br>他说自己是顾问还是别的什么类似的职业。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>something</b></td><td>have something ˈon sb (informal)</td><td>掌握某人的把柄</td><td>The editor clearly has something on him, or he'd have quit already.<br>编辑显然抓着他的把柄，不然他早辞职了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ing like nothing on sb (2) ˈsth</td><td>诸如此类的事物</td><td>She wants a cottage, a dog, something like that.<br>她想要个小屋、一条狗，诸如此类的东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>something ˈelse</td><td>了不起的人或事；另当别论</td><td>Honestly, that last goal in the final was really something else.<br>说实话，决赛最后那个进球真是绝了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈsomething like that ◆ ˌsomething like ˈsb/</td><td>类似的；大约</td><td>It cost three hundred pounds or something like that.<br>那东西花了三百英镑左右吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>our walk home turned out to be something of there's ˈsomething about sb/sth</td><td>某人或某物有点特别之处</td><td>There's something about that old house that makes me uneasy.<br>那所老房子总有点让我心里发毛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>son</b></td><td>a/the ˌson of a ˈbitch (also SOB especially in)</td><td>混蛋；王八蛋</td><td>That son of a bitch took my parking space again this morning.<br>那混蛋今早又抢了我的车位。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˌson of a ˈgun (AmE, informal, spoken)</td><td>家伙；捣蛋鬼</td><td>Well, you old son of a gun, I haven't seen you in years.<br>嘿，你这老家伙，好多年没见了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>song</b></td><td>(buy sth, go, etc.) for a ˈsong (informal)</td><td>极便宜地买到或卖掉</td><td>They picked up the piano for a song at a house clearance.<br>他们在清仓拍卖上用极低的价钱买下那架钢琴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a song and ˈdance about sth (informal, disapproving)</td><td>小题大做；大惊小怪</td><td>Don't make a song and dance about one late email.<br>一封邮件晚了而已，别小题大做。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈsong (informal)</td><td>状态极佳；表现出色</td><td>The whole team was on song in the second half.<br>下半场全队状态火热。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌanytime ˈsoon (especially AmE)</td><td>很快；短期内</td><td>I don't think prices will drop anytime soon.<br>我看短期内价格不会降。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>none too ˈsoon</td><td>来得正是时候；差点就晚了</td><td>The ambulance finally arrived at the scene, and none too soon.<br>救护车总算赶到现场，一点也不早。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lamp in the children's room. ˈNone too soon.</td><td>早该做了；来得正及时</td><td>I finally fixed the lamp in the children's room. None too soon.<br>我总算把孩子房里的灯修好了，早该修了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sooner</b></td><td>no ˌsooner ˌsaid than ˈdone</td><td>说到就做到；一说就办妥</td><td>She asked for extra chairs and, no sooner said than done, they appeared.<br>她要多加几把椅子，说到就做到，椅子马上就来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no sooner...than... (written)</td><td>刚…就…</td><td>No sooner had we sat down than the fire alarm went off.<br>我们刚坐下，火警就响了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌsooner the ˈbetter</td><td>越早越好</td><td>Book the tickets, and the sooner the better.<br>赶紧订票，越早越好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sooner or ˈlater</td><td>迟早；早晚</td><td>Sooner or later he'll have to tell his parents the truth.<br>他迟早得把实情告诉父母。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sooner rather than ˈlater</td><td>宜早不宜迟</td><td>We need that decision sooner rather than later.<br>这个决定我们得尽早拿到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I, etc. would sooner do sth (than sth else)</td><td>宁愿做某事</td><td>I'd sooner walk home than squeeze onto that bus.<br>我宁愿走回家，也不挤那班车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sore</b></td><td>a ˌsore ˈpoint (with sb)</td><td>痛处；忌讳的话题</td><td>Don't mention the promotion, it's a sore point with her.<br>别提升职的事，那是她的痛处。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stand/stick out like a sore ˈthumb (informal)</td><td>格格不入；扎眼</td><td>In jeans at that black-tie dinner, he stuck out like a sore thumb.<br>在正装晚宴上穿牛仔裤，他显得特别扎眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sorrow</b></td><td>do sth more in ˌsorrow than in ˈanger</td><td>出于痛心而非愤怒</td><td>She wrote the resignation letter more in sorrow than in anger.<br>她写辞职信更多是出于痛心而非气愤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sorry</b></td><td>be/feel ˈsorry for sb</td><td>同情某人</td><td>I felt sorry for the driver stuck in that downpour.<br>我很同情那个困在暴雨里的司机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/feel ˈsorry for yourself (informal, disapproving)</td><td>自怨自艾；自我可怜</td><td>Stop feeling sorry for yourself and go apply for something else.<br>别自怨自艾了，去投别的工作吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'm ˈsorry to say</td><td>我很遗憾地说</td><td>I'm sorry to say the repairs will cost more than we thought.<br>很遗憾，维修费比我们想的要高。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sorts</b></td><td>be, feel, etc. out of ˈsorts (especially BrE)</td><td>身体不适；心情不佳</td><td>She's been out of sorts since the flight home.<br>从回国的航班下来后她就一直不太舒服。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it takes all ˈsorts (to make a ˈworld) (saying)</td><td>林子大了什么鸟都有</td><td>He collects vacuum cleaners? Well, it takes all sorts.<br>他收集吸尘器？林子大了什么鸟都有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of ˈsorts (informal)</td><td>勉强算得上的；凑合的</td><td>We made a meal of sorts out of rice and old vegetables.<br>我们用米和剩菜凑合做了顿饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>soul</b></td><td>be the soul of sth</td><td>是…的化身；十分…</td><td>The old porter was the soul of discretion about the guests.<br>那位老门房对客人的事守口如瓶。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>good for the ˈsoul (humorous)</td><td>对身心有益；苦中有益</td><td>Cold showers in winter are supposedly good for the soul.<br>冬天冲冷水澡据说对身心有好处。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sound</b></td><td>like, love, etc. the ˌsound of your own</td><td>爱听自己说话；喜欢滔滔不绝</td><td>He just loves the sound of his own voice at these meetings.<br>开这种会他就爱听自己说个没完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈvoice (disapproving)</td><td>喜欢说个没完；自我陶醉地讲话</td><td>The chairman likes the sound of his own voice far too much.<br>主席太爱听自己讲话了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) sound as a ˈbell (informal)</td><td>状况极佳；十分健康</td><td>The old van's engine is still as sound as a bell.<br>那辆旧货车的发动机还好得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sound aˈsleep</td><td>熟睡的；睡得很香</td><td>By nine o'clock both kids were sound asleep.<br>九点钟两个孩子就睡熟了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sound the ˈdeath knell of sth</td><td>敲响…的丧钟；宣告…终结</td><td>Streaming sounded the death knell of the local video shop.<br>流媒体敲响了本地录像店的丧钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>soup</b></td><td>be in the ˈsoup ◆ land yourself/sb in the ˈsoup (informal)</td><td>使陷入困境；给某人惹麻烦</td><td>His careless remark landed the whole team in the soup.<br>他一句失言把全队害惨了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from ˌsoup to ˈnuts (AmE, informal)</td><td>从头到尾；一应俱全</td><td>She planned the wedding from soup to nuts in six weeks.<br>她六周内把婚礼从头到尾安排妥当。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>grapes</b></td><td>sour ˈgrapes (saying)</td><td>酸葡萄心理</td><td>Calling the prize meaningless is just sour grapes.<br>说那奖没意义，纯属吃不到葡萄说葡萄酸。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>A fox cannot reach some grapes so he decides</td><td>狐狸够不着葡萄的寓言</td><td>A fox cannot reach some grapes, so he decides they must be sour anyway.<br>狐狸够不着葡萄，就认定葡萄是酸的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sow</b></td><td>sow your wild ˈoats (informal)</td><td>年轻时纵情玩乐；放荡不羁</td><td>He sowed his wild oats in his twenties and settled down at thirty.<br>他二十几岁玩够了，三十岁就安定下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>reap you reap what you sow</td><td>种瓜得瓜；自食其果</td><td>He cheated his partners for years; you reap what you sow.<br>他坑了合伙人多年，如今自食其果。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>space</b></td><td>in the space of a ˈminute, an ˈhour, a ˈmorning, etc.</td><td>在一个上午等时段之内</td><td>In the space of a morning she cleared the whole attic.<br>一个上午的工夫，她把整个阁楼清空了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>during the period of a minute, an hour, etc.</td><td>在一分钟、一小时等时段内</td><td>Everything changed during the period of a minute on that platform.<br>在站台上那一分钟里，一切都变了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look/stare/gaze into ˈspace</td><td>茫然出神地望着前方</td><td>He sat staring into space long after the phone call ended.<br>电话挂了很久，他还坐在那儿发呆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>breathing a breathing space</td><td>喘息的机会；短暂的间歇</td><td>The loan gave the shop a breathing space until Christmas.<br>这笔贷款让小店撑到圣诞节前有了喘息之机。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spades</b></td><td>in ˈspades (informal)</td><td>大量地；十足地</td><td>She's got determination in spades, whatever else you say.<br>别的先不说，她的决心是十足的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spanner</b></td><td>put/throw a ˈspanner in the works (BrE)</td><td>从中作梗；破坏计划</td><td>The strike threw a spanner in the works of our launch plan.<br>罢工把我们的发布计划全搅乱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(AmE throw a (monkey) ˈwrench in the works)</td><td>破坏计划；阻挠进程</td><td>One missing signature threw a wrench in the works for weeks.<br>少了一个签名，事情卡了好几周。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spare</b></td><td>go ˈspare (BrE, informal)</td><td>大发雷霆；气急败坏</td><td>Dad went spare when he saw the scratch on the car.<br>爸看到车上的划痕，气得暴跳如雷。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spare sb's ˈfeelings</td><td>顾及某人感受；避免让人难过</td><td>She lied about the painting to spare his feelings.<br>为了照顾他的感受，她对那幅画说了谎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌspare the ˈrod and ˌspoil the ˈchild (saying)</td><td>孩子不打不成器</td><td>My grandmother believed in spare the rod and spoil the child.<br>我奶奶信奉孩子不打不成器那一套。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌspare ˈtyre (BrE) (AmE a ˌspare ˈtire)</td><td>腰间赘肉</td><td>Six months of desk work gave him a definite spare tyre.<br>伏案六个月，他腰上明显长出一圈赘肉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈspare</td><td>多余的；富余的</td><td>We arrived at the airport with two hours to spare.<br>我们到机场时还富余两个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sparks</b></td><td>fly the feathers/fur/sparks will fly</td><td>将大吵一架；将闹得不可开交</td><td>Put those two in one room and the sparks will fly.<br>把那两个人关一个屋里，非吵翻天不可。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spate</b></td><td>in (full) ˈspate (especially BrE)</td><td>河水暴涨；洪水泛滥</td><td>After three days of rain the river was in full spate.<br>下了三天雨，河水暴涨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>speak</b></td><td>no sth/nothing/not anything to ˈspeak of so to ˈspeak (also ˌas it ˈwere)</td><td>可以说；可谓</td><td>He's the family's black sheep, so to speak.<br>他可以说是家里的害群之马。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>speak for itˈself/themˈselves</td><td>不言而喻；显而易见</td><td>The sales figures speak for themselves, no presentation needed.<br>销售数字不言自明，不用做汇报了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>speak for myˈself, himˈself, etc.</td><td>自己表达意见；亲自说明</td><td>Let the boy speak for himself instead of answering for him.<br>让孩子自己说，别替他回答。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>express what you think or want yourself, rather</td><td>自己表达想法而不由他人代言</td><td>She's old enough to express what she wants herself, rather than through you.<br>她大了，能自己说想要什么，不必你代言。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>speak for yourˈself (spoken, informal)</td><td>那只是你的看法</td><td>Boring? Speak for yourself, I loved the second half.<br>无聊？那是你的看法，我很喜欢下半场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>speak ˈhighly of sb</td><td>高度评价某人；称赞某人</td><td>Everyone at the clinic speaks highly of the new nurse.<br>诊所里人人都夸那位新来的护士。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>speak your ˈmind</td><td>直言不讳；说心里话</td><td>She's never afraid to speak her mind in front of the board.<br>她在董事会面前从不怕直言。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>speak too ˈsoon</td><td>话说早了；言之过早</td><td>I said the weather was fine, but I spoke too soon.<br>我说天气不错，结果话说早了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>speak ˈvolumes (about/for sb/sth)</td><td>充分说明；很能说明问题</td><td>His silence at the meeting spoke volumes about his real opinion.<br>他在会上的沉默很说明他的真实想法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>speaking</b></td><td>be on ˈspeaking terms (with sb)</td><td>与某人还说话；关系未闹僵</td><td>After the argument they're barely on speaking terms.<br>吵完那一架，他们几乎不说话了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>manner in a manner of speaking</td><td>可以这么说；某种意义上</td><td>In a manner of speaking, we're all still beginners here.<br>某种意义上说，我们在这儿都还是新手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spec</b></td><td>do sth on ˈspec (BrE, informal)</td><td>碰运气去做某事</td><td>We went down to the theatre on spec and got returned tickets.<br>我们碰运气去剧院，买到了退票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spectacle</b></td><td>make a ˈspectacle of yourself</td><td>出洋相；当众出丑</td><td>He made a spectacle of himself singing on the office table.<br>他站在办公桌上唱歌，出尽了洋相。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spectacles</b></td><td>look at, see, etc. sth through ˌrose-tinted/</td><td>戴着玫瑰色眼镜看；过于乐观</td><td>You're seeing your school days through rose-tinted glasses again.<br>你又在用美化的眼光回忆学生时代了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌrose-coloured ˈspectacles</td><td>玫瑰色眼镜；过于乐观的眼光</td><td>He views the countryside through rose-coloured spectacles, having never farmed.<br>他没种过地，看乡村总戴着玫瑰色眼镜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>speed</b></td><td>a ˌturn of ˈspeed</td><td>突然的加速</td><td>The old dog showed a surprising turn of speed chasing that squirrel.<br>那条老狗追松鼠时突然快得惊人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up to ˈspeed (on sth)</td><td>了解最新情况；达到应有水平</td><td>Can you bring me up to speed on the contract before lunch?<br>午饭前能跟我说说合同的最新进展吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spell</b></td><td>(be) under sb's ˈspell</td><td>被某人迷住</td><td>The whole class was under her spell within a week.<br>一星期之内全班都被她迷住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spend</b></td><td>spend the ˈnight with sb/together</td><td>与某人共度一夜</td><td>They spent the night together and regretted it by morning.<br>他们共度一夜，天亮就后悔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spend a ˈpenny (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>上厕所；方便一下</td><td>Wait a second, I need to spend a penny before we leave.<br>等一下，走之前我得去趟洗手间。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spent</b></td><td>a ˌspent ˈforce</td><td>已失去影响力的人或团体</td><td>Critics wrote the party off as a spent force after the election.<br>选举过后，评论者认定该党已成强弩之末。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spic</b></td><td>spick and ˈspan (also ˌspic and ˈspan)</td><td>整洁干净；井井有条</td><td>She keeps that little kitchen spick and span every single day.<br>她天天把那间小厨房收拾得干干净净。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spike</b></td><td>spike sb's ˈdrink</td><td>在某人饮料中偷加酒或药</td><td>Someone spiked her drink at the party and she blacked out.<br>有人在派对上往她饮料里下了东西，她昏了过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spike sb's ˈguns (BrE)</td><td>挫败某人的计划</td><td>Announcing the merger early spiked their guns completely.<br>提前宣布合并，把他们的算盘全打乱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spill</b></td><td>spill the ˈbeans (informal)</td><td>泄露秘密；说漏嘴</td><td>Don't let him near the party plans, he'll spill the beans.<br>别让他知道派对安排，他准说漏嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spill (sb's) ˈblood (formal or literary)</td><td>使流血；杀伤</td><td>No cause is worth spilling innocent blood for.<br>没有哪种主张值得让无辜者流血。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spill your ˈguts (to sb) (AmE, informal)</td><td>和盘托出；倾诉心事</td><td>Two drinks in and he spilled his guts to a total stranger.<br>两杯下肚，他就跟陌生人掏了心窝子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spilled</b></td><td>ink much ink has been spilled (on/over sth)</td><td>对某事著述甚多；笔墨已耗费不少</td><td>Much ink has been spilled over who really wrote the play.<br>关于这剧本究竟出自谁手，已有大量笔墨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spin</b></td><td>in a (flat) ˈspin</td><td>晕头转向；惊慌失措</td><td>The sudden inspection put the whole office in a flat spin.<br>突击检查把整个办公室搞得手忙脚乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spin your ˈwheels</td><td>白费力气；原地打转</td><td>We're just spinning our wheels until the budget is approved.<br>预算批下来之前，我们只是在空转。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwheel-spinning noun: Save yourself some</td><td>空耗力气；白忙一场</td><td>Save yourself some wheel-spinning and go straight to the library.<br>别再白费工夫了，直接去图书馆吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spin (sb) a ˈyarn/ˈtale</td><td>编造故事；瞎编一通</td><td>He spun us a yarn about missing his train again.<br>他又编了套没赶上火车的说辞。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>unlikely stories of their adventures, which is be sb's ˌspiritual ˈhome</td><td>是某人的精神家园</td><td>Paris was always her spiritual home, even before she lived there.<br>巴黎一直是她的精神家园，尽管她还没住过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spine</b></td><td>shiver runs/goes down sb's spine</td><td>脊背发凉；不寒而栗</td><td>A shiver ran down my spine when the lights went out.<br>灯一灭，我脊背发凉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(do sth) as/if/when the spirit ˈmoves you</td><td>有兴致时做某事</td><td>He paints only when the spirit moves him, sometimes twice a year.<br>他兴致来了才画画，有时一年才两次。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be with sb in ˈspirit</td><td>精神上与某人同在</td><td>I can't attend the funeral, but I'll be with you in spirit.<br>我去不了葬礼，但心与你同在。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/enter into the ˈspirit of sth</td><td>积极投入；热情参与</td><td>Everyone entered into the spirit of the costume party.<br>大家都投入到化装派对的气氛里去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈweak (saying, humorous)</td><td>心有余而力不足</td><td>I meant to go running, but the spirit is willing and the flesh is weak.<br>本想去跑步，无奈心有余而力不足。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌthat's the ˈspirit!</td><td>这才对；有志气</td><td>So you'll take the exam again next month? That's the spirit!<br>这么说你下个月再考一次？这才对嘛！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in high/low ˈspirits (also in good/poor ˈspirits)</td><td>情绪高涨；情绪低落</td><td>She's been in low spirits since the results came out.<br>成绩出来后她一直情绪低落。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spliced</b></td><td>get ˈspliced (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>结婚</td><td>The two of them finally got spliced after eleven years together.<br>他俩在一起十一年，总算结婚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>split</b></td><td>split the ˈdifference</td><td>折中；各让一步</td><td>You want ninety, I said seventy; let's split the difference.<br>你要九十，我说七十，折中一下吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>split sth down the ˈmiddle</td><td>使分裂成两派</td><td>The vote split the committee right down the middle.<br>这次表决把委员会分成了对半的两派。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>split ˈhairs (disapproving)</td><td>吹毛求疵；在细节上纠缠</td><td>Stop splitting hairs and tell me whether it works.<br>别抠字眼了，就说它管不管用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌsplit ˈsecond</td><td>一瞬间；刹那</td><td>For a split second I thought the car would hit us.<br>有那么一瞬，我以为车要撞上我们了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>split your ˈsides (laughing/with laughter)</td><td>捧腹大笑；笑破肚皮</td><td>We split our sides watching him try to assemble that shelf.<br>看他装那个架子，我们笑得肚子疼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>split the ˈticket (AmE, politics)</td><td>把票分投给不同党派的候选人</td><td>Plenty of voters here split the ticket rather than back one party.<br>这里很多选民不专投一党，而是分票。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>reminding voters that they may ˈsplit their ticket"</td><td>提醒选民可以分票投给不同党派</td><td>The notice reminded voters that they may split their ticket in November.<br>通知提醒选民十一月可以分票投给不同党派。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the November election, unlike a state primary</td><td>在十一月大选中（与州初选不同）</td><td>You can split your ticket in the November election, unlike a state primary.<br>十一月大选可以分票，州初选则不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spoil</b></td><td>spoil sb ˈrotten (informal)</td><td>把某人宠坏</td><td>Their grandparents spoil those twins rotten every summer.<br>每年夏天，祖父母都把那对双胞胎宠得不像话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spoil the ˌship for a ha ˈporth/ha ˈpenny-worth of ˈtar (saying)</td><td>贪小失大；省小钱误大事</td><td>Don't spoil the ship for a ha'porth of tar; buy the proper bolts.<br>别为省点小钱坏了大事，买正规螺栓吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ha ˈporth or ha ˈpenny-worth referred to a very</td><td>指极少量的钱</td><td>Here ha'porth referred to a very small amount of money indeed.<br>这里的半便士指的是极小的一点钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spoiled</b></td><td>choice be spoilt/spoiled for choice</td><td>选择太多，难以取舍</td><td>With twelve dessert options we were spoilt for choice.<br>甜点有十二种，我们都挑花了眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spoiling</b></td><td>be ˌspoiling for a ˈfight, argument, etc.</td><td>一心想打架或吵架</td><td>He came in slamming doors, clearly spoiling for a fight.<br>他进门就摔门，明摆着想吵一架。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spoilt</b></td><td>choice be spoilt/spoiled for choice</td><td>可选的太多；挑花了眼</td><td>In that street of bookshops you're spoiled for choice.<br>在那条书店街上，你会挑花眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spoke</b></td><td>put a ˈspoke in sb's wheel (BrE)</td><td>从中作梗；阻挠某人</td><td>The landlord put a spoke in our wheel by refusing to renew.<br>房东拒绝续租，把我们的计划搅黄了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Dutch of spaak meaning ˈbar' or ˈstick.</td><td>源自荷兰语，意为棒或棍</td><td>The word comes from Dutch spaak, meaning bar or stick.<br>这个词源自荷兰语 spaak，意思是棒或棍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sport</b></td><td>be a (good) ˈsport (informal)</td><td>为人爽快；输得起</td><td>Be a good sport and give me a lift to the station.<br>你行行好，捎我去趟车站吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sporting</b></td><td>a ˌsporting ˈchance</td><td>相当大的成功机会</td><td>With another week we'd have a sporting chance of finishing.<br>再给一周，我们完工还是很有希望的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spot</b></td><td>ˌglued/ˌrooted to the ˈspot</td><td>呆立原地；一动不动</td><td>She stood rooted to the spot when the alarm went off.<br>警报响起时，她呆立在原地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈspot</td><td>在现场；当场</td><td>Luckily a doctor was on the spot when he collapsed.<br>幸好他倒下时现场有医生。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb on the ˈspot</td><td>使某人为难；让人下不来台</td><td>Asking about his salary in front of everyone really put him on the spot.<br>当众问他工资，真让他下不来台。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bang bang/spot on</td><td>完全正确；分毫不差</td><td>Your estimate of the repair cost was spot on.<br>你对维修费的估算分毫不差。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in</b></td><td>getting attention from newspapers, television</td><td>受媒体关注；处于聚光灯下</td><td>The scandal left him getting attention from newspapers and television for months.<br>这桩丑闻让他被报纸电视追了好几个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spout</b></td><td>be/go up the ˈspout (BrE, slang)</td><td>泡汤了；搞砸了</td><td>Our holiday plans went up the spout when the airline collapsed.<br>航空公司倒闭，我们的假期计划泡汤了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sprat</b></td><td>(be) a ˌsprat to catch a ˈmackerel (informal)</td><td>施小惠得大利；抛砖引玉</td><td>The free trial is just a sprat to catch a mackerel.<br>免费试用不过是放长线钓大鱼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spread</b></td><td>spread like wildfire</td><td>迅速蔓延；飞快传开</td><td>News of the resignation spread like wildfire through the building.<br>辞职的消息在楼里飞快传开。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spread your ˈwings</td><td>展翅高飞；独立闯荡</td><td>After graduation she spread her wings and moved abroad.<br>毕业后她展翅高飞，出国了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spread the ˈword</td><td>散布消息；广为宣传</td><td>Spread the word: the meeting has moved to Thursday.<br>帮忙通知一下，会议改到周四了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spread yourself too ˈthin</td><td>摊子铺得太大；分身乏术</td><td>Taking on three projects means you're spreading yourself too thin.<br>同时接三个项目，你是摊得太开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Don't you think you're spreading yourself a bit</td><td>你不觉得摊得太开了吗</td><td>Another night shift? Don't you think you're spreading yourself a bit thin?<br>又加一个夜班？你不觉得顾不过来吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>net cast/spread your net wide</td><td>广泛搜寻；扩大范围</td><td>We had to cast our net wide to find a decent candidate.<br>为找到合适人选，我们不得不广撒网。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spring</b></td><td>be ˌno spring ˈchicken (humorous)</td><td>不再年轻了</td><td>I'll help you move, but remember I'm no spring chicken.<br>我帮你搬家，不过我可不年轻了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spring a ˈleak</td><td>出现裂缝漏水</td><td>The boat sprang a leak about a mile from shore.<br>离岸大约一英里时，船开始漏水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spring to/into ˈlife/ˈaction</td><td>突然活跃起来；立即行动</td><td>The whole newsroom sprang into action when the story broke.<br>消息一出，整个编辑部立刻忙了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>spring a ˈtrap</td><td>触发陷阱；使圈套合上</td><td>The police sprang the trap just as the van pulled away.<br>货车刚要开走，警方就收网了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spur</b></td><td>(do sth) on the ˌspur of the ˈmoment</td><td>一时冲动；心血来潮</td><td>We booked the flight on the spur of the moment last Friday.<br>上周五我们一时冲动就订了机票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>spurs</b></td><td>win/earn your ˈspurs (formal)</td><td>崭露头角；赢得声誉</td><td>She earned her spurs covering the war as a young reporter.<br>她年轻时做战地记者，由此扬名。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a square ˈmeal</td><td>一顿丰盛的饭；饱餐</td><td>The kids get three square meals a day at that school.<br>那所学校每天给孩子三顿饱饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>squeaky</b></td><td>the squeaky wheel gets the ˈgrease/ˈoil</td><td>会哭的孩子有奶吃</td><td>Complain loudly; the squeaky wheel gets the grease around here.<br>大声抱怨吧，这儿是会哭的孩子有奶吃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>squeeze</b></td><td>put the ˈsqueeze on sb (to do sth) (informal)</td><td>向某人施压；逼迫某人</td><td>The bank put the squeeze on him to repay early.<br>银行逼他提前还款。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>squeeze sb ˈdry</td><td>榨干某人的钱财或信息</td><td>The landlords squeezed the tenants dry before selling up.<br>房东把租客榨干后就把房子卖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tight a tight squeeze</td><td>勉强挤下；空间紧巴巴</td><td>Six of us in that car was a tight squeeze.<br>我们六个挤那辆车，实在太挤了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stab</b></td><td>have a stab at sth/at doing sth (informal)</td><td>尝试做某事</td><td>I'll have a stab at fixing the tap myself tonight.<br>今晚我自己试试修那个水龙头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stab sb in the ˈback ◆ get, etc. a stab in the ˈback (informal)</td><td>被信任的人暗算；背后中伤</td><td>Losing the contract that way felt like a stab in the back.<br>那样丢掉合同，简直像被人背后捅了一刀。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈback-stabbing noun: This party is full of dark a shot/stab in the dark</td><td>瞎猜；无根据的猜测</td><td>It was a shot in the dark, but the password worked.<br>纯属瞎蒙，可那密码居然对了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stable</b></td><td>shut/lock/close the stable door after the horse has ˈbolted (BrE) (AmE shut, etc. the)</td><td>马已跑掉；补救已迟</td><td>They fixed the alarm after the horse had bolted, as usual.<br>照例是马跑了才修警报器。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>barn door after the horse has eˈscaped)</td><td>贼走关门；补救为时已晚</td><td>Backing up files now is closing the barn door after the horse has escaped.<br>现在才备份文件，早就晚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stacked</b></td><td>the cards/odds are stacked aˈgainst sb/sth</td><td>形势对某人不利</td><td>The odds were stacked against the small firm from day one.<br>从第一天起，形势就对这家小公司不利。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the cards/odds are stacked in ˈfavour of sb/</td><td>形势对某人有利</td><td>The odds are stacked in favour of the defending champion tonight.<br>今晚形势明显对卫冕冠军有利。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈfavor of sb/sth)</td><td>形势有利于某人或某事</td><td>Emily thought the odds were stacked in favor of her rival.<br>埃米莉以为形势对她的对手有利。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>staff</b></td><td>the ˌstaff of ˈlife (literary)</td><td>主食（尤指面包）</td><td>In that village bread is still the staff of life.<br>在那个村子里，面包仍是命根子般的主食。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stag</b></td><td>go ˈstag (AmE, old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>男子不带女伴赴宴</td><td>He decided to go stag to the graduation dance.<br>他决定不带舞伴去毕业舞会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stage</b></td><td>be/go on the ˈstage</td><td>当演员；登台表演</td><td>Against her parents' wishes, she went on the stage at nineteen.<br>她十九岁不顾父母反对当了演员。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stake</b></td><td>(be/have a lot, etc.) at ˈstake</td><td>利害攸关；处于成败关头</td><td>There's a lot at stake in tomorrow's negotiation.<br>明天的谈判利害攸关。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stake (out) a/your ˈclaim to sb/sth</td><td>宣称对某物拥有权利</td><td>She staked her claim to the corner office before anyone else moved in.<br>别人还没搬进来，她就先占下了那间角落办公室。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stakes</b></td><td>in the ... stakes</td><td>就某方面而言</td><td>He does badly in the punctuality stakes but writes beautifully.<br>论守时他很糟，可文章写得漂亮。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stand</b></td><td>etc. can't ˈstand the sight/sound of sb/sth</td><td>受不了看到或听到某人某物</td><td>I can't stand the sound of that drill next door.<br>隔壁那台电钻的声音我实在受不了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˈstand (against/for/over/about/on sth) ◆ take a ˈstand (on/over sth)</td><td>表明立场；起而抗争</td><td>Someone has to take a stand on how the money is spent.<br>总得有人对这笔钱怎么花表明立场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stand or ˈfall by sth</td><td>成败取决于某事</td><td>The whole campaign stands or falls by the first week's numbers.<br>整个活动的成败取决于第一周的数据。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>standby</b></td><td>on ˈstandby</td><td>待命；随时准备行动</td><td>Two ambulances were on standby outside the stadium all evening.<br>整晚有两辆救护车在体育场外待命。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>standing</b></td><td>do sth standing on your ˈhead (informal)</td><td>轻而易举地做某事</td><td>He could fix that engine standing on his head.<br>修那台发动机对他来说轻而易举。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave sb/sth ˈstanding (informal)</td><td>远远胜过；把对手甩在后面</td><td>Her new laptop leaves my old one standing.<br>她的新笔记本把我这台老的甩出几条街。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stands</b></td><td>it ˌstands to ˈreason (that...) (informal)</td><td>道理显而易见；这是自然的</td><td>It stands to reason that tired drivers make more mistakes.<br>司机疲劳就更容易出错，这是明摆着的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hair your hair stands on end</td><td>毛骨悚然；吓得头发直竖</td><td>That scream in the corridor made my hair stand on end.<br>走廊里那声尖叫吓得我汗毛倒竖。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stare</b></td><td>stare sth in the ˈface</td><td>近在眼前；不可避免</td><td>Bankruptcy was staring the family business in the face.<br>破产已经摆在这家家族企业面前。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stark</b></td><td>stark ˈnaked (BrE) (AmE buck ˈnaked)</td><td>一丝不挂</td><td>The toddler ran through the garden stark naked, laughing.<br>那小家伙光着身子笑着跑过花园。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stars</b></td><td>have ˈstars in your eyes</td><td>满怀憧憬；一心想成名</td><td>She arrived in the city with stars in her eyes and no money.<br>她满怀憧憬来到这座城市，身上却没钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see ˈstars (informal)</td><td>眼冒金星</td><td>I hit my head on the shelf and saw stars for a moment.<br>我头撞到架子上，眼前直冒金星。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>start</b></td><td>ˌdon't ˈstart (also ˌdon't ˈyou start) (spoken, informal)</td><td>别又来了；别唠叨了</td><td>Don't you start, I've already heard it from your brother.<br>你别又来了，你弟弟已经念叨过了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for a ˈstart ◆ to ˈstart with (also for ˈstarters informal)</td><td>首先；第一点</td><td>For a start, the price is double what we agreed.<br>首先，价钱比说好的贵了一倍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈstart something/anything (informal)</td><td>惹事；挑起争端</td><td>He'd had three beers and was clearly looking to start something.<br>他喝了三瓶啤酒，明显想找事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>started</b></td><td>you, he, she, etc. ˈstarted it (spoken, informal)</td><td>是你（或他、她）先挑起来的</td><td>Don't blame me, she started it by taking my chair.<br>别怪我，是她先抢我椅子的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>starters</b></td><td>under ˌstarters ˈorders</td><td>等待起跑令；一触即发</td><td>The runners are under starter's orders and the crowd goes quiet.<br>选手已就位待发令，观众安静下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>starving</b></td><td>be ˈstarving (for sth) (also be ˈstarved especially AmE) (informal)</td><td>饿极了</td><td>Is there anything to eat? I'm absolutely starving.<br>有吃的吗？我饿坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>state</b></td><td>be in a ˈstate ◆ get into a ˈstate (informal)</td><td>心烦意乱；紧张不安</td><td>She got into a real state waiting for the test results.<br>等检查结果时她紧张得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>OPP be/look a picture</td><td>十分好看；美极了</td><td>In that blue dress she looked a picture.<br>穿上那条蓝裙子，她美极了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a state of afˈfairs</td><td>事态；情况</td><td>Three managers in one year is a sorry state of affairs.<br>一年换三个经理，这局面真够糟的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>state of the ˈart</td><td>最先进的；顶尖水平的</td><td>The hospital's new scanner is genuinely state of the art.<br>医院的新扫描仪确实是顶尖水平。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>This computer uses state-of-the-art technology.</td><td>采用最尖端技术的</td><td>This computer uses state-of-the-art technology in every single component.<br>这台计算机每个部件都采用了最尖端的技术。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the state of ˈplay</td><td>进展情况；当前局势</td><td>Can you update me on the state of play with the lawsuit?<br>你能跟我说说官司的进展吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>statesman</b></td><td>elder an elder statesman</td><td>资深望重的元老</td><td>At seventy he's become an elder statesman of British theatre.<br>七十岁的他已成为英国戏剧界的元老。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>status</b></td><td>the status ˈquo (from Latin)</td><td>现状</td><td>Older members of the club want to preserve the status quo.<br>俱乐部里年长的会员想维持现状。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈstatus symbol</td><td>身份地位的象征</td><td>For him that watch is less a timepiece than a status symbol.<br>对他来说那块表与其说计时，不如说是身份象征。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stay</b></td><td>be here to ˈstay ◆ have come to ˈstay</td><td>已被普遍接受；将长期存在</td><td>Whatever critics say, remote working is here to stay.<br>不管批评者怎么说，远程办公是长久之势。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stay the ˈcourse</td><td>坚持到底；有始有终</td><td>Only four of the twelve trainees stayed the course.<br>十二名学员里只有四个坚持到了最后。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stay your/sb's ˈhand (old-fashioned or literary)</td><td>住手；使某人罢手</td><td>Only her plea stayed his hand at the last moment.<br>最后一刻，是她的哀求让他住了手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stay the ˈnight (especially BrE)</td><td>在某人家过夜</td><td>It's too late to drive back, why not stay the night?<br>开回去太晚了，不如住一晚吧？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stay ˈput (informal)</td><td>待在原地不动</td><td>Stay put by the fountain and I'll come find you.<br>你就在喷泉边别动，我来找你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stead</b></td><td>in sb's/sth's ˈstead (formal)</td><td>代替某人或某物</td><td>The deputy attended the ceremony in the minister's stead.<br>副手代替部长出席了仪式。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stand sb in good ˈstead</td><td>对某人大有裨益</td><td>Those years in the kitchen stood her in good stead later.<br>在厨房干的那几年后来让她受益匪浅。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>steady</b></td><td>go ˈsteady (with sb) (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>确定男女朋友关系</td><td>They've been going steady since the summer fair.<br>夏季集市之后他们就正式交往了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) steady as a ˈrock</td><td>稳如泰山；十分可靠</td><td>Even after twelve hours, the surgeon's hands were steady as a rock.<br>连做十二小时后，那位外科医生的手依然稳如磐石。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>steady ˈon! (informal)</td><td>慢着；说话注意点</td><td>Steady on! That's my brother you're talking about.<br>慢着，你说的可是我弟弟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ready ready, steady, go!</td><td>各就位，预备，跑！</td><td>The teacher shouted "Ready, steady, go!" and the children sprinted off.<br>老师喊了声预备跑，孩子们就冲了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>steal</b></td><td>be a ˈsteal (especially AmE)</td><td>极便宜；十分划算</td><td>Two hundred for that bike? It's a steal.<br>那辆车两百块？简直白捡。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>steal a ˈglance/ˈlook (at sb/sth) (written)</td><td>偷看一眼</td><td>He stole a glance at her across the crowded table.<br>隔着挤满人的桌子，他偷看了她一眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>steal sb's ˈheart (literary)</td><td>赢得某人的芳心</td><td>That scruffy little puppy stole her heart immediately.<br>那只脏兮兮的小狗一下就俘获了她的心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>steal a ˈkiss (from sb) (literary)</td><td>偷吻某人</td><td>He stole a kiss under the streetlamp before running for his train.<br>他在路灯下偷吻了她，然后赶火车去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>steal a ˈmarch on sb (written)</td><td>抢在某人前面；抢得先机</td><td>By launching in April they stole a march on their rivals.<br>四月就上市，他们抢在了对手前头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>steal the ˈshow</td><td>抢尽风头</td><td>The eight-year-old violinist stole the show at the concert.<br>那位八岁的小提琴手在音乐会上抢尽了风头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>steal sb's ˈthunder</td><td>抢先夺人风头；抢功劳</td><td>She announced the results early and stole my thunder completely.<br>她提前公布了结果，把我的风头全抢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>steam</b></td><td>get up/ˌpick up ˈsteam</td><td>逐渐加速；势头渐起</td><td>The campaign is finally picking up steam in the northern towns.<br>这场活动在北部各镇终于势头起来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌlet off ˈsteam (informal)</td><td>发泄情绪；释放精力</td><td>The kids need to run around and let off steam after school.<br>孩子们放学后得跑跑跳跳发泄一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run out of ˈsteam (informal)</td><td>后劲不足；精疲力竭</td><td>The project ran out of steam halfway through the second year.<br>项目到第二年中期就没了后劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(get/go somewhere) under your own ˈsteam</td><td>靠自己的力量前往</td><td>We'll meet you there; can you get to the hotel under your own steam?<br>我们在那儿碰头，你能自己到酒店吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>steamed</b></td><td>be/get (all) steamed ˈup (about/over sth)</td><td>为某事大为光火</td><td>He got all steamed up about a two-minute delay.<br>就晚了两分钟，他就气得不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(BrE) (AmE be ˈsteamed (about sth)) (informal)</td><td>非常气愤；十分激动</td><td>She was really steamed about being left off the list.<br>没被列进名单，她气坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>steel</b></td><td>of ˈsteel</td><td>钢铁般坚强的；冷酷的</td><td>You need nerves of steel to land a plane in that wind.<br>在那种风里降落飞机，你得有钢铁般的神经。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>steep</b></td><td>be a bit/rather ˈsteep (informal)</td><td>价格过高；要求过分</td><td>Forty pounds for a taxi across town seems a bit steep.<br>穿城打车四十镑，未免贵了点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>steeped</b></td><td>be ˈsteeped in sth (written)</td><td>充满着；深受…熏陶</td><td>The whole town is steeped in mining history.<br>整座小镇浸透着采矿业的历史。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stem</b></td><td>from ˌstem to ˈstern</td><td>从头到尾；彻头彻尾</td><td>They scrubbed the old boat from stem to stern in one weekend.<br>他们一个周末就把那条旧船从头到尾刷了一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌstem the ˈtide (of sth)</td><td>遏止…的势头；阻止蔓延</td><td>New rules did little to stem the tide of complaints.<br>新规几乎没能遏止投诉的浪潮。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>step</b></td><td>be in/out of ˈstep (with sb/sth)</td><td>步调一致；步调不一致</td><td>His views are badly out of step with the rest of the board.<br>他的看法和董事会其他人很不合拍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fall into ˈstep (beside/with sb) (written)</td><td>与某人齐步同行；与…步调一致</td><td>She fell into step beside me as we crossed the bridge.<br>过桥时她跟上来和我并肩同行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>mind/watch your ˈstep</td><td>走路小心；行事谨慎</td><td>Mind your step on those wet stairs, someone slipped there this morning.<br>下那几级湿台阶小心点，今早还有人在那儿滑倒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one step forward, two steps ˈback (saying)</td><td>进一步，退两步；进展反复</td><td>Fixing this app feels like one step forward, two steps back every single week.<br>修这个应用感觉每周都是进一步退两步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one step aˈhead (of sb/sth)</td><td>领先一步；先人一着</td><td>She stays one step ahead of her rivals by testing new ideas early.<br>她总是早早试验新点子，因此比对手领先一步。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>step by ˈstep</td><td>一步一步地；循序渐进地</td><td>He explained the recipe step by step until even I could follow it.<br>他一步一步讲这道菜，连我都跟得上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>step into the ˈbreach</td><td>顶替；临时接替他人工作</td><td>When the pianist fell ill, a student stepped into the breach at short notice.<br>钢琴师病了，一个学生临时顶了上来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>step into sb's ˈshoes</td><td>接替某人的职位</td><td>She'll step into her boss's shoes when he retires next spring.<br>等老板明年春天退休，她就接他的班。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈstep on it (also step on the ˈgas especially in AmE) (informal)</td><td>加速；踩油门；快点</td><td>Step on it, or we'll miss the last train home tonight.<br>快开，不然今晚末班车就赶不上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>step out of ˈline •be/get out of ˈline</td><td>行为出格；不守规矩</td><td>Step out of line once more and you'll be off the team.<br>再出格一次你就会被踢出队。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>steps</b></td><td>take ˈsteps to do sth</td><td>采取措施做某事</td><td>The council took steps to reduce traffic near the school after several accidents.<br>出了几次事故后，市政会采取措施减少学校附近的车流。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sterner</b></td><td>be made of sterner ˈstuff</td><td>性格坚强；意志过人</td><td>Most people would quit, but Ana is made of sterner stuff than that.<br>换了别人早不干了，可安娜没那么容易被打倒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stew</b></td><td>be in a ˈstew (about/over sth)</td><td>为某事焦虑不安</td><td>Dad's in a stew about the wedding seating plan again this evening.<br>今晚老爸又为婚礼座位安排的事急得团团转。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get (yourself) into a ˈstew (about/over sth) (informal)</td><td>为某事坐立不安；心烦意乱</td><td>Don't get yourself into a stew over one bad exam result.<br>别为一次考砸了就把自己急得心慌意乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>let sb ˈstew (in their own juice) (informal)</td><td>让某人自作自受；听其自食其果</td><td>He lied to us, so let him stew in his own juice for now.<br>他骗了我们，先让他自作自受吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stick</b></td><td>get/take ˈstick from sb (BrE, informal)</td><td>受到某人严厉批评</td><td>I got a lot of stick from my mates for that haircut.<br>就因为那个发型，我被哥们儿狠狠奚落了一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb ˈstick (BrE, informal)</td><td>批评某人；数落某人</td><td>The fans gave the referee stick for missing an obvious foul.<br>裁判漏判了一个明显犯规，球迷把他骂惨了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌstick ˈem ˈup! (spoken)</td><td>举起手来</td><td>The robber waved his gun and shouted 'Stick 'em up!' at the cashier.<br>劫匪挥着枪冲收银员大喊：举起手来！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stick ˈfast</td><td>卡住；牢牢粘住</td><td>The car's wheels stuck fast in the mud after two days of rain.<br>下了两天雨，车轮牢牢陷在泥里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stick in your ˈmind</td><td>留在记忆里；经久不忘</td><td>That final scene really sticks in my mind days after the film.<br>电影看完好几天了，最后那场戏还印在我脑子里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stick in your ˈthroat/ˈcraw/ˈgullet (informal)</td><td>难以接受；无法苟同</td><td>Apologizing to him really stuck in my throat, but I did it.<br>向他道歉实在让我咽不下这口气，但我还是道了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stick your ˈneck out (informal)</td><td>冒险直言；出头担风险</td><td>I'll stick my neck out and say we'll win the contract.<br>我就冒险说一句：这份合同我们拿定了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stick to your ˈguns (informal)</td><td>坚持立场；不改初衷</td><td>She stuck to her guns and refused to lower the price.<br>她坚持自己的立场，拒不降价。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a rod/stick to beat sb ˈwith</td><td>攻击某人的把柄</td><td>Those old emails gave his critics a stick to beat him with.<br>那些旧邮件成了对手攻击他的把柄。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sticks</b></td><td>(out) in the ˈsticks (informal)</td><td>在偏远乡下</td><td>They live out in the sticks, an hour from the nearest shop.<br>他们住在偏僻乡下，离最近的商店都有一小时车程。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up ˈsticks (and go, etc.) (BrE, informal)</td><td>搬家；迁居</td><td>At sixty he upped sticks and moved to a village in Spain.<br>六十岁时他收拾东西搬到了西班牙的一个村子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sticky</b></td><td>have sticky ˈfingers (informal)</td><td>手脚不干净；爱偷小东西</td><td>Watch the new intern, because word is that he has sticky fingers.<br>留神那个新实习生，据说他手脚不干净。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be on) a ˌsticky ˈwicket (BrE, informal)</td><td>处境困难</td><td>We're on a sticky wicket asking for more money after missing the deadline.<br>误了期限还要加钱，我们的处境很不利。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stiff</b></td><td>(as) stiff as a ˈboard</td><td>硬邦邦；僵硬如板</td><td>The towels froze on the line and came in stiff as a board.<br>毛巾在晾衣绳上冻住了，收进来硬得像块板。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) stiff as a ˈpoker (informal)</td><td>直挺挺的；僵直的</td><td>He sat stiff as a poker through the whole awkward interview.<br>整场尴尬的面试他都坐得直挺挺的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌstiff ˈdrink</td><td>一杯烈酒</td><td>After that phone call she poured herself a stiff drink and sat down.<br>接完那通电话，她给自己倒了杯烈酒坐了下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(keep) a stiff upper ˈlip</td><td>不动声色；坚忍克制</td><td>He kept a stiff upper lip even when the news was devastating.<br>即便消息如此沉重，他也不动声色。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>still</b></td><td>be still going ˈstrong (informal)</td><td>依然活跃；仍很兴旺</td><td>The band formed in 1975 and is still going strong today.<br>这支乐队 1975 年成立，如今依然活跃。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the still of the ˈnight (literary)</td><td>夜深人静之时</td><td>In the still of the night you can hear the river clearly.<br>夜深人静时，能清清楚楚听见河水声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the still small ˈvoice</td><td>良心的呼唤</td><td>The still small voice of conscience kept him awake most of the night.<br>良心的低语让他大半夜没睡着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>still waters run ˈdeep (saying)</td><td>静水流深；沉默者未必浅薄</td><td>He barely speaks, but still waters run deep and he notices everything.<br>他话很少，可静水流深，什么都逃不过他的眼睛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sting</b></td><td>a ˌsting in the ˈtail (informal)</td><td>出人意料的糟糕结局</td><td>The offer sounds great, but there's a sting in the tail: no refunds.<br>这优惠听着不错，可后头有个坑：概不退款。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈsting out of sth</td><td>减轻痛苦；使不那么难受</td><td>A small bonus took the sting out of losing the promotion.<br>一笔小奖金冲淡了没能升职的失落。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stink</b></td><td>kick up/make/create/raise a ˈstink (about sth) (informal)</td><td>大吵大闹；公开抗议</td><td>Parents kicked up a stink about the sudden change to school hours.<br>学校突然改上课时间，家长们大闹了一场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stinking</b></td><td>be stinking ˈrich (informal, usually disapproving)</td><td>十分富有；富得流油</td><td>His uncle is stinking rich and owns three houses by the sea.<br>他叔叔富得流油，海边有三套房子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stint</b></td><td>do sth without ˈstint (written)</td><td>慷慨地做；不遗余力地做</td><td>She gave her time without stint to the neighbourhood clinic for years.<br>多年来她毫无保留地把时间投入社区诊所。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stir</b></td><td>cause/create a ˈstir</td><td>引起轰动</td><td>Her resignation caused quite a stir in the office that morning.<br>那天上午她辞职的事在办公室引起了不小的轰动。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stir sb's/the ˈblood</td><td>使人热血沸腾；激起热情</td><td>The old marching song still stirs the blood of everyone in the hall.<br>那首老进行曲仍让全场的人热血沸腾。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stir your ˈstumps (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>赶快动身；快走</td><td>Stir your stumps, you two, or we'll be late for the ferry.<br>你们俩快点动身，不然赶不上渡轮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stitch</b></td><td>not have a stitch ˈon •without a stitch ˈon</td><td>一丝不挂；赤身裸体</td><td>He ran out of the sauna without a stitch on and everyone laughed.<br>他一丝不挂地从桑拿房跑出来，大家都笑翻了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌstitch in ˈtime (saves ˈnine) (saying)</td><td>及时处理可省大麻烦</td><td>Fix that small leak now, because a stitch in time saves nine.<br>趁漏得还小赶紧修，小洞不补大洞吃苦。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stitches</b></td><td>in ˈstitches (informal)</td><td>笑得前仰后合</td><td>His impression of the boss had us all in stitches for ages.<br>他学老板的样子把我们笑得半天直不起腰。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stock</b></td><td>(be) in/out of ˈstock</td><td>有现货；无现货</td><td>Sorry, that model is out of stock until the end of the month.<br>抱歉，那款要到月底才有货。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈstock (of sb/sth)</td><td>反思；仔细评估</td><td>After the layoffs I took stock of my career and changed direction.<br>裁员之后我重新审视了自己的职业，换了方向。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stocking</b></td><td>in your ˌstocking(ed) ˈfeet (old-fashioned)</td><td>只穿袜子不穿鞋</td><td>She padded downstairs in her stockinged feet so nobody would wake up.<br>她只穿袜子轻手轻脚下楼，怕吵醒别人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stocks</b></td><td>on the ˈstocks</td><td>在筹备中；在建造中</td><td>The studio has two more films on the stocks for next year.<br>这家制片厂明年还有两部片子在筹备中。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stock-still</b></td><td>be, stay, stand, etc. ˌstock-ˈstill</td><td>一动不动</td><td>The deer stood stock-still until the car finally drove past.<br>那头鹿一动不动，直到汽车终于开过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stomach</b></td><td>have no ˈstomach for sth</td><td>对某事没兴趣；不忍做</td><td>After the scandal he had no stomach for another election campaign.<br>丑闻之后，他再没心思去打一场选战。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn sb's ˈstomach •make sb's ˈstomach turn</td><td>使人恶心；令人作呕</td><td>The smell in that kitchen was enough to turn your stomach.<br>那间厨房的味道足以让人恶心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on an empty ˈstomach</td><td>空腹地</td><td>Never take these pills on an empty stomach or you'll feel sick.<br>这些药千万别空腹吃，不然会难受。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stone</b></td><td>be carved/set in ˈstone</td><td>不可更改；板上钉钉</td><td>The schedule isn't set in stone, so tell me if it clashes.<br>日程还不是定死的，冲突了就告诉我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave no stone unˈturned</td><td>想尽一切办法；竭尽全力</td><td>Police left no stone unturned in the search for the missing girl.<br>警方为寻找失踪女孩想尽了一切办法。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stone the ˈcrows •ˌstone ˈme (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>天哪；哎呀（表惊讶）</td><td>Stone the crows, you've painted the whole house in one weekend!<br>天哪，你一个周末就把整栋房子刷完了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈstone's throw</td><td>一箭之遥；很近的距离</td><td>Their flat is a stone's throw from the beach, which we loved.<br>他们的公寓离海滩一箭之遥，我们特别喜欢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stone-cold</b></td><td>ˌstone-cold ˈsober</td><td>滴酒未沾；完全清醒</td><td>He was stone-cold sober and still couldn't remember where he parked.<br>他一滴酒没喝，却还是想不起车停哪儿了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stoned</b></td><td>ˌstoned out of your ˈmind (slang)</td><td>吸毒后神志不清；晕乎乎</td><td>They were stoned out of their minds and missed the last bus.<br>他们嗑得晕头转向，错过了末班车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stony</b></td><td>fall on stony ˈground</td><td>未见成效；无人理会</td><td>His appeal for volunteers fell on stony ground at the parish meeting.<br>他在教区会上招募志愿者的呼吁没人搭理。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stoop</b></td><td>stoop so ˈlow (as to do sth) (written)</td><td>卑劣到某种地步</td><td>I never thought she'd stoop so low as to read my emails.<br>我没想到她会卑鄙到偷看我的邮件。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stop</b></td><td>stop at ˈnothing</td><td>不择手段</td><td>He'll stop at nothing to get his name on that report.<br>为了让报告署上自己的名字，他什么都干得出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stop the ˈrot</td><td>阻止进一步恶化</td><td>A new coach was hired to stop the rot after five straight defeats.<br>五连败之后，球队请了新教练来止住颓势。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stop ˈshort</td><td>突然停住；戛然而止</td><td>She stopped short in the doorway when she saw who was waiting.<br>她看清等在那儿的是谁，在门口猛地停住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stops</b></td><td>the buck stops ˈhere (saying)</td><td>责任到此为止；由我担责</td><td>I'm the manager, so the buck stops here when things go wrong.<br>我是经理，出了事责任就在我这儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>store</b></td><td>be in ˈstore (for sb)</td><td>即将来临；等着某人</td><td>Nobody knew what was in store for them on that first morning.<br>头一天早上谁也不知道等着他们的是什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/set (no, great, little, etc.) ˈstore by sth</td><td>重视；看重（或不重视）</td><td>She sets great store by punctuality, so don't arrive late tomorrow.<br>她非常看重守时，明天别迟到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>store up ˈtrouble, etc. for yourself</td><td>给自己埋下祸根</td><td>Ignoring that cough is just storing up trouble for yourself later on.<br>不管那咳嗽，只是给自己以后埋下麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>storm</b></td><td>the ˌcalm/ˌlull before the ˈstorm (saying)</td><td>暴风雨前的平静</td><td>The office is quiet today, but it's the calm before the storm.<br>今天办公室很安静，不过是暴风雨前的平静。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>dance, talk, etc. up a ˈstorm (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>起劲地跳（或谈等）</td><td>They danced up a storm at the wedding until the band packed up.<br>婚礼上他们一直跳得热火朝天，直到乐队收摊。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ride out/weather the ˈstorm (of sth)</td><td>渡过难关；平安挺过</td><td>Small shops that weathered the storm are now busier than ever.<br>挺过难关的小店如今生意比以前还好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a storm in a ˈteacup (BrE) (AmE a ˌtempest in a ˈteapot) (informal)</td><td>小题大做；茶杯里的风波</td><td>The whole argument was a storm in a teacup and blew over quickly.<br>整场争吵不过是小题大做，很快就过去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb/sth by ˈstorm</td><td>一举征服；风靡</td><td>Her debut album took the country by storm within just three weeks.<br>她的首张专辑三周之内就风靡全国。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>story</b></td><td>(quite) another ˈstory</td><td>完全是另一回事</td><td>Cooking at home is cheap; eating out every night is quite another story.<br>在家做饭便宜，天天下馆子就完全是另一回事了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a (quite) different ˈstory</td><td>情况完全不同；另一码事</td><td>He's polite at work, but at home it's a quite different story.<br>他在单位彬彬有礼，在家却完全是另一副样子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so the story ˈgoes •the story ˈgoes (that)...</td><td>据说；传闻如此</td><td>The house is haunted, or so the story goes around this village.<br>据村里人说，那栋房子闹鬼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's the ˌstory of my ˈlife (informal)</td><td>我总是这么倒霉</td><td>Missed the train by ten seconds, and that's the story of my life.<br>差十秒没赶上火车，我这辈子就这命。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>straight</b></td><td>give it to me ˈstraight (spoken, informal)</td><td>直说吧；有话直说</td><td>Give it to me straight, doctor: how long will the recovery take?<br>医生您直说吧，得多久才能恢复？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈstraight (informal)</td><td>改邪归正；重新做人</td><td>He's gone straight since prison and now runs a small bakery.<br>出狱后他改邪归正，现在开了家小面包房。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(keep to) the straight and ˈnarrow (informal)</td><td>走正道；恪守本分</td><td>Joining the club helped him keep to the straight and narrow.<br>加入那个俱乐部帮他一直走在正道上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play it ˈstraight (also play a straight ˈbat)</td><td>诚实坦率；照规矩来</td><td>Just play it straight with the client and admit the delay was ours.<br>跟客户实话实说，承认是我们拖延了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/set sb ˈstraight (about/on sth)</td><td>使某人弄清事实</td><td>Let me put you straight about what actually happened at the meeting.<br>我来跟你说清楚会上到底发生了什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sth ˈstraight</td><td>整理好；收拾整齐</td><td>Give me ten minutes to put the room straight before they arrive.<br>给我十分钟把房间收拾好，他们就到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(earn/get) straight ˈA's (especially AmE)</td><td>取得全优成绩</td><td>She got straight A's last term without ever missing a hockey practice.<br>上学期她门门拿优，还没落下一次曲棍球训练。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) straight as an ˈarrow</td><td>笔直；（人）正直</td><td>The new road runs straight as an arrow across the empty plain.<br>新修的公路笔直地穿过空旷的平原。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run as ˈstraight as an arrow</td><td>笔直地延伸；直通</td><td>Take this road; it runs as straight as an arrow through the forest.<br>走这条路，它笔直地穿过整片树林。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) straight as a ˈdie</td><td>笔直；（人）非常诚实</td><td>The old canal is straight as a die for almost ten miles.<br>那条老运河笔直地延伸了将近十英里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌstraight aˈway</td><td>立即；马上</td><td>Call me straight away if the fever gets any worse tonight.<br>今晚要是烧得更厉害，马上给我打电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(keep) a straight ˈface</td><td>板着脸；忍住不笑</td><td>I could hardly keep a straight face during his terrible karaoke.<br>他唱卡拉OK唱得那么惨，我差点没憋住笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌstraight from the ˈshoulder</td><td>直言不讳地</td><td>She told him straight from the shoulder that the plan wouldn't work.<br>她直截了当地告诉他这方案行不通。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌstraight ˈoff/ˈout (informal)</td><td>立刻；直截了当地</td><td>He asked her straight out whether she still wanted the job.<br>他直截了当地问她还想不想要这份工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌstraight ˈup (BrE, spoken, informal)</td><td>真的；的确如此</td><td>Straight up, I saw him carry that fridge upstairs on his own.<br>真的，我亲眼看见他一个人把冰箱扛上楼。</td></tr>
