<tr><td><b>strain</b></td><td>strain at the ˈleash (informal)</td><td>急不可耐；渴望摆脱束缚</td><td>The new recruits were straining at the leash to start real work.<br>新人个个跃跃欲试，急着上手真活儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be straining at the ˈleash (informal)</td><td>迫不及待；跃跃欲试</td><td>He's straining at the leash to leave Britain for somewhere sunny and warm.<br>他急不可待地想离开英国，去个阳光明媚的地方。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>strain every ˈnerve/ˈsinew (to do sth)</td><td>竭尽全力做某事</td><td>They strained every sinew to finish the bridge before the rains came.<br>他们竭尽全力，赶在雨季前修完了桥。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strange</b></td><td>be/make strange ˈbedfellows</td><td>奇怪的组合；不搭调的伙伴</td><td>Punk music and classical violin make strange bedfellows on this new album.<br>朋克和古典小提琴在这张新专辑里凑成了奇怪的组合。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stranger</b></td><td>be no/a ˈstranger to sth (formal)</td><td>熟悉某事；不熟悉某事</td><td>As a night nurse she is no stranger to difficult conversations.<br>身为夜班护士，她对难开口的谈话早已不陌生。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strapped</b></td><td>be ˌstrapped for ˈcash (informal)</td><td>手头紧；缺钱</td><td>We're strapped for cash this month, so let's cook at home.<br>这个月手头紧，咱们在家做饭吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>straw</b></td><td>be the last/final ˈstraw (also be the ˌstraw that breaks the camel's ˈback)</td><td>最后一根稻草；忍无可忍之事</td><td>His third late arrival was the last straw, and she fired him.<br>他第三次迟到成了最后一根稻草，她把他辞了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a straw in the ˈwind (BrE)</td><td>预示事态走向的迹象</td><td>Falling ticket sales may be a straw in the wind for the industry.<br>票房下滑也许是这个行业的一个风向信号。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>straws</b></td><td>clutch/grasp at ˈstraws</td><td>抓救命稻草；病急乱投医</td><td>Trying that herbal tea was clutching at straws, but she felt desperate.<br>喝那种草药茶纯属抓救命稻草，可她实在没辙了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stream</b></td><td>be/come on ˈstream</td><td>投入运行；开始生产</td><td>The second reactor comes on stream early next year, creating fifty jobs.<br>第二座反应堆明年初投产，将创造五十个岗位。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go, swim, etc. with the ˈstream/ˈtide</td><td>随大溜；顺应潮流</td><td>Most students just go with the stream and pick the popular courses.<br>多数学生都随大溜，挑热门课上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go, swim, etc. against the ˈstream/ˈtide</td><td>逆潮流而行；不随大溜</td><td>She swims against the tide by refusing to use social media at all.<br>她偏不随大溜，压根儿不用社交媒体。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>street</b></td><td>be (right) up your ˈstreet (especially BrE)</td><td>正合你意；对你的胃口</td><td>This puzzle book is right up your street and you'll finish it tonight.<br>这本谜题书正合你的口味，你今晚就能做完。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be (right) up your ˈalley (AmE usually) (informal)</td><td>正对某人胃口；正合适</td><td>A job mixing travel and photography is right up your alley.<br>又能旅行又能拍照的工作正对你的路子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>streets</b></td><td>be ˈstreets ahead (of sb/sth) (BrE, informal)</td><td>遥遥领先；强得多</td><td>Their software is streets ahead of anything else on the market.<br>他们的软件比市面上其他产品领先一大截。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈstreets (informal)</td><td>流落街头；无家可归</td><td>Losing that flat left him on the streets for most of the winter.<br>丢了那套公寓，他整个冬天大半时间都流落街头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the streets are ˌpaved with ˈgold (saying)</td><td>遍地是黄金（喻易发财）</td><td>He came south believing the streets are paved with gold, then found nothing.<br>他以为南方遍地黄金才南下，结果一无所获。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strength</b></td><td>go from ˌstrength to ˈstrength</td><td>越来越兴旺；蒸蒸日上</td><td>The little bakery has gone from strength to strength since it opened.<br>那家小面包店开业以来生意越做越红火。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the strength of sth</td><td>凭借；基于</td><td>She got the loan on the strength of one very optimistic forecast.<br>她凭着一份过于乐观的预测拿到了贷款。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a pillar/tower of ˈstrength</td><td>中流砥柱；精神支柱</td><td>My sister was a tower of strength during those months in hospital.<br>住院那几个月，姐姐是我最大的精神支柱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈforce/ˈstrength</td><td>大批地；大规模地</td><td>Fans turned out in force despite the rain and the early start.<br>尽管下雨又开赛早，球迷还是大批到场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strengthen</b></td><td>ˌstrengthen your ˈhand</td><td>增强实力；扩大权力</td><td>The election result strengthened her hand in the coming budget talks.<br>选举结果让她在接下来的预算谈判中更有底气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strengths</b></td><td>play to your ˈstrengths</td><td>发挥自己的长处</td><td>Play to your strengths and let someone else handle the spreadsheets.<br>发挥你的长处，表格让别人去弄。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stretch</b></td><td>at a ˈstretch</td><td>一口气；连续地</td><td>He can code for eight hours at a stretch without a break.<br>他能一口气写八小时代码不休息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by ˈno stretch of the imagination •not by ˌany stretch of the imagiˈnation</td><td>无论怎么想也不；绝对不是</td><td>By no stretch of the imagination could that meal be called cheap.<br>那顿饭再怎么说也算不上便宜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stretch your ˈlegs</td><td>活动腿脚；散散步</td><td>Let's stop at the next services and stretch our legs for ten minutes.<br>下个服务区停一下，活动活动腿脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stretch a ˈpoint</td><td>破例；通融</td><td>The librarian stretched a point and let me keep the book longer.<br>图书管理员破了个例，让我多借几天。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strictly</b></td><td>strictly ˈspeaking</td><td>严格说来</td><td>Strictly speaking, this cheese isn't vegetarian, though most people assume so.<br>严格说来这种奶酪并非素食，尽管大家都以为是。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stride</b></td><td>get into your ˈstride (BrE) (AmE hit (your) ˈstride)</td><td>进入状态；渐入佳境</td><td>By the second week the new teacher had got into her stride.<br>到第二周，新老师已经完全进入状态了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb off their ˈstride/ˈstroke</td><td>使某人分心；打乱节奏</td><td>The camera flash put the goalkeeper off his stride at the worst moment.<br>闪光灯在最要命的时刻让门将乱了阵脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(match sb) ˌstride for ˈstride</td><td>与某人并驾齐驱</td><td>The underdog matched the champion stride for stride until the final lap.<br>那位无名选手一直和冠军并驾齐驱到最后一圈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth in your ˈstride (BrE) (AmE take sth in ˈstride)</td><td>从容应对；处之泰然</td><td>She took the criticism in her stride and rewrote the chapter.<br>她从容接受批评，把那一章重写了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strides</b></td><td>make great, rapid, etc. ˈstrides (in sth/in doing sth)</td><td>取得巨大（或快速）进展</td><td>He has made great strides in Spanish since moving to Seville.<br>搬到塞维利亚后，他的西班牙语大有长进。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strike</b></td><td>strike a ˈbalance (between A and B)</td><td>找到平衡；折中兼顾</td><td>It's hard to strike a balance between work and time with kids.<br>在工作和陪孩子之间找平衡很难。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>strike a ˈbargain/ˈdeal (with sb)</td><td>与某人达成协议</td><td>They struck a deal with the landlord to paint the flat themselves.<br>他们和房东谈妥，自己动手粉刷公寓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>strike a blow for/against/at sth</td><td>维护（或打击）某事物</td><td>The ruling strikes a blow for tenants across the whole country.<br>这项裁决为全国的租户争了一口气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>strike ˌfear, ˌterror, etc. into sb/sb's ˈheart</td><td>使某人心生恐惧</td><td>The sound of that siren struck fear into everyone's heart that night.<br>那晚警报声让每个人都心头一紧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>strike ˈgold</td><td>挖到金矿；意外走运</td><td>The label struck gold with a band nobody else wanted to sign.<br>这家唱片公司签下一支没人要的乐队，结果大赚一笔。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>strike it ˈrich (informal)</td><td>发大财；暴富</td><td>He struck it rich selling phone cases online during the lockdown.<br>封城期间他在网上卖手机壳发了财。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>strike (it) ˈlucky (informal)</td><td>走运；碰上好运</td><td>We struck lucky and found a cheap flat near the university.<br>我们运气不错，在大学附近找到了便宜公寓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>strike a ˈpose/an ˈattitude</td><td>摆姿势；装模作样</td><td>She struck a pose on the steps while her friend took photos.<br>她在台阶上摆姿势，朋友给她拍照。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>strike while the ˌiron is ˈhot (saying)</td><td>趁热打铁</td><td>They liked your pitch, so strike while the iron is hot.<br>他们看好你的方案，趁热打铁吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>striking</b></td><td>within ˈstriking distance (of sth)</td><td>近在咫尺；触手可及</td><td>The cottage is within striking distance of both the lake and town.<br>那间小屋离湖和镇上都很近。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>string</b></td><td>have/keep sb on a ˈstring</td><td>牵着某人鼻子走；玩弄</td><td>She kept him on a string for months without ever saying yes.<br>她吊了他好几个月，始终没答应。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strings</b></td><td>(with) no ˈstrings attached (also without ˈstrings)</td><td>不附带任何条件</td><td>The loan comes with no strings attached, which sounds too good.<br>这笔贷款不附带任何条件，好得让人生疑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stroke</b></td><td>at a/one (single) ˈstroke</td><td>一举；一下子</td><td>The new law wiped out those fees at a stroke last April.<br>去年四月新法一出，那些收费一下子全取消了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not do a ˈstroke (of ˈwork)</td><td>一点活儿也不干</td><td>He hasn't done a stroke of work since the holidays began.<br>放假以来他一点活儿都没干过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on/at the ˌstroke of ˈeight, ˈmidnight, etc.</td><td>在八点（或午夜等）整</td><td>The bells rang on the stroke of midnight and everyone cheered loudly.<br>午夜钟声一响，大家高声欢呼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb off their ˈstroke</td><td>打乱某人的节奏</td><td>Constant questions put the surgeon off his stroke during the operation.<br>不停发问打乱了外科医生手术的节奏。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strong</b></td><td>be ˈstrong on sth</td><td>擅长某方面</td><td>This phone is strong on battery life but weak on camera quality.<br>这款手机胜在续航，摄像头就差些。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be your ˈstrong point/suit</td><td>是某人的强项</td><td>Patience has never been my strong point, as my students know.<br>耐心从来不是我的强项，学生都清楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come on ˈstrong (with sb) (informal)</td><td>言辞强硬；过于主动</td><td>He came on strong at the party and made everyone uncomfortable.<br>他在派对上太咄咄逼人，弄得大家都不自在。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a strong ˈstomach</td><td>不怕恶心；受得住</td><td>You need a strong stomach to watch that documentary about the slaughterhouse.<br>看那部屠宰场纪录片得有个好胃口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>struck</b></td><td>be ˈstruck by/on/with sb/sth (informal)</td><td>被打动；迷上</td><td>I was struck by how calm she stayed during the whole crisis.<br>整场危机中她那么镇定，我很受触动。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be struck ˈdumb (with sth)</td><td>惊得说不出话</td><td>We were struck dumb with shock when they announced the winner.<br>宣布获奖者时，我们惊得一句话都说不出。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈdumbstruck (adj.)</td><td>惊得目瞪口呆的</td><td>She stood dumbstruck when they read out her name as the winner.<br>念到她名字是冠军时，她愣在那里目瞪口呆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strut</b></td><td>ˌstrut your ˈstuff (informal)</td><td>炫技；露一手</td><td>The dancers strutted their stuff in the square all Saturday afternoon.<br>舞者们整个周六下午都在广场上大展身手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stubborn</b></td><td>(as) ˌstubborn as a ˈmule (often disapproving)</td><td>非常固执；倔得像头驴</td><td>Grandad is stubborn as a mule about using his old flip phone.<br>爷爷死活要用他那部老翻盖手机，倔得像头驴。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stuck</b></td><td>get stuck ˈin •get stuck ˈinto sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>起劲地干起来</td><td>Everyone got stuck into the painting and finished the hall by lunchtime.<br>大家撸起袖子刷漆，午饭前就把门厅刷完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stuff</b></td><td>do your ˈstuff (informal)</td><td>露一手；施展本领</td><td>Stand back and let the sound engineer do her stuff for once.<br>往后站，这回让音响师露一手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not give a ˈstuff (BrE, slang)</td><td>毫不在乎</td><td>He doesn't give a stuff what the neighbours think of his garden.<br>邻居怎么看他的花园，他压根不在乎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stuff and ˈnonsense (spoken, old-fashioned)</td><td>一派胡言；胡说八道</td><td>Stuff and nonsense, nobody ever caught a cold from wet hair.<br>一派胡言，谁会因为头发没干就感冒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stuff him, that, etc. (spoken, informal)</td><td>去他的；才不管那套</td><td>Stuff him, we're going to the concert whether he approves or not.<br>去他的，不管他同不同意我们都去看演唱会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's the ˈstuff (informal)</td><td>这就对了；正该如此</td><td>That's the stuff, keep your elbow up and hit through the ball.<br>这就对了，胳膊肘抬高，把球打透。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stuffed</b></td><td>get ˈstuffed (also get ˈknotted less frequent)</td><td>滚开；少来这套</td><td>I told the caller to get stuffed and hung up the phone.<br>我让那个打电话的滚开，然后挂了电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a stuffed ˈshirt (informal, disapproving)</td><td>一本正经的人；古板的人</td><td>The new director is a stuffed shirt who hates any kind of joke.<br>新主任古板得很，一点玩笑都开不得。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>style</b></td><td>be (not) sb's ˈstyle</td><td>（不）合某人的口味</td><td>Loud parties really aren't my style, but I'll come for an hour.<br>闹哄哄的派对不合我的口味，不过我会去待一小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sublime</b></td><td>from the subˈlime to the riˈdiculous</td><td>从崇高跌到荒唐</td><td>The concert went from the sublime to the ridiculous in about ten minutes.<br>这场音乐会十分钟内就从崇高滑向了荒唐。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>substance</b></td><td>a woman, man, person, etc. of ˈsubstance</td><td>有钱有势的人；举足轻重的人</td><td>Everyone treated him as a man of substance once the factory succeeded.<br>工厂一做起来，人人都把他当成有头有脸的人物。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>succeeds</b></td><td>nothing sucˌceeds like sucˈcess (saying)</td><td>一事成，事事顺</td><td>After one hit film she had five offers, since nothing succeeds like success.<br>一部电影火了，她就接到五个邀约，真是一顺百顺。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>such</b></td><td>as ˈsuch</td><td>就其本身而言；严格意义上</td><td>There's no rule as such, just a habit everyone here follows.<br>严格说没什么规定，只是这里大家的习惯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsuch as it ˈis</td><td>尽管质量不高；虽说不怎么样</td><td>You can borrow my bike, such as it is, but the brakes squeak.<br>我的自行车你可以骑，虽说破了点，刹车还吱吱响。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suck</b></td><td>suck it and ˈsee (BrE, informal)</td><td>试试才知道</td><td>We can't predict the result, so let's suck it and see.<br>结果没法预测，试试才知道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>suck it ˈup (AmE, informal)</td><td>忍着；坦然承受</td><td>Nobody likes the night shift, but we just suck it up.<br>谁都不爱上夜班，可我们只能忍着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sudden</b></td><td>all of a ˈsudden</td><td>突然；冷不防</td><td>All of a sudden the lights went out and the music stopped.<br>突然间灯灭了，音乐也停了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sudden ˈdeath</td><td>突然死亡法（加时决胜）</td><td>The final went to sudden death after ninety minutes without a goal.<br>九十分钟没进球，决赛进入了突然死亡决胜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suffer</b></td><td>not suffer fools ˈgladly</td><td>不能容忍蠢人</td><td>My editor doesn't suffer fools gladly, so check your facts twice.<br>我的编辑最容不得糊涂虫，材料你多核两遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sufferance</b></td><td>on ˈsufferance</td><td>勉强获准；受人容忍</td><td>He stayed in the flat on sufferance until he found his own place.<br>在找到自己的住处前，他勉强被容许住在那套公寓里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suffice</b></td><td>suffice (it) to say (that)... (formal)</td><td>只需说……就够了</td><td>Suffice it to say that the interview did not go very well.<br>只需说一句：面试很不顺利。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sugar</b></td><td>a ˈsugar daddy (informal)</td><td>包养年轻女子的阔老头</td><td>She joked that she needed a sugar daddy to pay her rent.<br>她开玩笑说自己需要个阔老头来付房租。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sugar/sweeten the ˈpill (BrE)</td><td>加点甜头；使坏事易于接受</td><td>They sugared the pill with a bonus before announcing the pay freeze.<br>宣布冻薪前，他们先发了笔奖金当甜头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suggestion</b></td><td>at/on sb's sugˈgestion</td><td>依某人的建议</td><td>At my sister's suggestion we booked the tickets three months early.<br>按我姐的建议，我们提前三个月订了票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suit</b></td><td>suit your/sb's ˈbook (BrE, informal)</td><td>合某人心意；对某人方便</td><td>The later meeting suits my book because I can drop the kids off.<br>会议改晚点正合我意，我可以先送孩子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>suit sb (right) ˌdown to the ˈground (BrE, informal)</td><td>完全合某人心意</td><td>Working from home suits me right down to the ground these days.<br>这阵子居家办公完全合我的心意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>suit yourˈself (informal)</td><td>随你便</td><td>Suit yourself, but I'm taking the early train whatever you decide.<br>随你便，反正不管你怎么定我都坐早班车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suits</b></td><td>(the) men in grey ˈsuits (BrE)</td><td>幕后掌权的官僚</td><td>The men in grey suits decided her fate long before the vote.<br>早在投票前，幕后那些人就定了她的命运。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sum</b></td><td>be greater/more than the ˌsum of its ˈparts</td><td>整体大于部分之和</td><td>This band is greater than the sum of its parts on stage.<br>这支乐队在台上的效果远胜过成员各自相加。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈsum (formal)</td><td>总之；总而言之</td><td>In sum, the trial worked but costs far more than we expected.<br>总之，试点有效，但花费远超预期。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>summer</b></td><td>an ˌIndian ˈsummer</td><td>深秋的晴暖时节；晚年的黄金期</td><td>We had an Indian summer that October and ate outside every evening.<br>那年十月出了个小阳春，我们天天在户外吃晚饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>summon</b></td><td>pluck/screw/summon up (your/the) ˈcourage (to do sth)</td><td>鼓起勇气（做某事）</td><td>He finally summoned up the courage to ask her out for coffee.<br>他终于鼓起勇气约她去喝咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sun</b></td><td>under the ˈsun</td><td>天底下；世上</td><td>They sell every kind of cheese under the sun at that market.<br>那个市场上天底下的奶酪品种都有得卖。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sunday</b></td><td>your Sunday ˈbest (informal, humorous)</td><td>最好的衣服；节日盛装</td><td>Grandma made us wear our Sunday best for the family photograph.<br>奶奶让我们穿上最好的衣服拍全家福。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sundry</b></td><td>all and ˈsundry (informal)</td><td>所有人；各色人等</td><td>He told all and sundry about the promotion before it was confirmed.<br>升职还没定，他就见人就说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sunk</b></td><td>be ˈsunk in sth</td><td>陷入（沉思或愁绪）中</td><td>She was sunk in thought and didn't hear me come in.<br>她陷在沉思里，没听见我进来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sunny-side</b></td><td>sunny-side ˈup (AmE)</td><td>（鸡蛋）只煎一面的</td><td>I'll have two eggs sunny-side up with toast and black coffee.<br>我要两个单面煎蛋，配吐司和黑咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suppose</b></td><td>I don't supˈpose you could...</td><td>不知你能否……（客气请求）</td><td>I don't suppose you could give me a lift to the station?<br>不知你能不能捎我去车站？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I supˈpose so</td><td>我想是吧（勉强同意）</td><td>'Can Tom come too?' 'I suppose so, if he behaves himself.'<br>“汤姆也能来吗？”“我想可以吧，只要他老实点。”</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>supposed</b></td><td>(not) be supˈposed to (do sth)</td><td>按规定（不）应当</td><td>You're not supposed to park here between eight and six on weekdays.<br>工作日八点到六点不准在这儿停车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's ˈthat supposed to mean? (informal)</td><td>你这话什么意思（表气愤或不解）</td><td>'You've changed a lot lately.' 'What's that supposed to mean, exactly?'<br>“你最近变了不少。”“你这话到底什么意思？”</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sure</b></td><td>be sure to do sth (also be sure and do sth spoken)</td><td>务必做某事</td><td>Be sure to lock the back door before you leave tomorrow morning.<br>明早出门前一定要锁好后门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈsure (informal)</td><td>肯定；无疑</td><td>He'll be late again, that's for sure, so order without him.<br>他肯定又要迟到，别等他先点吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈsure (of sth/that...)</td><td>弄清；确保</td><td>Make sure the oven is off before we head out to dinner.<br>出门吃饭前确认一下烤箱关了没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) sure as eggs is ˈeggs (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>千真万确；肯定无疑</td><td>Sure as eggs is eggs, he'll ask for money again next week.<br>千真万确，下周他准又来借钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) sure as ˈhell (AmE, informal)</td><td>的确；毫无疑问</td><td>I sure as hell won't drive four hours for a ten-minute meeting.<br>我才不会为个十分钟的会开四小时车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sure eˈnough</td><td>果然；果真</td><td>I said it would rain, and sure enough the picnic was cancelled.<br>我说会下雨，果然野餐取消了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈsure of yourself (sometimes disapproving)</td><td>自信；过于自信</td><td>She's very sure of herself for someone who started only last month.<br>上个月才来的人，她可真够自信的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌsure ˈthing (spoken, especially AmE)</td><td>当然；没问题</td><td>'Can you cover my shift?' 'Sure thing, just tell me when.'<br>“能替我上班吗？”“没问题，说个时间就行。”</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to be ˈsure (formal)</td><td>诚然；固然</td><td>The house is small, to be sure, but the garden is enormous.<br>房子固然小，但花园大得很。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>surface</b></td><td>below/beneath the ˈsurface</td><td>表象之下；实际上</td><td>Beneath the surface, the two sides still disagree about almost everything.<br>表面之下，双方几乎在所有问题上仍有分歧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈsurface</td><td>表面上看</td><td>On the surface everything seemed fine, but the accounts told another story.<br>表面上一切正常，账目却是另一回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>surprise</b></td><td>surˌprise, surˈprise (spoken, ironic)</td><td>果然不出所料</td><td>Surprise, surprise, he forgot to bring the tickets he promised to print.<br>瞧吧，他答应打印的票果然忘带了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb by surˈprise</td><td>使某人吃惊；出其不意</td><td>The question took me by surprise and I answered it badly.<br>那个问题把我问懵了，我答得很糟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>survival</b></td><td>(the) surˌvival of the ˈfittest</td><td>适者生存</td><td>In that market it's survival of the fittest and prices decide everything.<br>那个市场就是适者生存，价格决定一切。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suspicion</b></td><td>be aˌbove/beˌyond suˈspicion</td><td>无可怀疑；毫无嫌疑</td><td>As treasurer, her accounts must be above suspicion at all times.<br>身为司库，她的账目任何时候都必须清白无疑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be under suˈspicion (of sth)</td><td>受到怀疑；涉嫌</td><td>Two staff members are under suspicion of leaking the client list.<br>两名员工涉嫌泄露客户名单。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the finger of susˈpicion</td><td>怀疑的矛头</td><td>The finger of suspicion quickly pointed at the only key holder.<br>怀疑的矛头很快指向了唯一有钥匙的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suspiciously</b></td><td>look/sound suspiciously like sth (often humorous)</td><td>看（听）上去很像</td><td>That excuse sounds suspiciously like the one you used last Friday.<br>这借口听着跟你上周五用的那个特别像。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>swallow</b></td><td>one ˌswallow doesn't make a ˈsummer (saying)</td><td>一燕不成夏；勿以偏概全</td><td>We won once, but one swallow doesn't make a summer, so stay focused.<br>我们只赢了一场，一燕不成夏，别松劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one swallow does not make a ˈsummer (saying)</td><td>一花独放不是春；别过早乐观</td><td>One swallow does not make a summer, so don't celebrate a single order.<br>独燕不成夏，一张订单还不值得庆祝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>swallow the ˈbait (informal)</td><td>上钩；中圈套</td><td>They swallowed the bait and clicked the link in that fake email.<br>他们上了钩，点开了那封假邮件里的链接。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>swallow your ˈpride</td><td>忍气吞声；放下面子</td><td>He swallowed his pride and asked his younger brother for help.<br>他放下面子，向弟弟开口求助。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>swathe</b></td><td>cut a ˈswathe through sth</td><td>大肆破坏；横扫</td><td>The storm cut a swathe through the orchards along the whole valley.<br>风暴横扫了整条山谷的果园。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sway</b></td><td>hold ˈsway (over sb/sth) (literary)</td><td>支配；统治</td><td>That old theory held sway over economists for nearly fifty years.<br>那套旧理论主宰了经济学界将近五十年。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>swear</b></td><td>swear ˈblind (that)... (informal)</td><td>一口咬定；发誓说</td><td>He swore blind he'd posted the letter, but it was still there.<br>他一口咬定信寄了，可信还在那儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>swear like a ˈtrooper (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>满口脏话</td><td>My gentle aunt swears like a trooper whenever she watches football.<br>我那温柔的姑妈一看足球就满嘴脏话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>swear sb to ˈsecrecy</td><td>让某人发誓保密</td><td>She swore us all to secrecy about the surprise party next month.<br>她让我们全都发誓，对下月的惊喜派对保密。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweat</b></td><td>be in a ˈsweat</td><td>满身大汗；焦虑不安</td><td>I was in a sweat about the deadline all weekend long.<br>整个周末我都为截止日期急得冒汗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>break ˈsweat (BrE) (AmE break a ˈsweat)</td><td>费大力气；使大劲</td><td>He carried both heavy suitcases upstairs without even breaking sweat.<br>他把两只重箱子搬上楼，连汗都没出。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by the sweat of your ˈbrow (literary)</td><td>靠自己的辛勤劳动</td><td>He built that farm by the sweat of his brow over thirty years.<br>那片农场是他三十年血汗一点点挣出来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>don't ˈsweat it (AmE, spoken)</td><td>别担心；不必在意</td><td>Don't sweat it, we can easily reprint the flyers tomorrow morning.<br>别担心，明早重印传单很容易。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>don't sweat the ˈsmall stuff (AmE, spoken)</td><td>别为小事烦心</td><td>Don't sweat the small stuff; the guests won't notice the napkin colour.<br>别为鸡毛蒜皮操心，客人不会注意餐巾颜色。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no ˈsweat (spoken)</td><td>没问题；小事一桩</td><td>'Can you drive me over?' 'No sweat, I'm going that way anyway.'<br>“能开车送我过去吗？”“小事一桩，我正好顺路。”</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sweat ˈblood (informal)</td><td>拼命干；极度焦虑</td><td>We sweated blood to get the exhibition ready in three weeks.<br>为了三周内布好展，我们拼了命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sweat it ˈout (informal)</td><td>苦熬；坚持到最后</td><td>He sweated it out in the waiting room until the results came.<br>他在候诊室里苦等，直到结果出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sweat like a ˈpig (informal)</td><td>大汗淋漓</td><td>I was sweating like a pig by the time I reached the summit.<br>爬到山顶时我已经大汗淋漓。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweep</b></td><td>sweep the ˈboard</td><td>囊括所有奖项</td><td>The little Irish film swept the board at the awards last night.<br>昨晚那部爱尔兰小成本电影包揽了所有奖项。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sweep sb off their ˈfeet</td><td>使某人倾倒；令某人着迷</td><td>He swept her off her feet with letters and terrible poetry.<br>他用一封封信和蹩脚的诗把她迷得神魂颠倒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweet</b></td><td>do sth in your ˌown sweet ˈtime/way (informal)</td><td>随心所欲地做；不慌不忙</td><td>He'll finish the shed in his own sweet time, so stop asking.<br>他会按自己的节奏把棚子搭完，别再催了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a sweet ˈtooth</td><td>爱吃甜食</td><td>She has such a sweet tooth that dessert always comes first.<br>她太爱吃甜食了，永远先吃甜点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep sb ˈsweet (informal)</td><td>讨好某人；哄住某人</td><td>Keep the landlord sweet and he might fix the boiler quickly.<br>把房东哄好点，他也许会赶紧修锅炉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>she's ˈsweet (AustralE, New Zealand, informal)</td><td>一切都好；没问题</td><td>Don't worry about the booking, mate, she's sweet, I called them already.<br>订位的事别操心，兄弟，都搞定了，我打过电话了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sweet FˈA (also less frequent sweet Fanny ˈAdams) (BrE, informal)</td><td>什么也没有；屁事没干</td><td>I did sweet FA all weekend except watch films and eat toast.<br>整个周末我啥也没干，就看电影吃吐司。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sweet ˈnothings (informal, usually humorous)</td><td>甜言蜜语；绵绵情话</td><td>They sat whispering sweet nothings while the rest of us ordered food.<br>我们点菜的时候，他俩坐在那儿说悄悄情话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the sweet smell of sucˈcess (informal)</td><td>成功的喜悦</td><td>After ten years of rejection she finally tasted the sweet smell of success.<br>被拒了十年，她终于尝到了成功的滋味。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweetness</b></td><td>be all ˌsweetness and ˈlight</td><td>和蔼可亲；一团和气</td><td>He's all sweetness and light until you question his budget figures.<br>他一团和气，除非你质疑他的预算数字。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>swim</b></td><td>in(to) the ˈswim (of things) (informal)</td><td>融入活动；跟上潮流</td><td>Joining the choir got her back into the swim of things quickly.<br>加入合唱团让她很快重新融入了大家。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>swing</b></td><td>get in/into the ˈswing (of sth) (informal)</td><td>进入状态；投入其中</td><td>Give it a week and you'll get into the swing of things.<br>过一周你就适应节奏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go with a ˈswing (BrE)</td><td>（活动）热闹成功</td><td>The party went with a swing once the neighbours brought their guitars.<br>邻居抱来吉他后，派对一下子热闹起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>swing both ˈways (informal)</td><td>是双性恋</td><td>He mentioned casually that he swings both ways and nobody blinked.<br>他随口说自己是双性恋，谁也没觉得意外。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌswing into ˈaction</td><td>立即行动起来</td><td>The rescue team swung into action minutes after the call came in.<br>电话打来几分钟后，救援队就出动了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>swing the ˈlead (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>装病偷懒</td><td>The foreman thinks half the crew are swinging the lead today.<br>工头觉得今天有一半人在装病偷懒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>swings</b></td><td>swings and ˈroundabouts (BrE, informal)</td><td>有得有失；失之东隅收之桑榆</td><td>Cheaper rent but a much longer commute, so it's swings and roundabouts.<br>房租便宜可通勤远多了，算是有得有失。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what you gain on the swings you lose on the ˈroundabouts (saying)</td><td>有所得必有所失</td><td>What you gain on the swings you lose on the roundabouts, as Dad says.<br>正如老爸所说，有所得必有所失。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sword</b></td><td>a/the sword of ˈDamocles (literary)</td><td>达摩克利斯之剑；随时降临的祸患</td><td>The threat of redundancy hung over us like a sword of Damocles.<br>裁员的威胁像达摩克利斯之剑一样悬在我们头上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>swords</b></td><td>beat/turn swords into ˈploughshares (literary)</td><td>铸剑为犁；化干戈为玉帛</td><td>The treaty promised to turn swords into ploughshares across the whole region.<br>条约承诺让整个地区铸剑为犁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>syllable</b></td><td>in words of one ˈsyllable</td><td>用最浅显的话；通俗地说</td><td>Explain it in words of one syllable, because I'm completely lost.<br>用最简单的话讲吧，我完全听糊涂了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>symbol</b></td><td>a ˈstatus symbol</td><td>身份的象征</td><td>For him that watch is a status symbol rather than a timepiece.<br>对他来说那块表是身份象征，而不是看时间的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sympathy</b></td><td>in ˈsympathy with sth (written)</td><td>随……变动；受……影响</td><td>Share prices fell in sympathy with the slump in oil this week.<br>本周股价随油价大跌而下滑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of ˈsympathy with sb/sth (written)</td><td>不赞同；不支持</td><td>She resigned, being completely out of sympathy with the new party line.<br>她辞职了，因为完全不认同新的党派路线。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sync</b></td><td>in/out of ˈsync (informal)</td><td>同步；不同步</td><td>The sound was out of sync with the picture for the whole film.<br>整部电影的声音和画面都不同步。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>system</b></td><td>get sth out of your ˈsystem (informal)</td><td>发泄出来；排遣掉</td><td>Go for a run and get the anger out of your system.<br>去跑一圈，把这股火发出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>systems</b></td><td>all systems ˈgo (for sth) (informal)</td><td>一切就绪；万事俱备</td><td>It's all systems go for the launch on Friday at last.<br>周五的发布终于万事俱备了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>T</b></td><td>to a ˈT/tee (BrE, informal)</td><td>恰好；分毫不差</td><td>That jacket fits you to a T, as if it was tailored.<br>那件外套你穿正合身，像是量身做的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the smallest deˈtail</td><td>到最细微处；极其详尽</td><td>She described the room to the smallest detail, right down to the wallpaper.<br>她把房间描述得极其细致，连墙纸都说到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>table</b></td><td>on the ˈtable (BrE)</td><td>提交讨论中；供考虑</td><td>The pay offer is on the table until Friday afternoon at five.<br>这份薪资方案的有效期到周五下午五点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/lay your ˈcards on the table</td><td>摊牌；坦率说明</td><td>Let's put our cards on the table and discuss the real budget.<br>咱们摊开来谈，说说真实的预算。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tables</b></td><td>turn the ˈtables (on sb)</td><td>扭转局势；转败为胜</td><td>She turned the tables on her rivals with one very clever question.<br>她用一个巧妙的问题反将了对手一军。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tabs</b></td><td>keep (close) ˈtabs on sb/sth (informal)</td><td>密切注意；监视</td><td>The bank keeps close tabs on every transaction over ten thousand pounds.<br>银行密切监控每一笔超过一万英镑的交易。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tail</b></td><td>on sb's ˈtail (informal)</td><td>紧跟；尾随</td><td>There's a police car on our tail, so slow down a bit.<br>后面有辆警车跟着，慢一点开。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(at) the tail ˈend (of sth)</td><td>末尾；尾声</td><td>We arrived at the tail end of the party and missed the cake.<br>我们赶到时派对已近尾声，蛋糕都没吃上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the tail (is) wagging the ˈdog (also let the tail wag the ˈdog)</td><td>本末倒置；喧宾夺主</td><td>When marketing decides the science, that's the tail wagging the dog.<br>让营销来定科研方向，就是本末倒置。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn ˈtail (and run, flee, etc.)</td><td>转身逃跑；临阵脱逃</td><td>The fox turned tail and ran the moment the dog barked.<br>狗一叫，狐狸转身就跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with your tail between your ˈlegs (informal)</td><td>夹着尾巴；灰溜溜地</td><td>He came back with his tail between his legs after the argument.<br>吵完架他夹着尾巴回来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take</b></td><td>be on the ˈtake (informal)</td><td>收受贿赂</td><td>Two officers were on the take for years before anyone noticed.<br>两名警官受贿多年才被人察觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I, ˌyou, ˌetc. can't take sb ˈanywhere (informal, often humorous)</td><td>某人上不了台面</td><td>He spilled wine on the host, so honestly, you can't take him anywhere.<br>他把酒洒在主人身上，真是带不出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth as it ˈcomes</td><td>顺其自然；随遇而安</td><td>We have no plan for the trip; we'll take it as it comes.<br>这趟旅行没做计划，走到哪算哪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈtake it (informal)</td><td>忍受；承受得住</td><td>The training is brutal, but she can take it better than anyone.<br>训练很残酷，可她比谁都扛得住。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈtake it (that...)</td><td>认为；猜想；假定</td><td>I take it that you've already spoken to the landlord about this.<br>我想这事你已经跟房东说过了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take it from ˈhere/ˈthere</td><td>接手余下的事</td><td>Draft the outline and I'll take it from there next week.<br>你先拟个提纲，下周剩下的我来接手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take it from ˈme (that...) (informal)</td><td>相信我；我敢担保</td><td>Take it from me, that road is closed every single winter morning.<br>信我一句，那条路每个冬天早上都封。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take it on/upon yourself to do sth</td><td>自作主张做某事</td><td>She took it upon herself to rewrite the entire report overnight.<br>她自作主张，连夜把整份报告重写了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take it ˈout of sb •take a lot ˈout of sb</td><td>使人筋疲力尽</td><td>Those night shifts really take it out of you after a while.<br>上久了夜班真会把人累垮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take it ˈout on sb (informal)</td><td>拿某人出气</td><td>Don't take it out on the kids just because work was awful.<br>别因为工作不顺就拿孩子撒气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb ˈout of himself, herself, etc.</td><td>使某人排解忧愁</td><td>A weekend by the sea took her out of herself for once.<br>在海边过了个周末，她总算散了散心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>takes</b></td><td>have what it ˈtakes (to do sth) (informal)</td><td>具备成功的条件</td><td>He has what it takes to run this kitchen on his own.<br>他有本事独自撑起这间厨房。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>taking</b></td><td>be sb's for the ˈtaking</td><td>唾手可得</td><td>With two rivals injured, the title was hers for the taking.<br>两个对手受伤，冠军对她来说唾手可得。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be there for the ˈtaking</td><td>唾手可得；手到擒来</td><td>The market was there for the taking and nobody moved fast enough.<br>那块市场唾手可得，却没人动作够快。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk</b></td><td>be all ˈtalk (and no action) (disapproving)</td><td>光说不练</td><td>He's all talk and no action when it comes to fixing things.<br>一说到修东西，他就光说不做。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be the talk of sth (informal)</td><td>成为大家谈论的话题</td><td>Her wedding dress was the talk of the village for weeks afterwards.<br>她的婚纱成了村里好几周的谈资。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be the talk of the ˈtown</td><td>成为全城的话题</td><td>Overnight she became the talk of the town after that radio interview.<br>那次电台采访后，她一夜之间成了全城的话题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈyou can/can't talk (also look who's ˈtalking) (spoken)</td><td>你还好意思说别人</td><td>You can't talk, your desk is even messier than mine right now.<br>你还好意思说，你桌子比我的还乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you're a ˈfine one to talk (spoken)</td><td>你还有脸说别人</td><td>You're a fine one to talk about being late, Mr Nine-Thirty.<br>你还有脸说人家迟到，九点半先生。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈtalk about... (spoken)</td><td>真是……（用于强调）</td><td>Talk about bad luck, the tyre burst outside the wedding venue.<br>真是倒霉，轮胎就在婚礼场地门口爆了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk ˈbig (disapproving)</td><td>说大话；吹牛</td><td>He talks big about his contacts but never introduces anyone to us.<br>他把人脉吹得天花乱坠，却从没给我们引荐过谁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk ˈdirty (informal)</td><td>说下流话</td><td>He started talking dirty on the phone and she hung up.<br>他在电话里开始说下流话，她直接挂了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk sb's ˈear off (especially AmE, informal, especially disapproving)</td><td>对某人唠叨不停</td><td>My neighbour talked my ear off about her cats for an hour.<br>邻居拉着我聊了一小时她的猫，耳朵都磨出茧了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk your ˈhead off (informal)</td><td>说个不停</td><td>She talked her head off the whole way to the airport.<br>去机场一路上她嘴就没停过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk the hind leg(s) off a ˈdonkey (informal, humorous)</td><td>唠叨不休；滔滔不绝</td><td>Uncle Ray could talk the hind legs off a donkey at parties.<br>雷叔在聚会上能说得没完没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk ˈshop</td><td>在社交场合谈公事</td><td>No talking shop at dinner, we agreed that before we sat down.<br>吃饭不谈工作，坐下前就说好的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk through the back of your ˈhead (informal)</td><td>胡说八道</td><td>He's talking through the back of his head about those tax rules.<br>他讲那些税法完全是胡说八道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk through your ˈhat (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>信口开河；瞎扯</td><td>Ignore him, he's talking through his hat about the election again.<br>别理他，他又在瞎扯选举的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk to a brick ˈwall (informal)</td><td>对牛弹琴；白费口舌</td><td>Explaining anything to that department is like talking to a brick wall.<br>跟那个部门解释什么都跟对墙说话一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk ˈtough (on sth) (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>说话口气强硬</td><td>Politicians talk tough on crime, then cut the police budget again.<br>政客对犯罪问题口气强硬，转头又削减警力预算。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk ˈturkey (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>谈正事；开门见山</td><td>Let's stop the small talk and talk turkey about the price.<br>别寒暄了，咱们直接谈价钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talk your way out of sth/out of doing sth</td><td>靠嘴皮子脱身</td><td>He talked his way out of a speeding ticket somehow last night.<br>昨晚他不知怎么靠一张嘴躲过了超速罚单。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talker</b></td><td>a fast ˈtalker</td><td>花言巧语的人</td><td>The salesman was a fast talker and I signed without reading anything.<br>那推销员嘴皮子太溜，我什么都没看就签了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talking</b></td><td>ˈnow you're talking (spoken)</td><td>这话我爱听；正合我意</td><td>Free pizza? Now you're talking, count me in for the evening.<br>免费披萨？这话我爱听，晚上算我一个。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>talking of sb/sth (spoken, especially BrE)</td><td>说到；提起</td><td>Talking of holidays, have you booked anything for the summer yet?<br>说到假期，你暑假订好行程了吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tall</b></td><td>stand ˈtall (especially AmE)</td><td>昂首挺胸；自信坦然</td><td>She stood tall and read her statement to the whole courtroom.<br>她昂首挺胸，向全庭宣读了自己的陈述。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌtall ˈorder</td><td>难办的要求；苛求</td><td>Finishing this by Friday is a tall order with two people off.<br>两个人请假，周五完工实在强人所难。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌtall ˈstory (especially BrE) (AmE usually a ˌtall ˈtale)</td><td>荒诞的故事；吹牛</td><td>Grandpa told another tall story about wrestling a bear in Canada.<br>爷爷又讲了个在加拿大跟熊搏斗的离奇故事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tandem</b></td><td>in ˈtandem (with sb/sth)</td><td>协同；一前一后地</td><td>The two charities work in tandem to house families every winter.<br>这两家慈善机构每年冬天协同安置无家可归的家庭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tangent</b></td><td>go off at a ˈtangent (BrE) (AmE go off on a ˈtangent)</td><td>突然改变话题（或思路）</td><td>He goes off at a tangent whenever anyone mentions his old school.<br>一有人提起他的母校，他就扯到别处去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tank</b></td><td>in the ˈtank (AmE, informal, business)</td><td>（股价等）急剧下跌</td><td>The stock went in the tank after the recall was announced.<br>召回消息一出，股价就一路跳水。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tantrum</b></td><td>throw a ˈtantrum (BrE also throw a ˈwobbly)</td><td>大发脾气；耍性子</td><td>The toddler threw a tantrum in the cereal aisle again today.<br>今天那小家伙又在麦片货架前撒泼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tap</b></td><td>(be) on ˈtap</td><td>随时可用；现成的</td><td>There's free legal advice on tap for students during exam week.<br>考试周期间随时都有免费法律咨询供学生使用。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>taped</b></td><td>have sb/sth ˈtaped (BrE, informal)</td><td>摸清底细；彻底了解</td><td>After a month she had the whole filing system taped.<br>一个月后，整套归档系统她已摸得门儿清。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tar</b></td><td>tar sb/sth with the same ˈbrush</td><td>一概而论；视为一丘之貉</td><td>Don't tar every landlord with the same brush because of one.<br>别因为一个房东就把所有房东一竿子打死。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wouldn't do sth for all the ˌtea in ˈChina</td><td>无论如何也不做某事</td><td>I wouldn't move back to that town for all the tea in China.<br>给我再多好处，我也不搬回那个镇子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb to ˈtask (about/for/over sth)</td><td>严厉批评某人；训斥</td><td>The head took him to task over the missing exam papers.<br>校长为丢失试卷的事狠狠训了他一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in bad, the worst possible, etc. ˈtaste</td><td>趣味低俗；很不得体</td><td>That joke about the funeral was in the worst possible taste.<br>拿葬礼开的那个玩笑实在低俗透顶。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in good, the best possible, etc. ˈtaste</td><td>得体；有品位</td><td>The memorial was simple and in the best possible taste.<br>那场追思会朴素而得体。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave a bad/nasty ˈtaste in the/your mouth</td><td>使人心里不痛快</td><td>The way they fired him left a nasty taste in my mouth.<br>他们辞退他的方式让我心里很不是滋味。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈtaste</td><td>按各人口味（加调料）</td><td>Add salt and pepper to taste, then let the sauce simmer gently.<br>按口味加盐和胡椒，然后让酱汁慢慢煨着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tatters</b></td><td>be in ˈtatters</td><td>破烂不堪；彻底破灭</td><td>His reputation was in tatters after the newspaper published those photos.<br>报纸登出那些照片后，他的名声一败涂地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tear yourself/sth ˈloose (from sb/sth)</td><td>挣脱；奋力摆脱</td><td>She tore herself loose from his grip and ran towards the door.<br>她奋力挣脱他的手，朝门口跑去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tear ˈloose (informal)</td><td>用力挣脱；奋力逃开</td><td>The dog tore loose and chased the ducks across the whole park.<br>狗挣脱绳子，追着鸭子跑遍了整个公园。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tear sb ˈoff a strip •tear a ˈstrip off sb (BrE, informal)</td><td>痛骂某人</td><td>The coach tore a strip off him for arguing with the referee.<br>他跟裁判顶嘴，被教练骂得狗血淋头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tear sb/sth to ˈpieces/ˈshreds</td><td>批得体无完肤；撕成碎片</td><td>The critics tore his second novel to shreds within a single week.<br>评论界一周之内就把他的第二部小说批得体无完肤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tearing</b></td><td>(be in) a tearing ˈhurry/rush (especially BrE)</td><td>急急忙忙</td><td>She left in a tearing hurry and forgot her laptop on the table.<br>她走得慌慌张张，把笔记本电脑忘在桌上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tee</b></td><td>to a ˈT/tee</td><td>恰到好处；分毫不差</td><td>The description of my brother fits him to a tee.<br>对我弟弟的那段描述简直分毫不差。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>teeter</b></td><td>teeter on the ˈbrink/ˈedge of sth</td><td>处在……边缘；濒临</td><td>The company teetered on the brink of collapse for most of last year.<br>去年大半年里公司都在崩盘边缘摇摇欲坠。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>teeth</b></td><td>cut your ˈteeth on sth</td><td>初试身手；从中积累经验</td><td>She cut her teeth on local radio before moving to television news.<br>她先在地方电台练手，之后才转到电视新闻。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/sink your ˈteeth into sth (informal)</td><td>全力投入；专心去做</td><td>Finally a project I can really sink my teeth into this month.<br>这个月总算有个能让我全力投入的项目了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have ˈteeth (BrE, informal)</td><td>（法规等）有约束力</td><td>The new rules only work if the regulator's powers actually have teeth.<br>只有监管机构真有牙齿，新规才管用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>set sb's ˈteeth on edge</td><td>使人牙酸；令人难受</td><td>The scrape of that chalk sets my teeth on edge every time.<br>粉笔那种刮擦声每次都让我牙根发酸。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>teething</b></td><td>have, etc. ˈteething problems/troubles</td><td>初期的困难；起步阶段的问题</td><td>The app had teething problems, but the latest update fixed most bugs.<br>这款应用起步时毛病不少，最新更新修掉了大部分。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>telephone</b></td><td>be on the ˈtelephone/ˈphone</td><td>在通话中；装有电话</td><td>She's been on the phone with the insurance company for forty minutes.<br>她跟保险公司通电话已经四十分钟了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tell</b></td><td>don't ˈtell me (spoken, informal)</td><td>别说……（我猜到了）</td><td>Don't tell me you've locked the keys inside the car again.<br>别告诉我你又把钥匙锁车里了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I tell a ˈlie (spoken)</td><td>我说错了</td><td>We met in March, no, I tell a lie, it was April.<br>我们三月认识的，不对，我说错了，是四月。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I ˈtell you •I can ˈtell you •I'm ˈtelling you</td><td>我敢说；真的（用于强调）</td><td>I'm telling you, that was the best curry in the entire city.<br>我跟你说，那是全城最好吃的咖喱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I can't ˈtell you how, etc. ... (spoken)</td><td>我说不出有多……（强调）</td><td>I can't tell you how glad I am that you came tonight.<br>你今晚能来，我真是说不出的高兴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'll ˌtell you ˈwhat •I know ˈwhat (spoken)</td><td>我有个主意；我跟你说</td><td>I'll tell you what, let's split the bill and call it even.<br>我看这样吧，账平摊，就算扯平了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell it how/like it ˈis (informal)</td><td>实话实说；直言不讳</td><td>I like her because she tells it like it is, however awkward.<br>我喜欢她，因为她再难堪的话也照直说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(go) tell it/that to the maˈrines (saying, informal)</td><td>骗鬼去吧；我才不信</td><td>You fixed it yourself? Go tell that to the marines, mate.<br>你自己修好的？骗鬼去吧，兄弟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell its ˈown tale/story</td><td>不言而喻；说明一切</td><td>The empty shelves in the shop told their own story that winter.<br>那年冬天店里空空的货架已经说明了一切。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈtell me (spoken)</td><td>你说说看；告诉我</td><td>Tell me, how did you first get into repairing old clocks?<br>你说说，你当初怎么迷上修老钟表的？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈtell me about it (spoken)</td><td>可不是嘛；我深有同感</td><td>'Mondays are exhausting.' 'Tell me about it, I've had three meetings.'<br>“周一累死人。”“可不是嘛，我已经开了三个会。”</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell me aˈnother (spoken)</td><td>别胡扯了；我才不信</td><td>You ran a marathon without training? Tell me another, please.<br>你没训练就跑完马拉松？别逗了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell ˈporkies (BrE, informal, humorous)</td><td>撒谎；瞎编</td><td>He's telling porkies about how much that watch actually cost him.<br>那块表到底花了多少钱，他在瞎编。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell the same tale/story (of sth)</td><td>反映出同样的情况</td><td>Every farm in the valley tells the same story of falling prices.<br>山谷里每个农场都反映出同样的价格下跌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell a ˈdifferent, aˈnother, etc. tale/story</td><td>反映的情况截然不同</td><td>The official figures tell a different story from what workers describe.<br>官方数字反映的情况和工人说的截然不同。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell ˈtales (about sb/sth) (BrE)</td><td>告状；打小报告</td><td>Nobody likes a kid who tells tales about classmates to the teacher.<br>谁都不喜欢向老师打同学小报告的孩子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell ˌtales out of ˈschool</td><td>泄露内情；揭家丑</td><td>I shouldn't tell tales out of school, but the accounts were fiction.<br>我本不该外传，可那些账目纯属编的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell the ˈtime (BrE) (AmE tell ˈtime)</td><td>看钟表报时间</td><td>My daughter learned to tell the time on an old analogue clock.<br>我女儿是在一台老式指针钟上学会看时间的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell sb ˌwhere to get ˈoff (BrE, informal)</td><td>严厉斥责某人；叫某人放规矩些</td><td>When he criticized her cooking, she told him where to get off.<br>他挑剔她做的菜，她把他狠狠顶了回去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell sb ˌwhere they get ˈoff (BrE, informal)</td><td>让某人有点自知之明</td><td>Someone should tell that man where he gets off ordering us around.<br>该有人让那家伙明白，他没资格对我们指手画脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell sb where to ˈput/ˈstick sth (informal)</td><td>断然拒绝某人的提议</td><td>They offered half the fee, so I told them where to stick it.<br>他们只肯给一半费用，我直接让他们免谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell sb what they can ˈdo with sth (informal)</td><td>拒不接受；让某人收起那套</td><td>He told the boss exactly what he could do with the extra overtime.<br>他直截了当地让老板收起那些加班安排。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tell the (whole) ˈworld</td><td>到处张扬；公之于众</td><td>Keep it quiet, don't tell the whole world before the contract is signed.<br>先别声张，合同签之前别到处宣扬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to tell (you) the ˈtruth</td><td>说实话；老实说</td><td>To tell you the truth, I've never really liked that restaurant.<br>老实说，我从来没真心喜欢过那家餐厅。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what did I ˈtell you? (also I ˈtold you so)</td><td>我早就说过吧</td><td>What did I tell you? The queue is enormous on Saturday mornings.<br>我早说了吧？周六上午队伍长得吓人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you ˌnever can ˈtell •you can ˌnever ˈtell</td><td>很难说；谁也说不准</td><td>He might apologize tomorrow, but you never can tell with him.<br>他明天说不定会道歉，不过跟他这种人谁说得准。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not know/not be able to tell one ˈend of sth from the other</td><td>对某物一窍不通</td><td>I can't tell one end of a car engine from the other.<br>汽车发动机我完全一窍不通。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>telling</b></td><td>you're telling ˈme! (spoken, informal)</td><td>可不是嘛；说得太对了</td><td>'That hill is steep.' 'You're telling me, I pushed my bike up.'<br>“那坡真陡。”“可不是嘛，我是推着车上去的。”</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>temper</b></td><td>keep/lose your ˈtemper (with sb)</td><td>忍住怒气；发脾气</td><td>I lost my temper with the call centre after the third transfer.<br>被第三次转接后，我对客服发了火。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>temperature</b></td><td>have/run a ˈtemperature</td><td>发烧；体温升高</td><td>She's running a temperature, so keep her home from school today.<br>她在发烧，今天别让她去上学了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>raise/lower the ˈtemperature (informal)</td><td>使气氛更紧张（或缓和）</td><td>That tweet raised the temperature of an already bitter dispute.<br>那条推文让本已激烈的争端更加火上浇油。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb's ˈtemperature</td><td>给某人量体温</td><td>The nurse took his temperature twice before letting him into the ward.<br>护士给他量了两次体温才放他进病房。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tempt</b></td><td>tempt ˈfate/ˈprovidence</td><td>冒险行事；自找麻烦</td><td>Don't tempt fate by driving that old van across the mountains.<br>别开那辆破面包车翻山，纯属冒险。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ten</b></td><td>ten out of ˈten (for sth) (BrE, often ironic)</td><td>满分；完全正确</td><td>Ten out of ten for effort, but the spelling still needs work.<br>态度满分，可拼写还得下功夫。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ten to ˈone</td><td>十有八九；很可能</td><td>Ten to one he'll be late again and blame the traffic.<br>十有八九他又要迟到，然后怪路上堵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tenterhooks</b></td><td>(be) on ˈtenterhooks (AmE also be on ˌpins and ˈneedles)</td><td>如坐针毡；焦急不安</td><td>We were on tenterhooks waiting for the exam results all morning.<br>等成绩的那一上午我们如坐针毡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>term</b></td><td>in the ˈlong/ˈmedium/ˈshort term</td><td>从长（中、短）期看</td><td>In the long term, renting here will cost more than buying.<br>从长期看，在这儿租房比买房还贵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>terms</b></td><td>be on good, bad, friendly, etc. ˈterms (with sb)</td><td>与某人关系好（或不好等）</td><td>They're still on good terms with each other despite the divorce.<br>尽管离了婚，两人关系依然不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come to ˈterms with sth</td><td>接受（不快之事）；想通</td><td>It took him years to come to terms with his father's death.<br>他花了好几年才接受父亲去世的事实。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth on sb's/your (own) ˈterms</td><td>按自己的条件行事</td><td>She returned to work on her own terms, three days a week.<br>她按自己的条件复工，一周只上三天班。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in terms of... •in ... terms</td><td>就……而言；从……方面说</td><td>In terms of cost, the train beats flying for this short trip.<br>就费用而言，这趟短途坐火车比飞机划算。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>territory</b></td><td>ˌcome/ˌgo with the ˈterritory</td><td>是难免的；在所难免</td><td>Late nights come with the territory when you work in restaurants.<br>干餐饮这行，熬夜是免不了的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>test</b></td><td>put sb/sth to the ˈtest</td><td>考验；检验</td><td>The storm put our new roof to the test on the first night.<br>头一晚的暴风雨就把新屋顶考验了一番。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stand the test of ˈtime</td><td>经得起时间的考验</td><td>Few pop songs stand the test of time as well as this one.<br>没几首流行歌能像这首一样经得起时间考验。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>test the ˈwater/ˈwaters</td><td>试探反应；摸底</td><td>We're testing the water with a small pop-up shop before committing.<br>我们先开个快闪小店探探反应，再决定投入。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tete-a-tete</b></td><td>a ˌtete-a-ˈtete (from French)</td><td>两人间的促膝密谈</td><td>They had a long tete-a-tete in the corner about the merger.<br>他们在角落里就并购的事密谈了很久。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tether</b></td><td>be at the end of your ˈtether (BrE)</td><td>忍无可忍；山穷水尽</td><td>After three sleepless nights she was at the end of her tether.<br>三个晚上没合眼，她已经到了崩溃边缘。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thank</b></td><td>have sb to thank (for sth)</td><td>某事该归功（或归咎）于某人</td><td>We have Maria to thank for getting the whole project back on schedule.<br>整个项目能重回正轨，全靠玛丽亚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I'll thank you (not) to do sth • I'll thank you for sth</td><td>（恼火地要求）请你（不要）做某事</td><td>I'll thank you not to comment on my cooking until you've tried it.<br>没尝之前，请你别对我的菜指手画脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(Some people find the phrase thank God offensive.)</td><td>有人认为 thank God 一语含冒犯意</td><td>Some people find the phrase thank God offensive, so she avoids it at work.<br>有人觉得 thank God 冒犯人，所以她在单位不说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>thank your lucky ˈstars (that...)</td><td>谢天谢地；多亏运气好</td><td>You should thank your lucky stars that nobody was hurt in that crash.<br>那场车祸没伤到人，你该谢天谢地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>he, she, etc. won't ˈthank you for sth</td><td>某人不会为此感激你；某人会因此生气</td><td>Dad won't thank you for waking him up at six on his day off.<br>休息日六点把爸叫醒，他可不会谢你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thanks</b></td><td>(be) no thanks to sb/sth</td><td>并非由于；不归功于</td><td>We finished on time, and that was no thanks to the printing company.<br>我们按时完工了，这可不是印刷厂的功劳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>thanks to sb/sth (sometimes ironic)</td><td>多亏；由于；因为</td><td>Thanks to her quick thinking, the fire was out before anyone panicked.<br>多亏她反应快，火在大家慌乱前就扑灭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>that</b></td><td>and (all) ˈthat (BrE, informal)</td><td>以及诸如此类；等等</td><td>He talked about budgets, deadlines and all that for a solid hour.<br>他讲了整整一小时预算、期限之类的东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈthat</td><td>而且；就这样；于是</td><td>She bought a second-hand bike, and a rusty one at that.<br>她买了辆二手自行车，而且还是生了锈的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>is that ˈso? (informal)</td><td>（表示不害怕或不相信）是吗；当真</td><td>'I could have you fired.' 'Is that so? Go ahead and try.'<br>「我能让你卷铺盖。」「是吗？你试试看。」</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈnot that ˈthat's a good one (informal)</td><td>真有意思；说得妙；（讥讽）说得真好</td><td>'He says he's too busy to help.' 'That's a good one — he watches TV all day.'<br>「他说忙得没空帮忙。」「说得真好，他整天看电视。」</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's (about) ˈit (informal)</td><td>就是这样；到此为止</td><td>Sign here, hand in your badge, and that's about it — you're done.<br>这里签字，交回工牌，就这样，你可以走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(and/so) that's ˈthat</td><td>（事情已定）就这么定了；就这样吧</td><td>You're not going to the party on a school night, and that's that.<br>上学日晚上不许去派对，就这么定了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>them</b></td><td>ˌthem and ˈus</td><td>他们和我们；（对立的）两派之分</td><td>The new pay rules created a real them and us feeling in the office.<br>新的薪酬规定让办公室里真有了「他们和我们」的隔阂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>then</b></td><td>and ˈthen some (spoken)</td><td>还不止这些；甚至更多</td><td>The repair cost me two thousand pounds and then some.<br>这次维修花了我两千英镑，还不止。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>theory</b></td><td>in ˈtheory</td><td>理论上；按道理说</td><td>In theory the trains run every ten minutes, but I've waited half an hour.<br>理论上火车十分钟一班，可我等了半小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>there</b></td><td>be not all/quite ˈthere (informal)</td><td>头脑不太正常；神志不清</td><td>The old man mutters at lamp posts; I don't think he's quite there.<br>那老人对着路灯自言自语，我看他脑子不太正常。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈthere for sb</td><td>随时能帮忙；随叫随到</td><td>After the divorce, my sister was there for me every single day.<br>离婚以后，我姐姐每天都陪在我身边。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so ˈthere! (informal)</td><td>（强调拒绝或满意）就是这样，没什么可说的</td><td>I'm not sharing my sweets with you, so there!<br>我不把糖分给你，就这样！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(do sth) there and ˈthen • (do sth) then and ˈthere</td><td>当场；当时当地；立即</td><td>He read the offer, liked it, and signed the contract there and then.<br>他看完报价很满意，当场就把合同签了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(do sth) then and ˈthere</td><td>当场（做某事）；立即</td><td>She heard the news and booked a flight home then and there.<br>她一听到消息，当场就订了回家的机票。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌthere you ˈare (also ˌthere you ˈgo) (spoken)</td><td>给你；拿着</td><td>There you are — one black coffee and a croissant, just as you ordered.<br>给你，一杯黑咖啡和一个牛角包，跟你点的一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there you ˈgo (aˈgain)</td><td>（批评）你又来这一套</td><td>There you go again, blaming the weather for your own laziness.<br>你又来这一套，自己懒还怪天气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there is ˈthat</td><td>（表示赞同）说得没错；确实如此</td><td>'At least the rain kept the crowds away.' 'There is that, I suppose.'<br>「起码下雨把人群挡住了。」「这倒也是。」</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(and/but/so) there it ˈis</td><td>情况就是这样；事实如此</td><td>The funding was cut and the club closed; but there it is, nothing we can do.<br>经费砍了，俱乐部关门，事情就是这样，我们无能为力。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(and/but/so) there you ˈgo • (and/but/so) there we/you ˈare</td><td>情况就是这样；事实如此</td><td>He never apologized and he never will, but there you go.<br>他从没道歉，也永远不会，事情就是这样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌthere's ˈsth for you (spoken)</td><td>（绝好的例子）这才是；这才称得上</td><td>She cycled forty miles in the rain to visit him — there's devotion for you.<br>她冒雨骑车四十英里去看他，这才叫真心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈthere's a good boy, girl, dog, etc. (informal)</td><td>（赞扬或鼓励小孩、动物）乖，好孩子</td><td>Finish your vegetables, there's a good boy, and then you can play.<br>把菜吃完，乖孩子，然后就能去玩了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>therein</b></td><td>therein ˈlies... (formal)</td><td>那就是；此即缘由</td><td>He wants fame without effort, and therein lies the whole problem.<br>他想不劳而获出名，问题就在这里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thick</b></td><td>give sb/get a thick ˈear (BrE, informal)</td><td>打耳光；挨耳光</td><td>Say that to your grandmother again and you'll get a thick ear.<br>你再对奶奶那样说话，就要挨耳光了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈthick of sth/of doing sth</td><td>在…最紧张（或最忙）的时候</td><td>Don't call him now; he's in the thick of moving house this week.<br>别现在给他打电话，他这周正忙着搬家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌthick and ˈfast</td><td>又多又快地；频频</td><td>Once the story broke, the phone calls came thick and fast all night.<br>消息一出，电话整晚接连不断地打来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) thick as ˈthieves (with sb) (informal)</td><td>过从甚密；非常亲密（常令人生疑）</td><td>Those two have been as thick as thieves since they shared an office.<br>他俩自从同一间办公室起就形影不离。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) thick as two short ˈplanks (informal) (also (as) thick as ˈshit ⚠, slang) (BrE)</td><td>极其愚蠢；笨得要死</td><td>He's as thick as two short planks, but he's honest and works hard.<br>他笨得要死，可是老实肯干。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>thick means 'stupid' in informal language</td><td>thick 在非正式场合可表示愚蠢</td><td>In British slang, thick means 'stupid', so avoid calling a colleague that.<br>英式俚语里 thick 是「笨」的意思，别这么说同事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a thick ˈhead (informal)</td><td>（因病或宿醉）头昏脑涨</td><td>I woke up with a thick head after just two glasses of red wine.<br>才喝了两杯红酒，我醒来就头昏脑涨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>through ˌthick and ˈthin</td><td>不顾艰难险阻；甘苦与共</td><td>She stood by her brother through thick and thin for thirty years.<br>三十年来她与弟弟同甘共苦，不离不弃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thief</b></td><td>like a ˌthief in the ˈnight</td><td>悄悄地；出乎意料地</td><td>Winter arrived like a thief in the night and froze all the pipes.<br>冬天来得悄无声息，把水管全冻住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thieves</b></td><td>(there is) honour among ˈthieves (saying)</td><td>盗亦有道；坏人之间也讲义气</td><td>Neither burglar named the other, proving there is honour among thieves.<br>两个窃贼谁也没供出对方，可见盗亦有道。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thin</b></td><td>appear, etc. out of thin ˈair</td><td>凭空出现；突然冒出</td><td>A taxi appeared out of thin air just as the rain got heavier.<br>雨下大的时候，一辆出租车凭空冒了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be skating/walking on ˌthin ˈice</td><td>如履薄冰；身处险境</td><td>Joking about the boss's divorce means you're skating on thin ice.<br>拿老板离婚开玩笑，你可是在冒险。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get thin on ˈtop (informal)</td><td>头发稀疏；开始谢顶</td><td>He's only thirty but already getting a bit thin on top.<br>他才三十岁，头顶就已经有点稀疏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>disappear, etc. into thin ˈair</td><td>神秘消失；无影无踪</td><td>My keys were on the table and then vanished into thin air.<br>我的钥匙本来在桌上，后来就凭空不见了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a thin ˈtime (of it) (BrE, informal)</td><td>日子不好过；生意不景气</td><td>Small bookshops have had a thin time of it since the mall opened.<br>商场开了以后，小书店的日子一直不好过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) thin as a ˈrake</td><td>骨瘦如柴</td><td>She eats like a horse but stays as thin as a rake.<br>她饭量惊人，人却还是瘦得像根竹竿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the thin ˌend of the ˈwedge (especially BrE)</td><td>（坏事的）开端；苗头</td><td>Charging for water at the gym is the thin end of the wedge.<br>健身房连水都收费，这只是个开头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thing</b></td><td>aˌmount/ˌcome to the same ˈthing</td><td>结果都一样</td><td>Whether he resigned or was pushed, it amounts to the same thing.<br>他是辞职还是被赶走，结果都一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be just the ˈthing (also be the very ˈthing less frequent)</td><td>正是所需要的东西</td><td>A hot bowl of soup is just the thing after a long walk in the cold.<br>在寒风里走了半天，一碗热汤正合适。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be no bad ˈthing (that)...</td><td>不见得是坏事；或许是好事</td><td>It's no bad thing that the meeting was cancelled; we all needed a break.<br>会议取消倒不是坏事，大家都该歇歇。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be onto a good ˈthing</td><td>境遇不错；处于有利形势</td><td>Rent-free flat and a company car — she's onto a good thing there.<br>免租的公寓加公司配车，她这日子过得可真不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>can/could teach/tell sb a ˈthing or two</td><td>能教某人不少东西；懂得比某人多</td><td>That old fisherman could teach the experts a thing or two about tides.<br>那位老渔民在潮汐上能教专家不少东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a close/near ˈthing • a close-run ˈthing (informal)</td><td>险胜；侥幸过关</td><td>We caught the last train, but it was a close thing.<br>我们赶上了末班车，不过真是好险。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do your own ˈthing (informal)</td><td>做自己喜欢的事；自行其是</td><td>After she quit the bank, she moved to Lisbon and did her own thing.<br>从银行辞职后，她搬到里斯本，过起了自己想要的生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˈone thing, ... (, and for aˈnother, ...)</td><td>一来…（二来…）；一方面…（另一方面…）</td><td>I'm not going: for one thing it's too far, and for another it's expensive.<br>我不去，一来太远，二来太贵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈthing about sb/sth (informal)</td><td>对…有强烈的好感（或恶感）</td><td>My brother has a thing about spiders and won't go in the shed.<br>我弟弟特别怕蜘蛛，死活不肯进那间棚屋。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it isn't my, his, etc. ˈthing</td><td>这不是我（或他等）喜欢的事</td><td>Thanks for the invitation, but loud clubs really aren't my thing.<br>谢谢邀请，不过吵闹的夜店真不是我的菜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's ˌone thing to do ˈA, it's (quite) aˌnother (thing) to do ˈB</td><td>做甲是一回事，做乙则是另一回事</td><td>It's one thing to promise help, it's quite another to turn up at dawn.<br>答应帮忙是一回事，天亮就到场是另一回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>A is ˈone thing, B is (quite) aˈnother</td><td>甲是一回事，乙则是另一回事</td><td>Reading about cooking is one thing, feeding twenty guests is quite another.<br>看菜谱是一回事，招待二十位客人是另一回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's a... thing (informal)</td><td>这是…才懂的事</td><td>You wouldn't understand the joke — it's a medical student thing.<br>这个笑话你不会懂，是医学生之间才明白的梗。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a (big) ˈthing of/out of sth (informal)</td><td>小题大做；大惊小怪</td><td>Please don't make a big thing of my birthday; a quiet dinner is fine.<br>别把我的生日搞得那么隆重，安静吃顿饭就好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌone (damned/damn) thing after aˈnother</td><td>坏事一桩接一桩；祸不单行</td><td>Burst pipe, dead car, lost passport — it's one thing after another.<br>水管爆了，车坏了，护照丢了，真是祸不单行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(what with) ˌone thing and aˈnother</td><td>（因为）这样那样的事；忙这忙那</td><td>What with one thing and another, I never got round to calling her back.<br>忙这忙那的，我一直没顾上给她回电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌone thing leads to aˈnother (informal)</td><td>顺理成章；自然而然</td><td>We met at a wedding, one thing led to another, and now we're married.<br>我们在婚礼上认识，顺理成章，现在我们结婚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no such ˌthing as a free ˈlunch</td><td>天下没有免费的午餐</td><td>That free trial wants your card details — there's no such thing as a free lunch.<br>免费试用要你的银行卡号，天下没有免费的午餐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's only ˌone thing ˈfor it</td><td>只有一个办法；别无选择</td><td>The road is flooded, so there's only one thing for it — we walk.<br>路淹了，只有一个办法，我们走过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the (whole)... ˈthing (informal)</td><td>这种事；这一类活动</td><td>He's really into the whole camping thing now, tent and all.<br>他现在特别迷露营那一套，帐篷什么都齐了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the (only) thing ˈis... (spoken)</td><td>问题是；麻烦的是；只是</td><td>I'd love to come; the only thing is, I'm working till nine.<br>我很想来，只是我要工作到九点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌthing (about/with sth) ˈis (spoken)</td><td>事实是；主要原因是；问题是</td><td>The thing about this job is that nobody ever tells you the rules.<br>这份工作的问题在于，从来没人告诉你规矩。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a thing of the ˈpast</td><td>过时的东西；成为往事</td><td>Handwritten letters have become a thing of the past in our office.<br>在我们办公室，手写信早就成了老黄历。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not quite the ˈthing</td><td>不太得体；不合规矩</td><td>Wearing trainers to the funeral was not quite the thing, everyone noticed.<br>穿运动鞋去葬礼不太得体，大家都注意到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>things</b></td><td>all things conˈsidered</td><td>从总体来看；考虑到各种因素</td><td>All things considered, the trip went pretty well despite the rain.<br>总的来说，虽然下雨，这趟旅行还算顺利。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>and ˈthings (like ˈthat) (spoken, informal)</td><td>等等；诸如此类</td><td>She sells candles, soap and things like that at the weekend market.<br>她在周末集市上卖蜡烛、香皂之类的东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as things ˈstand</td><td>照目前的情况；就眼下的形势看</td><td>As things stand, we can't afford to hire anyone before spring.<br>照目前的情况，开春之前我们雇不起人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be all ˌthings to all ˈmen/people (saying)</td><td>八面玲珑；见风使舵</td><td>A good politician tries to be all things to all people and pleases nobody.<br>好政客想八面玲珑，结果谁也讨好不了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈdo things to sb (informal)</td><td>深深打动某人；让某人心动</td><td>That old jazz record really does things to me every time I hear it.<br>那张老爵士唱片我每次听都心头一颤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈall things (formal)</td><td>在任何情况下；总是</td><td>In all things he showed the same patience, even when the plan collapsed.<br>无论何事他都同样有耐心，连计划崩了也一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) ˌone of those ˈthings</td><td>难免的倒霉事；在所难免的事</td><td>Missing the ferry by two minutes was just one of those things.<br>差两分钟没赶上渡轮，这种倒霉事难免。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>other/all things being ˈequal</td><td>如果其他条件相同</td><td>All things being equal, I'd rather take the earlier train home.<br>其他条件相同的话，我宁愿坐早一班火车回家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put things ˈright</td><td>纠正错误；改善局面</td><td>He apologized and offered to pay, hoping to put things right.<br>他道了歉还提出赔钱，想把事情弥补过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈsee/ˈhear things (informal)</td><td>出现幻觉；幻视；幻听</td><td>I must be hearing things — did that cat just say my name?<br>我肯定是幻听了，那只猫刚叫我名字？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>these things are sent to ˈtry us (saying)</td><td>这是上天对我们的考验</td><td>The boiler broke on Christmas Day, but these things are sent to try us.<br>锅炉圣诞节坏了，只能说是上天考验我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌthese things ˈhappen</td><td>这种事总会发生；谁都会碰上</td><td>Don't cry over the broken vase — these things happen to everyone.<br>花瓶碎了别哭，这种事谁都会碰上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>things that go ˌbump in the ˈnight (informal, humorous)</td><td>夜里的怪响；无法解释的怪事</td><td>My little sister still won't sleep alone, afraid of things that go bump in the night.<br>我妹妹还是不敢独睡，怕夜里的怪响。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make the best of sth/things/a bad job</td><td>尽量把坏事往好里做；随遇而安</td><td>The tent leaked, but we made the best of things and lit a fire.<br>帐篷漏雨，我们只好将就着生了堆火。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>think</b></td><td>anyone would ˈthink (that)...</td><td>（评价怪异行为）别人还以为…呢</td><td>Anyone would think you'd won the lottery, the way you're smiling.<br>看你笑成那样，别人还以为你中彩票了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you would have ˈthought (that)...</td><td>（评价怪异行为）按说应该…；别人会以为…</td><td>You would have thought he'd call after borrowing my car for a week.<br>借了我一周的车，按说他总该打个电话吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come to ˈthink of it (also ˈthinking about it)</td><td>（突然想起）对了；想起来了</td><td>Come to think of it, I did see her at the station yesterday morning.<br>对了，我昨天上午确实在车站见过她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb something to think about (informal)</td><td>让某人好好想想；促使某人反省</td><td>Losing the first round gave the champion something to think about.<br>首轮失利让这位冠军好好反省了一番。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have (got) another thing ˈcoming (informal)</td><td>想错了；需要重新考虑</td><td>If he thinks I'll work every weekend, he's got another thing coming.<br>他要以为我会每个周末加班，那可想错了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if/when you ˈthink about it</td><td>仔细想想；细想之下</td><td>When you think about it, we've never actually met her parents.<br>仔细想想，我们其实从没见过她父母。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I should think ˈso/ˈnot (also I should think she, etc. ˈis/ˈdoes/ˈdid, etc.)</td><td>（强调赞同）我看也是；当然如此</td><td>'He apologized to the waiter.' 'I should think so too.'<br>「他向服务员道歉了。」「那是应该的。」</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I shudder/dread to ˈthink (how, what, etc....)</td><td>我都不敢想…</td><td>I dread to think what this kitchen renovation is going to cost us.<br>我都不敢想这次厨房翻修要花多少钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>just ˈthink</td><td>（表示兴奋或震惊）想想看；只要想想</td><td>Just think — this time next week we'll be swimming in the sea.<br>想想看，下周这时候我们就在海里游泳了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not ˈthink of sth/of doing sth</td><td>决不考虑；根本不会想到</td><td>She wouldn't think of leaving the dog alone for a whole weekend.<br>她根本不会考虑把狗独自留一整个周末。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(used with wouldn't, couldn't, won't or can't)</td><td>（与否定式连用）从没想过；肯定不会</td><td>Used with wouldn't or can't, the phrase means you would never consider it.<br>与 wouldn't 或 can't 连用时，这个说法表示你绝不会考虑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think aˈgain</td><td>再想想；重新考虑；三思</td><td>If you believe a diet alone will fix this, you should think again.<br>你要是觉得光靠节食就能解决，还是再想想吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌthink aˈloud • ˌthink out ˈloud</td><td>自言自语；把想法说出来</td><td>Sorry, ignore me — I'm just thinking aloud about next year's budget.<br>抱歉别理我，我只是在把明年预算的想法念叨出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think (the) ˈbetter of sb</td><td>对某人评价更高</td><td>I thought the better of him after he admitted the mistake publicly.<br>他当众承认错误后，我对他评价更高了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think ˈbetter of it/of doing sth</td><td>改变主意；决定不做</td><td>She raised her hand to argue, then thought better of it and sat down.<br>她举手想争辩，转念一想又坐了回去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think ˈbig (informal)</td><td>雄心勃勃；想大干一番</td><td>Stop planning a stall and think big — open a proper restaurant.<br>别老想着摆摊，眼光放大点，开家像样的餐馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think ˈhighly of sb/sth</td><td>对…评价很高；非常欣赏</td><td>Our clients think very highly of her, especially her attention to detail.<br>客户对她评价很高，尤其欣赏她注重细节。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think ˈnothing of sth/of doing sth</td><td>觉得不算什么；习以为常</td><td>My grandfather thinks nothing of walking ten miles before breakfast.<br>我爷爷早饭前走上十英里，根本不当回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not think ˈanything of sth/of doing sth</td><td>觉得不算什么；认为很平常</td><td>She doesn't think anything of driving five hours to see a concert.<br>开五小时车去看演唱会，她觉得不算什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think nothing ˈof it (spoken, formal)</td><td>别客气；不必放在心上</td><td>'Thanks for carrying my bags.' 'Think nothing of it, really.'<br>「谢谢你帮我拎包。」「别客气，真的。」</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think on your ˈfeet</td><td>思维敏捷；随机应变</td><td>When the projector died, she had to think on her feet and keep talking.<br>投影仪坏了，她只能随机应变继续讲下去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think out of the ˈbox (also think outside the ˈbox)</td><td>跳出常规思考；换个角度看问题</td><td>We need someone who can think outside the box, not follow old rules.<br>我们需要能跳出框框思考的人，而不是守旧的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think you ˈown the place (also behave/act as if you ˈown the place) (disapproving)</td><td>自以为是；颐指气使</td><td>The new intern walks around like he thinks he owns the place.<br>那个新来的实习生走起路来一副老板派头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>behave/act as if you ˈown the place (disapproving)</td><td>指手画脚；颐指气使</td><td>He acts as if he owns the place, rearranging everyone's desks without asking.<br>他一副主人做派，不打招呼就把大家的桌子挪来挪去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think ˈpositive</td><td>抱积极态度；往好处想</td><td>Think positive — the interview went badly, but there are other jobs.<br>往好处想，这次面试搞砸了，还有别的机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈthink straight</td><td>头脑清醒；思路清晰</td><td>I'd had four hours' sleep and simply couldn't think straight at the meeting.<br>我只睡了四小时，开会时脑子完全转不动。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think the sun shines out of sb's ˈarse ⚠ (BrE)</td><td>把某人捧上天；对某人极其崇拜</td><td>Her parents think the sun shines out of her arse, whatever she does.<br>不管她做什么，她父母都把她捧上天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think the sun shines out of sb's ˈbackside (BrE) (AmE think the sun shines out of sb's ˈass ⚠) (slang)</td><td>极为看重某人；对某人事事满意</td><td>The coach thinks the sun shines out of that striker's backside.<br>教练觉得那个前锋做什么都对。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) think ˈtwice about sth/about doing sth</td><td>（没有）三思；（毫不）犹豫</td><td>She didn't think twice about lending him the money she'd saved.<br>她二话不说就把攒的钱借给了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>think the ˈworld of sb/sth</td><td>非常喜爱；极为敬重</td><td>The children think the world of their swimming teacher.<br>孩子们特别喜欢他们的游泳老师。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈthink (that)...</td><td>（表示惊讶）真没想到；竟然</td><td>To think that this quiet street was once full of noisy factories!<br>真没想到这条安静的街当年满是喧闹的工厂！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>who does sb think they ˈare? (disapproving, informal)</td><td>…以为自己是谁</td><td>Who does he think he is, telling me how to raise my own children?<br>他以为自己是谁，教我怎么带孩子？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thinking</b></td><td>put your ˈthinking cap on (informal)</td><td>动脑筋；好好想想</td><td>Put your thinking cap on — we need a name for the new café by Friday.<br>动动脑筋，周五之前得给新咖啡馆起个名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>third</b></td><td>(give sb) the ˌthird deˈgree (informal)</td><td>逼供；盘问；严加审问</td><td>My mum gave me the third degree about where I'd been all night.<br>我妈追问了我一整晚上哪儿去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>third time ˈlucky (AmE also third time is the ˈcharm)</td><td>第三次就走运了；事不过三</td><td>He failed his driving test twice, but third time lucky — he passed.<br>他驾照考砸了两次，第三次总算过了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>this</b></td><td>ˌthis and ˈthat (also ˌthis, that and the ˈother)</td><td>这样那样的事；各种各样的东西</td><td>We sat in the kitchen chatting about this and that until midnight.<br>我们坐在厨房东拉西扯聊到半夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>this is ˈit (informal)</td><td>（赞同）的确如此；就是这样</td><td>'Nobody reads the manual anyway.' 'This is it — they just click around.'<br>「反正没人看说明书。」「就是这样，大家乱点一通。」</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thorn</b></td><td>be a thorn in your ˈflesh/ˈside</td><td>眼中钉；不断让人烦心的人（或事）</td><td>That noisy pub has been a thorn in our side for the past three years.<br>那家吵闹的酒吧三年来一直是我们的心头刺。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thought</b></td><td>I ˈthought as much</td><td>果然不出我所料</td><td>'He forgot the tickets.' 'I thought as much when he ran back inside.'<br>「他忘了带票。」「他跑回屋时我就料到了。」</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's the ˈthought that counts (saying)</td><td>重要的是心意；情义胜过礼物</td><td>The cake was burnt, but it's the thought that counts.<br>蛋糕烤糊了，不过心意最重要。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thrall</b></td><td>in (sb's/sth's) ˈthrall • in ˈthrall to sb/sth</td><td>受…控制；深受…影响</td><td>The whole village was in thrall to one wealthy landowner for decades.<br>几十年来整个村子都受一个大地主的控制。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thread</b></td><td>thread your way through (sth)</td><td>在…之间穿行</td><td>She threaded her way through the crowd to reach the front of the stage.<br>她在人群中穿行，挤到了舞台前面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>three</b></td><td>(yes sir, no sir) three bags ˈfull (sir) (old-fashioned, humorous)</td><td>唯唯诺诺；一味顺从（含讽刺）</td><td>It's all yes sir, no sir, three bags full sir with him around the manager.<br>他在经理面前就是一味点头哈腰。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(give) three ˈcheers (for sb/sth)</td><td>（为…）欢呼三声；喝彩</td><td>Let's give three cheers for the cooks who fed two hundred people today.<br>让我们为今天做了两百人饭的厨师们欢呼三声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the three ˈR's (old-fashioned)</td><td>读、写、算三门基础课</td><td>The old headmaster insisted the three R's mattered more than anything else.<br>老校长坚持认为读写算三门基础课最重要。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be) three sheets to the ˈwind (old-fashioned)</td><td>醉得东倒西歪</td><td>By ten o'clock the groom was already three sheets to the wind.<br>才十点钟，新郎就已经醉得东倒西歪了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>threshold</b></td><td>be on the ˈthreshold of sth (formal)</td><td>处于…的开端；即将开始</td><td>At eighteen she stood on the threshold of a completely new life.<br>十八岁的她正站在全新生活的门槛上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thrills</b></td><td>(the) thrills and ˈspills (of sth) (informal)</td><td>紧张与刺激；大起大落</td><td>He misses the thrills and spills of racing motorbikes every weekend.<br>他怀念每个周末赛摩托车的那种刺激。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>throat</b></td><td>cut your own ˈthroat</td><td>自取灭亡；搬起石头砸自己的脚</td><td>By insulting his only client, he was cutting his own throat.<br>他辱骂唯一的客户，这是自断财路。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ram, force, thrust, etc. sth down sb's ˈthroat (informal)</td><td>强行灌输；把…强加于人</td><td>Stop ramming your diet advice down my throat every single mealtime.<br>别每顿饭都把你的节食理论硬塞给我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>throats</b></td><td>(be) at each other's ˈthroats</td><td>激烈争吵；打得不可开交</td><td>The two brothers were at each other's throats over their father's house.<br>兄弟俩为父亲的房子吵得不可开交。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be) at one aˈnother's ˈthroats</td><td>激烈争吵（或打斗）；互不相让</td><td>Within an hour of the meeting, the two departments were at one another's throats.<br>会议开了不到一小时，两个部门就吵翻了天。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>throes</b></td><td>in the ˈthroes of sth/doing sth</td><td>正忙于（困难之事）；正处于…的困难期</td><td>We're in the throes of moving house, so the place is chaos.<br>我们正忙着搬家，家里乱成一团。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>through</b></td><td>ˌthrough and ˈthrough</td><td>彻底；完完全全</td><td>After two hours in that storm I was soaked through and through.<br>在那场暴雨里待了两小时，我浑身湿透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>throw</b></td><td>$100, £50, etc. a ˈthrow (informal)</td><td>每个（或每次）的价格为…</td><td>The concert tickets were eighty pounds a throw, so we stayed home.<br>演唱会门票每张八十镑，我们就待家里了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thrust</b></td><td>the cut and ˈthrust (of sth) (BrE)</td><td>激烈的论战；白热化的竞争</td><td>She loved the cut and thrust of courtroom debate far more than paperwork.<br>比起文书工作，她更爱法庭辩论的针锋相对。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thumb</b></td><td>thumb your ˈnose at sb/sth</td><td>对…嗤之以鼻；公然蔑视</td><td>The company thumbed its nose at the regulators and kept polluting.<br>这家公司无视监管部门，继续排污。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under sb's ˈthumb (informal)</td><td>完全受某人摆布</td><td>He's been under his older sister's thumb since they were children.<br>他从小就完全听姐姐的摆布。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thumbs</b></td><td>be all ˈthumbs (also be all ˌfingers and ˈthumbs)</td><td>笨手笨脚；毛手毛脚</td><td>I'm all thumbs today — that's the second glass I've dropped.<br>我今天笨手笨脚的，这已经是摔的第二个杯子了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold ˈthumbs (South African)</td><td>祈求成功；盼事情顺利</td><td>Hold thumbs for me — I hear about the scholarship tomorrow morning.<br>帮我祈祷吧，明天上午奖学金结果就出来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(give sb/sth/get) the thumbs ˈup/ˈdown</td><td>表示赞成（或反对）；获批准（或否决）</td><td>The council finally gave our playground plan the thumbs up.<br>市政会终于批准了我们的游乐场方案。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tick</b></td><td>get, buy, etc. sth on ˈtick (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>赊账；赊购</td><td>In those days you could buy groceries on tick and pay at month's end.<br>那年头买菜可以赊账，月底再结。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tick sth off on your ˈfingers</td><td>掰着手指头数</td><td>He ticked off on his fingers all the towns he'd cycled through.<br>他掰着手指数出骑车经过的每一座小镇。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what makes sb ˈtick (informal)</td><td>某人的行为动机；某人心里想什么</td><td>After ten years I still don't know what makes my neighbour tick.<br>认识十年了，我还是摸不透邻居到底怎么想。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ticket</b></td><td>ˈthat's the ticket (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>这正是所需要的；这才对</td><td>A hot bath and an early night — that's the ticket after a day like this.<br>洗个热水澡早点睡，这样一天下来正需要这个。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tickets</b></td><td>be ˈtickets (South African, informal)</td><td>完蛋了；到头了</td><td>If the rain doesn't stop by noon, it's tickets for the outdoor wedding.<br>中午前雨要不停，这场户外婚礼就完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tickled</b></td><td>be tickled ˈpink (also be tickled to ˈdeath)</td><td>非常高兴；乐不可支</td><td>Gran was tickled pink when the whole family turned up unannounced.<br>全家人突然登门，奶奶乐得合不拢嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tide</b></td><td>the tide ˈturns</td><td>形势发生变化（尤指好转）</td><td>The tide turned in the second half and our team scored three goals.<br>下半场形势逆转，我们队连进三球。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tie</b></td><td>tie sb's ˈhands</td><td>束缚某人的手脚；使某人无法自主</td><td>The new regulations tie our hands when it comes to hiring students.<br>新规定让我们在招学生这件事上束手束脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tie sb/yourself (up) in ˈknots</td><td>（使）晕头转向；（把自己）绕糊涂</td><td>The lawyer tied the witness in knots within five minutes.<br>律师五分钟内就把证人问得晕头转向。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tie the ˈknot (informal)</td><td>结婚；喜结连理</td><td>They finally tied the knot last June after twelve years together.<br>在一起十二年后，他们去年六月终于结婚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tie one ˈon (old-fashioned, AmE, slang)</td><td>喝得烂醉</td><td>He tied one on after the exams and slept until three the next day.<br>考完试他喝得烂醉，第二天睡到下午三点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tight</b></td><td>in a tight ˈcorner/ˈspot (informal)</td><td>身处困境；遇到大麻烦</td><td>Lending him the deposit put us in a tight spot that whole winter.<br>把押金借给他，害我们整个冬天都很拮据。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep a tight ˈrein on sb/sth (also keep sb/sth on a tight ˈleash)</td><td>对…严加约束；牢牢管住</td><td>The new manager keeps a tight rein on travel expenses.<br>新经理把差旅费管得很严。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>run a ˌtight ˈship</td><td>管理有方；治理严明</td><td>She runs a tight ship; nothing in that kitchen is ever out of place.<br>她管理有方，那间厨房里从没有东西乱放。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌtight ˈsqueeze</td><td>极其拥挤；勉强挤得下</td><td>Six of us in that little car was a tight squeeze, but we managed.<br>六个人挤那辆小车里真够呛，不过还是挤下了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tighten</b></td><td>tighten your ˈbelt</td><td>勒紧裤腰带；省吃俭用</td><td>With the rent going up again, we'll have to tighten our belts.<br>房租又涨了，我们只能勒紧裤腰带过日子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tightrope</b></td><td>tread/walk a ˈtightrope</td><td>走钢丝；如履薄冰地行事</td><td>He walks a tightrope between pleasing his boss and protecting his team.<br>他在讨好老板和保护团队之间走钢丝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be on a ˈtightrope</td><td>处境微妙；如走钢丝般艰难</td><td>The negotiator was on a tightrope with both sides threatening to leave.<br>两边都威胁要退出，谈判代表如走钢丝。</td></tr>
