<tr><td><b>till</b></td><td>have your ˌfingers/ˌhand in the ˈtill (BrE, informal)</td><td>监守自盗；偷单位的钱</td><td>The accountant had his hand in the till for almost four years.<br>那位会计监守自盗了将近四年。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tilt</b></td><td>tilt at ˈwindmills</td><td>跟假想敌搏斗；徒费精力</td><td>Complaining to that office is tilting at windmills; nobody ever replies.<br>向那个办公室投诉是白费劲，从来没人回。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>This expression comes from Cervantes' novel Don Quixote.</td><td>此语出自塞万提斯的小说《堂吉诃德》</td><td>This expression comes from Cervantes' novel, in which the hero fights windmills.<br>这个说法出自塞万提斯的小说，书中主人公与风车搏斗。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>time</b></td><td>(and) about ˈtime (ˈtoo)</td><td>早该如此；也该是时候了</td><td>They're finally fixing the road, and about time too.<br>他们总算要修那条路了，也该是时候了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(and) not before ˈtime (spoken)</td><td>早该如此；总算等到了</td><td>The heating came back on at last, and not before time.<br>暖气总算又来了，早就该修好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>against ˈtime (also against the ˈclock)</td><td>抢时间；争分夺秒</td><td>The rescue team worked against time to reach the trapped miners.<br>救援队争分夺秒地赶去营救被困矿工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ahead of/behind ˈtime</td><td>提前；迟于预定时间</td><td>The builders finished the extension two weeks ahead of time.<br>施工队提前两周完成了加建工程。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>all the ˈtime • the whole ˈtime</td><td>（某段时间内）一直；始终</td><td>I was looking for my glasses, and they were on my head the whole time.<br>我到处找眼镜，其实一直在我头上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈany time (spoken)</td><td>（回应致谢）不客气；随时乐意效劳</td><td>'Thanks for the lift home.' 'Any time, just give me a call.'<br>「谢谢你送我回家。」「随时效劳，打电话就行。」</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at a ˈtime</td><td>每次；一次…地</td><td>He climbed the stairs two at a time to catch her before she left.<br>他两级一步跑上楼，想在她走前拦住她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at the ˈtime</td><td>当时；那时候</td><td>It seemed like a good idea at the time, but now I regret it.<br>当时看着是个好主意，现在我后悔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈmy, ˈyour, etc. time of life</td><td>在我（或你等）这个年纪</td><td>At my time of life I'm not going to start learning to ski.<br>我这个岁数了，不会去学滑雪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ahead of/before/in advance of your ˈtime</td><td>超越时代；思想（或做法）超前</td><td>Her ideas about school design were well ahead of their time.<br>她关于校舍设计的想法远远超越了那个时代。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be before sb's ˈtime</td><td>在某人记事之前；早于某人的年代</td><td>The old cinema closed in 1975, so it was before my time.<br>那家老电影院一九七五年就关了，我那时还没出生。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be (stuck) in a ˈtime warp</td><td>停留在过去；仿佛困在旧时光里</td><td>That barber's shop is stuck in a time warp, right down to the posters.<br>那家理发店活像停在了过去，连海报都没换。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do/serve ˈtime (informal)</td><td>服刑；坐牢</td><td>He did time for fraud and now warns students about easy money.<br>他因诈骗坐过牢，如今告诫学生别想着走捷径。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈevery time</td><td>总是（选择）；只要可以就</td><td>Homemade bread over supermarket bread, every time.<br>自家烤的面包比超市的强，我永远选前者。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for the time ˈbeing (also for the ˈmoment/ˈpresent)</td><td>暂时；眼下</td><td>For the time being we're staying with my parents until the flat's ready.<br>房子弄好之前，我们暂时住在我父母家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from/since ˌtime immeˈmorial</td><td>自古以来；从很早以前</td><td>Fishermen have used this harbour since time immemorial.<br>自古以来渔民就使用这个港口。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from ˌtime to ˈtime</td><td>不时；偶尔</td><td>From time to time she still sends me a postcard from Athens.<br>她偶尔还会从雅典给我寄张明信片。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb a rough, hard, bad, etc. ˈtime (of it)</td><td>故意为难某人；让某人不好过</td><td>The other kids gave him a hard time about his accent all term.<br>整个学期其他孩子都拿他的口音取笑他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a lot of ˈtime for sb/sth (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>很喜欢；很欣赏</td><td>I have a lot of time for our postman; he checks on the elderly.<br>我很欣赏我们的邮递员，他会去看看独居老人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have no ˈtime for sb/sth</td><td>讨厌；瞧不上</td><td>She has no time for people who complain but never vote.<br>她瞧不上那些只会抱怨却从不投票的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have much ˈtime for sb/sth (informal)</td><td>不喜欢；不怎么看得上</td><td>He doesn't have much time for meetings that could have been emails.<br>他很不喜欢那些本可以发邮件解决的会议。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a (hard, rough, bad, etc.) ˈtime of it</td><td>日子不好过；困难重重</td><td>They've had a rough time of it since the factory closed last spring.<br>自从去年春天工厂关门，他们的日子一直很难过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have the ˌtime of your ˈlife (informal)</td><td>玩得非常痛快；快活极了</td><td>The kids had the time of their lives at the seaside last weekend.<br>上周末孩子们在海边玩得别提多开心了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have ˈtime on your hands (informal)</td><td>闲着没事；空闲时间太多</td><td>Since retiring he's had time on his hands and started painting.<br>退休后他闲得慌，就开始画画了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(all) in good ˈtime (spoken)</td><td>到时候自然会；不用着急</td><td>You'll hear the results all in good time, so stop refreshing your inbox.<br>结果到时候自然会通知，别老刷邮箱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in good ˈtime</td><td>提前；及早</td><td>We arrived at the airport in good time and had breakfast there.<br>我们提前到了机场，还在那儿吃了早饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in (less than/next to) ˈno time</td><td>立刻；转眼之间</td><td>She fixed the bike in no time and we were back on the road.<br>她三两下就把自行车修好，我们又上路了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in your own good ˈtime (informal)</td><td>等自己方便时；等自己准备好再说</td><td>He'll tell us what happened in his own good time; don't push him.<br>他想说的时候自然会说，别逼他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in your own ˈtime</td><td>在业余时间；用自己的时间</td><td>She learnt Spanish in her own time, mostly on the train to work.<br>她利用业余时间学西班牙语，大多是在上班的火车上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈtime</td><td>及时；来得及</td><td>We got to the hospital in time to see him before the operation.<br>我们及时赶到医院，在他手术前见了一面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's ˌhigh/aˌbout ˈtime (that)... (spoken)</td><td>早就该…了；也该…了</td><td>It's high time you learned to cook something other than noodles.<br>你早就该学着做点面条以外的东西了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's only, just, etc. a matter/a question of ˈtime (before...)</td><td>只是时间问题；迟早的事</td><td>It's only a matter of time before that old bridge has to close.<br>那座老桥关闭只是时间问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's only a matter/a question of ˈtime (before...)</td><td>迟早的事；只是时间问题</td><td>With those cracks, it's just a question of time before the wall falls.<br>裂成那样，墙塌下来是迟早的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep ˈtime</td><td>（钟表）走得准</td><td>That old kitchen clock still keeps perfect time after forty years.<br>厨房那只老钟用了四十年，走得还是很准。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose/waste no ˈtime (in doing sth)</td><td>毫不拖延；立即行动</td><td>She lost no time in reporting the leak to the landlord.<br>她一刻没耽误，马上向房东报告了漏水的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make good, etc. ˈtime</td><td>行程顺利；走得比预期快</td><td>We made good time on the motorway and arrived before lunch.<br>高速上走得挺顺，午饭前就到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈtime (to do sth)</td><td>抽出时间（做某事）</td><td>However busy he is, he makes time to read to his daughter.<br>不管多忙，他都抽时间给女儿读书。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈmany a time • ˈmany's the time (that)...</td><td>经常；许多次</td><td>Many a time I've walked home from that station in the rain.<br>我不知多少次冒雨从那个车站走回家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>but then we wouldn't see the children growing up</td><td>可那样就看不到孩子长大了</td><td>We could move to Australia, but then we wouldn't see the children growing up.<br>我们可以搬去澳大利亚，可那样就看不到孩子长大了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(the) next, first, second, etc. time aˈround/aˈround</td><td>下一次（或第一次等）同样的事发生时</td><td>The first time around we panicked; the second time around we knew better.<br>第一次我们慌了神，第二次就有数了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not give sb the ˌtime of ˈday</td><td>不理睬某人；不肯搭理</td><td>Ever since the argument, she won't give me the time of day.<br>自从那次争吵，她再也不肯搭理我。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(there's) no time like the ˈpresent (saying)</td><td>现在就是最好的时机；说做就做</td><td>You want to call her? There's no time like the present.<br>你想给她打电话？现在就打，别等了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>of all ˈtime</td><td>有史以来</td><td>Many fans still call him the greatest goalkeeper of all time.<br>很多球迷仍称他为有史以来最伟大的门将。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(right) on ˈtime (also bang on ˈtime) (informal)</td><td>准时；按时</td><td>For once the six-fifteen train arrived bang on time.<br>六点一刻那班火车难得地准点到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>play for ˈtime</td><td>拖延时间；争取时间</td><td>He kept asking pointless questions, clearly playing for time.<br>他不停问些没用的问题，明摆着是在拖时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take your ˈtime (doing sth/to do sth/over sth)</td><td>慢慢来；不着急</td><td>Take your time over the exam; you've still got forty minutes left.<br>考试慢慢做，你还有四十分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no time to ˈlose</td><td>刻不容缓；一刻也不能耽搁</td><td>The tide is coming in fast, so there's no time to lose.<br>潮水涨得快，一刻也不能耽搁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's no time to be ˈlost (saying)</td><td>必须立刻行动；没时间可耽搁</td><td>The storm is two hours away, so there's no time to be lost.<br>风暴两小时后就到，没时间可耽搁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtime after ˈtime • ˌtime and (time) aˈgain</td><td>一次又一次；屡次</td><td>Time and again I've told him to lock the back gate at night.<br>我一遍又一遍告诉他晚上要锁后门。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>time ˈflies (saying)</td><td>时间过得真快；光阴似箭</td><td>Time flies — our little nephew starts secondary school this autumn.<br>时间过得真快，小侄子今年秋天就上中学了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>time hangs/lies ˈheavy (on your ˈhands)</td><td>时间难熬；闲得无聊</td><td>Time hangs heavy on his hands now that the workshop has closed.<br>作坊关了以后，他闲得日子都不好打发。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>time is getting ˈon</td><td>时间不早了；没多少时间了</td><td>Time's getting on — we should leave if we want that last bus.<br>时间不早了，想赶末班车我们该走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>time is ˈmoney (saying)</td><td>时间就是金钱</td><td>Hurry up and load the van; time is money in this business.<br>快点装车，干这行时间就是金钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>time is on sb's ˈside (also have time on your side)</td><td>有的是时间；时间对某人有利</td><td>She's only twenty-two, so time is on her side.<br>她才二十二岁，有的是时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the time is ˈripe (for sb) (to do sth)</td><td>时机已经成熟</td><td>The time is ripe for us to open a second shop in the old town.<br>在老城区开第二家店，时机已经成熟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the time is ˈripe for sth/for doing sth (literary)</td><td>时机成熟；正是做某事的时候</td><td>With prices falling, the time is ripe for buying a small flat.<br>房价在跌，正是买小户型的好时机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>time ˈwas (when)... (old-fashioned)</td><td>曾经有那么个时候；那年头</td><td>Time was when you could leave your front door unlocked all night.<br>那年头你家大门整夜不锁都没事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>time (alone) will ˈtell • only time will ˈtell</td><td>时间会证明一切</td><td>Whether this new manager is any good, only time will tell.<br>这位新经理行不行，只有时间能证明。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>times</b></td><td>at all ˈtimes</td><td>总是；随时</td><td>Visitors must wear their badges at all times inside the laboratory.<br>在实验室内，访客必须随时佩戴证件。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈtimes</td><td>有时；间或</td><td>At times he can be difficult, but he's a loyal friend.<br>他有时挺难相处，但是个讲义气的朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be behind the ˈtimes</td><td>落后于时代；过时</td><td>Their booking system is paper-based; they're really behind the times.<br>他们的预订还用纸质记录，实在太落伍了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep up, move, etc. with the ˈtimes</td><td>与时俱进；跟上时代</td><td>The old library moved with the times and now lends e-books too.<br>那家老图书馆与时俱进，现在也出借电子书。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tin</b></td><td>have a tin ˈear (for sth) (informal)</td><td>没有乐感；分不清音高</td><td>I love singing, but I've got a tin ear and everybody knows it.<br>我爱唱歌，可惜五音不全，大家都知道。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tip</b></td><td>be on the tip of your ˈtongue</td><td>话到嘴边（却想不起来）</td><td>Her name was on the tip of my tongue the whole evening.<br>她的名字整晚都在我嘴边，就是想不起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be the tip of the ˈiceberg</td><td>只是冰山一角；只是问题的一小部分</td><td>Those two complaints are just the tip of the iceberg, believe me.<br>信我的，那两起投诉不过是冰山一角。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tip the ˈbalance/ˈscales (also swing the ˈbalance/ˈscales)</td><td>使天平倾斜；起决定性作用</td><td>Her experience abroad tipped the balance in favour of hiring her.<br>她的海外经历成了录用她的决定因素。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tip the scales at sth</td><td>体重（或重量）为…</td><td>The prize pumpkin tipped the scales at nearly ninety kilos.<br>那个获奖南瓜足足有近九十公斤重。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tip sb the ˈwink • tip the ˈwink to sb (BrE, informal)</td><td>向某人暗中通风报信</td><td>A friend at the agency tipped me the wink about the job opening.<br>中介的朋友偷偷给我透了那个职位的信儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tipping</b></td><td>it's ˈtipping (it) down (BrE, informal)</td><td>下着倾盆大雨</td><td>Don't go out now, it's absolutely tipping it down out there.<br>现在别出门，外面正下着瓢泼大雨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˈtipping point</td><td>引爆点；临界点</td><td>That rent rise was the tipping point that made us leave the city.<br>那次涨房租成了我们离开这座城市的临界点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tiptoe</b></td><td>on ˈtiptoe/ˈtiptoes</td><td>踮着脚尖</td><td>She crossed the room on tiptoe so as not to wake the baby.<br>她踮着脚穿过房间，怕吵醒宝宝。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tire</b></td><td>never tire of doing sth</td><td>不厌其烦地做某事</td><td>He never tires of telling that story about the fish he caught.<br>他百说不厌那条鱼的故事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tired</b></td><td>be/get tired of sth/doing sth</td><td>对…感到厌倦；受够了</td><td>I'm getting tired of hearing the same excuse every Monday morning.<br>每周一早上听同样的借口，我烦透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tissue</b></td><td>a ˌtissue of ˈlies (literary)</td><td>一派谎言；一整套谎话</td><td>His account of that night turned out to be a tissue of lies.<br>他对那晚的说法后来证明全是谎话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tit</b></td><td>ˌtit for ˈtat</td><td>以牙还牙；针锋相对</td><td>They blocked our driveway, so we parked in theirs — pure tit for tat.<br>他们堵我们车道，我们就停他们那儿，纯属以牙还牙。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get</b></td><td>be/get in/into a ˈtizzy/ˈtizz (about sth) (informal)</td><td>（为小事）慌成一团；紧张不安</td><td>Mum got into a tizzy about the guests arriving an hour early.<br>客人早到一小时，妈妈就慌了神。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to</b></td><td>to and ˈfro</td><td>来回地；往返地</td><td>The old ferry chugs to and fro across the river all day long.<br>那艘老渡轮整天突突地在河上来回。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(all) to yourˈself, himˈself, etc.</td><td>完全归某人独享（或独用）</td><td>With everyone away, I had the whole beach to myself.<br>大家都走了，整片沙滩就归我一个人了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>toast</b></td><td>be ˈtoast (slang)</td><td>完蛋了；没戏了</td><td>If the boss sees this spreadsheet, we're toast.<br>老板要是看到这张表，我们就完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be the toast of...</td><td>在…广受赞誉；成为…的红人</td><td>After that goal he was the toast of the entire town for weeks.<br>那个进球之后，他好几周都是全城的名人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tod</b></td><td>on your ˈtod (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>独自一人；单独地</td><td>He spent the whole bank holiday on his tod watching old films.<br>整个公休日他一个人在家看老电影。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>here toˌday, ˌgone toˈmorrow</td><td>来去匆匆；转瞬即逝</td><td>These trends are here today, gone tomorrow, so don't invest much.<br>这些潮流来得快去得也快，别投太多钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go toe to ˈtoe (AmE)</td><td>正面交锋；直接较量</td><td>The small firm went toe to toe with a giant and somehow won.<br>那家小公司跟巨头正面硬碰，居然赢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>toe the ˈline (AmE also toe the ˈmark)</td><td>服从命令；遵守规矩</td><td>New staff are expected to toe the line for the first six months.<br>新员工头六个月都得规规矩矩听指挥。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>toes</b></td><td>keep sb on their ˈtoes (informal)</td><td>使某人保持警惕；让人不敢松懈</td><td>Surprise inspections keep the kitchen staff on their toes.<br>突击检查让厨房的人不敢松懈。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make sb's ˈtoes curl</td><td>使某人尴尬；让人浑身不自在</td><td>His speech about my childhood made my toes curl.<br>他讲我童年的那段话让我尴尬得脚趾抠地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on your ˈtoes</td><td>随时待命；准备好行动</td><td>Stay on your toes; the fire alarm test could come any minute.<br>保持警觉，火警测试随时可能开始。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>toffee</b></td><td>can't do sth for ˈtoffee (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</td><td>做某事很蹩脚；完全不在行</td><td>She's a brilliant writer but can't spell for toffee.<br>她文章写得极好，可拼写差得一塌糊涂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>together</b></td><td>toˈgether with</td><td>连同；和…一起</td><td>Send your passport together with two recent photographs.<br>请把护照连同两张近照一并寄来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>toing</b></td><td>ˌtoing and ˈfroing</td><td>来来回回；往返奔波</td><td>After weeks of toing and froing, they finally agreed on a price.<br>来回折腾了好几周，他们总算谈妥了价钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>token</b></td><td>by the ˌsame ˈtoken</td><td>同理；出于同样的理由</td><td>He's never late, and by the same token he expects punctuality from us.<br>他从不迟到，同样地，他也要求我们守时。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>told</b></td><td>all ˈtold</td><td>总共；总计</td><td>All told, about two hundred people turned up for the beach clean-up.<br>总共有大约两百人来参加海滩清理。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>toll</b></td><td>take its ˈtoll (on sb/sth) (also take a (heavy) ˈtoll (of sth))</td><td>造成损失；带来严重后果</td><td>Those night shifts are taking their toll on his health.<br>那些夜班正在损害他的健康。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tom</b></td><td>every/any ˌTom, ˌDick and/or ˈHarry (usually disapproving)</td><td>随便什么人；张三李四</td><td>You can't let every Tom, Dick and Harry borrow the studio key.<br>你不能随便什么人都借给他工作室的钥匙。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tomorrow</b></td><td>do sth as if/like there's no toˈmorrow (informal)</td><td>拼命地做；仿佛没有明天似的</td><td>He was spending money like there's no tomorrow after the bonus arrived.<br>奖金一到手，他就花钱如流水。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ton</b></td><td>be/come down on sb like a ton of ˈbricks</td><td>严厉斥责某人；狠狠训一顿</td><td>The coach came down on him like a ton of bricks for missing training.<br>他缺席训练，被教练狠狠地骂了一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tone</b></td><td>set the ˈtone (of/for sth)</td><td>为…定下基调</td><td>Her warm welcome set the tone for the whole weekend.<br>她热情的欢迎为整个周末定下了基调。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tongue</b></td><td>get your ˈtongue round/around sth</td><td>把（难读的词）念准</td><td>I still can't get my tongue round the name of that Welsh village.<br>那个威尔士村名我到现在都念不利索。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>roll/slip/trip off the ˈtongue</td><td>顺口好念；朗朗上口</td><td>The new brand name doesn't exactly trip off the tongue, does it?<br>这个新牌子名字念着不太顺口，是吧？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌsilver/ˌsmooth ˈtongue</td><td>口才好；能说会道</td><td>With his silver tongue he talked the landlord into lowering the rent.<br>他嘴皮子利索，说得房东降了租金。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(with) tongue in ˈcheek (also with your tongue in your ˈcheek)</td><td>开玩笑地；半开玩笑不当真地</td><td>He suggested, tongue in cheek, that we hold the meeting in the pub.<br>他半开玩笑地提议把会开到酒吧去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tongues</b></td><td>set ˈtongues wagging (informal)</td><td>惹人说长道短；引起议论纷纷</td><td>Their arriving together at the party set tongues wagging immediately.<br>他俩一起到派对，立刻惹得众人议论纷纷。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tongues ˈwag (informal)</td><td>风言风语；说闲话</td><td>Tongues wagged for months after the manager left so suddenly.<br>经理走得那么突然，之后好几个月都有闲话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tools</b></td><td>ˌdown ˈtools (BrE)</td><td>停工；罢工</td><td>The builders downed tools at noon over the unpaid wages.<br>工人们因为拖欠工资，中午就停工了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the tools of the/your ˈtrade</td><td>行业用具；吃饭的家伙</td><td>A sharp knife and a heavy pan are the tools of her trade.<br>一把快刀和一口厚锅就是她吃饭的家伙。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>top</b></td><td>at the top of your ˈvoice</td><td>放开嗓门；大声地</td><td>He sang at the top of his voice all the way down the hill.<br>他一路下山都在扯着嗓子唱歌。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get on ˈtop of sth</td><td>能驾驭；有能力处理</td><td>It took a month, but she's finally on top of the paperwork.<br>花了一个月，她总算把文书工作理顺了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come out on ˈtop (of sth)</td><td>占上风；最终获胜</td><td>After a long legal fight, the tenants came out on top.<br>经过漫长的官司，租户们最终赢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from ˌtop to ˈbottom</td><td>彻底地；从头到尾</td><td>We cleaned the house from top to bottom before the inspection.<br>检查前我们把房子从上到下彻底打扫了一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from ˌtop to ˈtoe</td><td>从头到脚；浑身上下</td><td>He came in from the garden covered in mud from top to toe.<br>他从花园进来，浑身上下全是泥。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get on ˈtop of sb</td><td>（困难、工作等）压得某人受不了</td><td>The constant deadlines are really getting on top of him lately.<br>接连不断的截止日期最近压得他喘不过气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>off the ˌtop of your ˈhead (informal)</td><td>不加思索地；凭印象随口说</td><td>Off the top of my head, I'd say about forty people came.<br>我随口一说，大概来了四十个人吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on top of sb/sth</td><td>此外；除…之外还</td><td>On top of everything else, the washing machine broke this morning.<br>除了别的糟心事，今早洗衣机又坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˌtop of the ˈworld</td><td>欢天喜地；高兴到极点</td><td>She felt on top of the world after passing her final exam.<br>通过期末考试后，她觉得自己快乐得要飞起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>pay, earn, charge, etc. top ˈdollar</td><td>付高价；挣大钱</td><td>Collectors pay top dollar for early editions of that comic.<br>收藏者愿出高价买那套漫画的早期版本。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtake it from the ˈtop (informal)</td><td>（歌曲、演讲等）从头再来一遍</td><td>That was close, everyone — let's take it from the top once more.<br>差不多了，各位，我们再从头来一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtop and ˈtail sth (BrE)</td><td>去掉（果蔬的）头尾</td><td>Top and tail the green beans before you drop them in the water.<br>下锅前先把四季豆的头尾去掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(the) ˌtop ˈbrass (BrE, informal)</td><td>高层人物；高级官员</td><td>The top brass are flying in tomorrow to inspect the new plant.<br>高层明天飞过来视察新厂。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtop ˈdog (informal)</td><td>居首位的人（或团体）；巨头</td><td>That little bakery is now top dog in the local wedding-cake market.<br>那家小面包房如今是当地婚礼蛋糕市场的老大。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the top of the ˈhour (especially AmE)</td><td>整点（时刻）</td><td>We'll have the traffic report again at the top of the hour.<br>整点我们会再播一次路况。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>opposite: the bottom of the hour</td><td>反义词，指半点整</td><td>The opposite of the top of the hour is the bottom of the hour, meaning half past.<br>the top of the hour 的反义是 the bottom of the hour，即半点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(at) the top of the ˈtree/ˈladder</td><td>（处于）行业顶端</td><td>At forty she was already at the top of the tree in her profession.<br>四十岁时她已经站在本行业的顶端。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtop ˈsecret</td><td>绝密；最高机密</td><td>The recipe is top secret and only two people in the family know it.<br>这个配方是绝密，家里只有两个人知道。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌtop ˈten, ˈtwenty, etc.</td><td>（唱片等）前十名、前二十名</td><td>Their second single stayed in the top ten for eleven weeks.<br>他们的第二支单曲在前十名榜上待了十一周。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˌtop/ˌcap/ˌcrown it ˈall (spoken)</td><td>更糟的是；最要命的是</td><td>We missed the train and, to top it all, it started pouring.<br>我们没赶上火车，更要命的是还下起了大雨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up ˈtop (BrE, informal)</td><td>脑子；智力</td><td>He's not much to look at, but there's plenty going on up top.<br>他外表一般，脑子却很好使。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>head/top the ˈbill</td><td>领衔演出；名列演出海报之首</td><td>A local jazz trio will top the bill at the festival this year.<br>今年音乐节由一支本地爵士三重奏领衔演出。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>torch</b></td><td>put sth to the ˈtorch (literary)</td><td>放火烧毁；付之一炬</td><td>The retreating army put the whole warehouse district to the torch.<br>撤退的军队把整个仓库区付之一炬。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>torn</b></td><td>that's ˈtorn it (BrE, informal)</td><td>（计划被打乱时说）糟了；这下完了</td><td>The last bus has gone — well, that's torn it.<br>末班车开走了，这下完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>toss</b></td><td>not give a ˈtoss (about sb/sth) (BrE, slang)</td><td>对…毫不在乎</td><td>He doesn't give a toss about what the neighbours think of his garden.<br>邻居怎么看他的花园，他压根不在乎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>toss a ˈcoin • ˈtoss for sth (especially BrE)</td><td>掷硬币决定</td><td>We tossed a coin to see who would sleep on the sofa.<br>我们掷硬币决定谁睡沙发。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(also flip a ˈcoin, ˈflip for sth usually both AmE)</td><td>掷硬币决定某事</td><td>Let's flip a coin for the last slice of pizza.<br>最后一块披萨我们掷硬币决定吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>toss-up</b></td><td>be a ˈtoss-up (between A and B) (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>难以定夺；两者机会均等</td><td>It's a toss-up between the blue coat and the grey one.<br>蓝大衣还是灰大衣，我实在难以决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>touch</b></td><td>be, etc. in/out of ˈtouch (with sth)</td><td>了解（或不了解）某事的最新情况</td><td>After ten years abroad he's completely out of touch with local politics.<br>在国外待了十年，他对本地政治完全脱节了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be, keep, etc. in ˈtouch (with sb)</td><td>与某人保持联系</td><td>We've kept in touch with our old landlady for over twenty years.<br>我们和以前的房东太太保持联系二十多年了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be out of ˈtouch (with sb)</td><td>与某人失去联系</td><td>I've been out of touch with my cousins since the funeral.<br>葬礼之后我就和表亲们断了联系。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get in ˈtouch with sb/sth</td><td>与…取得联系</td><td>Get in touch with the landlord before you sign anything.<br>签任何东西之前先联系房东。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have, etc. a ˌtouch of ˈclass</td><td>有气派；显档次</td><td>The fresh flowers on every table give the café a touch of class.<br>每张桌上的鲜花让这家咖啡馆多了几分格调。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose ˈtouch/ˈcontact (with sb/sth)</td><td>与…失去联系</td><td>We lost touch after university and only met again last year.<br>大学毕业后我们就断了联系，去年才重逢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose your ˈtouch</td><td>手艺（或能力）不如从前</td><td>This cake is dry — I think Gran is losing her touch.<br>这蛋糕太干了，我看奶奶手艺不如从前了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not touch sb/sth with a ˈbargepole (BrE)</td><td>唯恐避之不及；不愿沾边</td><td>That flat is damp and overpriced; I wouldn't touch it with a bargepole.<br>那套房又潮又贵，我碰都不会碰。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb in ˈtouch with sb/sth</td><td>介绍某人与…联系</td><td>Can you put me in touch with a decent plumber in the area?<br>你能给我介绍个这一带靠谱的水管工吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a soft/an easy ˈtouch (informal)</td><td>心软的人；容易被说动的人</td><td>Ask Dad for the money; he's always been a soft touch.<br>找爸要钱吧，他一向心软。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>touch ˈbase (with sb) (informal)</td><td>（与某人）联络一下；碰个头</td><td>Let's touch base on Friday once the figures are in.<br>等数据出来，我们周五碰个头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>touch ˈbottom</td><td>触到水底；跌到最低点</td><td>Prices seem to have touched bottom and are slowly rising again.<br>价格似乎已经见底，正在慢慢回升。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>touch ˈwood (BrE) (AmE knock on ˈwood)</td><td>但愿好运；碰碰木头求吉利</td><td>I haven't had a cold all winter, touch wood.<br>整个冬天我都没感冒，但愿别乌鸦嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>People still often try to touch something wooden.</td><td>人们说此语时仍常去碰木质物件</td><td>People still often try to touch something wooden as they say the phrase.<br>人们说这句话时仍常常去碰碰木头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>touch-and-go</b></td><td>be ˌtouch-and-ˈgo (whether...) (informal)</td><td>结果难料；不确定；有风险</td><td>It was touch-and-go whether the surgeon could save his leg.<br>能不能保住他的腿，当时很难说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>touched</b></td><td>be touched with sth</td><td>略带；稍稍带有</td><td>Her voice was touched with sadness as she read the letter aloud.<br>她朗读那封信时，声音里带着一丝伤感。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tough</b></td><td>be/get ˈtough (on/with sb)</td><td>对…态度强硬；采取强硬手段</td><td>The school is getting tough with students who skip lessons.<br>学校对逃课的学生开始动真格了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) tough as ˈnails (informal)</td><td>身体强壮；意志坚强</td><td>She's seventy and as tough as nails; she still swims in the sea.<br>她七十岁了还硬朗得很，照样下海游泳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) tough as old ˈboots (informal)</td><td>（食物）硬得咬不动</td><td>The steak was as tough as old boots and we sent it back.<br>那块牛排硬得像鞋底，我们退了回去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a tough ˈcustomer/ˈcookie (informal)</td><td>很有主见的人；不易被说动的人</td><td>Don't expect a discount from her; she's a tough cookie.<br>别指望她给你打折，她可不好对付。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈtough guy (informal)</td><td>硬汉；顽强无畏的人</td><td>He plays the tough guy on screen but faints at the dentist.<br>他在银幕上演硬汉，看牙医却会晕过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tough ˈlove</td><td>严爱；用严厉方式表达关心</td><td>Cutting off his allowance was tough love, but it finally worked.<br>断了他的零花钱是严爱，可最后管用了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>when the ˌgoing gets ˈtough (the ˌtough get ˈgoing) (saying)</td><td>艰难之路唯勇者行；越难越向前</td><td>When the going gets tough, the tough get going — so let's start again.<br>艰难之路唯勇者行，我们重新来过吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a hard/tough ˈact to follow</td><td>难以超越的人（或事）</td><td>The previous head teacher was a hard act to follow.<br>前任校长是个很难超越的标杆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tour</b></td><td>a tour de ˈforce (from French)</td><td>绝妙的表演；杰作</td><td>Her final scene was a tour de force that left the audience silent.<br>她的最后一场戏堪称绝技，观众鸦雀无声。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>towel</b></td><td>(out) on the ˈtown (also a night (out) on the ˈtown/on the ˈtiles) (informal)</td><td>（尤指晚上）外出玩乐</td><td>After the exams we all went out on the town until three in the morning.<br>考完试我们出去嗨到凌晨三点。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sink, vanish, etc. without (a) ˈtrace</td><td>消失得无影无踪</td><td>The little fishing boat vanished without a trace off the north coast.<br>那条小渔船在北岸海域消失得无影无踪。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trade</b></td><td>a ˌtrade ˈsecret</td><td>商业机密；不外传的诀窍</td><td>How she gets the pastry so light is a trade secret.<br>她怎么把酥皮做得那么松，这是商业机密。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>train</b></td><td>bring sth in its ˈtrain (written)</td><td>带来；引起；导致</td><td>The factory closure brought unemployment and poverty in its train.<br>工厂倒闭带来了失业和贫困。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in sb's ˈtrain (written)</td><td>尾随某人；跟在某人后面</td><td>The old professor arrived with a dozen students in his train.<br>老教授来了，身后跟着十几个学生。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈtrain (formal)</td><td>在进行中；已着手准备</td><td>Plans for the new footbridge are already well in train.<br>新人行桥的规划已在顺利推进。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a train of ˈthought</td><td>思路；思绪</td><td>The phone rang and I completely lost my train of thought.<br>电话一响，我的思路全断了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trap</b></td><td>fall into/avoid the trap of doing sth</td><td>落入（或避免落入）…的陷阱</td><td>Don't fall into the trap of buying more than you can carry.<br>别掉进买得太多拿不动的陷阱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>travel</b></td><td>travel ˈlight</td><td>轻装旅行</td><td>She always travels light, just a rucksack and a toothbrush.<br>她出门总是轻装上阵，一个背包一把牙刷。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tread</b></td><td>ˌtread the ˈboards (humorous)</td><td>登台演出；当演员</td><td>He trod the boards for thirty years before turning to directing.<br>他登台演了三十年戏，后来转做导演。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tread ˈcarefully, ˈwarily, etc.</td><td>小心行事；谨言慎行</td><td>Tread carefully when you mention the redundancies to her.<br>跟她提裁员的事时要小心措辞。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>tread a difficult, solitary, etc. ˈpath</td><td>走一条艰难（或孤独等）的路</td><td>As the only woman on the board, she trod a lonely path for years.<br>作为董事会里唯一的女性，她孤独地走了很多年。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtread on sb's ˈheels</td><td>紧跟在某人后面</td><td>The younger runners were treading on his heels all the way up the hill.<br>上坡的一路上，年轻选手都紧咬着他不放。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtread on sb's ˈtoes (especially BrE)</td><td>冒犯某人；越界干涉</td><td>I don't want to tread on your toes, but that's really my department's job.<br>我不想越界，可那本来是我们部门的活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(AmE usually ˌstep on sb's ˈtoes) (informal)</td><td>得罪某人；插手他人职责</td><td>He rewrote her report and stepped on her toes badly.<br>他把她的报告重写了一遍，狠狠得罪了她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtread ˈwater</td><td>踩水；停滞不前；原地观望</td><td>The company is just treading water until the new owner arrives.<br>在新东家到来之前，公司只是在原地打转。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>treat</b></td><td>go down a ˈtreat (BrE, informal)</td><td>大受欢迎；反响极好</td><td>Your lemon cake went down a treat at the school fair.<br>你的柠檬蛋糕在学校义卖上大受欢迎。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>treat sb like ˈdirt (informal)</td><td>把某人当垃圾；蔑视某人</td><td>That restaurant treats its kitchen staff like dirt.<br>那家餐厅把后厨员工当垃圾对待。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>work a ˈtreat (BrE, informal)</td><td>非常有效；效果极好</td><td>A spoonful of salt worked a treat on that red wine stain.<br>一勺盐对付那块红酒渍效果特别好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>treatment</b></td><td>give sb/get the ˌsilent ˈtreatment</td><td>对某人不理不睬；冷战</td><td>She gave him the silent treatment for three whole days.<br>她整整三天没搭理他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tree</b></td><td>be out of your ˈtree (BrE also be out of your ˈbox) (informal)</td><td>（醉酒或嗑药后）疯疯癫癫</td><td>By midnight half the party was completely out of their trees.<br>到了半夜，派对上一半人都醉得不省人事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trial</b></td><td>by ˌtrial and ˈerror</td><td>反复试验；不断摸索</td><td>He learnt to bake sourdough by trial and error over two years.<br>他花了两年反复摸索，学会了烤酸面包。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌtrial ˈrun</td><td>试运行；初步试验</td><td>We did a trial run of the new booking system last Tuesday.<br>上周二我们对新预订系统做了一次试运行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trials</b></td><td>ˌtrials and tribuˈlations</td><td>艰难困苦；磨难</td><td>She wrote honestly about the trials and tribulations of single parenthood.<br>她如实写下了单亲育儿的种种艰辛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trice</b></td><td>in a ˈtrice</td><td>转瞬间；顷刻间</td><td>The waiter cleared the whole table in a trice.<br>服务员转眼间就把整桌收拾干净了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trick</b></td><td>ˌtrick or ˈtreat</td><td>不给糖就捣蛋（万圣节讨糖用语）</td><td>Three small witches knocked and shouted 'trick or treat' at our door.<br>三个小女巫敲门喊着「不给糖就捣蛋」。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>try, use, etc. every trick in the ˈbook</td><td>使尽浑身解数；千方百计</td><td>He used every trick in the book to get out of jury duty.<br>他使尽了各种花招想逃掉陪审义务。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn a ˈtrick/ˈtricks (AmE, slang)</td><td>卖淫；接客</td><td>The film follows a young woman turning tricks to pay her rent.<br>影片讲述一个年轻女子靠卖身付房租的故事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tricks</b></td><td>a bag/box of ˈtricks (informal)</td><td>全套本事；一整套办法</td><td>The old mechanic arrived with his usual bag of tricks.<br>老技工照例带着他那一整套家伙什来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be up to your (old) ˈtricks (informal, disapproving)</td><td>故伎重演；又耍老把戏</td><td>He's up to his old tricks, borrowing money he'll never repay.<br>他又故伎重演，借钱从来不还。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>how's ˈtricks? (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>（友好问候）近来怎么样</td><td>Hello stranger, how's tricks? I haven't seen you in months.<br>嘿，稀客，最近怎么样？好几个月没见你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌtricks of the ˈtrade</td><td>行业诀窍；门道</td><td>The old baker taught him all the tricks of the trade.<br>老面包师把行业里的门道全教给了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tried</b></td><td>ˌtried and ˈtested/ˈtrusted (BrE) (AmE ˌtried and ˈtrue)</td><td>久经考验的；屡试不爽的</td><td>For a sore throat she uses the tried and tested honey and lemon.<br>嗓子疼时她用蜂蜜柠檬这个老方子，屡试不爽。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trim</b></td><td>be, keep, etc. in ˈtrim (BrE, informal)</td><td>身体状态不错；保持健康</td><td>He cycles to work every day to keep in trim.<br>他每天骑车上班，保持身材。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>trim your ˈsails</td><td>见风使舵；缩减开支</td><td>With sales falling, the shop had to trim its sails sharply.<br>销量下滑，这家店只好大幅缩减开支。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trolley</b></td><td>off your ˈtrolley (BrE, informal)</td><td>发疯；犯傻</td><td>Swimming in that river in January? You're off your trolley.<br>一月份去那条河里游泳？你疯了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trot</b></td><td>on the ˈtrot (BrE, informal)</td><td>接连地；一个接一个</td><td>They've won five matches on the trot since the new coach arrived.<br>新教练来了以后，他们连赢五场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trouble</b></td><td>get sb into ˈtrouble (old-fashioned)</td><td>使未婚女子怀孕</td><td>In those days a boy who got a girl into trouble had to marry her.<br>那年头男孩让女孩怀了孕就得娶她。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give (sb) (some, no, any, etc.) ˈtrouble</td><td>给（某人）惹麻烦；带来问题</td><td>My knee has been giving me some trouble since the marathon.<br>跑完马拉松后我的膝盖一直有点毛病。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look for ˈtrouble</td><td>自找麻烦；惹是生非</td><td>Arguing with the referee like that is just looking for trouble.<br>那样跟裁判争执纯属自找麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take trouble over/with sth • take trouble to do sth</td><td>费心做某事；尽心尽力</td><td>She took great trouble over the seating plan for the dinner.<br>她为这次晚宴的座位安排费了不少心思。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's ˈtrouble brewing (informal)</td><td>要出乱子了；麻烦要来了</td><td>Judging by those emails, there's trouble brewing in the finance team.<br>从那些邮件看，财务组要出乱子了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a trouble ˌshared is a trouble ˈhalved (saying)</td><td>苦恼有人分担就减半</td><td>Tell me what's wrong — a trouble shared is a trouble halved.<br>说说怎么了，有人分担，烦恼就少一半。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>come</b></td><td>come/turn up ˈtrumps (informal)</td><td>关键时刻帮上大忙；出乎意料地成功</td><td>Our neighbour came up trumps and drove us to the airport at dawn.<br>邻居真够意思，天没亮就送我们去机场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trump</b></td><td>a/your ˈtrump card</td><td>王牌；杀手锏</td><td>Her fluent Japanese was the trump card in the interview.<br>她那口流利的日语是面试中的王牌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trust</b></td><td>in sb's ˈtrust • in the trust of sb</td><td>由某人保管；托付给某人照管</td><td>The house was left in his sister's trust until the children grew up.<br>房子交由他姐姐保管，直到孩子们长大。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not trust sb an ˈinch</td><td>根本不信任某人</td><td>He smiles a lot, but I wouldn't trust him an inch.<br>他老是笑呵呵的，可我一点也不信他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth on ˈtrust</td><td>不加证实就相信；凭信任接受</td><td>I took his story on trust, but it turned out to be completely false.<br>我当时轻信了他的说法，结果全是假的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>trust ˈyou, ˈhim, ˈher, etc. (to do sth) (spoken, informal)</td><td>（言行一贯如此）管保；就知道会这样</td><td>Trust him to show up late on the most important day of all.<br>就知道他会在最要紧的日子迟到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>truth</b></td><td>if (the) ˌtruth be ˈknown/ˈtold</td><td>说实话；说真的；事实上</td><td>If truth be told, I never really liked that job in the first place.<br>说实话，我从一开始就不喜欢那份工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈtruth (written)</td><td>其实；的确</td><td>She smiled politely, but in truth she was furious about the whole thing.<br>她礼貌地笑着，其实心里对整件事气坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtruth is stranger than ˈfiction (saying)</td><td>现实比虚构更离奇</td><td>He survived three plane crashes, which proves truth is stranger than fiction.<br>他从三次空难中生还，可见现实比小说更离奇。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(the) ˌtruth will ˈout (saying)</td><td>真相终会大白</td><td>Keep lying if you like, but the truth will out sooner or later.<br>你尽管撒谎，真相迟早会大白。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>try</b></td><td>try your ˈhand (at sth/doing sth)</td><td>尝试；试试身手</td><td>After retiring, he tried his hand at painting and turned out to be good.<br>退休后他试着画画，居然画得不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtry it ˈon (with sb) (BrE, informal)</td><td>试探某人的底线；耍花招</td><td>The kids always try it on with their grandmother because she never says no.<br>孩子们总跟奶奶蹬鼻子上脸，因为她从不拒绝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>try your ˈluck (at sth)</td><td>碰碰运气</td><td>I thought I would try my luck at the audition, even without any training.<br>我想去试镜碰碰运气，虽然一点儿也没受过训练。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>try sb's ˈpatience</td><td>使人不耐烦；让人忍无可忍</td><td>That child really tries my patience with his endless questions at bedtime.<br>那孩子睡前没完没了地问问题，真让我受不了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do/try your ˈdamnedest</td><td>竭尽全力；拼尽全力</td><td>She did her damnedest to finish the report before the midnight deadline.<br>她拼了命想在午夜截止前写完报告。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>trying</b></td><td>not for lack/want of ˈtrying</td><td>并非不努力；已经尽力了</td><td>We never won the contract, though not for lack of trying on our part.<br>我们始终没拿到合同，但并不是我们不努力。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tube</b></td><td>go down the ˈtube/tubes (informal)</td><td>失败；垮掉；付诸东流</td><td>Their family business went down the tubes after the second lockdown last winter.<br>去年冬天第二次封锁之后，他们的家族生意就垮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tug</b></td><td>tug at sb's ˈheartstrings</td><td>拨动心弦；打动人心</td><td>That advert with the abandoned puppy really tugs at your heartstrings.<br>那个流浪小狗的广告真是特别催泪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>touch/tug your ˈforelock</td><td>行触额礼；卑躬屈膝</td><td>He refuses to touch his forelock to anyone just because they have money.<br>他才不会因为谁有钱就对谁点头哈腰。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tune</b></td><td>be ˌin/ˌout of ˈtune (with sb/sth)</td><td>合拍；不合拍；音准；走调</td><td>The new manager is completely out of tune with what the staff actually want.<br>新经理跟员工真正的想法完全不在一个频道上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to the tune of $500, etc. (informal)</td><td>高达（五百美元等）之多</td><td>The repairs ended up costing us to the tune of three thousand pounds.<br>这次维修最后花了我们足足三千英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tunnel</b></td><td>(have) ˌtunnel ˈvision (disapproving)</td><td>目光狭隘；一孔之见</td><td>Coaches with tunnel vision only care about winning and ignore player welfare.<br>目光狭隘的教练只在乎赢球，不管球员死活。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turf</b></td><td>a ˈturf war (informal)</td><td>地盘之争</td><td>A turf war broke out between the two departments over the new budget.<br>两个部门为新预算打起了地盘之争。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turn</b></td><td>at every ˈturn</td><td>处处；时时；每每</td><td>Our plans were blocked at every turn by the local planning committee.<br>我们的计划处处受到当地规划委员会的阻挠。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by ˈturn(s)</td><td>轮流；交替地</td><td>During the trip she was by turns excited, exhausted and terribly homesick.<br>旅途中她时而兴奋，时而疲惫，时而想家想得厉害。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth out of ˈturn</td><td>不按次序做；说话不合时宜</td><td>Sorry if I spoke out of turn, but somebody had to say it.<br>抱歉我要是说了不该说的话，可总得有人说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb a ˈturn (old-fashioned)</td><td>把某人吓一跳</td><td>You gave me quite a turn, creeping up behind me like that.<br>你那样悄悄溜到我身后，真把我吓了一跳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈturn</td><td>依次；轮流；转而</td><td>Each student read a paragraph aloud in turn while the others listened quietly.<br>每个学生依次朗读一段，其他人安静地听。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈturn (especially BrE)</td><td>即将变化；（牛奶）快变质</td><td>The milk smells like it is on the turn, so do not drink it.<br>这牛奶闻着快坏了，别喝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>turn sth ˌinside ˈout/ˌupside ˈdown</td><td>翻个底朝天；翻得乱七八糟</td><td>Burglars turned the whole flat upside down looking for cash and jewellery.<br>窃贼把整套公寓翻得乱七八糟，就为找现金和首饰。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turned</b></td><td>as it/things turned ˈout</td><td>结果却；事实证明</td><td>As it turned out, the meeting was cancelled and nobody bothered to tell us.<br>结果会议取消了，却没人想着通知我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be well, badly, etc. turned ˈout</td><td>穿着讲究（或邋遢等）</td><td>He is always beautifully turned out, even for a casual Sunday lunch.<br>他总是衣着体面，哪怕只是周日的家常午饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turns</b></td><td>take ˈturns doing sth/to do sth (BrE also take it in ˈturns to do sth)</td><td>轮流做某事</td><td>We take turns doing the washing up so nobody gets stuck with it.<br>我们轮流洗碗，免得老落在一个人头上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turn-up</b></td><td>a ˌturn-up for the ˈbook(s) (BrE, informal)</td><td>出人意料的事</td><td>Him passing the exam first time was a real turn-up for the books.<br>他一次就考过了，真是出人意料。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turtle</b></td><td>turn ˈturtle</td><td>（船）翻个底朝天；倾覆</td><td>The little fishing boat turned turtle in the storm, but everyone was rescued.<br>那条小渔船在风暴中翻了，好在人都获救了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>twist</b></td><td>ˈtwist in the wind (especially AmE)</td><td>悬而未决；孤立无援任人责难</td><td>The company left him twisting in the wind while reporters demanded answers.<br>公司把他晾在那儿，任凭记者追问。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈtwixt</td><td>在两者之间（旧式或诗体用法）</td><td>There is many a slip twixt cup and lip, so do not celebrate yet.<br>没到最后关头什么都可能变，先别庆祝。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>two</b></td><td>be in two ˈminds about sth/about doing sth</td><td>拿不定主意；犹豫不决</td><td>I am in two minds about accepting the job offer in Shanghai.<br>我对要不要接受上海那份工作还拿不定主意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(BrE) (AmE be of two ˈminds about sth/about doing sth)</td><td>下不了决心；踌躇不决</td><td>She was of two minds about whether to sell the old family house.<br>她对要不要卖掉那栋老宅一直下不了决心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈday, ˈmoment, etc. or two</td><td>一两天（或一会儿等）</td><td>Give me a moment or two and I will have the answer ready.<br>给我一会儿，我马上就能给你答案。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>fall between two ˈstools (BrE)</td><td>两头落空；两边不讨好</td><td>The film falls between two stools: too silly for adults, too scary for kids.<br>这部电影两头不讨好：大人嫌幼稚，孩子嫌吓人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for two ˈpins (old-fashioned, BrE)</td><td>恨不得；巴不得</td><td>For two pins I would quit this job and move to the coast.<br>我真恨不得辞掉这份工作搬到海边去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have two left ˈfeet (informal)</td><td>笨手笨脚（尤指跳舞时）</td><td>Please do not ask me to dance, I have two left feet.<br>千万别叫我跳舞，我笨得要命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in two ˈshakes • in a ˌcouple of ˈshakes (also)</td><td>一会儿；转眼间</td><td>Hang on, I will be back in two shakes with the spare keys.<br>等一下，我马上拿备用钥匙回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in two ˌshakes of a ˈlamb's tail (old-fashioned)</td><td>很快；马上</td><td>She promised to be ready in two shakes of a lamb's tail.<br>她保证一转眼就收拾好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it takes ˈtwo (to do sth) (also it takes two to ˈtango) (saying)</td><td>一个巴掌拍不响；双方都有责任</td><td>Do not blame her for the argument; it takes two to tango.<br>别把吵架都怪到她头上，一个巴掌拍不响。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(there are) no two ways aˈbout it (informal)</td><td>毫无疑问；没有别的说法</td><td>There are no two ways about it, we have to cut costs now.<br>毫无疑问，我们现在必须削减开支。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not have two brain ˌcells, pennies, etc. to rub toˈgether (BrE, informal)</td><td>蠢得可以；穷得叮当响</td><td>She has not got two brain cells to rub together, but she means well.<br>她脑子不太够用，不过心是好的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>one or ˈtwo</td><td>少数几个；一两个</td><td>One or two people complained about the noise, but most enjoyed the party.<br>有一两个人抱怨吵，但多数人玩得很开心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put in your two ˈpennyworth/ˈpenn’orth</td><td>发表己见；插一句嘴</td><td>He always has to put in his two pennyworth at every family meeting.<br>每次家庭会议他都非要插上一嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(BrE) (AmE put in your two ˈcents' worth) (informal)</td><td>发表意见（即使别人不想听）</td><td>Nobody asked her, but she put in her two cents' worth anyway.<br>没人问她，她还是发表了一通意见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put ˌtwo and ˌtwo toˈgether</td><td>根据现有情况推断；猜出真相</td><td>She saw them leaving together and quickly put two and two together.<br>她看见他俩一起出去，很快就猜出是怎么回事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/stick two ˈfingers up at sb (BrE, informal)</td><td>对某人做侮辱手势；表示蔑视</td><td>The driver stuck two fingers up at me and sped off down the road.<br>那司机冲我做了个侮辱手势就飞驰而去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>stand on your own two feet</td><td>自立；自食其力</td><td>At twenty-five it is time you learned to stand on your own two feet.<br>都二十五了，该学着自食其力了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that makes ˈtwo of us</td><td>我也一样；我同意</td><td>You are exhausted? That makes two of us after last night's long shift.<br>你累坏了？昨晚那个长班上完，我也一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌtwo can play at ˈthat game (saying)</td><td>这一套我也会；以牙还牙</td><td>If he keeps ignoring my messages, two can play at that game.<br>他要是一直不回我信息，这一套我也会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>two heads are better than ˈone (saying)</td><td>人多智广；两人智慧胜一人</td><td>Let me look at your draft too; two heads are better than one.<br>让我也看看你的草稿，两个人想总比一个人强。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>two ˌsides of the same ˈcoin</td><td>同一事物的两面</td><td>Freedom and responsibility are really two sides of the same coin.<br>自由和责任其实是一体两面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>two ˌwrongs don't make a ˈright (saying)</td><td>以错纠错仍是错；冤冤相报无休止</td><td>Do not key his car; two wrongs don't make a right.<br>别去划他的车，以错纠错还是错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>two's ˈcompany (, three's a ˈcrowd) (saying)</td><td>两人成伴，三人不欢</td><td>I will skip the cinema tonight, since two's company and three's a crowd.<br>今晚电影我就不去了，两人成伴，三人不欢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush</td><td>一鸟在手胜过双鸟在林</td><td>Take the offer now, because a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.<br>现在就接受这个报价吧，一鸟在手胜过双鸟在林。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>type</b></td><td>(not) be sb's ˈtype (informal)</td><td>（不）是某人喜欢的类型</td><td>He is nice enough, but he is really not my type at all.<br>他人挺好，可实在不是我喜欢的类型。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ugly</b></td><td>an ˌugly ˈduckling (informal)</td><td>丑小鸭（先平庸后出众者）</td><td>She was the ugly duckling at school and is now a famous actress.<br>她上学时是只丑小鸭，如今成了名演员。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>um</b></td><td>ˌum and ˈaah (about sth) (also ˌhum/ˌhem and ˈhaw less frequent) (informal)</td><td>支支吾吾；犹豫不决</td><td>Stop umming and aahing about the tickets and just book them today.<br>别再为买票支支吾吾了，今天就订吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>After a lot of umming and aahing, he finally</td><td>支吾了半天；犹豫再三</td><td>After a lot of umming and aahing, he finally agreed to lend us the van.<br>他支吾了半天，终于同意把货车借给我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>umbrage</b></td><td>take ˈumbrage (at sth) (formal or humorous)</td><td>（常指无故）生气；见怪</td><td>My aunt took umbrage at not being invited to the family dinner.<br>我姑姑因为没被请去家宴而生了闷气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>unawares</b></td><td>catch/take sb unaˈwares</td><td>使某人措手不及；出其不意</td><td>The question caught me unawares and I had no answer ready.<br>这个问题问得我措手不及，我完全没准备。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>uncertain</b></td><td>in ˌno unˌcertain ˈterms</td><td>明白无误地；直截了当地</td><td>She told him in no uncertain terms that his behaviour was unacceptable.<br>她直截了当地告诉他，他的行为无法接受。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>uncle</b></td><td>Uncle ˈSam (informal)</td><td>山姆大叔（指美国或美国政府）</td><td>Every April a big chunk of my salary goes straight to Uncle Sam.<br>每年四月我工资的一大块都直接交给了山姆大叔。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>uncle</b></td><td>cry/say ˈuncle (AmE)</td><td>认输；服软</td><td>He twisted my arm until I finally cried uncle and let him win.<br>他把我胳膊拧得生疼，我只好认输让他赢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in which the child has to say the word ˈuncle</td><td>源自儿童游戏，认输者须喊叔叔</td><td>It comes from a game in which the child has to say the word uncle.<br>这个说法源自一种游戏，孩子必须喊出叔叔这个词。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>uncrowned</b></td><td>(be) the ˌuncrowned ˈking/queen (of sth)</td><td>无冕之王；某领域的头号人物</td><td>For twenty years she was the uncrowned queen of British crime writing.<br>二十年来她一直是英国犯罪小说的无冕之王。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>understanding</b></td><td>on the underˈstanding that... (formal)</td><td>在……的条件下；前提是</td><td>I lent him the car on the understanding that he would fill the tank.<br>我把车借给他，条件是他要把油加满。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>understood</b></td><td>ˌmake yourself underˈstood</td><td>把自己的意思说清楚</td><td>My Spanish is poor, but I can usually make myself understood in shops.<br>我西班牙语很差，但在商店里通常能把意思说清楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>undertone</b></td><td>in an ˈundertone • in ˈundertones</td><td>低声地；小声地</td><td>They discussed the bad news in an undertone so the children would not hear.<br>他们低声谈论那个坏消息，怕孩子们听见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>unearthly</b></td><td>at an unearthly/ungodly ˈhour</td><td>在极不合适的时间（尤指太早）</td><td>My flight leaves at some unearthly hour, so I will sleep at the airport.<br>我的航班时间早得离谱，我干脆在机场睡了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>unglued</b></td><td>come unˈglued (AmE, informal)</td><td>心烦意乱；崩溃；（计划）落空</td><td>He completely came unglued when he heard the verdict in court.<br>在法庭上听到判决时，他整个人崩溃了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ungodly</b></td><td>at an unearthly/ungodly ˈhour</td><td>在极不合适的时间；大清早</td><td>Who rings people at this ungodly hour on a Sunday morning?<br>谁会在周日大清早这种时候给人打电话？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>unison</b></td><td>in unison (with sb/sth)</td><td>一致；齐声；同步</td><td>The whole crowd shouted his name in unison as he walked onto the stage.<br>他走上台时，全场观众齐声喊他的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>unknown</b></td><td>an ˌunknown ˈquantity</td><td>未知数；不摸底的人或事</td><td>The new striker is still an unknown quantity in the Premier League.<br>这名新前锋在英超还是个未知数。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>unknown to sb</td><td>某人不知道地；瞒着某人</td><td>Unknown to his parents, he had already dropped out of university.<br>他父母毫不知情，其实他早就退学了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>unsound</b></td><td>of ˌunsound ˈmind (law)</td><td>精神失常（不负行为责任）</td><td>The court found that he was of unsound mind when the fire started.<br>法庭认定起火时他精神失常。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>unstuck</b></td><td>come unˈstuck (BrE, informal)</td><td>失败；出岔子</td><td>Their expansion plan came unstuck when the bank refused another loan.<br>银行拒绝再放贷，他们的扩张计划就此泡汤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>She came unstuck in the last part of the exam.</td><td>失败；栽跟头；出岔子</td><td>She came unstuck in the last part of the exam and lost thirty marks.<br>她在考试最后一部分栽了跟头，丢了三十分。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>untie</b></td><td>up for sth</td><td>乐意做某事；可供（出售等）</td><td>The old cottage is up for sale again after only six months.<br>那座老农舍才过半年就又挂牌出售了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>up ˈyours! (A, slang)</td><td>（愤怒的回应）去你的</td><td>When the boss told him to work Sunday, he just shouted up yours.<br>老板叫他周日加班，他直接吼了一句去你的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>uphill</b></td><td>an uphill ˈstruggle/ˈbattle/ˈtask</td><td>艰难的斗争；艰巨的任务</td><td>Getting teenagers to read books is an uphill struggle these days.<br>如今让青少年读书真是件难上加难的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>upon</b></td><td>(almost) uˈpon you (formal)</td><td>近在眼前；即将来临</td><td>The exam season is almost upon us and nobody has started revising.<br>考试季近在眼前，可谁都还没开始复习。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>upper</b></td><td>get, have, gain, etc. the ˌupper ˈhand (over sb)</td><td>占上风；取得控制权</td><td>By the second half our team had clearly gained the upper hand.<br>下半场我们队明显占了上风。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌupper ˈcrust (informal)</td><td>上层社会；上流阶层</td><td>The club was once reserved for the upper crust of London society.<br>这家俱乐部当年只对伦敦上流社会开放。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>uppers</b></td><td>on your ˈuppers (BrE, informal)</td><td>穷困潦倒；一贫如洗</td><td>He was on his uppers for a year before the new job came along.<br>找到新工作前，他潦倒了整整一年。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ups</b></td><td>ˌups and ˈdowns</td><td>起起伏伏；沉浮兴衰</td><td>Every long marriage has its ups and downs, and ours is no exception.<br>长久的婚姻都有起有落，我们也不例外。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>upset</b></td><td>upset the/sb's ˈapple cart (informal)</td><td>打乱计划；搅了局</td><td>Her sudden resignation really upset the apple cart just before the launch.<br>她突然辞职，把发布会前的安排全打乱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>uptake</b></td><td>be ˌquick/ˌslow on the ˈuptake (informal)</td><td>领悟得快；反应迟钝</td><td>Be patient with him, he is a bit slow on the uptake sometimes.<br>对他耐心点，他有时候反应是慢半拍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>use</b></td><td>be in/out of ˈuse</td><td>在使用中；已不再使用</td><td>That lift has been out of use since the flood last summer.<br>自从去年夏天发水，那部电梯就一直停用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be no ˈuse (to sb) (also be of no ˈuse formal)</td><td>对某人没有用处</td><td>A car is no use to me in a city with such good trains.<br>在火车这么方便的城市，车对我没什么用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be of ˈuse (to sb) (formal)</td><td>有用；有帮助</td><td>Please tell me if these old maps are of any use to you.<br>这些旧地图要是对你有用，就跟我说一声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come into/ˌgo out of ˈuse</td><td>开始使用；不再使用</td><td>Fax machines went out of use in our office years ago.<br>我们办公室的传真机好多年前就不用了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I, you, etc. could use a ˈdrink, etc. (spoken)</td><td>很想来一杯（等）；正需要</td><td>After that meeting I could really use a drink and a long walk.<br>开完那个会，我真想喝一杯，再好好走走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have no ˈuse for sb/sth</td><td>用不着；讨厌；瞧不上</td><td>I have no use for people who criticise but never offer any help.<br>我最烦那种只会批评、从不帮忙的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's no ˈuse (doing sth)</td><td>（做某事）没有用；没意义</td><td>It is no use arguing with him once he has made up his mind.<br>他一旦拿定主意，跟他争也没用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈuse of sb/sth</td><td>使用；利用</td><td>You should make use of the free gym while you still live here.<br>趁你还住这儿，该好好用用免费健身房。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sth to good ˈuse</td><td>好好利用；派上用场</td><td>She finally put her law degree to good use at the charity.<br>她终于在这家慈善机构把法律学位派上了用场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>use your ˈhead (BrE also use your ˈloaf) (informal)</td><td>动动脑子；好好想想</td><td>Use your head, you cannot post a parcel without a proper address.<br>动动脑子，没有详细地址怎么寄包裹？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>use a ˌsledgehammer to crack a ˈnut</td><td>小题大做；杀鸡用牛刀</td><td>Sending three lawyers over a parking fine is using a sledgehammer to crack a nut.<br>为张停车罚单派三个律师，纯属小题大做。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's the ˈuse (of doing sth)? (also what ˈuse is there (in doing sth)?)</td><td>（强调）有什么用呢</td><td>What is the use of saving money if you never enjoy any of it?<br>存钱要是从来不花，那有什么意义？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>useful</b></td><td>make yourself ˈuseful</td><td>帮把手；做点有用的事</td><td>Instead of watching me cook, make yourself useful and lay the table.<br>别光看我做饭，帮把手把桌子摆好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>uses</b></td><td>have your, his, its, etc. ˈuses (informal, often humorous)</td><td>有时还是挺有用的</td><td>My noisy old bicycle has its uses when the buses are on strike.<br>公交罢工时，我那辆破自行车还挺管用。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>usual</b></td><td>as ˈusual</td><td>像往常一样；照例</td><td>As usual, he arrived twenty minutes late and blamed the traffic.<br>照例，他晚到二十分钟，还怪路上堵车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>utmost</b></td><td>do/try your ˈutmost (to do sth)</td><td>竭尽全力（做某事）</td><td>The team did their utmost to finish the bridge before the rainy season.<br>施工队拼尽全力想在雨季前修完这座桥。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>vacuum</b></td><td>do sth in a ˈvacuum</td><td>脱离实际；孤立地做某事</td><td>Designers cannot work in a vacuum; they need feedback from real users.<br>设计师不能闭门造车，需要真实用户的反馈。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>vain</b></td><td>in ˈvain</td><td>徒劳；白费力气</td><td>We searched the whole beach in vain for her missing wedding ring.<br>我们把整片沙滩找遍了，还是没找到她丢的婚戒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>value</b></td><td>a value judgement (especially BrE) (AmE usu-</td><td>价值判断（凭主观意见的）</td><td>Calling the film immoral is a value judgement, not a piece of criticism.<br>说这部电影不道德是价值判断，算不上批评。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ally a ˈvalue judgment) (disapproving)</td><td>（根据主观意见的）价值判断</td><td>Try to describe what happened without making a value judgment about anyone.<br>尽量描述事情经过，别对任何人做价值判断。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb/sth at ˈface value</td><td>只看表面；信以为真</td><td>Do not take his promises at face value until you see a contract.<br>没看到合同之前，别把他的承诺当真。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>van</b></td><td>in the ˈvan (BrE, formal)</td><td>处于前列；处于领先地位</td><td>This small college has long been in the van of teaching reform.<br>这所小学院长期走在教学改革的前列。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>variance</b></td><td>at ˈvariance (with sb/sth) (formal)</td><td>不一致；有矛盾；相抵触</td><td>His account of the accident is at variance with what the witnesses said.<br>他对事故的说法与目击者所讲的不一致。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>variations</b></td><td>variations on the theme of sth</td><td>同一事物的不同做法或说法</td><td>Her three novels are really variations on the theme of leaving home.<br>她那三部小说其实都是离家主题的不同写法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>variety</b></td><td>variety is the spice of ˈlife (saying)</td><td>生活多变才有滋味</td><td>Try a different route to work sometimes; variety is the spice of life.<br>偶尔换条路上班，生活多变才有滋味。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>veil</b></td><td>cast/draw/throw a ˈveil over sth (written)</td><td>避而不谈；回避（不快之事）</td><td>Let us draw a veil over what happened at last year's office party.<br>去年公司聚会那档子事，咱们就不提了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>velvet</b></td><td>an ˌiron ˈfist/ˈhand (in a velvet glove)</td><td>外柔内刚；铁腕手段</td><td>She runs the department with an iron fist in a velvet glove.<br>她管理部门是笑里藏刀，手段其实很硬。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>vengeance</b></td><td>do sth with a ˈvengeance (informal)</td><td>猛烈地做；变本加厉地做</td><td>The rain came back with a vengeance just as we reached the tent.<br>我们刚回到帐篷，雨就又猛下起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>vent</b></td><td>give (full) ˈvent to sth (informal)</td><td>（尽情）发泄；抒发</td><td>He gave full vent to his anger once the customers had left.<br>客人一走，他就把火气全撒了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>vent your ˈspleen (literary)</td><td>发泄怒气；出气</td><td>She vented her spleen in a long email she later regretted sending.<br>她写了封长邮件泄愤，后来又后悔发了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ventured</b></td><td>nothing ˌventured, nothing ˈgained (saying)</td><td>不冒险就不会有收获</td><td>Apply for the scholarship anyway, nothing ventured, nothing gained.<br>奖学金还是申请一下吧，不试怎么知道。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>verge</b></td><td>on/to the verge of sth/of doing sth</td><td>濒于；行将；即将</td><td>The company was on the verge of collapse before the new investor arrived.<br>新投资人到来之前，这家公司濒临倒闭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>vested</b></td><td>have a vested ˈinterest (in sth)</td><td>有既得利益；从中获利</td><td>Oil companies have a vested interest in delaying stricter climate rules.<br>石油公司在拖延更严的气候法规上有既得利益。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>vexed</b></td><td>a vexed ˈquestion</td><td>棘手的问题；争论不休的问题</td><td>The vexed question of school funding came up again at the meeting.<br>学校经费这个老大难问题在会上又被提了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>vicious</b></td><td>a vicious ˈcircle</td><td>恶性循环</td><td>Debt and poor health can trap families in a vicious circle.<br>债务和健康不佳会让家庭陷入恶性循环。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>victim</b></td><td>fall ˈvictim (to sth) (written)</td><td>成为受害者；遭殃</td><td>Hundreds of small shops fell victim to the new shopping centre.<br>上百家小店都成了那家新购物中心的牺牲品。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>view</b></td><td>(have, etc. sth) in ˈview (formal)</td><td>心中有（目的、打算）</td><td>She bought the old barn with a small guesthouse in view.<br>她买下那座旧谷仓，心里打算开个小民宿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in view of sth</td><td>鉴于；考虑到；由于</td><td>In view of the weather, we have decided to postpone the picnic.<br>考虑到天气，我们决定把野餐推迟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on ˈview</td><td>在展出；陈列着</td><td>Her early sketches are on view at the museum until the end of May.<br>她的早期素描在博物馆展出到五月底。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a dim/poor ˈview of sb/sth</td><td>不赞同；不看好</td><td>My boss takes a dim view of people checking their phones in meetings.<br>我老板很不喜欢开会时有人看手机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the view (that) (formal)</td><td>认为；持……看法</td><td>The committee takes the view that the current rules are too strict.<br>委员会认为现行规定过于严苛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>villain</b></td><td>the ˈvillain of the piece (especially humorous)</td><td>罪魁祸首；症结所在</td><td>The villain of the piece turned out to be a faulty kitchen socket.<br>罪魁祸首原来是厨房里一个坏插座。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>virtue</b></td><td>by/in ˈvirtue of sth (formal)</td><td>由于；凭借；因为</td><td>She got the job by virtue of her long experience in the field.<br>她凭着在这行的多年经验拿到了这份工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make a ˌvirtue of neˈcessity</td><td>把不得已说成美德</td><td>With no car, he made a virtue of necessity and cycled everywhere.<br>没车，他索性顺水推舟，到哪儿都骑车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌvirtue is its own reˈward (saying)</td><td>为善本身就是回报</td><td>Nobody thanked her for helping, but virtue is its own reward.<br>没人谢她帮忙，可行善本身就是回报。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>vis-a-vis</b></td><td>vis-a-ˈvis (from French, written)</td><td>相对于；关于</td><td>What is our position vis-a-vis the new safety rules from Brussels?<br>就布鲁塞尔的新安全规定而言，我们是什么立场？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>voice</b></td><td>be in good, poor, etc. ˈvoice</td><td>嗓子状态好（或差等）</td><td>The tenor was in fine voice despite his terrible cold last night.<br>尽管重感冒，昨晚那位男高音的嗓子依然很棒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give ˈvoice to sth</td><td>表达；说出（想法、感受）</td><td>The report gives voice to workers who are rarely asked anything.<br>这份报告替那些很少被问及意见的工人发了声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep your ˈvoice down</td><td>说话小声点</td><td>Keep your voice down, the baby has only just fallen asleep.<br>小声点，宝宝刚睡着。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make your ˈvoice heard</td><td>让别人听到自己的意见</td><td>Parents marched to the town hall to make their voices heard.<br>家长们游行到市政厅，为的是让自己的声音被听见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a voice (crying) in the ˈwilderness</td><td>无人理会的呼声或警告</td><td>For years he was a voice in the wilderness warning about the dam.<br>多年来他关于大坝的警告一直无人理会。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with ˌone ˈvoice</td><td>异口同声；众口一词</td><td>The residents spoke with one voice against the new motorway plan.<br>居民们异口同声反对新的高速公路方案。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>volte-face</b></td><td>a volte-ˈface (from French, formal)</td><td>（意见或计划）大转变</td><td>The minister performed a complete volte-face on the tax proposal.<br>这位大臣在税收提案上来了个一百八十度大转弯。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>vote</b></td><td>put sth to the ˈvote</td><td>付诸表决</td><td>If we cannot agree, we will simply put the matter to the vote.<br>要是谈不拢，我们就直接把这事付诸表决。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌvote of ˈthanks</td><td>致谢词</td><td>The head teacher gave a short vote of thanks to all the volunteers.<br>校长向全体志愿者致了简短的谢词。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>vote with your ˈfeet</td><td>用脚投票；以离开表示不满</td><td>Customers voted with their feet when the shop raised its prices again.<br>店里又涨价，顾客们用脚投了票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wagon</b></td><td>be/go on the ˈwagon (informal)</td><td>戒酒；不再喝酒</td><td>He has been on the wagon since his doctor saw the test results.<br>自从医生看了化验结果，他就一直戒着酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>waifs</b></td><td>ˌwaifs and ˈstrays</td><td>无家可归者；流浪儿</td><td>She always collects waifs and strays and feeds them at Christmas.<br>她总把无家可归的人聚起来，圣诞节请他们吃饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wait</b></td><td>I, he, etc. can't ˈwait • I, he, etc. can</td><td>迫不及待；等不及了</td><td>I cannot wait to see their faces when we tell them the news.<br>我等不及想看他们听到消息时的表情。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hardly ˈwait</td><td>（我、他等）迫不及待</td><td>The children could hardly wait for the school holidays to begin.<br>孩子们盼着放假，一天也等不了了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌwait and ˈsee</td><td>等着瞧；耐心等待</td><td>We will just have to wait and see what the doctor says tomorrow.<br>我们只能等着瞧明天医生怎么说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wait for it (spoken, especially BrE)</td><td>稍等；（下文出人意料）听好了</td><td>He turned up late and, wait for it, asked us to pay for lunch.<br>他迟到了，你听好了，还让我们请他吃午饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wait a ˈminute/ˈmoment/ˈsecond</td><td>等一会儿；稍等一下</td><td>Wait a minute, I think we have taken the wrong turning again.<br>等一下，我觉得咱们又拐错弯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wait (on) ˈtables (AmE)</td><td>（在餐馆）当服务员</td><td>She waited tables at a diner while studying for her nursing degree.<br>她一边读护理学位，一边在小餐馆当服务员。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwait till/until... (spoken)</td><td>（兴奋地）等着，你就知道了</td><td>Wait till you taste my mother's dumplings, you will forget the restaurant.<br>等你尝了我妈包的饺子，就把饭馆忘了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(just) you ˈwait</td><td>（威胁或允诺）你就等着瞧吧</td><td>Just you wait, I will beat you at chess one of these days.<br>你等着瞧，总有一天我下棋能赢你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>waiting</b></td><td>an ˌaccident/a diˌsaster waiting to ˈhappen</td><td>迟早要出事的隐患</td><td>That broken staircase is an accident waiting to happen.<br>那段坏楼梯迟早要出事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep sb ˈwaiting</td><td>让某人等候</td><td>Sorry to keep you waiting, the earlier meeting ran on and on.<br>抱歉让你久等了，前一个会一直拖着没散。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈwaiting game</td><td>拖延战术；伺机而动</td><td>The buyers are playing a waiting game, hoping the price will drop.<br>买家在打拖延战，盼着价格降下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what are we ˈwaiting for? (spoken)</td><td>（建议动手）我们还等什么</td><td>The taxi is here and the tickets are booked, so what are we waiting for?<br>出租车到了，票也订好了，我们还等什么？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what are you ˈwaiting for? (spoken)</td><td>（催人行动）你还在等什么</td><td>The form takes five minutes, so what are you waiting for?<br>表格五分钟就填完了，你还在等什么？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wake</b></td><td>in the wake of sb/sth</td><td>紧随其后；作为……的结果</td><td>Food prices rose sharply in the wake of the summer drought.<br>夏季干旱之后，食品价格猛涨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wake the ˈdead</td><td>（噪音大得）能把死人吵醒</td><td>Turn that music down, it is loud enough to wake the dead.<br>把音乐关小点，吵得能把死人闹醒。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wake up and smell the ˈcoffee (AmE, informal)</td><td>认清现实；醒醒吧</td><td>Wake up and smell the coffee, nobody is going to fix this for you.<br>醒醒吧，没人会替你收拾这个烂摊子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wake-up</b></td><td>a ˈwake-up call</td><td>警钟；起警示作用的事件</td><td>His heart attack at forty was a real wake-up call for the whole family.<br>他四十岁心脏病发作，给全家敲响了警钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>walk</b></td><td>(try to) run before you can ˈwalk (informal)</td><td>还没学会走就想跑；急于求成</td><td>You are trying to run before you can walk with this business plan.<br>这份创业计划，你还没学会走就想跑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take a ˈwalk (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>（让人走开）走开；一边儿去</td><td>He kept bothering the waitress until the manager told him to take a walk.<br>他一直骚扰服务员，经理让他滚蛋。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>walk all ˈover sb (informal)</td><td>任意欺凌；对人苛刻</td><td>Do not let your new colleagues walk all over you like that.<br>别让新同事那样欺负你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>walk ˈfree</td><td>无罪释放；以自由之身离开法庭</td><td>Two of the accused walked free after the main witness changed her story.<br>主要证人改口后，两名被告被当庭释放。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a walk in the ˈpark (especially AmE)</td><td>轻而易举的事</td><td>After climbing that mountain, the morning run felt like a walk in the park.<br>爬完那座山，早上跑步简直不值一提。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwalk it (spoken)</td><td>轻易取胜；不费吹灰之力</td><td>With their best players back, our rivals will probably walk it this season.<br>主力都回来了，对手这赛季八成能轻松夺冠。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a walk of ˈlife</td><td>行业；职业；社会阶层</td><td>People from every walk of life turned up to support the campaign.<br>各行各业的人都来支持这场活动。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>walk off the job (AmE)</td><td>罢工；撂挑子</td><td>Three hundred drivers walked off the job over the new shift pattern.<br>三百名司机因新排班制度罢了工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>walk sb off their ˈfeet (informal)</td><td>让某人走得筋疲力尽</td><td>The guide walked us off our feet on the first day in Rome.<br>在罗马的头一天，导游就把我们走得腿都软了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>walk on ˈeggshells</td><td>小心翼翼；如履薄冰</td><td>Since the argument, everyone at home has been walking on eggshells.<br>那次争吵之后，家里人说话都小心翼翼。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>walk the ˈplank</td><td>走跳板受罚；被迫离职</td><td>Someone has to walk the plank for losing the biggest client.<br>丢了最大的客户，总得有人卷铺盖走人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>walk the ˈstreets</td><td>在街上闲逛；穿街走巷</td><td>He walked the streets for hours trying to clear his head.<br>他在街上转了好几个小时，想让脑子清静一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>walk ˈtall</td><td>昂首挺胸；感到自豪自信</td><td>After finishing the marathon she could finally walk tall again.<br>跑完马拉松，她终于又能昂首挺胸了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>walking</b></td><td>give sb their ˈwalking papers • get your a walking ˈdictionary, encycloˈpedia, etc.</td><td>活字典；活百科全书</td><td>Ask Priya about local history, she is a walking encyclopedia.<br>本地历史问普丽娅就行，她就是本活百科全书。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(informal)</td><td>活字典；活百科全书（指博学者）</td><td>My grandfather was a walking dictionary of old farming words.<br>我爷爷简直是一本关于旧时农事词汇的活字典。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be skating/walking on thin ˈice</td><td>如履薄冰；处境危险</td><td>Joking about the boss's divorce means you are skating on thin ice.<br>拿老板离婚的事开玩笑，你这是在冒险。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wall</b></td><td>drive/send sb up the ˈwall (informal)</td><td>把某人逼疯；使人抓狂</td><td>That dripping tap is driving me up the wall at night.<br>夜里那个滴水的龙头快把我逼疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go to the ˈwall (informal)</td><td>（因缺钱）垮台；破产</td><td>Several small bookshops went to the wall during the recession.<br>经济衰退期间，好几家小书店都倒闭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your ˈback to the wall</td><td>被逼到绝境；走投无路</td><td>With the rent due tomorrow, he really had his back to the wall.<br>房租明天就到期，他真是走投无路了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>off the ˈwall (informal)</td><td>古怪离奇；异想天开</td><td>Her ideas are a bit off the wall, but they often work.<br>她的点子有点古怪，可往往真管用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/come up against a brick ˈwall</td><td>碰壁；遇到难以逾越的障碍</td><td>We came up against a brick wall when we asked for the records.<br>我们要求查看记录时碰了一鼻子灰。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>walls</b></td><td>ˌwalls have ˈears (saying)</td><td>隔墙有耳</td><td>Keep your voice down in the corridor, walls have ears around here.<br>在走廊里小声点，这地方隔墙有耳。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wane</b></td><td>be on the ˈwane (written)</td><td>渐衰；减弱；衰落</td><td>Interest in the old festival has been on the wane for years.<br>人们对这个老节日的兴趣多年来一直在减退。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>want</b></td><td>for (the) want of sth</td><td>因为缺少；由于没有</td><td>The whole project failed for want of a few thousand pounds.<br>整个项目就因为缺那几千英镑而告吹。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in want of sth (formal)</td><td>需要；缺少</td><td>The old church roof is badly in want of repair before winter.<br>这座老教堂的屋顶入冬前急需修缮。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not want to ˈknow (about sth) (informal)</td><td>不想知道；不愿理会</td><td>I told him about the leak, but he just did not want to know.<br>我跟他说了漏水的事，他压根不想搭理。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>want for ˈnothing</td><td>什么都不缺；应有尽有</td><td>Their children want for nothing, yet they still seem unhappy.<br>他们的孩子什么都不缺，却似乎并不快乐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>want ˈrid of sb/sth (BrE, spoken, informal)</td><td>想摆脱；想甩掉</td><td>I want rid of that old sofa before the new one arrives.<br>新沙发到之前，我想把那张旧的处理掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>war</b></td><td>a ˌwar of ˈnerves</td><td>神经战；心理战</td><td>The two sides fought a war of nerves for weeks before signing.<br>签约前双方打了好几周的心理战。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌwar of ˈwords</td><td>舌战；论战</td><td>A bitter war of words broke out between the two candidates online.<br>两位候选人在网上展开了激烈的口水战。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>warm</b></td><td>keep sb's ˈseat, etc. warm (for them) (informal)</td><td>替某人暂时占位或代职</td><td>I am only keeping the chairman's seat warm until he returns.<br>我只是在主席回来之前替他暂时守着这个位子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(as) warm as ˈtoast</td><td>暖烘烘的</td><td>Under that thick duvet the children were as warm as toast.<br>盖着那床厚被子，孩子们暖烘烘的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>warm the ˈcockles (of sb's ˈheart) (BrE)</td><td>使人心里暖洋洋；令人欣慰</td><td>Seeing the neighbours help her move really warmed the cockles of my heart.<br>看到邻居帮她搬家，我心里暖烘烘的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>warpath</b></td><td>be/go on the ˈwarpath (informal)</td><td>怒气冲冲；准备兴师问罪</td><td>Look busy, the manager is on the warpath about the missing files.<br>装忙点，经理正为丢文件的事发火呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wars</b></td><td>in the ˈwars (spoken)</td><td>老是受点小伤；伤痕累累</td><td>Poor Tom has been in the wars again, that is his third bruise.<br>可怜的汤姆又挂彩了，这已经是第三处淤青。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>warts</b></td><td>warts and ˈall (informal)</td><td>缺点也不隐瞒；原原本本</td><td>The documentary shows the band warts and all, including the fights.<br>这部纪录片把乐队的一切都拍了，连争吵也不回避。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wash</b></td><td>it will (all) come out in the ˈwash (spoken)</td><td>事情终会解决；真相终会大白</td><td>Do not worry about the mix-up, it will all come out in the wash.<br>别为这场误会发愁，最后总会弄清楚的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wash your dirty linen in ˈpublic (BrE, disapproving)</td><td>家丑外扬；公开谈论私事</td><td>Posting about their divorce online is washing dirty linen in public.<br>把离婚的事发到网上，就是家丑外扬。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wash your ˈhands of sb/sth</td><td>不再过问；撇清关系</td><td>After the third warning, the school washed its hands of him.<br>第三次警告之后，学校就不管他了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>can't just wash my hands of the whole business.</td><td>撇清关系；不再过问</td><td>I cannot just wash my hands of the whole business, I signed the contract.<br>我不能说撇清就撇清，合同是我签的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sth won't/doesn't ˈwash (with sb)</td><td>（借口）站不住脚；说不过去</td><td>That excuse about the traffic will not wash with your teacher.<br>堵车这个借口在你老师那儿说不过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>waste</b></td><td>go/run to ˈwaste</td><td>白白浪费；荒废</td><td>Take the leftovers home so all this good food does not go to waste.<br>把剩菜带回家，别让这么好的东西白白糟蹋了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>waste your ˈbreath (on sb/sth)</td><td>白费口舌</td><td>Do not waste your breath arguing with him, he never changes his mind.<br>别白费口舌跟他争，他从不改主意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a waste of ˈspace (spoken)</td><td>废物；一无是处的人</td><td>He called the new intern a waste of space, which was unfair.<br>他说那个新实习生是废物，这话不公道。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>watch</b></td><td>be on the ˈwatch (for sb/sth)</td><td>留意；提防</td><td>Be on the watch for pickpockets around the station at night.<br>晚上在车站附近要提防扒手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep ˈwatch (for sb/sth)</td><td>守望；望风；警戒</td><td>You keep watch by the door while I look for the keys.<br>你在门口望风，我去找钥匙。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>watch the ˈclock (disapproving)</td><td>老看钟盼下班</td><td>Staff who watch the clock all afternoon rarely get promoted.<br>整个下午都盯着钟等下班的人很难升职。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwatch it (informal)</td><td>当心；留神</td><td>Watch it, that pan handle has been on the flame for ages.<br>当心，那锅把手在火上烤了半天了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>watch sb/sth like a ˈhawk</td><td>密切监视；紧盯不放</td><td>The examiner watched us like a hawk for the whole three hours.<br>监考老师整整三个小时都紧紧盯着我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>watch your ˈmouth/ˈtongue</td><td>说话注意点；管住嘴</td><td>Watch your mouth, my grandmother is sitting right behind you.<br>说话注意点，我奶奶就坐在你后面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>watch this ˈspace (informal)</td><td>关注后续；敬请留意</td><td>We cannot announce the venue yet, but watch this space.<br>场地还不能公布，请大家关注后续消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>watch the ˈworld go by keep a close ˈeye/ˈwatch on sb/sth</td><td>密切注意；照看好</td><td>Please keep a close eye on the soup while I answer the door.<br>我去开门，你帮我盯着点汤。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a watched pot never ˈboils (saying)</td><td>心急水不开；越盼越慢</td><td>Stop refreshing your inbox, a watched pot never boils.<br>别老刷邮箱了，越盯着越觉得慢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>Don't you know that a watched pot never boils?</td><td>越着急越觉得慢；心急水不开</td><td>Do not you know that a watched pot never boils? Go and read something.<br>你不知道越等越觉得慢吗？去看点书吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>water</b></td><td>be (like) water off a ˌduck's ˈback (informal)</td><td>（批评）像耳边风；毫不在意</td><td>Criticism from strangers is like water off a duck's back to her.<br>陌生人的批评对她来说就是耳边风。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be (all) water under the ˈbridge (spoken)</td><td>已成往事；都过去了</td><td>We argued a lot back then, but it is all water under the bridge now.<br>当年我们没少吵，但都是过去的事了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hold ˈwater (informal)</td><td>（理论等）站得住脚；经得起推敲</td><td>His alibi simply does not hold water once you check the times.<br>一核对时间，他的不在场证明就站不住脚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>like ˈwater (informal)</td><td>大量地；大手大脚地</td><td>He spends money like water whenever he goes back home for holidays.<br>他每次回家过节都花钱如流水。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>waters</b></td><td>waters</td><td>水域；（比喻）局面；处境</td><td>The company is heading into difficult waters with these new tariffs.<br>在这些新关税下，公司正驶入难以应付的水域。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(be in/get into) murky/uncharted ˈwaters</td><td>陷入未知或险恶的境地</td><td>Selling data to advertisers takes the app into murky waters legally.<br>把数据卖给广告商，这款应用在法律上进了灰色地带。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wave</b></td><td>wave a (magic) ˈwand (and do sth)</td><td>像变魔法一样解决问题</td><td>I cannot wave a magic wand and make your student debt disappear.<br>我又不能一挥魔杖就让你的助学贷款消失。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wavelength</b></td><td>be on the same ˈwavelength/on different</td><td>思路一致；想法合拍</td><td>My sister and I are on the same wavelength about almost everything.<br>我和我姐几乎在所有事情上都想到一块儿去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwavelengths (informal)</td><td>思路相同或不同；合拍与否</td><td>The two designers are clearly on different wavelengths about the colour scheme.<br>两位设计师在配色上明显不在一个频道上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>waves</b></td><td>make ˈwaves (informal)</td><td>兴风作浪；惹出事端</td><td>The new director likes to make waves in her first month.<br>这位新主管喜欢在上任头一个月就搅动一下局面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wax</b></td><td>ˌwax and ˈwane (literary)</td><td>盛衰交替；时增时减</td><td>Public interest in the scandal waxed and waned over several months.<br>几个月来，公众对这桩丑闻的兴趣时高时低。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wax ˈlyrical (about sth) (written)</td><td>兴致勃勃地大谈；盛赞</td><td>He waxed lyrical about the fish market for the entire train journey.<br>一路上他都在火车上眉飞色舞地大谈那个鱼市。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>way</b></td><td>across the ˈway (BrE also over the ˈway)</td><td>在（街道等的）对面</td><td>The family across the way have just bought a huge trampoline.<br>街对面那家人刚买了个巨大的蹦床。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>all the ˈway</td><td>一路上；自始至终；完全</td><td>She supported the project all the way, even when funding dried up.<br>她自始至终支持这个项目，连没钱的时候也是。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(that's/it's) always the ˈway (spoken)</td><td>老是这样；总是如此</td><td>The bus comes late when you are in a hurry, it is always the way.<br>你一赶时间公交就晚点，老是这样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>any way you ˈslice it (AmE, informal)</td><td>不管怎么看；无论如何</td><td>Any way you slice it, we are going to be short of money.<br>不管怎么算，我们的钱都不够。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be in a bad ˈway</td><td>情况很糟；病情严重</td><td>Her father is in a bad way after the second operation.<br>第二次手术之后，她父亲情况很不好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be on the way ˈout/ˈin</td><td>即将过时；正开始流行</td><td>Cash payments are on the way out in most of the city's cafes.<br>在这座城市多数咖啡馆，现金支付快要没人用了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be (well) on the/your way to/towards sth</td><td>即将实现；接近目标</td><td>With another win, they are well on their way to the final.<br>再赢一场，他们就基本上打进决赛了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈbe/be ˈborn/be ˈmade that way</td><td>（人）天性如此；生来就这样</td><td>He cannot help being blunt, he was just born that way.<br>他就是嘴直，天生这脾气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be underˈway</td><td>已经开始；正在进行中</td><td>Repairs on the bridge are already underway and should finish by autumn.<br>桥梁维修已经动工，预计秋天完工。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by the ˈway (also by the ˈby/ˈbye less frequent)</td><td>顺便说一句；附带问一句</td><td>By the way, did you ever return that book to the library?<br>顺便问一句，那本书你还给图书馆了吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come your ˈway</td><td>（机会等）落到你头上</td><td>Take the internship, chances like this do not come your way often.<br>接下这个实习吧，这种机会可不常有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth in a big/small ˈway</td><td>大张旗鼓地做；小打小闹地做</td><td>They celebrate birthdays in a big way, with fifty guests and a band.<br>他们过生日很铺张，请五十位客人还有乐队。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth on/along the ˈway</td><td>顺路做某事</td><td>I will pick up the dry cleaning on the way to the station.<br>我去车站的路上顺便取一下干洗的衣服。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈeither way • one way or the ˈother</td><td>两者都一样；不管怎样</td><td>We can drive or take the train, either way it takes three hours.<br>开车或坐火车都行，反正都要三小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>every ˈwhich way (informal)</td><td>四面八方；乱七八糟</td><td>When the alarm rang, people ran every which way across the car park.<br>警报一响，人们在停车场四散奔逃。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get in the ˈway (of sth)</td><td>妨碍；挡道</td><td>Do not let your phone get in the way of your revision tonight.<br>今晚别让手机耽误你复习。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get into/out of the way of sth/of doing sth</td><td>养成或改掉某种习惯</td><td>I have got into the way of walking to work every morning.<br>我已经养成了每天早上走路上班的习惯。</td></tr>
