<tr><td></td><td>get sth out of the ˈway</td><td>把某事处理掉；先解决掉</td><td>Let us get the paperwork out of the way before lunch.<br>咱们先把文书工作弄完再去吃午饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it/things/everything (all) your (own) ˈway</td><td>事事随心所欲；一切照自己的意思</td><td>You cannot always have everything your own way at work.<br>在单位你不可能事事都随自己的意思。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give ˈway</td><td>断裂；塌陷；垮掉</td><td>The old wooden balcony gave way under the weight of the guests.<br>客人一多，那个旧木阳台就塌了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give ˈway (to sb/sth)</td><td>让路；让步；被取代</td><td>Drivers must give way to cyclists at this junction.<br>在这个路口司机必须给骑车人让行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go all the ˈway (with sb) (informal)</td><td>完全赞同；与某人发生性关系</td><td>I go all the way with you on cutting the training budget.<br>在削减培训预算这件事上我完全同意你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go out of your ˈway (to do sth)</td><td>特意；不辞辛劳地</td><td>Our neighbours went out of their way to help us settle in.<br>邻居们特别费心帮我们安顿下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go your own ˈway</td><td>我行我素；一意孤行</td><td>He ignored all the advice and went his own way as usual.<br>他把所有建议都当耳旁风，照旧我行我素。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go sb's ˈway</td><td>与某人同路；（事情）合某人心意</td><td>Nothing went my way at all during that first month abroad.<br>刚出国那个月，什么事都不顺我的意。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go the way of all ˈflesh</td><td>走向人生终点；死亡</td><td>Even the greatest emperors go the way of all flesh in the end.<br>再伟大的帝王最后也难免一死。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a way of doing sth</td><td>往往会；总是这样</td><td>Problems have a way of solving themselves if you sleep on them.<br>很多问题搁一晚上往往就自己解决了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your (wicked) ˈway with sb (old-fashioned, humorous)</td><td>说服某人与自己发生性关系</td><td>In the film the count finally has his wicked way with the heroine.<br>电影里伯爵最终把女主角弄到了手。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in a ˈway • in ˈone way (also in ˈsome ways)</td><td>在某种程度上；从某方面说</td><td>In a way I am relieved that the whole thing is finally over.<br>从某种程度上说，这事总算结束了，我反而松了口气。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in his, her, its, etc. (own) ˈway</td><td>以其特有的方式</td><td>He is not romantic, but in his own way he is very caring.<br>他不浪漫，但用他自己的方式很体贴。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the/sb's ˈway</td><td>挡道；碍事</td><td>Those boxes are in the way, could you move them into the hall?<br>那些箱子挡道了，能搬到走廊去吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep/stay out of sb's ˈway</td><td>避开某人；躲着某人</td><td>Stay out of his way today, he lost a big client this morning.<br>今天躲着他点，他上午丢了个大客户。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look the other ˈway</td><td>视而不见；故意不管</td><td>Officials looked the other way while the factory dumped waste in the river.<br>工厂往河里排废水，官员们却装作没看见。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>lose your ˈway</td><td>迷路；迷失方向</td><td>We lost our way in the fog and ended up back at the car park.<br>我们在雾里迷了路，最后又转回了停车场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a lot, not much, etc. in the way of sth</td><td>（某物）不少；不多</td><td>The flat has a great view but not much in the way of storage.<br>这套公寓视野很好，但储物空间不多。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make ˈway (for sb/sth)</td><td>给……让路；腾出位置</td><td>The old market was demolished to make way for a car park.<br>老市场被拆掉，给停车场腾了地方。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make your ˈway (to/towards sth)</td><td>前往；走向</td><td>Please make your way to gate twelve, boarding starts in ten minutes.<br>请前往十二号登机口，十分钟后开始登机。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>make your ˈway in sth</td><td>（尤指事业上）闯出一片天</td><td>It is not easy to make your way in journalism without contacts.<br>没有人脉，在新闻界闯出名堂并不容易。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>my way or the ˈhighway (AmE, informal)</td><td>要么听我的，要么走人</td><td>With that coach it is always my way or the highway.<br>跟那个教练打交道，永远是要么听他的，要么走人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>no ˈway (informal)</td><td>不可能；决不；没门儿</td><td>No way am I lending him my car after what happened last time.<br>上次那事之后，我绝不会再把车借给他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not stand in sb's ˈway</td><td>不阻拦某人；不妨碍某人</td><td>If you really want to study abroad, I will not stand in your way.<br>你要是真想出国念书，我不会拦着你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(in) ˌone way and/or aˈnother/the ˈother</td><td>不管怎样；总有办法</td><td>One way or another, we will get the money together before Friday.<br>不管想什么办法，周五前我们都会把钱凑齐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on your/the/its ˈway</td><td>在路上；就要来了</td><td>The ambulance is on its way and should be here in five minutes.<br>救护车已经在路上，五分钟内应该就到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌother way aˈround/round</td><td>反过来；恰恰相反</td><td>She did not leave him, it was actually the other way around.<br>不是她甩了他，其实正相反。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of the ˈway</td><td>不再碍事；已经处理完</td><td>Once the exams are out of the way we can plan the trip.<br>等考完试没这事儿了，我们就能计划旅行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of your ˈway</td><td>不顺路；偏离既定路线</td><td>Dropping me home is completely out of your way, I will take the bus.<br>送我回家太绕路了，我坐公交就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see your ˈway (ˈclear) to doing sth</td><td>觉得能够做；方便做某事</td><td>If you could see your way clear to lending us the hall, we would be grateful.<br>您要是方便把礼堂借给我们，我们感激不尽。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see which way the ˈwind blows</td><td>观望形势；看风向</td><td>He is waiting to see which way the wind blows before choosing sides.<br>他在观望风向，然后再决定站哪边。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's the ˈway (informal)</td><td>（表示赞同）就是这样；对了</td><td>Keep your elbow down when you swing, that is the way.<br>挥杆时胳膊肘放低，对，就这样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>that's the way the cookie ˈcrumbles (also that's the way it ˈgoes) (informal)</td><td>情况就是这样，没别的办法</td><td>We lost the contract by one point, but that is the way the cookie crumbles.<br>就差一分丢了合同，可事情就是这样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>there's more than ˈone way to skin a ˈcat</td><td>办法不止一个；条条大路通罗马</td><td>If the front door is locked, remember there is more than one way to skin a cat.<br>前门锁了也没事，办法总不止一个。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>to ˈmy, ˈyour, etc. way of thinking</td><td>依我看；照某人的看法</td><td>To my way of thinking, we should fix the roof before buying furniture.<br>依我看，先修屋顶再买家具。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈway back (informal)</td><td>很久以前</td><td>We first met way back when we were both working night shifts.<br>我们初次见面还是很久以前一起上夜班的时候。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the/sb's way of ˈlife</td><td>生活方式；行为方式</td><td>Fishing is not just a job here, it is a whole way of life.<br>在这儿捕鱼不只是工作，而是一整套生活方式。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌway of the ˈworld</td><td>世道常情；事情的常理</td><td>The rich get the best seats, and sadly that is the way of the world.<br>好位子都归有钱人，可惜世道就是如此。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>way to ˈgo! (AmE, informal, spoken)</td><td>干得好；真棒</td><td>You finished the whole race in the rain? Way to go!<br>下着雨你还跑完了全程？干得漂亮！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the way to sb's ˈheart</td><td>赢得某人喜爱的办法</td><td>Home-made soup is definitely the way to my father's heart.<br>自家熬的汤绝对是讨我爸欢心的法宝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>work, etc. your way through sth</td><td>从头到尾做完；逐一处理</td><td>She worked her way through a pile of marking before midnight.<br>她在午夜前把一摞作业全批完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>eating his way through all the restaurants that ˌwork your way through ˈcollege, etc.</td><td>勤工俭学；半工半读</td><td>She worked her way through college by waiting tables at weekends.<br>她靠周末端盘子挣钱读完了大学。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌwork your way ˈup</td><td>从底层做起，步步高升</td><td>He worked his way up from cleaner to head of the department.<br>他从清洁工一路干到了部门主管。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>way out of a paper bag</td><td>极其无能；一点本事也没有</td><td>He could not fight his way out of a paper bag, let alone win the title.<br>他连个纸袋都打不破，更别说夺冠了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ways</b></td><td>be ˌset in your ˈways</td><td>墨守成规；固执己见</td><td>Grandad is too set in his ways to try a new phone.<br>爷爷太固执了，新手机说什么也不肯试。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you, etc. can't have it ˈboth ways</td><td>不可能两全其美</td><td>You cannot have it both ways, either you save or you travel.<br>鱼与熊掌不可兼得，要么存钱，要么旅行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>cut both/two ˈways</td><td>有利也有弊；是把双刃剑</td><td>Working from home cuts both ways: more freedom, but far more distractions.<br>居家办公是双刃剑：更自由，但也更分心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˌmore ways than ˈone</td><td>不止一层意思；在好几方面</td><td>Moving to the coast changed our lives in more ways than one.<br>搬到海边从好几方面改变了我们的生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌways and ˈmeans</td><td>方法和手段；门路</td><td>There are ways and means of getting tickets if you know the right people.<br>只要认识人，弄到票总有门路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wayside</b></td><td>fall by the ˈwayside</td><td>半途而废；被淘汰</td><td>Half the class started Japanese, but most fell by the wayside by March.<br>班上一半人开始学日语，三月前大都半途而废了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ORIGIN</td><td>词源说明（本书标注习语来源）</td><td>The ORIGIN note says the seed that fell by the wayside never grew.<br>词源说明指出，落在路旁的种子没有发芽。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌout/ˌup the waˈzoo (AmE, slang)</td><td>大量的；多得很</td><td>The new phone has features up the wazoo that nobody ever uses.<br>这款新手机功能多得要命，可根本没人用。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>weak</b></td><td>be/go ˌweak at the ˈknees (informal)</td><td>（因激动、疾病等）两腿发软</td><td>One look from him and she went weak at the knees.<br>他一个眼神就让她腿都软了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the weak ˈlink (in the ˈchain)</td><td>薄弱环节</td><td>Our defence is still the weak link in the chain this season.<br>这个赛季我们的防守仍然是最薄弱的一环。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a weak ˈmoment • a moment of ˈweakness</td><td>一时心软；意志薄弱的时候</td><td>In a weak moment I agreed to look after their three dogs.<br>我一时心软，答应帮他们照看三条狗。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wear</b></td><td>ˌwear and ˈtear</td><td>（正常使用造成的）磨损</td><td>The deposit covers damage but not normal wear and tear.<br>押金赔的是损坏，不包括正常磨损。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wear your ˌheart on your ˈsleeve</td><td>感情外露；喜怒形于色</td><td>He wears his heart on his sleeve, so you always know his mood.<br>他喜怒都写在脸上，心情如何一看便知。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wear ˈthin</td><td>（耐心）快耗尽；（借口）不管用</td><td>His excuses about the traffic are starting to wear a bit thin.<br>他那套堵车的借口越来越说不过去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wear the ˈtrousers (BrE) (AmE wear the ˈpants) (often disapproving)</td><td>（在家中）当家作主</td><td>Everyone knows who wears the trousers in that household.<br>谁都知道那家里是谁说了算。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>weather</b></td><td>keep a ˈweather eye on sth/open for sth</td><td>随时留意；小心提防</td><td>Keep a weather eye on the forecast before we set off tomorrow.<br>明天出发前留意一下天气预报。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>under the ˈweather (informal)</td><td>身体不适；情绪欠佳</td><td>I am feeling a bit under the weather, so I will skip dinner.<br>我有点不舒服，晚饭就不去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>weathers</b></td><td>in ˈall weathers (BrE)</td><td>不论天气好坏；风雨无阻</td><td>The postman cycles up that hill in all weathers.<br>不管什么天气，邮递员都骑车上那个坡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>weave</b></td><td>weave your ˈmagic • weave a ˈspell (over sb) (especially BrE)</td><td>表现出色令人入迷；施展魅力</td><td>The old pianist wove his magic over the audience for two hours.<br>那位老钢琴家让全场听众入迷了两个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wedding</b></td><td>a monkey's ˈwedding</td><td>（南非）太阳雨，晴天下雨</td><td>The children ran outside laughing at the monkey's wedding that afternoon.<br>那天下午下起太阳雨，孩子们笑着跑到外面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>week</b></td><td>ˌweek after ˈweek (informal)</td><td>一周又一周；一连数周</td><td>Week after week he sent applications and heard nothing back.<br>他一周又一周地投简历，却没有任何回音。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌweek by ˈweek</td><td>一周接一周；逐周</td><td>Week by week her Chinese improved until she could argue in it.<br>她的中文一周比一周好，最后都能用中文吵架了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>week ˌin, week ˈout</td><td>每星期都如此；周复一周</td><td>He drives two hundred miles week in, week out to see his mother.<br>他周复一周开两百英里去看母亲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌweek toˈmorrow, on ˈMonday, etc. (BrE)</td><td>一星期后的明天（或周一等）</td><td>Our exams start a week tomorrow, so revision begins tonight.<br>考试从下周的明天开始，所以今晚就得复习。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(also a ˌweek from toˈmorrow, ˈMonday, etc. AmE, BrE)</td><td>一星期后的明天（或周一等）</td><td>The lease ends a week from Monday, so we must pack soon.<br>租约到下下周一就到期，我们得赶紧收拾。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌweek ˈyesterday, last ˈMonday, etc. (especially BrE)</td><td>一星期前的昨天（或周一等）</td><td>They moved out a week yesterday and left the keys with me.<br>他们上周的昨天搬走了，钥匙留给了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>weigh</b></td><td>weigh ˈanchor</td><td>起锚；启航</td><td>The ferry weighed anchor just as the storm clouds appeared.<br>乌云刚一出现，渡轮就起锚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>weigh on your ˈmind</td><td>压在心头；成为负担</td><td>The unpaid bills have been weighing on my mind for weeks.<br>那些没付的账单压在我心头好几周了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>weigh (half) a ˈton (informal)</td><td>非常重</td><td>Careful with that suitcase, it weighs half a ton.<br>小心那个行李箱，重得要命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>weigh your ˈwords</td><td>斟酌词句；说话谨慎</td><td>She weighed her words carefully before replying to the journalist.<br>回答记者之前，她仔细斟酌了措辞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>weight</b></td><td>be a ˌweight off your ˈshoulders</td><td>卸下重担；如释重负</td><td>Handing in that thesis was a huge weight off my shoulders.<br>交上论文那一刻，我如释重负。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put/throw your weight behind sth</td><td>全力支持；鼎力相助</td><td>The mayor threw her weight behind the campaign to save the library.<br>市长全力支持了保住图书馆的活动。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈweight off your feet (informal)</td><td>坐下歇歇脚</td><td>Come in and take the weight off your feet, the kettle is on.<br>进来坐下歇歇脚，水正烧着呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>throw your ˈweight about/around (informal)</td><td>仗势欺人；耀武扬威</td><td>The new supervisor started throwing his weight around on day one.<br>新主管上任第一天就开始耀武扬威。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>weight of ˈnumbers</td><td>人多势众；靠人数取胜</td><td>The protesters won by sheer weight of numbers rather than argument.<br>抗议者靠的是人多势众，而不是道理。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>weird</b></td><td>weird and wonderful</td><td>稀奇古怪而有趣</td><td>The market sells all sorts of weird and wonderful kitchen gadgets.<br>这个市场卖各种稀奇古怪的厨房小工具。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>welcome</b></td><td>lay, put, roll, etc. out the ˈwelcome mat</td><td>热情迎客；设法吸引来访者</td><td>The village rolled out the welcome mat for the returning team.<br>全村热情迎接凯旋的球队。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>outstay/overstay your ˈwelcome</td><td>逗留过久而惹人厌</td><td>They stayed three weeks and definitely outstayed their welcome.<br>他们住了三个星期，实在是待得太久招人烦了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you're ˈwelcome (especially AmE)</td><td>不用谢；别客气</td><td>You are welcome, it was really no trouble at all to help.<br>不用谢，帮这点忙一点儿也不麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>well</b></td><td>ˌall being ˈwell</td><td>如果一切顺利</td><td>All being well, we should reach the campsite before dark.<br>一切顺利的话，我们天黑前能到营地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌall very ˈwell/fine (for sb) (to do sth) but...</td><td>（批评或反驳）说来容易，可是</td><td>It is all very well telling me to relax, but I have four children.<br>叫我放松说得轻巧，可我有四个孩子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>all well and ˈgood (informal)</td><td>固然好（但不尽如人意）</td><td>A pay rise is all well and good, but we also need shorter hours.<br>加薪固然好，可我们还需要缩短工时。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>all's well that ˈends well (saying)</td><td>结局好，一切都好</td><td>We missed the ferry but caught a better one; all's well that ends well.<br>我们错过了渡轮却赶上更好的一班，结局好就都好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>as well (as sb/sth)</td><td>除……之外也；还</td><td>She speaks Arabic as well as French and a little Portuguese.<br>她除法语外还会阿拉伯语，还懂点葡萄牙语。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>She's a talented musician as well as being a be (just) as ˈwell (to do sth)</td><td>还是……为好；不妨</td><td>It is just as well to book a table before the match starts.<br>比赛开始前还是先订个位子为好。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be doing ˈwell</td><td>（病后）恢复良好；进展顺利</td><td>Mother and baby are both doing well after a long night.<br>熬了一整夜，母子都恢复得不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌwell aˈware of sth • be ˌwell aˌware</td><td>十分清楚；深知</td><td>I am well aware of the risks, but I still want to try.<br>这些风险我很清楚，可我还是想试。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˈwell away (BrE, informal)</td><td>进展顺利；大有进步</td><td>Once he found a decent editor, he was well away with the novel.<br>找到一位好编辑后，他的小说就写得顺风顺水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌwell ˈin (with sb) (informal)</td><td>与（要人）关系密切；过往甚密</td><td>She is well in with the people who decide the funding.<br>她跟决定拨款的那些人关系很铁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌwell ˈoff</td><td>有钱；富裕</td><td>His grandparents were well off, but he never took a penny.<br>他祖父母很有钱，可他一分也没要过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be well ˈoff for sth</td><td>某物很充足；不缺</td><td>We are well off for blankets, so bring your own pillow instead.<br>我们毯子很多，你带个枕头就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌwell ˈout of sth (BrE, informal)</td><td>幸好没卷入；幸而无关</td><td>Given how that project ended, you are well out of it.<br>那个项目落得那种下场，你幸好没掺和。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be ˌwell ˈup on sth</td><td>精通；熟悉</td><td>Ask Meera, she is well up on the new tax rules.<br>问米拉吧，她对新税规很熟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do ˈwell</td><td>做得好；进展顺利；成功</td><td>Her small bakery has done well since the new estate was built.<br>新小区建好后，她那家小面包房生意一直不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwell by sb</td><td>待某人不薄；善待某人</td><td>The company has done well by its long-serving staff over the years.<br>这些年公司待老员工一直不薄。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwell for yourself</td><td>混得不错；发了财</td><td>He has done well for himself since he moved to Singapore.<br>搬到新加坡以后他混得相当不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwell out of sb/sth</td><td>从中获利；靠……赚了钱</td><td>The estate agents did very well out of the housing boom.<br>房地产中介靠这波楼市大涨赚了不少。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwell to do sth</td><td>最好做某事；做……才明智</td><td>You would do well to keep a copy of that email.<br>你最好把那封邮件留个备份。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>hanged/hung for a sheep as (for) a ˈlamb</td><td>一不做二不休；反正都要受罚</td><td>We have broken the diet already, so hanged for a sheep as a lamb.<br>反正减肥计划已经破了，索性一不做二不休。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>only too ˈwell</td><td>太清楚了；深有体会</td><td>I know only too well how hard the first year of teaching is.<br>头一年教书有多难，我太清楚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>very ˈwell (BrE, formal)</td><td>（勉强接受）好吧；可以</td><td>Very well, we will postpone the decision until the next meeting.<br>好吧，这个决定推迟到下次会议再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌwell and ˈtruly (informal)</td><td>彻底地；完全地</td><td>By the time we found the path, we were well and truly lost.<br>等找到那条小路时，我们已经彻底迷路了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>well ˈsaid! (spoken)</td><td>说得好；我完全同意</td><td>Well said! Somebody finally told the committee the truth.<br>说得好！总算有人跟委员会说了实话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wet</b></td><td>all ˈwet (AmE, informal)</td><td>完全错了；大错特错</td><td>If you think the deal is safe, you are all wet.<br>你要是觉得这笔交易稳当，那就大错特错了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wet the baby’s ˈhead (informal)</td><td>喝酒庆祝婴儿降生</td><td>The new father took us to the pub to wet the baby's head.<br>这位新爸爸带我们去酒吧喝酒庆祝孩子出生。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wet the/your ˈbed</td><td>尿床</td><td>He still wets the bed occasionally when he is anxious about school.<br>他一为上学的事紧张，偶尔还会尿床。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(still) ˌwet behind the ˈears (informal, disapproving)</td><td>乳臭未干；少不更事</td><td>That reporter is still wet behind the ears but asks sharp questions.<br>那个记者还嫩着呢，可问题问得挺尖锐。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌwet ˈblanket (informal, disapproving)</td><td>泼冷水的人；扫兴之人</td><td>Do not be such a wet blanket, everyone else wants to dance.<br>别这么扫兴，别人都想跳舞。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wet your ˈwhistle (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>喝一杯；润润喉咙</td><td>Come inside and wet your whistle before the second half starts.<br>下半场开始前先进来喝一杯润润嗓子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwet yourself • wet your ˈpants/ˈknickers</td><td>尿裤子</td><td>The children laughed so hard that the youngest nearly wet herself.<br>孩子们笑得太厉害，最小的那个差点尿了裤子。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get your ˈfeet wet</td><td>初步尝试；开始入门</td><td>Volunteer at the clinic to get your feet wet before applying properly.<br>正式申请前先去诊所做志愿者，试试水。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whack</b></td><td>out of ˈwhack (informal, especially AmE)</td><td>不对头；失调；不一致</td><td>The office thermostat is out of whack again, so bring a jumper.<br>办公室的温控器又不好使了，带件毛衣来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whale</b></td><td>have a ˈwhale of a time (informal)</td><td>玩得非常痛快</td><td>The kids had a whale of a time at the water park yesterday.<br>孩子们昨天在水上乐园玩得特别开心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whammy</b></td><td>a double ˈwhammy</td><td>双重打击</td><td>Rising rent and a pay freeze were a double whammy for young staff.<br>房租上涨加上工资冻结，对年轻员工是双重打击。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>what</b></td><td>and ˈwhat not • and what ˈhave you (informal)</td><td>诸如此类；以及其他类似的东西</td><td>The drawer is full of chargers, old keys and what have you.<br>抽屉里塞满了充电器、旧钥匙之类的东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/get what ˈfor (BrE, spoken)</td><td>痛骂某人；挨一顿骂</td><td>My mother gave me what for when she saw the broken window.<br>我妈看见碎玻璃窗，把我骂了个狗血淋头。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>so ˈwhat? (spoken)</td><td>那又怎样（表示不在乎）</td><td>So what if he disagrees? We still have enough votes to pass it.<br>他不同意又怎样？我们的票数照样够。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwhat-d’you-call-him/-her/-it/-them • what's ˈup? (informal)</td><td>那个什么（想不起名称）；怎么了</td><td>Pass me the what-d'you-call-it, the thing for opening wine bottles.<br>把那个什么递给我，就是开红酒瓶的那个东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's with sth? (AmE, spoken)</td><td>（问原因）怎么回事；为什么</td><td>What is with all these boxes in the hallway this morning?<br>今天早上走廊里这么多箱子是怎么回事？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what's ˈyours? (informal)</td><td>（酒吧里问）你想喝点什么</td><td>I am going to the bar now, so what is yours?<br>我这就去吧台，你想喝点什么？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whatever</b></td><td>or whatˈever (spoken)</td><td>或诸如此类；或别的什么</td><td>Bring a salad or some bread or whatever, it does not matter.<br>带个沙拉、面包或者别的什么都行，无所谓。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>whatˈever you do</td><td>（警告）无论如何都别</td><td>Whatever you do, do not mention her ex-husband at dinner tonight.<br>今晚吃饭时无论如何别提她前夫。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wheat</b></td><td>sort out/separate the ˌwheat from the ˈchaff</td><td>识别优劣；去芜存菁</td><td>A tough audition sorts the wheat from the chaff among young dancers.<br>严格的试镜能在年轻舞者中筛出真正的好苗子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wheel</b></td><td>at/behind the ˈwheel (of sth)</td><td>开车；驾驶；掌管</td><td>He fell asleep at the wheel and drove straight into a ditch.<br>他开车时睡着了，径直冲进了沟里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a fifth/third ˈwheel (AmE)</td><td>多余的人；累赘</td><td>Going to the movies with those two made me feel like a fifth wheel.<br>跟他们俩一起去看电影，让我觉得自己是个多余的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈwheel</td><td>接过方向盘；接替驾驶</td><td>You look exhausted — let me take the wheel for the next hundred miles.<br>你看着累坏了，接下来一百英里让我来开吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌwheel and ˈdeal (disapproving)</td><td>（在商界或政界）玩弄手段做交易</td><td>He spent years wheeling and dealing in property before the market collapsed.<br>他在房地产界投机钻营多年，直到市场崩盘。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌwheeler-ˈdealer noun</td><td>投机钻营者；玩弄手段的人</td><td>The company was founded by a wheeler-dealer who never took no for an answer.<br>这家公司是一个从不接受拒绝的投机高手创立的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌwheel has come/turned full ˈcircle</td><td>兜了一圈又回到原点；轮回</td><td>Vinyl records are selling well again — the wheel has come full circle.<br>黑胶唱片又好卖了，真是兜了一圈回到原点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wheels</b></td><td>(there are) ˌwheels within ˈwheels</td><td>错综复杂；盘根错节</td><td>Don't expect a simple answer; in this office there are wheels within wheels.<br>别指望有简单答案，这个办公室里的事盘根错节。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>where</b></td><td>where it's ˈat (informal)</td><td>（某领域的）中心；最热门之处</td><td>For live jazz in this city, that little basement bar is where it's at.<br>在这座城市听现场爵士，那家地下小酒吧才是最棒的去处。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wherefores</b></td><td>the ˌwhys and (the) ˈwherefores (of sth)</td><td>来龙去脉；前因后果</td><td>I don't need the whys and the wherefores of the delay, just a new date.<br>我不用知道延误的来龙去脉，给我个新日期就行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whet</b></td><td>whet sb's ˈappetite</td><td>引起某人的兴趣；吊胃口</td><td>The trailer really whetted my appetite for the film coming out next month.<br>预告片真把我对下个月上映那部电影的胃口吊起来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>which</b></td><td>which is ˈwhich</td><td>哪个是哪个</td><td>The twins dress identically, so I can never tell which is which.<br>这对双胞胎穿得一模一样，我从来分不清哪个是哪个。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whip</b></td><td>get, have, hold, etc. the ˈwhip hand (over sb)</td><td>占上风；控制（某人）</td><td>Now that she owns most of the shares, she has the whip hand over the board.<br>如今她持有大部分股份，在董事会里占了上风。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whipped</b></td><td>like a whipped ˈdog</td><td>（因失败或受罚）显得羞愧沮丧</td><td>He slunk back into the meeting like a whipped dog after his idea was rejected.<br>提议被否决后，他像条挨了打的狗一样溜回会议室。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whipping</b></td><td>a ˈwhipping boy</td><td>替罪羊；代人受过者</td><td>The junior staff became the whipping boy for every mistake the manager made.<br>经理犯的每个错都由初级员工来当替罪羊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whirl</b></td><td>give sth a ˈwhirl (informal)</td><td>试一试</td><td>I've never skated before, but I'll give it a whirl.<br>我从没滑过冰，不过我可以试一试。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in a ˈwhirl</td><td>晕头转向；心烦意乱</td><td>After three job offers in one week, my head was in a whirl.<br>一周内接到三份工作邀约，我脑子都晕了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whisker</b></td><td>be, come, etc. within a ˈwhisker of sth/of doing sth</td><td>差一点就；几乎</td><td>She came within a whisker of winning the race, losing by half a second.<br>她差一点就赢了比赛，仅以半秒之差落败。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth by a ˈwhisker (informal)</td><td>以毫厘之差做成某事</td><td>They won the election by a whisker after a recount of every ballot.<br>重新清点全部选票后，他们以毫厘之差赢得选举。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whistle</b></td><td>You, etc. can ˈwhistle for it (BrE, spoken)</td><td>休想得到；别想</td><td>If he wants his deposit back, he can whistle for it.<br>他要是想把押金要回去，那就休想。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>whistle in the ˈdark</td><td>故作镇静；给自己壮胆</td><td>Saying the company will recover next quarter is just whistling in the dark.<br>说公司下季度就能恢复，不过是自己壮胆罢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whistle-stop</b></td><td>a ˌwhistle-stop ˈtour</td><td>走马观花式的巡回访问</td><td>The minister made a whistle-stop tour of five factories in one afternoon.<br>部长一个下午走马观花地视察了五家工厂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whit</b></td><td>not a/one ˈwhit (old-fashioned)</td><td>丝毫不；一点也不</td><td>His confidence was not a whit shaken by the crowd's booing.<br>观众的嘘声丝毫没有动摇他的自信。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>white</b></td><td>(as) ˌwhite as a ˈsheet/ˈghost (informal)</td><td>脸色苍白</td><td>She came out of the doctor's office as white as a sheet.<br>她从医生办公室出来时脸色惨白。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a white ˈChristmas</td><td>白色圣诞节（下雪的圣诞节）</td><td>The kids are praying for snow so we finally get a white Christmas.<br>孩子们盼着下雪，好让我们终于过个白色圣诞节。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a white ˈelephant</td><td>昂贵而无用的东西；累赘</td><td>The new stadium has become a white elephant the city cannot afford.<br>这座新体育场成了这座城市负担不起的昂贵累赘。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a white ˈlie</td><td>善意的谎言</td><td>I told a white lie and said her new haircut looked great.<br>我撒了个善意的谎，说她的新发型很好看。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whiter</b></td><td>ˌwhiter than ˈwhite</td><td>清白无瑕；品行高尚</td><td>No politician in this scandal is whiter than white, whatever they claim.<br>这桩丑闻里没有哪个政客是清白的，不管他们怎么说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>white-van</b></td><td>ˌwhite-ˈvan man (BrE, informal)</td><td>粗野的货车司机</td><td>A white-van man cut me off at the roundabout and then swore at me.<br>一个开白色货车的莽汉在环岛抢我的道，还骂了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whizz-kid</b></td><td>a ˈwhizz-kid (also ˈwhiz-kid) (informal)</td><td>神童；年轻有为者</td><td>They hired a twenty-three-year-old whizz-kid to run the whole trading desk.<br>他们请了个二十三岁的神童来管理整个交易部门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>who</b></td><td>who am ˈI, are ˈyou, etc. to do sth?</td><td>某人有什么资格做某事</td><td>Who am I to tell her how to raise her own children?<br>我有什么资格教她怎么带自己的孩子？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>who's ˈwho</td><td>谁是谁；各人的身份情况</td><td>Give me a minute at the party to work out who's who.<br>在派对上给我点时间，好搞清楚谁是谁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whole</b></td><td>as a ˈwhole</td><td>总体而言；作为整体</td><td>The team played badly, but as a whole the season was a success.<br>球队打得不好，但总体而言这个赛季是成功的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈwhole</td><td>总的来说；大体上</td><td>On the whole, I'd rather spend the holiday at home than fly anywhere.<br>总的来说，假期我宁愿待在家里，也不想飞去哪儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈwhole lot (informal)</td><td>非常；……得多</td><td>This coffee tastes a whole lot better than the stuff at the office.<br>这咖啡比办公室里那种好喝多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈwhole lot (of sth) (informal)</td><td>大量；许许多多</td><td>We wasted a whole lot of money on furniture we never actually used.<br>我们在从没真正用过的家具上浪费了一大笔钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌwhole ˈlot</td><td>全部；所有</td><td>He ate the whole lot before anyone else got to the table.<br>别人还没上桌，他就把全部吃光了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whoop</b></td><td>ˌwhoop it ˈup (informal)</td><td>狂欢作乐；尽情欢闹</td><td>They were whooping it up downstairs until three in the morning.<br>他们在楼下狂欢作乐，一直闹到凌晨三点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whoopee</b></td><td>make ˈwhoopee (old-fashioned, informal)</td><td>狂欢；庆祝</td><td>The whole village made whoopee when the team finally won the cup.<br>球队终于捧杯时，全村人都狂欢庆祝。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>why</b></td><td>why ˈever...?</td><td>究竟为什么</td><td>Why ever did you tell him about the surprise party?<br>你究竟为什么要把惊喜派对的事告诉他？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>why ˈnot? (informal)</td><td>为什么不呢；好啊</td><td>A weekend in the mountains? Why not? I could use the fresh air.<br>去山里过周末？好啊，我正需要点新鲜空气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whys</b></td><td>the ˌwhys and (the) ˈwherefores (of sth)</td><td>原因；理由；缘故</td><td>Nobody explained the whys and the wherefores of the sudden policy change.<br>没人解释政策突然改变的原因和缘由。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wick</b></td><td>get on sb's ˈwick (BrE, informal)</td><td>惹恼某人；招惹某人</td><td>His constant humming really gets on my wick during meetings.<br>他开会时不停哼歌，真让我恼火。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wicked</b></td><td>there's no peace/rest for the ˈwicked (usually humorous)</td><td>恶人一刻不得闲（抱怨活太多）</td><td>Another late shift tonight — there's no rest for the wicked, I suppose.<br>今晚又要上晚班，看来是恶人一刻不得闲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wide</b></td><td>be/fall wide of the ˈmark (also be (a long) way off the ˈmark)</td><td>远离目标；不准确；离谱</td><td>Their sales forecast for the year turned out to be wide of the mark.<br>他们对全年销售额的预测结果偏得离谱。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be wide ˈopen</td><td>（比赛、选举等）胜负难料</td><td>With three teams on equal points, the championship is still wide open.<br>三支球队积分相同，冠军归属仍然难以预料。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb/sth a wide ˈberth</td><td>对……避而远之</td><td>I give that noisy pub a wide berth on Friday nights.<br>周五晚上我对那家吵闹的酒吧总是避而远之。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈwide boy (BrE, informal, disapproving)</td><td>做买卖不诚实的人；奸商</td><td>Some wide boy sold him a car with the mileage clocked back.<br>有个奸商把一辆调过里程表的车卖给了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(lay/leave yourself) wide ˈopen (to sth)</td><td>使自己易受攻击（或指责）</td><td>By signing without a lawyer you leave yourself wide open to a lawsuit.<br>不找律师就签字，等于让自己随时可能吃官司。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wild</b></td><td>run ˈwild (informal)</td><td>疯长；不受管束</td><td>Their kids run wild all summer while the parents are at work.<br>父母上班的整个夏天，他们家孩子都撒野没人管。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌwild ˈgoose chase</td><td>徒劳的追寻；白费力气</td><td>That address sent us on a wild goose chase across half the city.<br>那个地址让我们跑遍半座城，白忙一场。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wild ˈhorses couldn't/wouldn't drag sb (somewhere)</td><td>什么也无法阻止某人；八匹马也拉不回</td><td>Wild horses wouldn't drag me back to that awful restaurant again.<br>八匹马也拉不动我再去那家糟糕的餐厅。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wilderness</b></td><td>in the ˈwilderness</td><td>（政治家）在野；失势</td><td>After ten years in the wilderness, the party finally won an election.<br>在野十年之后，这个政党终于赢了一次选举。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wildest</b></td><td>beyond your wildest ˈdreams</td><td>做梦也想不到；远超想象</td><td>The little app made him rich beyond his wildest dreams.<br>这个小应用让他富得超出了自己最疯狂的想象。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>will</b></td><td>against your ˈwill</td><td>违心地；不情愿地</td><td>She was kept in the hospital against her will for three days.<br>她违背自己的意愿被留在医院三天。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>at ˈwill</td><td>任意；随意</td><td>Members can cancel the subscription at will, with no penalty at all.<br>会员可以随意取消订阅，不收任何违约金。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>where there's a ˌwill there's a ˈway (saying)</td><td>有志者事竟成</td><td>She learned Japanese at sixty — where there's a will there's a way.<br>她六十岁学会了日语，真是有志者事竟成。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with a ˈwill (written)</td><td>起劲地；热情地</td><td>The volunteers set to work with a will and cleared the beach by noon.<br>志愿者们干劲十足，中午前就把海滩清理干净了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>willies</b></td><td>give sb the ˈwillies/ˈheebie-jeebies/ˈcreeps</td><td>使某人紧张不安；令人毛骨悚然</td><td>That empty old hospital at night really gives me the willies.<br>那座夜里空荡荡的旧医院真让我心里发毛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>willy-nilly</b></td><td>do sth ˌwilly-ˈnilly (informal)</td><td>不由自主地做某事；违背意愿</td><td>He was dragged willy-nilly into a family argument he wanted no part of.<br>他不由自主地被卷进一场根本不想掺和的家庭争吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>win</b></td><td>I, you, etc. ˌcan't ˈwin (spoken)</td><td>怎么做都不讨好</td><td>If I cook she complains, if I don't she sulks — I can't win.<br>我做饭她抱怨，不做她生气，我怎么做都不对。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>win sb's ˈheart</td><td>赢得某人的心</td><td>He won her heart with nothing more than patience and terrible jokes.<br>他仅凭耐心和糟糕的笑话就赢得了她的心。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌwin or ˈlose</td><td>无论输赢；不管成败</td><td>Win or lose, I'm proud of how hard this team has worked.<br>无论输赢，我都为这支队伍的努力感到骄傲。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you ˌwin some, you ˈlose some (spoken)</td><td>有得必有失；不可能事事如意</td><td>We missed that contract, but you win some, you lose some.<br>那份合同没拿到，不过有得就有失嘛。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈyou win (spoken)</td><td>你赢了；我认输</td><td>All right, you win — we'll watch your film instead of mine.<br>好吧，你赢了，我们看你选的电影，不看我的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>carry/win the ˈday</td><td>获胜；占上风</td><td>Her calm arguments carried the day at the shareholders' meeting.<br>她冷静的论证在股东大会上占了上风。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wind</b></td><td>break ˈwind</td><td>放屁</td><td>Someone broke wind in the crowded lift and nobody said a word.<br>有人在拥挤的电梯里放了个屁，没人吭声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get ˈwind of sth (informal)</td><td>听到……的风声；获悉秘密消息</td><td>The press got wind of the merger before the board had even voted.<br>董事会还没表决，媒体就听到了合并的风声。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get/have the ˈwind up (about sth) (BrE, informal)</td><td>害怕；惊慌；忧虑</td><td>He got the wind up when the police asked to see his licence.<br>警察要看他驾照时，他慌了神。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go, run, etc. like the ˈwind</td><td>跑得飞快；疾行</td><td>The boy grabbed the ball and ran like the wind towards the goal.<br>男孩抓起球，像风一样朝球门冲去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈwind</td><td>即将发生；在酝酿中</td><td>There are big changes in the wind at head office, apparently.<br>据说总部那边正在酝酿重大变动。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put the ˈwind up sb (BrE, informal)</td><td>使某人害怕；使受惊</td><td>The tax inspector's letter really put the wind up my boss.<br>税务稽查员的信真把我老板吓坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the ˈwind out of sb's sails (informal)</td><td>挫某人锐气；使某人泄气</td><td>Her calm apology took the wind out of his sails completely.<br>她平静的道歉彻底让他没了脾气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>window</b></td><td>be, go, etc. ˌout of the ˈwindow (informal)</td><td>化为乌有；付诸东流</td><td>Once the rain started, our plans for a picnic went out of the window.<br>雨一下起来，我们野餐的计划就泡汤了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌwindow of opporˈtunity</td><td>可乘之机；机会窗口</td><td>We have a short window of opportunity to sell before prices drop.<br>在价格下跌前，我们只有很短的一段机会可以卖出。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌwindow on the ˈworld</td><td>了解世界的窗口</td><td>For my grandmother, the radio was her only window on the world.<br>对我奶奶来说，收音机是她了解世界的唯一窗口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wine</b></td><td>ˌwine and ˈdine (sb)</td><td>盛情款待；大吃大喝</td><td>The firm wined and dined us for two days before mentioning the contract.<br>那家公司连着两天盛情款待我们，之后才提合同的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wing</b></td><td>on a ˌwing and a ˈprayer</td><td>只有一线成功的希望；勉强硬撑</td><td>We finished the project on a wing and a prayer, with hours to spare.<br>我们全凭一线希望赶完了项目，只剩几小时富余。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˈwing (literary)</td><td>在飞行中；展翅而飞</td><td>A flock of geese passed overhead, on the wing towards the south.<br>一群大雁从头顶飞过，正振翅南飞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take</b></td><td>take ˈwing (literary)</td><td>展翅飞走；飞起</td><td>The startled pheasants took wing as the dog crashed through the hedge.<br>狗撞穿树篱时，受惊的野鸡展翅飞走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwing it (informal)</td><td>临时应付；即兴发挥</td><td>I hadn't prepared any slides, so I just winged it for twenty minutes.<br>我没准备幻灯片，就即兴讲了二十分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwing your/its way (to...)</td><td>快速前往；很快被送往</td><td>Your parcel is winging its way to you and should arrive tomorrow.<br>你的包裹正飞速送来，明天应该就能到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wings</b></td><td>(wait, stand, etc.) in the ˈwings</td><td>伺机而动；随时准备接替</td><td>A younger manager is waiting in the wings to take over the department.<br>有位更年轻的经理正伺机接管这个部门。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>winner</b></td><td>be onto a ˈwinner (informal)</td><td>稳操胜券；找到了赚钱的门路</td><td>With this recipe and that location, I think we're onto a winner.<br>有这个配方加上那个地段，我觉得我们稳赚不赔。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wipe</b></td><td>wipe the ˈfloor with sb (informal)</td><td>彻底击败某人</td><td>Our debating team wiped the floor with them in the final round.<br>我们的辩论队在决赛中把他们打得一败涂地。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wipe sth off the ˈmap</td><td>把……从地球上抹去；彻底摧毁</td><td>One flood was enough to wipe the little fishing village off the map.<br>一场洪水就足以把那个小渔村从地图上抹去。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wipe the slate ˈclean</td><td>既往不咎；一笔勾销</td><td>Let's wipe the slate clean and start the partnership again from scratch.<br>我们把过去一笔勾销，重新开始合作吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wipe the/that ˈsmile, ˈgrin, etc. off sb's face</td><td>让某人笑不出来</td><td>One look at the final bill wiped the grin off his face.<br>看一眼最后的账单，他脸上的笑容就没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wire</b></td><td>go, come, etc. (right) down to the ˈwire</td><td>僵持到最后一刻才分胜负</td><td>The election went right down to the wire, decided by a few hundred votes.<br>这场选举一直僵持到最后一刻，只靠几百票定胜负。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>down to the ˈwire (informal)</td><td>直到最后一刻；分秒必争</td><td>The match went down to the wire, with a goal in the final minute.<br>这场比赛直到最后一刻才见分晓，终场前一分钟才进球。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wisdom</b></td><td>conventional/received ˈwisdom</td><td>常人之见；普遍看法</td><td>Conventional wisdom says you should buy a house, but renting suits us.<br>传统观念说该买房，但租房更适合我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in your, his, etc. (infinite) ˈwisdom</td><td>以其（无限的）智慧（含讽刺）</td><td>Management, in their infinite wisdom, has decided to remove all the chairs.<br>管理层以其无穷的智慧，决定把所有椅子都撤走。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wise</b></td><td>be ˌwise after the eˈvent (often disapproving)</td><td>事后聪明；马后炮</td><td>It's easy to be wise after the event and say we should have sold earlier.<br>事后诸葛亮谁都会当，说什么当初该早点卖掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's no ˈgood (doing sth)</td><td>做……没有用；无济于事</td><td>It's no good complaining now; the tickets are completely sold out.<br>现在抱怨也没用，票已经全卖光了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/get ˈwise to sb/sth (informal)</td><td>识破；察觉；看穿</td><td>The neighbours finally got wise to his excuses about the missing rent.<br>邻居们终于识破了他关于欠租的种种借口。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put sb ˈwise (to sth) (informal)</td><td>告知；使某人明白</td><td>Someone should put the new intern wise to how this office really works.<br>该有人告诉新实习生这办公室实际是怎么运作的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈwise guy (informal, disapproving, especially AmE)</td><td>自以为什么都懂的人</td><td>Don't be a wise guy — just answer the question properly.<br>别自作聪明，好好回答问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wiser</b></td><td>be none the ˈwiser • not be any the ˈwiser</td><td>仍然不明白；还是没弄懂</td><td>He explained the rules twice and I was still none the wiser.<br>他把规则解释了两遍，我还是一头雾水。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be any the ˈwiser</td><td>毫不知情；没人察觉</td><td>If we put the money back tonight, nobody will be any the wiser.<br>只要今晚把钱放回去，就没人会察觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wish</b></td><td>(just) as you ˈwish (formal, especially BrE)</td><td>悉听尊便；如你所愿</td><td>Just as you wish, sir — we can deliver the order on Friday instead.<br>悉听尊便，先生，我们可以改到周五送货。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I ˈwish! (spoken)</td><td>但愿如此（可惜不可能）</td><td>A week off in Italy? I wish! I'll be here doing paperwork.<br>去意大利休一周假？想得美！我还得在这儿做文书。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the wish is father to the ˈthought (saying)</td><td>愿望是思想之父；一厢情愿</td><td>He's sure the team will win, but the wish is father to the thought.<br>他笃定球队会赢，可惜愿望是思想之父，不过一厢情愿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wish sb/sth ˈwell • wish sb/sth ˈill (formal)</td><td>祝某人顺利；希望某人倒霉</td><td>Whatever our differences, I genuinely wish her well in the new job.<br>不管我们有什么分歧，我真心祝她新工作顺利。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>wouldn't wish sth on my, your, etc. worst ˈenemy</td><td>连仇人也不希望遭此罪</td><td>That kind of back pain is something I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy.<br>那种背痛，我连最恨的人都不希望他遭这个罪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your wish is my comˈmand (humorous)</td><td>悉听阁下吩咐</td><td>Coffee with two sugars? Your wish is my command, madam.<br>加两块糖的咖啡？遵命，悉听吩咐，夫人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wishes</b></td><td>if wishes were ˌhorses, beggars would ˈride (saying)</td><td>空想无用；愿望不等于现实</td><td>Dreaming of a yacht won't help — if wishes were horses, beggars would ride.<br>空想游艇没用，要是愿望能当马，乞丐早骑上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wishful</b></td><td>ˌwishful ˈthinking</td><td>一厢情愿的想法</td><td>Expecting him to apologise first is pure wishful thinking.<br>指望他先道歉纯属一厢情愿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wit</b></td><td>to ˈwit (old-fashioned, formal)</td><td>即；也就是说</td><td>Only one person can sign the cheques, to wit, the treasurer.<br>只有一个人能签支票，即财务主管。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>with</b></td><td>be ˈwith sb (informal)</td><td>支持某人；与某人站在一起</td><td>We're with you all the way on this, whatever the committee decides.<br>不管委员会怎么决定，我们都全力支持你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get ˈwith it (informal)</td><td>跟上时势；顺应潮流</td><td>Get with it, Dad — nobody sends faxes any more these days.<br>跟上时代吧，爸，现在没人发传真了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwith it (informal)</td><td>时新的；时髦的</td><td>For a man of seventy he's remarkably with it about technology.<br>作为七十岁的人，他对科技出奇地跟得上潮流。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>with ˈthat (written)</td><td>说完便；随即；紧接着</td><td>She slammed the folder on the desk and with that, walked out.<br>她把文件夹摔在桌上，随即走了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wither</b></td><td>ˌwither on the ˈvine (formal)</td><td>逐渐消亡；无疾而终</td><td>Without funding, the whole research programme simply withered on the vine.<br>没有资金，整个研究项目就这样慢慢夭折了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>witless</b></td><td>be scared/bored ˈwitless (informal)</td><td>吓得魂不附体；无聊透顶</td><td>I was scared witless when the lift stopped between two floors.<br>电梯卡在两层之间时，我吓得魂都没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>witness</b></td><td>be (a) ˈwitness to sth</td><td>目击；亲眼看见（某事发生）</td><td>She was a witness to the whole argument outside the pub.<br>她目击了酒吧外的整场争吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bear/give ˈwitness (to sth)</td><td>为……作证；证明</td><td>The burnt fields bear witness to how dry this summer has been.<br>焦黑的田地证明了今年夏天有多干旱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wits</b></td><td>be at your ˈwits' end</td><td>束手无策；全然不知所措</td><td>I'm at my wits' end with this baby who refuses to sleep.<br>这孩子怎么都不肯睡，我实在束手无策了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>collect/gather your ˈwits</td><td>定下神来；保持镇静</td><td>Give me a second to gather my wits before I go on stage.<br>上台前给我一秒钟定定神。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>frighten/scare sb out of their ˈwits</td><td>把某人吓得魂飞魄散</td><td>You scared me out of my wits jumping out from behind that door!<br>你从门后跳出来，把我魂都吓飞了！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have/keep your ˈwits about you</td><td>保持机警；随机应变</td><td>Keep your wits about you when you're cycling through the city centre.<br>在市中心骑车时可得保持警觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>woe</b></td><td>ˌwoe beˈtide sb (formal or humorous)</td><td>某人可要倒霉了</td><td>Woe betide anyone who forgets Grandma's birthday in this family.<br>在我们家，谁要是忘了奶奶的生日可就倒霉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wolf</b></td><td>keep the ˈwolf from the door (informal)</td><td>勉强糊口；免于挨饿</td><td>Two evening shifts a week just about keep the wolf from the door.<br>一周两个晚班勉强能糊口。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a wolf in sheep's ˈclothing</td><td>披着羊皮的狼</td><td>That charming landlord turned out to be a wolf in sheep's clothing.<br>那个和气的房东原来是披着羊皮的狼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wolves</b></td><td>throw sb to the ˈwolves/ˈlions</td><td>置某人于险境而不顾</td><td>Management threw the junior engineer to the wolves at the press conference.<br>管理层在新闻发布会上把那位初级工程师推出来顶雷。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wonder</b></td><td>I ˌshouldn't ˈwonder (if...) (informal)</td><td>我一点也不觉得奇怪；很可能</td><td>They'll be late again, I shouldn't wonder, given the traffic tonight.<br>今晚这交通，他们又要迟到，我一点也不奇怪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's no/small/little ˈwonder (that)...</td><td>难怪；不足为奇</td><td>It's little wonder that she's tired, working twelve hours every single day.<br>她每天工作十二小时，累也不奇怪。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>it's a ˈwonder (that)... (especially spoken)</td><td>令人惊奇的是；真是奇迹</td><td>It's a wonder that nobody was hurt when the roof came down.<br>屋顶塌下来居然没人受伤，真是奇迹。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wonders</b></td><td>wonders will ˌnever ˈcease (spoken, usually ironic)</td><td>真是无奇不有；怪事年年有</td><td>He washed the dishes without being asked — wonders will never cease.<br>他没人催就把碗洗了，真是无奇不有。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌno ˈwonder (that)...</td><td>难怪；怪不得</td><td>No wonder you're cold — you're standing there in a thin T-shirt.<br>怪不得你冷，就穿件薄T恤站在那儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>work/do ˈwonders/ˈmiracles (for/on/with sb/sth) (informal)</td><td>创造奇迹；产生奇效</td><td>A week by the sea worked wonders for my mother's mood.<br>在海边待一周，我妈的心情大为好转。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˈmiracle-worker noun</td><td>能创造奇迹的人</td><td>Sorry, I need more time — I'm a doctor, not a miracle-worker.<br>抱歉，我需要更多时间，我是医生，不是神仙。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wood</b></td><td>not out of the ˈwood(s) (informal)</td><td>尚未摆脱困境；尚未渡过难关</td><td>The patient is stable, but she's not out of the woods yet.<br>病人情况稳定，但还没有脱离危险。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not see the ˌforest for the ˈtrees (informal)</td><td>见树不见林；只见细节不见全局</td><td>You're checking commas again — you can't see the forest for the trees.<br>你又在数逗号了，真是只见树木不见森林。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wooden</b></td><td>don't take any wooden ˈnickels (AmE)</td><td>请多保重；好好照顾自己</td><td>See you next month, Joe — and don't take any wooden nickels.<br>下个月见，乔，路上多保重。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get, win, take, etc. the ˌwooden ˈspoon (BrE, informal)</td><td>获得最后一名；成为末名</td><td>Our team took the wooden spoon again after losing every single match.<br>我们队一场没赢，又拿了倒数第一。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>woodwork</b></td><td>blend/fade into the ˈwoodwork</td><td>销声匿迹；隐没不见</td><td>When the bill arrived, he quietly faded into the woodwork.<br>账单一来，他就悄悄溜得没影了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come/crawl out of the ˈwoodwork (informal, disapproving)</td><td>突然纷纷冒出来</td><td>As soon as he won the lottery, distant cousins came out of the woodwork.<br>他一中彩票，远房表亲就纷纷冒了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>word</b></td><td>be as ˌgood as your ˈword</td><td>守信用；说话算数</td><td>He said he'd fix the fence, and he was as good as his word.<br>他说会修好篱笆，果然说到做到。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be a man/woman of his/her ˈword</td><td>守信用的人；说话算数的人</td><td>You can trust the builder; he's a man of his word.<br>这个建筑工你可以信任，他说话算数。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>by ˌword of ˈmouth</td><td>口头上；口口相传</td><td>The little bakery got all its customers by word of mouth.<br>这家小面包店的顾客全靠口口相传。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(right) from the word ˈgo (informal)</td><td>从一开始</td><td>The project was doomed right from the word go, honestly.<br>说实话，这个项目从一开始就注定要失败。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) get a word in ˈedgeways (BrE) (AmE (not) get a word in ˈedgewise) (informal)</td><td>插不上嘴</td><td>My aunt talked for an hour and I couldn't get a word in edgeways.<br>我姑妈讲了一小时，我一句嘴都插不上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>give sb your ˈword (that...) • have sb's ˈword (that...)</td><td>向某人许诺；得到某人的保证</td><td>I give you my word that the money will be back by Friday.<br>我向你保证，这笔钱周五前一定还上。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˌback on your ˈword</td><td>失约；食言</td><td>He went back on his word and sold the bike to someone else.<br>他食言了，把自行车卖给了别人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˈword (with sb) (about sth)</td><td>（与某人）简短谈谈</td><td>Can I have a word with you about next week's schedule?<br>下周的日程我能跟你谈两句吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a word in sb's ˈear (BrE)</td><td>与某人私下说几句</td><td>The coach had a quiet word in the striker's ear at half-time.<br>中场休息时教练私下和前锋说了几句。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in a ˈword (spoken)</td><td>简言之；一句话；总之</td><td>In a word, the whole evening was an absolute disaster.<br>一句话，整个晚上糟透了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>keep/break your ˈword</td><td>遵守诺言；食言</td><td>She kept her word and turned up at six with all the tools.<br>她说话算数，六点就带着全套工具来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your/the last/final ˈword (on/about sth)</td><td>最终的说法；最后决定</td><td>That's my final word on the subject — we are not moving house.<br>这事我最后表个态：我们不搬家。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>leave ˈword (with sb)</td><td>（给某人）留言</td><td>He left word with the receptionist that he'd be back by three.<br>他跟前台留了话，说三点前回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(upon) my ˈword! (old-fashioned)</td><td>哎呀（表示惊奇）</td><td>Upon my word, I never expected to see you here again!<br>哎呀，我真没想到还能在这儿见到你！</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be the ˈword for it</td><td>用这个词形容还不够</td><td>Annoyed isn't the word for it — I was absolutely furious with him.<br>说恼火根本不够，我简直被他气炸了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not/never have a good word to ˈsay about/for sb/sth</td><td>从不说……的好话</td><td>She never has a good word to say about her old employer.<br>她从不说前雇主一句好话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not a ˈword (to sb) (about sth)</td><td>只字不提；别透露半个字</td><td>Not a word to Mum about the party, or the surprise is ruined.<br>这派对的事别对妈妈说半个字，不然惊喜就没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put in a (good) ˈword (for sb)</td><td>为某人说好话；替某人美言</td><td>Could you put in a good word for me with the hiring manager?<br>你能在招聘经理面前替我美言几句吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the spoken/written ˈword</td><td>口语；书面语</td><td>Years of radio taught her the real power of the spoken word.<br>多年的广播生涯让她懂得了口头语言的力量。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb at their ˈword</td><td>完全相信某人的话并照办</td><td>He offered to help, so I took him at his word and called.<br>他说愿意帮忙，我就当真了，给他打了电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sb's ˈword for it</td><td>相信某人的话</td><td>I haven't checked the figures, so you'll have to take my word for it.<br>我没核对数字，你只能信我这一说了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌword for ˈword</td><td>一字不差地；逐字地</td><td>She repeated his apology word for word to the rest of us.<br>她把他的道歉一字不差地转述给了我们其他人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your, his, etc. word is your, his, etc. ˈbond</td><td>一诺千金；言而有信</td><td>Shake hands with old Tom and you're fine; his word is his bond.<br>跟老汤姆握个手就行，他一诺千金。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your, his, etc. ˌword is ˈlaw</td><td>某人说了算；某人之言即是法律</td><td>In that kitchen the head chef's word is law, and nobody argues.<br>在那间厨房里主厨说了算，没人敢争。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your, his, etc. ˌword of ˈhonour (BrE) (AmE your, his, etc. ˌword of ˈhonor)</td><td>用名誉担保</td><td>Give me your word of honour that you'll never mention this again.<br>你用名誉向我担保，绝不再提这件事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a ˌword to the ˈwise</td><td>对聪明人不用细说；提个醒</td><td>A word to the wise: don't argue with the boss on Mondays.<br>提个醒：周一别跟老板争论。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>words</b></td><td>have/exchange ˈwords (with sb) (about sth)</td><td>（与某人）争论；争吵</td><td>I had words with my neighbour about his barking dog again last night.<br>昨晚我又为他家狗叫的事跟邻居吵了几句。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in ˈother words</td><td>换句话说；也就是说</td><td>He's between jobs — in other words, he's unemployed at the moment.<br>他正处于职业过渡期，换句话说，他现在失业了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(not) in so/as many ˈwords</td><td>（并非）原原本本地；明说</td><td>He didn't say I was fired, not in so many words anyway.<br>他没直说我被解雇了，至少没那么明说。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in words of one ˈsyllable</td><td>简单明了地说；用大白话讲</td><td>Explain it to me in words of one syllable, please, because I'm lost.<br>请用最简单的话给我解释一下，我完全懵了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a play on ˈwords</td><td>双关语；语带双关</td><td>The shop's name is a clever play on words that always makes me smile.<br>这家店名是个巧妙的双关，总让我会心一笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put ˈwords in/into sb's mouth</td><td>硬说某人说过某些话</td><td>Don't put words into my mouth; I never said the plan was stupid.<br>别硬安我头上，我从没说过这计划愚蠢。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take the words (right) out of sb's ˈmouth</td><td>说出某人正想说的话</td><td>You took the words right out of my mouth — I was about to suggest that.<br>你把我想说的话说出来了，我正打算这么建议。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>too funny, sad, etc. for ˈwords</td><td>……得无法形容</td><td>The ending of that film was too sad for words.<br>那部电影的结局悲伤得无法形容。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>words ˈfail me</td><td>我不知道该说什么好</td><td>You cycled all the way here from Scotland? Words fail me.<br>你从苏格兰一路骑车过来的？我真是无话可说了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>work</b></td><td>all ˌwork and no ˈplay (makes Jack a dull ˈboy) (saying)</td><td>整天用功不玩耍，聪明孩子也变傻</td><td>Put the laptop away — all work and no play makes Jack a dull boy.<br>把电脑收起来吧，只知道干活不玩耍可不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be at ˈwork</td><td>起作用；在发挥影响</td><td>You can see the same forces at work in every failing high street.<br>在每条衰落的商业街上都能看到同样的力量在起作用。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go/set about your ˈwork</td><td>着手做自己的工作</td><td>She went about her work quietly, ignoring all the noise around her.<br>她不理会周围的嘈杂，安静地做着自己的工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go/set to ˈwork (on sth) (also get (down) to ˈwork (on sth))</td><td>开始动手；着手做某事</td><td>They set to work on the leaking roof before the rain got worse.<br>雨下大之前，他们就动手修那漏水的屋顶。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have your ˈwork cut out (to do sth/doing sth) (informal)</td><td>任务艰巨；有得忙了</td><td>You'll have your work cut out persuading her to move abroad.<br>要说服她移居国外，你可有得忙了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in/out of ˈwork</td><td>有工作；失业</td><td>He's been out of work since the factory closed down last spring.<br>自从去年春天工厂关门，他就一直失业。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˈwork it/things (so that...) (informal)</td><td>想办法巧妙安排</td><td>Can you work it so that we all fly out on the same day?<br>你能安排一下让我们同一天飞出去吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌwork like a ˈdog/ˈslave/ˈTrojan (informal)</td><td>埋头苦干；拼命干</td><td>She worked like a dog for two years to get the shop open.<br>她拼命干了两年才把这家店开起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>working</b></td><td>be working ˈovertime (informal)</td><td>（想象力等）过于活跃</td><td>It was only the cat — your imagination is working overtime again.<br>不过是只猫，你的想象力又在超负荷运转了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have a ˌworking ˈknowledge of sth</td><td>具备足够使用某物的知识</td><td>The job needs a working knowledge of Spanish and some basic accounting.<br>这份工作需要会用西班牙语，还要懂点基础会计。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in (full/good) working ˈorder (also in running ˈorder)</td><td>运转正常；状况良好</td><td>The old tractor is still in perfect working order after forty years.<br>这台老拖拉机用了四十年，仍然运转正常。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>works</b></td><td>good ˈworks</td><td>善举；好事</td><td>She's still remembered in the village for her good works during the war.<br>村里人至今记着她战时所做的种种善举。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈworks</td><td>在筹备中；在酝酿中</td><td>A sequel is already in the works, according to the director.<br>据导演说，续集已经在筹备中了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the (whole) ˈworks (informal)</td><td>全套；应有尽有</td><td>He ordered a burger with the works — cheese, bacon, onions, everything.<br>他点了个全套汉堡，奶酪、培根、洋葱，什么都有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>world</b></td><td>be, live, etc. in a world of your ˈown</td><td>活在自己的小天地里</td><td>My brother sits there in a world of his own for hours.<br>我弟弟能在那儿一坐几个钟头，活在自己的世界里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be/mean (ˌall) the ˈworld to sb</td><td>对某人极其重要；是某人的一切</td><td>That battered old guitar means all the world to him.<br>那把破旧的吉他对他来说就是一切。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come/go ˈdown/ˈup in the world</td><td>落魄；发迹</td><td>They've come up in the world since he sold the software company.<br>自从他卖掉那家软件公司，他们家就飞黄腾达了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come into the ˈworld (literary)</td><td>出生；降生人间</td><td>She came into the world during a snowstorm in the middle of February.<br>她是在二月中旬的一场暴风雪中降生的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for all the ˈworld as if/though...</td><td>完全就像；活像</td><td>He stared at me for all the world as though we had never met.<br>他盯着我看，活像我们素未谋面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>look, etc. for all the ˈworld like sb/sth (written)</td><td>看上去活像；酷似</td><td>In that hat she looked for all the world like her own grandmother.<br>戴上那顶帽子，她看上去活像她奶奶。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have the ˌworld at your ˈfeet</td><td>前途无量；春风得意</td><td>At twenty-one, with two gold medals, he had the world at his feet.<br>二十一岁拿下两枚金牌，他前途无量。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in an ˌideal/a ˌperfect ˈworld</td><td>在理想的状态下</td><td>In a perfect world we'd all work four days a week.<br>在理想的世界里，我们都可以每周只上四天班。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈworld</td><td>（用于强调）究竟；天下</td><td>What in the world made you paint the kitchen bright orange?<br>你究竟为什么把厨房刷成亮橙色？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a man/woman of the ˈworld</td><td>见多识广的人；老成持重的人</td><td>Talk to Ray about it; he's a man of the world.<br>这事跟雷谈谈吧，他见多识广。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not (do sth) for (all) the ˈworld</td><td>决不（做某事）</td><td>I wouldn't miss your wedding for all the world, you know that.<br>你知道的，你的婚礼我说什么也不会错过。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not/never set the ˈworld on fire (informal)</td><td>不会有惊人之举；不会引起轰动</td><td>His first novel won't set the world on fire, but it sells steadily.<br>他的第一部小说不会轰动一时，但销量稳定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not/never set the ˈThames on fire (BrE, informal)</td><td>成不了大器；不会引起轰动</td><td>He's a decent player, though he'll never set the Thames on fire.<br>他球打得不错，不过成不了什么大器。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ... of this ˈworld (informal)</td><td>像……这样的人；这类人</td><td>The Einsteins of this world don't come along very often.<br>像爱因斯坦这样的人可不是常有的。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>out of this ˈworld (informal)</td><td>好得不得了；妙不可言</td><td>The chocolate cake at that little café is out of this world.<br>那家小咖啡馆的巧克力蛋糕好吃得不得了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>see the ˈworld</td><td>周游世界；见世面</td><td>He joined the navy at eighteen because he wanted to see the world.<br>他十八岁参加海军，就是想去见见世面。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>what is the world ˈcoming to? (saying)</td><td>这世道成什么样了；太不像话</td><td>Children robbing children in broad daylight — what is the world coming to?<br>光天化日之下小孩抢小孩，这世道成什么样了？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>I don't know ˌwhat the world's ˈcoming to (saying)</td><td>真不知这世道要变成什么样</td><td>Six pounds for a coffee — I don't know what the world's coming to.<br>一杯咖啡六镑，真不知这世道要变成什么样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(all) the ˌworld and his ˈwife (informal)</td><td>所有人；人山人海</td><td>The world and his wife turned up at the beach on Sunday afternoon.<br>周日下午海滩上人山人海，谁都来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌworld is your ˈoyster</td><td>世界任你闯；前途无量</td><td>You've got a degree and no debts — the world is your oyster.<br>你有学位又没负债，天地任你闯。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>a/the ˈworld of difference (between A and B) (informal)</td><td>天壤之别；完全不同</td><td>There's a world of difference between reading about Rome and actually living there.<br>读关于罗马的书和真住在那里，有天壤之别。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the (whole) world ˈover</td><td>全世界；世界各地</td><td>Parents worry about exactly the same things the whole world over.<br>全世界的父母担心的事情都一模一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(think) the world ˌowes you a ˈliving (disapproving)</td><td>认为世界欠自己的</td><td>He's thirty and still thinks the world owes him a living.<br>他都三十了，还觉得这世界欠他的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>worlds</b></td><td>be ˈworlds/a world away (from sth)</td><td>与……有天壤之别</td><td>Village life here is worlds away from her old flat in London.<br>这里的乡村生活与她在伦敦的旧公寓有天壤之别。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>worm</b></td><td>the ˌworm ˈturns (informal)</td><td>兔子急了也咬人；老实人也会反抗</td><td>After years of insults he finally answered back — the worm turns.<br>忍了多年羞辱他终于回嘴了，兔子急了也咬人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌearly bird catches the ˈworm (saying)</td><td>早起的鸟儿有虫吃</td><td>I queued at six and got the last ticket — the early bird catches the worm.<br>我六点就去排队，抢到最后一张票，早起的鸟儿有虫吃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>worm's-eye</b></td><td>a worm's-eye ˈview</td><td>底层视角；小人物的看法</td><td>This memoir gives a worm's-eye view of life in a wartime factory.<br>这本回忆录提供了战时工厂生活的底层视角。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>worried</b></td><td>be worried ˈsick • be sick with ˈworry</td><td>非常担心；忧心如焚</td><td>Call your mother — she's been worried sick since last night.<br>给你妈打个电话，她从昨晚起就担心得要命。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you had me ˈworried (spoken)</td><td>你让我虚惊一场</td><td>You had me worried there — I thought you'd missed the flight.<br>你可把我吓着了，我还以为你误机了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>worries</b></td><td>ˌno ˈworries! (especially AustralE, informal)</td><td>没关系；不客气</td><td>No worries, mate — I'll drop the parcel off on my way home.<br>没问题，伙计，我回家路上顺道把包裹送过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>worry</b></td><td>not to ˈworry (informal, especially BrE)</td><td>别担心；没关系</td><td>Not to worry, we can always catch the later train instead.<br>别担心，我们可以改坐晚一班的火车。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you should ˈworry! (informal)</td><td>你根本不必担心</td><td>You should worry! You've already passed every one of your exams.<br>你有什么好担心的！你考试全都过了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>worse</b></td><td>be ˌworse ˈoff</td><td>处境更差；更穷</td><td>After the tax changes most families are worse off than last year.<br>税制改革后，多数家庭比去年境况更差。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you could do ˈworse (than do sth)</td><td>不妨试试；倒不失为可取</td><td>You could do worse than take the job while you look around.<br>你一边找工作一边先接下这份活儿，倒也不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>come off ˈworse</td><td>吃亏；输得更惨</td><td>He argued with the referee and definitely came off worse.<br>他跟裁判争执，结果明显吃了亏。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go from ˌbad to ˈworse</td><td>每况愈下；越来越糟</td><td>The weather went from bad to worse as we climbed higher.<br>我们越往上爬，天气就越糟。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>none the ˈworse for sth</td><td>没有因……而变差</td><td>The dog fell in the canal but seems none the worse for it.<br>狗掉进了运河，看上去倒也没什么事。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌworse for ˈdrink</td><td>喝醉了；带着醉意</td><td>He arrived at the party already clearly the worse for drink.<br>他到派对时显然已经喝多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌworse for ˈwear (informal)</td><td>用旧了；疲惫不堪</td><td>My boots look a bit the worse for wear after that long hike.<br>走完那趟长途山路，我的靴子看着有点破旧了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌworse ˈluck (BrE, spoken)</td><td>真不巧；真倒霉</td><td>I have to work on Saturday morning as well, worse luck.<br>我周六上午也得上班，真倒霉。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>sb's ˈbark is worse than their ˈbite (saying)</td><td>刀子嘴豆腐心；嘴狠心软</td><td>The old caretaker shouts a lot, but his bark is worse than his bite.<br>那老看门人爱嚷嚷，其实是刀子嘴豆腐心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>worst</b></td><td>be your ˌown worst ˈenemy</td><td>自己害自己；自讨苦吃</td><td>She's her own worst enemy, turning down every offer of help.<br>她自己害自己，别人给的帮助一概拒绝。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>bring out the ˈworst in sb</td><td>使某人显露最坏的一面</td><td>Long queues in the heat really bring out the worst in people.<br>大热天排长队真能把人最糟的一面激出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do your ˈworst</td><td>有什么手段尽管使出来</td><td>Tell the newspapers if you like — go on, do your worst.<br>你愿意就去告诉报社好了，尽管使出你的招数。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get the ˈworst of it • come off ˈworst</td><td>遭遇失败；吃最大的亏</td><td>Both cars were damaged, but the little hatchback got the worst of it.<br>两辆车都撞坏了，但那辆小两厢车损失最惨。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>if the ˌworst comes to the ˈworst (AmE also if ˌworst comes to ˈworst)</td><td>万一情况坏到极点</td><td>If the worst comes to the worst, we can always sleep in the car.<br>万一实在不行，我们可以睡在车里。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the worst of ˈboth/ˈall (possible) worlds</td><td>集各种不利因素于一身</td><td>Renting there gives you the worst of both worlds: high rent and long commutes.<br>在那儿租房是两头吃亏：房租高，通勤还远。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>worth</b></td><td>be ˈworth it</td><td>值得（花时间、金钱、精力等）</td><td>The queue took an hour, but the view from the top was worth it.<br>排了一小时队，但山顶的景色值了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be worth your/its ˌweight in ˈgold</td><td>非常有用；很有价值</td><td>A reliable babysitter is worth her weight in gold these days.<br>如今一个靠谱的保姆真是千金难求。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>do sth for ˌall you are ˈworth</td><td>竭尽全力；拼命</td><td>He rowed for all he was worth against the incoming tide.<br>他拼尽全力逆着涨潮划船。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>for ˌwhat it's ˈworth (spoken)</td><td>仅供参考；不论有用与否</td><td>For what it's worth, I think you should turn the offer down.<br>仅供参考，我觉得你应该拒绝这个提议。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not worth the paper it's ˈprinted/ˈwritten on</td><td>（文件等）一文不值</td><td>Without a signature that contract isn't worth the paper it's printed on.<br>没有签字，那份合同连纸都不值。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌworth your/its ˈsalt</td><td>称职的；胜任的</td><td>Any electrician worth his salt would have spotted that fault immediately.<br>但凡称职的电工都会立刻发现那个故障。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>(well) worth your ˈwhile (to do sth)</td><td>值得（做某事）；有用</td><td>It's well worth your while booking the tickets a month early.<br>提前一个月订票很值得。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>your ˌtwo ˈpennyworth/ˈpenn'orth (BrE, informal)</td><td>个人的浅见；一点看法</td><td>Everyone had spoken, so I added my two pennyworth about the parking.<br>大家都发言了，我就停车问题也说了点浅见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>worthy</b></td><td>worthy of the ˈname (also worth the ˈname)</td><td>名副其实的</td><td>No chef worthy of the name would ever use bottled lemon juice.<br>任何名副其实的厨师都不会用瓶装柠檬汁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wrap</b></td><td>wrap sb up in cotton ˈwool (informal)</td><td>过分呵护；娇惯</td><td>You can't wrap your kids up in cotton wool for ever.<br>你不可能永远把孩子捧在手心里过度保护。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wrapped</b></td><td>be ˌwrapped ˈup in sb/sth</td><td>全神贯注于；醉心于</td><td>He's so wrapped up in his research that he forgets to eat.<br>他一门心思扑在研究上，连吃饭都忘了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wraps</b></td><td>keep sth, stay, etc. under ˈwraps (informal)</td><td>把……保密；隐藏</td><td>The design was kept under wraps until the launch in March.<br>这个设计一直保密，直到三月发布。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wring</b></td><td>ˌwring your ˈhands</td><td>（因焦急）绞扭双手；干着急</td><td>Stop wringing your hands and just phone the insurance company.<br>别在那儿干着急了，给保险公司打电话吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌhand-ˈwringing noun</td><td>空自焦虑；徒然叹息</td><td>There was plenty of hand-wringing at the meeting but no real decisions.<br>会上一片唉声叹气，却没做出任何实际决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌwring sb's ˈneck (spoken, informal)</td><td>拧断某人的脖子（表示愤怒）</td><td>If he scratches my car again I swear I'll wring his neck.<br>他要是再刮花我的车，我发誓要拧断他脖子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wringer</b></td><td>go/put sb through the ˈwringer (informal)</td><td>（使）受尽磨难；备受折磨</td><td>The interview panel really put him through the wringer for two hours.<br>面试小组足足折腾了他两个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wrist</b></td><td>a ˌslap on the ˈwrist (informal)</td><td>轻微的责备；从轻处罚</td><td>He crashed the company van and got nothing but a slap on the wrist.<br>他撞了公司的货车，却只挨了轻描淡写的批评。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>writ</b></td><td>ˌwrit ˈlarge (literary)</td><td>显而易见；清清楚楚</td><td>Her disappointment was writ large across her face all evening.<br>整个晚上她的失望都明明白白写在脸上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>write</b></td><td>be nothing, not much, etc. to write ˈhome about (informal)</td><td>不怎么样；很普通</td><td>The hotel was clean but the breakfast was nothing to write home about.<br>酒店很干净，但早餐实在不怎么样。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>be nothing, not much, etc. to ˈshout about (informal)</td><td>没什么值得夸耀的；一般般</td><td>We won, though a one-nil result is nothing to shout about.<br>我们赢了，不过一比零的结果没什么好吹的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>writing</b></td><td>in ˈwriting</td><td>以书面形式（作为凭证）</td><td>Please confirm the cancellation in writing before the end of the month.<br>请在月底前以书面形式确认取消。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>the ˌwriting (is) on the ˈwall (AmE the ˌhandwriting (is) on the ˈwall) (saying)</td><td>不祥之兆；厄运临头的预兆</td><td>When they closed two branches, the writing was on the wall for us.<br>他们关掉两家分店时，我们就知道大事不妙了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>written</b></td><td>be written all over sb's ˈface</td><td>（情感）全挂在脸上</td><td>Guilt was written all over his face when I mentioned the missing cash.<br>我一提丢钱的事，他脸上就写满了心虚。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>have sb/sth written all ˈover it (informal)</td><td>明显带有……的印记</td><td>This prank has your little brother written all over it.<br>这个恶作剧一看就是你弟弟干的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wrong</b></td><td>ˌback the wrong ˈhorse (BrE)</td><td>押错宝；支持错了人</td><td>The investors backed the wrong horse and lost almost everything.<br>投资人押错了宝，几乎血本无归。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get sb ˈwrong (spoken)</td><td>误会；误解某人</td><td>Don't get me wrong, I like him — I just wouldn't hire him.<br>别误会，我喜欢他，只是不会雇他。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>get (hold of) the ˌwrong end of the ˈstick</td><td>完全弄错；误会</td><td>She got the wrong end of the stick and thought we were moving out.<br>她完全弄错了，以为我们要搬走。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>go ˈwrong</td><td>出错；出故障；弄错</td><td>Something went wrong with the boiler in the middle of winter.<br>隆冬时节锅炉出了毛病。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>in the ˈwrong</td><td>有错；理亏；负有责任</td><td>Admit you were in the wrong and she'll probably forgive you.<br>你承认自己错了，她多半就原谅你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>on the ˌwrong side of the ˈlaw</td><td>触犯法律；违法</td><td>He's been on the wrong side of the law since he was fifteen.<br>他从十五岁起就一直在跟法律作对。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take sth the wrong ˈway</td><td>误会（本意良好的话）</td><td>Please don't take this the wrong way, but that shirt doesn't suit you.<br>请别误会，不过那件衬衫不适合你。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you can't go ˈwrong (with sth) (spoken)</td><td>绝对不会出错；准没错</td><td>You can't go wrong with a black coat and a plain scarf.<br>黑大衣配素围巾，绝对错不了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wrote</b></td><td>that's all she ˈwrote (AmE, informal)</td><td>到此为止；就这么多</td><td>He missed the last putt, and that's all she wrote.<br>他最后一推没进，比赛就此结束。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>yank</b></td><td>yank sb's ˈchain (AmE, informal)</td><td>拿某人开涮；逗某人玩</td><td>Relax, I'm just yanking your chain about the parking ticket.<br>别紧张，罚单的事我只是逗你玩儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>yards</b></td><td>the whole ˌnine ˈyards (informal)</td><td>全部；一切；应有尽有</td><td>She planned the wedding with flowers, a band, fireworks — the whole nine yards.<br>她把婚礼安排得鲜花、乐队、烟花一应俱全。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>yeah</b></td><td>ˌoh ˈyeah? (spoken)</td><td>哦，是吗（表示怀疑）</td><td>Oh yeah? And who exactly told you that piece of news?<br>哦是吗？到底是谁跟你说的这个消息？</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌall (the) year ˈround</td><td>一年到头；终年</td><td>The pool is heated, so we can swim there all year round.<br>游泳池有供暖，我们一年到头都能在那儿游泳。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from, since, etc. the year ˈdot (BrE, informal)</td><td>从很久以前；从老早起</td><td>That pub has stood on the corner since the year dot.<br>那家酒吧从老早以前就立在那个街角了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>from, since, etc. the year ˈone (AmE, informal)</td><td>很久很久以前；从老早起</td><td>My grandfather has been telling that same joke since the year one.<br>我爷爷从老早以前就一直讲那个笑话。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>year after ˈyear</td><td>年复一年；每年</td><td>Year after year the same family wins the village flower competition.<br>年复一年，村里花卉比赛的冠军都是同一家人。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>year by ˈyear</td><td>逐年地；一年一年地</td><td>Year by year the coastline here is being eaten away by the sea.<br>这里的海岸线正被海水逐年侵蚀。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>year ˌin, year ˈout</td><td>年复一年（一成不变）</td><td>He takes the same two weeks in Cornwall, year in, year out.<br>他年复一年都去康沃尔度那同样的两周假。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>year on ˈyear (business)</td><td>同比；与前一年相比</td><td>Sales have risen eight percent year on year despite the downturn.<br>尽管经济下滑，销售额仍同比增长了百分之八。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>years</b></td><td>not/never in a hundred, etc. ˈyears (spoken)</td><td>绝对不会；永远不会</td><td>Not in a hundred years would I lend him my car again.<br>我再也绝不会把车借给他了。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>put ˈyears on sb</td><td>使某人显老；使人感到老迈</td><td>That long illness has really put years on my poor father.<br>那场大病让我可怜的父亲一下子老了许多。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>take ˈyears off sb</td><td>使某人显得年轻</td><td>That shorter haircut really takes years off you, you know.<br>说真的，这个短发让你看着年轻好几岁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>ˌdonkey's ˈyears (BrE, informal)</td><td>很久；许多年</td><td>I haven't seen Pete in donkey's years — how is he doing?<br>我好多年没见过皮特了，他还好吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>yellow</b></td><td>a ˈyellow streak (disapproving)</td><td>胆怯；懦弱</td><td>There's a yellow streak in him that shows whenever things get tough.<br>一遇到难事，他骨子里的怯懦就显露出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>yes</b></td><td>yes and ˈno</td><td>既是也不是；说不准</td><td>Are you happy here? Yes and no — the work's good, the hours aren't.<br>你在这儿开心吗？说不准，工作不错，时间不行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>yesterday</b></td><td>sb ˌwasn't born ˈyesterday</td><td>某人没那么好骗；不是三岁小孩</td><td>Don't try that excuse on me — I wasn't born yesterday.<br>别拿那种借口糊弄我，我又不是三岁小孩。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>yet</b></td><td>as ˈyet</td><td>到目前为止；直到此时</td><td>As yet, nobody has claimed responsibility for the damage to the fence.<br>到目前为止，还没有人对篱笆的损坏负责。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>yore</b></td><td>of ˈyore (old use or literary)</td><td>昔日的；很久以前的</td><td>The castle stands as a reminder of the knights of yore.<br>这座城堡让人想起昔日的骑士。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>young</b></td><td>be, stay, etc. young at ˈheart</td><td>人老心不老</td><td>At eighty he's still young at heart and dances every Friday night.<br>他八十岁了仍然人老心不老，每周五晚上都去跳舞。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>you're only young ˈonce (saying)</td><td>青春只有一次；及时行乐</td><td>Take the trip while you can — you're only young once.<br>能去就去旅行吧，毕竟青春只有一次。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>younger</b></td><td>be getting ˈyounger (spoken)</td><td>（某类人）越来越年轻了</td><td>Doctors are getting younger — mine looks about seventeen years old.<br>医生越来越年轻了，我的主治医生看着像十七岁。</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td>not be getting any ˈyounger (spoken)</td><td>上岁数了；岁月不饶人</td><td>I'd better book that hike now; I'm not getting any younger.<br>我还是趁早订那次徒步吧，毕竟岁月不饶人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>yours</b></td><td>you and ˈyours (informal)</td><td>你和你的家人</td><td>Best wishes to you and yours for a peaceful and happy Christmas.<br>祝你和家人圣诞平安喜乐。</td></tr>
</table>
